**“Take away from me”** — take away from me this truth
**“the way”** — which you teach
**“turn away the path from me, let the Holy One of Israel cease”** — at last
**“from before us”**
• in the presence
• his admonitions
**“the Holy One of Israel”** — therefore thus says the Lord
30.12:
**“Therefore”** — because you have rejected him
**“thus saith the Holy One of Israel”** — he thrusts himself upon the unwilling, so that you may feel as punisher the one whom you neglected as admonisher, and so that you might dwell in your land
**“Because you have rejected this word”** — this
**“Because you have rejected”** — Heretics also, and every doctrine contrary to the truth, trust in calumny and lying; therefore the city of their impiety will be destroyed, namely that which Cain built, on which sudden destruction will come when it has been captured by churchmen, and so destroyed and broken up that nothing remains in it that could rekindle the dead fire, or at least offer a little muddy water to the thirsty.
**“and have trusted”** — having confidence in the calumny and lie of the Egyptians
**“in oppression”** — deception
**“and tumult”** — the pride of Egypt
**“and have leaned”** — in hope
**“upon it”** — tumult
30.13:
**“Therefore shall this iniquity be to you”** — transgression of the precept
**“as a breach”** — of the wall
**“that falleth”** — so that you yourselves fall suddenly
**“As a breach”** — As the breach of a very high wall, which has drawn out a long collapse, can hardly be restored and recover its former beauty, so sudden destruction will come upon you.
**“and is found wanting in a high wall, for the destruction thereof shall come on a sudden, when it is not looked for”** — and found wanting in the high wall, because destruction of the wall will come suddenly while it is not looked for
30.14:
**“And it shall be broken small, as”** — another likeness
**“the potter's vessel is broken all to pieces with mighty breaking”** — a vessel of the potter broken with mighty breaking; so nothing useful will remain of you either, Nabuchodonosor pursuing
30.15:
**“For thus saith the Lord God the Holy One of Israel”** — who speaks to you through me and Jeremiah
**“For thus saith the Lord”** — Anagogically. He exhorts all to penance, especially and chiefly heretics, because if, returning from vices, they groan and do penance, they will be saved; whereas they, on the contrary, trusting in false masters and in the uncertainties of the world, desire Egyptian horses and rejoice in their swiftness, which the Lord forbade to multiply. Therefore churchmen will pursue them, and a thousand men, and the disordered crowd of fugitives, will not be able to withstand the voice of one warrior, or of five (which we ought to refer to the mind and to the five senses).
**“If you return”** — as if to do penance before captivity comes
**“and be quiet”** — in your land
**“you shall be saved: in silence”** — of quiet
**“and in hope”** — fixed in me and not in Egypt
**“shall your strength be. And you would not”** — to obey me
30.16:
**“But have said: No”** — we will remain here
**“but we will flee to horses”** — but to the horses of the Egyptians
**“we will flee; therefore shall you flee. And we will mount upon swift ones”** — we will go to them at swift pace
**“we will mount upon swift ones: therefore shall they be swifter”** — the Chaldeans, whom you will not be able to escape
30.17:
**“A thousand men”** — the Egyptians in whom you trust
**“for fear of one”** — the Chaldeans
**“and for fear of five shall you flee, till you be left”** — few, as a sign of so great a captivity
**“as the mast of a ship”** — fixed, as a sign of shipwreck
**“on the top of a mountain, and as an ensign upon a hill”** — to show the power of God, and whose word shall be fulfilled, mine or theirs
30.18:
**“Therefore the Lord waiteth”** — your penance
**“that he may have mercy on you”** — as if these things will come unless you do penance: therefore the Lord waits
**“and therefore shall he be exalted sparing you”**
• he is exalted in mercy; mercy exalts itself in judgment
• or on the cross, that he may spare all
**“because the Lord is the God of judgment”** — The Son: “For neither doth the Father judge any man, but hath given all judgment to the Son.”
**“blessed are all they that wait for him”**
• Wait for the Lord and act manfully, etc.
• with right hope
30.19:
**“For the people of Sion”** — of the Church, which is now in contemplation
**“shall dwell in Jerusalem”** — of the heavenly one, where there is the true vision of peace
**“weeping”** — before
**“thou shalt not”** — converted
**“thou shalt not weep”**
• God shall wipe away all tears from the eyes of the saints
• your weeping will be turned into joy
• Jerusalem
• Weeping thou shalt not weep. The Jews refer this to that time when, under Zorobabel and Jesus the high priest, after seventy years they returned from captivity to Jerusalem and wept for the good things they had had before. But we refer all the promises that exceed the modest measure of that time to the coming of Christ, in which the people once captive, freed by the Lord’s passion, dwells in Sion and in Jerusalem, that is, in the watchtower and the vision of peace, which is the Church.
**“he will surely have pity”** — daily
**“he will surely have pity on thee”** — altogether on the day of judgment
**“at the voice of”** — full of mercy
**“of thy cry”** — of prayer
**“thy”** — Jerusalem
**“as soon as he shall hear”** — if worthy to be heard
**“he will answer thee”**
• behold, I am here
• more in deed than in word
30.20:
**“will give you”** — The Jews say that, about to go out of captivity, they suffered want of food and drink
**“the Lord; spare bread”**
• the doctrine of the gospel, which by two commandments restricts all the commandments of the Old Testament
• Where Scripture is obscure, there is bread; where it is open, there is water
**“short water: and will not cause to flee away”** — to withdraw
**“from thee any more, thy teacher”** — “For one is your master, Christ.”
**“and thy eyes shall”** — of the heart
**“see thy teacher”** — now in hope, at last in reality
30.21:
**“and their ears”** — inner
**“shall hear”** — shall hear
**“the word of one admonishing thee behind thy back”** — of Christ
**“This is the way”**
• Christ speaks to believers.
• I am the way, and the truth, and the life.
• Imitate me. Whence: “Sell all, and follow me”; and “If any man minister to me, let him follow me.”
**“walk ye in it”**
• from virtue to virtue
• Be not overmuch just.
**“neither to the right hand, nor to the left”**
• you turn aside to evil
• Behind thy back, etc. In the first creation, as it were before his face, Adam heard from the Lord: “Increase and multiply, and fill the earth.” After sin, as though placed behind his back: “Cursed is the earth in thy work.” By his fall we all go backward, and now we hear from the Lord: “Be converted to me, and I will be converted to you,” and elsewhere: “Be converted to me with all your heart,” etc., that by these warnings we may seek the things that are before; and this is: “thy ears shall hear the word of one admonishing thee behind thy back.”
• Neither to the right hand, etc. One must not turn aside, but walk the public road, that is, the royal way, which does not deceive.
**“Neither to the right hand”** — On either side, whatever goes beyond measure is a vice.
30.22:
**“And thou shalt defile”** — Turned to the faith, you will reckon all idols defiled, graven and molten.
**“the plates of thy graven things of silver, and the garment”** — ornament
**“of thy molten things of gold, and shalt cast them away as the uncleanness of a menstruous woman; get thee hence”** — Isaias or Jeremias
**“Thou shalt say to it”** — to the believing people from the Gentiles
**“And thou shalt defile the plates”** — Idols, namely, which the artful tongue has composed in the likeness of truth: in the brilliance of eloquence, which signifies silver, and in the reasoning of wisdom, which signifies gold, you will crush, indeed scatter, and judge unclean.
30.23:
**“And rain shall be given”** — the grace of the Holy Spirit
**“to thy seed”** — to preaching
**“wheresoever thou shalt sow in the land”** — in whatever nation
**“and the bread of the corn of the land”** — “I am the living bread”
**“shall be most plentiful”** — in the hearts of the saints
**“and fat”** — by the grace and fatness of the Holy Spirit
**“shall feed”**
• with the bread of the word of God
• Some maintain that these things are hyperbolic, fulfilled in the time of Cyrus, who released the captivity of the people in Juda.
**“in thy possession”** — the Church
**“in that day”** — when you have broken the idols
**“The lamb; at large”**
• the meek in heart, who follows the Lamb wherever he goes, and is always at his right hand
• And rain shall be given, etc. In the book of Kings it is written that when the false prophets had been slain by Elias, rain was given to the land of Israel, and bread to Eliseus. And afterwards the Saviour’s bread was most plentiful and most fat, and had such fullness that many thousands of men were filled. In the present place also, rain is not given to the spiritual seed, nor is the bread of the land most plentiful and most fat, unless the idols silvered and gilded have been broken up and reckoned as dung; for unless they cast away vices, virtues do not come in.
30.24:
**“And thy oxen”**
• the apostles, leaders of the flock
• apostles, or apostolic men
**“and the ass colts”**
• that is, the sons of the Jews, who are signified by the she-ass, or the Gentiles, who are signified by the colt of the ass
• subject
**“that till the ground”**
• that they may bear fruit
• the Church, or each one his own body
**“mingled”** — the history with the spiritual sense
**“provender”** — a mixture is barley with chaff
**“shall eat in the floor”** — Scripture
**“as it was winnowed”** — examined by the Holy Spirit
**“Mingled provender”** — Mingled provender. Isaac sowed barley, because he was among the Philistines, and received a hundredfold crop of barley. And Osee hired an adulteress for a measure and a half of barley. The Saviour also filled with barley loaves the five thousand men, who followed the five senses of the body and the law of Moses; and in another place, breaking seven loaves and crumbling them into pieces, he filled the four thousand with wheaten loaves, who followed the evangelical number. A part of such a people eat of the chaff, in some following the letter; and through chaff and barley they gradually advance and pass to wheat.
30.25:
**“And there shall be”**
• of the day of judgment
• And there shall be. On the day of God’s judgment there will be streams of running waters over the mountains and hills, because the good works of the saints, who by observing the commandments fulfilled them, will shine; and as the day of judgment draws near, the teaching of the gospel will abound among almost all nations through the preaching of Elias and Enoch.
**“upon every high mountain, and upon every elevated hill”** — saints eminent in virtues, either more or less, or expounders of the divine words
**“rivers of running waters”**
• the teaching of the gospel
• And there shall be upon all the mountains. The Jews refer the many slain and the falling towers to the Roman empire; whence, “that he who now holdeth, do hold, until he be taken out of the way”; for at that time there would be so great a blessedness for the people of Israel that not only the valleys and plains but the mountains and hills would be watered with flowing waters. We understand the mountains and hills as those who are raised up by virtues, who hunger and thirst after justice, whom the Lord calls to drink; for he that shall drink of his waters shall not thirst for ever. Whence: “Bless the Lord from the fountains of Israel.”
**“in the day of the slaughter”** — of judgment
**“of many, when the tower shall fall”** — of many, when the towers shall fall: demons, the bulwark of evils, and the princes of this world
**“of the slaughter of many”** — For many are called, but few chosen. The towers are the powers of demons, or the proud, of whom it is said: “I have seen the wicked highly exalted, and lifted up like the cedars of Libanus.” They desired to build these towers who move their feet from the east, whose tongues were confounded in Babylon, and upon whom the tower in Siloe fell.
30.26:
**“And the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun”** — after judgment there will be a new heaven and a new earth; for the earth, made for man, was made worse by his fall, and the sun and moon were diminished in their light
**“and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold”** — the finite for the infinite
**“as the light of seven days”** — that is, when the world was created
**“in the day when the Lord shall bind up”** — in healing
**“wounds”** — the mortality of sin and all miseries
**“of his people”**
• absolutely, so as to signify all who serve God
• of the saints
• pain and groaning will flee
**“And the light”** — And the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun. When they receive the reward of their labour, because the creature shall be delivered from the servitude of corruption. It is no wonder if the moon receives the brightness of the sun, because the just shall shine as the sun.
30.27:
**“Behold”** — he promises rewards to the good, and threatens punishments to the scorners
**“the name of the Lord cometh”** — to condemn the wicked and to reward the good
**“from afar”** — after many ages
**“his wrath burneth”** — in vengeance, after our manner
**“and is heavy”** — to the reprobate
**“to bear: his lips”** — words
**“his”**
• Sons.
• saying: For I was hungry, and you gave me not to eat, etc.
**“are filled with indignation, and his tongue as a devouring fire”** — Go, you cursed, into everlasting fire.
**“Behold the name of the Lord”** — The Son in the name of the Father; for the name is one: the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit. Whence: baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost, not in the names but in the name, which is God.
30.28:
**“His breath”** — the devil and his members.
**“as a torrent overflowing even to the midst of the neck, to destroy the nations unto nothing, and the bridle of error”**
• the dominion of the devil.
• the devil, who drags his subjects into ruin.
**“that was in the jaws of the people”**
• His breath, etc. As an overflowing torrent, when it has reached the neck, suffocates the living creature, so the spirit of God’s wrath in judgment will suffocate the wicked.
• It signifies that the end of all has come: as a torrent suffocates him to whose neck it reaches, so God’s judgment will pass over no one unpunished.
• That was in the jaws, etc. So that they are carried about at the will of the devil, the Lord will destroy these on the day of judgment, or in the preaching of the apostles when the nations come to the faith and abandon idols.
30.29:
**“You shall have a song as in the night of the sanctified solemnity, and joy of heart, as when one goeth with a pipe, to come into”** — The Jews into the temple; the saints into heaven.
**“the mountain of the Lord, to the Mighty One of Israel”**
• You shall have a song, etc. After the punishment of the wicked, he speaks of the glory of the saints.
• As the children of Israel, having passed the Red Sea, when they saw Pharao and the Egyptians drowned, said with joy, “Let us sing to the Lord, for he is gloriously magnified,” etc. So on the day of judgment, the world having passed away and the devil and his members condemned, the saints will exult with joy in the praises of God; in the same way in the conversion of the Gentiles.
• As one goes with a pipe, etc. It was commanded to the sons of Israel that they should offer the tithes of their goods to the temple of the Lord, glorifying the giver of goods; so the saints in judgment will offer their sheaves, exulting and praising God, and the converted nations likewise.
30.30:
**“And the Lord shall make”**
• The Father.
• in judgment.
**“the glory”**
• the vengeance on the wicked.
• The hour cometh, wherein all that are in the graves shall hear the voice of the Son of God, and shall come forth, etc.
• He returns to the punishment of the wicked.
**“of his voice”**
• The Son, who is also the Word.
• Go, you cursed, into everlasting fire.
**“and shew the terror of his arm”** — The Son.
**“in the threatening”** — Go, you cursed, into everlasting fire.
**“of wrath, and the flame of devouring fire”** — “A fire is kindled in my wrath, and shall burn even to the lowest hell.”
**“he shall crush to pieces with whirlwind”** — round about him a mighty tempest.
**“and hailstones”** — by the stoning of tribulation.
30.31:
**“For at the voice of the Lord”** — by a terrible sentence.
**“the Assyrian shall fear”** — the devil and his members.
**“being struck with the rod”** — of vengeance.
30.32:
**“and”** — This is against Origen.
**“the passage of the rod shall be”** — of persecution of the earth.
**“strongly grounded”** — not transitory
**“which the Lord shall make to rest”** — that it may not pass away
**“upon him”** — the devil
**“with timbrels and harps”**
• the joy of the saints
• the just man will rejoice when he sees the vengeance
**“and in great battles he shall over throw them”**
• the reprobate
• demons
30.33:
**“For Topheth is prepared”** — “Depart, you cursed, into everlasting fire which was prepared for the devil and his angels”
**“from yesterday”** — from the beginning
**“Topheth”** — the valley of Gehenna
**“by the king”** — by the almighty
**“prepared”** — for the impious
**“deep, and wide. The nourishment thereof is fire and much wood”** — the wicked
**“the breath of the Lord”**
• wrath
• a metaphor: for it will be kindled by the breath and will of the Lord
**“as a torrent of brimstone”** — which stirs up or shakes out flames
**“kindling it”**
• hoping in idols, who boasts that he has the worship of God
• Gehenna
**“brimstone”** — In hell there is an intolerable stench and an unquenchable fire.

31.1:
**“Woe to them that go down to Egypt”**
• despising the commands of the Lord out of fear of the Chaldeans
• He has treated of the glory of the good and the punishment of the reprobate; now he turns to the remnant that remained in the land of Juda, Sedecias having been led away to Babylon, and others. But first he warned them not to go into Egypt; now, since they have gone, he threatens evil.
**“for help”** — to seek help
**“trusting in horses”** — not in the Lord; the horse is deceitful for salvation
**“and putting their confidence in”** — or: upon
**“chariots, because they are many”** — he cast the horse and rider of the Egyptians into the sea
**“and in horsemen, because they are very strong”** — who, to those remaining in their land, promised help through Jeremias
**“have not trusted”** — They did not seek with the heart but with words; for they said to Jeremias, “Pray for us to the Lord, what we ought to do,” and they were unwilling to obey. Like this, they did not call upon God, which was said of the wicked priests.
31.2:
**“But he that is the wise one”** — the almighty
**“hath brought evil”** — Nabuchodonosor; or evil absolutely, that is, the thing and not the person
**“and his words”** — which he spoke through Jeremias and Isaias
**“hath not removed”** — making void
**“and he will rise up against the house”** — the tribe of Juda
**“of the wicked”** — unbelievers
**“and against the aid of them that work”** — of the Egyptians
**“for their iniquity”** — But he that is the wise one, etc. “Cursed be the man that trusteth in man, and maketh flesh his arm,” etc.; and elsewhere: “vain is the salvation of man.” We can understand this of those who in time of persecution do not trust in the Lord but in the help of the world, not knowing that Abraham was imperilled in Egypt, and that there the people of God served in clay and in brick, which is spiritually called an iron furnace; whence in the Apocalypse the place where the Lord was crucified is specially called Sodom and Egypt.
31.3:
**“Egypt”** — Egyptian
**“man”** — frail
**“and not God”** — unconquerable
**“and their horses”** — in whom trusting
**“flesh”** — quickly failing
**“and not spirit: and the Lord shall put down his hand”** — loosens the reins
**“and the helper shall fall”** — Egyptian
**“and shall fall”** — Jew
**“and they shall all be confounded together”** — by Nabuchodonosor
31.4:
**“For thus saith the Lord to me: Like as the lion roareth”** — of the tribe of Juda
**“and the lion's whelp upon his prey, and when a multitude of shepherds shall come against him, he will not fear at their voice”** — trusting in his strength
**“nor be afraid of their multitude: so”** — in pity
**“so shall the Lord of hosts come down to fight”** — as defender
**“concerning”** — not against
**“mount Sion, and upon the hill thereof.”** — FOR THUS SAITH THE LORD TO ME, etc. This is said of those who, led into captivity with Sedecias, returned after seventy years, the Lord having mercy, the Israelites and the Egyptians in whose help they trusted having been cut down in Egypt.
31.5:
**“As birds dying”**
• over the chicks
• as a hen gathers her chicks
• as an eagle urges her chicks to fly
**“so will the Lord of hosts protect Jerusalem, protecting and delivering, passing over and saving.”** — as a vigorous and provident prince
**“So will the Lord of hosts protect Jerusalem”** — THE LORD OF HOSTS WILL PROTECT JERUSALEM. So the Lord did against the Samaritans, who tried to hinder the building of the temple; and in the time of the Machabees he routed many with few.
31.6:
**“Return”** — repenting, the Lord fighting for you
**“as you had deeply”** — who in deep counsel have withdrawn from the Lord by sin
**“had deeply revolted, O children of Israel.”**
• Return, for if you are converted on that day, etc.
• The prophet admonishes the tribe of Juda and Benjamin that, before Sennacherib returning from Egypt with the Assyrians came into Jerusalem, they should return with their whole mind’s affection, as they had withdrawn into the depths of evil.
**“Return as”** — Return as. In the prophecy he keeps neither the order of time nor of history; he has spoken of those who returned from captivity under Jesus the great priest; now he returns to the times of Ezechias.
31.7:
**“For in that day”**
• Ezechias admonishing, when the Lord had delivered him from the hand of the Assyrians
• or, according to some, from the return from the Babylonian captivity until the coming of the Lord, the sons of Israel never worshipped idols.
**“a man shall cast away his idols”** — for which your city was taken.
**“of silver, and his idols of gold, which your hands have made for you to sin.”** — under the father of Ezechias.
31.8:
**“And the Assyrian shall fall”** — The Assyrian, through fear of whom you flee.
**“by the sword not of a man, and the sword not of a man”** — but of God; who in one night struck down a hundred and eighty-five thousand of them.
**“shall devour him, and he shall flee”** — Sennacherib with a few.
**“not at the face of the sword: and his young men shall be tributaries.”** — tributaries to Nabuchodonosor, and afterwards to the Medes and Persians.
31.9:
**“And his strength”** — the army.
**“his strength shall pass away with dread”** — the angels.
**“he shall pass”** — will fail.
**“and his princes fleeing shall be afraid.”** — ten, as they say, who returned with him.
**“the Lord hath said it”** — he promised the things said above, namely.
**“whose fire is in Sion”**
• that he may consume his adversaries as a flame consumes straw or wood.
• of love, in the present Church, which looks toward the future.
**“and his furnace in Jerusalem.”** — the fullness of ardour and charity in the heavenly homeland, where there is the full vision of true peace.
**“fire in Sion”** — Sion is the Church, in which is the fire and furnace that consumes sinners, namely that consumes wood, hay and straw.

32.1:
**“Behold in justice”** — would not respect persons.
**“a king shall reign”** — Christ.
**“and princes”** — the apostles.
**“in judgment”** — just.
**“shall rule”** — Behold a king shall reign in justice, etc. The prophecy about those who went down into Egypt being finished, it begins about the coming of Christ and of his apostles.
32.2:
**“And a man shall be”**
• the faithful people.
• As if he will be safe in tribulations, as one who, fleeing the wind and the whirlwind, safely hides himself in a place, and as one who finds the purest springs in the desert, and as one who avoids the heat of the sun under a projecting rock.
**“as when one is hid from the wind”** — of demons.
**“and hideth himself from a storm”** — of this world.
**“as rivers of waters”** — the watering of doctrine.
**“in drought, and the shadow of a rock”** — of the Church.
32.3:
**“The eyes of them that see shall not be dim”**
• Blessed are the eyes that see the things which you see.
• of the apostles, believing.
**“and their ears”** — of the heart.
**“of them that hear”** — who before were deaf
**“shall hearken diligently”** — the Lord preaching
32.4:
**“And the heart of fools”**
• before
• of the unlearned or of the Gentiles
• “the foolish things of the world hath God chosen, that he may confound the wise”
**“shall understand knowledge”** — of the Lord
**“and the tongue of stammerers”**
• who could not proclaim Christ
• before
**“readily”**
• readily
• as far as the words of faith
**“shall speak”** — the Spirit suggesting
**“and plain.”** — openly
32.5:
**“The fool shall no more be called prince”**
• of wisdom
• the philosopher; “the wisdom of this world is foolishness with God”
**“neither shall the deceitful be called”** — the scribes and Pharisees, who deceitfully interpret the law of God
**“great.”** — in the law
32.6:
**“For the fool”** — who trembled where there was no fear
**“will speak foolish things”** — You have a demon, and such like.
**“and his heart will work iniquity”** — “The fool hath said in his heart: There is no God.”
**“to practise hypocrisy”** — “we know that thou art a true speaker, etc.”
**“and speak to the Lord deceitfully, and to make empty”** — with the bread of the word of God
**“the soul of the hungry”**
• of the people
• by turning away from the preaching of Christ
**“and take away drink”** — of doctrine
32.7:
**“of the deceitful”** — of the teacher
**“The vessels of the deceitful are most wicked.”** — hearts, or hearers: as the master, so the disciple
**“for he hath framed devices to destroy”** — he devised arguments by which he would prove that Christ is not; whence, to Nicodemus: “Search the scriptures, and see that out of Galilee a prophet riseth not.”
**“meek”** — the simple
**“with lying words, when the poor man speaketh judgment”**
• “If I do not the works of my Father, believe me not.”
• Christ, poor for us.
32.8:
**“But the prince”** — Jesus, who is also poor.
**“will devise such things as are worthy of a prince”** — I came forth from God; and “I and the Father are one,” and the like.
**“and he shall stand above the rulers”** — The apostles.
**“shall stand”** — as one anxious for us all.
32.9:
**“ye rich women”** — formerly.
**“Rise up”** — from vices.
**“and give ear”** — after the fall.
**“my voice”** — correction.
**“ye confident daughters”** — in riches.
**“Women”** — He addresses the matrons who are to be taken captive by the Romans, that they may repent; or by the women are signified the synagogue or the cities of Judea.
**“give ear to my speech”** — Ye rich women, etc. After the calling of the Gentiles, whom Christ taught in justice, the speech is directed to the rich women.
32.10:
**“after days and a year”** — two years and a half, and a year; that is, after three years and a half.
**“you that are confident shall be troubled”** — fulfilled.
**“for the vintage is”**
• or of the vintager.
• captivity.
**“the gathering shall come no more”**
• and this is the last and everlasting.
• That is, after the preaching of Christ; for since they were impenitent, and if not at once taken captive, yet at once troubled, because they would not receive the preaching of the Lord.

But when excuses are brought forward, both the beginnings of iniquity and its footsteps are hidden, since the one who corrects, losing everything he had known before, finds it wrapped up within the conscience by the evasion of a wicked defence. **“Thorns”** — Morally. Gregory. What is meant by thorns but the pricks of vices? What by nettles but the itchings of sins? In the houses of Babylon thorns and nettles spring up, because in the confusion of a reprobate mind there arise both desires of thoughts, which vex, and sins of works, which prick. The paliurus grows so thick with a surrounding of thorns that for its roughness it can scarcely be touched. Within, the nettle and thorn grow, but both are fenced on the outside by the paliurus; because lesser wicked men do any evil whatever if the greater and most wicked defend it.
**“And your strength shall be”** — there
**“the habitation of dragons, and the pasture of ostriches”** — signs of utter solitude
**“And it shall be the habitation”** — Gregory, in the Moralia. Against the perverse mind, under the figure of Judea, it is said: “It shall be the habitation of dragons.” What is meant by dragons but malice? And what is signified by the name of ostrich but hypocrisy? For the ostrich has the appearance of flying, because hypocrisy too offers to all who look an image of holiness, yet knows not the life of holiness. In the perverse mind, then, the dragon lies down and the ostrich is fed, because both the hidden malice is craftily covered and the pretence of goodness is set before the eyes of the beholders. And what is signified by the name of onocentaur but a slippery life, and the proud? For in the Greek tongue onos means ass, and by the name of ass lust is signified. The onocentaurs, therefore, are subject to lust and to vices; thence they lift up the neck. Whence it is well added: “and the hairy ones shall cry out one to another.” Who are figured by the name of the hairy ones, other than those whom the Greeks call planas and the Latins incubi? Their form begins from the human shape but ends in a bestial extremity. By the name of the hairy one, therefore, the roughness of anything whatever is signified, which, even if sometimes begun under pretext of reason, always tends to irrational movements. He ends as a man in a beast when, beginning a fault through an image of reason, he draws it on to an irrational effect. The hairy one cries to the other when malice committed provokes to committing malice.

34.15:
**“There hath the ericius had its hole”** — the prickly one
**“and brought up its young ones, and hath dug round about, and cherished them in the shadow thereof: thither are the kites gathered together”** — a bird of prey
**“one to another”**
• cried out
• There are gathered together, etc. Tropologically. The people of the Jews being expelled, under the names of beasts and monsters he signifies that idolaters and superstitious men will dwell in Jerusalem, and these he calls onocrotali, ericii, ibis, raven, dragons and ostriches, onocentaurs, and demons; and the lamia, which some of the Hebrews suppose to be a fury. And indeed if we consider that colonies from diverse nations were brought to Jerusalem, and that according to the rite of their own provinces, each province and family worshipped the monsters of their own demons, we shall affirm that all these monsters dwelt in Jerusalem.
34.16:
**“Search ye diligently”** — O you who are to come
**“in the book of the Lord, and read”** — that is, what I have learned from the Lord
**“not one of them”** — monsters
**“was wanting, one hath not sought for the other”** — each its mate, because the Lord brought both together
**“for that which proceedeth out of my mouth, he hath commanded”**
• “I will hear what the Lord God will speak”
• Christ
**“and his spirit it hath gathered them”** — monsters
34.17:
**“And he hath cast the lot for them”** — who should remain there
**“the lot”** — as if by his decree all things are fulfilled, and they do not abandon their order
**“and his hand”** — power
**“hath divided it to them”** — of possession
**“by line: they shall possess it for ever”** — not monsters but what they signify
**“from generation to generation they shall dwell therein”** — bestial, monstrous men

35.1:

• the Gentile world
• by God
**“desolate and impassable”**
• without Christ, who says, “I am the way, and the truth, and the life”
• without teachers of truth

**“and”** — that is
**“the wilderness shall rejoice, and shall flourish”** — with the odour of good repute: “we are the good odour of Christ unto God”
**“like the lily”** — As the lily among thorns, so is my love among the daughters
35.2:
**“It shall bud forth”**
• faith
• by hope
**“shall bud forth”** — work
**“and hath rejoiced”** — in hope
**“shall rejoice”** — having attained salvation by knowledge
**“and praise”** — God
**“the glory of Libanus”**
• of the temple of the law
• fertility of the land, for
**“is given to it”** — freely
**“the beauty of Carmel, and Saron”**
• there will be a desert in Carmel

**“they”** — the apostles and other spiritual people
**“shall see the glory of the Lord”** — one substance of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Ghost
**“and the beauty of our God”** — how the Father is in the Son and the Son in the Father; the Spirit in both
35.3:
**“Strengthen ye the feeble hands”** — of the Gentiles
**“feeble”**
• from good work
• Whence: “Stretch forth thy hand”
**“and the weak knees”** — limping steps among idols with diverse errors
**“confirm”** — in faith and truth
35.4:
**“Say to the fainthearted”**
• in faith
• that is, this

**“and fear not”** — the snares of the devil, the adversities of the world; the fear of the one God drives out the rest
**“Behold”**
• the cause of security
• because
**“your God”** — Christ, to whom the Father gave judgment
**“the revenge”** — in the judge
**“will bring the revenge of recompense”** — of the wicked
**“God himself will come”** — the cause of security
**“and will save you”** — good men
35.5:
**“Then shall be opened”**
• according to the letter
• In the first coming they shall see the light of truth.
**“the eyes”** — outer and inner
**“of the blind”** — without the light of truth
**“and their ears”** — both
**“of the deaf shall be unstopped”** — to the words of God
35.6:
**“Then shall the lame man leap as a hart”** — from vices to virtues, from the world to heaven
**“the lame man”** — without the step of faith and work
**“and the tongue shall be free”** — in the praise of God
**“the tongue of the dumb”** — whose mouths Satan had shut
**“for waters are broken out”** — because they have been broken; flowing out
**“in the wilderness”** — of the Gentiles
**“waters”** — of baptism
**“and streams”**
• abounding in the teaching of the Old and New Testament
• of spiritual grace
35.7:
**“And that which was dry land”** — without the dew of grace
**“a pool”** — into the fullness of knowledge
**“And”** — the same
**“the thirsty land springs of water, in the dens”** — in hearts
**“where dragons dwell before”** — demons
**“dwell before, shall rise up the verdure of the reed and the bulrush”** — in which the faith of the Lord is to be written, and the wearied limbs come to rest
**“The verdure of the reed”** — The fulfilment of Scripture, which is through the reed; and of the attentiveness of the hearers, which is through the rush. For reed and rush grow beside waters and are green.
35.8:
**“And a path shall be there”** — in the solitude of the Gentiles
**“and a way”**
• Christ
• “I am the way, and the truth, and the life.”
**“and it shall be called the holy way”** — holy
**“it shall be called”** — by the nations

**“the unclean”**
• blessed, unspotted in the way.
• the devil, a murderer from the beginning.
**“and this”** — the faith of Christ.

**“nor any mischievous beast”** — the devil’s attendants.

• the track of the serpent will not be found on the rock.
• cast out through faith.

**“that shall be delivered”** — from the bonds of sin and error.
35.10:
**“And the redeemed”** — by the blood of the lamb.
**“of the Lord shall return”** — through penance.
**“And they shall come”** — so.
**“in Sion”** — into the Church.
**“with praise”** — of God.
**“and everlasting joy”** — by hope of the eternal good.
**“upon their heads”** — the mind.
**“joy and gladness”** — “I have finished the course, I have kept the faith; there is laid up for me a crown of justice.”
**“they shall obtain”** — They shall obtain.

36.1:
**“And it came to pass”**
• the ten tribes having been taken captive and the cities of Judah laid waste, one comes to Jerusalem.
• The books of Kings and Paralipomenon agree that in the sixth year of the reign of Ezechias, Salmanasar king of the Assyrians came and carried off for the most part the ten tribes beyond the mountains of the Medes and Persians, with whom Tobias also was taken captive, as is held in his book. After Salmanasar, Phul, who himself also took the people partly captive; after him Teglatphalasar and Sargon followed, down to Sennacherib, who came up in the fourteenth year of king Ezechias. But how so many kings in so short a space? But the Hebrews hand down that one Sennacherib was called by so many names, and it is not unlike the truth.
• The sacred history relates that the first, Phul, king of the Assyrians, under Manahem king of Israel, laid waste the ten tribes; the second, Teglatphalasar, came into Samaria under Phacee the son of Romelia; the third, Salmanasar, under Osee king of Israel, took the whole of Samaria; the fourth was Sargon, who stormed Azotus; the fifth, Assaradon, who, Israel having been carried away, sent Samaritan settlers into Judea; the sixth, Sennacherib, who under Ezechias king of Juda, having taken Lachis and many others, besieged Jerusalem.
36.2:
**“And the king of the Assyrians sent Rabsaces from Lachis”** — which he was then assaulting.
**“to Jerusalem, to king Ezechias with a great army”** — multitude.
**“and he stood by the conduit of the upper pool”** — for it was also lower.
**“in the way of the fuller's field”** — where the fuller dwelt.
36.3:
**“And there went out to him Eliacim”** — the high priest, who succeeded proud Sobna.
**“the son of Helcias, who was over the house, and Sobna the scribe”** — the scribe.
**“Sobna”** — Sobna the scribe was another, not proud, who, as the Hebrews relate, terrified by the threat of Rapsaces, handed over the lower part of the city, while the citadel and the temple remained.
**“and Joahe the son of Asaph the recorder”** — the king’s chancellor
36.4:
**“And Rabsaces said to them”** — Some think this one was a son of Isaias, others that he was a Samaritan, and therefore spoke in Hebrew.
**“Tell Ezechias: Thus saith the great king”** — he strikes fear
**“Thus saith”** — As perhaps he had heard from his father, “Thus saith the Lord,” and so that his words might carry greater weight. Note the arrogance: “Thus saith the great king,” as if it were a contrary strength.
**“the king of the Assyrians: What is this confidence”** — the king’s words
36.5:
**“Or with what counsel or strength dost thou prepare for war”** — since you formerly paid tribute, whence now, moved by the desert of my severity, you incur it
**“on whom dost thou trust, that thou art revolted from me”** — by refusing tributes
36.6:
**“Lo thou trustest”**
• falsely
• He plainly lies. For nowhere is it read that Ezechias placed his hope in Egypt.
**“upon this broken staff of a reed”** — from the abundance of the waters of the Nile there are many reeds there, by which, mocking, he designates the strength of Egypt
**“upon Egypt”** — namely
**“upon which if a man lean, it will go into his hand, and pierce it: so”** — is
**“Pharao king of Egypt”** — unable to sustain
36.7:
**“But if thou wilt answer me”** — O Ezechias
**“We trust in the Lord our God”** — this is true
**“is it not he”**
• God
• this is false
**“whose high places and altars Ezechias hath taken away”** — which Achaz his father built and Ezechias destroyed, the idols having been cast down; but what he did for the cause of religion, this man perverts into sacrilege
**“and hath said to Juda and Jerusalem: You shall worship before this altar”** — alone
36.8:
**“And now deliver thyself up to my lord the king of the Assyrians, and I will give thee”** — in the person of the king
**“Two thousand horses, and thou wilt not be able”** — signifies the paucity of the besieged
**“their riders”** — Nor can you, etc. Not from weakness, but from observance of the commands of the Lord, who through Moses commanded concerning the king of Israel, saying: “You shall not multiply horses to yourself, nor chariots, nor very many wives.”
36.9: **“how wilt thou stand”** — as if you could not withstand even me, the least servant of Sennacherib; how will you withstand him himself?
36.10:
**“And am I now come up without the Lord”**
• as if in vain
• he refers to this: “If you answer me, We trust in the Lord our God,” quite cunningly
**“to destroy it”** — not because
36.11:
**“And Eliacim, and Sobna, and Joahe said to Rabsaces: Speak to thy servants”** — as if: why is there any need to stir the people with false terrors and to boast of vain strength
**“in the Syrian tongue”** — Chaldean
**“for we understand it”** — that which is common to both
**“speak not to us in the Jews’ language”** — He spoke in Hebrew, that terror might be struck into the people standing by.
36.12:
**“And Rabsaces said to them”** — Arrogantly.
**“Hath my master sent me to thy master”** — Elated into pride by the humility of the messengers, he addresses them all as one.
**“Hath my master sent me to thy master and to thee, to speak all these words; and not rather to the men that sit on the wall”** — Besieged.
**“that they may eat their own dung”** — By hunger.
**“and drink their urine”** — Driven by thirst.
**“with you”** — that flows at the feet.
36.13: **“Then Rabsaces stood, and cried out with a loud voice in the Jews’ language, and said”** — that the people might understand and fear.
36.14:
**“Thus saith the king”** — so that his power is set against that of which it is said: Thus saith the Lord God of Israel.
**“Let not Ezechias deceive you”**
• by encouraging.
• The accusation of Rabsaces is a testimony to Ezechias, that, trusting in the Lord, he has strengthened the people.
**“for he shall not be able to deliver you”** — although he promises.
36.15:
**“And let not Ezechias make you trust in the Lord”** — his own.
**“saying”** — He was conjecturing, or had heard from someone, that Ezechias persuaded the people thus.
36.16:
**“Do not hearken to Ezechias”**
• He mixes flattery with threats, so that those whom he does not overcome by terror he may overcome by promise.
• which may profit to your blessing.
• Do with me, etc. Praise me, bless me. Or as another edition has it: do what is useful to you, that you may receive me and peace may remain to you.
36.17:
**“Till I come and take you away”** — from Egypt; for he had decided to go thither, or Lobna having been captured.
**“to a land, like to your own”** — each one desires the land in which he was born.
**“a land of corn and of wine, a land of bread and vineyards”** — He promises a land of the Medes, which is like the land of the Jews in both cultivation and situation, for an equal cannot be found.
36.18: **“Neither let Ezechias trouble you”** — who are many, how much less.
36.19:
**“Where is the god of Emath and of Arphad”** — of Antioch and of the other cities.
**“where is the god of Sepharvaim”** — many gods also, whom the ten tribes worshipped before they were taken, and therefore perished.
**“have they delivered Samaria out of my hand”** — when he worshipped them.
36.20:
**“Who is there among all the gods of these lands, that hath delivered his country out of my hand”** — Likewise.
**“that the Lord may deliver”** — One, when the many could not deliver the ten tribes.
**“Jerusalem out of my hand”** — Answer not a fool according to his folly, lest you seem [like him]; and elsewhere, do not kindle coals.
36.21: **“And they held their peace, and answered him not a word”** — lest by answering back he should lead the people astray, or bring greater blasphemies; whence: “Do not kindle the coals of fire.”
36.22:
**“And Eliacim the son of Helcias, that was over the house, and Sobna the scribe, and Joahe the son of Asaph the recorder, went in”** — Jerome: leaving aside the clear things, let us defer the hidden.
**“to Ezechias with their garments rent”** — in the manner of their people, the blasphemy having been heard.

37.1:
**“And it came to pass, when king Ezechias had heard it”** — the blasphemy of Rabsaces
**“he rent his garments”**
• angry at his own sin, by which he thought the city was afflicted
• He rent his garments. They rend their garments, because they had heard Rabsaces blaspheming. The king rends them, believing that this had come about both by his own sins and by those of the people.
**“and covered himself with sackcloth”** — laying aside the royal purple
**“and went into the house of the Lord”** — fled to the help of prayer
37.2:
**“And he sent Eliacim who was over the house, and Sobna the scribe, and the ancients of the priests covered with sackcloth”**
• in a wretched dress
• not in robes
**“to Isaias the son of Amos the prophet”** — In the book of Kings it is read that he sent to the prophet Isaias; but here, because Isaias himself weaves the history, he does not call himself a prophet but names himself the son of a prophet.
37.3:
**“And they said to him: Thus saith Ezechias”** — they keep the humility of messengers, not of a king
**“This day is a day of tribulation”**
• complaint
• our
**“and of rebuke”** — divine
**“and of blasphemy”** — of enemies
**“for the children are come to the birth”**
• our counsels
• by the likeness of a woman in labour they signify their own pains
• as if we could not say: “We have conceived from your fear, O Lord, and have brought forth the spirit of salvation.”
**“and there is not strength to bring forth”** — of completing
37.4:
**“It may be”** — as if perhaps he will hear
**“the Lord thy God”** — we do not dare to say “our” God, whom we feel to be angry
**“the words of Rabsaces, whom the king of the Assyrians his master hath sent to blaspheme the living God”** — who is able to avenge
**“and”** — to
**“with words which the Lord thy God hath heard”** — lift up therefore our hidden prayer
**“for the remnant that is left”** — For now the ten tribes have been led away, the cities of Juda and Benjamin laid waste, and even the lower part of the city handed over into the hands of enemies by the impious and proud high priest Sobna.
37.5:
**“And the servants of Ezechias came”** — all kings, leaders, servants, counsellors, friends. Whence it is said to Chusi: “Why did you not go with your friend Absalom?”
**“to Isaias”** — Note the humility: he does not call himself a prophet.
37.6:
**“And Isaias said to them”** — Anticipating their prayer, foreknowing all things in the Spirit.
**“Thus shall you say to your master”** — not mine
**“Thus saith the Lord”** — my and his
**“Be not afraid of”** — threat
**“the words that thou hast heard, with which the servants of the king of the Assyrians have blasphemed me”** — servants
**“of the king of the Assyrians have blasphemed me”** — not you
37.7:
**“Behold, I will send a spirit upon him, and he shall hear a message”** — of Tharaca, as is clear in what follows
**“Behold, I”** — As if I were not saying all that I will do to the Assyrian, lest I seem to boast of my power, but only this one thing: Behold, I will send.
**“and shall return to his own country”** — of the Chaldeans
**“and I will cause him to fall by the sword in his own country”** — he says two things: that he desired to hear that Ezechias himself was to be freed from danger, and that the enemy was to die in his own land
37.8:
**“And Rabsaces returned”** — The Lord permitting he came; at his command he withdrew.
**“and found the king of the Assyrians”** — fighting
**“besieging Lobna. For he had heard that he was departed”** — now Lachis having been passed, where he had left him
**“from Lachis”**
• where he thought him to be
• And he found, etc. Herodotus and Berosus, the Chaldean writer of history, relate that Sennacherib king of the Assyrians fought against the Egyptians and besieged Pelusium, and, when the mounds had already been raised and the city was about to be taken, Theracha king of the Ethiopians came to its aid, and in one night a hundred and eighty-five thousand of the Assyrian army fell.
37.9:
**“And he heard”** — Sennacherib
**“say about Tharaca”** — now taken or deserted
**“king of Ethiopia”** — messengers
**“He is come forth”** — that is, this
**“to fight against thee. And when he heard it, he sent messengers”** — so that those whom he had not taken by force he might terrify by words
37.11:
**“Behold thou hast heard all that the kings”** — my fathers
**“kings of the Assyrians have done to all countries which they have destroyed, and canst thou”** — alone
**“be delivered”** — by one
37.12:
**“Have the gods of the nations delivered them”** — many, their own worshippers
**“whom my fathers have destroyed”** — the kings of the Assyrians
**“my”** — that is
**“Gozam, and Haram, and Reseph, and”** — destroyed
**“the children of Eden”** — of the eastern region
37.13: **“Where is the king of Emath, and the king of Arphad, and the king of the city of Sepharvaim, of Ana, and of Ava?”** — peoples, or according to others, cities
37.14:
**“And Ezechias took the letter”** — letters
**“from the hand of the messengers, and read it, and went up”** — against Sennacherib’s blasphemies he took up his usual weapons
37.15:
**“And Ezechias prayed”** — strengthened by Isaias saying, Fear not
**“prayed”** — Now more confident after deliberation. For before he went up, but it is not read that he prayed, because he feared these things would come on account of his sins.
37.16: **“O Lord of hosts”** — of men and angels
37.17:
**“Incline”**
• therefore
• by hearing
**“O Lord, thy ear, and hear: open”** — in mercy
**“O Lord, thy eyes, and see, and hear”** — in avenging
**“all the words of Sennacherib, which he hath sent to blaspheme the living God”** — not idols, not images of the dead
37.18:
**“For of a truth, O Lord, the kings of the Assyrians have laid waste lands”** — they likewise keep silent about us
**“and their countries”** — For of a truth, O Lord, etc. It is proved by many histories that the kings of the Persians came into Greece and overthrew and plundered the temples.
37.19:
**“And they have cast”** — idols
**“their gods into the fire”** — rightly
**“for they were not gods, but the works of men's hands, of wood”** — that is to say
**“and stone: and”** — therefore
37.20:
**“And now”** — thus
**“O Lord our God, save us out of his hand”** — thus
**“let all the kingdoms of the earth know”** — give glory to your name
37.21:
**“And Isaias the son of Amos sent”** — he did not go, because he had prayed so boldly, nor did he send to him as he had before
**“to Ezechias, saying”** — through messengers
**“Thus saith the Lord the God of Israel: For the prayer thou hast made to me concerning Sennacherib the king of the Assyrians”** — And Isaias the son of Amos sent, etc. The history of the Books of Kings and Paralipomenon is mixed into the prophecy, because the prophecy also concerns the deliverance of the city, the destruction of the Assyrian, the return of the sun, and the years added to Ezechias.
37.22:
**“This is the word”** — the sentence
**“which the Lord hath spoken of him: The virgin the daughter of Sion hath despised thee”**
• O Sennacherib
• when Ezechias’s messengers did not answer your messengers
**“laughed thee to scorn: the virgin the daughter of Sion”** — not corrupted by the worship of idols
**“the daughter of Jerusalem hath wagged the head after thee”** — fleeing, a hundred and eighty-five thousand having been slain
**“The daughter of Jerusalem”** — She who before had not answered, now sure of vengeance, safe from punishment.
37.23:
**“Whom hast thou reproached”**
• not to me but to God
• Ezechias to Sennacherib
**“and whom hast thou blasphemed”** — through your servants
**“and against whom hast thou exalted thy voice, and lifted up thy eyes on high”** — it is the mark of pride to raise the eyebrows
**“Against the Holy One of Israel.”** — not to me
37.24:
**“By the hand of thy servants”** — not your own, so that the arrogance might be greater
**“thou hast reproached the Lord”** — not to me
**“and hast said: With the multitude of my chariots I have gone up to the height”** — Jerusalem
**“of the mountains, to the top of Libanus”** — the temple
**“and I will cut down its tall”** — kingdoms
**“cedars, and its choice fir trees”** — powerful kings, kinsmen to the Jews
**“and will enter to the top of its height”** — the house of the Lord
**“Saltum”** — people
37.25:
**“I have digged, and drunk water”** — Metaphorically: as in passing, I subdued kings and regions with their inhabitants.
**“and have dried up with the sole of my foot, all the rivers shut up in banks”** — peoples
**“And have dried up”** — So great was the army that they dried up the streams, and therefore, for lack of water, made wells.
37.26:
**“Hast thou not heard”**
• The Lord to Isaias
• in spirit
**“what I have done to him”**
• from eternity
• I predestined
**“from the days of old”** — from the beginning
**“I have formed it”** — the evil that is brought by Sennacherib, not in that it is evil but in that it is just; and every just thing is good
**“and now I have brought it to effect”** — the same upon him
**“and it hath come to pass”** — this evil
**“to destroy”** — merits demanding it
**“hills”** — of princes
**“fighting together”** — among themselves
37.27:
**“The inhabitants of them were weak of hand”**
• my
• withdrawn from their help
**“They trembled”** — at his coming
**“and were confounded”** — with trembling
**“they became”** — were quickly consumed, sins hindering
**“like the grass of the field”** — they are not compared to olives, vines, nor fruitful trees
**“and the herb of the pasture”** — the thistle which impedes the harvest
**“and the herb of the housetops, which withered”** — in the hand of Sennacherib
**“before it was ripe”** — before the time of death
37.28:
**“Thy dwelling”** — Babylon
**“thy”** — O Sennacherib
**“thy going out”** — thence
**“thy coming in”** — into the land of the Jews
**“I know”** — I made the prophets know and announce
**“and thy rage”** — by which you said: Who God will be able to deliver you from my hand?
**“against me”** — I will go up into heaven, I will set my throne above the stars of heaven
37.29:
**“When thou wast mad against me, thy pride came up to my ears: therefore I will put a ring in thy nose”**
• by the power of the divinity restraining you
• Pride. I will no longer bear it, so that you may know that you could not do these things by your own strength but by my decision; for impious nations and barren trees deserved to be cut down by you as by an axe.
**“Therefore I will put”** — As if to say: by thinking you sigh after plots, but, being unable to accomplish what you desire, you bear the ring of my omnipotence in your nostrils; so that, while you pant more eagerly for the death of the good, you may return empty of their life.
**“and a bit between thy lips”** — with which you blasphemed me
**“and I will turn thee back”** — from Jerusalem into your land
37.30:
**“But to thee”**
• the prophet to Ezechias through messengers
• All this the prophet speaks to Ezechias through messengers: what he said to Sennacherib, and what the Lord answered him. Now he turns his words to Ezechias himself, that he may not doubt the things to come which he foretold. For in this chiefly the prophets were believed, that they testified to things not only far off in the future but to be fulfilled shortly.
**“this shall be a sign”** — of salvation and of those things which I foretell are to come
**“Eat this year the things that spring of themselves”** — which were sown, namely before the Assyrian came
**“and in the second year eat fruits: but in the third year sow”** — the Assyrian having been put to flight
**“and reap, and plant vineyards”** — which were laid waste
**“And in the second year”** — As the harvest was at hand the Assyrians rushed in and laid waste the crops and the vineyards and the oliveyards; and by reason of the excessive siege, what was found of the grain they had for food in the first year and the second; for because in the year of the siege they could not sow, they took what they found from the fruits and produce.
37.31:
**“and that which shall be saved”** — the remnant of the Jews, who do not believe they will escape but will receive such abundance that, like a most fruitful tree, they will be filled with fruit
**“of the house of Juda”** — that is
**“which is left, shall take root downward”** — by likeness of a fruitful tree
37.32:
**“For”** — because both the ten tribes and the cities of Juda were laid waste
**“out of Jerusalem shall go forth a remnant, and salvation”** — of those saved
**“from mount Sion: the zeal”** — love and mercy, not their merits
**“of the Lord of hosts”** — who was zealous for his people against their adversaries
37.33:
**“Wherefore thus saith the Lord concerning the king of the Assyrians: He shall not come into this city”** — although he besieges it
**“nor shoot an arrow into it”** — whence he may kill anyone
**“Wherefore”** — Therefore. He returns to his purpose and, after the hope of things to come, drives out present fear. For there will not be as great joy over the things promised for the future as there is care about the imminent ones.
37.35:
**“And I will protect this city, and will save it for my own sake”** — not by your merit
**“and for the sake of David”** — note that there are some who are heirs of David both in faith and in work
**“my servant”**
• God shows mercy for good fathers even to wicked sons
• For my own sake, etc. He signifies that they are preserved not by their own merit but by the clemency of God, indeed by the memory of their father David; in which David they are reminded of their own negligence, and of his faith and justice, which God loves so much that he protects the descendants of the saints for their merit.
37.36:
**“And the angel of the Lord went out”** — by the power of God, he killed without a wound and reduced to ash
**“and slew in the camp of the Assyrians a hundred and eighty-five thousand. And they arose in the morning”** — Sennacherib and a few with him, only ten, as the Hebrews and Israelites hand down
**“and behold they were all dead corpses”** — they were dead, corpses of the dead
37.37:
**“And Sennacherib the king of the Assyrians went out”** — from Judea
**“And returned”** — Therefore he was kept alive, that he might know the power of God, and might silence blasphemous mouths, and proclaim the majesty of him whom he had formerly despised.
37.38:
**“And it came to pass, as he was worshipping”** — a despiser of the true God, as a victor
**“in the temple of Nesroch his god, that Adramelech and Sarasar his sons slew him with the sword”**
• not by the angel, by whom the others were struck; he was reserved for the parricide of his sons
• In this he is shown more wicked than his people, because he was not struck down in God’s land by him, but, for the glory of God, like Pharaoh, was kept back amid many plagues to be slain by his sons in the temple of his god.
**“his sons”** — Envious, according to the tradition of the Jews, of Assaradon their brother by another mother, whom, for love of his mother, he had decided should succeed him in the kingdom; and because he had already begun to reign, they fled after their father was slain.
**“with the sword: and they fled into the land of Ararat, and Asarhaddon his son reigned in his stead”** — who sent inhabitants to Samaria, lest it remain uncultivated
**“Ararat”** — It is a region of Armenia, a plain, through which flows the Araxes, of incredible fertility, at the foot of Mount Taurus, which extends as far as there. But the ark of Noe was not carried to the mountains of Armenia in general, which is called Ararath, but to the very high mountains of Taurus, which overhang the plains of Ararath.

38.1:
**“In those days”** — in those days, that is, in which Sennacherib died
**“Ezechias was sick even to death, and Isaias the son of Amos the prophet came unto him, and said to him: Thus saith the Lord: Take order with thy house”** — who should succeed in the kingdom, etc.
**“was sick”** — Because he did not render thanks worthy of God for the victory, but vanished in pride, as the book of Kings and Paralipomenon reveals.
**“for thou shalt die, and not live.”** — Those whom God loves he corrects, lest he be lifted up in pride after incredible triumphs.
**“for thou shalt die, and not live”** — Likewise Nineveh will be overthrown, and many things foretold under threat, not fulfilled, not with God changing his sentence but provoking us to know him. For the Lord is repenting of the evil.
*Augustine:* In Psalm fifty: “The uncertain and hidden things of thy wisdom thou hast made manifest to me.” Under this uncertainty the Ninivites repented. For they said, “Who can tell if God will turn, and forgive?” Ninive therefore stood. Or was it overthrown? It appears one way to men, another to God. But I see that what the prophet foretold has been fulfilled. Consider what Ninive was, and see that it was overthrown in evil, and built up in good. So it was said to Jeremias: “Behold I will give you to root out, to dig under, and again to build up and to plant.” And hence also comes that saying, “I will strike, and I will heal.”
*Gregory:* Since prophecy declares the outcome of things with immovable truth, it seems false that Isaias said to the sick king, “Take order with thy house, for thou shalt die, and not live,” when the Lord added fifteen years to the life of the repenting and praying king. Likewise it is said of Jonas that he preached to the Ninivites, “Yet forty days, and Ninive shall be destroyed,” and yet afterwards, before forty days, the Ninivites obtained the mercy of God. But it must be said that the prophets, reading in that very book of God’s foreknowledge where all things are written, did not perceive all things but some, and in the same manner in which God permitted. For Isaias had read in that book that Ezechias, according to the works he had done, did not deserve a longer life, and according to the nature of the thing could not have it. But he had not read that he would obtain it by tears and prayers. Likewise Jonas had read in the same book that the wickedness of the Ninivites, according to what they were doing, was to be fulfilled on the fortieth day, and so their city to be destroyed. But he had not read that through his warning they would do penance and so obtain mercy. Each therefore preached what he had read, and as far as concerned them the truth was unchangeable, because they intended to deceive no one. For Augustine says: whoever believes as he speaks, even if he does not speak what is true, yet speaks faithfully. For the Lord, as Gregory says, changes the sentence but not the counsel. By sentence we ought to understand the sense of the words; the counsel, however, is from the eternal ordering. God had revealed the sentence to his servants, but not the counsel, so that by their threats he might strike repentance into his people and so have mercy on them. It seems, however, that they did not read in the book of life the words which they spoke. For since Isaias said simply “thou shalt die, and not live,” and Jonas “Ninive shall be destroyed,” and these things were not to come to pass, those things which were not to be do not seem to be in the book of God. But it must be known that God considers some things in two ways: according to merits and according to the nature of the thing, which are said to be inferior causes, and according to his own counsel. Whence God had foreseen that Ezechias would die, according to merit or according to nature, though it was not to be, and that he would not die, according to his own counsel. Both therefore were written in the book of life, but the one he permitted his prophet to read, the other was not permitted. He spoke the truth and was not deceived, because he read so; nor did he lie, because he so believed; and he spoke according to those inferior causes, although simply and without addition. If someone saw a blind man and said, “this man will see no more,” even if by divine counsel he received light, he would not be lying, because he followed the nature of the thing. In the same way Jonas also saw the overthrow of the Ninivites in the divine mind, which yet was not to be, because what he saw, he saw according to their merits. But that they were converted was of the counsel of God, which he did not see.
38.2:
**“And Ezechias turned his face toward the wall”**
• because he could not go to the temple
• of the house or of the temple, that his groaning might not be heard or his tears seen
**“toward the wall”** — Of the temple, namely; beside where Solomon built the palace. I beseech you, O Lord. About to go to the Lord, he recounts his works. Happy the conscience that in time of evils can call to mind good things.
38.3:
**“And said: I beseech thee, O Lord, remember how I have walked before thee in truth”** — of religion
**“with a perfect heart”** — not limping after idols; for who boasts of having a clean heart
**“I beseech thee, O Lord”** — Hearing that he is to die, he does not ask for many years but leaves to God’s judgment what he is willing to grant. He knew that Solomon pleased God because he did not ask for more years of life.
**“and have done that which is good”** — He destroyed his father’s idols, opened the doors of the Lord’s house which he had shut, broke the bronze serpent which the Jews worshipped in Gabaon, and threw it into the wind.
**“And Ezechias wept with great weeping.”** — He wept, because he was dying without sons, and feared that the promise made to his fathers would perish because of his sins, concerning which it was said to David: “When thou shalt sleep with thy fathers, I will raise up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels,” and “I will establish the throne of his kingdom over Israel for ever; and he shall be a son to me, and I will be a father to him.” Others assert that even the saints are terrified by death because of the uncertainty of the judgment. But it is to be noted that the day of death is not allotted to each by necessity but by the will of God, and for causes unknown to mortals one lives or dies; especially since now the appointed necessity of death is put off, and we read that very many were raised up after death.
38.4:
**“And the word of the Lord came to Isaias”** — before he went out to the middle part of the court
**“saying:”** — And it came to pass, etc. Here the history is related in an inverted order, which in the book of Kings is read in its proper sequence.
38.5:
**“Go and say to Ezechias: Thus saith the Lord the God of David thy father”** — whose promise you desire, you pursue by works; for he did right as David his father did, because you walked in truth and with a perfect heart
**“I have heard thy prayer, and I have seen thy tears”** — because you wept with great weeping
**“behold I will add to thy days fifteen years”**
• which you did not ask for
• Some say that by living badly one does not deserve to reach the end of his life, or that by acting well one deserves to be taken before the time to the rewards of life. Whence: “Bloody men shall not live out half their days.” And that: “He was taken away lest wickedness should alter his understanding.
• The history of the books of Kings and Paralipomenon is mingled with prophecy, because the prophecy is also joined to the history: concerning the deliverance of the city, the destruction of the Assyrian, the return of the sun, and the years added to Ezechias.
**“behold I will add to thy days”** — According to what appeared. For in foreknowledge, in which these years also were, nothing was added; for God foresaw that he would indeed be afflicted with sickness unto death, but would recover by prayer and penance.
38.6: **“out of the hand of the king of the Assyrians”** — moreover, security of the kingdom is promised
38.7:
**“And this shall be a sign to thee from the Lord”**
• The Jews always seek a sign
• Of the present time, namely, and of the future: as when the sun returns to its beginning. So Ezechias’s life returns to the years that have run out. For us too, living in the week and the eighth day after Christ’s resurrection, the spans of life are prolonged.
38.8: **“Behold I will bring again the shadow of the lines, by which it is now gone down in the sun dial of Achaz with the sun, ten lines backward.”** — For from the tenth hour back to the first, and the day was nearly doubled.
38.9: **“The writing of Ezechias king of Juda”** — The Septuagint: a prayer; but this is better, because it tells of past things, giving thanks for a benefit.
38.10:
**“I said: In the midst of my days”**
• because I shall not complete the number of my years as my fathers did.
• despairing
• in distress
**“I shall go to the gates of hell”** — to the gates, that is, the vices which are the gates of hell.
**“I sought for the residue of my years”** — taken from me on account of pride.
**“I said”** — When God had given Ezechias the victory without labour, and he had not rendered him worthy thanks, constrained by sickness he paid the praises which he had neglected in prosperity; and after he recovered, he proclaimed what he had thought in his distress. I said: In the midst, etc. The saints fulfil their holy days; Abraham died “full of days, in a good old age”; sinners die in the midst of their days.
**“In the midst of my days”** — Wicked men do not live out half their days, because they do not fulfill works of virtue, nor by repenting amend their sins.
**“to the gates of hell”** — Where a house is appointed for every one that liveth, before the coming of Christ.
38.11:
**“I said”** — within myself
**“I shall not see the Lord God”**
• condemned among the dead in hell
• The Lord, according to Jerome.
**“the Lord God in the land”** — in blessedness
**“of the living”** — of the saints
**“I shall behold man no more”**
• he fears lest he look upon the saints of God, and dwell in rest, and see God.
• Christ, promised to us, true man and true God.
**“nor the inhabitant”** — Christ himself, or any just man.
**“rest”** — eternally
**“of rest”** — Some copies have 'my generation has rested,' which Jerome at one time also translated, deceived by the ambiguity of the word, and afterwards corrected.
38.12:
**“My generation”** — of sons
**“is at an end”**
• from me
• or, the generation of rest is taken away, so that the verse thus begins.
**“and it is rolled away from me, as a shepherd's tent”** — folded up, so that my generation is not extended to posterity.
**“is cut off”** — before time
**“as by a weaver”** — the unfinished web
**“My life is cut off, as by a weaver: whilst I was yet but beginning, he cut me off”**
• in youth
• I was saying
**“from morning even to night thou wilt make an end of me”**
• O Lord
• in the manner of the sick man who hopes that his sickness will be ended or changed by a change of time.
38.13:
**“I hoped till morning”**
• And from night I hoped till morning.
• As Job, who in the day waited for night, and the reverse.
**“As”** — That is.
**“a lion”** — The Almighty.
**“so hath he broken”** — breaking all things to pieces
**“all my bones”** — not only the flesh
**“from morning even to night thou wilt make an end of me”**
• He speaks in suspense, as if: either in the morning or in the evening you will give me an end.
• and he was saying this
38.14:
**“like a young swallow”** — it cries to its mother that it may receive food
**“I will cry”** — to God
**“I will meditate”** — in the Lord
**“like a dove”** — pricked with groaning
**“my eyes are weakened looking upward”** — to the Lord, whence help
**“Lord, I suffer violence”** — the violence of infirmity beyond the strength of the body
**“I suffer violence”** — more than my merits ask
**“answer thou for me”** — or: to pledge is the same
**“Answer”** — That I have erred I will amend; you be surety and protector. For “it is not of him that willeth, nor of him that runneth, but of God that sheweth mercy.”
38.15:
**“What shall I say”**
• to my maker
• it turns back on itself
**“or what shall he answer for me”** — a little pot to clay
**“whereas he himself hath done it”** — or: he made it
**“I will recount”**
• others: I will consider
• What is past does not help one who endures. Hence the saying of Epicurus is foolish, who asserts that by recollecting past good things present evils are softened.
**“all my years”** — even the unhappy ones
**“Whereas he himself hath done it”** — This is justly mine; nothing remains but to bear patiently and to entreat him, the strong one, who did what he willed.
**“in the bitterness”** — Likewise these also in bitterness, because present tribulation feels nothing of past good, and human happiness is always sprinkled with some adversities.
38.16:
**“O Lord, if man's life be such”** — either so or so
**“Life is lived”** — he philosophizes about the state of human life, now secure
**“and in such things is the life”** — fragile and fleeting life, full of miseries, so that it may easily fall
**“of my spirit; thou shalt correct me”** — with your severity and my fault
**“And”** — thus
**“thou shalt make me to live”**
• mercy
• giving health and life
38.17:
**“Behold in peace is my bitterness most bitter”** — for when the Assyrian was struck down, there was peace among the people
**“but thou hast delivered”**
• by correcting
• through scourges
**“my soul that it should not perish”** — now in hell, of the present life or of the future
**“thou hast cast”** — that you may not remember
**“behind thy back”** — either your sense or mine
**“all my sins”** — that I should not look upon them, but your mercy
38.18:
**“For hell”**
• the reprobate, once condemned
• but in hell, who will confess to you
**“shall confess to thee”** — by praising
**“neither shall death”** — the devil
**“shall praise thee; nor shall they that go down look for”** — who are altogether condemned
**“into the pit”** — of hell
**“thy truth”** — the liberation of the Son, who says: I am the way, and the truth, and the life
**“For not”** — The damned, without end, neither do penance in hell nor render praises to God.
38.19:
**“The living, the living, he shall”** — now by your protection
**“shall confess to thee”**
• in future rest
• by praising
**“as I do this day”** — freed from enemies, I give thanks
**“the father”** — a good father, as David
**“to the children”** — to those whom he begot afterwards, because at that time he had no sons
**“make thy truth known”** — the worship of true religion
**“The living, the living, shall give praise”** — Not hell or death; the father to the sons. Ask your father, and they will tell you.
38.20:
**“O Lord, save me”** — from the Assyrian, from death of the soul
**“and we will sing our psalms”** — I and my people praise him even to this day, the Jews; and even if it does not profit them
**“all the days of our life in the house of the Lord”**
• the temple
• in heart
38.21:
**“and he commanded”** — the king’s servants
**“Isaias had ordered that they should take a lump of figs”** — that the power might be more wonderful by the miracle of God; for he was suffering from the royal disease, according to Symmachus, to which all sweet things are harmful, whether touched or tasted, as they say.
**“and lay it as a plaster upon the wound”** — inflicted by the Lord, not the whole body.
**“and that he should be healed”** — Upon the wound. The Hebrews say that the word means an ulcer, not a wound; Aquila and Symmachus interpreted it as the royal disease. Others have supposed it to be not an ulcer but an abscess, which according to the art of physicians is relieved with dried and crushed figs, by which the corruption is drawn to the surface of the skin; and medicine is not to be despised, since God made it.
38.22: **“And Ezechias had said: What shall be the sign that I shall go up to the house of the Lord”** — Hysteron proteron: for these things were said before those that went before concerning health and prayer.

39.1:
**“At that time”** — With the Assyrian slain, Ezechias healed.
**“Merodach Baladan, the son of Baladan king of Babylon, sent letters”** — letters.
**“and presents to Ezechias; for he had heard that he had been sick and was recovered”**
• At that time, etc. It was said above that Assaradon succeeded Sennacherib, who ruled over the Assyrians and Babylonians; but here, that Maradach, who sent messengers to Ezechias, was king of the Babylonians while he was still living. But there were two kingdoms, and the one ruled the Assyrians, the other the Babylonians. They report in the history that Maradach was the father of Nabuchodonosor, who united those kingdoms when subdued. The messengers came because they had seen a portent in the sun and could not understand it by their art; so they came to Jerusalem to learn this from the prophets and wise men.
• The Hebrews relate that Ezechias fell sick for this reason, that after an unheard-of victory he had not sung praises to the Lord, as Moses did when Pharao was drowned, and Debora when Sisara was slain, and Anna when Samuel was born; whence he was reminded of his frailty through sickness. And again, after the health of his body and the greatness of the sign, another occasion of pride is offered, which as a prudent worshipper of God he ought to have avoided, and not to have shown to foreigners the riches which he possessed by God’s giving. We also, according to the tropological sense, ought not to cast pearls before swine nor give what is holy to dogs. For he who is faithful in spirit hides his affairs. But he who does this, his strength is weakened and his posterity perishes, and, manly vigour being lost, he is reduced to womanish softness.
39.2:
**“And Ezechias rejoiced at their coming”** — by the offering of gifts and the congratulation of health.
**“and he shewed them the storehouses of his aromatical spices”** — that is, a remarkable house, namely the epiphanum, in which the bodies of kings were buried.
**“and of the silver, and of the gold, and of the sweet odours”** — treasuries, and on all sides many spices.
**“and of the precious ointment, and all the storehouses”** — storerooms.
**“of his furniture, and all things that were found in his treasures. There was nothing that Ezechias shewed them not”** — any matter, whether in the Hebrew language or Hebrew custom.
**“Ezechias in his house”** — in his treasuries.
**“and in all his dominion”** — In the treasuries of the house of the Lord, in which he chiefly sinned. For this was not within his power. Yet he had already taken plates of gold from the doors of that temple.
39.3:
**“Then Isaias the prophet came to king Ezechias, and said to him: What said these men, and from whence came they to thee?”** — he asks two things.
**“And Ezechias said: From a far country”** — with great labour.
**“they came to me”** — with the weight of pride.
**“from Babylon”**
• which is most powerful.
• he does not say, to praise God for the sign.
• he answers one and is silent on the other.
39.4:
**“And he said: What saw they in thy house? And Ezechias said: All things”** — precious things.
**“that are in my house have they seen, there was not any thing”** — was not a wonderful thing.
