**“In my treasures”** — He is silent about the treasures of the Lord, fearing to be reproved, namely that he showed them whatever he had in the power of the temple, that is, the furniture. Whence Isaias adds: hear the word of the Lord, etc.
39.5: **“And Isaias said to Ezechias: Hear the word of the Lord of hosts”** — you who revealed secrets to foreigners.
39.6:
**“Behold the days shall come”** — he foretells the punishment of the crime.
**“that all that is in thy house, and that thy fathers have laid up in store until this day, shall be carried away into Babylon: there shall not any thing be left, saith the Lord”** — whose sentence is firm.
39.7:
**“And of thy children, that shall issue from thee”** — from your seed.
**“And they shall be eunuchs”** — The Hebrews relate that this was fulfilled in Daniel and his companions, who, when Joachim the son of Josias was taken, were taken with his people and led into Babylon and made eunuchs or unmanned; for it is not to be thought that they were eunuchs in body but in mind, like those who have made themselves eunuchs for the kingdom of heaven.
39.8:
**“And Ezechias said”** — just.
**“to Isaias: The word of the Lord, which he hath spoken, is good”** — to Isaias, good, just.
**“The word of the Lord”** — is.
**“which he hath spoken. And he said: Only let peace”** — by the Assyrians.
**“and truth”** — of religion.
**“Only let peace”** — He ought to have confessed his sin with David and removed the wrath of God from his descendants, or to have shown compassion with Moses, who says: “Forgive them this trespass, or if thou do not, strike me out of the book that thou hast written.” Because he did not do this, therefore he does not answer him, but turning to the people says: Be comforted, etc.

40.1:
**“Be comforted, be comforted, my people”** — faithful
**“Be comforted”** — As if because your king does not suffer with you: be comforted in Christ. It can also be referred to the Gentiles, of whom the Lord says through Zacharias: “I will gather the people of the east, and they shall be my people, and I will be their God.”
40.2:
**“Speak ye to the heart of Jerusalem”**
• gently comforting
• the Jews and the Gentiles
• Jerusalem, etc. Jerusalem, by the Chaldeans and Romans, in body and soul; the Church, by persecutors, tormented in body, distressed in spirit.
**“Speak ye to the heart”** — He speaks to the heart who comforts one who is sad, as it is said of Sichem: he spoke to her heart and comforted her.
**“and call to her”** — from sadness and from idolatry
**“for her evil is come to an end”** — affliction, and rest restored
**“her evil”** — Malice: affliction, as in: “Shall there be evil in the city, which the Lord hath not done?”
**“her iniquity is forgiven”**
• by the Lord, in baptism or in martyrdom
• because
• Her iniquity is forgiven, etc. The cause of consolation is the remission of sins; the cause of remission is that she has received double. It is to be noted that our sins are not loosed unless we have received them from the hand of the Lord. Nor is it the same for sins to be loosed and to be forgiven; for he to whom they are forgiven does not need payment, whence: “Thy sins are forgiven thee.” But those which are loosed for someone are loosed for this reason, that they have been purged and paid for through punishments.
**“she hath received of the hand of the Lord double for all her sins”** — he who knows the will of his lord and does not do it shall be beaten with many stripes
40.3:
**“The voice”**
• apostles
• John
• of Christ
**“of one crying in the desert”** — of the Jews or of the Gentiles
**“Prepare ye the way of the Lord”** — good works by which the Lord enters into you
**“make straight in the wilderness the paths”** — thoughts
**“of our God.”** — of Christ
**“The voice of one crying”** — Mindful of this voice, the Jews sent to John to ask him: “Who art thou?”
40.4:
**“Every valley”** — a Jew or a Gentile, humble, simple
**“shall be exalted”** — by faith and work
**“Every valley shall be exalted”** — He who exalts himself shall be humbled, and he who humbles himself shall be exalted. Until today the teachers cry this out in the desert of the Gentile churches.
**“and every mountain”** — proud
**“and hill”** — haughty
**“shall be made low, and the crooked shall become”** — perverse, twisted hearts
**“straight”** — to faith and working
**“and the rough ways”** — fierceness
**“plain”** — soft and gentle
40.5:
**“And the glory of the Lord shall be revealed”** — in preaching; in baptism, when the heavens were opened and the Spirit remained upon him
**“the glory of the Lord”** — The Son, of whom the Father says: Arise, my glory.
**“and all flesh together shall see”**
• at the judgment or at the first coming.
• man, not spirit, first, because he did not yet have the spirit.
**“together, that the mouth of the Lord”** — prophets.
**“And all flesh together shall see”** — He speaks of the first coming, passing suddenly to the second: and all flesh shall see.
**“the mouth of the Lord”** — The prophets who preached the future Christ, that is, the salvation of our God.
40.6:
**“The voice”**
• Christ.
• to me.
**“of one, saying: Cry.”** — O Isaias.
**“And I said:”** — to the Jews or to all.
**“What shall I cry? All flesh”** — man.
**“grass”** — frail.
**“and all the glory”** — youth.
**“thereof as the flower of the field”**
• power, and all the rest: “Vanity of vanities, and all is vanity.”
• Grass, when it springs up, has greenness, and in growing has beauty, then a flower; at last, dried by the heat of the sun, it is reduced to dust. So man, through the successions of ages, loses his beauty and falls into death.
**“What shall I cry?”** — He does not ask without cause; for when he had offered himself willingly, saying “Here I am, send me,” he announced hard things to his people, and now he himself is afraid.
**“All flesh is grass”** — He who bears the image of the earthly man and serves vices is grass and a passing flower; he who keeps the image of the heavenly is flesh, but flesh that sees the salvation of God, that is renewed daily according to the image of its creator, and at last, incorruptible and immortal, changes its glory, not its nature.
40.7: **“The grass is withered, and the flower is fallen, because the spirit of the Lord hath blown upon it.”** — the sentence shook off the present life.
40.8:
**“The grass is withered, and the flower is fallen”** — youth, which serves vices, especially lust.
**“but the word of our Lord endureth”**
• shall reign.
• others: the word of God remains for ever.
**“but the word of our Lord”** — The Word is Christ with his body, which is the Church.
40.9:
**“Get thee up upon a high mountain”** — Christ, that you announce nothing except what you have from him.
**“Get thee up, thou that bringest good tidings”**
• you who bring good tidings.
• note that Sion, which is a mountain, is bidden to ascend the mountain, that is, Christ.
• O.
**“Upon a high mountain”** — Gregory. He who uses heavenly preaching, already forsaking the lowest level of earthly works, is seen to stand on the height of things, and draws his subjects to better things the more easily, the more through the merit of his life he cries out from on high. For that voice pierces the heart of the hearers more willingly which the life of the speaker commends, because what he commands by speaking he helps by showing, that it may be done; whence in the law the right shoulder, set apart, is commanded to be given to the priests.
**“to Sion: lift up thy voice with strength”** — that many may hear.
**“thy voice”** — preaching.
**“Sion”** — By Sion and Jerusalem he means the apostles and other teachers, whom he admonishes to preach what they have received from the Lord, and, climbing the heights of virtue, to teach by word and example.
**“thou that bringest good tidings”** — O.
**“Jerusalem: lift it up, fear not.”** — the cruelty of persecutors, the cunning of the devil.
**“Say to the cities”**
• To the churches or the synagogues.
• Whence: I was not sent but to the sheep that are lost of the house of Israel.
**“of Juda: Behold your God”** — The apostles, concerning the second coming.
**“your God”** — Promised to you, O Jews, or to the Gentiles: receive him.
40.10:
**“Behold the Lord God”** — Whom you despised as vile and weak.
**“shall come with strength, and his arm”** — Strength.
**“his”** — Who took the form of a servant.
**“shall rule: Behold his reward”** — The recompense of all.
**“with him and his work”** — The power of judgment.
40.11:
**“like a shepherd”**
• Who is to come in majesty.
• I am the good shepherd.
• The prophet, concerning the first coming.
**“his flock ... with his arm”** — In strength.
**“He shall feed his flock”** — Now in contemplation; in the future in the vision itself; now by teaching, afterwards by saving or satisfying.
**“he shall gather together”** — From all nations.
**“the lambs”** — Feed my lambs: meek, not proud.
**“in his bosom”** — By protection.
**“shall take them up”** — To heaven.
**“that are with young”** — Teachers, daily bringing forth sons to God; whence the apostle: “My little children, of whom I am in labour again.”
40.12:
**“Who hath measured the waters in the hollow of his hand”** — Easily.
**“the waters ... weighed the heavens with his palm?”** — The waters and the heavens with the palm? For he knows the measures and weights of all things.
**“Who hath measured”** — Lest the calling of the Gentiles be doubted, the greatness of the one calling is described.
**“in the hollow of his hand”** — A handful, with the fingers drawn in, is a fist; a palm is the hand stretched out from the thumb to the little finger; so that by the palm and the handful we may know the heavens stretched out and the globe of the earth.
**“who hath poised”** — Over nothing.
**“with three fingers”**
• Metaphorically.
• The power of the Trinity.
**“the bulk of the earth, and weighed the mountains in scales”** — He made them balanced by their own weight.
40.13:
**“Who”** — No one.
**“hath forwarded the spirit of the Lord”**
• In creating.
• By the word of the Lord the heavens were established; and all the power of them by the spirit of his mouth.
**“or who hath been his counsellor, and hath taught him?”** — what he should do
**“The spirit of the Lord”** — “The spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach to the meek; he hath sent me;” and: “the spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him.”
40.14:
**“With whom”** — how he ought to act
**“hath consulted, and who hath instructed him, and taught him the path of justice”** — the rule of acting
**“and taught him knowledge, and shewed him the way of understanding?”**
• no one
• because
40.15:
**“Behold the Gentiles”** — those worshipping idols, or all nations
**“are as a drop of a bucket”**
• which, falling, is said to be as nothing
• in comparison with him
**“and are counted as the smallest grain”** — which is turned to either side as if from nothing
**“of a balance: behold the islands are as a little dust”** — in comparison with him
**“as a little dust”** — The Hebrews think that by this word the finest dust is signified, which is felt rather than seen. This, then, perhaps Democritus with his Epicurus calls atoms. But there are many names which are read thus in Greek and in Hebrew because of the difficulty of interpreting and the poverty of both the Greek and the Latin tongue.
40.16:
**“And Libanus”** — He adds this to move the nations away from idolatry by removing the sacrifices, because neither the wood nor the animals suffice.
**“shall not be enough to burn”** — the fire of the victims
**“Libanus shall not”** — Lebanon is most rich in pastures and trees; but even if all the wood is cut down to kindle it, and all the animals are slain for a burnt offering, they do not suffice to fulfil or appease the power of the majesty.
40.17:
**“All nations”** — which are under heaven
**“as if they had no being at all, and are counted to him as nothing”** — in comparison with him
40.18:
**“To whom”** — to the image
**“then have you likened God”** — the one who made all things
**“or what image will you make for him?”** — who is Spirit, is in all things and everywhere
**“To whom then have you likened God”** — Tropologically. The leaders of the heretics are rebuked, who fashion various idols from their own heart, either with the charm of speech, that is, silver, or with the splendour of understanding, which is signified in gold, or with incorruptible wood; which are the viler teachings that are strengthened by the art of dialectic lest they fall.
40.19:
**“Hath the workman cast a graven statue?”** — the Lord to all nations
**“or hath the goldsmith formed it with gold”** — like God, who is everywhere
**“or the silversmith with plates of silver?”** — no
**“Art thou glorified?”** — He refutes the folly of the nations, so that they may turn away from idolatry.
40.20:
**“He hath chosen strong wood, and that will not rot”** — durable, so that the image made from it may last a long time
**“He hath chosen the skillful workman”** — skilled in this craft
**“strong wood”** — In Hebrew it is succam, a kind of wood that does not rot, from which idols are chiefly made. He says this beforehand so that, the idols being rejected, the teaching of the gospel may be received, the glory of the Lord revealed, and every flesh may see the salvation of God.
40.21:
**“Do you not know?”**
• O nations
• by natural reason, that idols are nothing and that God is eternal
**“Do you not know”** — From the beginning of the law of Moses, or from the beginning of the world, in the creatures themselves, each of which in its own way proclaims its maker.
**“hath it not been heard? hath it not been told you from the beginning?”** — at least according to the written law, which forbids this
**“have you not understood the foundations of the earth?”** — founded by the Lord
40.22:
**“It is he that sitteth upon the globe of the earth”** — he rules and encompasses all things
**“Upon the globe”** — Hence some contend that the earth is like a point and a globe.
**“and the inhabitants thereof”** — of the earth
**“are as locusts”** — why then are they proud
**“As locusts”** — In comparison with him, or considering the greatness of the earth.
**“That”** — also
**“stretcheth out the heavens as nothing”** — thin, subtle
**“and spreadeth them out as a tent to dwell in”** — under them, as under a tent, men dwell; above them, angels and saints
**“A tent”** — Hence also some contend that heaven is in the likeness of a sphere, and that its hemisphere hangs over the lands.
40.23:
**“that”** — also
**“bringeth the searchers of secrets”** — philosophers
**“That bringeth the searchers of secrets to nothing”** — God made the wisdom of this world foolish, and this is he who brings the searchers of secrets to nothing, as though they were not.
**“as if there were not judges of the earth”**
• rulers
• all the dead, given over to oblivion
**“hath made as vanity”** — because they pass quickly
40.24:
**“And surely neither planted”** — that is, firmly established
**“neither sown nor rooted in the earth”** — in the present life
**“Stock”** — state
**“he hath blown upon them”** — the Spirit of God
**“upon them and they are withered”**
• dead
• And I passed by, and lo, he was not
**“and a whirlwind”** — sudden sentence of God
**“shall take them away as stubble”** — from this life
40.25:
**“And to whom”**
• of your gods
• since such is his power
**“have ye likened me”** — O Jews or Gentiles worshipping idols
**“or made me equal, saith”** — singly
**“To whom have ye likened”** — As if to say: why do you compare me to the likeness of God, and from the greatness of creatures do not understand God the Creator? If you do not believe the words, believe your eyes, and consider the power of the Lord from the servitude of all the elements.
40.26:
**“Lift up on high”** — heaven
**“your eyes”** — understand at least through the creatures
**“and see who hath created these things”** — which are in heaven
**“who bringeth out”** — that is, he who brings out
**“their host by number”**
• of heaven
• angels and stars
• who numbers the multitude of the stars
**“By number”** — To him are numbered the things which Abraham could not number, and they serve the office assigned them, so that the sun completes the course of the sky in one year, and the rest in their own way.
**“Their host”** — Namely the angels, whence: “thousand thousands ministered to him.” Hence also the Lord is called Sabaoth, that is, of hosts, or of armies, or of powers.
**“and calleth them all”** — the stars
**“by their names”** — as because he is almighty
**“by the greatness of his might, and strength, and power, not one of them”** — of all these
**“was missing”** — alien to his number and to his knowledge
40.27:
**“Why”**
• therefore
• since God’s greatness is so great, when all things are ruled by his nod
**“sayest”** — or you will say
**“O Jacob”** — two tribes
**“and speakest, O Israel”** — the ten tribes already led into captivity
**“Why sayest thou, O Jacob”** — When the prophet said this, the ten tribes were already captive; the two remained to be taken captive. Now in captivity all, despairing, said: God does not consider earthly things, nor care what each one does. Therefore we are without king, without judge, and are afflicted undeservedly.
**“My way is hid”** — does not see it
**“from the Lord, and my judgment from my God”** — because he has prejudged me
**“is passed over”** — or: will pass over
**“My way”** — Good works do not concern him; he does not consider earthly things, what each one does. Hence we are unjustly oppressed, like beasts and fish without a ruler.
40.28:
**“Knowest thou not”** — through yourself
**“or hast thou not heard”**
• in the Scriptures
• namely this
**“the Lord is the everlasting God”** — is one
**“who hath created”** — from nothing
**“Created”** — He knows all things, contains all things, and orders all things by his majesty.
**“the ends of the earth”** — because he is not flesh
**“he shall not labour”** — because he is the almighty Spirit
**“nor is there any searching out”** — because he knows all things
**“of his wisdom”** — It seems that the saying of the Apostle is taken from this place: “How incomprehensible are his judgments, and how unsearchable his ways!” As if God alone is eternal, impassible and immutable; all other things fall short.
40.29:
**“It is he that giveth”** — to the wavering in faith
**“strength”** — of faith and of work
**“to them that are not, strength and might”** — strong in the world
40.30:
**“Youths shall faint”**
• wholly condemned
• from childhood
• who live childishly
• Youths shall faint, etc. That is, those who rejoice in bodily health and think that childhood and youth are everlasting.
**“and labour”** — in sickness
**“and young men”** — who are strong and healthy
**“in”** — in this life
**“fall by infirmity”**
• burning with vices
• of soul and body
40.31:
**“But they that hope in the Lord”** — not in themselves
**“shall renew”** — So that, as those who are strong in God become weak to the world, so after the death of the flesh they will become immortal.
**“shall take wings”** — by which they will fly to God
**“as eagles”** — renewed
**“As eagles”** — As the eagle, according to the natural philosophers, when its beak, hooked by excessive age, is struck against a rock, is renewed; so those who mortify the old age of sin through the rock, which is Christ, die to the world and are renewed to God. Whence: “Thy youth shall be renewed like the eagle’s.”
**“they shall run”** — to God
**“and not be weary”** — all things are easy for the one who loves
**“they shall walk”** — they will make progress
**“and not faint”** — because they will live for ever

41.1:
**“Let keep silence”** — hear, Israel, and be silent
**“to me”** — to hear through the apostles
**“Let the islands”** — That the nations are placed in the sea, that is, those that are beaten by the salt and bitter waves of the world.
**“and the nations take new strength”** — let those who were strong in the world be strong in God; the strength of the world: to fulfil the will of God, to mortify
**“let them come near”** — to me in faith
**“and then speak”** — let them preach to others
**“let us come near to judgment together”** — that they may discern between God and idols, and whether God arranges all things justly
41.2:
**“Who”** — Except I.
**“hath raised up the just one from the east”**
• or justice
• in Judea, which is in the eastern region, he willed that Christ be made flesh, die, and be raised up.
**“hath called him”** — by inspiring, and speaking from the sepulchre, “Arise, my glory,” and he, secure, answered, “I will arise early.”
**“to follow him”** — obedient even unto death.
**“he shall give the nations in his sight”** — “Ask of me, and I will give you the Gentiles for your inheritance and your possession.”
**“and he shall rule over kings”** — converted.
**“he shall rule”** — with the bonds of faith.
**“he shall give”** — The Father.
**“as the dust”** — the opposing powers.
**“to his sword”** — of the word.
**“as stubble driven by the wind, to his bow”**
• of preaching.
• of the Son.
• Who hath raised up from the east, etc. Some of the Hebrews refer this to Cyrus, king of the Persians, that he was raised up from the east against the Babylonians, because the Lord made many nations obey him, subjecting them to his sword and his bow. So also they refer the rest to him, namely that to the Babylonians the idols made by human skill did not profit. Others of the Hebrews refer this to Abraham, who was called just from the east, that is, from the Chaldeans, because he alone was found just, and followed God, going out from his land; and he gave him the kings who had come against Sodom and Gomorrha, and made them before his sword and his bow as dust and stubble; and he pursued them and returned in peace, and did not feel the course of the long journey; and this he did not by his own strength but by the mercy of the Lord, who knew these things from the beginning. The islands saw, that is, the nations round about, and were terrified by his power; and the ends of the earth, that is, Sem the son of Noe, who at the last time of the earth escaped the flood with his father and brothers, and was kept until the time of that man, whom they would have to be understood as Melchisedech, and to have come to meet Abraham returning from the battle, and to have blessed him and strengthened him with the blessings of God. They say also that he is a brazier, a smith, who forged Abraham, and with the hammer of his art brought him forth to better things, and said: It is good that thou be joined fast to the fear of the Lord and united to him; and he strengthened him with the nails of the precepts, that he might remain in the fear of the Lord.
41.3:
**“He shall pursue”** — The Son.
**“them”** — adversaries.
**“he shall pass”** — from the world to the Father.
**“in peace”** — “Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you.”
**“after his feet”** — He will feel no toil or weariness of this life. “Hath rejoiced as a giant to run the way.”
41.4:
**“Who hath wrought and done these things”** — the things foretold.
**“hath wrought and done”** — through.
**“calling”** — to himself.
**“the generations”** — all.
**“from the beginning”** — of the world.
**“I the Lord”** — I the Lord have made them, because I am first, etc.
**“I am the first”** — without beginning.
**“and the last”** — without end.
41.5:
**“saw it”** — God through faith.
**“The islands”** — the Gentiles, or the Church.
**“and feared”** — “The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord.”
**“the ends of the earth”** — “Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth, and unto the ends of the world.”
**“were astonished”** — when the preaching of the apostles was heard
**“drew near, and came”** — by faith, to God
41.6:
**“Every one”** — of the faithful
**“his neighbour”** — in faith
**“shall help”** — by word and deed
**“and to his brother”** — to the weak
**“shall say to his brother: Be of good courage”** — in the Lord God, living and true, because idols are not gods but the works of men; and this is to strengthen
41.7:
**“The coppersmith striking with the hammer encouraged”** — zealously making his own god
**“striking with the hammer encouraged him that forged”** — the form of the image
**“at that time”** — at that time, when idols were worshipped
**“saying: It is ready for soldering”** — this glue
**“and he strengthened it”** — God
**“with nails, that it should not be moved”** — with nails, that it may not be moved by any push
41.8:
**“thou too”** — truly
**“art my servant”** — formerly by a spirit of fear
**“O Jacob”** — a wrestler against demons
**“whom I have chosen”** — “You have not chosen me: but I have chosen you”
**“the seed of Abraham”** — by flesh and by faith
**“my friend”**
• by the spirit of charity
• And thou Israel. It was said to carnal Israel: “Why sayest thou, O Jacob, and speakest: My way is hid from the Lord,” etc. Now he speaks to the spiritual Israel, who received the coming of the Lord. This one he calls first servant, then elect, and finally the seed of Abraham. For first we received the spirit of bondage in fear; afterwards, as the elect, we are joined to the friendship of God.
**“But thou Israel, art my servant”** — The Lord to the apostles, with affection. The Jews, however, refer this to themselves. Note that the prophecy does not keep the order of history. For after the calling of the Gentiles, the calling of the apostles is foretold.
41.9:
**“In whom”** — in whose faith
**“I have taken thee”** — and those like you
**“from the ends of the earth”** — where you were scattered
**“and from the remote parts”** — regions
**“thereof have called thee, and said to thee”** — spiritually, one who was also to preach to others
**“Thou art my servant, I have chosen thee, and have not cast thee away”** — from the face of persecutors
**“And from the remote parts”** — Already the Jews had been scattered to the ends of the earth, and from there many were called to the faith, whence “to you it behoved us first to speak the word of God,” etc.
41.10:
**“Fear not, for I am with thee”** — behold, I am with you even to the consummation
**“turn not aside”** — from me
**“for I am thy God”** — way, truth, and life
**“I have strengthened thee”** — that you be not overcome
**“and have helped thee”** — that you may overcome
**“and the right hand of my just one hath upheld thee”** — by the power of my Son
41.11:
**“Behold”** — therefore
**“shall be confounded”**
• within
• your adversaries, the people of the Jews
**“and ashamed”** — without
**“all that fight against thee”** — Jews and Gentiles
**“they shall be as nothing”**
• they will soon fail
• because
**“and the men shall perish”** — even the strong
41.12: **“Thou shalt seek them”** — “I have seen the wicked highly exalted, and lifted up like the cedars of Libanus. And he passed away, and lo, he was not, and his place was not found.”
41.13:
**“For I am the Lord thy God”**
• as if you ought not to fear
• protector
**“who take thee by the hand”** — the working
**“and say to thee: Fear not”** — do not fear
**“I have helped thee”** — or I will help
41.14:
**“Fear not, thou worm of Jacob”**
• although lowly
• “I am a worm and no man, the reproach of men and the outcast of the people.”
**“thou worm of Jacob”** — The apostles are called worms, as those who imitate him who says, “I am a worm,” etc.; and as a worm penetrates the earth, so their preaching penetrates the hearts of those who hear.
**“you that are dead”** — to the world
**“of Israel”** — no other
**“I have helped thee, saith the Lord: and thy Redeemer”** — by the blood of the Son
**“thy”** — who is
**“you that are dead of Israel”** — Like him who says, “I die daily, by your glory, brethren,” and elsewhere, “And I live, now not I; but Christ liveth in me.”
41.15:
**“I have made thee as a new thrashing wain”** — that you may crush the opposing powers
**“with teeth like a saw: thou shall thrash the mountains”** — kings
**“and break them in pieces”** — leaders and companions
**“I have made thee”** — The churchman has the saw-toothed points of preaching on a new wain, which works not in the oldness of the letter but in the newness of the Spirit; he thrashes the hardest hearts of unbelievers, separating the wheat from the chaff, and breaking in pieces the mountains and hills, that is, the princes of the heretics, who, broken in pieces, are reduced to dust and are said to be nothing, so that those who were badly gathered together may be well divided.
41.16:
**“Thou shalt fan them”** — separating the wheat from the chaff
**“and the wind”** — their pride
**“shall carry them away, and the whirlwind shall scatter them: and thou shalt rejoice in the Lord, in the Holy One of Israel thou shalt be joyful”** — By the faith of the good, the power of miracles; by the scattering of the wicked.
41.17:
**“The needy and the poor seek for waters”**
• the Gentiles not having a teacher of truth
• from the philosophers
• doctrine
**“and there are none”**
• among the philosophers
• therefore
**“their tongue hath been dry with thirst”** — without law and prophets
**“I the Lord will hear them”**
• no other can
• and
**“I the God of Israel will not forsake them”** — altogether
41.18:
**“I will open rivers in the high hills”**
• to the proud Gentiles
• otherwise, high
**“rivers”**
• rivers: preachers; from Christ the river; “The river of God is filled with water.”
• “The stream of the river maketh the city of God joyful.”
**“and fountains in the midst of the plains”** — of the humble
**“fountains”** — Bless ye God, the Lord, from the fountains of Israel.
**“I will turn the desert”**
• the Gentiles
• Let him who thirsts come and drink.
**“into pools of waters”** — the abundance of heavenly wisdom
**“and”** — the same
**“the impassable land into streams of waters”**
• to teachers
• whoever drinks of this will not thirst forever
41.19:
**“I will plant in the wilderness”**
• of the Gentiles
• in watered land trees arise
• of the Gentiles
• the most high, whose conversation is in heaven
**“the cedar”** — saints who will live forever, in whom is the fragrance of good report
**“and the thorn”** — the rebuke of preachers
**“and the myrtle, and the olive tree”** — the merciful
**“the fir tree, the elm”** — the rich of the world, who, if they are fruitful in themselves, bear preachers, as the elm bears the vine
**“and the box tree together”**
• humble, flourishing in faith
• I will give in the wilderness, etc. The variety of trees signifies the diversity of spiritual grace, lest even one string of the Lord’s harp, or any power of the graces, should seem to be wanting to the Church; whose loftiness, hastening to heavenly things, the wood of the olive illuminates, the fuel of light, the rest of one who labours or is weary.
• The myrtle, an aromatic kind that does not rot, strengthens and restores weary limbs, and therefore signifies the comforters of holy Church; whence the Apostle: “Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who comforteth us in all our tribulation.”
**“The thorn”** — In the Septuagint: sethim, which is the tree of the white thorn, of wonderful softness and strength and beauty, and incorruptible, of which the ark was made. From this too the land was called Sethim. The thorn was given to the first man as a punishment; whence: “When thou shalt have worked the earth, it shall not yield fruit, but shall bring forth thorns and thistles to thee.” But for the Gentiles, for glory, the thorns are the preachers, who do not caress the vices of their subjects but prick them.
41.20:
**“That they may see”** — the lesser, examples of the greater
**“and know, and consider”** — in memory
**“and understand together”** — that is, understanding, let them imitate
**“that the hand of the Lord hath done”** — “God is wonderful in his saints.”
**“this, and the Holy One of Israel hath created”** — “He made us, and not we ourselves.”
**“it”** — that wonderful thing
41.21:
**“Bring your cause near”**
• as if we were going on the roads, that you may answer why you did not understand that the hand of the Lord made these things
• O nations, who scorn to believe the others who believe, as it is written, that Israel is believing and not believing
**“saith the Lord: bring hither”**
• why are you unwilling to believe?
• counsels of reason: why do you not receive the truth?
**“if you have any thing”** — “They have a mouth, but they speak not.”
41.22:
**“let them come near”**
• the idols in which you trust
• let the idols judge whether they ought to be worshipped, or he
**“and tell us all things that are to come”** — the coming of the Son; the faith of the nations; their own destruction
**“tell us the former things what they were”**
• if you can
• how the world was made out of nothing
• It is clear that the idols lost their voice after the coming of Christ.
**“Tell us”** — Declare. It signifies that idols have neither the power of hearing nor of answering: declare things to come, that by the outcome of events you may show your power. It is to be noted that after the coming of Christ the idols that promised knowledge of the future fell silent; concerning Christ also and the apostles and their own abolition they could foretell nothing; much less then could they declare the good or evil of others. And if they ever foretold anything, they always joined falsehood to truth, and so tempered the saying that whatever happened would suit the oracle, as this: I say that you, descendant of Aeacus, can conquer the Romans.
**“and we will set our heart upon them”**
• that we may worship you
• “They have a mouth, but they speak not.”
**“and shall know”** — that you are gods
**“the latter end of them”** — the faith of each
41.23:
**“Shew the things that are to come hereafter, and”** — thus
**“we shall know that ye are gods. Do ye also good or evil, if you can”** — by another sign he shows that idols are not gods
**“and let us speak”** — foretell things to be done or things to come, as I do
**“and see together”** — who ought to be worshipped
**“If you can”** — Neither can the demons, who sit by idols, do anything except by the permission of God; they could not destroy the swine, nor the cattle of holy Job, without God’s permission. Paul also delivered certain men to Satan.
41.24:
**“Behold, you are of nothing”** — Behold, you are of nothing; an idol is nothing
**“and your work of that which hath no being”**
• and your work of that which is not, an abomination; abominable
• because you are thought to be gods, which is nothing
**“he that hath chosen you is”** — made and worshipped
41.25:
**“I have raised up”**
• as I indeed
• He still speaks against idols and against their worshippers. After the coming of Christ, while some remain in error, the people of the nations is raised up.
**“from the north”** — from whom evils blaze up
**“and he shall come”** — Christ
**“from the rising of the sun”**
• Christ’s
• because Judea is in the east
• The Hebrews interpret being raised up from the north and coming from the rising of the sun as the Assyrian and the Persian, who came to Jerusalem and trampled its princes; and none of the idols which they worshipped knew that this was to come, except God alone, who avenged them for their sins.
• I have raised up from the north. The nations, which are cold and sluggish without the warmth of love, that they may believe in him who comes from the rising of the sun. Whence above: “Who hath raised up the just one from the east?”
**“he shall call”** — that, leaving idols, they may worship one God; whence I came in the name of my Father
**“upon my name, and he shall make princes”** — of the world
**“as dirt”** — you will break them like a potter’s vessel
**“and as the potter”** — a potter
**“treading clay”** — that he may make one vessel unto honour, and another unto dishonour
41.26:
**“Who hath declared from the beginning, that we may know”** — which are still future, I say I have done, as though past
**“and from time of old, that we may say”** — because
**“Thou art just. There is none”** — of your gods
**“that sheweth, nor that foretelleth”**
• past things
• because they are dumb
• future things
**“nor that heareth”** — because they are deaf
**“your words”**
• Who hath declared, etc. As if there was no God among the nations who declared the coming of the Son; if, however, there is one who declared it, we will say that he is just.
• At the coming of the Son the demons, who used to announce future things through idols, fell silent.
**“That heareth”** — Because the dull hearts of the Gentiles understood their error and abandoned false prophecies.
41.27:
**“The first”** — my firstborn
**“to Sion”** — preachers
**“shall say: Behold they are here”** — help to you
**“The first shall say to Sion”** — The Church: behold, your sons are here, namely those whom I gave you through my faith, namely the apostles, by whose preaching sons were born to you.
**“and Jerusalem”** — of the Church
**“I will give an evangelist”** — announcing good things
41.28:
**“And I saw”** — I, the almighty, saw.
**“and there was no one even among them”** — Idols.
**“to consult”** — Of foretelling or answering.
**“and when I asked”** — By the worshippers.
41.29:
**“Behold they are all in the wrong”** — The worshippers of idols.
**“and their works are vain”** — The worship, or the idol itself.
**“wind and vanity”** — Useless.
**“Behold, they are all in the wrong”** — Whatever we have said about idols or the Gentiles, let us refer to the heresiarchs and the doctrines of perversity, because, while Christ announces the peace of the Church and shows the truth, they follow error and are compared to wind and whirlwind.

42.1:
**“Behold my servant”**
• The Son according to the humanity.
• It is to be noted that the apostles are called Jacob, Israel, and the seed of Abraham, to whom afterwards, as to servants and men, it is said: “Fear not, thou worm of Jacob,” etc. But Christ is called not Jacob or Israel but servant. Whence: my servant, etc.; for he humbled himself, taking the form of a servant.
**“I will uphold him”** — On the day of the ascension.
**“my elect”**
• Chosen from thousands for the redemption of the world.
• This is my Son.
**“my soul delighteth in him”** — In whom are all virtues, who is the power and wisdom of God.
**“I have given my spirit upon him, he shall bring forth judgment”** — Which before they did not know.
**“to the Gentiles”** — Those who believed, the Jews having been blinded.
**“he shall bring forth”**
• Through the apostles.
• Through each one.
**“I have given my spirit”** — In the conception, whence “The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the most High shall overshadow thee.” Which was made clear at baptism, when the Spirit rested upon him in the form of a dove.
42.2:
**“He shall not cry”**
• He was led as a sheep to the slaughter.
• Meek and gentle.
**“nor have respect to person”** — In judgment.
**“neither shall be heard abroad”** — From Judea.
**“his voice”** — “I was not sent but to the sheep that are lost of the house of Israel”; yet he was on the borders of Tyre and Sidon and Caesarea Philippi, but he did not enter them.
42.3:
**“The bruised reed he shall not break”** — Because merciful to sinners.
**“and smoking flax”** — And the flax, near to extinction.
**“he shall not quench, in truth”** — In truth, according to the works of each.
**“he shall bring forth”**
• The Son.
• He will bring forth judgment, namely not fearing the scribes and Pharisees.
**“judgment”**
• The last judgment.
• The reed, etc. The scribes and Pharisees, bright outwardly, empty within: they did not worship idols, whence they shone, but they had not faith within, whence they were empty. These he did not break but called to penance. So he says reed in reference to them, and also the kingdom of the Jews, shattered, because a foreigner was already reigning.
**“smoking flax”** — The priesthood, now almost extinguished; but from flax is made the priestly vestment.
42.4:
**“He shall not be sad”** — For he was always cheerful and always joyful.
**“He shall not”** — Matthew did not put this, or between judgment and judgment the middle part was removed by the scribe’s error. The sense, however, is: he will preserve an evenness of countenance at all times; of which the philosophers falsely boast of Socrates, that he was neither sadder nor merrier than usual.
**“nor troublesome, till he set”** — earthly
**“judgment”** — last
**“Judgment”** — Whence: “For judgment I am come into this world; that they who see not, may see; and they who see, may become blind.” etc.
**“and the islands shall wait for his law”** — the gospel
**“the islands shall wait”** — nations smitten on every side with tribulations
42.5:
**“Thus”**
• the above
• do not doubt about the author
**“Thus saith the Lord God that created”** — creator, that is, of all things
**“the heavens”**
• material
• the dwelling place of angels
**“and stretched them out, that established”** — over the void
**“the earth”** — so that the Creator may be understood from creatures
**“and the things that spring out of it”** — daily
**“breath”** — the soul, according to that: and he breathed into his face the breath of life
**“to the people upon it, and spirit”** — Holy
**“to them that tread”** — by the power of reason
**“it”** — earthliness
42.6:
**“I the Lord”** — of all
**“have called thee”**
• O Son
• from Judea to the nations
**“in justice”** — whence: Just Father, the world hath not known thee
**“In justice”** — In justice: It was just that he should pass through the apostles to the nations, despised by the Jews.
**“and taken thee by the hand”** — Father, abiding in me, he himself does the works
**“and preserved thee”**
• from death
• who preserves all things
**“And I have given thee for a covenant of the people”** — to be fulfilled, as I had covenanted with my people Israel
**“for a light of the Gentiles”** — those who were in darkness
42.7:
**“That thou mightest open the eyes”** — of the heart
**“of the blind”** — of the unbelievers
**“and bring forth”** — demons
**“the prisoner”** — with the cords of sins
**“out of prison”** — of sin
**“them that sit in darkness”** — of ignorance
**“The prisoner”** — With the cords of sins: the Lord loosed him whom Satan had bound, in the gospel.
42.8:
**“I the Lord”** — not another
**“this is my name”** — the Lord
**“my glory”** — have glorified and will glorify again
**“to another”** — to idols
**“To another”** — The Son and the Holy Spirit in the Godhead are not another than the Father, and therefore have the same glory and praise.
**“I will not give”** — except you, to whom I have given, to whom I am about to give
42.9:
**“The things that were first”** — foretold by the prophets
**“behold they are come”** — fulfilled in the Son
**“and new things”** — the gospel: the rejection of the Jews, the overthrow of Jerusalem, the conversion of the Gentiles
**“I declare”** — they are done in fact
**“I will make you hear them”** — That you may know that I am the Lord, and there is no other; and that you who see the former things fulfilled may believe what I promise will be in the future.
42.10:
**“Sing ye to the Lord”** — O apostles, preach the gospel
**“a new song”** — these new things
**“new”** — In the newness of the Spirit, not in the oldness of the letter; not only in the Old Testament but also in the New.
**“his praise”** — their sound has gone out into all the earth, etc.; his going out is from the highest heaven
**“from the ends of the earth”** — by miracles, from the rising of the sun and from its setting, the praiseworthy name of the Lord
**“you that go down to the sea”** — the storms of the world
**“You that go down to the sea”** — First fishermen of fish, afterwards of men; whence, literally, many seas were crossed; whence: “Go ye into the whole world, and preach the gospel to every creature.”
**“and all that are therein”** — let him praise
**“the inhabitants of this isle”** — the various Church, or the Gentiles
**“and ye inhabitants of them”**
• the Gentiles
• a voice in praise, because he has delivered, and let him rejoice in his salvation
42.11:
**“Let the desert be exalted”** — let him praise and rejoice
**“and the cities thereof”** — the churches
**“Cedar shall dwell”**
• who was not wont to
• darkness, that is, the Gentiles who do not know God
**“Cedar”** — The son of Ismael: the Saracens, from him, who are better called Agarenes, but by the name of the free woman they veiled the disgrace of the handmaid. For Ismael was the son of the handmaid Agar; from her are the Saracens, for he begot twelve leaders. By his name also the province itself is called.
**“give praise”** — the Lord
**“ye inhabitants”** — the Gentiles
**“of Petra”**
• a city in Palestine, but here it signifies the hardness of the Gentiles
• Christ
**“they shall cry from the top of the mountains”**
• the apostles and others
• in the hearers
**“from the top of the mountains”** — “Get thee up upon a high mountain, thou that bringest good tidings to Sion.” From the top of the mountain: from the height of virtue and contemplation, so that they also teach by example what they preach.
42.12: **“They shall give glory to the Lord, and shall declare his praise in the islands”** — the Gentiles
42.13:
**“The Lord shall go forth as a mighty man”**
• who seemed weak
• He describes the coming of the Saviour and compares him to a most valiant man about to fight against adversaries.
**“shall go forth”**
• from the captivity of the Jews
• from mercy, in opinion not in reality
**“as a man of war”** — against his enemies
**“shall he stir up zeal”** — of vengeance
**“he shall shout and cry”** — saying: you are of the father, the devil
**“he shall shout”** — Whence: “They have provoked me with that which was no god ... and I will provoke them with a foolish nation.”
**“against his enemies”** — the Jews
**“he shall prevail”** — through the Romans
42.14:
**“I have always held my peace”** — O Jews
**“I have always held my peace, I have been patient”** — waiting for your repentance
**“I will speak now as a woman in labour”**
• your counsels
• I will reveal what I have thought
**“and swallow up at once”** — I will utterly destroy you
**“as a woman in labour”** — I will bring forth the offspring of my counsel into the light, as a woman brings forth her child; so I will bring forth the grief I have concealed.
42.15:
**“I will lay waste the mountains”**
• the greater ones
• the varieties of the proud
**“and hills”** — the middling ones
**“and will make all their grass”** — the people
**“and will dry up”** — by the Romans
**“And”** — then
**“and I will turn rivers”** — a river of wisdom
**“into islands”** — of the Gentiles
**“and will dry up the standing pools”** — the teaching of the Jews, so that reading the prophets they may not understand
42.16:
**“And I will lead the blind”** — the Gentiles
**“in the way”** — Christ, who is the way, the truth and the life
**“which they know not”** — now
**“in the paths which they were ignorant of”** — to make progress
**“I will make them walk”** — it is not of him that willeth, nor of him that runneth, but of God that sheweth mercy
**“In the paths”** — In the knowledge of the prophets, who are the paths to Christ, while they foretell his birth, resurrection and ascension.
**“I will make darkness”** — ignorance
**“before them”** — to the Gentiles
**“light, and crooked things straight”**
• so that in the Old Testament they may receive the light of Christ
• their hearts
**“these things”** — foretold
**“have I done to them”** — that, being terrified, they may repent
**“and have not forsaken them”** — I do not promise things to come, but now render things promised
**“them”** — the uncorrected
42.17:
**“They are turned back”** — these things having been heard
**“back”** — also by driving out the apostles
**“let them be greatly confounded”** — concerning the Gentiles who would not believe when the apostles preached
**“confounded, that trust”** — the Gentiles
**“in graven things”** — Let all be confounded that adore graven things
**“that say to the molten thing: You are our god”** — Let them be confounded, etc. When the fullness of the Gentiles has come in, then also Israel, converted, will repent of his error, he who formerly served idols.
42.18:
**“Hear, ye deaf”** — Hear, ye deaf
**“and, ye blind”** — in mind
**“And, ye blind”** — He is called blind in the chief sense who once saw; he in an improper sense who never did. So the Jew is blind properly, the Gentile improperly.
**“behold that you may see”**
• the true light
• explained
42.19:
**“Who is blind, but my servant”**
• not the Gentiles, as the Jews falsely claim
• Israel, who formerly served the Lord
**“or deaf, but he to whom I have sent my messengers”** — the prophets
**“my messengers”** — now
**“Who is blind, but he that is sold”** — under sin
**“Who is blind, but the servant of the Lord”** — formerly
42.20:
**“Thou that seest”** — O Israel
**“many things”** — he means the law and the prophets
**“wilt thou not observe them”** — which are commanded there
**“thou that hast ears open”**
• of the body
• of which above: “Hearing, you shall hear, and shall not understand.”
**“wilt thou not hear”** — you will obey
42.21:
**“and”** — yet
**“the Lord was willing”** — freely
**“to sanctify”** — by observing
**“him”** — the people
**“to magnify the law, and exalt it”** — from vices to virtues
42.22:
**“himself”** — lying low
**“But this is a people”**
• the disobedient people
• by unclean spirits
**“that is robbed and wasted”** — by the Chaldean and Roman enemies
**“the snare”** — a hindrance, so that they do not believe in Christ
**“of young men, all”**
• of the foolish
• The snare of the young men, etc. He returns to the Lord’s preaching, rebuking the scribes and Pharisees; for these are a snare to the simple, so that they might not turn to the Lord.
**“and they are hid in the houses of prisons”**
• in the heart, and with the heart they spoke
• in the hidden place of the heart: “Master, we know that thou art a true speaker.”
**“they are made a prey”** — of enemies
**“and there is none to deliver them”** — there is none to deliver them: neither prophet nor leader who intercedes with the Lord for them, as Moses and others did
**“a spoil”** — for plunder, the spoil of enemies
**“and there is none that saith”** — and there is none who says to the Lord
**“Restore”** — liberty to them
42.23:
**“Who is there among you that will give ear to this”** — at least a few hear
**“that will attend”** — what I foretell
**“and hearken for times to come”** — Who is there, etc. The prophet exhorts them that at least some may hear, understand the causes of their captivity, and take heed.
42.24:
**“Who hath given”** — of the Romans
**“Jacob and Israel to robbers; hath not the Lord”** — the Father
**“himself”** — not another
**“against whom we have sinned”**
• by killing the Son
• because
**“And they would not walk in his ways”** — commandments
**“to walk”** — and
**“and they have not hearkened”** — from the Son
**“to his law”** — gospel
42.25:
**“And”** — therefore
**“he hath poured out”** — through the Romans
**“against him”** — the people
**“the indignation of his fury, and a strong battle”**
• famine, sword, captivity
• Upon him. That he who had been silent before should no longer be silent, but should rebuke him, not with words but with torments.
**“and”** — this being in vengeance for the death of Christ
**“hath burnt him”** — with material fire and of tribulation
**“round about, and he knew not, and set him on fire, and he understood not”** — that he was punished because he did not receive the Son of God
**“and he knew not”** — As histories relate, neither the Gentiles understood that this was done in vengeance for the Son, nor the Jews, blinded by their malice.

43.1:
**“And now thus saith the Lord”** — And now these things. Above he spoke of the captivity of the Jews and of the malice of those who would not believe; now he addresses the primitive Church, which is of the Jews, that they may understand the Creator of their soul and body.
**“that created thee, O Jacob”** — first a wrestler
**“and formed thee, O Israel”** — afterwards a contemplator
**“Fear not, for I have redeemed thee”** — by the blood of the Son
**“and called thee by thy name”**
• O Israel
• as a familiar, so that you may preach unavoidably and fear nothing
• a servant
**“thou art mine”** — Creating you, Jacob, etc. Jacob, a supplanter; Israel, a man seeing God. These are the apostles and apostolic men, who both supplanted vices and merited to see God.
43.2:
**“When thou shalt pass through the waters”** — By this he signifies the countless torments of the apostles and of other preachers.
**“I will be with thee”** — a guardian
**“and the rivers shall not cover thee; when thou shalt walk in the fire, thou shalt not be burnt”** — the soul, although with the body
**“Through the waters”** — According to the Hebrews, by the waters is meant Egypt, because of the greatness of the Nile; by the rivers, the Chaldeans, because among them are many rivers; by the fire (because they were cruel and fiery) the Macedonians are designated. By the flame (which consumes all things), the Romans. The apostles also passed through these kingdoms by preaching, and the Lord everywhere with them.
43.3:
**“For I am”** — Fear not.
**“the Lord thy God, the Holy One of Israel”** — because I am with you until the consummation of the age
**“thy Saviour”** — who make you a preacher
**“I have given thy atonement”** — O Israel
**“Egypt, Ethiopia and Saba”** — by converting
**“for thee”**
• for your profit
• I have given Egypt for thy atonement, etc. That from it you may acquire for yourself mercy and a crown, by preaching, namely to the Egyptians and Ethiopians, who are almost the last, and to the Sabeans; Saba is a city situated on the borders of Ethiopia. “Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth.”
• Since they heard from the Lord. “Go ye into the whole world, and preach the gospel to every creature.” But they, having set out, preached.
43.4:
**“Since thou becamest honourable”** — for those converted
**“in my eyes”** — not of men
**“thou art glorious: I”** — therefore
**“I have loved thee”** — first; whence he himself loved us first
**“and I will give men for thee”** — whence you have the reward
**“and people”** — converted by your preaching
**“for thy life”** — salvation
43.5:
**“Fear not”** — therefore
**“fear”** — the adversities of the world
**“for I am with thee”** — to the Church
**“I will bring thy seed”** — your sons in faith
**“and gather thee from the west”** — like you
**“From the east”** — “Many shall come from the east and the west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob,” from all parts of the world, that is.
43.6:
**“I will say to the north: Give up”** — To the devil; give back those you have captured.
**“and to the south: Keep not back: bring”** — O Israel
**“my sons”** — the predestinated
**“from afar”**
• from the ends of the earth
• you who were far off have been made near by the blood of Christ
**“and my daughters”** — souls or holy women
**“I will say to the north”** — Gregory. To the north it is said: Give up; for the Gentiles are commanded to offer to God the gifts of their faith. To the south it is commanded: Keep not back; for the Hebrews, who trust in faith, are instructed not to reject the life of the Gentiles by despising them, etc.
43.7:
**“And every one”** — I will bring
**“that calleth upon my name, I have created him for my glory”** — in body
**“I have formed him”** — in soul
**“and made him”** — faithful
43.8:
**“Bring forth”**
• O son
• Voice of the Father to the Son concerning the Jews blind in mind. And note that the calling of the Jews came first, then that of the Gentiles. Whence also Paul: “To you it behoved us first to speak the word of God.”
**“forth the people that are blind”** — under unbelief of mind
**“and their eyes”** — of body
**“that are deaf”** — in mind
**“and have ears”** — in body
43.9:
**“All the nations are assembled together”** — after the calling of the Jews
**“together”** — into the sheepfold of sheep, of which there is also one shepherd
**“and”**
• first
• so
**“the tribes are gathered”** — the predestined Jews
**“All the nations”** — The prophet, rebuking the Gentiles about idolatry and marvelling that no one among the Gentiles could foreknow this, but only the people of God who received the law of God had prophets. Whence God is known in Judea.
**“Who”** — of your gods
**“among you”** — O Gentiles
**“can declare this”** — what I say
**“and the former things”** — past
**“shall make us hear”** — as our God
**“let them bring forth their witnesses”** — the gods themselves prove themselves by testimonies
**“let them be justified”** — the true gods are proved
**“and hear”** — that they doubt
**“and say”** — that they are the true gods
**“It is truth”**
• O prophets, O apostles
• as if they themselves have none; but truly you are the witnesses
43.10:
**“saith the Lord”** — the Father
**“and my servant”** — Christ
**“whom I have chosen”**
• from all, for the salvation of all
• in whom I am well pleased
**“that you may know”** — all these things, namely, will be done
**“and believe me, and understand”** — who before were brutish and senseless
**“For I am”** — alone
**“myself am”**
• God
• I created all things, because before etc.
**“Before me”** — who am the beginning, etc.
**“there was no God formed”**
• formed: another reading
• of anything
**“and there shall be none after me”** — because I am the end
**“There was no God formed”** — Some copies have plasmatus, but it does not fit well; yet it can be so explained. Before me no idol was formed, because I made man just, by whom an idol was unjustly formed.
43.11:
**“I”** — not another
**“I am the Lord”** — repetition, confirmation
**“and there is no saviour besides me”** — because the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit are one in substance; or, without me there is no Son, who is the salvation of the world
43.12:
**“I have declared, and have saved”**
• the human race in the Son
• I have declared the past or the future
**“I have declared”** — Through the prophets: the birth of the Son, the calling of the Gentiles, the expulsion of demons.
**“I have made it heard, and there was no strange one among you”**
• the prophets and apostles preaching
• namely, God; but I only
**“You are my witnesses, saith the Lord, and I am God”** — prophets and apostles, because I foretold, not another
43.13:
**“And from the beginning I am the same, and there is none that can deliver out of my hand”** — by power
**“deliver”** — who from the beginning foretell the future
**“I will work”** — the salvation of the Gentiles
**“and who shall turn it away”** — the work
43.14:
**“Thus saith the Lord your redeemer”**
• or: redeemer
• through the Son
• O apostles
**“the Holy One of Israel: For your sake I sent”** — the Son
**“to Babylon”** — the world confounded by sin
**“and have brought down”** — from the hearts of men
**“all their bars”**
• the hindrances of the princes of demons
• Thus saith the Lord, etc. That is, these things which follow. The Father to the apostles. For you, who are indeed my witnesses, that is, who preach the gospel, to whom he said: “Fear not.”
**“and the Chaldeans”** — demons, leading wretched souls about through the waves of this world, and glorying from this
**“the Chaldeans glorying in their ships”** — Historically. The Chaldeans abound in rivers and are skilled with ships, and glory in them.
43.15:
**“I the Lord”** — no other
**“your Holy One”**
• I have decreed this
• sanctifying you
**“I am the Lord your Holy One”** — Once to the sons of Israel, now to you. O apostles, in the world, with the demons cast out and all the princes conquered.
**“the Creator of Israel”** — contemplatives
**“your King”** — ruling you

• Whatever is said of idols can be referred to the leaders of heretics, who with artful heart compose the images of their own doctrines and venerate what they know they have feigned. Nor is their own error enough for them, unless they deceive the simple by their adoration, who think godliness is gain and devour the houses of widows, abusing the ignorance of the common people. So by the art of dialectic, as with auger and file and plane, they form their god, and with hammers they beat it out and gild it with the charm of rhetorical speech; “whose God is their belly; and whose glory is in their shame.”

**“who say to the deep”**

**“I will dry up”** — I will dry up your rivers. Under Darius, namely, and Cyrus his nephew. For on the night when Balthasar was slain by them, the river Euphrates, which flowed through the midst of the city, was divided by their army into channels so that they might enter the city through its bed.

45.1:
**“Thus saith the Lord to my anointed”** — that is, to the king
**“my anointed Cyrus, whose right hand I have taken hold of”** — a leader and helper, so that no one can resist
**“to subdue nations before his face”** — the Chaldeans, Babylonians, Medes and many others
**“and to turn the backs of kings”** — before him into flight
**“and to open the doors before him”** — another reading: before him
**“and the gates shall not be shut”**
• To my anointed Cyrus, etc. Allegorically. We can say this of an ecclesiastical man to whom God gives speech and wisdom, that by his disputation he may overthrow opposing sects, as with Stephen, whose wisdom his enemies could not resist; and that he may subject to his power the kings, that is, the patriarchs of the several heresies, and open and break open what by the art of dialectic seemed shut up, and bring into the open the secrets of the heretics, overcoming and convincing them; or that he may know the secrets of Christ, “in whom are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.” God calls such a man by name because he is the defender of his servant Jacob and of his elect Israel. Him he takes up and likens to his own word; which everyone ought to beware of, lest he think that what he speaks is his own, lest he deserve to hear: “I girded thee, and thou hast not known me.” For when he has taught all that there is no other God but the one God of Jacob and Israel, Marcion will be confounded, who understands two gods: one good, the other unjust; one the maker of visible things, the other of invisible. Of whom the first makes light, the second darkness; the former peace, the latter evil; whereas one and the same God has made both according to the difference of merits.
• And the backs of kings, etc. What city did not lie open to him? Which of the kings did not turn his back? Which walls, before unassailable, were not overthrown by his siege? You will find these things more fully accomplished in the history of Xenophon.
**“anointed”** — Among the Romans the diadem, among the Jews anointing, makes both kings and priests, from which they are also called anointed ones (Christs). Cyrus is Christ not by anointing but by dignity.
45.2:
**“I”** — O Cyrus
**“I will go before thee, and will humble the great ones of the earth”** — the Babylonians, Chaldeans
**“I will humble; I will break in pieces the gates of brass”** — to you
**“and will burst the bars of iron”** — all power is from the Lord God
45.3:
**“And I will give thee hidden treasures, and the concealed riches of secret places: that thou mayest know that I am the Lord who call thee by thy name, the God of Israel”** — before you are, by foretelling to you what is to come
**“hidden treasures”** — Of all cities, so that, with idols cast aside and drawn by benefits, you might perceive the one God, who named you before you were.
45.4:
**“For the sake of my servant”** — not for your sake
**“Jacob, and Israel my elect”** — that you might free him from captivity, acknowledging the good things I have done for you on his account, and the things to be done that I have foretold
**“I have even called thee by thy name”** — that is, Cyrus
**“I have made a likeness of thee, and”** — yet
**“thou hast not known me”**
• And I called you, etc. As I called Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and foretold many, so Isaac and Josias, lest you seem to be that one in whose type you went before; and you did not know me.
• And I have called thee by thy name. I have made thee like my Son, namely in name. For Cyrus is an heir, because he received his uncle’s inheritance. Christ also is an heir, according to that: “Ask of me, and I will give thee the Gentiles for thy inheritance.” Cyrus also is a christ by the dignity of his empire; but the Son is Christ, anointed with the oil of gladness above his fellows.
45.5:
**“I the Lord”** — the one God, but you worshipped idols, which profited you nothing
**“and there is none else”** — another
**“there is no God, besides me: I girded thee”**
• with the strength of many nations
• with power, so that you might subdue kingdoms
**“and thou hast not known me”** — who gave you these things
**“besides me”** — Because the Son and the Holy Spirit are in the Father: apart from my word, indeed, and my reason and power and the wisdom that is in me, there is no other God.
45.6:
**“That they may know who are from the rising of the sun”** — of the whole world
**“and they who are from the west, that there is none besides me”** — the Father in the Son, the Son in the Father; whence: “I and the Father are one.”
**“I the Lord”** — distinctively
**“That they may know who”** — Esdras says that Cyrus wrote to all nations that there is no God but the God of Israel. Or, from the freeing of the captives the mercy and power of God became better known to all. Josephus, however, in the Book of Antiquities, says that the people was dismissed because Cyrus read in the book of Isaias what the Lord had said of him beforehand through the prophet.
45.7:
**“I form the light”** — day or deliverance
**“and create darkness”** — namely things contrary to one another; for as darkness is contrary to light, so war is to peace
**“I make peace, and create evil: I the Lord”** — because
**“that do all these things”**
• In this it is proved that the Lord does all these things.
• I form the light and create darkness, because when the darkness of pain is created outwardly by scourges, the light of the mind is kindled within through instruction. I make peace and create evil, because peace with God is then restored to us when these things, which were well made but not well desired, are turned for us into evil scourges.
**“I form the light, and create darkness”** — Gregory. Evils, which subsist by no nature of their own, are not created by the Lord; but the Lord indicates that he creates evils when he forms things well created into a scourge for us who act badly, so that those very things are evil by the pain they cause to the guilty, and good by the nature in which they exist; whence poison is indeed death to a man and life to a serpent.
**“darkness”** — Night, or captivity. As if, having mercy on the penitent, I bring them back from captivity; angry with sinners, I hold them captive.
**“evil”** — War, that is, affliction, according as it is said: “Sufficient for the day is the evil thereof.” Let them be confounded, therefore, who think God the maker of evils. For here evil is put not for what is contrary to good but for affliction and war.
45.8:
**“Drop down dew, ye heavens, from above”** — Let Gabriel come and send us the dew, that is, announce salvation.
**“and let the clouds rain”** — Announcing.
**“the just”** — Christ, or justice.
**“let the earth be opened”**
• Mary, for believing.
• “Truth is sprung out of the earth,” etc.
**“and bud forth a saviour”** — Jesus: “For he shall save his people from their sins.”
**“and let justice”** — All.
**“spring up”** — To the world.
**“together”** — With him.
**“I”** — Father.
**“the Lord have created him”**
• According to his humanity.
• “Drop down dew, ye heavens,” etc. He appropriately adds this about the coming of Christ, signified through Cyrus, because he freed the human race from the captivity of the devil. Or these words may cling to what precedes, so that, with Cyrus loosing the captivity, the heavens and the earth rejoice by metonymy.
**“and let the clouds”** — The prophets, watering our hearts with saving rain and announcing the birth, passion, resurrection and ascension of Christ. Whence: “I will command the clouds to rain no rain upon it,” and elsewhere: “Thy truth reacheth, even to the clouds.”
**“have created him”** — He who indeed was a worm, and is read to have sprouted from the earth, according to his humanity.
45.9:
**“Woe to him that”** — As if to say: believe what I preach, namely that Christ is to come, for woe to him who contradicts his maker; or Cyrus, to whom through the liberation of my people I will subject all kingdoms.

**“a sherd”** — It is itself.
**“of the earthen pots”** — Earthen: Samos is a city where the art of potters was discovered.
**“shall the clay say”** — Man.
**“to him that fashioneth it”** — God.
45.10:
**“Woe to him that saith to his father”** — To the almighty.

**“and to the woman”** — Mary.
**“Why dost thou bring forth?”**
• Whence, born of a woman, made under the law.
• Since you did not conceive from a man.
**“woman”** — A man powerful over a woman. A woman powerful over a man.
45.11:
**“Thus saith the Lord the Holy One of Israel, his maker”** — Moulder.
**“His maker”** — Of the Son, according to the humanity, in the virginal womb. Whence: “The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the most High shall overshadow thee,” etc.
**“things to come”** — mysteries
**“Ask me”**
• ironically
• O Jews
**“concerning my children”** — adopted ones, who through the Son are about to believe, how we ought to rule them
**“and concerning the work of my hands give ye charge to me”** — ironically
45.12:
**“I made the earth”** — as to one especially ignorant of how I would arrange created things
**“and I created man upon it”** — as a lord
**“I created”** — to be inhabited by men
**“my hand stretched forth the heavens, and all their host”** — by the stars and angels
**“I have commanded”** — that they should do

45.13:
**“I have raised him up”**
• from the dead
• or I will raise
• He died for our sins and rose again for our justification.

45.14:
**“Thus saith the Lord: The labour of Egypt”** — the worship of idols, over which Egypt in particular was subject
**“The labour of Egypt”** — The worship of idols. For it labours much in carrying out the sacrifices of idols. But when the apostles preached, they were converted, and more than all kingdoms there abound there the religious orders of monks, so that where sin abounded, grace might also abound more.
**“and the merchandise”** — earthly
**“of Ethiopia”** — turned to God
**“and of Sabaim”**

45.15:

45.16:
**“They are all confounded and ashamed”** — from confusion

45.17:
**“Israel”**
• but

**“in the Lord with an eternal salvation: you shall not be confounded”**
• O apostles and other faithful
• “Whoever shall be ashamed of me before men, I will be ashamed of him before my Father.”

45.18:

45.20:
**“Assemble yourselves”**

**“and draw near together, ye that are saved”** — by my blood.
**“of the Gentiles: they have no knowledge that set up the wood of their graven work”** — an idol.
**“and pray to a god that cannot save”**
• themselves and others.

45.21:
**“Tell ye, and come, and consult together”** — into one.

47.1:
**“Come down”** — He inveighs against Babylon and the Chaldeans.
**“sit”** — Sit, O Babylon, down from the throne of the kingdom.
**“in the dust”** — As a captive.
**“O virgin daughter of Babylon”**
• Barren of good works.
• The people of Babylon.
**“sit on the ground”** — As a handmaid, because there is no throne.
**“there is no throne”** — The dignity of the kingdom.
**“daughter of the Chaldeans”** — Because founded by the Chaldeans.
**“for thou shalt no more be called delicate and tender”** — Pampered, abounding in delights.
**“Come down, sit in the dust”** — Because we are all creatures of God. Nor, according to the heretics, is the nature of Babylon condemnable, or on account of luxury and the adornment of a most powerful city, which is now old and near its setting; she boasts of herself as a little maiden and girl.
*Morally:* Gregory. Come down, sit in the dust, O daughter of Babylon. In this place the human mind is called a virgin, not as uncorrupted (as I think) but as unfruitful. And because Babylon means confusion, the unfruitful mind is rightly called the daughter of Babylon, which, in that it brings forth no good works (since it is not ordered by any rule of right living), is begotten as it were of its mother, confusion. But if she is called a virgin not as unfruitful but as corrupted, after she has lost the state of salvation, then what was said, “come down,” is spoken to heap up her confusion. For the human mind stands on high when it longs for heavenly rewards. But it comes down from this state when, shamefully bound, it submits itself to the fleeting desires of the world; to which it is fittingly added at once: Sit in the dust. For one who comes down sits in the dust, because, forsaking heavenly things, sprinkled with earthly thoughts, he grows vile among the lowest things. Sit on the ground, because you were unwilling to raise yourself from heavenly conversation, to humble yourself prostrate beneath yourself among earthly things. Whence it is necessarily added: There is no throne for the daughter of the Chaldeans. Chaldeans are interpreted as fierce; and they are very fierce who, following their own pleasures, do not know how to spare even their own impulses. But the daughter of the fierce has no throne, because the mind that is born from wicked desires to the love of the world, and is darkened in them, in that it submits itself to earthly desires loses its seat, and as it were is driven from the session of its judge, since it wanders through outward lusts; and often by just judgment it is left to its own will, and under the things it anxiously seeks the toilsome services of the world are relaxed. For thou shalt no more be called delicate and tender. It is certain that parents spare their tender daughters and do not afflict them with hard and servile works. Almighty God therefore calls a soul as it were a tender daughter when he calls back each one’s beloved soul from the toilsome servitudes of this world, lest while it is affected by outward things it be hardened by inward desires. But the daughter of the Chaldeans is not called delicate and tender, because the mind given to wicked desires is left to the labor of this age, so that outwardly it serves the world like a handmaid, because inwardly it does not love God as a daughter. Whence also she is said to take the millstone and grind meal. The mill is turned in a circle and meal is brought forth. Every action of this world is evil, which while it heaps up many cares turns human minds as it were in a circle, and casts out from itself as it were meal, because the seduced heart always begets the most minute thoughts. Sometimes, however, one who in quiet was believed to be of some importance is laid bare when set in any action. Be uncovered, etc. For the baseness is laid bare by the empty performance of work, when a mind vile and abject is recognized in the display of action, which in quiet was before thought great. The mind uncovers the shoulder when it shows its work, which was unknown; it reveals the leg when it makes known that by certain steps of desires it gapes after the gains of the world. She also crosses the rivers when she ceaselessly seeks the actions of this age, which daily flow away to their end. And while she leaves some and follows others, she passes as it were from river to river.
**“thou shalt no more be called delicate”** — Metaphor. Queens are wont to be soft and delicate, and not bearing themselves through tenderness; under this appearance Babylon is addressed.
47.2:
**“Take a millstone”** — Who a little before was queen.
**“and grind meal”** — O captive, for this is the work of captives.
**“meal”** — Or: offer intercourse to the Medes and Persians, who are most ardent in this. According to this the Hebrews say that the Philistines, having put out Samson’s eyes, forced him to grind, that is, to lie with their women, so that from him they might have men of great and invincible stature.
**“uncover thy shame”** — To your lords the Medes and Persians, the victors.
**“strip thy shoulder”** — That you may be seen as a woman.
**“make bare thy legs”** — For the lust of the victors.
**“pass over the rivers”**
• Or that you may cross the rivers going into captivity.
• Tigris, Euphrates, Chobar.
47.3:
**“shall be discovered”** — To enemies.
**“thy nakedness; and thy shame shall be seen”** — The misery of captivity.
**“I will take vengeance”**
• From you.
• For I will avenge my people whom you oppressed; for if I commanded that you should afflict, yet not that you should utterly oppress.
**“and no man shall resist”** — As Moses, when God wished to destroy the sons of Israel. It signifies, moreover, the angel placed over Babylon, who with the others says: “We would have cured Babylon, but she is not healed.”
47.4:
**“Our redeemer”**
• From the servitude of captivity.
• The voice of the people returning from captivity after seventy years.
**“the Lord of hosts”** — Of men and of angels.
**“is his name”** — is
**“the Holy One of Israel”** — who says: Be holy, for I am holy.
47.5:
**“Sit thou silent”** — through confusion, lest you be seen
**“and get thee into darkness”** — through confusion, hardly bearing the light
**“daughter of the Chaldeans”** — because built by the Chaldeans
**“for thou shalt no more be called”** — as before
**“the lady of kingdoms”** — of the Egyptians, Assyrians and others
**“Sit”** — The discourse is addressed to Babylon, and speaks to her as to a once-queen, now a handmaid. Sit low, be humble and vile, be silent, as one sad who considers your misery.
47.6:
**“I was angry with my people”** — the Jews
**“I have polluted”** — I allowed you to be defiled
**“my inheritance”** — but
**“and have given them into thy bend”** — that is, that you should scourge them, not kill them
**“thou hast shewn no mercy to them”** — you have shown mercy to no one
**“mercy upon the ancient”** — even him who is to be pitied, and an enemy
**“thou hast laid”** — cruelty
**“thy yoke exceeding heavy”**
• or mine
• I was angry, etc. He gives the reason why he afflicted the Chaldeans so, lest he seem to have acted without cause, he who works nothing without cause; and that the Chaldeans may know that they did not overcome the people of God by their own strength.
47.7:
**“And thou hast said: I shall be a lady for ever”** — pride
**“I shall be a lady”** — I will always reign
**“thou hast not laid these things”** — which you now suffer
**“to thy heart”** — in prosperity we avoid adversity
**“neither hast thou remembered thy latter end”**
• considering the future
• of coming evil
47.8:
**“and”** — therefore
**“now hear these things”** — to be foretold
**“thou that art delicate”** — abounding in delights
**“and dwellest confidently”** — fearing nothing
**“that sayest in thy heart: I am”** — I am the mistress of the world
**“and there is none else”** — who rules
**“besides me: I shall not sit as a widow”** — without a king
**“and I shall not know barrenness”** — because there will always be someone to reign from me
47.9:
**“These two things shall come upon thee suddenly in one day, barrenness”** — of peoples, as of sons
**“and widowhood”** — of a king
**“All things are come upon thee”** — foretold by me and by the prophets
**“because of the multitude”** — not only on account of your cruelty and your pride
**“of thy sorceries”** — because you trust in your magicians and sorcerers and their counsels
