**“and for the great hardness of thy enchanters”** — because lying men kept making you believe that you would always reign, hard and proud
**“Suddenly”** — Of the sudden attack by Cyrus and Darius; for she did not fear that she could be overcome by the Medes and Persians, who, compared with her, were of no strength and were themselves subject.
47.10:
**“And thou hast trusted”** — and confidence in reigning
**“hast trusted in thy wickedness”** — in the counsel of your sorcerers
**“and hast said: There is none that seeth me”** — who corrects what I do
**“Thy wisdom”** — diviners, magicians, soothsayers
**“and thy knowledge”** — divination by the stars, observation
**“this hath deceived thee. And thou hast said”** — which is worse
**“in thy heart: I am”** — mistress of the world
**“and besides me there is no other”** — about to reign
47.11:
**“Evil shall come upon thee”** — the repayment of the evil that you have done
**“and thou shalt not know the rising”** — the beginning
**“his”**
• of evil. Thou shalt not know the rising thereof. The calamity will come unexpectedly, foretold neither by magicians nor by diviners; for they did not fear a despised and subject people.
• Thou shalt not know the rising thereof. Calamity will come unexpectedly, and was foretold neither by the magi nor by the diviners; for they did not fear a people despised and subject.
**“and shall fall violently”** — evils will rush in
**“upon thee calamity, which thou canst not keep off”** — to drive away from you
**“misery shall come upon thee suddenly, which thou shalt not know”** — now
47.12:
**“Stand now”** — against Cyrus and Darius
**“with thy enchanters”**
• Irony.
• in whom you trust
**“and with the multitude of thy sorceries, in which thou hast laboured”** — with great zeal
**“from thy youth”** — from the beginning of their reign you arrange everything by counsel
**“if so be it may profit thee any thing, or if thou mayst become”** — through them
**“stronger”** — but
47.13:
**“Thou hast failed in the multitude of thy counsels”** — by which you formerly overcame many nations.
**“let now the astrologers stand”** — Ironically.
**“and save thee, let the astrologers”** — astrologers.
**“they that gazed at the stars, and counted the months, that from them they might tell the things that shall come to thee”** — which the Lord has devised against you.
**“The astrologers”** — Astrologers, who think that all things are ruled by the stars. As if to say: why did they not provide all things for you? These are commonly called mathematicians, who think that worldly things are ruled by the course of the stars; whence: “there came wise men from the east, saying: We have seen his star in the east.” Or, they were moved by the prophecy of Balaam, who said: “A star shall rise out of Jacob.”
47.14:
**“Behold”** — while they are silent, the prophet announces the things to come.
**“they are as stubble”** — powerless to resist.
**“fire”** — of the city, or of tribulation.
**“hath burnt them”** — with you.
**“not”** — even.
**“deliver themselves”** — life.
**“from the power of the flames: there are no coals”** — divine wisdom, by which they may foresee and escape, and drive out the cold of error.
**“wherewith they may be warmed, nor fire, that they may sit thereat”**
• that they may shake off the darkness, but by which they are consumed.
• They are become as stubble, etc. Septuagint. You have coals of fire; you shall sit upon them; these shall be a help to you. As the Gazarenes and magi lead you by error to pride. But the burning of Babylon calls you by punishments to penance.
47.15:
**“Such are all the things become”** — thus they are made low.
**“to thee, in which thou hast laboured”** — in whatever you had toiled, since the light of true wisdom is lacking to you.
**“thy merchants”**
• magicians.
• your enchanters, selling you lies.
**“thy merchants from thy youth”** — deceiving you from the beginning of your reign.
**“every one in his own way”** — a different sect.
**“hath erred; there is none”** — of them.
**“that can save thee”** — from misery.

48.1:
**“Hear ye these things”**
• what I am to say.
• as if he said: what I foretold to Babylon must be fulfilled; but you, hear more attentively what I am about to say.
• It is the custom that when the carnal Israel is spoken of simply, without the addition of a name, Jacob or Israel is said, as in this place, where he addresses those who are called by the name Jacob or Israel.
**“O house of Jacob”**
• not Jacob, not Israel, you who do not have the deeds of the name.
• Judah and Benjamin and Levi.
**“you that are called”** — in name only.
**“by the name of Israel, and are come forth out of the waters of Juda”** — by seed and by flesh, that is, not by faith.
**“and are come forth out of the waters of Juda”** — He makes mention of Judah, because when the ten tribes were carried captive, Judah and Benjamin and the Levites remained in the land and had a king from Judah.
**“you who swear by the name of the Lord, and make mention of the God of Israel”**
• not in honor of the Lord, but in confirmation of your lie, because you worship idols, whose abomination is why it was commanded that one swear by the name of the Lord.
• And make mention of the God of Israel. “This people honoureth me with their lips: but their heart is far from me.”
48.2:
**“For they are called of the holy city”** — Irony.
**“of the holy city”** — As if he said: you boast that you are inhabitants of Jerusalem, and that you have the privilege of the Lord of hosts; with empty claim you take to yourselves the names of Jacob, Israel, of the holy city, and of the almighty God.
**“they are called”**
• as they boast.
• from Jerusalem, Jerusalemites.
**“and are established upon the God”** — protector.
**“of Israel, are established”** — founded.
**“the Lord of hosts”** — of which we are indeed witnesses.
**“his name”** — is.
48.3:
**“The former things”** — ancient things.
**“of old I have declared”** — from when I began to speak against Babylon, the burden of Babylon, etc.
**“and they went forth out of my mouth”** — by the prophets.
**“and I have made them to be heard: I did them suddenly and they came to pass”** — or I will do.
**“And they went forth”**
• or they will come.
• The overthrow of the Chaldeans, your return.
• The former things; from that time. I foretold that the Babylonians would be overcome, and I will suddenly do what I threatened, so that when those things foretold come to pass you may know they happened neither by chance nor by the will of your gods.
• The former miracles, namely those which he did in the midst of them from the time they went out of Egypt, and when the captivity by Nabuchodonosor was imminent. But now, before they are taken captive, he foretells their deliverance and the devastation of the Chaldeans; whence suddenly, namely: I have done what I now declare is to come.
48.4:
**“For I knew that thou art stubborn”**
• unbelieving.
• as if I speak for your benefit.
**“And thy neck is as an iron sinew”** — irrevocable pride.
**“And thy forehead as brass”** — shameless.
**“Iron sinew”** — Hence Stephen: “stiffnecked and uncircumcised in heart”; your forehead is brass. Whence Ezechiel: “Thou hadst a harlot’s forehead, thou wouldst not blush.”
48.5:
**“I foretold thee”** — future things to you and to Babylon.
**“Before they came to pass I told thee”** — from when I began to speak against Babylon by the prophets, lest perhaps you should say, my idols etc.
**“Lest thou shouldst say: My idols have done these things”** — that Cyrus and Darius should avenge me on the Babylonians.
48.6:
**“Which thou hast heard”** — to be fulfilled through the prophets.
**“See all”** — fulfilled.
**“But have you declared them”** — to your sons what was to come upon Babylon, but you hid the truth.
**“I have shewn thee new things”** — about the miseries of Babylon.
**“From that time”** — not that I led you out of Egypt and such things.
**“And things are kept”**
• by me.
• As though I were about to announce many things, but since you do not remember what I say, I keep back what I was going to say.
48.7:
**“They are created now”**
• by me
• with me before they come to be
**“And not”** — you knew
**“From that time”** — from the time they were created
**“And before the day”** — when they are fulfilled
**“And thou heardest them not”** — by your gods
**“Lest thou shouldst say: Behold I knew them”** — by my gods
48.8:
**“Thou hast neither heard, nor known, neither was thy ear opened of old”**
• hearing them
• of the heart or of the body
• from when they were with me
**“For I know that transgressing”** — the law of Moses
**“Thou wilt transgress”** — at the coming of the Son, the law of the gospel
**“And a transgressor”** — from when you received the law, because at once you worshipped an idol
**“I have called thee from the womb”** — when freed from Egypt, as if you were conceived in my womb
48.9:
**“For my name's sake”**
• lest it be cheapened
• not by your merit
**“Far off”**
• from you
• by deferring
**“I will remove my wrath”**
• I did so, namely, lest I destroy
• by bringing back from captivity
**“And for my praise”** — that you may praise me
**“I will bridle thee, lest thou shouldst perish”**
• with the bridle of the law, so that you follow me like a beast of burden
• For my name’s sake, etc. That is, lest it be violated, I will remove far off; I did, that is, my wrath, lest it destroy you, because you adored the calf; and my praise, that is, that you should praise me; I will bridle you with my law.
48.10:
**“Behold I have refined thee”** — in the furnace of tribulation
**“But not as silver”** — because you have not been purged
**“In the furnace of poverty”** — Purging by poverty your riches, giving them to enemies, or in Egypt, where it is shown that many are tempted by riches and by poverty.
48.11:
**“For my own sake, for my own sake”**
• my mercy
• I will deliver you not for your merits
**“I will do it, that I may not be blasphemed”** — among the nations, as one unable to deliver
**“And my glory”** — praise
**“To another”** — idol
**“I will not give”** — lest it seem to have oppressed the people of God
48.12:
**“Hearken to me, O Jacob”**
• carnal
• He still speaks to those to whom he had said: “Hear me, house of Jacob, who are called Israel in name, not in reality; for many are called, but few are chosen.” Therefore he calls them not chosen, because they had not yet received the Saviour, but calls them called.
**“And thou Israel”** — in name, not in reality
**“Whom I call”** — to penance and to salvation
**“I am he, I am the first”**
• living
• beginning
**“and I am the last”**
• end
• dead
• because I live, and I was dead
48.13:
**“My hand also”** — The Son; whence you made all things in wisdom
**“Hath founded the earth, and my right hand”** — The Son
**“Hath measured the heavens”** — the heavens, that they may lie open to my sight
**“I shall call them, and they shall stand together”** — before me
48.14:
**“Assemble yourselves together, all you”**
• the heavens, or all creatures, or the children of Israel
• Assemble yourselves. Why then does earth and ash glory, not knowing its own frailty?
**“and give ear”** — which I am about to say
**“Who among them”** — the heavens or creatures
**“Hath declared these things; the Lord hath loved him”** — Cyrus and Darius, because he sent away his people
**“He will do his pleasure in Babylon, and his arm shall be on the Chaldeans”** — because he will kill them
**“Hath declared these things”** — That Cyrus would destroy Babylon, or that my Son was to be born of a virgin.
**“The Lord hath loved him”** — These things properly pertain to Christ; yet they can be referred to Cyrus and Darius, up to the place where his way has been directed.
**“His pleasure”** — Because he will take it. Or the Son, who in redeeming the world also cast out the Chaldeans, that is, demons; whence the prince of this world will be cast out.
48.15:
**“I, even I have spoken”** — of Cyrus, through my prophets, or of the Son
**“And called him”** — by his own name, through Isaias, before he was born
**“Called him”** — Cyrus or the Son, through Gabriel saying: “and thou shalt call his name Jesus.”
**“I have brought him”** — that is, I sent the Son into the flesh
**“is made prosperous”** — from the east against Babylon
**“his way”** — His way: not of Cyrus, who was an idolater, but of Christ, who “did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth.”
48.16:
**“Come ye near unto me, and hear this”** — The Son to the Gentiles: “Come to me, all you that labour, and are burdened, and I will refresh you.”
**“I have not spoken in secret from the beginning”** — For many heard the things that I spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai.
**“from the time before it was done”** — the things that were done.
**“I was there”** — in the Father.
**“and now the Lord God”** — The Father.
**“hath sent me”**
• The Son.
• He determined to be incarnate.
**“and his spirit”** — was conceived of the Holy Spirit.
**“Hath sent me”** — He distinguishes the whole Trinity briefly, fully and openly.
48.17:
**“Thus saith the Lord”** — He addresses the apostles.
**“redeemer”** — by blood.
**“I am the Lord thy God”** — He who promises Israel the future. He gives the reason why he had first afflicted them.
**“that teach thee profitable things”** — the gospel.
**“that govern thee in the way”** — of preaching.
48.18:
**“O that”** — with the feeling of one wishing.
**“hadst hearkened”**
• in mind.
• O Israel, or the apostles.
**“my commandments”** — because thence.
**“had been as a river”** — abundant.
**“thy peace”** — in heaven.
**“and thy justice as the waves of the sea”** — a hyperbole, overflowing hither and thither.
48.19:
**“had been as the sand”** — innumerable.
**“thy seed”** — spiritual, apostolic.
**“And”** — the same.
**“the offspring of thy bowels”** — the offspring of my little sons, for whom I am in labour again until Christ be formed in you.
**“like the gravel thereof”** — of sand.
**“should not have perished”** — seed.
**“nor have been destroyed”** — they would always be true Israelites, or the Christian name; for from Christ all the sons of the apostles are Christians.
**“his name”** — Israel.
48.20:
**“Come forth”** — O Jews, from Babylon with Cyrus permitting it, or faithful from the world.
**“out of Babylon, flee ye from the Chaldeans”** — Without the body or the mind.
**“declare it with the voice of joy”** — O Jews, the liberation; or, O you apostles, the redemption of souls.
**“make this to be heard, and speak it out”** — By preaching.
**“speak it out even to the ends of the earth. Say”** — O Jews, or apostles.
**“The Lord hath redeemed”** — By the price of blood.
**“his servant Jacob”**
• Literally; or supplanters of vices.
• From Babylon, or from the world.
48.21:
**“They thirsted not”** — who went out of Babylon under Zorobabel and other leaders, who went out of Egypt, not only thirsted but murmured.
**“in the wilderness”** — of the world.
**“when he led them out”** — From Babylon, or from the world.
**“he brought forth water out of the rock for them”** — Literally, to those coming from Egypt.
**“and he clove”** — He permitted it to be cleft.
**“the rock”** — The side of Christ.
**“and the waters gushed out”**
• Of washing.
• They did not thirst, etc. Literally, for those coming from Egypt; but for those returning from the Babylonian captivity we do not read that this was fulfilled in fact, but it is to be taken hyperbolically, as many other things are; but for the apostles, by the grace of the Holy Spirit, it flowed forth from Christ.
• They did not thirst: faithful ones from the world, going out in mind, satisfied with the water of wisdom.
• “He clove the rock.” The rock was Christ. The divine word is divided into parts, so that what we cannot receive whole we may take in parts.
• “And the waters gushed out,” etc. One of the soldiers opened his side with a lance, and immediately there came out blood: that is our redemption; the water is the baptism, dedicating to us baptism and martyrdom.
48.22:
**“There is no peace, saith the Lord”** — Christ, who is our peace, who hath made both one.
**“to the wicked”** — To the unbelievers, who remained in error, who merited not to drink of the rock.

49.1:
**“Give ear, ye islands”**
• Of the Church, shaken on all sides by the waves of the world.
• After the calling of the remnant of Israel and the rejection of the unbelievers (of whom: “There is no peace to the wicked, saith the Lord”), under the name of islands he addresses, in the person of the son, the Church from the Gentiles.
**“and hearken, ye people from afar”** — From the ends of the earth.
**“The Lord hath called me from the womb”** — You shall call his name Jesus.
**“from the bowels of my mother”** — Before I was born.
**“he hath been mindful of my name”** — Through Gabriel, saying: You shall call his name Jesus.
49.2:
**“And he hath made my mouth”**
• that he may slay the wicked with the spirit of his mouth.
• the words of my mouth; whence “the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God.”
**“like a sharp sword”** — “I came not to send peace, but the sword,” namely separating the evil from the good.
**“in the shadow”** — by protection
**“of his hand”** — of the power of the divinity
**“he hath protected me”** — from all evil; so that the lowliness of the flesh might be covered by the power of the divinity; whence: “The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the most High shall overshadow thee.”
**“and hath made me as a chosen arrow”** — over others; for the prophets and apostles are arrows, arrows of the mighty one, sharp
**“in his quiver”** — in the flesh
**“he hath hidden me”**
• the divinity
• whence above: “Verily thou art a hidden God”
49.3:
**“And he said to me”** — obedient even unto death
**“thou art my servant, O Israel”** — of the stock of Israel according to the flesh
**“for in thee will I glory”** — The Father abiding in me does the works himself
**“will I glory”** — That this is not said of other servants. Father, I have glorified thy name; and elsewhere: “Arise, my glory,” etc.
49.4:
**“And I said”** — The Father
**“I said”** — As if to say: how have I glorified thee, who could not call the greater part of the Jews back to thee? Here, however, the free will of man is shown: for it is God’s to call, ours to believe, yet with him helping, so that we may obtain the reward of a righteous will.
**“in vain”** — as far as the unbelievers are concerned
**“I have laboured”** — by suffering
**“without cause and in vain”** — because it profited them not
**“I have spent my strength”** — by dying
**“therefore my judgment is with the Lord, and my work with my God”** — which I did for them
**“when”** — before
**“Judgment”** — The Father will judge whether I have done for them all that I ought. I have manifested thy name to the men whom thou hast given me; and elsewhere: I have glorified thee upon the earth.
**“my work”** — Another: my labour and my grief, because he wept over the city, and says in the Psalm: “What profit is there in my blood?” According to the Hebrew, hanging on the cross, far from my salvation are the words of my lamentation.
49.5:
**“And now saith the Lord”**
• The Father
• answers the Son, namely the one who asked: I have laboured in vain
**“that formed me from the womb to be his servant”** — because a servant is called one who is formed from the womb; whence: “From my mother’s womb thou art my God,” etc.
**“that I may bring back”** — through faith
**“O Jacob”** — wandering, the Creator forsaken, worshipping idols; whence: “I was not sent but to the sheep that are lost of the house of Israel.”
**“unto him, and Israel”** — yet
**“will not be gathered together”** — in the unity of faith
**“And I am glorified in the eyes of the Lord, and my God is made”** — according to the man
**“my strength”** — in the resurrection
**“glorified”** — As if I had lost the Jews, but I am glorified among the Gentiles. Whence: “All power is given to me in heaven and in earth.”
49.6:
**“And he said”** — comforting over the abjection of my people
**“It is a small thing”**
• to thee
• The Seventy: it is a great thing for thee to be called my servant
**“that thou shouldst be my servant to”**
• from the death of the soul
• only
**“the tribes of Jacob”** — who fell by their own fault
**“and to convert the dregs of Israel”** — despised
**“to convert”**
• to the faith
• and therefore
**“I have given”** — for them
**“thee”**
• O Isaias
• also
**“for a light of the Gentiles”** — that you may bring the enlightened Gentiles to the faith
**“that thou mayst be my salvation”** — of mine
49.7:
**“Thus saith the Lord”** — The Father
**“the redeemer of Israel”** — of the faithful
**“his Holy One”** — sanctifying
**“to the soul that is despised”** — “We saw him despised,” etc.
**“soul”** — Christ
**“to the nation that is abhorred, to the servant of rulers”**
• Christ, who before Pilate and Caiphas was judged as a servant
• Abominated. Christ and his Nazarenes, whom the Jews curse daily in their synagogues, because on account of them they lost kingdom, place and nation.
**“Kings shall see”** — according to the letter; or, whose heart is in the hand of God
**“KINGS SHALL SEE”** — The prophet to the Son. Kings will see you coming to judgment: that is, the kings, namely the apostles and the others who will judge with the Lord.
**“and princes shall rise up”** — in honour of you
**“princes”** — of the Church
**“and adore”**
• you
• when he shall come in the glory of his Father with the holy angels
• fulfilling your glorification and the salvation of the Gentiles
**“for the Lord's sake”** — the Father
**“because he is faithful, and for the Holy One of Israel, who hath chosen thee”** — unto the salvation of the world
49.8:
**“Thus saith the Lord”** — The Father to the Son
**“In an acceptable time”** — of grace; of which: “Behold, now is the acceptable time; behold, now is the day of salvation.”
**“IN AN ACCEPTABLE TIME”** — Of the passion and resurrection, in which it pleased God to redeem the human race.
**“I have heard thee”** — saying: “Father, glorify thy Son, that thy Son may glorify thee.”
**“and in the day of salvation”** — human
**“I have helped thee”**
• on the cross
• saying: “Why hast thou forsaken me?”
**“And I have preserved thee”**
• death overcome
• from death to life
**“and given thee to be a covenant”** — of friendship and charity
**“people”** — faithful
**“that thou mightest raise up”** — to the life of the soul
**“the earth”**
• of the Jews who were unwilling to believe
• earthly ones who lay in the errors of idolatry
**“and possess the inheritances”** — “Ask of me, and I will give thee the Gentiles.”
**“that were destroyed”** — through various errors
49.9:
**“that thou mightest say to them that are bound”** — with the cords of sins; for each man is bound with the cords of his own sins
**“Come forth: and to them that are in darkness”** — of unbelief and ignorance, who could not see the light
**“shew yourselves”**
• be enlightened
• and so
**“They shall feed in the ways”**
• converted, looking upon the light of Christ
• the teachings of the apostles and prophets
• “The Lord feeds me, and I shall want nothing,” etc.
**“and their pastures shall be in every plain”**
• shall be
• with the Scriptures opened
49.10:
**“They shall not hunger”** — the bread of the word
**“nor thirst”** — the water of wisdom
**“neither shall the heat nor the sun strike them”** — the adversities of the world will not harm; “The sun shall not burn thee by day: nor the moon by night.”
**“for he that is merciful to them”** — Christ, who redeemed in his mercy
**“shall be their shepherd, and at the fountains”** — Bless the Lord, from the fountains of Israel; and elsewhere: “You shall draw waters from the fountains of the Saviour.”
**“of waters”** — Of the Old and New Testament.
49.11:
**“And I will make”** — to them
**“all my mountains”** — the hindrances of the world, or the apostles, who are a way for others
**“a way”** — level
**“and my paths”** — walking along my paths
49.12:
**“Behold these”** — for whom the way is prepared
**“shall come from afar”**
• from the east
• to the faith, to the unity of the Church
**“and behold these”** — other faithful
**“from the north and from the sea”**
• from the west
• as if from all parts of the world
49.13:
**“give praise”** — The Lord, for the salvation of mankind
**“O ye heavens”** — O angels
**“and rejoice, O earth”** — inhabitants of the earth
**“give praise with jubilation”** — with immense joy of heart
**“the mountains”** — excelling in virtue
**“give praise: because the Lord hath comforted”** — through the Son
**“The Lord”** — the Father
**“his people”** — faithful, namely those of the Jews who believed
**“and will have mercy on his poor ones”**
• “Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.”
• of the Gentiles, who were without law and without God
• who, abandoned, were subject to demons
49.14:
**“And Sion said”** — the congregation of the saints
**“The Lord hath forsaken me”** — captive
**“and the Lord hath forgotten me”** — now for a long time
**“Sion said”** — Jerusalem and Sion are spoken of in four ways: the earthly one, of which: “Jerusalem, that killest the prophets.” The congregation of the just placed on earth, whence: “The Lord loveth the gates of Sion.” The multitude of the heavenly powers and of the saints already reigning with the Lord, whence: “that Jerusalem which is above is free: which is our mother.” And that which the Jews and our judaizers imagine to come down from heaven adorned, according to the Apocalypse of John. But it must be known that the congregation of the saints in the captivity of Babylon says this: God hath forsaken me.
49.15:
**“Can a woman forget her infant”** — the Lord’s answer, using a natural likeness
**“so as not to have pity on the son of her womb”** — not
**“And”** — yet
**“and if she should forget”**
• as though I were to say something more
• hardness of mind overcoming the laws of nature
**“I”** — creator
**“yet will not I forget thee”**
• creature
• I will always keep the souls of the saints in the midst of my heart
49.16:
**“Behold, I have graven thee in my hands”** — Septuagint: I have painted your walls upon my hands
**“I have graven thee”** — that I may always see and remember you, lest you think yourself utterly forsaken
**“thy walls”** — patriarchs and prophets, who fortify you by their prayers
**“are always before my eyes”** — Behold, I have graven thee in my hands, etc. From this we say that Jerusalem is not to be sought in the region of Palestine, which, the worst of the whole province and roughened by rocky mountains, suffers a lack of springs.
49.17:
**“Thy builders are come”** — scribes and Pharisees with their traditions
**“they that destroy thee and make thee waste”** — wicked teachers, by their own wicked examples, so that you follow the traditions of men and not the law of God
**“shall go out of thee”** — taken captive by the Romans
**“Builders”** — The apostles and others. The fault of the Jews, that is, of the scribes and Pharisees, is destroyed by the preaching of certain Jews, that is, the apostles; it is gathered together, both from Jews and from Gentiles.
49.18:
**“Lift up”** — lift up your eyes, and see the countries; for they are white already to harvest
**“thy eyes”** — O apostles, the early Church
**“and see all these are gathered together, they are come to thee: I live, saith the Lord”** — he makes them secure by swearing; that is, the oath of the Old Testament
**“thou shalt be clothed with all these”**
• you shall be adorned
• to the faithful, both Jews and Gentiles; happy is he who is so great that he is called the ornament of the Church
**“and as a bride thou shalt put them about thee”**
• the Church, which is the body of Christ; whence he speaks of them as one person, according to the first rule of Tyconius
• All these, etc. The Jews “out of every nation under heaven” on the day of Pentecost; for they had been scattered in the time of the Machabees by Antiochus Epiphanes. Of these three thousand believed on one day, and five thousand on another. The Gentiles also from all parts of the world are daily gathered to the faith of the Church.
**“with an ornament”** — The bride’s adornment with the various graces of the Holy Spirit, of which it is said: “The queen stood on thy right hand, in gilded clothing; surrounded with variety.”
49.19:
**“For thy deserts”** — of the unbelievers
**“and thy desolate places”** — without God
**“and the land of thy destruction shall now”** — when the gospel comes
**“be too narrow by reason of the inhabitants”** — because the faithful will come in
**“and they shall be chased far away”** — by the Romans
**“that”**
• Pharisees and scribes
• persecutors
**“swallowed thee up”** — they separated from God by false teaching and evil works
49.20:
**“shall still say in thy ears”** — O early Church
**“The children of thy barrenness”** — because you were barren for a long time
**“The place is too strait for me”** — in Judea, in the synagogues
**“make”** — more widely, lest I be hemmed in by the blasphemies of the Jews
49.21:
**“And thou shalt say in thy heart”** — marvelling, not able to utter with the mouth the greatness of your joy
**“Who hath begotten these?”** — sons
**“I”** — I was
**“was barren and brought not forth”**
• in the begetting of believers
• to God
**“led away, and captive”** — into Babylon
**“and these”**
• and these sons
• and these sons
**“who hath brought up these? I was destitute and alone”** — by God my husband
**“where were they?”**
• she marvels how she has begotten so quickly so many and such
• I was barren, etc. Because after Aggeus, Zacharias and Malachias, and Esdras, they had no prophets to nourish them in the law until John the Baptist.
49.22:
**“Thus saith the Lord God.”**
• The Father
• as if you did not wonder whence you have sons, etc. Behold, etc.
**“Behold I will lift up my hand to the Gentiles”**
• The Son
• I reveal him who will rise to rule the nations; the nations will hope
**“and will set up my standard to the people”**
• the cross
• on the banner of the cross
• how admirable is thy name in the whole earth!
**“and”** — Then
**“they shall bring thy sons”**
• the apostles, to faith; or angels, after death, to rest
• “My little children, of whom I am in labour again”
**“thy”** — O primitive Church
**“in their arms”** — in word and deed
49.23:
**“And kings shall be”**
• The apostles
• whose heart is in the hand of God; whence to Abraham: “Thou art a king with God among us”
**“thy nursing fathers”** — in the milk of the word
**“and queens thy nurses. With their face toward the earth”** — suppliants, with face to the earth
**“they shall worship thee”** — they will worship thee, O primitive Church, in thy head, which is Christ
**“Queens”** — The same, but more affectionately: “The queen stood on thy right hand, in gilded clothing; surrounded with variety”, that is, the one who daily nourishes Christ’s little ones and leads them to perfect age.
**“Shall worship”** — They shall reverence him, according to that: “Adore ye the footstool of his feet”; in which foot majesty is shown.
**“the dust of thy feet”** — That is, they will cleanse all earthliness by word and example, according to what is said: “whatsoever thou shalt loose upon earth, it shall be loosed”; whence: “shake off the dust from your feet.”
**“And thou shalt know”** — through all these things
**“For I am”** — not another
**“The Lord”** — the Trinity
**“upon which”** — upon me, that is
**“they shall not be confounded”** — in judgment
**“that wait for him”** — the faithful
49.24:
**“Art”** — through whichever of the saints
**“be taken from the strong”** — by the devil
**“the prey”**
• the human race
• When the strong armed man guards his court, then all that he possesses is in peace.
**“or”** — the same
**“that which was taken”** — the world is set in evil
**“be delivered from the mighty?”** — can it be saved from the strong? Who dares to say: “All these will I give thee, if falling down thou wilt adore me”
49.25:
**“For thus saith the Lord: Yea verily, even the captivity”** — the human race; “he led captivity captive”
**“For thus saith the Lord”** — Answering the question: because these things will be fulfilled at his coming.
**“from the strong”** — by the devil
**“shall be taken away, and that which was taken away”** — through the Son
**“from the mighty”** — by the devil
**“shall be delivered”** — by the blood of the Son
**“them”** — the demons
**“that have judged”** — unjustly
**“I will judge thee”**
• and in the present
• on the day of judgment
**“and thy children”** — in faith
**“I will save”** — from eternal death
49.26:
**“And I will feed”** — now and in the future
**“thy enemies”** — the contrary powers
**“with their own flesh”**
• the punishment of carnality, namely by their sins
• not by another’s death but their own
• Not by another’s death but by their own, so that those who are carnal (because they have lost the Spirit of the Lord) are filled with their own flesh. Whence: “Whilst the wicked draw near against me, to eat my flesh.” For it is not the Spirit, which is incorporeal, but the flesh that is eaten, lying open to the bites of fierce beasts.
**“and they shall be made drunk with their own blood, as with new wine”** — the punishment of the blood which they shed
**“And”** — and so
**“shall know”** — then
**“all flesh”** — who will see the salvation of God
**“that I am the Lord that save thee, and thy Redeemer”** — in the blood of the Son
**“the Mighty One of Jacob”**
• I who wrestled with Jacob, or was the helper of the strength of Jacob, so that, overcome in the passion, he might well say to those crucifying him, “Father, forgive them,” etc.
• I who gave Jacob strength to wrestle with the angel, by prayer (as they say), not by hands. For the angel who guarded him on his journey wished to depart to God. But he prevailed by prayer that he should bless him, and he heard. “If thou hast been strong against God,” that is, in prayer, “how much more shalt thou prevail against men?” As if to say: and by prayer you will prevail against Esau, whom you fear.

50.1:
**“Thus saith the Lord: What is this bill of the divorce of your mother”**
• as if you were to say, O Jews, that I cast off your mother; but she herself cast me off first
• Thus saith the Lord, etc. After the calling of the Gentiles, after the captivity of the strong one whose spoil was divided among the apostles, he speaks to the people of the Jews about Sion, of whom he said above: “The Lord hath forsaken me,” etc.
**“Wherewith I have put her away”** — as if no one
**“or”** — as if he were saying: you cannot show a bill of divorce; but perhaps you will say that I entrusted you to my creditor, having nothing else
**“who is my creditor, to whom I sold you”** — as though you had nothing else that I might give back
**“Behold you are sold for your iniquities”** — as if I did not sell you, but you yourselves
**“you are sold”**
• for lust, greed, and such things
• to the devil, who received souls on account of your sins
**“and for your wicked deeds”** — not by my fault
**“have I put your mother away”** — while she was committing fornication
**“You are sold”** — But I am carnal, sold under sin; whosoever commits sin is the servant of sin. Whence: “Let not sin reign in your mortal body.”
50.2:
**“Because I came”**
• in the flesh
• That is, so that you may know that I did not cast off your mother, but she withdrew by her own will. After many benefits I took on flesh, and no longer spoke through the prophets but spoke myself, in person.
**“and there was not a man”**
• man, when he was in honour, did not understand
• because all are like beasts
**“There was not a man”** — To Herod, on account of his malice, it was said: “Tell that fox.” And to the Pharisees: “Generation of vipers.” And of the lustful: horses raging after females. Of the voluptuous: “Cast not your pearls before swine.” Of the shameless: “Give not that which is holy to dogs.” Of all in common: the vision of four-footed beasts in the desert.
**“I called”**
• to repentance
• As to reasonable beings: “Incline your ear to the words of my mouth.” “He that thirsteth, let him come and drink,” and the like.
**“and there was none that would hear”** — calling
**“Is my hand shortened and become little”** — power
**“that I cannot redeem”**
• from the devil, as I freed from Egypt
• from the Babylonians
**“or is there no strength in me to deliver”** — my people, as formerly
**“Behold at my rebuke”** — by my command
**“a desert”** — with waters
**“I will make”** — if I will, as I made the Red Sea
**“the sea”**
• the world, that its bitterness may be dried up
• perverse teachings, of which the dragon said: “These rivers are mine, and I made them.”
**“and I will turn rivers”** — others, like the Arnon and the Jordan
**“into dry land”** — in its own dung
**“the fishes”**
• the curious
• as in the river of Egypt
**“for want of water”** — the grace of the Holy Spirit
**“and shall die”** — separated from the good little fishes
**“for thirst”**
• living waters
• as the rivers drying up in Egypt
• Is my hand shortened, etc. He inveighs against those who thought the Lord had not been able to free his people from captivity, setting down the reason and the plainest examples. As if to say: I who formerly did these things could now also free my people. Or: I who make heaven, earths and seas serve me, could I not escape the cross? According to that: “Thinkest thou that I cannot ask my Father, and he will give me presently more than twelve legions of angels?”
50.3:
**“I will clothe the heavens”**
• airy
• The philosophers say that clouds are lifted up on high not more than ten stadia from the earth, and the splendor of the sun is hidden; so with the light of heaven shut out, the lower air is darkened.
**“with darkness, and will make sackcloth their covering”** — for three days in Egypt he made darkness that could be felt, so that the sky seemed covered with sackcloth
**“I will clothe the heavens with darkness”** — Namely, the saints, so that sinners may know themselves. Whence the righteous man at first is his own accuser; and: “I will put sackcloth as their covering,” that they may do penance in ashes and haircloth.
50.4:
**“The Lord”** — the Father
**“hath given me”** — to man
**“a learned tongue”**
• knowledge and wisdom
• As if: I who once did such things, and can now do similar things, my power is not diminished.
**“The Lord hath given”** — although these can properly be referred to Isaias, yet they are referred to Christ.
**“that I should know how to uphold”** — the human race
**“him that is weary”** — into sin, into death
**“by word”** — of preaching
**“he wakeneth in the morning”** — as a master
**“in the morning he wakeneth”**
• from birth
• or from the beginning of preaching
**“my ear”** — of the mind
**“that I may hear him as a master”** — But I do not speak from myself
50.5:
**“The Lord God hath opened my ear”** — of understanding
**“and I do not resist”** — to his will
**“I have not gone back”** — withdrawing from him
50.6:
**“I have given my body”** — of my own accord
**“to the strikers”** — to the Jews or to the Roman soldiers
**“and my cheeks to them that plucked them”** — because they gave him slaps
**“I have not turned away my face from them that rebuked me, and spit upon me”** — all these things were fulfilled in the passion
50.7:
**“The Lord God”** — The Father
**“is my helper”** — in the passion
**“therefore am I not confounded”** — in the hope of the resurrection
**“Therefore have I set my face”** — to those who mock and strike
50.8:
**“He is near”** — ready to help
**“that justifieth me”** — saying: “This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased”
**“who will contend with me”** — as if I were not just
**“let us stand together”** — in judgment
**“who is my adversary”** — saying that I was rightly crucified
**“let him come near to me”** — that we may be judged together by comparison, not by authority, according to that: “Sodom thy sister is justified in comparison of thee”
50.9:
**“Behold the Lord God is my helper: who is he that shall condemn me?”** — no one, because
**“Lo, all”**
• adversaries
• because no one can be justified in the presence of the Lord
**“as a garment be destroyed”**
• by the Romans
• in hell
**“and the moth shall eat them up”** — the conscience of sins, or the zeal of the Gentiles
**“As a garment”** — A garment is consumed by age and by the moth. The Jews also, after the passion, were called to penance for forty-two years; at last, being negligent, they were crushed by the coming of the Romans, and devoured by the moth of an evil conscience.
50.10:
**“Who is there among you”** — to the unbelieving Jews
**“that feareth the Lord”**
• “the beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord”; but “perfect charity casteth out fear”
• as the Son the Father
**“that heareth”** — with the heart
**“the voice”** — Do penance, etc.
**“of his servant?”**
• Of the Son
• according to the flesh
**“that hath walked in darkness, and hath no light?”** — Christ cast out. Whence: “We have esteemed him, etc.” And there is no light of him: that is, glory among his own people, as he says: “A prophet is not without honour, save in his own country.”
**“let him hope”** — henceforth
**“in the name of the Lord”**
• not in idols
• so light of joy and gladness will come to him
• Christ, or the Gentile people
**“and lean upon his God.”**
• that human frailty may be sustained for a long time now by majesty
• Who is there among you, etc. He who fears is not perfect in charity, but here fear is put for goodness. Whence: blessed is he who fears all things, that is, who is God-fearing in the religion of God. Of this fear it is written: “The fear of the Lord” overcomes all things, and “the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom,” and elsewhere: “there is no want to them that fear him,” and “the fear of the Lord is holy, enduring for ever and ever.” This keeps the souls of the saints whole and chaste and pure. Whence: “Fear the Lord, and give glory to him.”
• Who is there that hath walked in darkness, and hath no light? The Gentile people in the darkness of unbelief, and there is no light for them: Christ, who says: “I am the light of the world.”
• As if you had scourged and spat upon me, yet I call you to penance. “For I desire not the death of a sinner.”
50.11:
**“Behold all you”**
• O Jews
• Behold, all of you, etc. As if exhortation profits nothing, and there is no hope of salvation after crimes. Whence: “They are all gone aside, they are become unprofitable together,” etc.
**“that kindle”** — against you
**“a fire”**
• of envy or tribulation
• with hay, wood, straw, thorns
**“encompassed with flames.”**
• with sins
• with tribulations. Whence in Proverbs: “Where there is much wood, the fire grows strong.”
**“walk”** — Ironically.
**“in the light of your fire”** — infernal
**“and in the flames”**
• in the tribulation of captivity which you have deserved
• of desolation and misery
**“which you have kindled.”**
• by sinning
• From this we learn that each one kindles a fire for himself according to the quality of his sin. And as in the same place or bed some are healthy and others feverish, feeling different torments from the diversity of their humours, so in sinners the matter of diverse sin is kindled more or less.
**“That kindle a fire”** — The fire of the city, which was set alight by the Romans. They kindled it when they blazed with the fire of jealousy and envy against Christ.
**“by my hand”** — by the power of Christ
**“this is done to you.”** — the evil, affliction
**“you shall sleep in sorrows.”** — of desolation, or of captivity, or of hell
**“In sorrows”** — Because they were willing to receive the Son of God neither by benefits nor by torments. Whence: “Depart from me, you cursed, into everlasting fire.”

51.1:
**“Give ear to me”**
• as if, because others are unwilling, you at least, O people, hear me
• in heart, others sleeping in sorrow
**“you that follow”**
• through faith
• imitate
**“that which is just”**
• Christ
• Others: judgment.
**“and you that seek”** — It signifies the apostles and apostolic men.
**“the Lord”** — Not earthly things.
**“look unto the rock”** — Abraham, firm in faith.
**“whence you are hewn”** — Born.
**“and to the hole”** — Sarah.
**“of the pit from which you are dug out”** — By the law of begetting.
51.2:
**“look unto Abraham your father”** — Christ, father of many nations.
**“and unto Sara who bore you”** — The Church, which before was barren.
**“For I called him alone”** — Only: “Go forth out of thy country, and from thy kindred.”
**“I called him and blessed him”** — In his works.
**“and multiplied him”** — In substance, to his sons.
51.3:
**“The Lord therefore will comfort”** — as I who once multiplied Abraham and comforted him, I can also multiply and comfort the Church.
**“Sion”** — And Sion: the Church.
**“will comfort”** — He will comfort: in the apostles.
**“all the ruins thereof”** — He will fill up the ruins of the Jews with the multitude of the Gentiles.
**“and he will make her desert as a place of pleasure”** — Which before was forsaken by God will be delightful when he dwells in it, bearing the flowers of virtue and the fruits of perfection.
**“and her wilderness as the garden of the Lord. Joy and gladness shall be found therein, thanksgiving”** — Thanksgiving for the benefits of God.
**“and the voice of praise”**
• And the voice of praise: of God.
• Joy, etc. Note that Sion, which is compared to the paradise of God, ought to have only joy and gladness and confession and the voice of praise, so that what they are going to do in heaven with the angels they may constantly practise on earth.
51.4:
**“hearken”** — Diligently.
**“unto me, O my people”**
• To me, my people: the apostles.
• The Gentiles or the remnant of Israel. Whence: “Rejoice, ye Gentiles, with his people.”
**“and give ear to me, O my tribes”** — Faithful.
**“give ear to me, for a law”** — Hear me, for the law of the gospel.
**“shall go forth from me, and my judgment”** — A decree, namely that while the Jews are unwilling to believe, the Gentiles are called to the faith.
**“to be a light of the nations”** — The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light.
51.5:
**“My just one is near at hand”**
• What was said above; but the Father says this of the Son.
• The Son will soon be born of a virgin, so that what I promise may be fulfilled.
**“He is come forth”** — Begotten of the Father without time.
**“is my saviour”** — who will save his people from their sins
**“and my arms”**
• power
• the apostles judging the twelve tribes of Israel
**“shall judge the people”** — on the last day
**“the islands shall look for me”** — the nations, or the Church, or the holy soul
**“shall look for”** — he himself will be the expectation of the nations
**“and my arm”** — the Son, through whom I made all
**“shall patiently wait”** — will patiently wait
**“My just one”** — Justifying all, or justice; elegantly, so that not one nation but the whole world is saved.
51.6:
**“lift ye up”** — O nations, or Church
**“your eyes to heaven”** — of the mind
**“and look down to the earth beneath: for the heavens”** — of the air
**“vanish like smoke”** — according to the figure, not according to the essence
**“and the earth shall be worn away like a garment”** — heaven and earth will pass away
**“and the inhabitants thereof”** — who will be found alive
**“shall perish in like manner”**
• From this we have that the rest will not be reduced to nothing but will be changed for the better
• according to the figure and to old age
**“but my salvation”** — The Son, of whom “Because my eyes have seen thy salvation,” and elsewhere “I will wait for thy salvation, O Lord”
**“shall be for ever, and”**
• therefore
• the same
**“my justice shall not fail”** — The heavens like smoke. It is said of the saints that we shall be changed; how much more then is it to be believed of the heaven, the sun and the stars? When the moon shall receive the light of the sun, and the sun shall shine with sevenfold brightness. Whence “every creature groaneth and travaileth in pain, even till now,” awaiting the deliverance of the sons of God, that is, that they may be changed for the better, not only the souls, which will be immortal, but also the bodies, whose substance will be made bright. Some, however, take “perish” and “grow old” for abolition and death.
51.7:
**“Hearken to me”**
• For a law shall go forth from me, etc.
• understand
**“you that know what is just”** — Christ, or the judgment by which you do all things discerningly
**“The people”** — faithful
**“my law”** — the gospel
**“in your heart”** — “The law of his God is in his heart,” etc.
**“and fear not”**
• O apostles
• Fear not those who kill the body: he exhorts them against persecutors, whom he foreknew would come.
• not in the mouth only
**“the reproach of men, and be not afraid of their blasphemies”** — or blasphemy
51.8:
**“as a garment”** — as though they will quickly pass away, and their reproach like a garment consumed by age and moth-eaten.
**“the worm shall eat them up”** — of conscience, which does not die.
**“and the moth shall consume them as wool”** — of an unjust mind.
**“but my salvation”** — Christ.
**“shall be for ever, and my justice from generation to generation”**
• for eternity.
• of the former people and of the later, who received his coming, of whom above: my justice is near.
51.9:
**“Arise”**
• from the throne of the Father’s glory.
• O Son.
• by redeeming the human race.
• from the throne of the Father’s glory.
**“arise”** — by redeeming the human race.
**“put on strength, O thou arm of the Lord”** — of the divinity, against the prince of the world.
**“as in the days of old”**
• by freeing from the Egyptians.
• and as.
**“in the ancient generations”**
• as you showed your power to our fathers.
• Arise, arise, etc. The voice of the prophet and of the faithful people, pleading for the coming of the Son, in whom help had been promised.
**“Hast not thou”** — O Son.
**“struck”** — with the Father.
**“the proud one”** — the devil.
**“wounded the dragon”** — Pharao or the devil.
51.10:
**“Hast not thou”** — O Son.
**“dried up”** — as one who has done these things, so also you will do this.
**“the sea”**
• Red.
• of this world.
**“the water”**
• philosophical teaching.
• doctrine.
**“of the mighty deep”** — of worldly depth.
**“who madest the depth”** — of which: “I am come into the depth of the sea, and a tempest hath overwhelmed me.”
**“of the sea”** — of this world.
**“a way, that the delivered might pass over”** — by the Egyptians.
51.11:
**“And now they that are redeemed”** — by the blood of the Son
**“by the Lord, shall return”** — to the way of righteousness
**“and shall come into Sion”** — the present Church, and to eternal blessedness
**“singing praises, and joy”** — “Blessed are they that dwell in thy house”
**“everlasting”** — which will not fail
**“upon their heads”** — minds
**“they shall obtain joy and gladness”** — in heaven
51.12:
**“I”**
• The Son: as if you had called upon me, and I will comfort you, etc.
• because no other can
**“I am the same”**
• not through the prophets but by myself
• God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes
**“will comfort you”** — God himself, the God of mercies and of consolation
**“who art thou, that thou shouldst be afraid”** — as if I had said: fear not the reproaches of men and their blasphemies; how then do you fear things that so quickly wither like grass?
**“of a mortal man, and of the son of man, who shall wither away like grass”** — Who art thou, etc. He rebukes the faithful that they not fear the threats or torments of princes, because all flesh is grass. He also rebukes those who fled in the passion and, terrified, denied, that they may blush and do penance.
51.13:
**“And thou hast forgotten”** — fearing man
**“the Lord thy maker”** — otherwise: maker
**“who stretched out the heavens”** — he hangs by incredible power
**“and founded the earth”** — by a stable mass
**“and thou hast been afraid continually all the day”**
• of the passion
• not for an hour; which is pardonable
**“at the presence of his fury who afflicted thee”** — in the body
**“had prepared himself”** — in the soul
**“to destroy thee: where is now the fury of the oppressor”** — as if what passes quickly is not to be feared
51.14:
**“quickly”** — The Son
**“shall come that is going”** — according to his humanity
**“to open”** — the heart of the proud, or hell
**“and shall not kill”** — sinners, but will call them to penance
**“unto utter destruction, neither shall his bread fail”**
• I am the living bread
• the bread: his body and blood; the teaching of the gospel
51.15:
**“But I am”** — The Father to the Son
**“the Lord thy God”** — according to the flesh
**“who trouble”** — I permit to be troubled
**“the sea”** — the world
**“and the waves thereof swell”** — against the elect and against the Son himself; whence the water will be moved, and the wonderful exaltations of the sea, wonderful in the heights, the Lord
51.16:
**“I have put”** — O Son
**“my words”** — wisdom and knowledge
**“in thy mouth”** — whatever the Son speaks are the words of the Father
**“and in the shadow of my hand”** — by the protection of the divinity
**“have protected thee”** — that he may not be made vile by sin; and the humanity united to the Word
**“that thou mightest plant”** — in faith
**“the heavens”** — new apostles, namely, and others
**“and found the earth”** — new
**“and mightest say to Sion”**
• the Church
• Sion, then, is nothing other than the people of God
51.17:
**“Arise, arise”** — from vices
**“Arise”**
• from the sleep of sin to repentance
• He exhorts to repentance those who in the passion denied, or who stood firm in faithfulness, crying out, Crucify, etc.
*Morally:* We can understand this, according to the anagogical sense, of the sinful soul, which, unwilling to drink the cup of the Lord’s wrath, says: “O Lord, rebuke me not in thy indignation,” etc. But if it has drunk, it is good for it to feel its punishments, and to hear God saying: when the heat of my wrath has passed I will heal again; and elsewhere: “Shall he that falleth not rise again?”
**“O Jerusalem, which hast drunk at the hand”** — by power
**“of the Lord the cup of his wrath”** — the devastation by the Romans
**“even to the bottom of the cup of dead sleep”** — of death
**“thou hast drunk”** — as if you will endure this captivity until the end of the world
**“even to the dregs”** — The cup of wrath, etc. Physicians are accustomed to give to a nauseated stomach a most bitter antidote, which has taken its name from the taste, that it may vomit up the harmful humours and be able to pass on to the belly the food cooked and digested, which the abundance of phlegm did not allow to be digested. Therefore Jerusalem also, who drank of the cup of the Lord’s wrath, is bidden to arise from her drunkenness, because she has drunk it all. For if she were still drinking, she would not arise; whence it is clear that this is said of the last captivity.
51.18:
**“There is none that can uphold her”** — as Moses, as Daniel, and other prophets who often upheld the Jews; but now they have neither prophet nor priest nor comforter
**“among all the children that she hath brought forth: and there is none that taketh her by the hand”** — as leader and teacher of good works
**“among all the children that she hath brought up”** — for the apostles too passed over to the Gentiles
51.19:
**“There are two things that have happened”** — he who, seeing the city, wept over it
**“thee”** — O Jerusalem
**“who shall be sorry for thee”** — as Jeremias, Daniel, and Jesus himself
**“desolation, and destruction, and the famine, and the sword”**
• that is, death
• he rendered two for four; but desolation is followed by destruction, famine by sword
**“who shall comfort thee”** — as if either no one or very few
51.20:
**“Thy children are cast forth”** — from their own land
**“at the head of all the ways, as the wild ox”**
• an unclean animal, not fit for sacrifice
• snared with the cords of sins
• Orix. The Septuagint: half-cooked beet
51.21:
**“Therefore”** — because you have no comforter
**“hear this, thou poor little one”** — not having spiritual riches
**“and thou that art drunk but not with wine”** — he has made me drunk with wormwood
51.22:
**“Thus saith thy Sovereign the Lord and thy God, who will fight”** — namely against the Egyptians and many others
**“for his people: Behold I have taken”** — I will take away, namely if you repent
**“out of thy hand the cup”** — the captivity of death
**“dead sleep, the dregs of the cup of my indignation, thou shalt not”** — if you do penance
**“drink it again any more”** — Behold I have taken. He foretold the captivity to come; now he exhorts to penance, that they may escape.
51.23:
**“And I will put”** — I will render them their recompense
**“it in the hand of them”** — of the persecuting demons
**“that have oppressed thee, and have said to thy soul”** — by suggesting
**“Bow down”** — from their natural dignity
**“that we may go over”**
• unless you subject yourself, the demons will not harm you
• over you
**“and thou hast laid thy body as the ground”** — to be trodden on by them
**“and as a way”** — which lies open to all
**“to them that went over”** — to those passing over: by demons
**“I will put it in the hand of them that have oppressed thee”** — According to the letter, the Chaldeans humbled them, and were themselves humbled by the Medes and Persians; and the Romans humbled them, and were themselves humbled in many things; the demons humbled them by persuading them to crucify Christ, and were themselves humbled in this, because they thus lost their power, and in the judgment they will be utterly humbled. Morally, however, the soul, while it sins, is subject to the devil as a captive; when it does penance it is raised up and rises, and the devil, humbled, falls.

52.1:
**“Arise, arise”**
• to the powers
• The prophet exhorts those who believed after the Ascension, when the apostles were preaching.
*Allegorically:* We can say the same also of the Church, which is the vision of peace and a watchtower: if she falls into heresy she is bidden to depart and take up again the ornaments of her former faith. And if her holiness has been raised up, the rewards of continence also are promised, that the uncircumcised or unclean shall not pass through her, which can be referred to works of uncleanness. For the uncircumcised and unclean are those who serve the pleasure and lust of the body.
**“put on thy strength”** — because you have fallen through weakness
**“Sion”** — Sion, the citadel and city of David; Jerusalem, the rest of the city
**“put on the garments of thy glory”** — with powers
**“Jerusalem”** — and so you will be
**“the city of the Holy One”** — of God, or of the temple
**“for henceforth shall no more”** — if you repent, if you keep my commandments
**“pass through thee”** — “what communion hath light with darkness? And what concord hath Christ with Belial?”
**“the uncircumcised”** — Spiritually.
**“And”** — That is.
**“Put on the garments”** — Morally. The soul also, if through penance it has received back its former strength, will be called the dwelling of the holy one, and so will become the temple of God; and the uncircumcised and unclean, of whom it is said: “If they shall have no dominion over me, then shall I be without spot,” will not pass through it. But all that is promised to Sion and Jerusalem is not said, as the Jews dream, of her stones and ashes, that they may be restored to their former state, but of the people of Jerusalem which killed the prophets, which, falling in the passion of Christ, was raised again in his resurrection, when many thousands of the Jews believed and the remnant were made safe.
**“For henceforth shall no more”** — This refers to the heavenly Jerusalem, which no unclean one enters.
52.2:
**“Shake thyself”** — turn aside from evil
**“from the dust”** — of sin
**“arise”** — do good
**“sit up, O Jerusalem”** — with a quiet mind
**“loose”** — captive
**“the bonds”** — sins
**“from off thy neck, O captive daughter of Sion”**
• for whom captivity now threatens
• Through effeminacy of mind, the people of the Jews to this day bears the yoke of Nabuchodonosor and is bound with the cords of sins.
• Shake thyself, etc. The soul defiled with filth loses its former brightness. But it shakes off the dust with the apostles, because it had received the image of the earthly, that it may bear the image of the heavenly. Of this dust it is said: “Shall dust confess to thee?” etc. The bonds of the neck are also loosed, that the iron sinew may not hear, your neck like a necklace, so that, freed from a heavy burden and receiving its former ornaments, it may cease to be a captive, redeemed by him who came to preach release to captives, not with corruptible silver and gold, but with the blood of the spotless lamb.
52.3:
**“For thus saith the Lord: You were sold gratis”** — of your own will
**“You were sold”** — to the devil
**“and you shall be redeemed without money”**
• not by any merit of yours but by the free gift of God’s kindness
• by the blood of the Son
• Gratis, etc. You gained no advantage, nor did you escape any harm, when you handed over the Son of God.
52.4:
**“For thus saith the Lord God: My people went down into Egypt”** — into the world, which is sorrow and darkness
**“went down”** — in the fathers
**“my people”** — the human race
**“at the beginning”** — in Adam
**“to sojourn there”** — as a stranger, because our homeland is paradise
**“there”** — in the land of Gessen
**“and the Assyrian”**
• the devil
• the Assyrians with Nabuchodonosor
**“without any cause at all”** — for Adam had done him no harm by which he might compel him to sin
**“hath oppressed them”**
• in the land of promise
• My people went down into Egypt. As if to say: the Egyptians wished to oppress my people with slavery, and seemed to have some reason for it, because they had relieved them in the need of famine. But I delivered them and brought them out through the desert into the land of promise. But what cause has the Assyrian to oppress them even in their own land and to slander them?
**“into Egypt”** — He rebukes the Jews and foretells what is to come: namely, that they went down of their own will to the Egyptians in time of famine, and afterwards were oppressed without cause by the Assyrians.
52.5:
**“And now what have I here, saith the Lord”** — as if: why should I stay longer in Judea, where there are so few believers? I shall pass over to the Gentiles, whence the faithful may pass from these seats.
**“for my people is taken away gratis”**
• from their land, or by living badly before God
• whence my people was taken away freely
**“They that rule over them”** — kings, princes, priests, through whose sins the people is often taken captive, both in body and in soul
**“his”** — of the people
**“treat them unjustly, saith the Lord, and continually all the day long”** — thrice daily they curse the Lord and his Nazarites
**“my name is blasphemed”** — in the synagogues or among the Gentiles, whence through you the name of the Lord is blasphemed among the Gentiles
52.6:
**“Therefore”** — because I am blasphemed by the Jews
**“my people shall know my name”** — the faithful, called Christians from Christ
**“in that day”**
• of the incarnation
• “Abraham your father rejoiced that he might see my day”
**“for I myself that spoke”** — formerly through the prophets
**“behold I am here”** — through myself
52.7:
**“How beautiful”**
• the prophet concerning the Son
• clean from the dust of sin
• Of him who had said above: “I myself who spoke, behold I am here”: the prophet bears witness that he himself preached the gospel upon the mountains.
**“upon the mountains”**
• holy ones
• of Judea, or the apostles, eminent in virtues
**“the feet”** — the apostles, whose feet the Lord washed
**“of him that bringeth good tidings”**
• of Christ, through the apostles, through himself
• the gospel, the grace of the Holy Spirit
• Of Christ, through himself and through the apostles, to whom he said: “Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you”; the Lord, sitting above them, preached; they themselves also are the feet of Christ, carrying his preaching.
**“and that preacheth peace”**
• to us
• to us through himself
**“peace”**
• with God and with the angels
• “peace to them that are afar off and to them that are near: for he is our peace, who hath made both one”
**“that preacheth”** — to us
**“salvation”**
• which he gave
• redemption and blessedness
**“that saith”** — O
**“to Sion: Thy God shall reign”** — the devil being conquered
**“Thy God”** — not sin
52.8:
**“The voice”** — A voice will be heard throughout the whole world
**“of thy watchmen”** — upon thy walls watchmen are appointed
**“they have lifted up their voice”**
• they themselves
• speaking loudly
• their sound went out into all the earth, in preaching
**“together”** — together: a heart that is discordant does not praise
**“shall praise”** — the Lord
**“for they shall see eye to eye”** — of the heart
**“eye to eye”**
• “My eyes are ever towards the Lord”
• face to face
**“shall see when the Lord shall convert”**
• to faith
• “When the Lord brought back the captivity of Sion, we became like men comforted”
**“the Lord Sion”** — the Church
**“The voice of thy watchmen”** — Of the apostles and of others who are on the watchtower, always so that they foresee all things and forewarn those under them.
52.9:
**“Rejoice”** — because restored
**“and give praise together, O ye deserts of Jerusalem”** — the remnant of the Jews, the apostles and others
**“for the Lord hath comforted”** — through the Holy Spirit, the multitude of the Gentiles coming in
**“his people”** — faithful
**“he hath redeemed Jerusalem”**
• by the blood of the Son
• the universal Church
• Rejoice and give praise, etc. He consoles the primitive Church over the multitude of the Gentiles, who, the Jews being blinded, entered in their place. But when the people had been led away by the Romans into captivity and the cities burned, either no inhabitant remained or few. But the Church, which was once in them, was both restored and multiplied by the multitude of the Gentiles; whence it is said to those who believed: rejoice, etc.
52.10:
**“The Lord hath prepared”** — made the Son to be incarnate, or to be preached everywhere
**“his holy arm in the sight”** — of hearts
**“of all the Gentiles, and”** — in heart, or even in body, at judgment
**“all ye ends of the earth”** — all the hinges of the world
**“the salvation of our God”** — the Son
**“His holy arm”** — “In my arm shall the Gentiles hope”; and elsewhere, “thy arm with power.”
52.11:
**“Depart, depart”** — O apostles, do not be entangled in their sins, or any saints
**“go ye out”** — from Jerusalem
**“from thence, touch no unclean thing”** — the Jews, by the death and blood of Christ
**“touch no unclean thing”** — “He that toucheth pitch, shall be defiled with it.”
**“go out of the midst of her”** — Jerusalem
**“be ye clean”**
• O apostles.
• from vices, from the company of blasphemers, to the destruction of whom the Roman army is readied.
**“you that carry the vessels of the Lord”**
• yourselves, in whom the Lord is, or the arms of righteousness.
• Depart, depart, etc. The Jews refer this to themselves, when with Cyrus permitting they returned to Jerusalem and brought back the vessels of the Lord which Nabuchodonosor had carried away. To them, as they say, cleanness is enjoined, that the holy vessels may be brought back by them, and it is foretold that they shall not go out in tumult or flight. But we better refer this to the apostles and the primitive Church; for before the Romans came, the apostles were divided among the nations, and other believers passed over into the kingdom of Agrippa, warned by the Holy Spirit.
**“Go ye out”** — Preaching the gospel in the world: “Going therefore, teach ye all nations.”
**“The vessels of the Lord”** — The temple of the Lord is holy, “which you are”: vessels, namely of gold or silver, whence Paul is called a vessel of election. Or the vessels of the Lord: the armour of God, the breastplate of justice, the shield of faith, the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of the Lord.
52.12:
**“For you shall not go out in a tumult”**
• with fear.
• as before out of Egypt, but in the peace of the king.
**“you shall go out”**
• for although they were slain, yet they came out victors.
• by the Jews.
• as the vanquished, but victors, subjecting every day many thousands of Jews to the faith.
**“neither shall you make haste by flight”** — to the Gentiles.
**“For the Lord will go before you”** — going to the Gentiles.
**“The Lord”** — leader and governor.
**“and the God of Israel will gather you together”** — from Jews and Gentiles, so that he makes “one fold”.
52.13:
**“Behold my servant shall understand”**
• my will.
• the word of God and the wisdom of God.
**“my servant”**
• the Son, obedient even unto death.
• therefore.
**“he shall be exalted, and extolled”**
• to the heavens, or through the preaching of the apostles.
• above all the heavens.
• to the right hand of the Father.
**“and shall be exceeding high”** — Behold, he shall understand. So that no one doubt who has said, “and I who spoke, behold, I am present”; and the Father teaches plainly what the arm of the Lord is.
52.14:
**“As many have been astonished”** — marveling at the miracles before the passion.
**“at thee”** — whence the greater miracles.
**“so shall his visage be inglorious among men”**
• in the passion.
• because spat upon, scourged, crucified, in truth when he was “beautiful above the sons of men”.
**“his visage, and his form”** — beauty without honor.
**“As many have been astonished at thee”** — The order of the history is not kept. For above the prophet was speaking in the person of the Father about the ascension of the Son, and suddenly returned to the passion.
52.15:
**“He shall sprinkle”**
• in baptism.
• he shall wash with his own blood, not as in the law with the blood of a lamb.
**“many nations”** — over their wisdom, the apostles preaching
**“kings shall shut their mouth”** — philosophers whose wisdom was overthrown by the preaching of the cross
**“for they to whom”**
• to the Gentiles
• By comparison with these, the hardness of the Jews is rebuked, of whom it is said: “By hearing you shall hear, and shall not understand.”
**“it was not told of him”** — by the prophets
**“have seen”**
• or: they have seen
• with the heart, and they will believe
**“and they that heard not”** — by him preaching in the flesh; of whom: “Blessed are they that have not seen, and have believed,” etc.
**“have beheld”** — by faith

53.1:
**“Who hath believed”**
• as if to say, how few of the Jews
• The prophet, in the person of the prophets, complains that few of the Jews believe what they hear from them about the coming of the Son.
**“our report”** — those things which he heard from us
**“and the arm of the Lord”**
• The Son, through whom the Father made all things
• The Father announced his Son as about to come, and before the scandal of the cross he sent ahead the glory of the one who rises. “He shall be exalted and extolled, etc.” The choir of prophets therefore answers that it has fulfilled its office and proclaimed the arm of the Lord.
**“to whom is revealed”**
• that he might believe, although he heard it from us
• by rising, ascending, and filling the world with faith
53.2:
**“And he shall grow up”** — “there shall come forth a rod out of the root of Jesse”
**“as a tender plant before him”** — pleasing in all things
**“and as a root out of a thirsty ground”**
• dry
• from the womb of the virgin, clean from male intercourse
**“there is no beauty in him, nor comeliness”** — in the opinion of the wicked
**“and we have seen him”** — we prophets with the eyes of the heart
**“and there was no sightliness”** — in his passion
**“that we should be desirous of him”** — to see long before
**“A tender plant”** — Symmachus: the branch signifying a man who came forth from the womb of a virgin.
**“a thirsty ground”** — Aquila: “untrodden,” where the privilege of virginity is shown, because he was created without seed from a land previously untrodden.
53.3:
**“Despised”** — by the Jews, hanging on the cross and for us accursed
**“and the most abject”** — most vile in opinion
**“of men”** — of all
**“a man of sorrows”** — the true man truly suffered
**“and acquainted”** — to suffer
**“with infirmity”** — taken up for us, which he overcame by his divinity
**“and his look was as it were hidden”**
• divinity hidden in the body
• Whence above: “Verily thou art a hidden God,” and we did not know.
**“and despised”** — By the Jews.
**“whereupon we esteemed him not”**
• the Son of God
• many of us, though afterwards to believe
53.4:
**“Surely”** — not in appearance but truly crucified, truly grieved; whence: “My soul is sorrowful even unto death.”
**“infirmities”** — sins
**“our”** — not his own
**“himself”** — not another
**“hath borne”** — from us
**“and carried our sorrows”** — not his own
**“he hath borne”** — in his body upon the tree
**“and we”** — and we, who sinned in ignorance but, repenting, believe; for Isaias speaks in their person.
**“we have thought him as it were a leper”** — a sinner
**“and as one struck by God”** — for his own sins
**“and afflicted”** — cast down for us, because he was crucified with robbers
53.5:
**“himself”** — We thought him a leper, but he
**“was wounded”** — “They have dug my hands and feet.”
**“for our iniquities”**
• not his own
• so that our wounds might be healed by his wound
**“was bruised”** — made accursed for us by scourges and blows
**“for our sins. The chastisement of our peace was upon him”** — “For he is our peace, who hath made both one.”
**“and by his bruises”** — of the rods
**“we are healed”** — from sin
**“By his bruises”** — It is clear that just as his body was torn and scourged, so his soul truly grieved for us, lest in Christ it be believed that part was truth and part falsehood.
53.6:
**“All we”**
• needy of mercy
• “For there is no distinction of the Jew and the Greek.”
**“like sheep have gone astray”**
• delivering him to death
• I went astray like a sheep, which, that is, is carried back on the shoulders of the loving shepherd.
**“every one hath turned aside into his own way”**
• wicked
• feeling different things about the crucified, each his own error.
**“hath turned aside”** — from Christ, who is the true way, crying out: Crucify him, etc.
**“And the Lord hath laid on him the iniquity”** — the punishment of all our iniquities or sins, which we could not bear; the God-man bore it.
53.7:
**“He was offered”** — a victim for us on the altar of the cross.
**“because it was his own will”** — No one compelled him. Whence: “I have power to lay it down: and I have power to take it up again.”
**“and he opened not his mouth. As a sheep”** — innocent, meek.
**“to the slaughter”** — “Christ our pasch is sacrificed.”
**“he shall be led and as a lamb”** — “who taketh away the sin of the world.”
**“before his shearer shall be dumb”** — not resisting; and when he was struck by the soldiers, he fell silent.
**“he opened not his mouth”** — To Pilate or to Herod. For he answered little, lest the salvation of the human race be delayed.
**“as a lamb”** — In whose figure the people of Israel ate the lamb in Egypt. This is the lamb “who taketh away the sin of the world,” who was “slain from the beginning of the world,” who feeds us with his own flesh and blood and clothes us with the fleece of protection.
53.8:
**“From distress”** — of the passion.
**“and from judgment”** — by an unjust judgment.
**“was taken away”** — in the resurrection, when all power in heaven and in earth was given to him.
**“from judgment”** — The judge of all found no truth in the judgment. But he was condemned without fault. Whence the prophet marvels that God of all gave himself over to the passion.
**“His generation”** — divine or human, which no one comprehends or discusses by human reason.
**“who shall declare”** — few or none.
**“That”**
• or: because.
• by the Jews.
**“is cut off”** — although he knew it by God’s inspiration.
**“out of the land of the living”**
• from the company of men; whence: “let us cut him off from the land of the living.”
• that he might live in heaven.
**“for the wickedness”** — to be wiped out.
**“of my people”** — peculiar.
**“have I struck him”** — by permission; whence: “I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock shall be dispersed.”
53.9:
**“And he shall give”** — to the Romans.
**“the ungodly”** — the Jews.
**“For the burial”** — because they persecuted him even to death, and made the sepulchre sure, sealing the stone and setting guards.
**“and the rich for his death”** — because they delivered him to death
**“because he hath done”** — was just in deed
**“no”** — which can be said of no other; for no one is clean from filth
**“neither was there deceit in his mouth”** — was true in word
**“He shall give the ungodly”** — That is, the Gentiles, who were without piety; because he died and was buried, he acquired them for God the Father; and the rich, namely the Jews, glorying in the riches of the law and the prophets.
**“the rich”** — The scribes and Pharisees, glorying in the riches of the teaching of the law.
53.10:
**“And”** — and therefore because
**“The Lord”** — The Father
**“was pleased to bruise”**
• to be bruised
• thus
**“him”**
• by grace alone
• I will strike the shepherd, etc.
**“in infirmity”** — of the flesh
**“if he shall lay down”** — The Son
**“his life”** — his life
**“for sin”** — our
**“he shall see a seed”** — the faithful reigning forever
**“long-lived and the will of the Lord”**
• of the Father
• the redemption of the human race
**“in his hand”** — by work
**“shall be prosperous”**
• will be fulfilled
• A long-lived seed. Namely the word of the Gospel, which does not grow old as the Old Testament does; whence: “The sower went out to sow his seed.”
**“And the will”** — That whatever the Father willed may be fulfilled by his powers; whence: “While I was with them, I kept them in thy name. Those whom thou gavest me have I kept.”
53.11:
**“Because”** — In preaching to the Jews, working miracles, and suffering, he found no rest among them; whence: “The foxes have holes, etc.” and elsewhere: laboring, enduring.
**“his soul hath laboured”** — in vain, because they would not be converted
**“he shall see”** — he will see churches in the whole world from the Gentiles
**“and be filled by his knowledge”** — by teaching
**“justify”** — not justified but justifying
**“this my just servant”**
• who did not commit sin
• The Son, taking the form of a servant
**“many”** — not all, because many are called, but few are chosen
**“and he shall bear their iniquities”** — the punishment of iniquities
**“himself”** — because they could not
**“shall bear”** — in his body upon the tree
**“He shall be filled”** — By the faith of the Gentiles, whence, hungry and thirsty beside the well of Jacob, he wished to use bought food, when he was already satisfied by the faith of the Samaritan woman and of those who came out of the city to him.
53.12:
**“Therefore”** — because he was made obedient to the Father even unto death
**“I will distribute to him very many”** — for the Jews who neglected, the faithful Gentiles: “Ask of me, and I will give thee the Gentiles for thy inheritance”
**“and of the strong”**
• of demons
• to the apostles, so that one should preside over the Jews, another over the Gentiles
**“he shall divide the spoils”** — the human race snatched from the devil
**“for”** — this will be done
**“because he hath delivered”**
• the Son
• willingly
**“his soul unto death”** — life
