**“he shall divide the spoils of the strong”** — Whence: “When the heavenly one,” or the Most High, divided the nations; and elsewhere: “The king of powers of the beloved”; and of Paul: “In the morning he shall eat the prey, and in the evening shall divide the spoil.”
**“and was reputed with the wicked”** — robbers
**“was reputed with the wicked”**
• by the Jews
• Whence: “I am counted among them that go down to the pit,” etc.
**“with the wicked”** — That he might redeem the wicked from sin, becoming all things to all. For he bore our sins in his body. Whose imitator Paul says: “I became all things to all men, that I might gain all.”
**“And he hath borne the sins of many”** — of the predestined
**“hath borne”** — he washed with blood
**“and hath prayed for the transgressors”** — the Jews, the persecutors
**“hath prayed”**
• or prayed
• Father, forgive them. At this voice, according to the Gospel of the Nazarenes, many thousands of the Jews standing about the cross believed.

54.1:
**“Give praise”** — your creator
**“O thou barren”** — the Church
**“that bearest not”** — because you will not bear
**“sing forth praise and make a joyful noise”** — with great joy, as a horse to victory
**“for many are the children of the desolate”**
• in opinion
• of the Church or of the Gentiles
**“more than”** — because she too bore the apostles, and through them many.
**“his”** — the synagogue, from which she was made empty, who bore seven times, on account of the mystery, namely of the sabbath, to which the former people was bound.
**“that hath”** — seemed to have.
**“a husband”** — God.
**“saith the Lord”**
• whose saying is doing.
• Give praise, O barren, etc. So far of the nativity, passion, and resurrection; now of the calling of the Gentiles and of the Jews. The barren Gentile world, which then bore no children to God because it had neither law nor prophets, now however begets more than the synagogue, which thinks that it has God as husband. Or the Church which was desolate among the Jews, which at the Lord’s coming did not bear children to him, that we may refer this to the Church gathered as much from the Jews as from the Gentiles.

**“will lay thy foundations with sapphires”** — Jerome. The Septuagint: I will give thee a carbuncle, etc. The carbuncle is the fiery word, which, the darkness of errors being put to flight, enlightens the hearts of believers. This is that by which the lips of Isaias are purged, and according to Genesis it is born in the land of Evilath. The sapphire has the likeness of heaven, signifying those who say with Socrates: I climb the air and look down on the sun, and with Paul: “our conversation is in heaven.” The jasper fortifies the bulwarks of those who can destroy every height that exalts itself against the knowledge of God and subject falsehood to truth. There are many kinds of jasper: one is like the emerald, which is found in the springs of Thermodon and is called amastisios, by which they think all phantoms are put to flight. Another is greener than the sea and tinted as if with flowers, which is found in Phrygia on Ida, in the deepest places, a mirror. Another is found near the Hiberians and Hyrcanians and the Caspian Sea, and especially the lake Neusis. Another is like snow and sea foam, reddish with a gently mingled colour. We have said these things so that we may recognize all the spiritual graces in the bulwarks of the Church, by which vain fears are put to flight; and he who has them says: “my cousin, the beloved, is white and ruddy.”

• The whole burnt offering is offered to God and burned. A part of the victim is given to the priests. He gives the holocaust to God who leaves the world, that he may always give himself to prayer. The victim is he who serves God and rightly orders the things that are of the world.
**“upon my altar”** — Faith, upon which all things are offered, or without which it is impossible to please God. Whence: “But my just man liveth by faith; but if he withdraw himself, he shall not please my soul.”
56.8:
**“saith the Lord God”** — promising this.
**“who gathereth”** — into one fold; whence, to gather together in one the children of God, that were dispersed.
**“the scattered of Israel”**

• to whom Peter writes, as to the elect strangers of the dispersion.
**“still”** — the scattered being gathered.
**“I will gather”** — I, the Father.
**“unto it”** — Christ.
**“his congregation”** — in predestination.
56.9:
**“All ye beasts”**
• the nations without reason.
• The voice of the prophet, who calls the Romans to the destruction of Jerusalem, whom almost the whole world served. Or by the beast the demons, to whom the Jews were handed over to be devoured.
**“of the field”** — of the world.
**“come”** — from afar.
**“to devour”**
• the Jew not believing in Christ.
• the heavenly bread, the flesh of the lamb.
**“all ye beasts”**
• non tradas b a con tibi
• uncultivated of the Gentiles
56.10:
**“His watchmen”** — scribes and Pharisees, priests, kings, princes; so also today in the Church
**“are all blind”** — if a blind man lead a blind man, both fall into the pit
**“they are all ignorant”**
• God, the true light
• Blind: not having Christ, the true light, or faith and the other virtues.
**“dumb dogs”** — without the voice of preaching, against enemies
**“not able to bark”**
• to preach
• because bound by vices
**“they that see”** — wise in evil
**“vain things, sleeping”** — in sins
**“and loving dreams”** — by which they were deceived by demons; all, as it were, cannot speak the truth but lies
56.11:
**“And most impudent dogs, they never had enough”** — of sinners; whence: “the dog is returned to his vomit”; and elsewhere: “who devour my people as they eat bread”
**“the shepherds themselves”** — who are also dogs
**“knew no understanding”** — of the law and the prophets; whence: “you err, not knowing the scriptures”
**“all have turned aside into their own way”**
• crooked
• not of God
**“have turned aside”** — all have turned aside together; they have become unprofitable
**“Every one”** — because they have turned aside from the way of the Lord
**“after his own gain”** — seeking what is their own, not what is of Jesus Christ
**“from the first”** — from the chief
**“even to the last”**
• to the people
• “from the sole of the foot to the top of the head there is no soundness in it”
**“Dogs”** — As dogs guard the flock, so prelates ought to guard the people.
**“Most impudent dogs”** — That is, as dogs without discernment often persecute even the good, so the Jews also shamelessly cried out, “Crucify, crucify him,” and were not sated even with the reproaches of the Lord.
56.12:
**“Come, let us take wine”** — let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we shall die
**“and be filled with drunkenness”** — or strong drink; for in Hebrew sicera is everything that can make drunk
**“and it shall be as today, so also tomorrow”** — whence above: “they knew not satiety”
**“Come, let us take”** — Thus did those pervert who ought to have corrected. And because all have sinned, they were handed over into the hands of the Romans. Whence above: “They knew not satiety.”
*Morally:* Let us shun the examples of the wicked, nor be made drunk with wine, in which is luxury, nor be overwhelmed by pleasures, nor be silent against adversaries.

57.1:
**“The just”**
• because
• Christ
**“perisheth”**
• dies
• by the opinion of unbelievers, or by the immensity of torments
**“and no man”** — of the reprobate Jews
**“layeth it to heart”**
• because the blind, not knowing wisdom, do not think on the things that are of God
• that he was tormented for us, not for himself
**“and men of mercy”** — the apostles, sent to us by the mercy of God
**“are taken away”** — they pass from the world to the Lord through torments
**“because there is none that understandeth”** — that they suffer unjustly and therefore are crowned justly
**“from before the face of evil”** — from the presence of sin; or because he bore our sins in his body upon the tree, that we, being dead to sins, should live to justice
**“is taken away”** — is taken away, that is, so that he may not see the evils of the world
**“just man”**
• Christ
• at the right hand of the Father
• The just perisheth, etc. The Jews refer this to Isaias, who was sawn in two with a wooden saw by Manasses, a most impious king; and the other prophets whom he killed they call men of mercy. But more truly it is said here of him who is supremely just, of whom: “Have nothing to do with that just man”; and Pilate: “What shall I do with Jesus, who is called the just?”
• And no man layeth it to heart, etc. Because of the blind watchmen and the dumb dogs, no man: because the blind and dumb, not knowing wisdom, do not think on the things that are of God.
57.2:
**“Let peace come”**
• of Christ
• to the Gentiles through the apostles, to whom it was said: “Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you”
• Let peace come. The prophet prays that Christ may come, and rising from the dead may rest in his bed, namely in the glory of the Father’s majesty, or in the Church, in which he walked in uprightness, because he committed no sin, and “neither was guile found in his mouth.”
**“let him rest in his bed”** — with eternal blessedness
**“that hath walked in his uprightness”** — returning to the Father by the straight path
57.3:
**“But you”** — the just man being taken away
**“Come near”** — Draw near: hear my words.
**“hither, you sons of the sorceress”** — of the Jewish people, who both worshipped idols and observed auguries
**“the seed of the adulterer”** — who committed adultery with wood and stone
**“and of the harlot”** — who, having abandoned God, clings to the devil
57.4:
**“Upon whom”**
• except upon me
• The voice of the Son. Upon whom have you jested, as if upon me only, saying: “Prophesy, who is it that struck thee?”
**“have you jested”**
• in the passion
• by spitting on his face and plucking his beard
**“Upon whom have you opened your mouth wide”**
• in crying out: Crucify him, crucify him
• Whence: they set their mouth in heaven.
**“and put out your tongue”** — that thou art a Samaritan, and hast a devil
**“are not you wicked children”** — as if you had made yourselves so, who are wicked sons
**“a false seed”**
• you are of your father the devil
• sons of the devil, who is the father of lies, whence he is a liar and the father thereof
**“are not you”** — Tropologically. These things can be read of heretics, who are wicked children, a lying seed, the seed of the devil, who is the father of lies; who take comfort in the idols of their sect under a leafy tree, namely their pleasures. As Adam after sin hid himself under a tree, lest he lie open to the sight of God. These sacrifice the children whom they have deceived in the valleys. These are in the pit of impiety, beneath overhanging rocks that always threaten ruin. Because of the diversity of falsehood and the variety of perverse doctrines, these are called many rocks. But we have one rock, which always follows the people of God, of which the people of Israel drank when they enjoyed the familiarity of the Lord.
57.5:
**“Who seek your comfort in idols”** — strange
**“under every green tree, sacrificing”** — gods
**“the children”**
• innocent
• they sacrificed their sons and their daughters to devils
**“in the torrents, under the high rocks”** — or: overhanging
57.6:
**“In the parts of the torrent”** — as if, leaving the house of God, you sacrificed beside the torrents
**“thy portion”** — O Jerusalem
**“this is thy lot”** — the worship of idols
**“to them”** — to the gods
**“thou hast poured out”** — you sacrificed
**“thou hast offered sacrifice. Shall I not be angry at these things?”** — over these, your sins
**“Shall I not be angry”**
• by punishing
• as if I should justly be angry because
**“libations”** — Wine, oil, and such liquids. Sacrifice of bread, victim, and such.
57.7:
**“Upon a high and lofty mountain thou hast laid thy bed”**
• that you might worship idols and fulfil lust
• this in the time of Isaias, especially under King Achaz
**“and hast gone up thither to offer victims”** — Upon a high and lofty mountain, etc. Heretics also, who are lifted up in pride, who, having despised the humility of the Church, promise themselves lofty things, climb the mountains of their doctrines and there prostitute their bed to demons. And because they have turned backward, imitating Lot’s wife, they are changed into a statue of salt, having the image of the Church’s seasoning and not having the savour, and are cast out to be trodden underfoot by men.
57.8:
**“And behind the door”**
• an image of the guardian, for the protection of houses
• As if you had not only worshipped idols on the mountains but had set them behind the door, so that as you went in and out you might see them and always worship.
**“and”** — that is
**“behind the post thou hast set up thy remembrance”** — an idol to be kept in memory
**“for”** — also
**“thou hast discovered thyself near me”** — yourself
**“For thou hast discovered thyself near me”** — A metaphor of an adulteress, as above of a harlot: as if, her husband sleeping, she secretly receives an adulterer and uncovers her cloak, enlarges the bed, and makes a covenant, like an instrument of dowry. In which he signifies that he even set up in the temple the idol of Baal; as he had also accused the harlot that at the entrance of houses and in dark places, behind the door, she was prostituted, exposed to all who entered.
**“and hast received an adulterer”** — the devil
**“thou hast enlarged”** — that you might receive
**“thy bed, and made a covenant with them”** — so that you would not return to me
**“thou hast loved”** — covetous and unclean
**“bed”** — adultery
**“Their”** — of adulterers
**“Thou hast set up”** — by deed
**“discovered”** — without shame, so that you would not hide your shame
57.9:
**“And thou hast adorned thyself for the king with ointment”**
• devilish; for the devil is king over all the sons of pride
• the idol of the Moabites: Moloch or Melon is interpreted king, to whom Jerusalem adorned herself
**“and hast multiplied thy perfumes”** — as if you sought vain ornaments, so that by sight and smell you might provoke adulterers
**“Thou hast sent”** — moreover
**“thy messengers far off, and”** — therefore
**“wast debased”** — from the height of chastity into the pit of lust
**“Thou hast sent thy messengers”** — That they might bring distant idols, as if nearby ones did not suffice. And in this he signifies the gods of the Babylonians and Egyptians.
57.10:
**“in the multitude of thy ways”** — of wicked conduct
**“Thou hast been wearied”** — by turning aside to the right or to the left
**“yet thou saidst not: I will rest”**
• by repenting
• from evil work
**“life”**
• Otherwise: way.
• abundance of riches
**“thou hast found life of thy hand, therefore thou hast not asked”**
• with the heart, and if not with the mouth
• me
**“In the multitude”** — He who walks the royal way does not labor. There is one way of truth; he who says, “I am the way, and the truth, and the life.” The many ways of worldly men. Whence: “my ways are not your ways.”
57.11:
**“For whom hast thou been solicitous and afraid”**
• for guarding riches
• because, trusting in riches, you were unwilling to ask me; therefore you feared greatly
• enemies or gods from whom you thought you had them
**“that thou hast lied”** — because you lied, saying, “We will do all that God has spoken.”
**“and hast not been mindful of me”**
• saying, “Honor the Lord, and you will be strengthened”
• in your gladness
**“nor thought on me in thy heart”** — that is, this
**“for I am silent”**
• I being silent, as if pretending; and if not for fear, at least you would return for my penance
• not always, only for an hour. Whence: “I have been silent; shall I be silent forever?”
**“and as one that seeth not”** — thy sins
57.12:
**“I”** — who have been silent for a long time
**“will declare”** — to all
**“thy justice”**
• ironically
• at last delivering thee to the Chaldeans, the Romans, or to judgment
**“and thy works”**
• idols
• which thou didst against me in the time of the passion
**“shall not profit thee”** — in judgment
57.13:
**“When thou shalt cry”** — to me in the time of captivity or in the day of judgment
**“let deliver thee”** — from danger
**“thy companies”** — gods acquired from diverse nations
**“and all of them”** — gods
**“shall carry off”** — in the time of captivity
**“the wind”** — the assault of enemies
**“a breeze shall take them away”** — it is the same
**“but he that putteth his trust in me”** — in the Lord Jesus Christ
**“shall inherit the land”** — of the living
**“and shall possess my holy mount”**
• Christ
• the heavenly Jerusalem or the holy scriptures
• But he that putteth his trust, etc. Allegorically. Those who truly trust in him will inherit the land of the living, according to that: “I believe to see the good things of the Lord in the land of the living.” They will possess my holy mount, and the law of the old and new testament, for each was given on a mountain, and it invites to the height of the first; or Christ, of whom: “Come, let us go up to the mountain of the Lord,” etc.
**“But he that”** — But he that putteth his trust in me. Those who did not worship idols, or who, led into captivity, repented, and returned under Zorobabel and other leaders, and worshipped their Lord in his place, according to the Hebrews.
57.14:
**“And I will say”**
• to Cyrus and his princes
• I will say. I, namely Christ, to the apostles. Make a way, as it were a journey, by preaching well; give it, that is, as an example to them by doing good; take away the stumbling-blocks by washing away sins through baptism, removing the worship of idols by preaching.
**“Make a way”** — give to my people leave to return home
**“give free passage”** — teachers
**“turn out of the path”** — that you do not hinder their path
**“take away the stumblingblocks out of the way of my people”** — dissolve by your interpretation all things that are harmful, or whatever seem difficult
57.15:
**“For thus saith the High”** — the Lord above all nations, not by place but by the merit of those in whom he dwells. Whence: I will extol thee, O Lord, for thou hast upheld me
**“and the Eminent that inhabiteth eternity”** — without end, without beginning
**“and his name is Holy”**
• let thy name be sanctified
• the Son, or any other thing, through faith and love
**“on high”** — heaven, or the heavenly ones
**“who dwelleth in the holy place, and with”** — dwells
**“with a contrite and humble spirit”** — a contrite and humbled heart, O God, thou wilt not despise
**“to revive the spirit of the humble”** — by the forgiveness of sins and the increase of virtues
**“and to revive the heart of the contrite”** — that by consolation they may pass from the sorrow of the world to joy, from death to life
**“For thus saith”** — With the rebuke against Jerusalem finished, he comes to those who trust in the Lord, whose return he had ordered to be prepared. Whence he also begins with the praises of God, and consequently shows what he promised to the returning people.
57.16:
**“For I will not contend for ever”**
• I, the high Father, sublime
• I will not keep my wrath for ever, nor will I contend with my creature, but I will strike in the present so that I may heal in the future.
**“neither will I be angry unto the end”** — as if to say: I will not always pour out wrath and vengeance upon them
**“because the spirit”** — the holy spirit
**“shall go forth from my face, and breathings”** — souls; whence he breathed into his face the breath of life
**“I will make”**
• I will make, or I make
• For the spirit, etc. Peace, joy, the life of all, who gives sense and understanding. As if: I both give the life-giving spirit and create the soul; it is unworthy that they perish eternally. These things, however, are referred generally to all the faithful who are chastised in the present by the Lord, specially to the Jews.
57.17:
**“For the iniquity of his covetousness”**
• of the Jewish people
• because, namely, he coveted iniquity, not content with one
**“I was angry, and I struck him”**
• for a short time, that I might heal
• through the Assyrians, through the Chaldeans, and at last through the Romans
**“I hid my face from thee”**
• O Juda
• Namely, my help, so that you might desire it the more, saying: “Show thy face, and we shall be saved.”
**“and was angry”** — against you, on account of idolatry and for the death of my Son
**“and he went away”** — that he might repent not in the face of men but in his heart
**“wandering”** — out of his mind, like Cain, to whom it was said: Thou shalt be a vagabond and a fugitive
**“in his own heart”** — by a wicked deed
**“He went away”** — Which someone understanding says: “I walked sad all the day long.”
57.18:
**“ways”**
• ways of conversion
• good works
**“his”** — of the Jewish people
**“I saw, and let him go”** — whom I had wounded
**“and brought him back”**
• whom I had cast out
• to the homeland
• to penance
• from captivity; while in captivity he wept over his sins
**“and restored comforts”**
• true ones; for many are false
• their own inheritance
**“they”** — to the people or to the princes
**“and to them that mourn”** — to the subjects
**“His ways”** — Allegorically. He sees the good actions of the believing people and gives back the consolation of the Holy Spirit, who is called the Paraclete, that is, the comforter, which Adam lost through disobedience, and restores it to penitents and to those who mourn their sins.
57.19:
**“I created the fruit of the lips”**
• I prefer the penitence of the sinner to his death
• I created the fruit of the lips. Allegorically: what I foretold of the Son through the prophets I have fulfilled, making through him peace for the Jews, who are near through the law, and for the Gentiles, who are far from God because they are without the law; and I healed him of sin, namely both peoples.
**“I created”** — As it were, the deliverance from captivity, which I promised through Jeremias after seventy years, I have fulfilled in deed.
**“peace”** — this is his promise: “Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you”
**“peace to him”** — peace to him, namely
**“that is far off”** — who is far off: his own land
**“and to him that is near”** — and to him who is near: not to one nation only but to the whole world
**“said the Lord, and I healed him”**
• said the Lord; and I healed him
• the penitent
57.20:
**“But the wicked”**
• The Jews, crying out: he is guilty of death
• Above he spoke of those who did penance in captivity and for that reason were freed, and of those who believed after the ascension. Here he speaks specifically of those who remained in their unbelief; whence: “To you it behoved us first to speak the word of God,” etc.
**“like the raging sea”** — always troubled, angry
**“which cannot rest”** — because they said: “His blood be upon us and upon our children.”
**“and the waves thereof cast up”** — against the Christians
**“the waves”** — persecutions
**“his”** — of the sea
**“for trampling”**
• by demons
• they will be trampled, namely, like mud by the Romans who are approaching
**“and mire”** — of sin
57.21:
**“There is no peace”** — Christ
**“saith the Lord God to the wicked”** — the wicked walk round about

58.1:
**“Cry”**
• you, however
• openly, with fear cast aside, announce the captivity now at hand and the slaughter of many by the approaching Romans
**“cease not”** — from preaching
**“like a trumpet, lift up thy voice”** — that you may be heard by all
**“and shew my people”** — as if it can still repent
**“their wicked doings”**
• greater
• detestable: idolatry, homicide and the like
**“their, and the house of Jacob their sins”** — lesser
**“Cry, cease not”** — The Lord to the prophets, or to the apostles, the former chapter being finished, namely, in which peace to the just and no rest to the wicked is announced.
**“their”** — As a trumpet, etc. Where it is said to the apostles, “Get thee up upon a high mountain, thou that bringest good tidings to Sion,” neither horn nor trumpet is taken up, but he is bidden to climb the mountain and sound forth with his own voice. But here, because they are sinners and below, to whom the message is to be brought, the prophet is not bidden to go up into the mountain, but only to lift up his voice like a trumpet and to announce wars to come; that as the dead are to be made alive at the voice of the trumpet (whence: “the trumpet shall sound, and the dead shall rise again”), so Israel, dead in sin, may hear its crimes.
**“my people”** — As if he said: let them see what kind of Father they have lost, who calls even sinners his people.
58.2:
**“For they seek me from day to day”**
• in word, though not in heart, by gathering at the temple and the synagogue, reading the law of God
• daily
**“and desire to know my ways”** — actions, wills
**“desire”** — not truly
**“as a nation that hath done justice”** — because he did not worship idols
**“and hath not forsaken the judgment of their God”**
• Christ, who justifies all; the same judgment, since the Father judges no one
• the law, or the true faith, by which the just lives
**“they ask of me”** — that is, that I should do it
**“the judgments of justice: they are willing to approach to God”**
• in voice; whence: “This people honoureth me with their lips: but their heart is far from me.”
• in voice only
• to whom one draws near not by place but by merit
• as if therefore I will not hear
**“As”** — This is why I will not hear them as I hear those who in the Church do justice, living justly and piously, confessing Christ, true God and true man.
**“They ask”** — Another rashness of the Jews, who as if trusting in a good conscience demand a just judgment, according to that: “Judge me, O Lord, for I have walked in my innocence.”
58.3:
**“Why”** — They accuse God of injustice, as if he does not regard good works
**“have we fasted”** — They think the hunger of the belly is virtue; whence: I fast twice on the sabbath.
**“and thou hast not regarded”** — as pleasing
**“have we humbled”** — afflicted by fasting
**“our souls”** — animal life
**“and thou hast not taken notice”** — did not please you
**“Why have we fasted”** — They have forgotten the old history, since the Lord did not regard the gifts of Cain, because he did not divide rightly with his brother, to whom he envied God’s love.
**“Behold”** — the answer
**“in the day of your fast”**
• not mine
• as if not from hearing, because you fast without mercy and for praise and for vain glory
**“your own will is found”**
• not of God
• fleshly
• I do not despise fasts, but the things that hinder fasts
• or the will in foods, namely the more luxurious ones
• Gregory. The will pertains to justice, the pledge to anger. In vain is the body worn down by penance if the mind is scattered by vices in its ordered movements.
**“and your debtors”** — therefore perhaps they often fasted so that they might be free for demanding back their debts
**“you exact”**
• with strife
• He who demands repayment from one who does not have it does violence to God.
**“Behold in the day of your fast”** — Fasting is acceptable to God when one abstains not only from foods but from all unlawful things.
58.4:
**“Behold”** — because
**“for debates”** — against debtors
**“and strife”** — the inner man is not known; by the flesh of the dragon, which was given as food to the peoples of Ethiopia
**“you fast”** — outwardly
**“and strike”** — resisting
**“with the fist wickedly”**
• which is worse
• demanding even what you have not lent
**“Do not fast”** — as if you wish me to hear you
**“as you have done until this day”**
• without mercy
• for the praise of men, that it may be heard while you pray in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that you may be seen by men
**“to make your cry to be heard on high”**
• Enter into your chamber, and having shut the door, pray to your Father.
• Lest it seem that he reproves fasting, he teaches how fasting ought to be done.
58.5:
**“Is this such a fast”** — such as you do
**“as I have chosen for a day”** — whole
**“for a man to afflict his soul”**
• not to amend
• by abstaining from foods, not from unlawful things
**“wilt thou call”**
• outwardly only
• bowing to the feet or in a circle, as monks do
**“to wind his head about like a circle”** — these are good and acceptable to God if they are done with a pure heart
**“and sackcloth”** — to put on
**“and to spread ashes”** — otherwise you will call
**“a fast”** — acceptable to God
**“and a day acceptable to the Lord”** — No, but this is rather
58.6:
**“Is not this rather the fast that I have chosen”** — What fast he rejects is shown, and what fast he approves is shown.
**“loose the bands”** — false bonds, by which the poor were said to be bound
**“of wickedness”**
• he does not forbid reclaiming what is one’s own
• that is
**“loose”** — without dispute
**“the bundles that oppress”**
• of the bonds
• false bonds by which usurers oppressed the innocent
**“let them that are broken go free”**
• by hunger or long servitude; for sometimes they held them beyond the term
• by which, for hunger, they sold themselves, which they often did
**“free”** — from servitude
**“and break asunder every burden”** — of servitude or of sin
**“Bands”** — We understand sins, which on the day of fasting we are ordered to forgive our neighbours, so that God may forgive us, and that we may confidently say: And forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors.
**“Septuagint”** — More openly: tear up every unjust writing, that is, the false bonds by which the poor were often wickedly oppressed. For if it is wicked to demand a debt from those who cannot repay, much more is it so from those who do not owe.
**“Tropologically”** — Whoever fasts from all evils and wishes his fast to be regarded, let him not only turn aside from evil but also do good, that he may loose the bands of wickedness by which the simple are bound in the jaws of heretics. Whence: “But such as turn aside into bonds, the Lord shall lead out with the workers of iniquity.” Such as are broken, the man of the Church ought to let go, and to undo every writing of the heretics. Whence the prophet: Woe to them that write iniquity, etc. Let him also break the bread of doctrine to the hungry; for the Lord gave broken loaves to the apostles, which in the gospel he left to them crushed and broken up in the seven baskets and the twelve baskets, not whole as they were in the law, that they might have something to give to the poor. Those who have not the warmth of faith and are chilled outside the Church by the cold of unbelief, needy and strangers, let him bring into the house of the Church and cover with the cloak of incorruption, that being then clothed by Christ they may not remain in the sepulchres; which we read of him who, possessed by a legion of demons, dwelt naked among the tombs of the dead. And when he has done this, he will not despise his own flesh, that is, spiritually, the household of the faith; which the Seventy said: “Despise not the household of thy seed.”
58.7:
**“Deal thy bread to the hungry”**
• as if someone should say: I have no debtors; what shall I do so that my fast may be accepted? “Deal thy bread to the hungry.”
• We break bread to the hungry when we make known to others the faith of Christ, who is the living bread, and the holy Scripture, which is spiritual food for us.
**“thy”**
• your own, not another’s
• If you cannot give all, or so that it may benefit many: “he hath distributed, he hath given to the poor.” What you were going to eat if you were not fasting, give to the poor, so that your fast may not be a gain for the purse but a satisfying of the soul.
**“and”** — lest you plead poverty as an excuse
**“the needy”** — from whom you do not expect reward
**“and the harbourless”**
• hospitable to one another
• we bring the needy and wanderers into the house when we call back those at odds into brotherly peace and the unity of charity
**“bring into thy house”**
• hired, if you do not have your own
• provide shelter; receive heaven, if you cannot provide bread
**“when thou shalt see one naked”** — by faith, virtues and works
**“cover him”** — by word and example
**“and despise not thy own flesh”** — a sinner like yourself
**“despise not”** — considering yourself, lest you too, etc.
**“and thy own flesh”** — Recognize your neighbour in any necessity as like yourself, considering that you are mortal and subject to suffering. Whence: “visiting thy beauty thou shalt not sin.”
58.8:
**“Then shall break forth”** — when you have done these things
**“as the morning, thy light”** — Christ
**“Thy light”** — As the morning light dispels the darkness, so the light of truth drives away errors.
**“and thy health”** — forgiveness of all sins
**“shall speedily arise”**
• as the sun in the morning
• whence: to those who fear my name the sun of justice will rise
**“shall go before thy face”** — to the presence of the judge, to blessedness; whence: behold the man and his work
**“thy justice”** — good works
**“and the glory of the Lord”** — the Son, concerning whom: arise, my glory
**“shall gather thee up”**
• in the protection of mercy
• that you may be glorified before God and man
**“Justice”** — Christ, who justifies all, goes before to glory: whence, “I go to prepare a place for you.” The same: and the glory of the Lord shall gather you up, that is, he will receive to himself the one who said, “Where I am, there also shall my minister be.”
58.9:
**“Then shalt thou call”** — by mouth, heart and deed
**“and the Lord shall hear”**
• whose will you have done
• answering with benefits
**“thou shalt cry, and he shall say, Here I am”** — to reward, I who am present to help in good works
**“If thou wilt take away”** — put away
**“take away the chain out of the midst of thee, and cease to stretch out the finger”** — to detract
**“and to speak that which profiteth not”** — but harms
**“The chain”** — Of sins. Whence: “The cords of the wicked have encompassed me”; and: each one is fast bound with the ropes of his own sins.
**“To stretch out the finger”** — Not to brand one’s neighbours by detraction; that is, not only should you not think and not do these things, but you should not detract either.
58.10:
**“When thou shalt pour out”** — with generous pity
**“to the hungry”** — spiritual or bodily bread
**“thy soul”** — a sympathetic will
**“and the afflicted soul”** — by whatever distress
**“shalt satisfy”** — by whatever benefit, not only sustaining but also satisfying, if you can
**“shall rise up in darkness”** — by driving away sins
**“thy light”** — Christ
**“and thy darkness”**
• sins
• You were once darkness, but now light in the Lord.
**“shall be as the noonday”** — brightness of justice
58.11:
**“and”** — then
**“rest”** — everlasting
**“the Lord will give thee continually”** — when thy darkness shall be as the noonday
**“and will fill”** — Whence: “With thee is the principality in the day of thy strength: in the brightness of the saints.”
**“thy soul with brightness”** — by virtues, or by the vision of the Godhead
**“and deliver thy bones”**
• from eternal fire
• that the virtues may not fail; or he will raise up the body on the day of judgment
**“and thou shalt be like a garden”** — the faithful, or the Church
**“watered”** — conspicuous for the flowers of virtues and the fruits of works
**“A watered garden”** — The paradise of pleasure, which the Lord God planted from the beginning, that is, the Church. The fountain in the middle is Christ, whose spiritual waters of doctrine, which water the Church, do not fail; and this is: “And thou shalt be like a watered garden,” O faithful one or Church.
**“and like a fountain of water”**
• Christ
• spiritual
**“whose waters shall not fail”** — Heaven and earth shall pass, but my words shall not pass.
**“Like a fountain”** — Thou shalt be made like to Christ thy head.
58.12:
**“and”** — above all else
**“shall be built”** — in the Church through faith
**“in thee”** — O Church
**“the places that have been desolate”**
• on account of unbelief
• the assemblies of the Jews
**“for ages”** — of many
**“the foundations of generation and generation”** — of both peoples
**“thou shalt raise up”**
• O Church
• by confessing Christ as true God and true man
**“and thou shalt be called”** — a preacher
**“the repairer of the fences”** — of the doctrines by which the Church is fortified
**“turning the paths into rest”**
• or into rest
• of errors, which have no rest nor peace; who is Christ
**“Shall be built”** — The Jews refer this to the restoration that was made under Zorobabel and Jesus the high priest, or to that which they rave will be in the last times. It is better that these things be referred to the Church.
**“The foundations”** — Apostles, prophets and the like; whence “his foundation is in the mountains.” The foundation, however, in the singular, is Christ; whence: “For other foundation no man can lay, but that which is laid; which is Christ Jesus.”
**“Iniquities”** — Or into rest: that is, the paths of error into rest, or true peace.
58.13:
**“If thou turn away”**
• that you not transgress
• that you not do evil on the day of the sabbath
**“from the sabbath”** — rest of the soul, which is to be celebrated at all times
**“thy foot”** — “my feet were almost moved”
**“from doing thy own will”** — of the flesh
**“in my holy day, and call”** — celebrating to the Lord sabbaths delightful
**“the sabbath delightful”** — acceptable to God
**“and the holy”** — pure
**“of the Lord”** — not yours
**“glorious, and glorify”** — in your works
**“him”**
• the Lord
• or the day of the sabbath
**“while thou dost not thy own ways”** — wicked actions
**“and thy own will is not found”** — that is, neither sin by work nor by will
**“to speak a word”** — hateful or idle
58.14:
**“Then”** — when you have done the above things
**“shalt thou be delighted”** — “Delight in the Lord, and he will give thee the requests of thy heart.”
**“in the Lord, and I will lift thee up”** — in eternal blessedness
**“above the high places”** — other heights
**“of the earth”** — of eternal stability; for this alone is the element immobile and solid
**“of the land”** — Of those who live, who go upward, not downward. Whence Lot is told: “save thyself in the mountain.”
**“and will feed thee with the inheritance of Jacob thy father”**
• namely the true homeland
• which “That eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither hath it entered into the heart of man.”
**“For the mouth of the Lord”** — all these things are as true; for the mouth of the Lord
**“hath spoken it”**
• through the prophet
• namely the word
**“Inheritance”** — To the heavenly inheritance which I gave to Jacob, whose son you are through faith and work, supplanting vices and sins; for whoever is the imitator of another is called his son.

59.1:
**“Behold”** — The prophet to the Jews.
**“the hand of the Lord is not shortened”** — shortened in power, since he freed you from Egypt
**“that it cannot save”** — you, if you believe
**“neither is his ear heavy that it cannot hear”** — if you call upon him purely, as he once heard Moses and others
59.2:
**“But your iniquities”**
• as a wall set between
• the worship of idols
• He shows why they were not heard and were led into captivity.
**“have divided”** — Christ has broken down the middle wall of partition
**“between you and your God”** — that he may not save you or hear you
**“and your sins”** — he cannot endure the face of your sins
**“have hid”**
• so that he does not see your filthiness but strikes at once
• as a wall set between
**“his ground”** — presence, help, grace
**“from you that he should not hear”** — in time of tribulation
59.3:
**“For your hands are defiled with blood”** — of the prophets and of Christ himself
**“and your fingers with iniquity”** — when they said: “All things that the Lord hath commanded us we will do”; or: you have a demon, and such like
**“your lips have spoken lies”** — they put forward or promise Antichrist in place of Christ
**“and your tongue uttereth iniquity”** — blasphemy
**“your hands”** — He sets out the iniquities part by part, and does not charge them with idolatry, which was practised in Isaias' time, but with the shedding of blood, whence above: “The just perisheth, and no man layeth it to heart”
**“uttereth”** — Your hands indeed. They stoned Jeremias. They sawed Isaias. They killed Ezechiel in Babylon, and at last, crying out against the Son of God: “His blood be upon us and upon our children.”
59.4:
**“There is none that calleth upon justice”** — let him believe in Christ
**“neither is there any one that judgeth truly”** — because they chose Barabbas and crucified Christ
**“but they trust in a mere nothing”** — in an idol, an idol is nothing; or in some Messiah yet to come, I know not who
**“and speak vanities”**
• Jewish fables
• blaspheming Christ three times daily in the synagogues, still awaiting the Messiah
**“they have conceived labour”** — devising the death of Christ with great labour
**“and brought forth iniquity”** — that is, they bring forth, receiving Antichrist
**“have conceived”** — Who await Antichrist. For whom they seek with great labour, they will receive in iniquity.
59.5:
**“the eggs of asps”** — poisonous counsels
**“have broken”** — revealing
**“The eggs of asps”** — From the egg, the offspring; from the heart, counsel; from counsel, the deed. So they broke the eggs when they revealed their wicked hearts and poisonous counsels in words, saying: “He is guilty of death.”
**“of asps”** — The asp, at the first voice of the charmer, presses one ear to the ground and stops the other with its tail, that it may not be charmed. So the Jews, clinging to earthly things, fearing to lose their place and nation, rejected the preaching of Christ, poisoned, the sons of the poisoned; whence, brood of vipers.
**“and the webs of spiders”** — counsels, works, vain and unprofitable, the gnats and flies, that is, the foolish and simple, catching
**“have woven”** — plotting against Christ
**“he that shall eat”** — by consenting
**“of their eggs”** — counsels
**“their”** — of the Jews
**“shall die”**
• with eternal death
• as Abel, consenting when Cain said, Let us go out into the field
**“and that which is brought out”** — nourished from the eggs
**“shall be hatched”** — while they showed wicked hearts and poisonous counsels in words, saying, He is guilty of death
**“into a basilisk”** — Antichrist, king of all evils
**“shall be hatched into a basilisk”** — Of the eggs of asps comes the little king, who is also the basilisk, Antichrist out of the Jews. For out of them he will be born, killing many by his poisonous breath, that is, by his speech, those flying toward the heavenly homeland. For the basilisk kills by his breath the birds flying through the air.
59.6:
**“Their webs”** — counsels, works, teaching
**“shall not be for clothing”** — souls
**“neither shall they cover themselves”** — against the cold of hell
**“with their works”**
• the garments of the saints, good works, whence your priests are clothed
• by evils, because
**“their works”**
• the webs of spiders
• all have turned aside together; they have become unprofitable
**“their works are unprofitable works, and the work of iniquity”** — the death of Christ
**“is in their hands”** — although they say to us, It is not lawful to put anyone to death
59.7:
**“the feet”** — affections
**“run to evil”**
• by working
• with lanterns and torches to seize Christ
**“and make haste”** — wearisomely, by asking Pilate
**“to shed”** — that they may pour out, as cheap water
**“innocent blood”** — of Christ or of the prophets, whence: Jerusalem, that killest the prophets, etc.
**“their thoughts”** — against God, let us root him out of the land of the living, and the like
**“are unprofitable thoughts: wasting”** — from enemies, from the devil
**“and destruction are in their ways”** — by wicked actions, for which they are laid waste and crushed
**“wasting”** — The apostle placed this in Romans, as well as that: “Their feet swift to shed blood.” Many, not knowing this, think it was taken from the thirteenth psalm; which verses were added in the Vulgate edition and are not found in the Hebrew.
59.8:
**“the way of peace”** — Christ, who is true peace, who said: “Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you.”
**“have not known”**
• not willing to believe
• discernment of good and evil, or uprightness
**“and there is no judgment”**
• Christ
• of whom he will bring judgment to the Gentiles
**“in their steps”** — works
**“Their way”** — actions
**“Are become crooked”**
• not by nature but by will; for whatever is bent is twisted from straight into crooked
• from good to evil
**“every one that treadeth in them”** — imitates
**“knoweth no peace”**
• Christ
• not only does he not find it, but he does not know what he ought to seek
59.9:
**“Therefore”**
• because we have not known peace
• The prophet, in the person of the penitent people, answers after the accusation what penitents ought to say.
**“is judgment far”** — passing over to the Gentiles
**“judgment”** — the Son, to whom judgment has been given
**“from us, and justice shall not overtake us”** — drawing by faith
**“us”** — but the Gentiles
**“justice”**
• Christ
• grasped by the Gentiles
**“We looked for light”** — Christ, promised in the law, of whom: “Send forth thy light and thy truth,” etc.
**“and behold darkness”** — unbelief, antichrist
**“brightness”** — Christ, who is “the brightness of his glory, and the figure of his substance”
**“and we have walked in the dark”** — of the sin of ignorance
59.10:
**“We have groped”** — the holy Scripture, not seeing Christ in it, seeking only the words and leaves, not the sense and fruit
**“We have groped for the wall, and like the blind we have groped as if we had no eyes”** — because Christ is offered almost even visibly to the eyes
**“we have stumbled at noonday”**
• in the holy Scripture, which is like noon, clear and open to the saints
• throughout the whole world, with the sun of justice shining
**“as in darkness”** — not understanding
**“in dark places”** — in obscure mysteries; for as long as Moses is read, the veil is over their hearts
59.11:
**“We shall roar all of us like bears, and shall lament as mournful doves”** — not having a heart
**“shall lament, looked for judgment”** — Christ, of whom: Give to the king thy judgment, O God.
**“and there is none: for salvation”** — for us, but for the Gentiles
**“and it is far from us”**
• even to the Gentiles. Behold, your house shall be left to you, desolate.
• “Your house shall be left to you desolate”
• We shall roar all of us like bears, etc. The meditation and teaching of the Jews in the sacred Scripture is compared to the roaring of the bear and the moaning of the dove, as useless and vain like theirs. Toward those under them they rage like bears; against their superiors or equals they moan like doves, as in that: Ephraim is become as a dove that hath no heart.
59.12:
**“are multiplied”** — because they both despised the Scripture and killed the author
**“For our iniquities”** — from whom turning away his face, lest you should see, lest you should strike
**“before thee”** — to whom nothing is hidden
**“and our sins have testified against us”** — we receive according to our iniquities
**“for our wicked doings are with us”**
• are still
• according to our petition: His blood be upon us and our children.
**“and we have known our iniquities”**
• as if we thought it were justice
• repenting, when pricked in heart, they said: What shall we do, men and brethren? and so on
59.13:
**“In sinning”** — to sin, by handing him over to Pilate
**“and lying”** — and to lie, by saying he is guilty of death, etc.
**“against the Lord: and we have turned away”**
• against the Lord, and we have turned away from the Lord
• saying: “We know that God spoke to Moses: but as to this man, we know not from whence he is.”
**“so that we went not”** — that we should not go, imitating. Whence: “If any man minister to me, let him follow me”; and that: “You shall walk after the Lord your God.”
**“after our God”** — behind the back of our God, that: “This man is not of God, who keepeth not the sabbath.”
**“but spoke calumny”** — we spoke calumny against Christ
**“and transgression”** — and transgression of the law
**“we have conceived”** — we conceived malice
**“and uttered from the heart”** — and spoke from the heart knowingly
**“words of falsehood”**
• words of falsehood: the traditions of men
• we found him subverting our nation
59.14:
**“And judgment is turned away”** — and it is turned to the Gentiles
**“judgment is turned away backward”** — judgment backward: Christ
**“and”** — and, that is,
**“justice”** — justice, which is the part of the just
**“hath stood far off”** — far from us
**“stood”** — among the Gentiles
**“because truth hath fallen down”** — as it did not remain in those who follow the breadth and will of the world, the scribes and Pharisees and such like
**“in the street”** — or street
**“truth and equity”** — the same
**“could not come in”**
• the hearts of the Jews
• which dwells in hearts through faith could not enter because of unbelief
59.15:
**“And truth hath been forgotten”** — Christ
**“forgotten”**
• by the Jews
• Truth. Christ, who is the way, the truth, and the life. Whence: “Truth is sprung out of the earth: and justice hath looked down from heaven.” And it is to be noted that truth is often named so that the person of Christ may be shown, whom those who forsake followed falsehood.
**“and they that”** — and who, by believing in Christ
**“departed from evil”** — departed from evil, of unbelief
**“lay open to be a prey”** — of other Jews who plundered the goods of the faithful; whence you took with joy the being stripped of your own goods
**“and the Lord saw”** — their penance unfruitful
**“and it appeared evil in his eyes”**
• because not with a pure heart
• who sees all things
**“because there is no”**
• in them
• because it has been transferred to the Gentiles
**“judgment”**
• discernment of good and evil, or between simplicity and duplicity, or in their penance the judgment of uprightness
• And the Lord saw, etc. Having shown that they repented, he shows that their penance did not please the Lord, because many repented not with a pure heart.
59.16:
**“And he saw”** — the Father
**“because there is no”** — among the Jews
**“a man”**
• holy
• as Moses, David, and others
**“That there is not a man”** — Because there is not a man. In mind all have become effeminate, as that: “I came, and there was none that would hear.”
**“and he stood astonished”** — and he was grieved at their unbelief
**“because there is none to oppose himself”**
• because there is none to oppose: the Jews obstinate in unbelief
• to intercede for them, as Moses in the desert
• lest he strike, for God
**“and his own arm brought salvation”**
• or shall save
• from their persecution, raising up from the dead
**“to him, his own arm”** — The Son, through whom all things were made.
**“and his own justice”** — that is, the Son, through whom is all justice.
**“supported”**
• or will confirm.
• among the Gentiles, through faith.
**“him”** — The Father.
59.17:
**“he was clothed”**
• by freeing his elect from the persecution of their enemies, and by fighting for them, saving them.
• that is, he came justly, as one armed with breastplate and helmet, in vengeance on his enemies, when he overthrew Judea through the Romans.
**“justice as a breastplate, and a helmet of salvation upon his head; he was clothed with garments of vengeance”** — by the Roman soldiers.
**“and covered as with a cloak of zeal”** — the wrath of vengeance.
59.18:
**“as unto revenge, as it were to repay”** — that they may receive according to their works.
**“wrath to his adversaries”** — The Jews.
**“and”** — that as they killed the prophets and Christ himself, so they may be killed by the Romans.
**“a reward to his enemies”** — to be repaid for iniquity.
**“to the islands”** — the cities of the Jews.
**“the like”** — the reward.
**“he will repay”** — by destroying them.
59.19:
**“And they shall be afraid”** — holily, chastely, filially; whence: “Blessed is the man that feareth the Lord”; or with servile fear.
**“they from the west”** — Many shall come from the east and the west, etc.
**“the name of the Lord”** — of the Father. Whence: “I have manifested thy name to the men.”
**“and they from the rising of the sun”** — The Son, to whom it is said: “Arise, my glory.”
**“his glory”** — of the Father.
**“when he shall come”**
• the author of blessedness.
• the Son made flesh, or to the nations in the preaching of the apostles.
**“as a violent stream”**
• because in him is the fountain of wisdom, and of teaching, and of knowledge; who says: “If any man thirst, let him come to me and drink.”
• Which most swiftly filled the world with his preaching and faith; of which: “His word runneth swiftly.”
**“violent”** — to whom nothing resists; whence: “All power is given to me in heaven and in earth.”
**“which the spirit of the Lord driveth on”**
• love, goodness, charity.
• The Holy Spirit, namely, to redeem the human race. Whence: who was conceived of the Holy Spirit, and “the spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him,” etc.
**“and they shall fear who”** — The vengeance of God foreshown against the Jews through the Romans describes the faith of the Gentiles coming from the four parts of the world, the preaching of the apostles having been heard.
59.20:
**“and there shall come a redeemer to Sion”**
• Christ.
• to the faithful Jews, or the Church
**“and to them”** — not to all
**“that return”** — who have faith, that is, and operation
**“from iniquity”**
• of unbelief and denial
• to those who fight against vices and concupiscences
59.21:
**“This is my covenant with them”** — namely those who return from iniquity
**“saith the Lord: My spirit”** — holy, from prophecy
**“that is in thee”** — O Isaias
**“and my words”** — my gospel, to which no other law succeeds; whence John says the eternal gospel
**“that I have put in thy mouth, shall not depart out of thy mouth, nor out of the mouth of thy seed, nor out of the mouth of thy seed's seed, saith the Lord, from henceforth and for ever”**
• heaven and earth shall pass, but my words shall not pass
• This is my covenant, etc. That is, that I may redeem them by the blood of the Son, and that they themselves may do my commandments and hold them in memory; and this is my Spirit, etc.
**“of the seed”** — Of the following prophets, apostles, and martyrs, who were filled with the same Spirit. For the Holy Spirit, who taught Isaias, passes by a kind of succession to others. And this is “from henceforth and for ever.”

60.1:
thus
**“Arise, be enlightened”**
• by faith
• you who fell by unbelief
• you who lie in vices
• O
• The Jews refer this to the time of their Christ, whom we call Antichrist, and they understand that Jerusalem which they affirm will descend from heaven, golden and adorned. John makes mention of it in the Apocalypse, and by it we understand holy Church. For they say that then all nations will serve them, the camels, the dromedaries of Madian and Epha, all coming from Saba, will bring gold and frankincense; and the sheep of Cedar and the rams of Nabaioth will be gathered to be offered to the Lord upon the altar of the temple which they will then have built. But we, despising their follies, refer this to the primitive Church. Some, however, say that all these things were promised to the Jews carnally, that they might receive the Son of God even by rewards.
**“O Jerusalem”** — Arise in the churches, you who were slain in the synagogues; arise among the Gentiles, you who fell among the Jews; arise through confession, through virtues, you who fell through denial and through vices; and when you have risen, be enlightened, that is, receive the faith of Christ.
**“for thy light is come”**
• made man
• the Son of God
**“and the glory of the Lord”**
• of miracles, or the Son of God
• “Glorious things are said of thee, O city of God.”
**“upon thee”** — O Church
**“Thy light”** — promised to you long before to come for your redemption: “which enlighteneth every man that cometh into this world”; namely he who says, “I am the light of the world,” by whom you will be enlightened if you receive the faith of Christ.
**“the glory of the Lord”** — To enlighten: the Son, namely, as the rising sun lights the world; in whose figure the glory of the Lord is shown to Moses, who built the tabernacle, and to Solomon, the other, who built the temple. The glory of the Lord was also the raising of the dead, the cleansing of the leper, and the like.
60.2:
**“for behold darkness”** — of unbelief
**“the land”** — The Jews, who love only earthly things, to whom it is said, “you shall eat the good things of the land,” which they take carnally.
**“and a mist”** — of sins
**“the people upon thee”** — to be enlightened
**“but the Lord shall arise”** — the true sun
**“and his glory”** — miracles, whence we saw his glory, etc. Glory as of the only begotten of the Father, full of grace, etc.
60.3:
**“and the Gentiles shall walk”** — who before were in darkness
**“in thy light”** — by faith, or by Christ, who is the light of the world
**“and he shall rule over kings”**
• the heart of kings is in the hand of God, and he turns it wherever he wills
• Constantine, Heraclius, Theodosius; or the saints, who rule themselves and others well
**“in the brightness of thy rising”** — By which, namely, “of water and the Holy Ghost” you were born: we all walk in the splendour of the rising of the primitive Church, because we have the same faith and are born again by the same baptism.
60.4:
**“Lift up”** — O primitive Church
**“round about”** — of the world
**“thy eyes”** — of the mind
**“and see”** — understand
**“all these are gathered together”** — to be joined in faith
**“they are come to thee: thy sons”** — the faithful, stronger in faith
**“from afar”** — to the faith
**“shall come, and thy daughters”** — little ones in Christ, to whom the apostle says, “I gave you milk to drink, not meat”; and Peter, “as newborn babes”
**“shall rise up at thy side”**
• or they will suck milk
• Lift up round about, etc. To which is like: “Lift up your eyes, and see the countries, for they are white already to harvest.”
• The first believers from the Jews, when the Spirit was given, were in Jerusalem, devout men out of every nation under heaven, or Gentiles from all parts of the world.
**“Thy sons”** — Whom you begot in faith. Whence Paul: “For in Christ Jesus, by the gospel, I have begotten you.”
**“shall come from afar”** — Because they were far from God through idolatry. Whence: “you, who some time were afar off, are made nigh.”
**“at thy side”** — Jerome. Some copies have: shall rise from the side. For when the side of the Lord was pierced on the cross, there flowed out the blood of redemption and the water of baptism, of which the Church was made, as Eve, the mother of all, from the rib of Adam’s side. The one of these does not profit without the other. For unless we believe the passion and resurrection of Christ for our redemption, though we be baptized we shall not be saved; nor if we believe these, unless we be baptized. But this is found neither in the Hebrew nor in the Septuagint, nor does the sense of Jerome incline to this.
60.5:
**“Then”** — when you lift up your eyes
**“shalt thou see”** — by sons, whom the river with sudden waters
**“and abound; and shall wonder”** — the multitude
**“and thy heart shall be enlarged”**
• for joy
• that you may receive Christ as guest
• according to that: “my heart is enlarged”; “be you also enlarged”
**“when ... shall be converted”** — through faith
**“the multitude of the sea shall be converted to thee”** — all the nations of the world
**“the strength of the Gentiles”** — kings, princes
**“shall come to thee”** — to be joined in faith
60.6:
**“The multitude of camels”** — the abundance of the rich coming to the faith
**“of camels”** — A camel is a humped animal that carries burdens. These are the rich, carrying the burden of riches and the hump of sins.
**“shall cover thee”**
• he will adorn with his gifts
• because
**“the dromedaries”** — nations
**“The dromedaries”** — A dromedary, or dromas (for both are said), is an animal smaller than the camel but swifter, in which are figured the nations hastening swiftly to the faith.
**“of Madian”** — iniquity
**“and Epha”**
• otherwise: Epha
• dissolved or pouring out
**“all they from Saba”** — captivity or way of life
**“they shall come”** — to the faith
**“gold”** — faith, charity and wisdom
**“and frankincense”**
• of sacrifice
• prayer. Whence: “Let my prayer be directed as incense in thy sight.”
**“bringing, and shewing forth praise to the Lord”**
• the works of the Son
• the Son in whom the Father is praised
**“shewing forth”**
• to others, as if not content with their own salvation
• Madian: iniquity. Epha: loosed, or pouring out. Saba: conversation, or captivity. The rich and powerful of this age, therefore, and the nations coming swiftly to the faith, the bonds of iniquity loosed, poured out their souls to the Lord; and, returning from the captivity of the devil and of vain conversation, they offered to the Lord the gift of faith, which is figured by gold, and of pure prayer, which is figured by frankincense.
**“Madian and Epha”** — Regions beyond Arabia, abounding in camels and dromedaries, through which are designated all parts of the world from which the nations come to the faith.
60.7:
**“All the flocks of Cedar”** — Simple folk who were before darkness and sorrow. Whence: “For you were heretofore darkness, but now light in the Lord.” For Cedar is interpreted as darkness and sorrow.
**“all the flocks of Cedar”** — Cedar, son of Ismael, from whom the region received its name, where the Saracens dwell, born of his stock.
**“shall be gathered together unto thee, the rams of Nabaioth”** — “Bring to the Lord, O ye children of God: bring to the Lord the offspring of rams.”
**“The rams”** — Preachers of the flock, leaders, sons of the prophets, who taught that what the prophets foretold about Christ has been fulfilled.
**“of Nabaioth”** — Son of Ismael; and it is interpreted as prophecy.
**“shall minister to thee”** — Holy bishops, priests, and ministers of the Church, ministering the body and blood of Christ to the faithful.
**“shall be offered”** — the rams: as Titus from Paul, and others, Mark from Peter
**“upon my acceptable altar”** — by faith, upon which all good things are offered
**“the house of my majesty”** — the Church
**“I will glorify”** — in such
60.8:
**“Who are these”** — nations
**“Who are”** — The prophet marvels at the nations hastening so quickly to the faith, or the primitive Church.
**“that fly as clouds”** — removed from the storms of the world
**“fly”** — to me from the whole world on the wings of the Holy Spirit
**“as clouds fly”** — That fly as clouds: they rain with words, they flash with miracles; they fly to heaven by contemplation of the mind.
*Gregory:* The whirlpools of rain-storms flow from the clouds, because through the deep preaching of those who follow, they received the origin of understanding from the holy apostles; whence the dark water in the clouds of the air.
**“and as doves”** — the simple
**“to their windows”**
• the entrance of faith through which they desire to enter into the Church
• To their windows the saints stand, guarding the five senses of the body, lest death enter into souls through them as through windows; whence: “Be ye wise as serpents, and simple as doves.”
60.9:
**“For, the islands wait for me”**
• whence he himself will be the expectation of the nations
• diverse nations
**“and the ships”** — the Church
**“of the sea”** — of the world
**“at the beginning”** — of faith
**“that I may bring thy sons”** — nations
**“thy”** — O primitive Church
**“from afar”** — from idolatry
**“their silver”** — eloquence
**“Their silver”** — This is: “with the heart, we believe unto justice; but, with the mouth, confession is made unto salvation.”
**“and their gold”**
• confession of faith
• wisdom
**“their, with them, to the name of the Lord thy God”** — they will come, namely that he may be glorified over them
**“and to the Holy One of Israel, because he hath glorified thee”** — through them
60.10:
**“And the children shall build up”**
• beyond the other goods
• these things literally and spiritually
**“of strangers”**
• of the nations
• Constantine and others who built churches throughout the world
**“The children of strangers”** — The princes of the nations who built Churches throughout the world, as Constantine, who made twelve Churches at Rome in honor of the twelve apostles, and many others who built many Churches and supplied what was needed. Allegorically, he calls the martyrs and teachers of the nations the sons of strangers and their kings, by whose faith and virtues holy Church is founded.
**“thy walls”** — lest an enemy be able to enter
**“and their kings”** — spiritual and secular
**“shall minister to thee: for in my wrath have I struck thee”**
• in the Jews
• by present tribulation, that I might correct; through tyrants, through many captivities
**“and in my reconciliation have I had mercy upon thee”** — in the Gentiles
60.11:
**“And thy gates shall be open”**
• ready to receive others
• Ministers of the Church, who lead others in.
**“continually, day nor night”**
• In prosperity and in adversity.
• In joy and in tribulation.
**“they shall not be shut, that the strength of the Gentiles may be brought to thee”** — Princes or martyrs, strong in faith.
**“and their kings”** — Such as Constantine, or saints who rule themselves and others and direct them into the way of justice.
**“may be brought”** — To the faith: captives.
60.12:
**“The nation”** — Of the Jews, or any nation.
**“For and the kingdom”** — Ruling ones.
**“that will not serve”** — In faith and in deed.
**“thee”** — O Church.
**“shall perish”**
• As if it were not.
• On the day of judgment.
**“and the Gentiles”** — Gentiles.
**“with desolation”** — Forsaken by God, whom they would not receive as guest.
**“shall be wasted”** — By the devil or the fire of hell.
60.13:
**“The glory”** — The power of the world.
**“of Libanus shall come to thee”** — By faith.
**“the fir tree, and the box tree”** — Flourishing in faith.
**“and the pine tree together, to beautify”** — In wisdom, teaching, and virtues.
**“the place”** — That is, the Church which the apostles founded.
**“of my sanctuary: and I will glorify the place of my feet”**
• By the multitude of believers.
• The diversity of trees signifies the diverse orders in the Church. Out of all these the Church is built, distinguished with wondrous beauty.
**“The glory of Libanus”** — Libanus is a mountain bordering on the land of promise, from which Hiram, king of Tyre, furnished David for the palace, and Solomon for the temple, beautiful and incorruptible timber. Its glory is the height of its trees, their variety, and the abundance of beasts. Libanus therefore is the world; its glory, the loftiness of the world, that is, the kings and princes who have come to the Church.
**“The fir tree, and”** — The proud, namely the rich philosophers; for pride follows riches and knowledge. Cyprian and Hilary, trees lofty in the world, built the Church of God.
**“the place of my feet”** — The Church, in which are the apostles, who are the feet of the Lord, that is, carrying him about by preaching. Whence: “I will dwell in them and walk in them.” And elsewhere: Blessed are the feet of them that carry peace, that is, Christ. Or the preachers are called feet, who, set up to sustain the whole body, that is, the Church, do so by miracles and examples.
60.14:
**“And shall come bowing down to thee”** — With the steps of faith.
**“the children of them that afflict thee”** — The humble, or those who are Christians by necessity, lest they offend the princes.
**“their”**
• Both Jews and Gentiles.
• Of persecutors.
**“that afflict thee”** — By afflicting the saints.
**“and adore”** — They will reverence.
**“the steps of thy feet”** — The signs and works of the apostles.
**“all that slandered thee”** — first, as Paul
**“and shall call thee”**
• Truly.
• when these things shall have been fulfilled
**“the city of the Lord”** — “A city seated on a mountain cannot be hid.”
**“Sion”** — that is, the watcher of eternal life.
**“The city of the Lord”** — For a city is so called from fellowship. The Church, however, is one for all and has all things in common. “One Lord, one faith, one baptism”; whence: “And the multitude of believers had but one heart and one soul.”
60.15:
**“Because thou wast forsaken”** — by God
**“Forsaken”** — When Christ came, there was among the Jews or the Gentiles no prophet or apostle who would go about diligently and give help.
**“and hated”** — by the unbelieving Jews and Gentiles
**“Hated”** — To the Jews, because he preached the faith of Christ and destroyed the observances of the law. To the Gentiles, because he asserted one God and affirmed that idols are nothing.
**“and there was none that passed through thee”** — the unfruitful branches having been broken off
**“There was none that passed through”** — Would pass by and bless you; whence: “And they that have passed by have not said: The blessing of the Lord be upon you.” For those passing by used, by custom, to bless the workers; whence Booz said to his reapers: “The Lord be with you.”
**“I will make thee to be an everlasting glory”**
• height
• in place of the broken branches, others grafted in
**“everlasting”** — that is, so that you may always rejoice
**“unto generation”** — of the Gentiles
**“and generation”** — of the Jews
**“an everlasting glory”** — Pride is sometimes evil, sometimes good; whence: the riches of pride and justice.
60.16:
**“And thou shalt suck”** — in little ones
**“the milk of the Gentiles”** — the simple teaching of teachers coming from the Gentiles
**“and thou shalt be nursed with the breasts of kings”** — the teaching of the apostles, of whom you will set princes over all the earth
**“and”** — then
**“Know that I”** — the Father
**“saving thee”**
• in the blood of the Son
• from eternal death
**“and thy Redeemer”** — by the price of blood
**“the Mighty One of Jacob”** — giving strength to wrestlers against vices, lest they fail in the struggle
60.17:
**“For brass I will bring gold, and for iron I will bring silver, and for wood”** — for the brutish
**“brass, and for stones”** — for the insensible ones
**“iron”**
• that is, so that they may provide some usefulness to the city
• For wood brass. By the wood and the stones are meant the hard and foolish and senseless, worshippers of idols, who, believing, have been converted to some use of the Church. This is signified by brass and iron. And again by gold and silver, when they come to the perfect sense of the faith and pure confession. Or by iron and brass we have those among the nations who are of some usefulness, according to which the faithful receive diverse graces: so that some sound forth in preaching, like brass; others are made distinguished in doctrine and wisdom, which is signified by gold and silver. Whence: a treasure to be desired rests in the mouth of the wise. Others strong in faith, as Cyprian. And other martyrs, like iron.
**“and I will make thy visitation peace”**
• Christ or the apostles, who preach peace.
• a visitor, as in the epistle of Paul: “He gave them the operation of iniquity,” that is, an operator.
**“visitation”** — Christ or the apostles, peacemakers, and just overseers, so that they may teach and judge rightly.
60.18:
**“Iniquity shall no more be heard”**
• under these things set forth.
• from the time when you have attained blessedness.
**“in thy land”** — of the living; whence I believe to see the good things of the Lord, etc.
**“wasting nor destruction in thy borders”** — There will be none; whence: “Who hath placed peace in thy borders.”
**“and salvation shall possess”** — will fill.
**“salvation”** — or saviour, which in Hebrew
**“thy walls”** — preachers, who are also gates.
**“and thy gates”** — so that those who enter the gates may learn to praise and confess thy name, O Lord.
60.19:
**“Thou shalt no more have”**
• in eternal blessedness.
• This is of the day of judgment. By this chapter we are compelled to refer whatever has been or will be said to the last time, when for us the office of the heavens and earth, of the sun and moon, will cease, and the Lord himself will be light forever.
**“the sun for thy light by day”**
• here, visible; the just shall shine as the sun in the kingdom of their Father.
• Isidore, in the book of Creatures. After the judgment the sun will receive the reward of its labor; whence the prophet: it will shine sevenfold, and neither sun nor moon will come to setting, but they will stand in the order in which they were created, lest the wicked, placed in torments under the earth, enjoy their light; whence Habacuc: “The sun and the moon stood still in their habitation.”
**“neither shall the brightness of the moon enlighten thee”** — which we now see.
**“but the Lord shall be unto thee for an everlasting light”** — the vision of the Godhead.
**“and thy God for thy glory”** — as the sun of mercy sets for the false prophets, the sun of justice always rises for those who fear the Lord.
60.20:
**“Thy sun shall go down no more”**
• Christ.
• because Samuel is dead.
**“and thy moon shall not decrease”** — The Church, which now seems to grow, now to be diminished.
**“for the Lord”** — to you.
**“shall be unto thee for an everlasting light”** — by day the sun will not burn you, nor the moon by night.
**“and the days of thy mourning shall be ended”**
• will be ended: “God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes,” etc.
• in the building up of the Church: “Blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted.”
**“of thy mourning”** — the Church now weeps for its own and others’ sins, or because glory is deferred.
60.21:
**“And thy people”** — with mourning ended.
**“shall be all just”** — the elect angels.
**“for ever”** — not for an hour.
**“they shall inherit the land”** — of the living: when the wicked go into eternal fire, but the just, always seeing the Creator, will not be able to sin.
**“the branch of my planting”**
• they will be.
• Not that which shall be rooted up, of which: “Every plant which my Father hath not planted shall be rooted up.”
**“The branch of the planting”** — All the elect angels, who fulfil with works the faith they have. They themselves are the branch of the Lord’s planting and the work of his hands, because they were created by him and planted in the Church through faith, to glorify their creator; whence through Jeremias: “Whom I created for my praise and the glory of my name.”
60.22:
**“The least”** — Humble. Whence: whosoever will be greater among you, shall be your minister; and elsewhere: “Well done, good and faithful servant,” etc.
**“shall become a thousand”** — As a ciliarchus.
**“and a little one”** — in his own eyes
**“a most strong nation”**
• These things will be more fully fulfilled at the end of the world.
• over those whom he taught by word and example
**“I the Lord will do this thing in its time”** — when all things have been despaired of
**“suddenly”** — “The day of the Lord shall so come, as a thief in the night.”
**“will do this thing”** — The least into a thousand, etc.
**“In its time”** — That is, the coming of Christ. Or at the fitting or appointed time, when the Son of man sends his angels, and they gather out of his kingdom all scandals.

61.1:
**“The spirit of the Lord is upon me”**
• Because greater. Whence: “And the spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him.”
• The spirit of the Lord is upon me. Christ, according to his humanity, who had said above: “I the Lord will gather them in their time,” etc.
**“because the Lord hath anointed me”**
• the joy of eternal life
• With the oil of gladness: the abundance of grace. Jerome: this anointing was completed in baptism, because the Spirit of the Lord descended in the form of a dove and remained on him; whence after baptism it is found written in Luke: “The spirit of the Lord is upon me,” etc.
**“to the meek”** — to the humble in spirit. Whence: “Blessed are the meek: for they shall possess the land”; “Blessed are the peacemakers,” etc.
**“he hath sent me to heal”** — by the forgiveness of sins
**“the contrite of heart”**
• by compunction
• “A contrite and humbled heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.”
**“and to preach”** — saying: Do penance
**“to the captives”** — under the devil and various errors
**“a release, and deliverance to them that are shut up”** — in the prison of unbelief and ignorance
**“deliverance”** — That is, release; for so Symmachus translated it more plainly.
61.2:
**“To proclaim the acceptable year”**
• the whole time in which he lived in the flesh; whence Paul, of the first coming: “Behold, now is the acceptable time.”
• the time of grace; whence: “Behold, now is the acceptable time.”
**“acceptable”** — by faith and the salvation of men
**“of the Lord, and the day of vengeance of our God”** — For God is the Father of Christ according to his humanity.
**“the day of vengeance”** — Of the damnation which was through the Romans, according to that: “The days shall come upon thee, and thy enemies shall cast a trench about thee,” etc. And: “When you shall see Jerusalem compassed with an army,” etc.
**“to comfort all that mourn”** — their own sins and those of others. Whence: “Blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted.”
61.3:
**“To appoint to the mourners”** — to the apostles. Whence: “I have great sadness and continual sorrow for my brethren, and I wished to be anathema for my brethren.”
**“of Sion, and to give them a crown”** — eternal reward
**“for ashes”**
• a mourning garb
• For ashes. For the grief and sorrow over their fruits: when, namely, they shall have seen the Gentiles flocking together to the faith, then they shall have the oil of joy for mourning, the mantle of praise for the spirit of sorrow.
**“a crown for ashes”** — When, namely, they shall have seen many of the Jews believing, and receiving in place of the mournful garment the most pure stole.
**“the oil of joy for mourning, a garment”** — a garment of gladness for the mournful
**“of praise for the spirit of grief, and”** — then
**“shall be called”** — at that time
**“in it”** — the Church
**“the mighty ones”** — the apostles and others
**“of justice”**
• to do justice
• but
**“the planting of the Lord”** — planted in the house of the Lord by him
**“to glorify him”** — God
61.4:
**“And they shall build”** — the apostles, planted by word and example
**“places that have been waste from of old”** — by God, the hearts of the Gentiles and of the Jews
**“and ancient ruins”** — the unbelief of the Jews
**“shall raise up”**
• to the faith
• through those who from that people believed
**“and shall repair the desolate cities”** — the various Churches of the various Gentiles, or the five bodily senses
**“desolate”** — by God
**“that were destroyed”** — through various errors
**“unto generation”** — of the Jews
**“and generation”** — of the Gentiles
61.5:
**“and shall stand”** — upright in faith and work
**“strangers”**
• by God
• the Gentiles, of whom many preachers
**“and shall feed”**
• with the food of the word of God
• the wicked shepherds having been driven off
**“your flocks”** — the simple and gentle, whence: Feed my sheep, feed my lambs
**“and”** — the same
**“the sons of strangers shall be your husbandmen”** — the tillers of the Church
**“and the dressers of your vines”** — keeping the vineyard and tilling it. “For the vineyard of the Lord of hosts is the house of Israel.”
