**“Dressers”** — The wicked tillers of the vineyard: the scribes and Pharisees, of whom: “He will bring those evil men to an evil end; and will let out his vineyard to other husbandmen.”
61.6:
**“But you shall be called the priests of the Lord”**
• as sons of strangers, tillers, etc. But you, apostles.
• their teachers.
**“But you”** — This is said of the preachers from the Gentiles, who are sons of strangers. Or of the apostles, from whom the remnant will be saved, so that they who are called priests of the Lord, of greater dignity, as that said of the sons of David, who were priests in the house of the Lord.
**“you shall be called”** — because
**“Ye ministers of our God”** — or our
**“to you it shall be said; you shall eat the riches of the Gentiles”**
• martyrs overcoming all things
• O apostles, delighted, refreshed by the victory of the martyrs.
**“and you shall pride yourselves in their glory”** — you shall be exalted.
61.7:
**“For your confusion”** — O apostles.
**“double”**
• of the unbelief of the Jews and the apostasy or idolatry of the Gentiles.
• rewards of soul and body.
**“and shame, they shall praise their part”** — Jews and Gentiles converted to the faith.
**“therefore in their land”** — of the living, which is upward, not downward; whence to Lot: “Save thyself in the mountain.”
**“Their part”** — The Lord; whence: “The Lord is the portion of my inheritance,” etc. Which no one truly says who seeks another portion.
61.8:
**“For I am the Lord that love judgment, and hate robbery in a holocaust: and I will make their work”** — of the faithful.
**“in truth, and I will make a perpetual covenant”** — Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away.
**“with them”**
• For I am the Lord, etc. As if the Lord would do this, who loves the justice of the poor and true judgment more than the gifts of the rich, which are often from robbery; nor do they please the Lord any more than the price of a harlot, or the sacrifice of a dog, or if anyone should offer up a son.
• In truth. That they eat the lamb in truth, that they make circumcision of the heart, which were given in figure; that they do all things in truth.
**“A perpetual covenant”** — An eternal gospel, not like the Old Testament, which the gospel succeeds.
61.9:
**“Their seed”** — The faithful, to whom the apostles committed the seed of the Word, which they received from the Lord; whence: “Going therefore, teach ye all nations; baptizing them,” etc.
**“and”** — that is
**“offspring”** — sons in faith.
**“their offspring in the midst of peoples: all that shall see them”** — the apostles and their imitators.
**“shall know”**
• at once
• in faith, by virtues, by miracles.
61.10:
**“I will greatly rejoice”**
• in the person of the Church.
• I will rejoice in the Lord, not in the world; whence: “Rejoice in the Lord always.”
**“in the Lord”** — not because I am of the stock of Abraham and of the other fathers.
**“and my soul shall be joyful”** — my heart and my flesh have rejoiced in the living God of the fathers
**“in my God: for he hath clothed”** — the Lord
**“me with the garments of salvation, and with the robe of justice”** — let your priests be clothed with justice
**“he hath covered me”**
• Christ adorned me; understand it
• in the perfect
**“as a bridegroom decked”** — in Christ, in the greater ones
**“with a crown, and as a bride adorned”**
• in the lesser ones
• with various virtues
**“with her jewels”**
• holiness: without which no man shall see God
• “The garments of salvation,” etc. By the virtues, Christ himself. Whence: “you have put on Christ,” etc. For Christ is the garment to the saints, and they to him.
• As a bridegroom, etc. Christ is the bridegroom of the Church, yet he deigns to give the same name to the perfect in the Church, of whom it is said: “We speak wisdom among the perfect.” The imperfect are the bride, of whom it is said: “As unto little ones in Christ, I gave you milk to drink, not meat.” Therefore Christ himself, the bridegroom, makes bridegrooms and brides, and yet the Church is one in head and in members.
**“and as a bride”** — He sets out examples of the second comparison, of which the first refers to the bridegroom and the following to the bride.
61.11:
**“For as the earth”** — watered by heavenly rains
**“bringeth forth her bud, and as the garden”** — which desires the waters of springs and rivers
**“as the garden causeth her seed to shoot forth: so shall the Lord God make justice to spring forth”** — Christ, who justifies all
**“and praise”** — of his elect
**“before all the nations”** — not only to the Jews; in which the pride of the Jews is struck down
**“And praise”** — Its own. Whence: “Praise the Lord, all ye nations.” And elsewhere: “O Lord, our Lord,” etc. As the earth and the watered garden send forth their sprouts, so the Church, made fruitful by the Holy Spirit, will render to the Lord the fruit of praise and of good works.

62.1:
**“For Sion's sake”**
• kings and princes
• therefore
• The prophet, in his own person, is greatly gladdened by all the things that the incarnate Son bestows on the world. And this is: for Sion I will not be silent, though he forbid me to speak, though he threaten death.
**“I will not hold my peace”** — rather, I will proclaim the coming of the Lord
**“and for the sake of Jerusalem”** — priests
**“I will not rest”** — from prayers until the Son of God comes; whence elsewhere: “O that thou wouldst rend the heavens, and wouldst come down”
**“till her just one come forth”** — from the womb of the virgin
**“as brightness”** — as brightness: Christ, the splendour of the Father and the sun of justice
**“her just one”** — his just one: from whom is all justice
**“and her saviour”** — and his saviour: Jesus
**“his”** — of the Church
**“as a lamp”** — as a lamp: he who says, “I am the light of the world”
**“be lighted”** — be lighted in the hearts of the faithful
**“as a lamp be lighted”** — A lamp, in Greek, is flame in Latin. Whence: “I am come to cast fire on the earth; and what will I, but that it be kindled?” This is what the apostles, kindled, spoke in various tongues.
62.2:
**“and”** — then
**“The Gentiles shall see”**
• minds by faith
• Whence: “Blessed are they that have not seen,” etc.
**“thy just one”** — Christ
**“thy”** — O primitive Church
**“and all kings”** — the faithful
**“thy glorious one: and”** — then
**“thou shalt be called”** — O Church
**“a new name”** — Christians; and she who before was the synagogue, Sion, Jerusalem, is now the Church.
**“A new name”** — It is the custom of the Hebrews to give new names from new things. For, as they say, Abraham was first called Ram, which they conjecture from this: Heliu the son of Barachel the Buzite, of the kindred of Ram. Then he was called Abram, that is, high father, and at last Abraham. Likewise first Simon, afterwards Peter.
62.3:
**“And thou shalt be a crown of glory in the hand of the Lord”** — power; or in Christ, who is the Father’s hand
**“and a royal diadem”**
• of honour, which the martyrs adorned with their variety
• that the Father may crown his Son with their victories
**“A crown of glory”** — Of the faithful coming from all parts of the world, like a crown.
62.4:
**“Thou shalt no more be called Forsaken”**
• by God
• He addresses the Church of both peoples, as if you were not to be content with this end of names.
**“and thy land”** — habitation
**“shall no more be called Desolate”** — because Christ will be in the midst of you
**“but thou shalt be called My pleasure in her”** — that is, because she does the will of God
**“and thy land inhabited”** — by God
**“Because the Lord hath been well pleased with thee”** — not by your merits, as formerly he was displeased; for all, as much Jews as Gentiles, were sinning
**“and thy land shall be inhabited”** — by God
62.5:
**“For the young man shall dwell with the virgin”** — chastely and holily, as Mary with Joseph; Chrysanthus and Daria
**“and thy children shall dwell in thee”** — spiritual
**“And the bridegroom shall rejoice”** — Christ, of whom it is said: “as a bridegroom coming out of his bride chamber”
**“over the bride”** — the Church, of whom he who has the bride is the bridegroom
**“shall rejoice over thee”** — O Church
**“thy God”** — almighty
**“And shall rejoice”** — For this cause a man shall leave his father and mother. This is a great sacrament in Christ and in the Church.
62.6:
**“Upon thy walls”** — God the Father to Jerusalem
**“Jerusalem”** — O Church, which is the vision of peace.
**“I have appointed watchmen all the day”** — in prosperity
**“and all the night”** — in adversity
**“they shall never hold their peace”**
• Whence we cannot but speak what we have seen and heard.
• from prayers and from preaching
**“You that are mindful”** — The prophet says to the guardians of the walls.
**“of the Lord”** — Therefore, O guardians of the walls, who know the will of the Lord.
**“hold not your peace”** — from prayers and from vows
**“upon the brick walls”** — The apostles, the preachers who fortify the Church, whose guardians are angels. Whence: “Are they not all ministering spirits, sent for the sake of them who shall receive the inheritance of salvation?” Or, the walls of the churches are the disciples of the apostles, whose guardians are the apostles themselves.
62.7:
**“And give him no silence”** — Be instant, in season and out of season, as the widow wearying the hard judge with prayer overcomes him.
**“to the vineyard”** — to the Lord
**“till he establish”** — by confirming
**“and till he make Jerusalem”** — the Church
**“a praise”** — his
**“Till he make Jerusalem”** — That is, either she herself, spread far and wide, is praised everywhere, or she everywhere always praises her Creator.
62.8:
**“hath sworn”**
• firmly and immovably decrees
• That is, through the Son, who is the power of God and the wisdom of God.
**“The Lord”** — the Father
**“by his right hand, and by the arm of his strength: Surely I will no more give thy corn to be meat for thy enemies: and the sons of the strangers shall not drink”** — from faith
**“thy wine, for which thou hast laboured”**
• Aposiopesis.
• by exercising the body with familiar groans and prayers with all strength.
• That is, the praises and works which, when you spent them on idols, the demons ate. But after the coming of the Son, the Lord took delight in them. The wheat also and the wine, the food of the Jews, signified the body and blood of Christ. Whence: “My flesh is meat indeed, and my blood is drink indeed.” This is not received today by heretics, pagans, Jews, the enemies of the Church.
**“By his right hand”** — In the Son. Whence: “Thou hast made all things in wisdom”; he who is both the arm and the strength of the Father, whence: “All things were made by him.”
**“Surely I will no more give thy corn”** — The wheat and wine of the Jews he often gave to their enemies, as is read in the book of Judges, that in the time of harvest the Madianites rushed in and gathered their crops. And when they were led captive, the Samaritans were put in their place to eat their harvests. But in this place he understands the food of the Church to be virtues and good works, the body and blood of Christ.
62.9:
**“For they that gather it”**
• bishops, priests, deacons, ministers of the Church
• gather, by consecrating, prepare
**“shall eat it”**
• the wheat: virtues, or the body of Christ on the altar
• I shall be satisfied when your glory appears.
**“and shall praise the Lord: and they that bring it together”** — the wine
**“shall drink it in my holy courts”**
• the churches
• “In my Father’s house there are many mansions.”
62.10:
**“Go through, go through the gates”**
• as watchmen, foreseeing all things, lest the ministers either fall or grow numb with sleep.
• Through the gates. The ministers of the Church who lead others in. Or the virtues that lead to heaven, as it were from virtue to virtue.
**“prepare”** — by teaching and example
**“a way”** — straight
**“for the people, make the road plain”** — to the one wishing to enter
**“make the road plain”** — By removing stumbling-blocks, in baptism by remitting sins.
**“pick out”** — Or, cast out, according to the Septuagint, which means: remove the hardness of unbelief from men’s hearts, or the reprobate and hard from the fellowship of the faithful.
**“lift up”** — by preaching
**“the standard”** — of the cross, that is, by announcing the passion and resurrection
**“to the people”** — of the nations, not only in Judea
62.11:
**“Behold the Lord hath made it to be heard”** — the faith of the passion and resurrection
**“hath made it to be heard in the ends of the earth”** — through the apostles
**“tell”** — O guards of the walls
**“daughters of Sion”** — of the Church
**“Tell the daughter of Sion”** — That is, the primitive Church, which was first from the Jews. Whence: “The sons of my mother have fought against me.” Or according to that: “But as many as received him, etc.”
**“Behold thy Saviour cometh”** — at the second coming, that is, on the day of judgment, with great power and majesty
**“behold his reward”** — of good and of evil
**“is with him, and his work before him”** — with the power of judging
62.12:
**“And they shall call them”** — the apostles and other teachers, rejoicing with those whom they won
**“And they shall call him”** — Saying: you are a holy people, you are redeemed by the Lord God; for so some copies have it.
**“The holy people, the redeemed”** — otherwise: redeemed
**“of the Lord”** — the people, that is, by God; so the Hebrew truth has it, so says Jerome, and the plain sense.
**“But thou”** — O Church
**“shalt be called: A city sought after”** — by God
**“and not forsaken”** — by the blood of the Son. Whence: “The Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost.” For this is the sheep which the good shepherd came to seek, the others being left in the desert.

63.1:
**“Who is this”**
• this in the person of the angels, as if of those who do not understand the mystery and therefore ask
• how great, how powerful, how wonderful, with so great an army
• Who is this, etc. Certain angels, not fully knowing the mystery of the incarnation, passion and resurrection, seeing the Lord ascend to heaven with a multitude of angels and holy men by his own power, not by the help of angels, marvel at the mystery of the incarnation and passion and resurrection and ascension, and at how he opens the kingdom of heaven for himself and for others. Whence also they say to the angels accompanying the Lord: Who is this that cometh from Edom? And David likewise: “Who is this King of Glory?” Yet Augustine seems to say on Genesis that all the angels, from their very creation, at once knew in the contemplation of their creator whatever he was to do. But Jerome openly declares that certain angels did not know fully until the mystery of the incarnation was accomplished.
**“that cometh”** — into heaven
**“from Edom”** — the world
**“From Edom”** — Edom, from the eating of the red lentil, for which he sold his birthright. Or it is interpreted as heat; for it means earthly or bloody, and signifies the world. Esau means oaken or strong as oak. Seir, rough, that is, hairy. Here, however, according to the interpretation, it signifies not the man himself but the world. So also Bosra, that is, fortified or strong, signifies here not its own thing but, according to its interpretation, hell, where the souls were held firmly as if under many guards; whence: “Who will bring me into the strong city?” Or the earthly Jerusalem, which was fortified with very strong walls, in which the Lord suffered. Whence Homer, according to Josephus, Jerome says, from whom Jerusalem is interpreted fortified or strong. Bosra, however, is a city situated neither in the promised land nor in Edom but in Moab. Therefore Christ came from the bloody world; “he came from Bosra with dyed garments,” that is, with bodily members, from the fortified city, namely Jerusalem, where he suffered. Or from hell despoiled, a victor with his faithful.
**“dyed”** — first by blood, that is, on the cross; or because his scars then also appeared
**“garments”** — bodily limbs
**“from Bosra, this”** — who is this
**“beautiful one”** — “Beautiful in form above the sons of men”
**“in his robe”**
• in the appearance of humanity
• Beautiful, etc. Beautiful, warm. Whence beautiful as if warm, because from heat the face becomes red and rosy, and thence comely.
**“walking”**
• or walking above all the heavens
• needing no help
**“in the greatness of his strength”**
• or of strength
• or in the fullness of his divinity
• to whom judgment has been given
**“I, that speak”** — the angels being silent, he himself answers
**“justice”** — rendering to each according to his works
**“and am a defender”** — against demons
**“to save”**
• the human race
• murderers, adulterers and the like
63.2:
**“Why then”**
• again the angels ask
• if you are such
• As if the angels were to say: We have learned that thou speakest justice and that the salvation of all is in thy judgment; but we wish to know why thy garments are as if dyed with must, and why the tunic, which is woven from the top and cannot be torn, and which from the virginal womb had such whiteness as no fuller on earth can make, is stained with blood. Mercy befits thee more than cruelty. To them it is answered: “I have trodden the winepress alone.”
**“red”** — with your blood
**“is thy apparel”** — the body
**“and thy garments”**
• the limbs red like black must, somewhat reddened
• as if these things did not belong to you, but to murderers and adulterers and the like
63.3:
**“I have trodden the winepress alone”**
• Christ answers the questioners so fully that there is no need to ask further; thus the winepress
• although trodden, I rose on the third day
• I alone endured the pressure of the cross
• The winepress is put for the punishments of sinners, whence Jeremias: “The Lord hath trodden the winepress for the virgin daughter of Juda.” Sometimes for the gathering of new fruits. Whence some Psalms are entitled in a good sense for winepresses.
• Alone, etc. Alone Samson, with his hair cut, is set before the Philistines; neither angel nor archangel nor any celestial spirit, nor finally any helper of the human race, whether Gentile or Jew. He fights alone, he alone overcomes.
**“I have trodden the winepress”** — Namely the cross and all the torments of the passion, in which, pressed as in a press, even blood was poured out.
**“and of the Gentiles”** — all the apostles fled, leaving him
**“there is not a man with me”**
• to help me
• nor Peter
**“I have trodden”** — although slain
**“them”** — The Jews, demons.
**“in my wrath”**
• vengeance
• Fury is sudden anger; wrath is long-lasting. Whence: “Fury is brief anger.”
**“And I have trodden them down”** — taking away from the demons the rule of the world, and from the Jews place, and from the nation priesthood, temple, and all dignity, through the Romans
**“in my indignation, and their blood is sprinkled”** — my
**“their”** — shed by them
**“upon my garments”** — limbs
**“and”** — that is
**“I have stained all my apparel”**
• by their opinion
• I permitted to be defiled
• on the demons or on the Jews
• It is sprinkled, etc. My blood, shed by their rancor, by the persuasion of demons. Whence: the devil put it into the heart of Judas to betray him, etc. Their blood was shed by persuasion, and they themselves were conquered and slain in the same place. Similarly the blood of Christ is called the blood of the Jews, because they shed it and from it endured vengeance. And it is said by comparison with the victor and the vanquished, whose blood is often sprinkled upon the garments of the victor.
63.4:
**“For the day of vengeance is in my heart”**
• while I hung on the cross
• because
**“the year”** — an acceptable time
**“of my redemption”**
• or of recompense
• of the human race
63.5:
**“I looked about”** — on the cross, whence I looked to the right and saw, and there was none who knew me
**“and there was none”** — to me
**“to help”** — anyone
**“I sought, and there was none to give aid”** — a helper, whence I looked for one who would grieve with me at once, and there was none who would comfort, and I did not find one
**“and there was none to give aid”** — Whence: “All my friends have forsaken me”; and “my acquaintance like strangers have departed from me.”
**“and my own arm hath saved for me”** — he made salvation for me, namely the resurrection
**“my own arm”** — the Word united to flesh; or my strength saved for me all predestined to life
**“and my indignation itself”** — vengeance on the Jews and demons
**“and my indignation itself hath helped me”** — Jerome to Augustine and Alypius. Avoiding the impiety of Sabellius, we distinguish three persons, expressed under their own property: not saying that he is Father to himself, Son to himself, Holy Spirit to himself, but saying that the person of the Father is one, that of the Son another, that of the Holy Spirit another. For we confess not only the names but also the properties of the names.
63.6:
**“And I have trodden down the people”** — the Jews
**“in my wrath, and have made them drunk in my indignation”** — I filled with affliction and misery, through the Romans
**“them in my indignation, and have brought down in the earth”** — to nothing
**“their strength”** — of the Jews or of the demons
63.7:
**“I will remember the tender mercies of the Lord”** — pressed by the weight of evils
**“The tender mercies of the Lord”** — The prophet, in the person of the penitent Jewish people, acknowledging the mercy of the Lord.
**“the praise of the Lord”**
• signs and miracles
• preaching that “the Lord is just in all his ways”
**“for all the things”** — good or evil things, which for our sins
**“that the Lord hath bestowed”** — for the evil things
**“upon us, and for the multitude of his good things”** — of gifts
**“to the house of Israel, which he hath given them according to his kindness”** — not their merits
**“and”** — that is
**“according to the multitude of his mercies”** — or of mercies
**“According to his kindness”** — For as though led into Babylon for our sins, we have been brought back by his mercy.
63.8:
**“And he said”** — The Lord, that is, seeing their penance
**“Surely they are my people”** — Israel
**“are”** — because, that is, they are
**“children that will not deny”**
• me
• as others
• or those sons, that is, are of the people not denying, of the patriarchs and prophets who truly believed in me
**“And he is become”** — the Lord
**“their”** — to the penitent
63.9:
**“In all their affliction”** — in Egypt, in the desert
**“he was not troubled”** — or the Saviour himself suffered with them
**“He was not troubled”** — The word which is “lo” among the Hebrews is ambiguous, and signifies “not” or “and he himself.” Whence we can read it either way, namely: in all their affliction he was not troubled, by compassion, but for a time put off help, that he might compel them to ask. Or he himself was troubled, having compassion at last on their injuries and miseries. And he sent them an angel who should save them, namely Michael, who was set over that people. Whence: “There is none that is my helper, but Michael your prince, who standeth up for the children of my people.”
**“and the angel of his presence saved them”**
• Whence their angels always see the face of the Father, etc., because they are always in the presence of God
• not by their merits
**“in his love, and in his mercy”** — of his mercy
**“he redeemed them”** — from Egypt, from Babylon, or from eternal death in the blood of the Son
**“and he carried them”** — from Egypt into the land of promise. Whence: “He spread his wings, and hath taken them and carried them on his shoulders.”
**“and lifted them up”** — above the other nations
**“all the days of old”** — from the beginning, from when he chose them as a people
63.10:
**“But they provoked to wrath, and afflicted the spirit of his Holy One”** — or holy
**“and he was turned”** — and he was turned: because before he was a friend, healing the sick and raising the dead
**“their”** — to those acting wickedly
**“enemy”**
• in opinion
• the avenger of evil
**“and he fought”** — by the Romans, in the fortieth, the other year of the ascension
**“against them”**
• the enemies being sent against them
• not willing to believe; for this can refer to the time of the incarnation
• The spirit of his holy one. Some copies have, but the Holy Spirit, whom he grieves who grieves the spiritual man. Whence: “He that toucheth you, toucheth the apple of my eye.” Or the angel sent to guard them, whom they often offended by doing evil.
**“the spirit of his Holy One”** — Of Moses. Whence: “They provoked Moses in the camp, Aaron the holy one of the Lord.” Or, his holy one: Christ, whom they would not believe. For the Son of God, who redeemed us, freed them from Egypt and from the Red Sea.
63.11:
**“And he remembered the days of old of Moses”** — afterwards turned to mercy for Moses the servant, who prayed for them in the desert: either forgive them or blot me out of the book
**“Moses”** — Because there is no one else who prays for them.
**“of his people”** — saved by the prayer of Moses
**“Where is he that”** — namely Moses
**“brought them up out of the sea, with the shepherds of his flock”** — Moses and Aaron, Mary, Ur and others
**“of his flock”** — the ineffable mercy of God
**“Where is he that brought them up”** — The prophet, seeing the abjection, misery and affliction of his people now impending on account of the denial of the Son of God, grieving exclaims, saying: where is he, etc. As if it were the clemency of the Almighty.
**“where is he that put in the midst of them”** — of the people
**“wind”** — the Paraclete
**“of his Holy One”**
• of the Son
• Where is he that put, etc. Of Moses, namely, because at Moses’ prayer the Lord took of his spirit and gave it to seventy men.
63.12:
**“He that brought out”** — out of Egypt
**“by the right hand, Moses”** — prosperously
**“by the arm”**
• by the Son, who is the power and virtue of the Father
• “who divided the Red Sea into parts,” namely into twelve ways
**“of his majesty”** — where is his power
**“that divided the waters”** — the Red Sea
**“before them, to make himself an everlasting name”** — praise
**“that divided”** — As is said: when Moses had struck the sea and split it into twelve ways, and others hesitating, the tribe of Juda entered, and for this reason obtained the dignity of the kingdom.
63.13:
**“that led them through the deep”** — the depths of the sea
**“as a horse in the wilderness that stumbleth not”** — without hindrance
63.14:
**“as a beast in the field”** — with an unhindered course
**“that goeth down”** — that is, they went down into the land of promise
**“the spirit of the Lord”** — for that reason, namely, it could not stumble, because the Spirit of the Lord, etc.
**“was their leader”**
• of the people
• without offence
• into the land of promise
**“so didst thou lead thy people, to make thyself”** — through so many miracles
**“a glorious name”** — glorious
**“The spirit of the Lord”** — Namely an angel, whence also: “My angel shall go before thee.” For spirit is the name of nature; angel, of office.
63.15:
**“Look down from heaven”**
• in the person of the penitent people
• our misery
• The Lord is everywhere whole and always; whence: “I fill heaven and earth.” Yet he is said to have his seat in heaven, according to that: “Heaven is my seat”; he who sits in the heavenly angels and just men, whose conversation, that is, is in heaven, and in whom his will is especially done.
**“and see”**
• have mercy, according to that: “I have seen the affliction of my people”
• who have done so great things for us
**“from thy holy habitation”** — to the angels and other just ones
**“and the place of thy glory, where is”** — whence I will no longer be angry with you, and my zeal has departed from you
**“thy zeal”** — with which you loved us and our fathers
**“and thy strength”**
• because you led out our fathers
• where is
**“the multitude of thy bowels”** — of affections toward us
**“and of thy mercies”** — as if God would forget to show mercy
**“they have held back themselves from me”** — Where is thy zeal. As if to say: because we have sinned and you began to hate us, your zeal has departed; with it departing, strength departs, and the affection of paternal bowels is overcome.
63.16:
**“for thou”** — because we offended you: he does not know his sons
**“our father”** — creator
**“and Abraham hath not known us”** — Augustine says: because the dead, even the saints, do not know what the living do, even their children
**“and Israel hath been ignorant of us”** — namely Jacob. Isaac would also have been added, had he not meant the middle to be understood through the extremes
**“thou, O Lord, art our father”** — creator
**“our redeemer, from everlasting”** — endures
**“by thy name”**
• praise
• Abraham knew us not, etc. Abraham was called from the Gentiles to the faith, and according to the quality of his former and later condition he obtained a change of name. Jacob also acquired, with much labour, to be called Israel; whence Abraham had three wives, Jacob four. Isaac kept his old name to the end, and, signifying the chastity of the Church, was content with one wife. These, therefore, who pray out of worse things, take on the likeness of a change to a better state of those to whom joys succeeded after sorrows. And this is what they ask: that he who is their father may not forget his sons, lest through them the name of God be blasphemed among the Gentiles.
**“And Abraham hath not known”** — Because we have offended him, he does not acknowledge his sons to be his sons; for we have departed from God, unlike him. For this reason he does not pray for us, because he would obtain nothing. Whence to Jeremias: “Do not thou pray for this people... for I will not hear thee”; for perverse sons cannot be delivered by the prayer of holy fathers. Whence to Ezechiel: “If there be three men in the midst of Jerusalem, Noe, Daniel, and Job, they shall deliver neither son nor daughter, but they shall only deliver their own souls by their justice”; and likewise of Jacob.
63.17:
**“Why hast thou made us to err”**
• you permitted
• Paul, writing to the Corinthians, that is, to the people of one city, because of the variety of its inhabitants, saints that is and sinners, now praises, now reproves; so the present chapter, which is woven from the prayer of the people of the Lord entreating God, now praises the Lord, now accuses him, according to the second rule of Tyconius, which concerns the mixed body of the Lord.
**“O Lord, from thy ways”**
• commandments
• the cause of error and hardness seems to be that he does not correct the offenders
**“why hast thou hardened our heart”** — you allowed it to be hardened, withholding the scourges, according to that: “I will harden the heart of Pharao,” etc.
**“that we should not fear thee”**
• or: convert
• to mercy
• Abraham and Israel, who did not know us
**“for the sake of thy servants”** — our fathers
**“the tribes”** — that is
**“of thy inheritance”** — or of possession
63.18:
**“They have possessed as nothing”** — without fight, without labour
**“thy people”** — us
**“holy”** — formerly
**“our enemies have trodden down thy sanctuary”** — Chaldeans, Babylonians, Romans
**“have trodden down thy sanctuary”** — the temple
63.19:
**“We are become as in the beginning”** — without God
**“when thou didst not rule over us, and when we were not called by thy name”** — while the people of God are not called
**“As in the beginning”** — Before you called us in Abraham. Or when in Egypt we worshipped idols, without king, without prince, without prophets, without God, without law, without priest; which things were in part fulfilled at the coming of Christ, and wholly after his ascension. And they are fulfilled daily according to that curse: “His blood be upon us,” etc. For so long as they remain in the old age of the law and do not receive the truth of the gospel, they will not be called the people of God, that is, Christians, from Christ.

64.1:
**“That thou wouldst rend the heavens”**
• because our enemies have trodden down thy sanctuary
• by coming near, by fulfilling the promises
• Isaias speaks in his own person and in that of all the prophets who desired the coming of Christ, foreseeing the coming of the Son, the rejection of his people, and the calling of the Gentile. And this is: “Oh that thou wouldst rend the heavens.” Likewise David: “And he bowed the heavens, and came down.”
**“and wouldst come down”**
• visible in the flesh
• Stir up, O Lord, thy power, and come
**“at thy presence”**
• from the majesty
• by which invisible to us
• because if thou shouldst come down, from the face, that is, from the presence
**“the mountains”** — the pride of the Jews or of demons
64.2:
**“As the burning”** — wood, hay, stubble: “For our God is a consuming fire.”
**“They would melt, the waters would burn with fire”** — this sentence being received, this will be fulfilled on the day of judgment, “Depart into everlasting fire”; yet daily it is in part fulfilled
**“The waters would burn”** — Symmachus. The waters of the sea would burn with fire; that is, the peoples of the world would be inflamed with the fire of charity. Whence: “I am come to cast fire on the earth; and what will I, but that it be kindled?” And so thy name, which is Jesus, would be made known to thy enemies, that is, the Jews.
**“That thy name might be made known”** — through power
**“by thy name”** — Jesus
**“to thy enemies”** — demons, Jews, any adversaries
**“that the nations might tremble at thy presence”**
• the Gentiles moved to penance
• another translation has: they will be moved
64.3:
**“when”** — yet
**“thou shalt do wonderful things”**
• incarnate
• by raising the dead and other such things
**“we shall not bear them”** — your coming
**“thou didst come down”** — into the virgin’s womb, that is, “And the Word was made flesh”
**“and at thy presence”** — presence
**“the mountains”** — Jews, demons
**“We shall not bear them”** — We Jews; but we shall blaspheme, saying: “In the prince of devils he casteth out devils.” For the prophet says this in the person of unbelievers.
**“Thou didst come down”** — As though his prayers were heard, he says: “Thou didst come down.”
**“The mountains melted away”** — Their power lost. Whence now the prince of this world shall be cast out. And it is said to the Jews: “the kingdom of God shall be taken from you”, namely the holy Scripture and all glory and all dignity.
64.4:
**“From the beginning”** — from the beginning of the world
**“They have not heard, nor with the ears”** — of the body, because there is no sound
**“perceived”** — the good things, namely
**“the eye”** — and
**“the eye hath not seen, O God, besides thee, what things thou hast prepared for them that wait for thee”**
• or those who wait
• From the beginning of the world they have not heard, etc. Hence Paul takes the testimony to the Corinthians, not word for word but expressing the sense.
**“The eye hath not seen”** — Because he is not a body or a colour. What the apostle puts: it has not “entered into the heart of man”, because the heart, that is, ought to be directed to that which is greater; for he has prepared himself, the knowledge of himself, the knowledge of the holy Trinity. Whence: “Now this is eternal life: that they may know thee, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom thou hast sent.” This no one can see. Whence that saying: “No man hath seen God at any time.”
64.5:
**“Thou hast met him that rejoiceth”** — visible, as to Simeon, or in help, as to David, the Maccabees, and others
**“and doth justice”** — as to Simeon rejoicing at your coming, of whom: “Simeon, just and devout, waiting for the consolation of Israel”, etc.
**“in thy ways”** — in your commands
**“they shall remember”**
• as the same Anna
• but
**“behold thou art angry”** — because, namely
**“and we have sinned”**
• whence these evils to us
• hysteron proteron
**“in them”** — in the sins themselves
**“we have been always, and we shall be saved”**
• by your grace, not by our merits
• Behold thou, etc. In the person of the unbelieving people who, wishing to pass over to the truth of the gospel, put forward with the mouth a penitence that they did not have in the heart.
64.6:
**“And we are all become as one unclean”** — a leper
**“all of us as the rag”** — than which nothing is more unclean
**“menstruous”**
• menstruous woman
• are
**“Menstruous”** — Mene in Hebrew is luna in Latin. Whence menstruous women, who are wont to suffer a flow of blood every month, and at that time men ought to abstain from them. For then the condemned are conceived, with their limbs blind, lame, leprous, and the like. And because the parents were not ashamed to be joined together in their chamber, their sins are laid open to all and openly rebuked in their little ones.
**“all our justices”** — circumcision and offering, the sacrifice after death, namely of the true lamb
**“and we have fallen”** — slain by the Romans
**“as a leaf”** — lightly
**“and our iniquities”** — in Christ
**“like the wind”**
• leaves
• the wicked, like dust which the wind casts from the face
• temptation of demons, persecution of the Romans
**“have taken us away”**
• from our land, from thy presence
• because we have fallen like leaves
**“The wind”** — A stirring of the air, as there: “He commanded the winds and the sea.” Or the Holy Spirit, as there: “of a mighty wind coming.” For here spirit is put for wind in the signification of the Holy Spirit. Or the temptation of demons and wicked men, as that: “the floods came, and the winds blew”; and this is as it were a wind.
64.7:
**“There is none that calleth upon thy name”** — for us, in voice, heart, and work
**“that riseth up”**
• strong in adversity, for prayer
• from the ruin of iniquities
**“and taketh hold of thee”**
• with prayers
• as Moses: “Do not pour out thy wrath upon us.”
• Whence: “I found him whom my soul loveth: I held him, and will not let him go.”
**“thou hast hid thy face from us”** — mercy, presence, help
**“and hast crushed us in the hand of our iniquity”** — by the work by which vices hold us, as with hands; whence: “Death and life are in the power of the tongue.”
64.8:
**“And now, O Lord, thou art our father”** — Whence: “I have begotten sons and exalted them,” etc., and “Israel is my son, my firstborn.”
**“we are clay”** — the mud of the earth
**“and thou art our maker”** — moulder
**“and we all are the works of thy hands”**
• therefore we cannot resist thy will
• as: “Thy hands have made me, and fashioned me wholly round about,” etc.
• And now, O Lord. As if he said: If we consider our merits, we must despair; if we consider thy mercy, thou who scourgest every son whom thou receivest, we dare to pour out prayers, for thou art our father.
• The mystery of the Trinity: right confession is the ignorance of knowledge.
**“The works of thy hands”** — As if: look upon thy work, not our merits.
64.9:
**“Be not”** — therefore
**“be angry”** — to thy work
**“very, O Lord”**
• too much
• that is
**“and remember no longer”** — even according to justice, because we cannot bear it
**“our iniquity”** — but of your work
**“behold, see we are all thy people”** — we were once, to wit
**“we are all”** — Be not very angry, etc. That is, we do not shun wrath, nor seek patience any longer, through which we store up wrath for the day of vengeance. But we beg you: be not angry with us too much, and in the time of vengeance do not remember our iniquity.
64.10:
**“a city”** — which the force of the river gladdens, and in which once was the watchtower of virtues
**“of thy sanctuary”** — of the sanctuary of your temple
**“is made a desert”** — by you
**“Sion is made a desert”**
• by you
• Sion and Jerusalem in this place signify the same: the temple, that is, and the city, where once was the watchtower of virtues and the vision of peace. But after the people of the Jews denied Christ their king and added, “We have no king but Caesar,” Jerusalem was forsaken by God; whence “your house shall be left to you desolate,” and that: “Arise, let us go hence.” And in the temple (as the Ecclesiastical History says) voices were heard: “Let us depart from these seats.”
64.11:
**“the house”** — the temple
**“of our holiness”** — where we were sanctified, we sacrificed, we gloried
**“and of our glory, where our fathers praised thee, is burnt with fire”** — burned by the Romans
**“and all our lovely things are turned into ruins”** — the holy of holies
**“The house”** — Allegorically. The house of God is the Church, and every faithful soul, which at times is corrupted by the fires of lust and of avarice.
64.12:
**“Wilt thou refrain thyself, O Lord, upon these things”** — our miseries, the crimes of enemies
**“Wilt thou refrain thyself, O Lord”** — from mercy
**“wilt thou hold thy peace”** — blaspheming adversaries
**“and afflict”** — forever
**“us”** — humble
**“vehemently”**
• not in the usual manner
• as one hard, disdaining to hear us

65.1:
**“They have sought me”** — the nations, through faith
**“that before”**
• before I was made man
• A people, which I knew not, hath served me
**“asked not for me, they have found me”** — that I am merciful
**“that”** — who before
**“sought me not. I said”**
• taking the form of a servant
• The Son, who before said to Moses: I am who am
**“Behold me, behold me, to”** — that I might make one, of the name of Christian, out of all nations
**“a nation that did not call upon my name”**
• who did not know me
• They have sought, etc. To this the Son replies: “Why hast thou made us to err from thy ways?” As if to say: if strangers seeking me found me so merciful, it is not my cruelty that denies you help, but your iniquity and your impenitent heart. Whence: “A people which I knew not hath served me; strange children have lied to me.”
65.2:
**“I have spread forth my hands”** — as one generous, denying nothing to the penitent
**“all the day”** — of the passion
**“to an unbelieving people”** — Of the Jews.
**“who walk in a way that is not good”**
• Having left Christ, who is the way.
• broad and fair, which leads to death.
**“after their own thoughts”**
• wicked.
• from my secret ones cleanse me.
• I have spread forth my hands all the day, etc. Praying for them on the cross: “Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do”; or that I might receive them and place them in my bosom. Or by bestowing the benefits of works, from the time I brought them out of Egypt. Made flesh also, I healed their sick, I raised their dead, I fed them with a few loaves. Yet they have always remained unbelieving.
65.3:
**“A people”**
• Whence: “This people honoureth me with their lips, but their heart is far from me,” etc.
• This the people did.
**“that continually provoke me to anger”** — vengeance.
**“provoke me”** — by eagerness in sinning.
**“before my face”**
• openly, which is worse.
• that is, in my temple they set up idols, in which I have often shown my patience.
• to whom all things are open.
**“that continually”** — joining lust to idolatry with strange gods.
**“immolate in gardens, and sacrifice”**
• to demons.
• incense.
**“upon bricks”** — they made several altars in place of the one altar that was in the temple, and sacrificed upon them.
**“A people that continually provoke me to anger”** — Allegorically. Every heretic provokes God to anger; in the falsity of doctrine he offers unclean sacrifices, not to abide for ever, but like gardens, green for a short time. For he provides for the delights of the flesh; whence “all flesh is grass.” Hence too is praised the saying of that wisest man among the Greeks, who calls all the pleasures of the world, and the pomp of the world, and swiftly passing luxury, the gardens of Adonis. And heretics sacrifice upon bricks when they desire to confirm choice falsehoods by the art of dialectic, and to build them square, and to strengthen them with lines cut in the brick of dust.
65.4:
**“That dwell in sepulchres”** — of the dead, which the Jews make in the manner of houses.
**“and sleep in the temple of idols”** — that is, upon the skins of the victims, so that they might dream of the future.
**“in the temple of idols”** — Shrines are so called from delere, to blot out, because there the soul was thought to be washed. Or because near them were pools where both the priest and the victim were washed.
*Allegorically:* Heretics sleep in the memorials of their masters and in caves; leaving the light of the Holy Spirit and the upper room in which the apostles dwelt, they abide in the darkness of the devil, and love caves, of which: “but you have made it a den.” They believe in dreams and fancies. They eat the flesh of swine, of whom it is said: “Cast not your pearls before swine”; and the profane broth, which in their books is seasoned by heretical art. Their vessels are unclean, both of doctrine, that is, and of bodies. And they come to such madness that whoever is not like them they detest as lost.
**“that eat”** — against the precept of the law.
**“swine's flesh, and profane broth”** — of swine.
65.5:
**“That say”**
• unclean.
• others, to one not eating, not worshipping idols.
**“Depart from me, come not near me, because thou art unclean”** — who do such things and are proud against others.
**“these shall be smoke”**
• nothing.
• and.
**“in my anger, a fire”**
• will be.
• of hell.
**“burning”** — in them.
**“all the day”** — always.
**“in my anger”** — We ought to take fury, forgetfulness, anger, repentance in this way in God, just as hands, feet, eyes, ears, and the other members which he is said to have: not that he lies open to these disturbances, he who extinguishes them in us, but through our words we understand God’s disposition toward us.
65.6:
**“Behold it is written before me”** — their evil, that I may not forget.
**“I will not be silent, but I will render”** — Nay, I will say: Depart, you cursed, into everlasting fire.
**“and repay into their bosom”** — into the inner parts of the mind, that they may be tormented by their own conscience.
**“I will not be silent”** — He who said above, “I have always held my peace, I have kept silence, I have been patient,” now says, “I will not be silent,” that is, I will spare no longer, nor endure their iniquities.
65.7:
**“Your iniquities, and the iniquities of your fathers”** — of idolaters.
**“the iniquities of your fathers”** — That is, that you may be punished not only for your own sins but also for the iniquities of your fathers, whom you have imitated. For otherwise the son does not bear the iniquity of the father.
**“saith the Lord”** — that you may be punished as those whom you imitated, and so in a sense are their sons.
**“who have sacrificed”** — sons and daughters to demons.
**“upon the mountains and upon the hills have reproached me”** — by despising me and sacrificing to idols.
**“who have sacrificed upon”** — When they worshipped the golden calves in Bethel and in Dan. A heretic too, despising the simplicity of the Church, sacrifices on the mountains and reproaches God while he despises his precepts.
**“and I will measure back their first work”** — by measuring out punishment for fault, or by measuring.
**“in their bosom”** — in the soul after judgment, and in the body, where “their worm dieth not, and the fire is not extinguished.”
65.8:
**“Thus saith the Lord: As if a grain be found”** — after the storm.
**“a grain”** — unharmed.
**“in a cluster, and it be said”** — if one wishing to touch it.
**“Destroy it not”** — let it grow.
**“because it is a blessing”**
• that is, it pleased the Lord to reserve it, as a blessing, from so great an abundance.
• by reserving some.
**“so will I do for the sake of my servants”** — Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, to whom the promise was made; or for those who serve me among many sinners.
**“that I may not destroy the whole”**
• the human race.
• As if, etc. As though I would not destroy the good for the sake of the wicked, but “as if, etc.” For he had said that Israel would perish.
65.9:
**“A seed out of Jacob”** — The seed of Jacob and of Juda: the apostles, possessing other mountains, that is, believers eminent in virtues. Whence: “Unless the Lord of Sabaoth had left us a seed, we had been made as Sodom.”
**“And I will bring forth ... out of Jacob”** — “The sceptre shall not be taken away from Juda,” etc.
**“seed”** — Christ, the grain in the cluster above.
**“and out of Juda a possessor of my mountains”** — the apostles; whence: “I have lifted up my eyes to the mountains,” and elsewhere: “Mountains are round about it,” etc.
**“Holy mountains”** — Septuagint. My mountain, that is, Christ, who is the mountain of mountains. For the mountains are the apostles, who from the Jews possessed Christ, in whom they were founded.
**“and shall inherit”** — that is, the inheritance of which: “I will give thee the Gentiles for thy inheritance.”
**“it”** — that is, the Church.
**“And shall inherit”** — Whence: “O ye seed of Abraham his servant; ye sons of Jacob his chosen.” Whoever are as yet seed and not formed into sons are servants of the Lord, to whom it is said: “I know that you are the seed of Abraham,” not yet sons. But he who is a son of the Lord is chosen. Whence the elect possess Jerusalem, the servants dwell in it; whence: “You have not received the spirit of bondage again in fear, but the spirit of adoption of sons.”
**“my elect”** — the apostles; whence: “You have not chosen me: but I have chosen you.”
**“and my servants”** — the faithful.
65.10:
**“And the plains shall be turned to folds”** — Churches
**“of flocks”** — of the faithful, who had but one heart and one soul
**“and the valley of Achor into a place for the herds to lie down in”** — rest
**“to my people”** — faithful, that is
**“that have sought me”**
• these things will be done for them, that is, for those who sought me
• by faith and work
**“Plains”** — Others: pastures. Whence the Lord will reveal the thickets of the woods, so that robbers cease to lurk there, and beasts and poisonous animals pass into the Church of God.
**“to folds of flocks”** — Another translation has Saron, which is a region between Joppa and Lydda and Ramma, fertile and rich in pasture but infested by robbers; whence it is interpreted “a valley pouring out blood.”
**“And the valley of Achor”** — Where Achor the son of Charmi, having stolen from the spoils of Jericho, perished with all his house, the place is called the valley of Achor, that is, of trouble or tumult, in which the Gentile world is signified, as also by Saron, which is interpreted a valley pouring out blood, which, full of the shedding of blood, abode in the tumult and trouble of vices. But Achor was turned into folds of flocks, or sheepfolds, and into a place for the herds to lie down in, that is, the Churches, and the rest of the preachers and of the other faithful, who are designated by the herds and the flocks of sheep.
**“for the herds”** — Of preachers, who arm and defend the Church. For “herd” (armentum) is so called from arming (armando).
65.11:
**“And you”** — O Jews
**“that have forsaken the Lord, that have forgotten my holy mount”** — the temple, which is on the mountain; or the heavenly Jerusalem; or Christ, who is the mountain of mountains
**“that set”** — another translation: you prepare
**“And you, that have forsaken”** — Allegorically. All who forsake the Church and forget the holy mount of God, giving themselves up to spirits of error or unclean spirits and to the doctrines of devils, prepare a table for fortune, and believing that nothing pertains to God but that all things are governed by the course of the stars or the changeableness of fortune, these shall be handed over to eternal punishments, so that none of them can escape.
**“for fortune”** — The goddess of the Egyptians, to whom at the end of the year they offered a table laden with all kinds of food and cups mixed with honeyed wine; either because she had provided a happy year, or because she would provide a happy one to come.
65.12:
**“I will number you”** — lest anyone escape
**“in the sword”** — by any affliction
**“and you shall all fall by slaughter”**
• by oppression; for not all are slain, or all afflicted
• of the Chaldeans, of the Romans, of demons
**“for”** — beyond the rest
**“because I called”** — I did all that I ought.
**“Because I called”** — Saying through the prophets: “Be converted to me, and you shall be saved.” And through himself: “Do penance.” And elsewhere: “Come to me, all you that labour, and are burdened, and I will refresh you.”
**“and you did not answer”** — by obeying, by following
**“I spoke”**
• present with us, Emmanuel
• in parables
**“and you did not hear”** — in mind
**“and you did”** — moreover
**“evil in my eyes”** — because I see all things, or those worshipping idols in the temple
**“and the things”** — idolatry
**“you have chosen the things that displease me”** — God wills one thing, and permits another.
65.13:
**“Therefore”**
• evil, that is
• that you asked for Barabbas, a doer of murder and sedition.
**“Therefore thus saith the Lord God: Behold my servants shall eat, and you shall be hungry: behold my servants shall drink”** — my blood
**“and you shall be thirsty”** — living water
**“Behold my servants”** — As if to say: you will not only fall by the sword for your iniquities, but will also hunger and thirst in the present. But the Gentiles, converted to the faith, will in the present be satisfied with the food of the body, and with the blood of the Lord, and with spiritual teaching, and at the end with the vision of the Trinity.
**“shall eat”** — My body. Whence: “they who eat the flesh of the Son of man.” Or spiritual teaching, the mysteries of faith. Or in the future, the knowledge of the godhead; whence: “that you may eat and drink at my table in the kingdom of my Father.” And “I shall be satisfied when thy glory shall appear.”
65.14:
**“Behold my servants shall rejoice”** — in eternal blessedness; whence: “your joy no man shall take from you.”
**“and you shall be confounded”** — seeing others have succeeded in your place
**“behold my servants shall praise for joyfulness of heart”** — according to that: “Let praise be to thee for ever.”
**“and you shall cry”** — in hell
**“for sorrow of heart”** — the conscience of sinners
**“and shall howl for grief of spirit”** — whence: “there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth”; or at the judgment, with the kids set on the left and the sheep on the right
65.15:
**“And you shall leave your name”**
• others succeeding in your place
• So that some, affirming, may say: If I shall have done otherwise, let it befall me as it did the Jews slain by the sword of the Romans. Or thus: I swear by God, in whom the Jews once believed. Or because their oath was God, which Christians now swear, compelled by necessity: that is, “the Lord liveth.”
• So that you may not even have this name, of him who says: “I am the way, the truth, and the life.” Nor shall you be called circumcision, but concision.
**“for an execration”** — sacred
**“to my elect”** — that they may be called sons of Abraham, as you once were
**“and the Lord God shall slay thee”** — by the spiritual sword in judgment
**“the Lord God shall call his servants by another name”** — Christian
65.16:
**“In whom”** — in which: by the name or by Christ
**“he that is blessed upon the earth”**
• a Christian, so called, who has kept that very name well in this land
• that is, now
**“shall be blessed in God, amen”** — in the future; whence: “Come, blessed of my Father,” etc., and elsewhere: “that you may possess the blessing by inheritance.”
**“and he that sweareth”**
• faithfully and truly
• speaks the truth
**“shall swear by God, amen”** — on this day of judgment he will praise God truly and faithfully
**“for”** — with eternal goods succeeding, he wipes away [garbled in the printing: d o la a o s]
**“the former distresses are forgotten”** — The former distresses are forgotten, so that the former distress is not to be remembered as part of the evils.
**“Because they are forgotten”** — That they may not remember the idols and the former error, not by forgetfulness of memory but by the kindling of good things. Whence: “In the good day, forgetfulness of good things,” and elsewhere: “The affliction of an hour maketh one forget great delights.” And perhaps in the future also the memory of the former way of life will be wholly blotted out.
65.17:
**“For behold I create”** — he joins himself to them, because he too suffered much, sawn with a wooden saw by the Jews
**“new heavens”** — holy ones who are renewed daily; whence: “I will see thy heavens,” etc.
**“and a new earth”**
• good
• which bears fruit in patience
• by improving its qualities and changing them; whence John: “And I saw a new heaven and a new earth”; and the apostle: the figure of this world passes away.
**“and the former things shall not be in remembrance”** — evil torments
**“and they shall not come up”** — in your memory, namely
**“upon the heart”** — your
65.18:
**“But you shall be glad and rejoice for ever”** — without end
**“in these things which I create”** — all things made by me
**“for behold I create Jerusalem”**
• heavenly
• of angels and men
**“a rejoicing”**
• Emphasis.
• Of the whole earth; so that what was the old joy of the only-begotten becomes a new gladness for all nations.
**“For behold I create Jerusalem a rejoicing”** — Of angels, that is, and of men, one Church; and they shall exult and rejoice, as I who created them exult and rejoice in them.
**“joy”** — Which we can understand either after the resurrection or after baptism, in the first resurrection.
**“and the people thereof joy”** — This refers to the general resurrection, in which all will rise in perfect age; and this is “there shall not be.”
65.19:
**“And I will rejoice in Jerusalem, and joy in my people, and the voice of weeping shall no more be heard in her”** — God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes.
**“nor the voice of crying”**
• where there is joy and exultation; for contraries cannot be together.
• not as the Jews, who will make an outcry for judgment.
65.20:
**“There shall no more be an infant of days there”** — “For we shall all rise unto a perfect man, in the measure of the age of the fulness of Christ.”
**“nor an old man”** — anticipated by death
**“that shall not fill up his days”** — because no one will die.
**“for the child shall die a hundred years old”** — even if he lives here a long time.
**“a child of a hundred years”** — That is, he who, though he lived long, nevertheless lived childishly, serving vices; and he explains it thus: and the sinner, etc.
*Gregory:* In the Morals. The life of the child is indeed drawn out at length, that he may be corrected of childish deeds. But if he is restrained from the commission of sin not even by length of time, this very length of life, which he received through the mercy of God, grows for him to the height of cursing.
65.21:
**“And they shall build”** — in the present
**“houses”** — virtues
**“and inhabit them; and they shall plant vineyards”**
• good works. Whence: “They shall be inebriated with the plenty of thy house”; and elsewhere, “I shall be satisfied when thy glory shall appear.”
• This is the vine of which he said: “I am the true vine; and you are the branches; and my Father is the husbandman.”
**“Houses”** — The virtues for which they will rest in the heavenly places. Whence: “In my Father’s house there are many mansions”; each one will receive his own reward according to his own labor. The midwives are said to have built such houses for themselves because they feared God. Jacob also dwells in the house which Esau, who delighted in wild beasts, could not possess. For it cannot stand according to the letter; for many saints build houses and do not dwell in them.
65.22:
**“They shall not build, and another inhabit”** — namely the devil
**“inhabit”** — in the midst of them
**“they shall not plant, and another eat”** — the devil, that is, will not devour their virtues.
**“for as the days of a tree”** — of the vine
**“shall be”** — of whom the just man shall flourish like the palm, namely he who daily wins a triumph over his adversaries.
**“the days of my people”** — faithful
**“As the days of a tree”** — As Christ now dieth no more, “death shall no more have dominion over him,” but he reigns forever with the Father, so also they; for the tree of life is Christ, which was in the midst of paradise, that is, of the Church. Whence Solomon: “She is a tree of life to them that lay hold on her,” that is, wisdom, which is Christ.
**“The works of thy hands”** — They will make old the faith, doctrine, and working of the apostles until the end of the world, by preserving the faithful, their imitators, that is. Or, as some copies have, “to my elect they shall make old,” that is, they will save them eternally; their works, that is, the apostles' works.
65.23:
**“My elect”** — or the elect
**“my”**
• or my
• therefore
**“shall not labour in vain, nor bring forth in trouble”** — spiritual sons, as Rachel a fleshly son
**“for they are the seed”** — of the apostles
**“of the blessed of the Lord, and their posterity with them”** — are the Lord’s, or will rejoice for ever
**“The seed of the blessed”** — The apostles and other teachers, in preaching or in other works, as the Jews; because they will receive eternal reward, because they will come with exultation carrying their sheaves.
**“posterity”** — Whom their sons begat in faith, as Mark, Peter’s disciple, and Luke, Paul’s son.
65.24:
**“And it shall come to pass, that before they call”** — by mouth
**“I will hear”**
• crying out in heart
• what they asked, by giving miracles, by working
• confirming their word with signs
**“yet”** — the apostles
**“speaking”** — preaching, or praying for someone
**“Before they call”** — Not in trouble, in grief of mind, but in joy and gladness. Whence: “For what is our joy, or crown of glory? Are not you?” etc.
65.25:
**“The wolf”** — Saul
**“and the lamb”** — Ananias
**“shall feed together”**
• by the faith of believers, with the bread of God’s word
• at the coming of Christ
• together in the Church
**“the lion and the ox”** — preachers, plowing the hearts of hearers with the plowshare of preaching
**“straw”** — they will be fed with simple teaching together with depth of mystery, as some copies have
**“and the serpent”** — the devil
**“dust”**
• light, unfruitful
• the impious, like dust which the wind casts from the face of the earth
**“his food”** — Whence: “Earth thou shalt eat.”
**“They shall not hurt”** — to the lambs and oxen
**“nor kill”** — the wolf and the lion converted
**“in all my holy mountain”** — the Church, in confession of Christ, who is the mountain at the top of mountains
**“The wolf and”** — The wolf: Saul, that is, the persecutor, of whom: “Benjamin a ravening wolf.”
**“The lamb”** — Who, clothed in white garments, follow the Lamb wherever he goes. Of whom it is said to Peter: Feed my lambs.
**“saith the Lord”** — The lion and the ox, etc. A man, that is, eloquent and most powerful in the world, having despised the eloquence of philosophy, will eat straw, that is, the lowliness and surface of history, with the oxen, that is, the preachers of the Church. These lions eat this until by many labors they come to the depth of the mystery, as Augustine and Cyprian and others.
**“Shall not hurt nor kill”** — Their fierceness laid aside, either in the present or in the future; and this is: “In all my holy mountain.” The Jews take this carnally, saying that in the time of their Christ there will be so great peace and security for them that wolves and lambs, lions and oxen, serpents and men will dwell together and eat, and will not harm those who dwell in the temple and on the holy mountain. From this it is gathered that all others will be slain. But this is shown to be false by these words: “Thus saith the Lord: Heaven is my throne, and the earth my footstool,” etc. And yet the Jews understand this carnally.

66.1:
**“Thus saith the Lord: Heaven is my throne”** — where my will is done
**“Heaven”** — All the saints, whose conversation is in heaven. Whence: “The soul of the just is the seat of God. Heaven is my seat.” As if lest you think these things are to be fulfilled literally.
**“and the earth”** — of earthly things, by the power of an angel, whom he trod under by his own virtue
**“my footstool; what is this house”** — that I may be enclosed in it
**“that you will build to me? and what is this place of my rest?”** — humble and quiet, and trembling at my words
**“What is this”** — As if you thought me local and remaining only in the temple. But what is this house, etc.
66.2:
**“all these things”** — as if none, because all things, etc.
**“My hand made all these things, and all these things were made”** — namely by me
**“all these things, saith the Lord. But to whom shall I have respect”** — as if this is rest and my seat, not that which you think, of which the holy temple of God is, which you are
**“but to him that is poor and little, and of a contrite spirit”**
• humble in spirit: blessed are the poor, namely; and elsewhere: “A contrite and humbled heart, O God, thou wilt not despise,” etc.
• for his own sins and those of others
**“and that trembleth”**
• “Blessed is the man that feareth the Lord.”
• “The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord.”
**“But to whom shall I have respect”** — And so on. With the altar and the earthly temple, which a human hand built, taken away, the sacrifices of the Jews are rightly taken away, lest perhaps they should say: We are not so foolish as to think that God can be shut up in this place; but in a place set apart for glorifying God we offer victims, as is commanded in the law.
66.3:
**“He that sacrificeth”** — “I will have mercy, and not sacrifice.”
**“an ox”**
• in sacrifice
• He that sacrifices an ox, etc. As if your sacrifice did not please me after the immolation of the true sacrifice, in whose shadow I permitted you those sacrifices, and that you should not sacrifice to idols.
**“is as if he slew a man”** — which is forbidden
**“he that killeth a sheep in sacrifice, as if he should brain a dog: he that offereth an oblation”** — according to the law
**“a dog”** — Of which, through Moses: “Thou shalt not offer the hire of a harlot, nor the price of a dog, in the house of the Lord thy God.” And well are the dog and the harlot joined, because they lust alike.
**“as if he should offer swine's blood”** — which is against the law
**“he that remembereth incense”** — that he may offer what the law commands
**“as if he should bless an idol”** — praise, venerate
**“All these things”** — aforesaid
**“have they chosen”** — by their own will
**“in their ways”** — not of God, namely, who is the way
**“have chosen”** — Not by my will, since the true Lamb has been sacrificed. Whence: “Christ our pasch is sacrificed.”
**“and in their abominations”** — in those things, namely, which ought to have been abhorred
**“their soul”** — animal nature, not reason
**“is delighted”** — because lovers of themselves rather than of God
66.4:
**“Wherefore I also will choose”** — by permission
**“their mockeries”**
• of demons and of the Romans, by whom they are mocked
• that is, the mockers: the devil, antichrist, wicked princes, priests, scribes and Pharisees
**“and will bring upon them the things they feared”** — The Romans, whence the Romans will come and take away our place and nation. Or famine, pestilence, captivity.
**“will bring upon them, because I called”**
• them
• “Come to me, all you that labour, and are burdened, and I will refresh you,” and do penance.
**“and there was none”** — of them
**“that would answer”** — as above: by obeying, by imitating
**“I spoke”** — the same
**“and they heard not”** — they heard
**“and they have done evil in my eyes”** — they openly proclaimed their evil, as Sodom did
**“and have chosen the things that displease me”** — error
**“have they chosen”** — Barabbas
66.5:
**“Hear”** — the prophet to the apostles
**“Hear the word of the Lord, you that tremble”** — reverent, revering
**“Your brethren have said at his word”** — Jews according to the flesh
**“that hate you, and cast you out for my name's sake; Let the Lord be glorified”** — your
**“and we shall see”** — him in his very majesty
**“in your joy; but they shall be confounded”**
• who say such things
• On the day of judgment, when he comes in his glory, “with great power and majesty”, and virtue. Or also in the present, whence it is added: a voice of the people.
**“That hate you”** — Because you are not of the world, because you believe in me, because you have my name from Christ, being called Christians. For the Jews had already conspired that “if any man should confess him to be Christ, he should be put out of the synagogue.”
**“Let the Lord be glorified”** — As if he who is your joy appears glorious, so that we may believe you, who now proclaim one vile and abject.
66.6:
**“A voice of the people”** — of grief and lamentation
**“from the city”** — is heard
**“a voice from the temple”** — of the priests
**“the voice of the Lord that rendereth”**
• of exultation among the Romans
• is heard
**“recompense”** — for the death of the patriarchs, the prophets, and Christ himself
**“to his enemies”**
• to the Jews, namely those who were once sons
• to the Jews, through the Romans
• To the Jews, condemned for their impiety.
• A voice of the people from the city, etc. Josephus: When the Roman army came, according to John, the Jews were divided into three parts, contending for the leadership, some setting up one prince over themselves, others another. One part of the people and of the priests held the temple; the citadel and the royal house, a part of the people and of the princes; the rest of the city, the third part, and chiefly the common people. So they fought both outside against the enemies and within against their fellow citizens. When the Romans were breaking into the city, there was heard the voice of the people lamenting from the city, the voice of the priests and of those who were with them from the temple; the voice of the Lord also was heard in the exulting Romans, who even came by the will of God, rendering recompense to his enemies, that is, to the Jews, through the Romans.
66.7:
**“Before she was in labour, she brought forth”**
• Mary
• the primitive Church
**“before”**
• The same.
• as if unexpectedly, very quickly
**“before her time came to be delivered”**
• Mother
• of the primitive Church
**“she brought forth”**
• The Father
• begot without time
• “in one day three thousand, another five thousand,” who could die sooner than be separated from the faith and charity of Christ
**“a man child”**
• the strong Son, through whom all things were made and subsist
• Before she was in labour, etc. Not little by little, nor over a long time, as the people of the Jews, did the Church grow; but at once the world conceived, when the preaching was heard, and brought forth a man child, whom Pharao and Herod tried to kill, who in Moses and in Christ was saved in Egypt. Abraham also and Isaac had male sons. Jacob, among many sons, begot Dina, for whom he suffered much. So Sion, that is, the remnant of Israel, brought forth a man child, that is, Christ, who is begotten in the whole world at once, which no one has heard, no history has told, so that by the teaching of one all nations might believe at once, and one people be made of diverse nations. Whence: “All the kindreds of the Gentiles shall adore in his sight.” And David says: “The hope of all the ends of the earth, and in the sea afar off.”
**“A man child”** — A strong people, of whom Stephen and Paul, who says: “Who shall separate us from the love of Christ?”
66.8:
**“Who hath ever heard such a thing?”** — that she should bring forth before she is in labour, since naturally labour precedes birth, and in so short a space should beget so many thousands of men
**“and who hath seen the like to this? shall the earth bring forth”** — once, as if all things were to come into the light
**“in one day”** — which the sun of justice illumines
**“In one day”** — The apostles begot their sons as if in one day and at once, because in Christ, who is light and day, and in the unity of faith.
**“or shall a nation be brought forth”**
• the whole
• “My little children, whom I am again in labour with, until Christ be formed in you.”
**“at once, because Sion hath been in labour”** — as if she begot with great labour in faith
**“and hath brought forth”** — the apostles
**“her children”** — spiritual
66.9:
**“Shall not I”** — Like: “He that planted the ear, shall he not hear?”
**“that make others to bring forth children”** — carnally
**“myself bring forth”** — spiritually, the co-eternal Son, and others spiritual; whence: “he gave them power to be made the sons of God.”
**“saith the Lord? shall I, that give generation to others, be barren”** — as if it will be
**“saith the Lord thy God”** — If I, etc. As if I, who created all men out of nothing, will create for myself out of all nations one Church, which is built of living stones.
66.10:
**“Rejoice with Jerusalem”**
• which is built of living stones
• the heavenly and the present Church
**“and be glad”** — in the faith of her sons
**“with her, all”** — gathered from the nations
**“you that love her: rejoice for joy with her”** — indeed
**“all you that mourn”**
• concerning the faithlessness of the Jews
• “Blessed are they that mourn, for they shall be comforted.”
**“Rejoice”** — O angels, or apostles, sorrowful over the loss of the unbelieving Jews. Rejoice, comforted by the faith and salvation of the Gentiles, from whom the Church is built up.
66.11:
**“That you may suck, and be filled with the breasts”** — by the two testaments, whence the teaching of simple folk is drawn, like the milk of infants; whence she herself is also comforted; or by the gifts of the Holy Spirit
**“of her consolations: that you may milk out”** — the faith of simple folk
**“and”** — so
**“and flow with delights, from the abundance”** — by faith, virtues, works, and knowledge of the divinity and humanity of Christ
**“That you may suck”** — The faith of simple folk and good works, being delighted. The faith of believers is milk and food, and of preachers. Whence also Christ: “I have meat to eat, which you know not.”
**“of her glory”** — That you may suck, etc. The woman in childbed who brought forth the man child does not lack abundance of milk in the rearing of the nation and of the little ones who were born together, so that she might give them two breasts, the Old and the New Testament. And it is to be noted that the little ones need the milk of consolation, as being still in the flesh; but those who after the milk of consolation have advanced to solid food flow with the delights of truth and with the knowledge of every kind of glory.
**“That you may milk out”** — Holy Church is one in all things; in some she has simple milk, namely faith and works; in others every kind of glory of gifts flows abundantly, namely abundance and knowledge of the divinity and of the humanity of Christ. So the holy preachers are delighted in all things, as gathering this from some, that from others.
66.12:
**“For thus saith the Lord: Behold I”**
• I will pour out
• the Church built up through the apostles
**“will bring”** — from the Jews who turn away from me
**“over it”** — Jerusalem
**“as it were a river of peace”**
• the abundance of the Holy Spirit, by which we are made at peace with God and the angels
• “The streams of the river make glad the city of God”; and “Out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water.”
**“and as an overflowing torrent”** — the swiftest faith; whence: “At the hearing of the ear they have obeyed me”; whence the Gentiles are glorious
**“the glory of the Gentiles, which you shall suck”** — delighted
**“you shall be carried at the breasts”** — O Gentiles who are to believe
**“and upon the knees they shall caress you”** — apostles
**“You shall be carried at the breasts”** — From the apostles and preachers, to the gifts of the Holy Spirit, or to the teaching of the Old and New Testaments. For what they preach they show by their works, so that thus they may give guidance to their hearers.
**“they shall caress you”** — Sustaining, nursing, as he who says: “I beseech you, brethren, by the mercy of God, that you present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, pleasing unto God”; I beseech you as strangers and pilgrims.
66.13:
**“As one whom the mother caresseth, so”** — and more; whence: and if she should forget, yet will not I forget
**“will I comfort you”** — in the present; whence: I am with you even to the consummation of the world
**“and you shall be comforted in Jerusalem”** — heavenly
**“you shall be comforted”**
• my presence
• As, etc. Almighty God, as merciful and compassionate, compares himself now to an eagle, now to a hen, now to a caressing mother, that he may at least win you over with caresses. As also the eagle makes her nest on inaccessible rocks, that access may be open to no one; and in the middle she places an amethyst stone, which, according to the naturalists, drives away all poisons, to keep off serpents, and certain other secrets of nature. So he himself in our hearts places a stone, that is, his faith, namely himself, who is the stone cut out without hands from the mountain, by which all the poisons of the devil are driven away. For the eagle loves her young more than all beasts and cattle, flocks and birds, as say those who have written on the natures of living things.
66.14:
**“You shall see”**
• O faithful, in eternal blessedness, God, namely as he is. Whence: “Blessed are the clean of heart, for they shall see God.”
• O apostles, the multitude coming to faith. And your heart will rejoice at their salvation, and your bones, that is virtues, will sprout in the hearts of others, the fruits of good will and of action. For as the body is sustained by the bones, so the soul is sustained by virtues.
**“and your heart shall rejoice”**
• without end
• and your joy no man shall take from you
**“your heart and your bones shall flourish like an herb”** — winter dead, spring come back to life
**“and your bones”** — In the day of judgment your bodies will revive in immortality, so that as you served God in body and soul in the present life, so in body and soul you may receive rewards.
**“and shall be known”** — in the day of judgment, or here
**“the hand of the Lord”** — power, operation; whence to Pharaoh through Moses: “the hand of the Lord is upon thee and upon thy people”
**“to his servants”** — to whom he will say: “Come, ye blessed of my Father”
**“shall be known”** — At the judgment, namely: the Son, sweet and gentle to the good, an avenger and strong to the wicked, will be known, who is the hand of the Father, through whom he works all things.
**“and he shall be angry with his enemies”** — to the demons, to the Jews, to the reprobate works, to whom he will say: “Depart from me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire”
66.15:
**“For behold the Lord ... with fire”** — “A fire shall go before him,” and the fire shall blaze up in his sight
**“will come”** — to judgment
**“With fire”** — Which will be eternal to the wicked, whom it will wrap up and lead to eternal punishment, by which will be purged what in the good is to be purged.
**“and his chariots are like a whirlwind”** — angels accompanying him in judgment
**“His chariots”** — Chariot, because then he is about to triumph and to vanquish all adversaries, not because he needs the ministry of angels.
**“to render his wrath in indignation”** — saying: “Depart from me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire”
