**“from the neck of Jeremias the prophet, and broke it”** — And he took, etc. The prudence, humility and patience of Jeremias are to be considered. The false prophet does injury to the matter; he breaks the yoke from his neck, which he would not have done if it had been of iron. Jeremias is silent and hides his pain. For he had not yet received from the Lord what he should say; in which Holy Scripture tacitly hints that prophets do not speak merely by their own judgment but by the will of the Lord, especially of future things, the knowledge of which belongs to God alone.
28.11: **“And Jeremias the prophet went his way”** — as if beaten; as if singing that: “And I became as a man that heareth not: and that hath no reproofs in his mouth.”
28.12:
**“Hananias the prophet”** — Supposedly. For many things in the holy Scriptures are said according to the opinion of the time in which the events are related, not according to the truth of the matter. Whence: “I and thy father sought thee sorrowing.”
**“And the word of the Lord came to Jeremias, after that Hananias the prophet had broken the chain from off the neck of Jeremias the prophet, saying:”** — And the word of the Lord came, etc. When Jeremias had gone away and had swallowed down the injuries in silence, the word of the Lord came to him, not that he should speak with his own words to Hananias boasting in a lie, but that he should say, “Thus saith the Lord,” which the other had nevertheless said; but a lie always imitates the truth.
28.13:
**“Go, and tell Hananias: Thus saith the Lord: Thou hast broken chains of wood, and thou shalt make for them chains of iron.”**
• Wooden chains, etc. He shows that by keeping the lesser punishment he is the cause of a greater one.
• And in this place the allegorical interpreter raves, calling the yokes and chains of wood the ethereal and aerial bodies, namely of demons and of the adverse powers, and the chains of iron our grosser bodies, which are made of sinews, bones, flesh and veins; so that those who will not, from the heavenly Jerusalem, undergo lesser torments according to the quality of their sin, are condemned to the chains of our bodies, and endure the wailing of infancy, the bonds of swaddling clothes and filth, and serve the devil, the king of Babylon, that is, of the world, with the beasts of the earth, which are bound in the bodies of brute animals.
28.15:
**“And Jeremias the prophet said to Hananias the prophet”** — The truth of the history is kept, not according to what was, but according to what was thought at that time.
**“Hear now, Hananias”** — he does not here call him a prophet whom he denies was sent by the Lord
**“the Lord hath not sent thee, and thou hast made this people to trust in a lie.”** — so that he does not yield to the sentence of the Lord
**“And Jeremias the prophet said”** — It is to be noted that Jeremias, having suffered the injury while the word of the Lord had not yet come to him, keeps silent; afterwards, however, sent by the Lord, he boldly rebukes the liar, announcing his near death.
28.16: **“Therefore thus saith the Lord: Behold I will send thee away from off the face of the earth: this year shalt thou die: for thou hast spoken against the Lord.”** — This year, etc. If at any time we die, we are freed from the prisons of the body, according to that which heretics wrongly interpret: “Bring my soul out of prison,” because death is imposed as a punishment.
28.17: **“In the seventh month”** — Perhaps in the seventh month, which is wont to signify rest, they pretend he died, so that he is freed from the evils of the body, according to that: “Death is rest for a man.” But we know that the bodies of believers are temples of God, if the Holy Spirit dwells in them.

29.1:
**“Now these are the words of the letter which Jeremias the prophet sent from Jerusalem to the residue of the ancients that were carried into captivity, and to the priests, and to the prophets, and to all the people, whom Nabuchodonosor had carried away from Jerusalem to Babylon:”**
• And these are, etc. He intends to persuade them not to give heed to the false prophets who promised them a return to Jerusalem after a short time. But let them know that they will stay in Babylon for a long time.
• To the remnant of the elders, etc. First the word of God is directed to the old men, then to the priests, third to the prophets, fourth to all the people; or the letter of the prophet is sent according to the order of their age.
• Mystically: after we have been cast out of Jerusalem, that is, out of the Church, for our sins, and delivered to Nabuchodonosor, of whom the apostle said, “to deliver such a one to Satan for the destruction of the flesh,” etc., and elsewhere, “whom I have delivered up to Satan, that they may learn not to blaspheme,” we ought not to be wholly secure, or grow torpid in idleness, or utterly despair; but first to build houses, not upon sand but upon rock, such as the midwives built in Exodus because they feared the Lord; then to plant gardens, such as the Lord planted, paradise, and placed in it the tree of life, of which “she is a tree of life to them that lay hold on her,” etc. Third, to take wives, of whom one is wisdom, of whom Solomon says: “Love her, and she shall keep thee,” etc., and elsewhere: “Her I sought to take for my spouse,” etc. Nor is one wife enough; we ought to have several: let us add fortitude, temperance and justice, that we may beget more sons; and let us join our daughters, that is, good works, to husbands, that is, to the truth of faith; and begetting such sons and daughters, let us be multiplied, and destroying the things that are of a child, and growing into a perfect man, let us hear: “I write unto you, fathers, because you have known him who is from the beginning,” and with the apostle let us say, “for in the gospel I have begotten you.” Let us therefore seek the peace of the Church, the city and our land, that we may deserve to return to it, from which we were carried away by the judgment of the Lord, that we might dwell in the confusion of error. For so we shall have peace. And the clemency of the Lord is to be considered: we ought to pray even for enemies, that we may do good to those who hate us.
**“The words of the letter”** — This little book of Jeremias is sent to Babylon to those who had been carried away with Jechonias, so that by the occasion of a royal embassy the prophet might complete his work and persuade the people of what the Lord had commanded him.
29.2:
**“After that ... were departed”** — because they were carried away not only by the power of the Babylonians but also by the will of the Lord
**“Jechonias the king, and the queen”** — others: the queen
**“and the eunuchs, and the princes of Juda, and of Jerusalem”** — he sent, I say, Jeremias by these
29.5: **“Build ye houses, and dwell in them: and plant orchards”** — or orchards
29.6:
**“Take ye wives, and beget sons and daughters: and take wives for your sons, and give your daughters to husbands, and let them bear sons and daughters: and”** — there
**“be ye multiplied there, and be not few in number.”** — Take ye wives, etc. Jeremias, because the captivity of Jerusalem is near, is commanded not to take a wife, not to beget sons; whence the apostle: “The time is short. It remains that they who have wives be as if they had none.” But if, because of the shortness of the time, the use of wives is taken away from those who have them, how much more are those who have none commanded not to take them.
29.7:
**“And seek the peace”** — of it
**“of the city, to which I have caused you to be carried away captives; and pray to the Lord for it: for in the peace thereof shall be your peace.”** — Seek the peace, etc. Whence the Apostle: “I desire therefore, first of all, that supplications, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings be made for all men: for kings, and for all that are in high station: that we may lead a quiet and a peaceable life,” etc.
29.8:
**“Let not your prophets that are in the midst of you, and your diviners deceive you”** — Ezechiel testifies that there were false prophets and diviners and dreamers in Babylon among those who were carried away with Jechonias; yet when these letters were being sent, he was not yet prophesying, who began to prophesy in the fifth year of the captivity of Jechonias, which was the same as of the reign of Sedecias.
**“Tropologically.”** — Let not the prophets deceive you, etc. False prophets are those who expound the Scriptures apart from the sense of the Holy Spirit. Diviners are those who proclaim the conjecture of their own mind, and uncertain things of the future, as if true. Dreamers are those who do not hear that: “Give not sleep to thy eyes, neither let thy eyelids slumber”; their mind does not watch, weighed down by the slumber of error; to whom it is said: “Arise, thou that sleepest,” “and Christ shall enlighten thee.”
29.10:
**“When ... shall begin”** — Do not believe the false prophets who promise you a near return; for the seventy years will be fulfilled for you before you return.
**“For thus saith the Lord: When the seventy years shall begin to be accomplished in Babylon, I will visit you: and I will perform my good word in your favour, to bring you again to this place.”** — Seventy years, etc. We are involved in the confusion of the world for so long as it takes us to deserve to receive the rest of the sevenfold number; and when penance has been accepted, God fulfils what he promised and brings us back to our place, that is, to the Church; he who strikes that he may heal, who will give an end to labour and patience. For we shall call upon him and pray, and we shall be heard; we shall seek him with all our heart, and we shall find him. Some understand the seventy years according to that: “The days of our years in them are threescore and ten years.” When these have been fulfilled, we return to the Lord with our whole heart, and are heard; and then is the end of our labour and of our patience.
29.11:
**“For I know”** — but not to others, for knowing the future belongs to God alone
**“the thoughts that I think towards you, saith the Lord, thoughts of peace, and not of affliction”** — of captivity
**“to give you an end and patience.”** — of present labours
29.12:
**“And you shall call upon me”** — then, or in hope of the future
**“and you shall go: and you shall pray”** — He could have fulfilled what he had promised without invocation and prayer, but he urges prayer so that they may merit the promises.
29.13: **“You shall seek me”** — seek and you shall find
29.14: **“and I will bring you back”** — That you may know more surely that you ought not to hope for so near a return, but to build houses, plant orchards, beget sons, and await the promised time.
29.15: **“Because you have said”** — as if you think in vain that you have prophets in Babylon
29.16:
**“For thus saith the Lord to the king”** — Sedecias
**“that sitteth upon the throne of David, and to all the people that dwell in this city, to your brethren”** — unwilling to obey my sentence
29.17:
**“Thus saith the Lord of hosts: Behold I will send”** — captivity, but they will not be able to escape
**“like bad figs”** — Theodotion. Suarina, that is, the second; Symmachus: the last; which in Hebrew is suarim.
29.18:
**“And I will persecute them”** — who are in Jerusalem
**“with the sword, and with famine, and with the pestilence: and I will give them up”** — scattered
**“unto affliction to all the kingdoms of the earth: to be a curse”** — that they may be an example of cursing to all
29.19: **“Rising by night”** — I have not ceased to warn them to imitate you, who enjoy secure leisure in exile until the promises of God are fulfilled.
29.20: **“Hear ye therefore”** — who have obeyed my will
29.21:
**“Thus saith the Lord of hosts the God of Israel, to Achab the son of Colias, and to Sedecias the son of Maasias, who prophesy unto you in my name falsely: Behold I will deliver them up into the hands of Nabuchodonosor the king of Babylon: and he shall kill them before your eyes.”**
• To Achab the son, etc. The Hebrews say that these are the elders whom Daniel mentions, saying to one of them: “Thou that art grown old in evil days,” etc.; to the other: “O thou seed of Chanaan, and not of Juda, beauty hath deceived thee,” etc. “Who prophesy to you in my name” a lie, because, as they say, they boasted to the poor women that they were of the tribe of Juda and that Christ was to be born of their offspring; whence the women, enticed by desire, yielded, as if they were to be the future mothers of Christ. But this seems to stand in the way, that the king of Babylon is said to have fried them, whereas Daniel says they were stoned; whence by most, and almost all, of the Hebrews that is neglected as a fable; for they do not think that captives had power to stone their princes and prophets; and they affirm it to be truer what Jeremias says, that they were indeed convicted by Daniel, but the sentence was given by the king. But many of our own flock prophesy a lie in the name. They defile the wives of their fellow citizens, whom the old Nabuchodonosor fries in the fire of sin, according to that: “They are all adulterers, like an oven heated by the baker.” But happy is he who bears the yoke of the Lord from his youth, who sits alone, who is full of bitterness, so that he may say: I sat not with the council of the malignant.
• In this chapter the allegorical interpreter dreams of the ruin of the heavenly Jerusalem, and suspects that the prophecy is directed to those who dwell in the Babylon of this world; because they did well, descending of their own will into these bodies, building houses, begetting sons, and being zealous for good works, after seventy years they will be sent into the heavenly Jerusalem. But he says that those who refused to descend to earthly things will suffer what the Lord threatens to Sedechias: because they refuse to imitate their brothers or to come into Babylon, the Lord will send upon them the sword, the famine and the pestilence, that is, the want of all things, and will make them like the worst figs, and will pursue them with an everlasting sword, and will give them over to vexation to all kingdoms; and they will not become men but demons, and will be a curse to all the angels who preside over the individual provinces; because in the heavenly Jerusalem they refused to hear the words of the prophets urging them to descend to earthly things, that, penance having been done, after the true sabbath they might possess their former place.
29.23: **“Because they have acted folly in Israel, and have committed adultery with the wives of their friends, and have spoken lying words in my name, which I commanded them not: I am the judge and the witness, saith the Lord.”** — as having known not by opinion but by the thing itself that these things are true; they cannot hide them nor assume the truth of judgment
29.24:
**“And to Semeias the Nehelamite thou shalt say”**
• To Semeias, etc. Semeias, from the place Nehelam, which is interpreted “torrent,” was led into Babylon with Jeconias, and prophesied a lie to the people, namely that they would soon return to Jerusalem. Therefore, since Jeremias had sent letters to those who were in Babylon, saying: “Build houses,” etc., and afterwards had added: “Let not your prophets deceive you,” etc., Semeias, understanding that this was written against himself, sends letters to Jerusalem, to Sophonias the son of Maasias and to the rest of the priests, asking why Jeremias is not rebuked by Sophonias, whose office it is to discern between false and true prophets; and it is ordered that he be shut up in prison and pay the penalty of a lie, because he has seduced the people. But Joiadas was the priest who handed the kingdom to Joas after the killing of Athalia, and killed the priests of Baal. As if to say: Why do you not imitate Joiadas? Why do you not kill Jeremias, the false prophet? For the Lord has appointed you in place of Joiadas, that you may discern by what spirit each one speaks. But the discernment of spirits is a spiritual grace.
• Athalia was a woman who killed those of royal seed whom she could, from whom the priest Joiada saved Joas; and after she was slain by the people, he handed over the rule to him.
29.27: **“And now why hast thou not rebuked”** — He forestalls the truth with a lie, which he himself deserved, and imposes it on another, because the sons of darkness are more prudent than the sons of light, and they inflict on others what they fear for themselves.
29.28: **“For he hath also sent to us in Babylon, saying: It is a long time: build ye houses”** — This is what he grieves: that against his lie Jeremias wrote the truth.
29.29: **“So Sophonias the priest read this letter”** — as if by the reading itself you brand him, because he dared to write such things to Babylon
29.31: **“Thus saith the Lord”** — Semeias, truly a Nehelamite, who had taken turbid waters from the torrent, is angry that Jeremias has written against his lie, and sends letters to Sophonias, asking why he dared to write the truth, and desires that he be shut up in prison so that he may not speak. He also accuses Sophonias secretly, and casts a letter in accusation. In like manner they are guilty who defend false prophets and make the lies of others their own sins; against whom is added: Behold, I will visit.
29.32:
**“Therefore thus saith the Lord: behold I will visit”** — will visit their enemies with a rod
**“upon Semeias the Nehelamite, and upon his seed”** — the disciples whom he deceived by his error
**“he shall not have a man to sit in the midst of this people”** — that he may not sit in the midst of those at rest, who refused to stand with those who stand
**“and he shall not see the good that I will do to my people, saith the Lord: because he hath spoken treason against the Lord.”** — that is, that their sins are now already forgiven, that the captives are now already to return

30.1: **“This is the word that came to Jeremias from the Lord, saying:”** — This is the word which, etc. Jeremias promised a return, not within two years as those men falsely claimed. But when the seventy years are finished, he is now commanded to write and commit to memory what the Lord pronounces; whence it can be gathered that the prophecy is not soon fulfilled. But when Israel and Juda shall return to their own land, and as Ezechiel prophesied, the two rods will be joined together, and David will be king and shepherd of the sheep.
30.5: **“For thus saith the Lord: We have heard a voice of terror: there is fear and no peace.”** — And a voice of terror, etc. Some expound this place according to tropology, so as to think of that testimony: “From thy fear, O Lord, we have conceived, and have brought forth,” etc. This also: “My little children, of whom I am in labour again, until Christ be formed in you,” can be compared to this example; since it is plain that it pertains not to terror but to joy, whereas the present Scripture signifies a time of devastation and ruin.
30.7:
**“Alas,”** — He foretells a time of misery that he may bring in a time of joy.
**“for that day is great, neither is there the like to it; and it is the time of tribulation to Jacob”** — of the people of God
**“and out of it”** — and of him, of the twelve tribes; in the time of the gospel, not under Zorobabel as they think
**“Alas, for that day is great”** — Sad things are announced first, so that after the greatness of the evils joyful things may follow, and the greatness of grief be turned into joy. For health is more welcome after sickness. Peace having been put to flight by war, all things will be filled with blood, and the men who ought to fight will fear like women, and will hold not arms in their hands but their loins, like a woman in labour.
30.9: **“and David”** — Namely Christ. For since Adam the first and Adam the second are written according to the truth of the body, so also David: for Christ is of David according to the flesh.
30.10:
**“Therefore fear thou not, my servant Jacob”**
• two tribes
• This passage is not found in the Septuagint.
**“saith the Lord, neither be dismayed, O Israel”** — ten tribes
**“for behold, I will save thee”** — by bringing back
**“from a country afar off, and thy seed from the land of their captivity: and Jacob shall return, and be at rest, and abound with all good things”** — according to that: Let peace be in thy strength, and abundance in thy towers.
**“my servant”** — He calls him familiarly, as Abraham, Isaac and Jacob are called servants of God; Moses too and the other prophets; and Paul in the beginning of his epistles glories in this title.
30.11:
**“For I am with thee, saith the Lord, to save thee: for I will utterly consume all the nations”** — destroying them
**“among which I have scattered thee: but I will not utterly consume thee: but I will chastise thee in judgment, that thou mayst not seem to thyself innocent.”**
• as a bride
• as if I did not hand you over to punishment but to correction, that I might judge you as my own, lest I destroy you as strangers; for whoever does not believe is already judged, that is, prejudged to destruction
**“but I will chastise”** — Symmachus: And cleansing, I will not cleanse thee. Aquila: When I have instructed thee by judgment, I will by no means make thee innocent; and this is it: the whole world, princes or angels, need the mercy of God, and no one, however holy, goes secure to the judge; against the new and the old heresy, namely, which thinks that in this mortal flesh there is perfection in anything, and that all the virtues of the just can be fulfilled at once.
30.12: **“For thus saith the Lord: Thy bruise is incurable”** — not from me who broke you
30.13: **“There is none to judge thy judgment to bind it up: thou hast no healing medicines.”** — wherever you turn, because you have offended the true physician
30.14:
**“All thy lovers”** — priests
**“have forgotten thee, and will not seek after thee: for I have wounded thee with the wound of an enemy, with a cruel chastisement: by reason of”** — because
**“for I have wounded thee with the wound”** — A friend strikes in one way, an enemy in another; a father in one way, a foe in another: for the one strikes to correct, the other strikes to kill. Whence: “O Lord, rebuke me not in thy indignation.”
*Gregory:* As often as God corrects a sinner by striking, he sends the scourge in order to spare. But when by striking he brings to an end a life that remains in sin, he sends scourges but does not spare. For he who sent the scourge in order to spare, sometimes sends it so as not to spare. For in this life the Lord is the more zealous to spare, the more he scourges by scourging and by waiting; whence: “Such as I love, I rebuke and chastise”; and elsewhere: “Whom the Lord loveth, he chastiseth; and he scourgeth every son whom he receiveth.” But of the scourge of damnation it is written: “The sinner hath been caught in the works of his own hands”; and in Jeremias: “I have wounded thee with the wound of an enemy, with a cruel chastisement,” etc.
30.15:
**“Why criest thou for thy affliction? thy sorrow is incurable: for the multitude of thy iniquity”** — not by my will but by the cure of medicine compelling
**“and for thy hardened sins I have done these things to thee.”** — they cannot be healed except with a most biting powder and a most sharp iron, with which I would cut away the putrid and incurable flesh
30.16: **“Therefore all they that devour thee shall be devoured: and all thy enemies shall be carried into captivity: and they that waste thee shall be wasted, and all that prey upon thee will I give for a prey.”** — Therefore all, etc. We know that these things were done under Zorobabel, when the Babylonians and Chaldeans laid waste the Assyrians, that is, Ninive, and the Medes and Persians laid waste them, and Babylon was destroyed. Then Sion began to have the Lord seeking her, and her scar was closed over. But they are fulfilled more fully and more perfectly in Christ.
30.17: **“For I will close up thy scar, and will heal thee of thy wounds, saith the Lord. Because they have called thee, O Sion, an outcast”** — or have called
30.18:
**“Thus saith the Lord: Behold I will bring back the captivity of the pavilions of Jacob, and will have pity on his houses, and the city shall be built”** — A city seated on a mountain cannot be hid.
**“in her high place, and the temple”** — so that whatever was done bodily among the former people is fulfilled spiritually in the Church
**“shall be founded according to the order thereof.”** — Behold, I will bring back, etc. Their type went before in Zorobabel and Esdras, when the people returned and the city began to be built in her high place, and the religion of the temple to be observed, etc.; the things which are contained in Esdras are contained more fully and more perfectly in Christ and in the apostles.
30.19:
**“And out of them shall come forth”** — the apostles saying: grace to you and peace
**“praise, and the voice of them that play: and I will multiply them”** — that the whole world may believe in Christ
**“and they shall not be made few: and I will glorify them”** — Glorious things are said of thee, O city of God.
**“of them that play”** — Not according to that: “The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.” But according to that: “They played before the ark of the Lord.”
30.20:
**“And their children shall be”** — apostles
**“as from the beginning”** — Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, the princes of the Israelite race
**“and their assembly shall be permanent before me: and I will visit against all”** — the contrary powers
30.21:
**“And their leader shall be”** — Christ, of the stock of Israel according to the flesh
**“of themselves: and their prince shall come forth from the midst of them: and I will bring him near”** — I, the Father
**“and he shall come to me”** — saying: “I am in the Father, and the Father in me.”
**“for who is this”** — as if no one can so apply his heart to the Lord, nor be so joined to the Father as the Son is
30.22:
**“And you shall be my people”** — This is not found in the Hebrew.
**“and I will be your God.”** — We see this fulfilled from the Father in Israel, and wholly among the Gentiles.
30.23: **“Behold the whirlwind of the Lord, his fury going forth, a violent storm, it shall rest upon the head of the wicked.”** — of demons, or of those blaspheming the Son of God
30.24: **“The Lord will not turn away the wrath of his indignation, till he have executed”** — that Jerusalem be surrounded by an army and utterly destroyed

31.1:
**“At that time”** — when my thought is fulfilled, my fury resting upon the head of the wicked
**“saith the Lord, I will be the God of all the families of Israel, and they shall be my people.”**
• not according to the flesh but according to the spirit, who perceives God with the mind
• At that time, etc. The craftsman is known when the work is complete, the skill of medicine having achieved health. So, Jerusalem overthrown and the former people cast off, it is understood that the rejection of the Jews is the salvation of the Gentiles.
31.2:
**“Thus saith the Lord: The people found grace in the desert”** — of the Gentiles, in whose crowd the Church is saved
**“that were left and escaped from the sword”** — of the Roman, or of the Lord’s wrath
**“Israel shall go to his rest.”** — as long as he hoped for what the company of prophets promised
31.3: **“The Lord hath appeared from afar to me”** — Because Israel had offended the Lord, saying: “We have no king but Caesar,” and “Come, let us kill him, and the inheritance shall be ours,” and had withdrawn far from God. Therefore after a long time he appeared to it, not in the time of Zorobabel and Esdras when they were taken captive again, but he loved it with an everlasting love and drew it, taking pity; for it was saved by mercy, not by merit.
31.4:
**“And I will build thee again”** — This properly in the Church: for they rave who imagine a golden and jewelled Jerusalem, consecrating their own covetousness to the mystery of the city of the Lord.
**“and thou shalt be built, O virgin of Israel: thou shalt again be adorned with thy timbrels”** — that you sing to God in the churches, all flesh of evil works being consumed
**“and shalt go forth in the dances of them that make merry.”** — with the crowds of the Gentiles
31.5:
**“Thou shalt yet plant vineyards in the mountains of Samaria”** — not in valleys and lowly places
**“the planters shall plant”** — The planters shall plant. Those who after the captivity of Israel were possessed by aliens, to whom it is said: Plant plantings and gather the vintage.
31.6:
**“For there shall be a day”** — of the Lord
**“in which the watchmen on mount Ephraim, shall cry”**
• apostles and apostolic men
• of the guard
**“on mount Ephraim”** — of fertility
**“Arise, and let us go up”** — you who lie low, leave lowly things, despise the figurative sacrifices; a sacrifice to God is a contrite spirit
**“to Sion to the Lord our God.”** — the Church, in which is the watch of God; but when we shall have gone up into it, we shall ascend to the Lord
31.7:
**“For thus saith the Lord: Rejoice ye in the joy of Jacob”** — who are Jacob
**“and neigh before the head of the Gentiles”** — referring all things to the head of the Gentiles, because the tail has been turned into the head
**“shout ye, and sing, and say: Save, O Lord”** — that is to say, this
**“thy people, the remnant of Israel”**
• that is to say
• not all of it
**“The remnant of Israel”** — Who are saved according to election. Whence: “Unless the Lord of Sabaoth had left us a seed, etc.”
31.8:
**“Behold I will bring them from the north country”**
• from the unbelief and coldness of the Lord’s charity
• Behold, I will bring them through the apostles and apostolic men, who are the watchmen crying on the mount of Samaria, to whom it is commanded: Sound, sing, etc.
**“and will gather them”** — like a very hard wind, by name Dexter
**“from the ends of the earth: and among them shall be the blind, and the lame”**
• the blind see, the lame walk, etc.
• first he was enlightened by unbelief; afterwards by the faith of Christ
**“The lame”** — The Church.
**“she that is bringing forth”** — Sons for God.
**“together, a great company”** — that is
**“of them returning hither”** — to faith
31.9:
**“They shall come with weeping”** — For joy.
**“and I will bring them back in mercy”** — not in the faithlessness of the Jews
**“and I will bring them through the torrents of waters”** — apostles and apostolic men full of living water, whom the river of God, filled with waters, fills
**“in a right way”** — of faith or of Christ, in which whoever walks will not stumble
**“and they shall not stumble in it: for I am a father to Israel”** — because they have ceased to be blind, to whom it was said: “If you were blind, you should not have sin.”
**“and Ephraim is my firstborn”**
• “where sin abounded, grace did more abound.”
• They shall come with weeping, etc. The Jews think this was fulfilled when, under Esdras, after the day of the Passover, they went out of Babylon to return to Jerusalem. But there was a type there, not the truth; for they cannot prove that all these things were fulfilled at that time.
• And I will bring them back, etc. The Seventy. At the solemnity of the Passover, that is, in the days of the Lord’s passion, when Christ crucified drew all things to himself.
• And Ephraim, etc. Ephraim, who is a type of the Gentile people, was the younger son of Joseph, and he took away the birthright from Manasses, who by nature was the first; but in the mystery of the cross, with hands crossed, Jacob received the blessing for the one who stood at his left with his right hand, and the one who was at his right, blessed with the left, was brought down to the second place. And as Jacob took it from Esau, so Ephraim took the birthright from Manasses. And the whole people of the ten tribes was called Ephraim, because Jeroboam the son of Nabath, of this tribe, was the first to obtain the kingdom in Samaria, etc.
31.10:
**“Hear the word of the Lord”** — the calling of the Gentiles is plainly shown
**“O ye nations, and declare it in the islands that are afar off, and say”** — that is, this
**“He that scattered”** — not by the power of enemies but by the Lord’s will
**“Israel will gather him: and he will keep him as the shepherd doth his flock”** — who giveth his life for his sheep
31.11:
**“For the Lord hath redeemed”** — by the price of his own blood
**“the Lord hath redeemed Jacob, and delivered him out of the hand of one that was mightier than he”** — Out of the hand of the mightier, etc. The adverse parties, which are stronger by nature or stronger in faith. If, however, they are freed by him who binds the strong man and plunders his house.
31.12:
**“And they shall come”** — the freed
**“and shall give praise”** — their deliverer
**“in mount Sion”** — The Church.
**“and they shall flow together to the good things of the Lord”** — the abundance of all things, which is felt not in fruits and carnal food but in the variety of virtues
**“for the corn, and wine”** — of which the bread of God and his blood is made
**“and oil”** — “God, thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.”
**“and the increase of cattle”** — of the simple in the Church
**“and herds”** — who with their horns toss about the adversaries
**“and their soul shall be”** — because these blessings are not of the body
**“as a watered garden”** — the paradise of the Lord in delights
**“and they shall be hungry no more”** — having fullness of all things
31.13:
**“Then shall the virgin rejoice”** — For I have espoused you to one husband that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ.
**“in the dance, the young men and old men together”** — of whom the same John says: “I write unto you, fathers, because you have known him, who is from the beginning.”
**“and I will turn their mourning into joy”** — that the resurrection may gladden those whom the cross terrified
**“and will comfort them, and make them joyful after their sorrow”** — “Blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted.”
31.14:
**“And I will fill”** — that, burning with faith, they may speak as if full of new wine
**“the soul of the priests with fatness”** — The priests being made drunk with the doctrine of the Lord, and saying: Thy cup that inebriates, how excellent it is
**“and my people shall be filled with my good things, saith the Lord”** — here they are filled in part; in the future they will be filled wholly
**“The soul of the priests”** — Who have the knowledge of God, from whose mouth they ask the law, who believe in him who is a priest for ever.
**“With fatness”** — The Lord was seized in the valley of Gethsemani, that is, of fatness.
31.15:
**“A voice was heard on high”** — Some of the Jews explain this place thus: that when Jerusalem was taken under Vespasian, endless thousands of captives were sent along this road. Others, however, say that when the city was overthrown under Hadrian, an innumerable people of every age and sex was sold at the market of the terebinth; and for that reason it is abominable to the Jews to visit the very famous market.
**“Septuagint”** — “A voice in Rama was heard of lamentation and weeping and mourning, Rachel weeping for her children, and she would not be at rest, because they are not.” But Matthew did not bring forward the testimony according to the Hebrew nor according to the Septuagint: “A voice in Rama was heard, lamentation and great mourning; Rachel bewailing her children, and would not be comforted, because they are not.” Whence it is clear that the evangelists and apostles did not follow the translation of anyone from the Hebrew, but, being Hebrews, expressed in their own words what they read in Hebrew.
**“Rachel weeping”** — Rachel, mother of Joseph, when she came to Bethlehem, was suddenly seized by the pains of labour and bore a son, whom the midwife called Benoni because she was dying; but the father, changing the name, called him Benjamin, that is, son of the right hand.
**“Thus saith the Lord: A voice was heard on high of lamentation, of mourning, and weeping, of Rachel weeping for her children, and refusing to be comforted for them, because they are not”** — The question is therefore how Matthew applied the prophet’s testimony to the killing of the little ones, since it is plainly written of the ten tribes, whose chief is Ephraim, and Ephratha is not in the tribe of Ephraim but in the tribe of Juda. For it is Bethlehem itself, and the names agree: for Bethlehem is “house of bread,” and Ephratha is “fruitfulness.” But because Rachel was buried in Ephratha, that is, in Bethlehem, as holy Scripture and the inscription on her tomb testify, she is said to weep for the boys killed near her.
31.16:
**“Thus saith the Lord: Let thy voice cease”** — O Rachel.
**“thy voice from weeping, and thy eyes from tears: for there is a reward for thy work”** — that is, the Lord has regarded your former works.
**“saith the Lord: and they shall return”**
• at the coming of Christ
• the sons saved from the whole world
**“out of the land of the enemy”**
• of the devil
• And they shall return, etc. We better understand this of the little ones, that they have a reward for the blood shed for Christ, and in place of the land of Herod the enemy they hold the kingdoms of heaven; and they shall return to their former seat, receiving a glorious body for the body of lowliness. This is the last hope, when the just shall shine as the sun, and infants shall rise again unto a perfect man.
31.17:
**“And here is hope for thy last end”** — lest you be tormented by present sorrow
**“saith the Lord: and the children shall return to their own borders”** — which their fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, possessed
31.18:
**“Hearing I heard Ephraim”** — the ten tribes, over whom first reigned Jeroboam, who made the golden calves
**“when he went into captivity: thou hast chastised me, and I was instructed, as a young bullock”** — that is, instructed by much toil and stripes, he advanced to penance
**“I was instructed”** — As correction advances to salvation, and what seems at present to be sadness afterwards yields the fruit of peace.
**“unaccustomed to the yoke. Convert me, and I shall be converted”** — we accomplish this very penance we perform with the help of God alone
31.19:
**“after”** — not before, not through myself
**“For after thou didst convert me, I did penance: and after thou didst shew unto me”** — the judgment, or the knowledge of thee
**“I struck my thigh”**
• a sign of one grieving and lamenting his former error
• What is understood by the thigh but the pleasure of the flesh? And what is it that he says, “after thou didst shew unto me, I struck my thigh,” except that he saw heavenly things spiritually and put out everything lower in himself that lived carnally, so that the more the highest things fed him, the less the lowest pleased him? For the more anyone begins to live above, the more he begins to die below; whence: “And I live, now not I; but Christ liveth in me.”
**“I am confounded and ashamed”** — the memory of sins
**“because I have borne”** — He says that he sinned through the ignorance of his age, so that he may more easily obtain pardon; whence: “The sins of my youth and my ignorances do not remember.” And in what follows, God called him a little child, and one abounding in delights, namely because of the greatness of his riches and the fertility of the land.
31.20:
**“Surely Ephraim is an honourable son”** — who, against the order of nature, by the Lord’s favour received the honour of the firstborn
**“to me, Ephraim ... surely he is a tender child”** — deservedly
**“for since I spoke of him”** — others: because my words are in him, not in the mouth but in the heart
**“of him, I will still remember him”** — because he kept my words with the affection of his heart
**“Therefore are my bowels troubled”** — Osee says a similar thing: “My bowels are troubled; I will not execute the fierceness of my wrath”
**“for him: pitying I will pity him, saith the Lord”**
• Jerome. It is sacrilege to argue about the words of the Lord by human sense
• And Ephraim is an honourable son, etc. While Ephraim does penance and says, “Thou hast chastised me, and I was instructed, etc.,” the Lord answers; and to one fully converted he gives support with such an oracle: an honourable son, etc.
**“a tender child”** — Of whom: “The sons of Ephraim, who bend and shoot with the bow, have turned back in the day of battle.” But let us take “delights” according to that: “Delight in the Lord, and he will give thee the requests of thy heart”; for in Greek and in Hebrew it has “abound in delights.”
**“Therefore”** — But if he received my words with an eager mind and kept them, yet I will have mercy on him, because even human justice needs mercy
31.21:
**“Set thee up a watchtower”** — whence: let such great happiness be foretold to you
**“make to thee bitterness”** — for the old sins, or for the greatness of joy
**“direct thy heart into the right way, wherein thou hast walked”** — because he is to return by it
**“return, O virgin of Israel, return to these thy cities”**
• which you served while a captive
• Set up for thyself, etc. He calls to satisfaction, that he may consider in how many things he has offended, and doing penance return to his former grace, according to that: “Be mindful therefore from whence thou art fallen: and do penance, and do the first works.” Tropologically, however, it admonishes each one to look around with foresighted discretion, and as from the tower of contemplation to detect the fault before it comes.
• Direct thy heart, etc. He directs his heart into the right way, in which he has walked, who sets his mind on the heavenly way of justice, in which he promised in baptism that he would walk, and determines to go forward according to the teaching of the Scriptures, and does not consent to turn aside either by the way of error or by the luxuries of the world.
• Return, O virgin, etc. Although some refer these things, according to the history, to the return of the Jews from Babylon into their own land, to rebuild the ruined cities and the ancient dwellings, according to that: “Remove out of the midst of Babylon, and go forth out of the land of the Chaldeans,” etc.; yet it seems to me more fitting to refer all of it to the time of the New Testament, in which the virgin’s childbearing brought forth the Saviour for the whole world, so that the virgin of Israel, whom the Lord has espoused to himself “in justice, and judgment, and in mercy,” after her former pollutions may return to the cities of the Church, and cease to wander through the luxuries of the world.
*Gregory:* Statute. To set up a watchtower for oneself is to foreknow, by deep consideration, the coming struggles of the vices. And my elect one sets bitterness for himself when, even in the established peace of the virtues, seeing the evils that lie in ambush, he does not consent to rest secure. First, that he may not do any evil. Second, he considers lest he do good things carelessly; and after he has subdued the wicked things, he strives to subject even the right things to himself, lest, if it pass beyond the mind’s mastery, it be turned into the fault of pride. For from good things, through the fault of carelessness, evils are born: from learning, arrogance; from justice, cruelty; from piety, laxity; from zeal, anger; from meekness, sluggishness; and the like. “Direct,” he says, “thy heart into the right way.” The right way is the path of God’s commandments, in which one must walk, and not turn aside to the right hand or to the left.
31.22:
**“How long wilt thou be dissolute in deliciousness, O wandering daughter?”** — as if to say: look at what I am about to say, and whence your blessedness is to be hoped for; I have heard it, that the Lord hath created a new thing
**“for the Lord hath created a new thing upon the earth”** — note that the birth of the Saviour and the conception of God are called creation
**“A woman”**
• Mary
• in the bosom of the womb
• without the seed of a man
**“shall compass a man”**
• Behold a man, the Orient is his name
• from conception: because, according to the increase of age, he will be seen to cry out as a baby and to grow in wisdom and age as a child; but as a perfect man he is contained in a woman’s womb for the usual months
31.23:
**“Thus saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: As yet shall they say”** — the faithful
**“this word in the land of Juda”**
• that is, the Church
• namely of confession
**“and in the cities thereof, when I shall bring back”** — into their own land
**“their captivity: The Lord bless thee”** — because truly it is the beauty of justice, and the holy mountain, in which whoever dwells will fear no snares
**“the beauty of justice”** — “Thou art beautiful above the sons of men”
**“the holy mountain”** — “Come, let us go up to the mountain of the Lord”
**“As yet shall they say”** — That is, in Christian times, in which the Lord turned the captivity of his people
**“The Lord bless thee”** — These things under Zorobabel seem to have been fulfilled in part; but the fullness of the prophecy is referred to Christ, since at the first coming these things were done spiritually. In the second, however, all will be fulfilled. According to us, spiritually; according to the Jews and our Judaizers, carnally.
31.24:
**“shall dwell”** — without iniquity
**“Juda ... therein”** — confessing
**“and all his cities”** — and the churches of the nations, which the one catholic faith holds, which is the city of the great king
**“together: the husbandmen”** — preachers
**“and they that drive the flocks”**
• subjects
• And the multitude of believers had but one heart and one soul.
31.25:
**“For I have inebriated”**
• in a good sense, according to that: “Eat, friends, and be inebriated, dearest ones”; Joseph was inebriated with this drunkenness with his brothers at noon.
• The change of persons makes the understanding of the prophets obscure. The Lord had said: “As yet shall they say this word in the land of Juda,” etc.; and to those saying it he answered: “For I have inebriated the weary soul,” etc. When he says this, the people returned from captivity answers: “Upon this I was awaked,” etc.
**“the weary soul ... every hungry soul ... I have filled”**
• Blessed are they that hunger and thirst after justice: for they shall have their fill.
• If any man thirst, let him come to me, and drink.
31.26:
**“Upon this”** — Those who had been weary and hungry, inebriated and satisfied, answer giving thanks.
**“I was as it were awaked out of a sleep”** — or I was awakened.
**“and I saw, and my sleep was sweet to me”**
• Christ awakening and saying: Arise, thou that sleepest, etc.
• Therefore as if, etc. That I might imitate him who says: I have slept and taken my rest, etc.
• Upon this, as it were, etc. That is, through the grace of Christ, who rose from the sleep of death in glory, the prophet is roused by divine revelation from the sleep of weariness and sadness; comforted by God’s promises, he finds the sleep of rest and peace. Whence: “If thou sleep, thou shalt not fear: thou shalt rest, and thy sleep shall be sweet.” For according to the letter, he sleeps secure and wakes, rests and walks, who remembers that he is innocent before God and lives justly. But also the just man, when he sleeps in death, not only does not fear the powers of the malignant spirits, but even rests in peace and sleeps secure, and awaits the day of resurrection.
31.27:
**“Behold the days come”** — of the new testament.
**“saith the Lord: and I will sow the house of Israel and the house of Juda”** — the catholic Church
**“with the seed of men”**
• of rational beings
• of the Jews, instituted under divine law
**“and with the seed of beasts”**
• of the simple
• namely of the Gentiles: “God is not a respecter of persons”; nor is there “distinction of the Jew and the Greek.”
**“Behold the days”** — All promises of this kind are awaited, according to the Jews and our Judaizers, in the kingdom of a thousand years. But we maintain that they were fulfilled in part, spiritually, in the first coming of Christ, because now “we see through a glass in a dark manner,” and do not know as we ought to know; or we believe they are to be fulfilled in the second, when the Lord will appear in his majesty, and the fullness of the Gentiles shall have come in, so that all Israel may be saved, and not in part, through individuals, but “that God may be all in all.”
31.28:
**“And”** — that I should do what I threatened.
**“As I have watched over them, to pluck up”** — all nations on account of original and actual sins.
**“to throw down, and to scatter, and destroy”** — Whence: that you may root up, and destroy, and scatter, and build, and plant.
**“and to afflict: so will I watch over them, to build up, and to plant them”** — For you are God’s husbandry, God’s building.
**“saith the Lord”** — Appeased by the death of Christ and the shedding of his blood.
31.29:
**“In those days they shall say no more: The fathers have eaten a sour grape”**
• vices and sins.
• Gillibertus, explaining this, has glossed Ezechiel fully.
31.30:
**“But every one shall die for his own iniquity”** — For the Lord does not make death, but sin; whence “the soul that sinneth, the same shall die”, as if Israel offended not by the sins of the fathers but by its own; and after many times it will be saved by faith in Christ.
**“every man that shall eat”** — Gregory. For what is the sour grape but sin? The sour grape is fruit before its time. For whoever desires to be filled with the delights of the present life hastens, as it were, to eat fruit before its time. He, therefore, who eats the sour grape, his teeth are set on edge; because he who feeds on the delights of the present world, his senses are bound in earthly things, so that he can no longer chew spiritual things, that is, understand them; because those who have delighted in outward things are thence made dull in inward things; and while the soul is fed on sin, it cannot eat the bread of justice, because teeth bound by the habit of sin cannot eat the just thing which they savour within.
**“his teeth shall be set on edge”** — The teeth of those who eat cannot perceive the sweetness of which it is said: “O taste, and see that the Lord is sweet.” Whoever does not understand the Scriptures as the truth has them eats a sour grape. Whence: heretics cannot eat the bread that came down from heaven, because their teeth are set on edge, not by the harshness of the foods but by the defect of the teeth.
31.31:
**“Behold the days shall come, saith the Lord, and I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel, and with the house of Juda”** — testament, namely, that which is written by the Holy Spirit in the hearts of the faithful.
**“Behold the days”** — Paul, or whoever else wrote the epistle to the Hebrews, used this testimony; and all churchmen thereafter say that everything was fulfilled in the first coming of the Saviour, and that the New Testament, that is, the gospel, succeeded the old; and that the law of the letter was exchanged for the law of the spirit, so that all the sacrifices and circumcision and the sabbath are fulfilled spiritually.
31.32:
**“Not according to the covenant which I made with their fathers”** — of the old testament, which is written on tablets of stone, to a hard and unbelieving nation.
**“in the day that I took them by the hand”** — as a familiar.
**“to bring them out of the land of Egypt: the covenant which they made void, and”** — therefore.
**“I had dominion over them”** — by justly avenging.
31.33:
**“But this shall be the covenant that I will make with the house”** — or to the house
**“Israel, after those days”** — after the cross, that is, the resurrection and the ascension
**“saith the Lord: I will give my law”** — the law shall go forth from Sion, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem
**“in their bowels”** — his law in his heart
**“and in their heart”** — not on tables of stone but on the fleshly tables of the heart
**“I will write it, and I will be their God”** — after these
31.34:
**“And they shall teach no more every man his neighbour, and every man his brother, saying: Know the Lord: for all shall know me from the least of them even to the greatest, saith the Lord: for I will forgive”** — that is, at the first coming
**“And they shall teach no more”** — And let them not seek Jewish teachers and the commandments of men, but be taught by the Holy Spirit, if indeed they are the temple of God and the Holy Spirit dwells in them, who “breatheth where he will,” and has diverse graces. Yet the knowledge of the one God is the possession of all virtues.
**“For all shall know”** — Because all will be in the contemplation of the truth. Whence: “We see now through a glass in a dark manner; but then face to face.” And elsewhere: “We shall see him as he is”; not as men see, that is, or saw, when he appeared in the form he willed, not in the nature in which he lay hidden in himself even when he was seen.
31.35: **“who giveth the sun”** — According to the kind. The sun is set in the sky for the light of the day; the moon and the stars for the light of the night. In the psalm too it is read: “Day to day uttereth speech, and night to night sheweth knowledge,” because day and night succeed one another in turn.
31.36:
**“If these ordinances shall fail”** — the constitution and order of nature
**“before me, saith the Lord: then also the seed of Israel shall fail”** — as the heavens will not perish, so the seed of Israel by the will of the Lord will be perpetual and will never cease
**“so as not to be a nation before me for ever”** — If they shall fail, etc. If the heavens shall perish and grow old like a garment, how can the seed of Israel be everlasting? But the heavens will perish; whence Jacob says to his sons: “Come together, that I may tell you the things that shall befall you in the last days,” in which it is plain that the world is not everlasting. Whence: “Heaven and earth shall pass away.” And elsewhere: “Behold I am with you even to the consummation of the world.” Or otherwise. Allegorically: as long as this world shall be, the seed of Israel will remain, not in those who are unbelieving, but in those who believed in the apostles and through the apostles, that the remnant might be saved.
31.37:
**“Thus saith the Lord: If the heavens above can be measured”** — that their greatness may be known
**“the heavens above, and the foundations of the earth searched out beneath”** — that they may be grasped by reason; as it is impossible, so is that; and if we hear the Jews boasting of this testimony, let us agree that the whole seed of Israel has not been cast off, but only the unbelievers
**“If ... can be measured”** — As if to say: since the order of things, and above all of the heavenly stars, cannot be changed, and the waves of the sea roll to the shores, and the roar of the deep is heard terrible, and goes not beyond the command. Whence: “Thou hast set them a bound which they shall not pass over,” etc. So the seed of Israel will be everlasting by the will of the Lord, and will never cease.
31.38:
**“Behold the days come, saith the Lord, that the city shall be built”**
• “Glorious things are said of thee, O city of God”; and elsewhere, “The stream of the river maketh the city of God joyful”
• The Church
**“to the Lord from the tower”** — of obedience or of grace
**“Behold the days come”** — Those who look for a kingdom of a thousand years in Judea try to show that from the tower of Hananeel to the gate of the corner, the hill Gareb and Goatha, etc., the sanctuary of the Lord is to be built in the temple and to remain for ever. Because they cannot show this fulfilled under Zorobabel himself, they pass to the times of Christ, who they say will come at the consummation of the world, so that a golden Jerusalem may descend from heaven and be built on this space of earth round about. They conjecture this because the foundations of the city are to be laid from the tower of Anathoth, which is called Jeremias’s and is separated from Jerusalem by a distance of three thousand paces, as far as the torrent Cedron. They say that Hananeel the son of Sellum was Jeremias’s cousin, whose field he bought, and this, they say, is the tower of Hananeel, not knowing the Hebrew truth. For this Hananeel is written with the letter nun in the middle, but the other Hananeel with the letter mem.
**“Hanameel even to the gate of the corner”**
• Even to the gate of the corner, etc. At the corner the two walls of the city are joined; so it is said the city is built from the tower of Ananehel to the gate of the corner, because the Church, beginning from the height of grace, is built up to the entry and the regard of the Jewish and the Gentile people.
• Even to the gate of the corner, etc. Although the Church seems to have a lofty beginning, yet in this life the corners cannot possess the straight line of truth. For we stand in a corner while we live; and with the lines broken, it also goes out beyond the measuring line, over against the gate of the corner, upon the hill Gareb, which is interpreted sojourning or itch. In this we are signified as strangers and pilgrims, and as having itching ears and readily receiving the novelty of the worst doctrine. And it compasses Goatha, which the Septuagint interpreted as circuit, namely of the elect, the living stones, which are rolled over the face of the earth and are bound together by the corner stone; and you understand that it will go round the whole valley of Phagar, which is interpreted of ruins, and of ashes, so that although we seem to ourselves always to be on the hills, we may yet fear ruins and consider ashes, and say in penance: “I did eat ashes like bread.” And all Sedemoch, which Jerome turned into “the country of death,” dividing one name into two. For sade means country, and mooch means of death. But the country of death is the country of sinners, which goes on as far as the torrent Cedron, where the Lord was delivered up, which is interpreted darkness. See how many places the Church has, and that she will at last be “without spot or wrinkle” in the heavenly places. You hear of corners and itch, you hear of ruins and ashes, the country of death and darkness, and never glory. Finally it follows: even to the corner of the horse gate. For there is no true justice or sure victory in this world. The very corner of the gate, although eastern, whence the light comes forth, is called of the horses, to teach us that we need running and struggle, that at last we may deserve to hear with the Lord: “Thou hast mounted thy horses, and thy riding is salvation.” In the eastern gate and in the gate of the chariots is the holiness of the Lord, that we may then think ourselves perfect when we shall have said: “The chariot of God is attended by ten thousands; thousands of them that rejoice: the Lord is among them in Sina, in the holy place.” This building will remain for ever.
31.39: **“And the measuring line shall go out farther in his sight upon the hill Gareb: and it shall compass Goatha”** — The Seventy: a circuit
31.40: **“And the whole valley of dead bodies”** — Theodotion. He put the Hebrew itself, fagarim, or “of ruins”; another reading

32.1: **“The word that”** — Not only the words but also the deeds of the prophets are for us examples of virtues. Jeremiah could announce prosperity and enjoy the king’s friendship, but he preferred to obey God, “who can destroy both soul and body in hell.”
32.2: **“At that time the army of the king of Babylon besieged Jerusalem: and Jeremias the prophet was shut up in the court of the prison, which was in the house of the king of Juda.”** — In the court of the prison, etc. The king’s mercy is to be noted, who ordered the prophet shut up not in the prison but in the vestibule, in free custody, that is, so that he could not escape, as if all Jerusalem, closed in by its fortifications, were not a common prison.
32.3:
**“For Sedecias king of Juda had shut him up, saying: Why dost thou prophesy, saying:”** — the king is angry at him because he speaks in the name of the Lord what had been enjoined on him
**“For Sedecias king of Juda had shut him up”** — Now captivity being near, the city now consumed by plague and famine, and yet Sedecias persists in his opinion.
**“Thus saith the Lord: Behold I will give this city into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he shall take it”** — Why dost thou prophesy, etc. The terror before the rebuke of words is heavier than to endure torment and to see him whom you fear.
32.4:
**“And Sedecias king of Juda shall not escape out of the hand of the Chaldeans: but he shall be delivered into the hands of the king of Babylon: and he shall speak to him mouth to mouth”** — of a humble captive
**“mouth to mouth”** — of the powerful and the mad
32.5:
**“And he shall lead Sedecias to Babylon: and he shall be there till I visit him, saith the Lord”** — He uses an ambiguous word, lest torment and misery seem to be prophesied
**“But if you will fight against the Chaldeans, you shall have no success”** — Visit, etc. He tempered the sentence so that the visitation could be referred to the good or the bad part; for visitation signifies both consolation and punishment.
32.6: **“And Jeremias said: The word of the Lord came to me, saying”** — no one could know this unless Jeremiah himself indicated it
32.7:
**“Behold, Hanameel”** — Helcias and Sellum were brothers german. Jeremias was the son of Helcias; Hananeel, of Sellum. Helcias is interpreted the portion of the Lord. Jeremias, the height of the Lord; and rightly the height of the Lord is born of the portion of the Lord. But Sellum means peaceable, or peace. Hananeel, the gift or grace of God; and fittingly peace and grace are joined, according to that: “Grace to us and peace,” etc. First, then, for peace we deserve the gift of God, and after peace grace is born to us, which is not in the choice of the possessor but of the giver. But the grace of God brings the purchase to him who is on high, that although he seems exalted, he may yet need grace. That Jeremias was the son of Helcias, of the priests who were in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin, the beginning of this volume shows.
**“Buy thee my field”** — This priestly field, whose purchase and possession is ascribed to Jeremias, is in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin; the first of these sounds like obedience, the second “son of the right hand”; and it fittingly seeks his purchase, in which the obedience and power of the Lord was at work.
32.8:
**“came to me”** — that the prophecy might be fulfilled by the deed
**“Hanameel”** — the grace of God
**“my uncle's son”** — of peace
**“my uncle's son, according to the word of the Lord, to the entry of the prison, and said to me”** — which the Lord had foretold
**“Buy my field, which is in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin: for the right of inheritance is thine, and thou art next of kin to possess it. And I understood that this was the word of the Lord.”**
• In the land of Benjamin, etc. This is of the suburbs which were given by the law to the priests in each of the tribes and cities; nor was it lawful to transfer a possession from tribe to tribe, nor from family to family; whence also the daughters of Salphaad received a lot among their brethren. But especially the suburbs of the priests could not be sold until the year of release, except to the one to whom it belonged by nearness of blood.
• He bought the field for seventeen sicles; in which number the servant of the Lord, David, sang on the day in which the Lord delivered him from the hand of his enemies and from the hand of Saul, and said: “I will love thee, O Lord, my strength,” etc. That ten is a mystical number the decalogue written by the finger of God shows. Seven also, in which is the true sabbath and holy rest, is commended by many testimonies. And with this number the prophet and priest bought the possession, and it is written in a book and sealed, witnesses are called in, and the silver is carefully weighed, that all the rights of sale and purchase may be kept, and the possession may be sure, confirmed by the stipulation, the common forms and the replies. Let those hear this who try to claim false testaments, and sometimes even without testaments or witnesses called.
**“And I understood”** — It seemed laughable that he, who was already prophesying that the city was about to be taken and the nearby captivity, should buy a field which he could not possess; but he understood that the word was of the Lord and that the purchase agreed with the Lord’s prophecy.
32.9: **“And I bought the field of Hanameel my uncle's son, that is in Anathoth: and I weighed him the money, seven staters, and ten pieces of silver.”** — shekels. A shekel has twenty obols.
32.12:
**“And I gave the deed”** — although the possession was soon to be left behind
**“of the purchase to Baruch the son”** — to so great and such a man
**“of Neri the son of Maasias in the sight of Hanameel”** — who had sold
**“my uncle's son, in the presence of the witnesses that subscribed the book of the purchase, and before all the Jews that sat in the court of the prison”** — either they had come to console the prophet, or they desired to hear the words of the Lord
32.13:
**“And I charged Baruch before them, saying”** — present and seeing, as said above
**“And I charged Baruch”** — Baruch, which is interpreted blessed, who was the son of Neri, that is, of my lamp, of which it is said: “Thy word is a lamp to my feet, and a light to my paths.” Neri also was the son of Maasias, that is, of the making and work of the Lord. Note then with how great privileges of virtues Baruch served Jeremias, according to that: “The man that walked in the perfect way, he served me.” Whence Eliseus, the minister of Elias, so pleased God that when his master was taken up he deserved to receive a double spirit. This is said against those who abuse the services of the wicked and do not dare to cast off those who are conscious of their iniquity.
32.14:
**“Thus saith the Lord of hosts the God of Israel”** — as if the Lord commanded through me
**“Take these writings”** — This custom is kept to this day: that the open volume is offered to those wishing to read what the sealed inside contains.
**“Take these writings, this deed of the purchase that is sealed up, and this deed that is open: and put them in an earthen vessel, that they may continue many days.”** — In an earthen vessel, etc. Lest, being placed in the open, they lie exposed to plunder, and, entrusted to the ground, be dissolved by damp. And this is done so that those who see may understand that Jerusalem is to be inhabited again and the possession possessed; and although they could understand of themselves, they are nevertheless admonished by the word of God.
32.15: **“Houses, and fields, and vineyards shall be possessed again”** — And this is what Jeremiah said above, that he understood the word of God, and for that reason bought the field.
32.16: **“And I prayed to the Lord”** — the purchase of the field having been completed and the sentence of the Lord received, that houses and fields and vineyards are still to be possessed
32.17:
**“Alas, alas, alas, O Lord God”** — the groan expresses the grief of the heart
**“behold thou hast made heaven and earth”** — Christ, the power of God and the wisdom of God; whence “Thou hast made all things in wisdom”
**“by thy great power, and thy stretched out arm”** — the arm of the Lord, to whom it has been revealed
**“stretched out”** — stretched out: indicates the one striking
**“no word shall be hard to thee”** — which are impossible with men are possible with God, that is
32.18:
**“Thou shewest mercy unto thousands, and returnest the iniquity of the fathers into the bosom of their children after them: O most mighty, great, and powerful, the Lord of hosts is thy name.”**
• Who showest mercy, etc. Great is the mercy of the Creator: to extend his mercy to a thousand generations, and to show justice in another generation, which nevertheless is mixed with mercy. For he does not punish the offender at once, but waits for repentance, so that the punishment, long deferred, may be repaid to the children if they have imitated the vices of their parents.
• O most mighty, etc. These names indicate the power of the Creator, but properly the name of God is Father; whence: “Father, I have manifested thy name to the men.”
32.19:
**“Great in counsel and incomprehensible in thought”** — which thought does not comprehend; how can speech comprehend it?
**“whose eyes are open”** — therefore let no one think he can hide
**“Great in counsel”** — Let no one thrust himself into the secrets of God and presume to judge his judgments.
**“upon all the ways of the children of Adam, to render unto every one according to his ways, and according to the fruit of his devices.”** — That thou mayest render, etc. It signifies that at times, because of his too great patience, his judgments seem unjust; whence: “Knowest thou not that the benignity of God leadeth thee to penance?” The later the vengeance, therefore, the more just, as is plain in Pharaoh, who, warned by ten plagues and not punished, and persevering in hardness, was at last overwhelmed by the waves of the Red Sea.
32.20:
**“Who hast set signs and wonders in the land of Egypt even until this day, and in Israel, and amongst men, and hast made thee a name as at this day.”**
• your praises are celebrated throughout the whole world
• Who hast set signs, etc. He passes from the general to the particular and briefly runs through what in particular he granted to Israel.
• And wonders, etc. “Wherewith it was afflicted unto this day” is to be joined to what follows. As if to say: and in Israel and among all mortals thy signs are daily fulfilled; or it is nourished. Signs and wonders thou didst work not only in Egypt, but even to this day the same strength of thy mercy saves thy people, and thou comest to the aid of mankind by the power of the Creator. And it is to be noted that he separates Israel from all others. According to that: “Israel is my first-born son.”
32.21:
**“And hast brought forth”** — for when he was led out, he served your command
**“thy people Israel, out of the land of Egypt with signs”** — when the Red Sea gave Israel a way and overwhelmed the Egyptians
32.22:
**“And hast given them this land which thou didst swear to their fathers”** — Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; for they received the land of promise not by their own merit but by the virtues of the fathers
**“to give them a land flowing with milk and honey.”**
• because they could not yet take solid food
• by which infancy is nourished, or by the abundance of all things
32.23:
**“And they came in, and possessed it: but they obeyed not thy voice, and they walked not in thy law: and they did not any of those things that thou didst command them to do, and all these evils are come upon them.”** — according to the Lord’s sentence he returns good to each one according to his works
**“And they came in”** — There is nothing in between possession and disobedience. For abundance produces security, security negligence, and negligence contempt.
**“but they obeyed not”** — Therefore they promised in vain, saying: Whatever the Lord has commanded, we will do; for reward lies not in promise but in deed.
32.24:
**“Behold works are built up against the city to take it: and the city is given into the hands of the Chaldeans, who fight against it, by the sword, and the famine, and the pestilence: and what thou hast spoken, is all come to pass, as thou thyself seest.”** — Behold works are built up, etc. It was the tenth year of Sedecias, and the city was besieged, as was said above; and Jeremias was in the court of the prison, whence it is added: behold, the works are built up.
**“to take it”** — As if they had no one to conquer, but people to seize, now consumed by famine and pestilence.
**“And what thou hast spoken”** — From creatures he proclaims the Creator, and first his power and miracles and justice toward the whole race of men; then he passes to Israel and describes how much he has bestowed on it. And after such great benefits, being unmindful of the good things, they provoked his clemency to bitterness, so that the city is besieged and, before it is taken, is consumed by sword and famine and pestilence. All this, however, he sets forward in order to bring in, as if in reproof, the divine sentence: “And thou sayest to me, O Lord God, buy a field.”
32.25: **“And sayest thou”** — He does not rebuke but asks; nor does he say it so much to himself as to others who were sitting in the court of the prison and perhaps silently rebuking. How can the prophet, whom they believed to proclaim the truth, say that the city is to be taken and buy a field which he nonetheless does not possess?
32.27:
**“Behold I am the Lord the God of all flesh: shall any thing be hard for me?”** — nothing will be impossible; every word with God, that is, whatever thing one pleases
**“Behold I am the Lord the God of all flesh”** — Not of all nations, nor of the people of Israel only, nor as is said of the saints, the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob, but let him be believed to have made all flesh, that is, rational and brute living creatures. For there are those who confess the providence of the Creator as far as rational creatures, but say that brutes perish or live by chance. Therefore the prophet declares that there is nothing that escapes the providence and knowledge of God, because some things were made for thee, others for the use of men.
32.28:
**“Behold I will deliver”** — Because it is my care to rule all things, to arrange everything, and to render to each according to his ways.
**“this city”** — First it was surrounded by the army of the Chaldeans, Nabuchodonosor being absent, and it was taken; and Sedecias was handed over to the king at Reblatha.
32.29:
**“And the Chaldeans that fight against this city, shall come and set it on fire, and burn it, with the houses upon whose roofs they offered sacrifice to Baal”**
• to the idol of the Sidonians
• not from error but from contention, so that they seem to do insult to the Creator
**“shall come”** — Aquila: “they shall enter” is better; for those who besiege the city were not absent, that they should come; but the Hebrew word sounds “and they shall come and they shall enter.”
**“with the houses”** — As the world is written of as about to perish, according to that: Heaven and earth shall pass away; because it is placed in evil, so also the house itself and the places in which crimes were committed will be subject to the wrath of God.
32.30:
**“For the children of Israel”** — ten tribes
**“and the children of Juda”** — two tribes
**“have continually done evil”** — Without end. Where then is everlasting justice? The Septuagint: for they alone had knowledge of God, and withdrew from him. Therefore they alone sin in his Churches who have remained unbelieving; they offend as though he did not see and were negligent. Whence David, a holy man and penitent, says: “I have done evil before thee,” that is, in thy sight.
32.32:
**“Because of all the evil of the children of Israel, and of the children of Juda”** — what he foretold in general he enumerates in parts
**“which they have done, provoking me to wrath, they and their kings, their princes, and their priests, and their prophets”** — not of me
32.33:
**“And they have turned their backs to me, and not their faces: when I taught them early in the morning, and instructed them, and they would not hearken”** — signifies free will
**“to receive instruction.”** — And they turned, etc. Whence elsewhere: they turn their back against me, withdrawing. For one who prays, with neck bowed, falls prone on the ground; but one who turns his back shows by bodily gesture that he disregards the one threatening.
**“when I taught them”** — With the darkness of error dispelled and the worship of idols, I desired to enlighten them and to teach what is right.
32.34: **“And they have set their idols in the house, in which my name is called upon, to defile it.”** — And they set, etc. Not only then did Judah set an idol in the temple of God, but even today an idol is set up in the Church or in the heart of believers when a new dogma is constructed and is worshipped in secret.
32.35:
**“And they have built the high places of Baal”** — in Hebrew, Bamoth
**“which are in the valley of the son of Ennom, to consecrate their sons and their daughters to Moloch”** — to the idol of the Ammonites, which is interpreted king; for they did not serve Baal only
**“which I commanded them not, neither entered it into my heart”** — anthropospathos
**“that they should do this abomination, and cause Juda to sin.”** — And they built, etc. Properly the tribes of Judah and Benjamin worshipped at the shrine of Baal and Moloch, the images of demons; the golden calves at Dan and Bethel, the ten tribes; which is so abominable that the Lord bears witness he never even thought of it.
**“In the valley”** — In the valley: which lies under the springs of Siloe, and by its pleasantness provoked the people to luxury, which is followed by the worship of idols.
32.37:
**“Behold I will gather them together”** — into the Church
**“out of all the lands”** — whence: “to gather together in one the children of God, that were dispersed.”
**“to which I have cast them out in my anger, and in my wrath, and in my great indignation: and I will bring them again into this place, and will cause them to dwell securely.”** — Behold I, etc. Many think this was fulfilled in the time of Zorobabel, when the temple was built under Nehemias and the walls raised round about. But how will it be true: “I will cause them to dwell securely,” and “I will make an everlasting covenant with them”? For they have often been captured, not only by neighbouring nations but by the Persians and Macedonians, by the Egyptians and Romans, and even to this day are in servitude. Everything, therefore, is to be referred to the coming of Christ, in whom we see it fulfilled, and the choice of the remnant is saved.
**“and I will bring them again”** — As to those who hope for help and trust in the strength of the walls, the city is foretold or prophesied to be overthrown, and the people to perish in every distress; so to those who despair, and after the overthrow of the city expect no deliverance, he promises his help, that confidence and pride may deserve the just sentence, and despair and humility may deserve the help of God.
32.38: **“And they shall be my people, and I will be their God.”** — They shall be my people, etc. He adds joy to the sorrowful and promises return to the captives; but first he shows the cause of offense and of just wrath, and how much greater the fault, so much the greater clemency toward sinners.
32.39:
**“And I will give them one heart, and one way”** — The multitude of believers had but one heart and one soul.
**“that they may fear me”** — filially: “Blessed is the man that feareth the Lord”
**“all days: and that it may be well with them, and with their children after them.”** — And I will give them, etc. Cassiodorus. It plainly shows that the beginning of good will is granted to us by the inspiration of the Lord, when either by himself, or by the exhortation of some man, or by necessity, he draws us back or transfers us to the way of salvation, and that perfection likewise is bestowed by the same.
