Whence of the widows: “Having damnation, because they have made void their first faith.” It is better not to promise than not to perform what is promised. Anna offered Samuel, who remained in eternal holiness. Manue offered his son Samson, but the lust of Dalila troubled the sanctification of his hair, and the Lord departed from him, and he was condemned to blindness; except that afterwards, as his hair grew, he received his former strength, and, in the type of Christ, he fell having slain many more of the foreigners in death than in life.
**“They shall put off their garments wherein they ministered”** — Rabanus. Lest, if they have holy garments, they sanctify the people who stand outside, who have not yet been sanctified nor prepared themselves in the sanctification of the temple, so as to be a Nazarite of the Lord. Whence: we learn that we ought not to enter the holy of holies in everyday garments, defiled by the common use of life, but with a clean conscience and clean garments to hold the sacraments of the Lord.
44.20:
**“But their heads”** — The hairs of the apostles’ heads are all numbered. Of this head it is said: “The eyes of a wise man are in his head”; and the head of the man is Christ.
**“Neither shall they shave their heads, nor wear long hair”** — So that they are not with shaven heads, as is the custom for priests and worshippers of Isis and Serapis; nor again let them let their hair grow, which properly belongs to the lustful, to barbarians and to soldiers; but let the dress of the priests be honourable.
**“but they shall only poll their heads”** — But they shall not shave their head. Rabanus. The Lord wills that his priests have the hair of sanctification perpetual, and that their heads be covered not by any covering from outside but by their own natural hair, not for ornament and luxury but for decency. Whence: “the very hairs of your head are all numbered.” Of which head it is read: “the eyes of a wise man are in his head”; the head of man is Christ, which the sinner tramples upon and despises, and shaves with a razor and takes away its beauty. This the sons of Ammon also did to those whom David had sent as ambassadors. But if the transgressor of the law dishonours God, he who keeps the precepts of the king honours him, “that all men may honour the Son, as they honour” the Father.
*Jerome:* Shall not shave. Pagan superstition has shaven heads.
44.21:
**“And no priest shall drink wine when he is to go into the inner court”** — In which there is luxury; of which: “It is good not to drink wine and not to eat flesh.” “The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.” The apostle allows wine to Timothy, but because of infirmity.
**“And no priest shall drink wine”** — Because by drunkenness the steadiness of the mind is overturned, which is understood of all vices and of all worldly business, by which the mind is made drunk and wavers and cannot hold steady. And because we are surrounded with frail flesh and are compelled, for food, drink, clothing and the necessities of the body, to do what we ought not, this at least is required of us: that when we return to ourselves and know why we were born and enter the inner parts of the temple, we depart from vices and commit not even the least sins; by which it is shown both that we sin for the needs of the flesh, with light sins, and again that there is a time when, entering the court beyond, we ought to be altogether free of all the drunkenness of the world.
44.22:
**“a widow”** — The synagogue, which does not receive the Lord; whence she was rightly cast out.
**“nor one that is divorced”** — The multitude of heretics who went out from us but were not of us.
**“they shall not take to wife, but they shall take virgins”** — Who were nurtured in the house of God in the law and the prophets. Whence: “For I have espoused you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ.” Of this virgin it is said: “Love her, and she shall keep thee”: namely, wisdom.
**“of the seed of the house of Israel: but they may take a widow also”** — knowledge, namely, which another worshipper of God has found; for we ought not to be content with new teaching only, but also to cultivate the old and join it to our own accompanying teaching, provided it has been instructed in sacred worship.
44.23:
**“And they shall teach my people”** — This is the office of the priest.
**“they shall teach”** — By teaching doctrine.
**“the difference between holy and profane, and shew them how to discern between clean and unclean”** — By doing.
44.24:
**“And when there shall be a controversy”** — About any matter.
**“they shall stand in my judgments”** — Namely, that they accept not the person either of the poor or of the rich.
**“and shall judge: they shall keep my laws, and my ordinances in all my solemnities”** — that they may know how Christ our pasch was sacrificed for us, how we ought to fulfil the seven weeks of joy and gladness, and afflict our souls in fasting, and understand the sounding of the trumpets, and the spiritual feasts of tabernacles, in which we say: “I am a stranger with thee, and a sojourner as all my fathers were.”
**“and sanctify my sabbaths”**
• Not of those of whom it is said: “Your new moons and your sabbaths my soul hateth.” And elsewhere: “The priests in the temple break the sabbath, and are without blame”: the sabbath, namely, of the Jews, which they rightly break who are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood.
• Rabanus. Namely those that are left, namely to the people of God. Whence: “If they shall enter into my rest,” which in Hebrew is called the sabbath. He sanctifies these who does not carry the burden of sin on the sabbath, nor says: “as a heavy burden are become heavy upon me.” Such a one also does not gather sticks on the sabbath, nor builds upon the foundation of Christ wood, hay, stubble, nor kindles a fire to consume useless matter; and on the sabbath day he abides in one place, nor goes out abroad, but remains as a pillar set in the temple of God. Whence: “He that shall overcome, I will make him a pillar in the temple of my God; and he shall go out no more.”
**“They shall stand”** — Mindful of that saying: “God hath stood in the congregation of gods: and being in the midst of them he judgeth gods.” He calls gods those who have the power of judging men, who will be judged by the judgment in which they have judged.
**“my laws, and my ordinances in all my solemnities”** — Rabanus. The first virtue of a priest is not only to teach what he knows but to keep all the festivals of God, that he may be able to command others to keep them, since he himself is zealous to observe them. And it is the priest’s office to have knowledge of the law. Whence Malachias: “the lips of the priest shall keep knowledge,” etc.
44.25:
**“near no dead person”** — Let the dead bury their dead.
**“they shall come near no”** — It is not for a priest to touch a carcase, since he, who is to plead for the faults of others, ought to approach the altar clean.
**“lest they be defiled, only their father and mother, and son”** — thought
**“and daughter”** — deed
**“and brother and sister”** — who is born again by the same Spirit; if he thinks him dead, he is defiled
**“that hath not had another husband: for whom they may become unclean”**
• Rabanus. If she remains a virgin, stained by the embrace of no man; whence we understand the privilege of virginity, that the touch of any man whatever takes away perfect purity.
• Except for father, etc. Rabanus. Herein the affection of nature is approved, so that in the order of charity, as it is written: “he set in order charity in me,” after God, the father of all, the father of the flesh also is loved, and mother, and son and daughter, brother and sister; so, namely, if she has not gone out of the house nor passed into another’s power.
• For whom they may become unclean. They are defiled in a dead father when they forsake their creator, and in a mother, if the church.
• It must be known that all that the Lord here speaks through the prophet he had also foretold through Moses. But what had been blotted out of the minds of men by neglect of reading, or contempt of hearing, and forgetfulness, is renewed by the living voice, being written not with pen and ink but with the Spirit and Word of God. Whence also the Saviour left no volume of doctrine, though the apocrypha falsely claim this, but speaks daily by the Father and his Spirit in the heart of the faithful. This also is the reason why what is said in the Pentateuch is repeated in the prophets.
44.26:
**“And after one is cleansed”** — according to the Mosaic law
**“seven days”** — which is the more perfect number of fullness, so that after the consummation of the world, when passing over to the true ogdoad, one enters the holy of holies
44.27: **“And in the day that he goeth into the sanctuary, to the inner court”** — The holy of holies.
44.28:
**“And they shall have inheritance, I am their inheritance, and”** — therefore
**“neither shall you give them any possession in Israel”**
• among the common people
• Rabanus. He who shall be such as to minister in the sanctuary, and enter the inner court, and always offer sacrifice to the Lord, an imitator of the true priest, who is “a priest for ever, according to the order of Melchisedech,” shall have no inheritance but God, who is his inheritance. Nor shall he receive a possession in Israel among the ignoble common people, but a priestly one, because the Lord himself is his inheritance.
**“for I am their possession”** — The Lord is the portion of my inheritance.
44.29:
**“the victim both for sin and for trespass”** — Whence: they shall eat the sins of my people.
**“the victim”** — Of conscience, nor is there any time when it does not recall having been defiled over father and mother, son and daughter, brother and sister. For it is compelled to do many things amid the straits of this age, or the condition of the flesh, or the frailty of nature.
**“For trespass”** — Jerome. We are not so much to rejoice at the offering of gifts as to fear the condemnation of honour if we abuse them.
44.30:
**“And the firstfruits of all the firstborn”** — of living and lifeless things, which are born first, which the earth first brings forth
**“and all the libations of all things that are offered, shall be the priest's”** — of our food, so that we taste nothing unless the priest has first tasted it, namely of the new fruits
**“And the firstfruits”** — Great is the dignity of priests, but if they sin, the fall is grievous; let us rejoice at the ascent, but fear the fall. There is not so great joy in having held high places as there is grief in having fallen from high places; for we render account not only for our own sins, but for those of all whose gifts we abuse.
*Rabanus:* Allegorically. All these things are to be referred to the Church, which labours in the world and hastens to heavenly things: namely, that out of the whole world some be chosen for the possession of God, who may possess the holy place; others, who have advanced to greater things, may hold the holy of holies. Among the ministers also the order is different, namely of priests and Levites: some of whom by their prayers and virtues offer sacrifices to God daily; others, in a second and lesser rank, that they may minister to these and advance through those who have climbed to the heights of virtue. And lastly let there be a leader or prince, who may be able so far as to receive a possession against one tribe, that the merit of many may make up for the merit of each one. And first, while he lives in the world, let him possess breadth “from sea to sea.” Then from the west, or from the sea, to the east, that leaving present things behind he may hasten to the future. And let him have his own fixed possession, and let the prince not desire what belongs to others. And let each tribe hold its own part; which properly regards the apostles and priests, to whom it is said that they should not lay waste and plunder the people of God, nor possess the land of Israel by inheritance, but that each one should have his own possession, which is appointed for his rank.
44.31:
**“any thing that is dead of itself”** — without the shedding of blood
**“or caught by a beast, whether it be fowl”** — which set their mouth in heaven
**“or cattle”** — which are bent toward the earth and obedient to the belly
**“The priests shall not eat”** — Anything dead of itself, etc. Rabanus. And according to the letter, to every chosen kind, royal and priestly, that is, Christian, which is anointed with spiritual oil; whence: “God, thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.” These precepts agree, that they not eat what is dead of itself, of birds as of cattle, whose blood has not been poured out, which in the Acts of the Apostles is called “strangled,” which the letter of the apostles from Jerusalem admonishes must necessarily be observed; and what is caught by a beast, because that too is likewise strangled. And he condemns priests who do not keep these precepts through the greed of the gullet, for thrushes, fig-peckers, dormice, and the like.
*Rabanus:* Allegorically. The dead of itself is that in which the blood of the soul has died. And it imitates Nabal of Carmel, whose name means fool, who, having heard David’s anger, trembled with fear, and “his heart died within him.” But he is said to be caught by beasts (from whose bites the prophet begs not to be torn, saying: “Deliver not up to beasts the souls that confess to thee”) who is devoured by the bites of the lion, that is, the adversary; and of the leopard, who does not change his variety; and of the she-bear, which rages when her cubs are taken; and of wolves and the other beasts, which we understand in the variety of demons.

45.1:
**“And when you shall begin to divide the land by lot, separate ye firstfruits to the Lord, a portion of the land to be holy”** — that is
**“of the land, in length twenty-five thousand”** — of reeds
**“and in breadth ten thousand: it shall be holy in all the borders thereof”** — of the land
**“on every side”** — And when you shall begin, etc. After the ceremonies of the priests, and their attire, and the food which they ought to take and which to avoid, he makes a description of the holy land. And before he divides it among the tribes, he commands that out of all the tribes a place be chosen which in length shall have twenty-five thousand. And because he does not add of cubits or feet or ells, it is to be understood that the reed is meant, which was in the man’s hand and had a measure of six cubits and the sixth part of one cubit, that is, the Palestinian. Let the diligent reader reckon how many reeds make a thousand paces, and how many thousands there were in length and breadth.
45.2:
**“it shall be holy on every side”** — from the land of the priests, for building the temple
**“five hundred by five hundred, foursquare round about: and fifty cubits”** — lest other buildings be joined to the building of the temple
**“for the suburbs thereof round about”**
• so that namely the land be empty
• And there shall be on every side, etc. After the first description, he namely commands that another land be chosen for building the sanctuary, that is the temple, within, of five hundred reeds around, that is, two thousand.
45.3:
**“And with this measure thou shalt measure the length of five and twenty thousand, and the breadth of ten thousand, and in it shall be”** — measured
**“the temple and the holy of holies”**
• that is, not only the temple but the holy of holies
• And with this measure, etc. Rabanus. In the former temple, which is called the sanctuary, five hundred reeds are described on each side. And again five hundred cubits, by which the whole possession of the priests is separated. But in the second sanctuary, where is the holy of holies, the breadth and space of the temple are not described, but the number is uncertain; which we find also in the possession of the prince, who without any number has a possession among the people of Israel, since the progress of all overflows to the prince, and the salvation of the disciples to the teacher.
45.4:
**“The holy portion of the land shall be for the priests the ministers of the sanctuary, who come near to the ministry of the Lord”** — as if priests will dwell in it, but only then when they perform the priestly office
**“and it shall be a place”** — here, namely
**“for their houses”** — of the priests
45.5:
**“And five and twenty thousand”** — reeds, namely
**“of length, and ten thousand of breadth shall be for the Levites”** — but
**“that minister in the house”** — who serve the priests
**“they shall possess twenty store chambers”** — And five and twenty thousand, etc. Rabanus. Twenty-five refers to the five senses, which are set down four times. Ten thousand, to perfect knowledge, so that in the one case only simple history is held, and in the other there is discussion also of theology and the supernal powers. For ten is perfect. But it must be noted that the priests, who are in the higher rank, possess twenty-five thousand in length and ten in breadth. But the Levites, who are of a lower rank, have indeed the same number in length, that is, twenty-five thousand; but the breadth is limited by five. Whence also they hold only twenty store chambers, a number in which the gifts of Esau are offered. But the prince, who is truly a prince among the people and deserves to receive the name of leader, receives a possession of the sanctuary on this side and on that, that is, from all who are subject to him by their will, and is an inhabitant of the city and makes the salvation of many his reward.
**“They shall possess twenty store chambers.”** — They will take, namely, a place for building storehouses or exedrae, according to Aquila. Chambers according to Symmachus. According to Theodotion or the Seventy, a city. Whence we understand that a certain separate place for the dwelling of the Levites is called by the name of a city.
45.6:
**“And you shall appoint the possession of the city”** — namely
**“five thousand”** — of reeds
**“According to the separation of the sanctuary.”** — All these, namely the sanctuary and the other sanctuary, and the made holy dwellings, the priests' houses, and the Levites' houses who minister to the priests, are called separated places and consecrated for the ministry and for the sanctification of the house of Israel.
45.7:
**“For the prince also”** — you shall give, namely
**“on the one side and on the other side, according to the separation of the sanctuary”** — on each side of the sanctuary
**“and according to the possession of the city”** — its possession looks, namely
**“over against the separation of the sanctuary, and over against the possession of the city: from the side of the sea”** — from the west, namely
**“even to the sea”** — to the other side of the sea
**“and from the side of the east”** — having, namely, the breadth which the prophet describes below in the description of the individual tribes
**“even to the east. And the length according to every part”** — which each tribe receives, that is, from the western boundary, etc.
**“from the west border”** — of the sea, namely
**“to the east border”** — which, how it is ended in the description of the tribes, we do not know
**“For the prince also on the one side”** — After the fourfold division of the holy land a fifth is placed, so that the prince or leader may receive on each side, etc., and may dwell in the city.
45.8: **“He shall have a portion of the land in Israel”** — aforesaid
45.9:
**“Thus saith the Lord God”** — to have sinned until now
**“Let it suffice you, O princes of Israel: cease from iniquity”** — therefore
**“and robberies”** — while you seize what belongs to others
**“cease”** — turn aside from evil
**“and judgment”** — do good. It is not enough to refrain from evil.
**“and execute justice”** — so that you do not harm the humbler man, who cannot withstand the haughtiness of the greater and more powerful
**“Let it suffice you.”** — Because you have received your possession, and your power is so great that your possession equals the part of one tribe.
*Rabanus:* Let it suffice you, princes of Israel, iniquity. This precept can be applied also to our princes, who after the manner of Pharao and the Egyptians oppress the sons of Israel, contrary also to what is written: “Have they made thee ruler? be not lifted up, but be among them all as one of them.” But they say: “My lord is long a coming,” and they strike the menservants, and the maidservants, they eat, they drink, they are drunk. Whereas it is written: “The kings of the Gentiles lord it over them; and they that are the greater, exercise power upon them. But he that will be first among you,” let him become as, that is, as the Son of man, who came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, etc.
45.10:
**“You shall have just balances, and a just ephi, and a just bate.”**
• in those things that are weighed
• Scales. Jerome. Whence: “Thou shalt not have divers weights in thy bag, a greater and a less.” The balance shall be true and just for you, which is to be observed not only in trade but in all things. Whence: “Make a balance for thy words.”
**“Ephi.”** — In Hebrew, efa; in Greek, ephi (corrupted). It pertains to the measure of dry produce: of wheat, barley, pulse.
**“Bate.”** — In Hebrew, bath: the same measure as the ephi, but only for liquids: wine, oil and the like.
45.11: **“Core.”** — The core, which holds thirty modii, and in either measure, that is, of dry as well as liquid things, holds the first place: the tenth part of a core, in those things measured by the modius, is called an epha, that is, three modii; and the tenth part of a core in liquid kinds is called a bath.
45.12:
**“sicle”** — which in Greek is stater
**“Obols.”** — In which is signified the smallest little portion; whence: the whole world of riches belongs to him who is faithful. But he who is unfaithful possesses not even an obol, that is, nothing in the world, and lacks even the smallest portion. Of which: “He shall not go out thence till he pay the last farthing,” that is, the last and smallest number.
**“Now twenty sicles, and five and twenty sicles”** — R. We read of ten minas given for trading. And elsewhere: talents divided among servants. And debtors of ten denarii and of fifty. And the labourers of the vineyard, who each receive a denarius. And the woman who lost a drachma and, with the lamp lit, scarcely found it.
**“And the sicle hath twenty obols. Now twenty sicles, and five and twenty sicles, and fifteen sicles make a mna.”**
• The mina, which in Greek is mna, which has sixty sicles, that is, twelve hundred obols.
• The difficulty is set down in numbers so that it may make the hearer’s soul attentive, as also here: “He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.” For all prophecy has both truth and obscurity, so that the disciples may hear inwardly, and the ignoble crowd, set outside, may not know what is said.
45.13:
**“And these are the firstfruits”** — which we offer, while we attribute to God, who gives the fruits of virtue, whatever good we have, and not to ourselves
**“which you shall take: the sixth part of an ephi of a core of wheat”** — while we teach men, that is, the rational animal, the mysteries of Scripture
**“and the sixth part of an ephi of a core of barley.”** — And these are the firstfruits, etc. Rabanus. According to the letter, the people were bound by the law to give the decades, that is, the tenth part of all fruits, to the Levites. Again, out of those tithes the Levites, that is, the lower ministers, gave tithes to the priests. There were also other tithes, which each one of the people of Israel set apart in his barns, that he might eat them when he went up to the temple in the city of Jerusalem, and in the porch of the temple, and invite the priests and Levites to banquets. And there were still other tithes, which they laid up for the poor. But the firstfruits which they offered from the crops were not fixed by a spiritual number but left to the choice of the offerers; and we have received a tradition of the Hebrews, not commanded by the law but put in place by the choice of the masters, that he who gave the most gave the fortieth part to the priests, he who gave the least, the sixtieth. And it was lawful to offer anything between the fortieth and the sixtieth, as they wished. What therefore was left in doubt in the Pentateuch is here defined spiritually, on account of the avarice of the priests, lest they demand more from the people, that is, that they offer the sixtieth part of what is produced from the earth. For if the cor, which in Hebrew is called omer, and by the Septuagint gomer, has thirty measures, in dry things as well as in liquids; and the ephi and the bath are the tenth part of the cor; and it is commanded that the sixth part of the ephi, as of the bath, be given to the priests in the firstfruits to be offered, which from three measures makes half a measure, it is plainly reckoned that the priests ought to receive the sixtieth part of the firstfruits.
**“Of a core of barley.”** — Of the core of barley. We give the firstfruits of barley when, being simple, we teach history. Whence: “Men and beasts thou wilt preserve, O Lord”; and then we say: “The Lord ruleth me: and I shall want nothing.” When we feed rational beings with wheat, we say with confidence: “Thou hast prepared a table before me against them that afflict me.” Let him who offers the firstfruits of wine and oil say: “Thou hast anointed my head with oil; and my chalice which inebriateth me, how goodly is it!” And when he has become an olive, let him say with the prophet: “But I, as a fruitful olive tree in the house of God.” And the wine is from the true vine, who says: “I am the true vine, and you the branches; my Father is the husbandman.” This overflows in the winepresses of Christ, whence the psalms are entitled that refer to the sacraments of the Church.
*Rabanus:* In the Old Testament the firstfruits were without measure or number, for “God doth not give the Spirit by measure.” But in the second building of the temple of Ezechiel there is a fixed measure, namely the sixtieth number, by which the world is completed. And it is said to us: “With what measure you mete, it shall be measured to you again.”
45.14:
**“The measure of oil also”** — of the Holy Spirit
**“a bate of oil”**
• Rabanus. That is, the oil which is prepared most pure for the lamps of the Lord.
• Whence: Christ, anointed above his fellows.
45.15:
**“And one ram”**
• in Hebrew, any animal
• Above he said what part of those things that are weighed and measured, both of dry and of liquid kinds, ought to be offered to the prince; now he keeps the same order of firstfruits among living things, so that he commands one ram from a flock of two hundred to be offered.
**“out of a flock of two hundred, of those that Israel feedeth for sacrifice”** — of fine flour, meal and oil
**“and for holocausts”** — which is all burnt by holy fire
**“and for peace offerings”** — when we are reconciled to God. Whence: “For Christ we beseech you, be reconciled to God.” And: “For God indeed was in Christ, reconciling the world to himself.”
*Rabanus:* One ram out of the flock. It is shown that by the precept of the law the people are subject, so that they offer to the leader or prince, that through him the holocausts and sacrifices and libations may be offered by the people on each solemnity, and the house of God be expiated. For the prince in turn is a debtor to the people, that he may offer victims for them. Here, allegorically, it is Christ; here he takes up an animal, or a ram, which was nourished in well-watered places, that is, the Scriptures, according to Symmachus. And he can say: “The Lord ruleth me: and I shall want nothing. In a place of pasture,” etc. “He hath brought me up on the water of refreshment.” These were the watered places, or rather the channels to which Jacob led his flocks, that they might drink there and conceive, and according to the color of the rods bring forth young for the Lord.
45.16: **“For the prince.”** — This is the king, as is shown on the title of the cross in Hebrew, Greek and Latin letters. When the Jews tried to take away this triumphal title, they heard: “What I have written, I have written.”
45.17:
**“And the prince shall give the holocaust, and the sacrifice, and the libations on the feasts, and on the new moons, and on the sabbaths, and on all the solemnities of the house of Israel”** — which is the church of the living God, which needs the expiation of sins
**“he”** — He: the prince
**“And the prince shall give”** — The priestly dignity is admonished to what office it is bound, that it may know that it ought to offer, for the people, the sacrifice and the libations which are offered of wine, on all the solemnities, on the kalends, that is, the new moons, when, with darkness covering all things, the beginning of the moon’s light comes; and on the sabbaths, that is, the rest.
**“he shall offer the sacrifice for sin, and the holocaust, and the peace offerings to make expiation for the house of Israel.”** — On the sabbaths and on all the solemnities, etc. “My soul hateth your solemnities.” He who hates the solemnities of the Jews loves his own sabbath, namely that which is left to the people of God, that we may see the things that have been given us by God. For in the present age, which is “seated in wickedness,” we cannot see good days, but in the new one; whence: “Remember the days of old.” And elsewhere: “I had in my mind the eternal years.” Whence Isaias: “There shall be month after month, and sabbath after sabbath.”
45.18:
**“Thus saith the Lord God: In the first month”** — Nisan, namely
**“the first of the month”** — namely on the first day
**“thou shalt take a calf”** — not reared at home
**“of the herd without blemish”** — “Who did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth”; a young calf putting forth horns and hooves, in whom the sanctuary is cleansed
**“and thou shalt expiate the sanctuary”** — In the first month, etc. Rabanus. Whence Isaias: “There shall be month after month, and sabbath after sabbath. And all flesh shall come to adore the Lord,” namely when the true adorers shall adore neither on mount Garizim nor in Jerusalem but in spirit and in truth; when there shall be a new heaven and a new earth, and “every creature shall be delivered from the servitude of corruption into the liberty of the glory of the children of God,” and the sun shall receive sevenfold light and the moon shall be likened to the sun. So the solemnities are spiritual, and the victims are spiritual.
45.19:
**“And the priest shall take of the blood”**
• in whom the world is redeemed
• of the calf, which in other words is called the lamb: “Behold the Lamb of God, behold him who taketh away the sin of the world”; by whose flesh we are fed and by whose blood we are given to drink
**“of the sin offering: and he shall put it on the posts of the house, and on the four corners of the brim of the altar, and on the posts of the gate of the inner court.”** — or of the temple, according to others, so that the house and altar are signified; for all the elements of the world are sanctified by this blood, so that when someone has been expiated and cleansed he may enter the gate of the inner court
**“And on the posts”** — Rabanus. That, being cleansed, he may be able to know the secrets of the Lord, and consequently come to the seventh day of the first month and obtain rest, and offer sacrifice to the Lord, both for ignorance, of which it is said: “The sins of my youth and my ignorances do not remember,” and for the little child, who, when he shall have come to the measure of a perfect man, will say with confidence: “When I was a child, I spoke as a child,” etc. Or for him who has been deceived by error and has sinned not so much by will as by good opinion.
45.20:
**“And so shalt thou do in the seventh day of the month”**
• of the same, namely of the month
• These two solemnities, namely the first day of the first month and the seventh of the same, are not held in the Mosaic law.
45.21:
**“In the first month, the fourteenth day of the month, you shall observe the solemnity of the pasch”** — or Pasch
**“the solemnity of the pasch: seven days unleavened bread shall be eaten.”** — In the first month, etc. When the two solemnities of the first month are completed, that is, of the first day and of the seventh of the same, he comes to the fourteenth day of the month, on which is the solemnity of the pasch; whence: “For Christ our pasch is sacrificed.” Then we shall eat unleavened bread for seven days, in the rest and security of all those things, when, destroying the leaven of malice and wickedness, we eat the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth; our Prince offering all things for us, and first for himself. He took up a human body, and “condemned sin in the flesh”; he grieved for us and bore our infirmities; then for his own house, which is written in the Septuagint but is not had in the Hebrew, that is, for the Church.
**“The fourteenth day”** — Moses commanded this when we eat unleavened bread for seven days. But the fourth solemnity, of which he says: “In the seventh month, on the fifteenth day of the month,” etc., seems to signify the feast of Tabernacles, which he has set down here without naming it.
45.22: **“And the prince on that day shall offer for himself, and for all the people of the land, a calf for sin.”** — the human race; for the Saviour is the saviour of all men, and most of all of the faithful, and he himself is the propitiation for our sins, and not only for us but for the whole world
45.23:
**“And in the solemnity of the seven days he shall offer for a holocaust to the Lord, seven calves, and seven rams without blemish daily for seven days: and for sin a he goat daily.”** — that is, for seven days
**“And in the solemnity of the seven days”** — When the calf has been offered for the whole people of the land, on the remaining seven days of the Lord’s passion seven calves and seven rams without blemish are offered daily, that they may be consumed in the holocaust and the fire of the Lord.
**“seven calves”** — Rabanus. The seven calves and seven rams are those who are configured to the Lord’s passion, that they may imitate the true calf and the true ram, and that through the seven days the sins of the whole world may be cleansed by the blood of the martyrs.
45.24: **“And he shall offer the sacrifice of an ephi”** — Rabanus. It is to be carefully noted that in the sacrifice of the ephi, an ephi for a calf and an ephi for a ram, and a hin of oil are offered, as were commanded by the law. But in the offering of the he-goat neither an ephi nor, as the Septuagint translated, a boiling is set down; for they interpreted ephi itself as a boiling. The hin, however (which is a fixed measure of oil), is taken in the sacrifice of the calf and the ram, that we may deserve to receive the nourishment of the everlasting light, rest from labour, and healing of weariness, after the appeasing of sins.
45.25: **“In the seventh month”** — Rabanus. Also in the seventh month, on the fifteenth day of the month, in the solemnity of tabernacles, the same order of offering and of sacrifices is to be kept, as well for sin as for the holocaust, and in the sacrifice and in the oil, that, with darkness put to flight and the light of the oil risen, we may attain the feast of the Lord, and have brighter solemnities in which all our sins are forgiven us.

46.1:
**“Thus saith the Lord God: The gate of the inner court that looketh toward the east”** — whence: the sun of righteousness rises
**“shall be shut the six days”** — whence: Six days shalt thou labour, and shalt do all thy works
**“on which work is done; but on the sabbath day”** — that is, the seventh, in which is rest
**“it shall be opened”** — through each week
**“Thus saith the Lord God”** — First the words must be unfolded paraphrastically.
**“the six days, on which work is done”** — Rabanus. The east gate of the court is shut to us. But after we have come to the sabbath, in which is rest, or to the day of the calends, when after the blind night and dreadful darkness there is the beginning of light, the east gate is opened to us.
**“on the day of the new moon”** — That is, when thirty days are completed, on the day of the new moon, which is the end of the higher month and the beginning of another; so that what privilege the seventh day has in the week, the month’s beginning may have this.
46.2:
**“And the prince shall enter”**
• the cause by which it is opened
• Jerome. He who shall have attained the name and dignity of a leader.
**“by the way of the porch of the gate from without”** — of the outer court, namely
**“and he shall stand at the threshold of the gate”** — of the inner court, that is, which looks toward the east; nor shall he enter the inner court, but while he stands there the priests shall make the holocaust, etc.
**“and the priests shall offer”** — the angelic powers
**“his holocaust”**
• for him, namely
• For we need the mercy of God, and every creature, in comparison with the Creator, is unclean and must be purged by the divine fire. Whence in Isaias the lips were purged.
**“and his peace offerings: and he shall adore upon the threshold of the gate, and shall go out: but the gate”** — after the prince’s going out
**“shall not be shut”** — but it will be open
**“by the way of the porch”** — That is, through the labours of this world and the gate of the Church, which is still set in earthly bounds; but he shall not enter the inner court, and he shall stand at the threshold of the inner gate.
**“till the evening”** — He shall stand at the threshold, etc. Rabanus. If the prince in the present writing does not enter the inner court but stands at its threshold, it is plain that now he can see in part and know in part, and cannot yet contemplate the glory of the Lord with face unveiled.
**“and he shall adore upon the threshold”** — So that after the prince’s victim has been burnt by the sacred fire, he himself, reconciled to God, may then be able to worship upon the threshold of the inner gate in which he stood, and afterwards go out.
46.3:
**“And the people of the land shall adore”**
• therefore the gate is not shut, so that the people may worship after the prince
• Rabanus. That after he has received peace through the sacrifice, he may then, standing at the threshold, adore the almighty power of God, and confess himself unworthy of entering the inner court, and go out at once. But after he who is first has gone out, the gate of the inner court itself will not be shut until the evening of this world, but will be open, that the people of the land also may be at the door and adore, not at every time, but when it has rested from sins and, with the darkness put to flight, has received the light of faith and knowledge.
**“at the door of that gate on the sabbaths”** — when, namely, the gate is opened
46.4:
**“And the holocaust”** — because above he had not given the number of the holocausts, here he gives it
**“that the prince shall offer”** — through the priests
**“And the holocaust that”** — Rabanus. The holocaust, however, which the prince offers through the priests on the sabbath day, will be of six lambs without blemish, namely for the six days in which we work in the world. And a ram without blemish, who is the prince of the flock, so that with each ram an ephi, that is, the tenth part of a core, is offered in the sacrifice. But in the sacrifice of the six lambs no fixed measure is set, but as much as the hand of him who offers shall give, that is, according to the quality and measure of the works.
46.5:
**“And the sacrifice of an ephi”** — which in Hebrew is epha
**“for a ram”** — that is, in the sacrifice of the ram
**“but for the lambs what sacrifice”** — it will be, namely
**“his hand shall allow”** — that is, what the hand of the one who offers is able to offer
**“and a hin of oil”**
• measure
• Rabanus. He shall offer a hin of oil for each ephi (that is, the oil which the five virgins prepared for themselves), that he may anoint or mix the fine flour, and that every offering of God may be full of the light of truth, and the face of the offerer be made glad in oil.
**“for every ephi”** — it will be
46.6:
**“And on the day of the new moon a calf of the herd without blemish: and the six lambs, and the rams shall be without blemish.”**
• In the day, etc. The day of the new moons, namely, has this privilege beyond the sabbath day, that a calf of the herd is sacrificed, or, as others have translated, a bull without blemish; but the rest, that is, the six lambs without blemish and the ram without blemish, and their sacrifices, will keep the rite of the sabbath; so, namely, that as in the ram an ephi is offered for the sacrifice, that is, likewise, and a hin of oil, so it is offered also with the calf.
• And in the day of the calends. The thirtieth, namely, when the firstborn and the Levites are numbered in the law, a calf of the herd without blemish is offered for all Israel (on which we have treated more fully in the preceding chapter), and six lambs and rams without blemish, and the rest that are offered on the sabbaths, that we may attain eternal rest and deserve to hear: “Well done, good and faithful servant,” etc. And that we may be able not only to come to the gate of the inner court but also to enter, that being planted in the house of the Lord, “in the courts of the house of our God,” we may flourish.
46.8:
**“And when the prince is to go in”** — the aforesaid
**“is to go in”** — For he is of free will and has power to lay down his life and to take it up again; both coming to us and ascending to the heavens, he uses the same freedom of his majesty. Finally, he seeks no fairs or solemnities, nor observes any difference of days, because every time is a feast to him.
46.9:
**“But when the people of the land shall go in before the Lord in the solemn feasts, he that goeth in by the north gate to adore, shall go out by the way of the south gate”** — the people enter and go out only at fairs and solemnities, and not by the same way but by one and another
**“he that goeth in by the north gate”** — Rabanus. The people is commanded that if it has entered by the north gate to adore, it go out by the way of the south gate. This is the people of the Gentiles, which, leaving the north gate, from which evils break forth upon the earth, if it has entered the temple, ought not to go out except by the way of the south gate, that is, of light and heat, in which the bridegroom lies down at noon. Whence: “Arise, O north wind, and come, O south wind.” But he that goeth in by the way of the south gate, etc.: this is the people of the Jews, which, leaving the way of the gate of light, passes over to the north gate. Of which it is said: the north wind is a most hard wind; and: the pot of Jeremias is kindled from the face of the north. Otherwise: he enters by the north gate who gives up sins; he goes out by the south gate who follows virtues. Conversely, if the just man has fallen into sins, he enters indeed by the south gate, but goes out by the way of the north gate.
**“he shall not return by the way of the gate whereby he came in”** — For not only those who go out of Sodom are commanded not to look back, nor those who put their hand to the plough, that they look not behind them, but also those established in the house of the Lord, that they may not, namely, return to “the weak and needy elements,” and having begun in the spirit not be consummated in the flesh, but from spiritual things go on to greater (whence: “forgetting the things that are behind, I stretch forth myself to those that are before,” or the first), that they may not, namely, know in part but come to the perfect, as far as human frailty can, so that, namely, when they have done all things, they say: we are unprofitable servants. Whence Paul, as one imperfect: “Not that I have already attained.” And elsewhere, as one perfect, he says: “as many as are perfect,” etc. Hence it is plain that every man and the whole creature, though he has come to perfection, needs the mercy of God, and possesses full perfection by grace, not by merit.
46.10:
**“And the prince”** — standing by as witness of both, namely of virtue or of sin
**“in the midst of them”** — of those entering, that is, and leaving. Whence: “there hath stood one in the midst of you, whom you know not.” And the Apostle: “Know you not that Christ is in you?”
**“in the midst”** — Rabanus. Whence the Apostle: “Know you not that Christ is in you?” If he is in those who do not know, how much more in those who know. But when the body shall have stood among those of knowledge, it will be dead because of sin, and the spirit shall live because of justice.
46.11:
**“And”** — therefore
**“in the fairs, and in the solemnities”** — of the sabbaths, that is, and of the new moons
**“there shall be the sacrifice of an ephi to a calf, and an ephi to a ram: and to the lambs, the sacrifice shall be as his hand shall find: and a hin of oil to every ephi.”** — An ephi for a calf, etc. An ephi for each of the two is offered in the sacrifice. But with the lambs there is no fixed number, nor is the choice left to the will, but each uses the strength of a good conscience, that he may offer as much as he can, not as much as he wishes; and above all a hin of oil to every ephi, that the fine flour may be anointed and the lamp lighted in the sight of the Lord, and that those who use it may say: “But I, as a fruitful olive tree in the house of God.”
46.12:
**“But when the prince shall offer a voluntary holocaust”** — Septuagint: confession
**“or voluntary peace offerings to the Lord: the gate that looketh towards the east shall be opened to him, and he shall offer his holocaust”** — because it is voluntary, not another on his behalf
**“and his peace offerings”** — Septuagint: salvations, because the reconciliation of peace offerings is the salvation of the one offering
**“As it is wont to be done on the sabbath day”** — immediately after he has offered
**“and the gate shall be shut after he is gone forth”** — others: he shall shut the gate, so that his privilege is preserved for the prince, that his sacrifices not be mixed with those of the people
**“the prince”** — Septuagint: leader. Whence Isaias: “I have given him for a leader and a master to the Gentiles.” And Ezechiel: “David the prince in the midst of them.” Who, that is, does this of his own will, saying: “The free offerings of my mouth make acceptable, O Lord,” and a holocaust, that he may offer it wholly to God.
**“voluntary peace offerings”** — Which was not said above. For it is written: and the priests shall offer his holocaust and his peace offerings; and of the spontaneous and voluntary offerings nothing is said at all. After the holocaust let him offer peace offerings and be reconciled to God. Whence also virginity is greater than marriage, because it is neither exacted nor rendered but offered. When the prince has done this, the gate that looketh to the east will be opened to him. Of which: “This is the gate of the Lord, the just shall enter into it.” And whence the sun of justice rises.
46.13:
**“and a lamb of the same year without blemish”** — he specifies that it is a holocaust
**“he shall offer a holocaust every day”** — not on set days
**“And he shall offer a holocaust”** — Rabanus. Not the priests for him, as is wont to be done on the sabbath day. But at every time the holocaust and peace offering which is offered voluntarily has the gate of the Lord open, nor does it keep the sabbath, but all days are reckoned as the sabbath, that is, rest.
**“to the Lord he shall offer it always in the morning”**
• And a lamb of the same year, etc. Rabanus. Whence Isaias: “as a lamb he shall be dumb, and shall not open his mouth.” And John: “Behold the Lamb of God, behold him who taketh away the sin of the world.” Who, namely, is sacrificed in Egypt, with whose blood the doorposts of faith are armed, and the destroyer is shut out.
• He shall offer always in the morning, etc. Not at any hour, but when the sun has risen and it is the beginning of light, of which David: “In the morning thou shalt hear my voice.” “In the morning I will stand before thee, and will see.” And elsewhere: “At evening weeping shall have place, and in the morning gladness.” And: “O God, my God, to thee do I watch at break of day.”
• Let not the reader wonder if the same one is both prince and priest, and calf and ram and lamb, since in the Scriptures, according to the variety of reasons, we read that the same one is Lord and God and man and prophet and rod and root and flower and prince and judge and just king and justice, apostle and bishop, arm, servant, only-begotten, son, shepherd and firstborn, door, way, angel, arrow, and wisdom, and many things of the same kind.
*Rabanus:* Of the same year. Others: a yearling, because he preached the acceptable year of the Lord and the day of retribution.
46.14:
**“and the sacrifice”** — Septuagint: manaa
**“he shall offer for it morning by morning”** — that is, at morning, at daybreak
**“morning the sixth part of an ephi”**
• understand “like”
• that is, half a modius of an ephi; for the ephi is the tenth part of a chorus, that is, three modii
**“and of oil the third part of a hin, that it be mingled”** — others: let it be sprinkled
**“like”** — that is
**“a sacrifice to the Lord by ordinance continual”** — not interrupted on any day
**“and everlasting”** — to be offered at every time, the sun having risen in the morning
46.15:
**“he shall offer”** — thus
**“the lamb”** — the leader
46.16:
**“Thus saith the Lord God: if the prince shall give”** — or inheritance
**“to any of his sons, the inheritance of it shall be to his sons; they shall possess it by inheritance”** — by right of succession, and it shall not pass from one to another
**“Thus saith the Lord”** — Thus far it has spoken of the prince; now it speaks of his heirs: to whom he ought to give, and whose possession it is, either for a time or in perpetuity.
46.17:
**“but if he give a legacy out of his inheritance to one of his servants, it shall be his”** — that is, the seventh
**“And”** — then
**“until the year”** — The seventh, which is called “decor,” or until the jubilee, that is the fiftieth, comes, when every purchase or gift returns to its former lords. For the servant has the use for a time; the son of the prince has the ownership of the possession.
46.18:
**“and the prince shall not take of the inheritance of the people by violence, and of their possession, but of his own possession he shall give an inheritance to his sons, that my people be not dispersed, each man from his possession”**
• that is, if the prince could either take or seize, or under the appearance of honour hold, what is not his own, and leave it to his children
• Be dispersed, etc. Into parts is he dispersed who had been gathered in the name of the Lord; or, according to the law, the inheritance of one passes to another, and the line of division perishes, by which the inheritance came by lot to each one. But he disperses the people of God and takes away the everlasting possession of the faith, who leaves to sons, brothers and kinsmen goods that are another’s, whether by plunder or by flattery or by blandishments or under the pretext of religion.
**“And the prince shall not take”** — He rebukes not only the priests or princes of that time but ours also, who become richer through the occasion of their dignity than they were before, that they take not from the poor by violence, nor under the name of honour despoil the rich, and leave nothing to their sons, to whom the paternal inheritance is due, except what was left to themselves by their parents. Therefore the priest who is richer, when he comes to the sacrifice, whatever more he has he ought to give not to his sons but to the poor and to the holy brethren, the household of the faith, who surpass the merits of books; and let him render to the Lord the things that are the Lord’s, who says: “As long as you did it to one of these my least brethren, you did it to me.” For he himself in his poor is received in hospitality, visited in prison, clothed when naked, given drink when thirsty, filled when hungry.
46.19:
**“and he brought me in by the entrance”** — the man who held a reed in his hand and the mason’s line by which the building is measured
**“which was at the side”** — or behind his back
**“of the gate”** — he does not say whose: eastern, southern, or any
**“into the chambers of the sanctuary”** — others: the chambers of the priests
**“for the priests”** — namely
**“toward the west”** — Toward the west. Others: the sea. For holy Scripture, describing the situation of Judea, often calls the sea the west. It is to be noted that the place of the priests, who boil the sacrifices for trespass or for ignorance and sin, that they may not be offered raw into the outer court, is placed to the west and the north, whence the coldest wind rises, where the light of the sun sets. From this it is shown that whatever pertains to food is either for error or for sin. But if a sacrifice is offered for ignorance, how much more for a trespass of conscience; whence in Job: “Lest perhaps my sons have sinned,” namely through ignorance.
46.20: **“And let the people be sanctified”** — Rabanus. Who, namely, had not been prepared for sanctification, lest we readily give holy things to the unsanctified, or cast pearls before swine, or give what is holy to dogs. Whence Moses wishes the people to be sanctified for three days from all uncleanness and from the embrace of wives, that they may come to Mount Sinai and, sanctified, receive holy things. But if those who are to approach to hear the words of God and receive them are commanded to be sanctified from their wives, it is manifest that even in the law that apostolic saying is contained: “Defraud not one another, except, perhaps, by consent, that you may give yourselves to prayer.” And: by consent we must abstain from our wives that we may give ourselves to prayer.
46.21:
**“And he led me”** — the aforesaid man, namely
**“into the outward court”** — from the place of the priests, which faced north
**“and he led me about by the four corners of the court; and behold, there was a little court in the corner of the court, a little court at each corner of the court”** — at each corner, namely, it had four little courts
**“the outward court”** — That from which he had gone out is clearly the inner one, and there are many courts in the holy Scriptures; whence: “You that stand in the house of the Lord, in the courts of the house of our God.” And Jesus says: “Other sheep I have, that are not of this court: them also I must bring, and there shall be one court and one shepherd.” For so it is in the Greek, which the Latin translator, unable to render fully in one word, rendered as “fold.” For when he says “of this court” he shows there is another, which is pointed out either in the crowd of the Gentiles, as distinct from Israel, or in the heavens, as distinct from the earthly court; for according to the quality of merits a court is assigned to each office.
46.22:
**“in the four corners of the court little courts disposed, forty cubits long”** — in which number are labours and tribulations
**“and thirty broad”** — this number signifies the perfect age at which one arrives at the priestly office. Whence: “And Jesus himself was beginning about thirty years of age,” who came to baptism
**“forty cubits”** — Rabanus. By which number Moses and Elias and Christ himself fasted; where there is food, there is distress and temptation, by which they are prepared; but where one comes to the age of the perfect man, all things are to be trodden underfoot, and we must say: “Having food, and wherewith to be covered, with these we are content.” And: “If the Lord shall give me bread to eat, and raiment to put on,” etc.; or that: “Meat for the belly, and the belly for the meats; but God shall destroy both it and them.” For in the future we shall neither eat nor drink, but shall feed on that bread of which it is said: “Man ate the bread of angels,” etc. And: “My meat is to do the will of him that sent me.”
**“of one measure”** — Rabanus. The one measure, which occupied the four greater corners, signifies the quarters of the world, by which “in the sweat of thy face thou shalt eat bread”; and all our labour profits the belly and the dung.
46.23:
**“and a wall”** — one
**“round about compassing the four little courts, and kitchens”** — where food and the preparation of tables
46.24:
**“And he said to me: This is the house of the kitchens”** — as though you did not know what you see
**“the victims of the people”** — Which are offered for sin, or for offence and ignorance, but only for the food and refreshment of the priests, so that they may remember that they ought to desire nothing else, since even in the temple their flesh is prepared for their refreshment.

47.1:
**“And he brought me again to the gate of the house”** — namely of the temple
**“and behold, waters issued out from under the threshold of the house toward the east”** — not to the north or the west
**“for the forefront of the house looked toward the east, but the waters came down to the right side of the temple”** — that is
**“to the south”**
• From this it is clear that the waters are sacred and signify the teaching of the Saviour.
• where the bridegroom feeds and reclines with his guests
**“of the altar”**
• not of just any place.
• But the waters, etc. Rabanus. There are also bitter and very evil waters. Whence: “What hast thou to do with the way of Egypt, to drink the troubled water,” of Gihon, which in Hebrew is called Sior, that is, turbid and muddy. Whence: “I will give them the water of gall to drink,” that is, that in which dwells the dragon who said: “The rivers are mine,” etc. Whence: “The waters are come in even unto my soul.” And elsewhere: “Perhaps the water had swallowed us up.” This water is called by another name Mara, that is, bitterness, into which the wood of the cross is cast, and bitter things are turned into sweet. For the law of Moses, if it is understood in the sense of the flesh, is bitter, digging out “eye for eye, tooth for tooth”; see in Thamar fornication, and Osee joined to a harlot, Jeremias’s girdle, Moses’s Ethiopian wife, the killing of the Egyptian, and such things, which are bitter according to the killing letter and do not so much edify the reader as destroy him.
• But the waters came down. The living waters, namely the Holy Spirit; whence: “On the water of refreshment he hath brought me up.” Of which it is said: “You shall draw waters with joy out of the saviour’s fountains,” and elsewhere: “Bless ye the Lord from the fountains of Israel.” And elsewhere: “They have forsaken me, the fountain of living water,” which are namely the waters of doctrine.
**“to the south of the altar”** — Not to the north, not to the west. Note that these waters, which flow out through the east gate, flee so far toward the left parts that they go to the south at the right side of the altar.
47.2:
**“And he led me out by the way of the north gate, and he caused me to turn to the way outside the outward gate, to the way that looked toward the east; and behold, waters”** — of baptism.
**“And he led me out by the way”** — It signifies that we cannot come at once to the east gate unless we come to it by the way of the north gate, by a long circuit. For unless we have overcome the coldest wind by the heat of faith and trodden down its regions, according to that: “And the God of peace shall crush Satan under our feet,” we cannot enter the gate through which the waters go out, and are on the right side.
47.3:
**“a thousand cubits”** — Rabanus. That we say cubitos in the masculine and not cubita in the neuter is not from ignorance of grammar but on account of the simple and unlearned, of whom the greater part is in the gathering of the church, we do.
**“up to the ankles”** — Those who are near the sole and heel, which lie open to the bites of the serpent; whence: “He shall lie in wait for thy heel”; and concerning Judas the traitor: “He hath magnified his heel against me.”
**“he brought me through”** — Rabanus. After the remission of sins, indeed, and the beginnings of progress, when we strive to ascend a little from earthly things to higher, we bend the knee to the Lord, to whom “every knee should bow, of those that are in heaven, on earth, and under the earth. And every tongue should confess that the Lord Jesus Christ is in the glory of God the Father,” etc.
47.4:
**“And again he measured”** — the same waters.
**“is a thousand”** — The sins that are forgiven us through the waters of baptism; these are the beginnings of progress.
47.5:
**“and he measured”** — in the water, namely.
**“a thousand”** — cubits.
**“And he measured a thousand”** — cubits.
**“a torrent”** — of thoughts, namely the incitement or the incitements of vices.
**“which I could not pass over”**
• the fourth thousand cubits. David, however, says: “Our soul hath passed through a torrent”; but in Hebrew it has: “the torrent has passed over my soul.”
• Rabanus. For neither the prophet nor human nature can cross the torrent of thoughts after the loins. Or the incitements of vices; but that man clothed in linen, the leader of the prophet, can clearly cross, who did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth.
**“for the waters were risen”** — of the torrent.
**“of the torrent”** — concerning which: “He shall drink of the torrent in the way.” And: “Turn again our captivity, O Lord, as a stream in the south.”
**“up to the loins”** — By these steps we come to the heights; yet these heights themselves reach up to the loins and reins, that all lust in us may be cut off, and we may possess the sanctification of the body, “without which no man shall see God.” Whence: from the feet up to the loins God is seen as fire. For the work of the loins needs fire and purging. Whence: “my loins are filled with illusions.” For by these the enemy mocks us night and day with phantasms; but from the loins up to the head and crown he shone with the most precious metal, with the brightness of amber, so that there is nothing foul in him, nothing of baseness.
**“which cannot be passed over”** — Who can glory that he has a clean heart? For the world is set in the wicked one; from childhood the heart of man is set toward evil, so that not even a man of one day, from the beginning of his birth, is without sin. Whence: “For behold I was conceived in iniquities; and in sins did my mother conceive me.” Not, that is, in the iniquities of my mother or my own, but those of the human condition. Whence: “death reigned from Adam unto Moses.”
47.6:
**“And he said to me”** — The aforesaid man, the leader of Ezechiel, warns the prophet in each thing that he look more carefully and see the hidden mysteries.
**“Surely thou hast seen, O son of man. And he brought me out, and he caused me to turn to the bank of the torrent”** — others: of the river.
**“Son of man”** — Rabanus. In the figure, namely, of the Saviour. For Ezechiel is interpreted as the strength of God or dominion, and he is called son of man as a reminder of human frailty, lest he forget his condition while great things are shown to him.
**“to the bank”** — Rabanus. So that he who could not cross the middle depth may at least recognize those things that are on the banks.
**“of the torrent”** — Rabanus. This torrent, which is borne along like a torrent by the abundance of its waters and receives the rains, is called a river by the Septuagint because it has perpetual waters, not gathered from rains here and there but flowing from a living and perpetual fountain. Of which: “The stream of the river maketh the city of God joyful.” And elsewhere: “The river of God is filled with water.” And: “The floods have lifted up, O Lord, the floods have lifted up their voice.”
47.7:
**“And when I had turned myself”** — others: had turned.
**“behold on the bank of the torrent were very many trees on both sides”** — which abound in paradise with various fruits, or trees.
47.8:
**“And he said”** — the guide going before.
**“to me these waters”** — of baptismal grace, or evangelical teaching.
**“that issue forth”** — from the threshold of the temple of the Lord.
**“toward the hillocks of sand to the east, and go down to the plains of the desert, shall go into the sea, and shall go out, and the waters shall be healed”** — eastern, that is, the dead (sea), in which nothing could live, and which is very bitter; the Greeks call it asphaltum, that is, a pool of bitumen.
**“toward the hillocks of sand to the east”** — That they, watering the plains and deserts, make the barren fruitful, and express the sacrament of the spring of Jericho, which Eliseus healed with the gospel and apostolic salt, so that where before there was barrenness and death, there might be fruitfulness and life.
**“and the waters shall be healed”** — Rabanus. In a wonderful manner the dead waters, in which nothing can live, which have not known him who says, “I am the life,” are healed by the evangelical waters, whose torrents are to heal very many fishes, and all things shall live to which they come, so that fishermen stand on the banks from Engaddi even to Engallim. Engaddi is “fountain” or “eye.” Engallim is at the beginning of the dead sea, where the Jordan enters. Engaddi, where the dead sea is healed: I think this is that of which Zacharias says: “In that day living waters shall go out from Jerusalem, and the half of them to the former sea.” And Daniel: “the four winds of heaven were rushing upon the great sea.” And David: “wonderful are the elevations of the sea.” And: “I am come into the depth of the sea, and a tempest hath overwhelmed me.” The king of Egypt is called a dragon, who lies in the sea and stirs up the rivers as with his horns. And this sea is great and wide with hands. Unless it receives into itself the water of the river or torrent of God, it deadens what it has in itself. This most salt sea, and of exceeding bitterness, Christ healed by his death. Whence: “The spirit of the Lord is upon me, because the Lord hath anointed me: he hath sent me to preach to the meek, to heal the contrite of heart,” etc. And in Jeremias: “Heal me, O Lord, and I shall be healed,” etc. The angels also who were set over the Jews, when they cried, “His blood be upon us,” etc., and the veil of the temple was rent and all the sacraments of the Hebrews were laid open, answered the Lord who commanded: “We have cured Babylon, and she is not healed; let us forsake her,” that is, the city of confusion and of vices.
47.9: **“And every living creature that creepeth whithersoever the torrent shall come, shall live: and there shall be fishes in abundance after these waters shall come thither, and they shall be healed, and all things shall live to which the torrent shall come”** — evangelical.
47.10:
**“shall live and the fishers shall stand over these waters”** — to whom it is said: “I will make you to become fishers of men.”
**“from Engaddi”** — the eye, that is, the spring, of the kid, which is always offered for sins.
**“even to Engallim”** — the spring of the calves, which are slain for the Lord, and the calf bringing forth horns and hooves, which they imitate, and which in a figure of our Lord Saviour is slain at the altar.
**“there shall be drying of nets: there shall be many sorts of the fishes thereof”** — in the sea that was once dead
**“as the fishes of the great sea”** — of the world, namely
**“a very great multitude”**
• of the human race
• Very many kinds, etc. Rabanus. These fishes Peter drew to the right side at the Lord’s command, a hundred and fifty-three, so that for their multitude the nets were broken. Now those who have written on the natures of living creatures say that there are a hundred and fifty-three kinds of fishes, all of which were taken by the apostles, while they draw out of the sea of this world to salvation the noble and the lowly, the poor and the rich, and every kind of men.
47.11:
**“But on the shore thereof, and in the fenny places they shall not be healed, because they shall be turned into saltpits”** — For whoever is not in the ark of Noe will perish in the flood. Likewise those whom this river does not touch are not saved.
**“they shall be turned into saltpits”** — “The wicked man being scourged, the fool shall be wiser”; for the examples of the worse instruct the good. Or according to that: “Salt is good. But if the salt become unsavoury, it is good for nothing.” So that they may be without fruits and greenness for ever, as a city also shows, sprinkled with salt after its ruin.
47.12:
**“And by the torrent on the banks thereof on both sides shall grow all trees that bear fruit: their leaf shall not fall off”** — Whence: “And his leaf shall not fall off: and all whatsoever he shall do shall prosper.”
**“and their fruit shall not fail: every month shall they bring forth firstfruits”** — And he shall be like a tree which is planted near the running waters, which shall bring forth its fruit in due season.
**“because the waters thereof shall issue out of the sanctuary”** — As if these things come about because “its waters, etc.” Let us not think it is of the banks, or of the trees, or of such great abundant harvests; but because “its waters, etc.” For it is not of him that willeth, nor of him that runneth, but of God that showeth mercy.
**“and the fruits thereof shall be for food”** — It shows the sacraments of the divine books, of which one part belongs to the letter and the other to the spirit.
**“and the leaves thereof for medicine”**
• which contain moral teaching and give health, so that they heal the wounds of sinners
• And its leaves, etc. Rabanus. The Septuagint. Its ascent to health, so that, after the food of the fruits, we may by the warnings of words climb to heavenly things.
**“all trees that bear fruit”** — Jerome. The tree of life, that is, wisdom, holds the chief place among all these trees. Of which it is said: “She is a tree of life to them that lay hold on her.”
**“firstfruits”** — The Septuagint. Its fruit. In its renewal it will give firstfruits, so that all the fruits of believers may be firstfruits, and each month be assigned to each apostle.
47.13:
**“Thus saith the Lord God: This is the border, by which you shall possess the land according to the twelve tribes of Israel: for Joseph hath a double portion”** — As if two tribes.
**“for Joseph hath a double portion”** — Jerome. With the tribe of Levi removed, which was given over to the service of the Lord, the tribe of Joseph was divided into two, Ephraim and Manasses; which said to Josue: “Why hast thou given me but one lot and one portion to possess, whereas I am of so great a multitude, etc.”
47.14: **“And you shall possess it, every man in like manner as his brother: concerning which I lifted up my hand to give it to your fathers: and this land shall fall unto you for a possession”** — And you shall possess it, etc. Equally. Equal spaces of land, that is, according to their multitude, and not by the choice of the one dividing, but by lot, which stands by the power of the Lord. Josue himself also, the divider of the land, did not set apart a portion for himself, lest he seem to have chosen the best land for himself, but received it from the princes of all the tribes.
47.15:
**“And this is the border of the land: toward the north side, from the great sea by the way of Hethalon”** — into the cradle of sorrow
**“as men go to Sedada”**
• its side
• And this is the border of the land, etc. Rabanus. The northern side begins from the great sea and by the way of Ethalon, which is interpreted “in the cradle of sorrow,” that is, through penance, comes to Sadada, where there is a turning aside at the side. For we understand the indignation, that is, of the Lord, hanging over us at Emath; or, when the truth of Emath has been found, the wells of Berotha are opened to us, which the princes Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob dug, and by a long circuit we come to the mountains of Sabarim, which are set between Damascus, that is, the blood of sackcloth, and the border of Emath, that is, of truth. For as through sorrow we turn aside from evils that threaten and avoid them at the side, so after the blood and sackcloth of a bloody life, before we come to the borders of Emath, we go around and come to the mountains. Of which it is said: “mountains are round about it”; which place is called the court of Tycon, that is, the middle, near the borders of Auran, that is, wrath, that we may say: “I will bear the wrath of the Lord, because I have sinned against him.” And from the sea to the borders of Damascus. In which Paul also, from Jewish fury and the shedding of the Church’s blood, beheld the light through blindness. And having taken sackcloth, through the pursuit of the old way he preached the gospel, that he might come to the court of the eternal fountain, and, once set in the north, lay hold of the border of truth.
47.16:
**“Emath”**
• wrath
• which is now Epiphania, from Antiochus Epiphanes
**“Berotha”** — wells
**“Sabarim”** — circuits of mountains
**“which is between”** — that is, border
**“the border”** — Otherwise: boundary
**“of Damascus”** — of blood, of a sack, and of a kiss or of a cup
**“and the border of Emath, the house”** — Symmachus: middle court
**“Atticon”** — middle
**“which is by the border of Auran”** — others: Aserenon, that is, court of the fountain
47.18:
**“And the east side is from the midst of Auran”** — which is the town of Damascus in the wilderness
**“And the east side”** — Rabanus. Allegorically. After the borders of the north, by a long circuit through Ethalon and Sadada and Berotha, Sabarim also and Thicon and Auran and Damascus and the court of Enon, one comes as far as Emath. The eastern side comes from the midst of wrath, that is, Auran, and from the midst of Damascus, that is, the blood of penance, and from the midst of Galaad, that is, of revelation or of the heap of witness, so that after wrath and penance it may show hope of salvation, and from the midst of the land of Israel, which holds the vision of peace, it reaches to the sweetest streams of the Jordan, which, the sea being far separated, receives the light of the east, so that it is ended by the river Jordan (which is interpreted “stream of judgment”) and by the bound of the torrent.
**“Galaad”** — Which is a mountain of Libanus joined to hills, in the lot of Ruben and Gad and the half tribe of Manasses, the border of Phenice and Arabia; coming to which, Jacob, on his way from Carram, was overtaken by Laban. But the end of this side is the river Jordan and the eastern sea, that is, the dead sea; in this place the Red Sea is not understood by the word “sea.”
47.19:
**“And the south side southward”**
• namely
• Rabanus. After the northern and eastern side, when the sun of justice has risen upon us, we receive the southern side, when the whole light is poured upon us from above, and when we enter with Abraham into the banquet and are inebriated with the wine that “maketh glad the heart of man”, with Joseph and his brethren. Now this possession begins from Thamar, that is, from the palm and the victory over vices, reaching even to the waters of contradiction. For virtues are always contradicted. Whence also the Jews, disputing against Paul, assert that the evangelical preaching is contradicted in the whole world. And elsewhere: “for a sign which shall be contradicted.” But all contradiction is holiness, which is the interpretation of Cades. Whence: “The Lord shall shake the desert of Cades”, which, that is, at first did not have the holiness of the Lord, but was shaken and moved that it might receive the guest of the Lord, who says: “Upon whom shall my spirit rest, but upon him that is humble and quiet, and that trembleth at my words.” After the desert of Cades, as far as the great sea, on the south of the southern side, is the torrent mentioned above, which has its waters not from the earth but from heaven, gathered together by the variety of diverse virtues.
**“from Thamar”**
• begins, namely
• which is a city in the wilderness, which today is called Palmyra; in Hebrew Thamar, that is, palm
**“even to the waters of contradiction of Cades”** — which is in the desert of the Red Sea
**“and the torrent even to the great sea”** — which is enclosed by the shores of Egypt and Palestine
**“and this is the south side”** — that is
**“southward”** — as far as
47.20:
**“And the side toward the sea”** — western, that is
**“the great sea”** — is
**“The side of the sea”** — Rabanus. Allegorically. The west is always in the sea, always in the deep, always in the waves, where every day shipwrecks arise, and the deaths of the wretched, and loss of riches and merchandise; and yet when we have broken through all these by patience, we shall come straight on to Emath, that is, the truth of the Lord, who, persecutions having been overcome, has promised us eternal rewards.
47.22:
**“And you shall divide it by lot for an inheritance”** — for there is no distinction between Jew and Greek; an equal inheritance is due to all, and the possession is one for the Israelite and the stranger
**“to you, and to the strangers”** — the pride of the Jews who despise the Gentiles is struck down
**“that shall come over to you, that shall beget children”** — good works, that is
**“among you”** — And mayest thou see thy children’s children, peace upon Israel.
**“And they shall be unto you as men of the same country”** — fellow members of the body and fellow heirs
**“among the children of Israel”** — seeing God
47.23: **“And in what tribe soever the stranger shall be, there shall you give him possession, saith the Lord God.”** — they receive according to their own works, that is

48.1:
**“And these are the names”** — The possession of the holy land having been described, the possession of the individual tribes is described from the eastern side to the western side, that is, the sea. And first they receive their borders from the north, for those going by the way of Ethalon: Emath, the court, or Aserenon, the border of Damascus toward the north, by Emath. The first tribe begins with Dan. The second, Aser. The third, Nephthali. The fourth, Manasses. The fifth, Ephraim. The sixth, Ruben. The seventh, Juda; this on the left side, and the sevenfold number is completed. Then the firstfruits of the priests and Levites, and the sanctuary of the Lord in the midst, and the holy of holies. The city itself also is described, on each side a square, having four thousand five hundred reeds. The suburbs also of the priests and Levites, and the possession of the prince. And again on the right side five tribes follow, likewise from the eastern side to the western side. The first of these is Benjamin; the second Simeon, having his own possession specially, and not, as before, mixed with Juda. The third, Issachar. The fourth, Zabulon. The fifth, Gad; and the gates of the city, three on each side, and the name of the city, which is contained on the golden plate on the forehead of the high priest.
