**“minister of Christ Jesus”** — chosen by Christ, or because he administers the gifts of God, or offers your goods to Christ.
1.8:
**“Who also hath manifested to us your love”**
• toward God and neighbour.
• founded.
**“in the spirit”** — in the Holy Spirit, not in the flesh.
**“In the spirit”** — Because you love spiritual things, not carnal things.
1.9:
**“Therefore”** — Behold what he prays.
**“we also, from the day that we heard it”** — these things concerning you.
**“cease not to pray for you”** — for you.
**“and to beg”** — as if for the merits which we show on your behalf.
**“that you may be filled with the knowledge of his will”** — that you may fully know what God wills and what he does not will, and he carries this out part by part.
**“in all”** — that is.
**“wisdom”** — of the things that belong to the active life.
**“That you may be filled in all wisdom”** — It is a great thing to know fully what God wills, in all things of the active and contemplative life.
**“and spiritual understanding”** — knowledge of spiritual things, which are contemplative
1.10:
**“That”** — after
**“walk”**
• doing well
• that you may act through good works
**“worthy”** — as befits God, or worthy of that reward
**“of God”** — so, that is
**“in all things”** — the affairs of the active and contemplative life
**“pleasing”**
• to God
• and
**“being fruitful in every good work”** — unto more
**“and increasing”** — through this purity of life
**“in the knowledge of God”** — in the thought of the divinity
**“In the knowledge of God”** — That they may not be ignorant of the form of their faith, that is, the hoped-for thing, by which they will be made firm.
1.11:
**“Strengthened with all might”** — and after this advancement we pray that you do not fall back
**“With all might”** — I say that you are strengthened by God in all might, namely in chastity and the rest. This he who is the brightness of the Father, that is, the Son, can well do. Or insofar as he has given you a clear knowledge.
**“according to the power of his glory”** — by him who was able to enlighten
**“in all patience”**
• remaining
• against adversities
**“and longsuffering”** — of long labour
**“with joy”** — and this not from sadness or necessity
1.12:
**“Giving thanks to God the Father”** — who alone can re-create and wills to, because he is Father
**“Giving thanks”** — Thus far, why he gives thanks and what he prays for them. Now he begins to show that the law does not profit but harms, and that Christ suffices for all good things. This can be known from the fact that he himself and the other apostles, who had been under the legal observances, left them and fled to Christ. We pray for you, giving thanks to God, because he makes us worthy, which the law could never do. The lot is the inheritance, which is given not by merits but by divine election to the holy patriarchs and prophets, and therefore it is to be sought through grace, not through the law. He hath made us worthy. Not in the law but in light, that is, through God, who is light of light, by whose grace we are enlightened. Or in light, that is, in clear knowledge, from which he who strays falls into darkness.
**“who hath made us worthy”** — the Gentiles also, in the promise to the Jews
**“to be partakers”** — participation
**“of the lot”** — inheritance
**“Lot”** — The will of God in the human race is the lot, with whom there is no iniquity, but who does all things through justice, even if hidden.
**“of the saints in light”** — that is, in the knowledge of himself
1.13:
**“Who”** — so he made worthy
**“hath delivered”** — in baptism
**“us from the power”** — because they truly ruled over us
**“of darkness”** — of the ignorance of sins, of the demons
**“and hath translated us into the kingdom”**
• that we might be the kingdom
• into heaven
**“of the Son of his love”**
• so that we too are loved through him, if we are not hateful to him
• Or thus. He hath delivered us from the power, that is, from hell, in which we were held by the devil, as much by our own fault as by the offence of Adam. And hath translated us into the kingdom of the Son. Because, lifting us from the depth of Tartarus, he brought us into heaven with his only Son. For now believers who are devout with steadfast mind, leaving the world, are led into heaven by the angel, the guide of the Father’s right hand.
**“The kingdom of the Son”** — Augustine. Of which he himself says: “My kingdom is not of this world”; he does not say: it is not here, but it is not from hence, because it is indeed a pilgrim in the world but is not of the world. For to his kingdom he says: “You are not of the world, but I have chosen you out of the world.” They were of the world when they belonged to the prince of the world.
**“Of the Son of his love”** — Augustine, On the Trinity, book 15. If the charity by which the Father loves the Son, and the Son loves the Father, shows ineffably the union or communion of them both, what is more fitting than that he should be properly called charity who is the Spirit common to both? Otherwise, if in that Trinity the Holy Spirit alone is charity, then the Son is found to be the Son not of the Father alone, but also of the Holy Spirit. For he did not say “of his Son,” which if he said he would say most truly, but he says: “of the Son of his love.” The Son, then, is also the Son of the Holy Spirit, if in that Trinity the charity of God is none other than the Holy Spirit. Since this is most absurd, it remains that the Holy Spirit is not only charity there, but on account of those things of which I have discoursed sufficiently, is properly so called. And as to what is said, “of the Son of his love,” let nothing else be understood than his beloved Son, the Son of his substance. For the charity of the Father is his nature and substance, as we have often said. And therefore the Son of his charity is no other than he who is begotten of his substance.
1.14:
**“In whom”**
• as if: I have translated you into the kingdom of the Son, through whom also he redeemed
• the Son
**“we have”** — we Jews
**“redemption”** — The power of the devil being destroyed, the capacity of freedom is given to us by the shedding of his blood, who had no sin. For the devil rightly held those whom he had bound as guilty of sin by the condition of death; these he would rightly release through him whom, guilty of no sin, he had undeservedly afflicted with the punishment of death.
**“the remission of sins”** — daily, if we sin, and there is no need of other victims
1.15:
**“Who”** — rightly these things through him, because he is
**“is the image of God”**
• fully like the Father
• because he is from him and differs nothing from him
• Who is the image. Augustine. The image of a king is on a coin otherwise than in a son. We are the coin, in whom the image of God is Christ the Son. No image of God ought to be worshipped, except that which is what he himself is; nor that image for him, but with him.
**“invisible”** — incomprehensible
**“the firstborn”**
• he alone begotten, others created
• here he is truly shown to be coeternal
• begotten before every creature
1.16:
**“For in him were all things created”** — truly begotten before every creature, because all things were made through him; behold, co-almighty
**“all things”**
• that are
• because also the elements, whence all things
**“in heaven and on earth, visible”** — sun and moon
**“and invisible”** — angels and souls
**“whether thrones”** — even these most high
**“or dominations, or principalities, or powers”** — therefore the Son is in nothing less than the Father
**“were created by him and in him”** — thus through him beforehand, what were life in him
**“and in him”** — Or all things are in Christ, whom they do not exceed, because he is immeasurable.
1.17:
**“And he is before all”**
• no one is equal to him, even as man
• not only in eternity and power but also in dignity
**“and by him all things consist”** — as he created all things, so he sustains and rules all things
1.18:
**“And he is the head of the body”** — even though such, according to both natures
**“The head of the body”** — Augustine. The head of the Church, that is, of the body, because he stands to the Church as the head to the body. And since the Church began from Abel, how is he its head? Well: because he is the beginning of the Church, that is, its founder.
**“the church”** — which is united to Christ by grace and nature, as to the head
**“who is the beginning”**
• namely
• founder
**“the firstborn”**
• He is well the head and beginning, that is, ruler and founder, who is the firstborn rising again to immortality.
• Others have the Word of God in themselves, but it is said of no one: “And the Word was made flesh.” Man therefore, assumed more excellently, bears as it were the person of the wisdom of God, as the head, in which are all the senses, bears the person of the soul which gives life to the whole body.
**“The firstborn”** — As he was born before all things of God that he might create all things, so the man rises first that he might restore, so that he may always be first and prince.
**“Who is the beginning”** — Of the Church according to the divinity, that is, the founder of the Church, because he enlightened by the power of his divinity and the gift of his mercy all the just who are begotten from Abel to the last just man. According to the humanity too he can be called the beginning of the Church, because it is founded upon faith in his humanity. And well is he head and beginning, and ruler and founder, because he is the firstborn, etc.
**“from the dead; that”** — by this
**“in all things”** — both to those before and to those after
**“he may hold the primacy”** — himself holding the primacy: lordship, because he can raise up others
1.19:
**“Because in him, it hath well pleased the Father, that all fulness should dwell”** — And he well has the primacy, not only because he is firstborn, but because it pleased the Trinity that in him should be all fullness of knowledge and virtues, not only be, but dwell, and reconcile all things, Jews and Gentiles.
**“All fulness”** — Augustine. Because he can do all things of himself. Whence: “As the Father has life in himself, so also the Son, who raises up and gives life to whom he will”; thus he is shown to be perfect God.
1.20:
**“And through him to reconcile all things unto himself”** — who is the eternal light, that is, eternal truth
**“making peace through the blood”**
• not through another victim
• Through him to reconcile all things to himself, making peace, etc. It pleased God to reconcile through him, and he made peace, not freely, but through the blood, both things celestial and terrestrial, because the way into heaven lies open to man.
**“All things”** — Things made through him live in him their author.
**“of his cross”** — which is the more shameful death
**“the things that are in heaven”**
• that is, things celestial and terrestrial
• already they are, like Abraham and the others
**“the things that are on earth”** — still in this life
1.21:
**“And you”** — O Colossians, he has made peace, although you were estranged, having nothing with God, and enemies by contradicting, and in this sense because you thought you did well
**“whereas”** — although
**“you were some time alienated and enemies in mind”** — Or: alienated and enemies in mind, that is, of his counsel, which comes to the same, because, devoted to their idols, they did not receive what God commanded through Moses.
**“in evil works”** — living in deed
1.22:
**“Yet now”** — in the time of grace and no other
**“hath reconciled”** — by the forgiveness of sins
**“in the body of his flesh”**
• that is, of frailty, that is, passible and mortal; and this through death also, so that at last he might present
• He reconciled in the body, etc. If he who was mortal and dead could reconcile, now immortal he can do all things.
**“through death, to present you holy”** — by virtues
**“and unspotted”** — from sins
**“and blameless”**
• to such a degree that
• because then there will be nothing evil in them
**“before him”** — who sees all things; or when you will be present to him, seeing him as he is
1.23:
**“If so”** — to present yourselves, however, on this condition
**“ye continue in the faith, grounded”** — firm, not wavering
**“If so ye continue”** — Therefore he had said so many and such great things about Christ, that they should place their hope in him alone, in whom all things are, and not think that they must submit themselves to any of the elements or angels. He alone is to be worshipped, and no one is to be reckoned equal to him.
**“and settled”** — in hope of reward, so that by yourselves you do not fall away
**“and immoveable”** — another pushing you
**“from the hope of the gospel which you have heard”** — which you ought to hold, because you have understood it; and therefore it is impious to turn back. For it is better not to know the way of truth than, having known it, to go backward
**“which is preached”** — and remains
**“in all the creation that is under heaven”**
• to all men who are a new creature, however many they are and wherever they are
• In all the creation that is under heaven, etc. Or: the creature which, though new, is now under heaven and still a pilgrim, will at last come to glory.
**“whereof”** — of the gospel
**“I Paul am made a minister”** — and so you can know that it is true
1.24:
**“Who now”** — placed in prison at Ephesus for the gospel
**“rejoice”** — because believers thereby progress
**“in my sufferings”** — which I endure
**“for you”** — to be strengthened in the truth of the gospel
**“and fill up”**
• each pays what he owes according to his measure
• I fill up. I fill up those sufferings that Christ endured, or that he now commands to be endured, which are still lacking; that is, I am ready to suffer.
**“those things that are wanting of the sufferings of Christ”** — are ours, for they are Christ’s, because they are his members
**“in my flesh”** — not in my own
**“for his body”** — by multiplying
**“which is the church”** — which is the Church, I say, and no other
1.25:
**“whereof”** — of the body
**“I am made a minister”**
• that I may minister spiritual things to it
• He says that he was made a minister of the gospel by God through Christ, so that the mystery begun by God might be fulfilled through a fit servant, a mystery which was unknown from the ages.
**“according to the dispensation of God”**
• that I may actually dispense God to them, through the grace of the apostleship entrusted to me by God
• or according to the grace of the apostleship dispensed to me by God
**“which is given me towards you”** — not only the office but the carrying out of the office
**“that I may fulfill the word of God”**
• I will show the ordinance of God concerning you Gentiles fulfilled
• Given to me. That I may fulfil what God foreordained concerning you: that you, namely, should be saved through the incarnation, lest it seem that salvation was not promised to the Gentiles.
• Or: it is given to me in you; for what is required of my people is as much as if it were required of myself.
1.26:
**“The mystery which hath been hidden”** — which word was so hidden that it is also a mystery, that is, hidden
**“which hath been hidden”** — If it was known: “In the beginning was the Word,” it had nowhere been read: “And the Word was made flesh.” Whence: “Thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them to the little ones.”
**“from ages”** — from the beginning of the ages
*Augustine:* For I saw certain books of the Platonists translated from the Greek tongue into Latin, and there I read, not indeed in these words, but this very thing, urged by many and manifold reasons: “In the beginning was the Word: and the Word was with God.” But that “the Word was made flesh” I did not read. I searched, indeed, and found it said in various ways in those books that the Son is in the form of the Father, but that he emptied himself is not found in them.
**“and generations”** — to all, not only to some part, except to whom he showed it by the Spirit
**“but now”** — in the time of grace
**“is manifested to his saints”** — not to all
1.27:
**“To whom God would”** — not to all these, but to whom he willed, from grace alone
**“make known the riches of the glory of this mystery”** — the abundant glory of so worthy a sacrament, in which are many things: faith, forgiveness, righteousness, gifts of the Spirit, future blessedness; and therefore he says “riches”
**“among the Gentiles”** — being
**“which”** — the sacrament
**“is Christ”** — the incarnation of Christ
**“in you”** — to the Gentiles
**“the hope of glory”** — that through him you may hope for glory without the law
1.28:
**“Whom”** — such Christ
**“we”** — the apostles
**“preach”** — that he saves the Gentiles without the law
**“admonishing”**
• reproving those who go astray
• Or: we reprove those who contradict, and conquer them, and teach those who obey.
**“every man”**
• not only you
• both Jew and Gentile alike
**“and teaching”** — those who are ignorant
**“in all”** — not blind, like the false ones
**“wisdom”** — true and of the Lord
**“In all wisdom”** — True wisdom is when Christ is acknowledged.
**“that we may present”** — we may offer to God as a sacrifice
**“perfect in Christ Jesus”**
• not in the law
• in understanding of the mystery
1.29:
**“In whom”**
• in Christ Jesus
• in which thing
• that every man may be perfect in Christ
**“I labour, striving”** — against the rebellious
**“according to his working which he worketh in me in power”** — of miracles
**“I labour in power”** — As if: God adds miracles to my labour for confirmation.

2.1:
**“For I would have you know”** — therefore I report this about myself to you
**“what manner of care”** — that, having understood these things, you may seek to be made perfect in Christ
**“for you”** — For he was no less anxious for those whom he has not seen than for those whom he has seen.
**“and for them that are at Laodicea”** — because these also had been forestalled by the false
**“and whosoever”** — and for those who are near you, whoever they are
**“have not seen my face in the flesh”** — although they have heard of the knowledge
2.2:
**“that their hearts may be comforted”**
• or receive consolation
• I aim at this, that they with you may comfort their hearts
**“Being instructed in charity”** — Which God had toward us, who delivered up his Son for us. If anyone attends to this, he can be comforted in this misery, because from it he perceives that, pride being trampled down, he can return to his country by humility. And instructed. Tending thereby to the knowledge of God. Unto all riches, that is, the abundance of full understanding, where they may have perfect understanding of things human and divine, as of the soul and of the higher spirits: for otherwise no one ascends to the knowledge of God. In the knowledge of God. I do not say as to his works, but of the mystery of God, that you may know what is a secret known to few. Of God the Father of Jesus Christ. That you may know that he is another person than the Son, though the same in substance with him. If you aim at this knowledge, run back to Christ alone, because in him are all riches, but hidden; and therefore do not wonder if you are in Christ and have not yet found them, because they are not open to all, but to those who ask and knock.
**“being instructed in charity”** — Another reading: When they shall have been instructed in charity, unto all riches of fulness of understanding, unto the knowledge of the mystery of God in Christ. The Apostle wishes to cherish their minds in charity, that they might be ready to receive through the epistle the knowledge of the sacrament of God in Christ, observing that these are the riches of wisdom and knowledge, if Christ is acknowledged, to be adored in the fulness of his Godhead. Ambrose. The whole mystery of the sacrament of God in Christ is that he who knows him may be seen to have knowledge of all things. For the whole account of the higher knowledge of the whole creation, heavenly or earthly, is in him who is their head and author, so that he who knows him seeks nothing beyond, because this is perfect power and wisdom. Whatever is sought elsewhere is found perfectly here. In Daniel and Solomon he shows to unbelievers that he is the author of all knowledge and wisdom, which unbelievers do not think, because they do not read in the gospels and prophets astrology, geometry, and other such things, which are therefore despised by us, because nothing in them pertains to salvation, but they send men into error, and while they study them they have no care of the soul. But he who knows Christ finds the treasure of wisdom and knowledge, because he knows what is useful.
**“and unto all”**
• or by this aiming
• that from all
**“riches of fulness of understanding”** — may have full understanding
**“unto the knowledge”** — instructed
**“of the mystery”** — which is Christ, the Word made flesh
**“of God the Father and of Christ Jesus”** — that this is the mystery
2.3:
**“In whom are hid all the treasures”** — that through humiliation the proud are redeemed
**“of wisdom”**
• concerning divine things
• that the Word was with God
**“and knowledge”**
• concerning human things
• that man is with us
2.4:
**“Now this I say”**
• that you may be instructed
• Not only that you strive for those things you do not yet have, but that no one deceive you and by worldly reasoning draw you away from the hope that is in Christ.
**“I say, that”** — however wise
**“that no man may deceive you”**
• as it seems
• or: 'subtlety'
• which is only in words
2.5:
**“For though I be absent in body”** — As if: I say this lest he deceive; for I see by the Spirit of God what is going on among you.
**“I be absent”** — Lest he deceive; I say, for I know that they are not yet deceived.
**“yet in spirit I am with you”** — As the spirit of Eliseus with Giezi going to Naaman the Syrian, that he should receive under his name things which he himself had not commanded.
**“yet in spirit”** — It was given to the saints to see distant things in the Spirit. Let those therefore beware, whose deeds are not hidden from their master.
**“rejoicing”** — By this he makes them more eager about the gospel, because he says he rejoices in the disposition of their conduct and the steadfastness of their faith, so that, knowing whereby they please God, they might become firmer in it.
**“and beholding”** — because
**“your order”** — how each of you lives according to his own order
**“and the steadfastness”** — steadfastness
**“of your faith which is in Christ”** — not in the law
2.6:
**“As therefore”** — since you stand well on the foundation of faith
**“you have received”** — for it was a good receiving
**“Jesus Christ the Lord”** — not outside
**“walk ye”** — make progress
2.7:
**“Rooted”**
• as a tree for bearing fruit
• The lesser ones, in the active life, are built up above others; you greater ones, who are in contemplation, are those.
**“and built up in him”** — into the temple of God, whence he may speak to others
**“and confirmed in the faith, as also you have learned”** — As if to say: walk, I say, in the action of thanksgiving, firm in faith, not otherwise than you have received and learned by knowledge, and you have matter for thanksgiving abounding in him; and in this walk see that no one deceive you.
**“abounding”** — gifts
**“in him”** — who alone gives the increase
2.8:
**“Beware lest any man cheat you by philosophy”** — reasonings sought out to prove or disprove what is said of the law
**“By philosophy”** — Earthly philosophy, which composes by arguments and subtlety and deceives, while in plausible causes and invented things nothing is so truly esteemed as what is seen in the elements, which were not ordained by God but by men; and these are to be avoided, because it is a worshipper of the world, not of God, and draws away from Christ, in whom is perfection, because he has all things that the Father has.
**“and vain deceit”** — that is, through that which is proved
**“deceit”** — What the false preachers say of the law. And vain, because in this falsehood there is no profit, which is sometimes found in falsehoods. According to the elements. He touches those who explain idols more prudently, saying: Juno is the air, Neptune the sea. Therefore, when he had said according to philosophy and vain deceit, he adds: according to the elements of the world. As if warning that not only worshippers of images of whatever kind are to be avoided, but also, as it were, the teachers and interpreters of signs.
**“according to”** — Acting
**“the tradition of men”** — that is, legal observances; for after the truth was shown, the law is not a tradition of God but of men
**“according to the tradition of men”** — The philosophers, whom they call men, teach that God cannot become a creature, that a man cannot be born of a virgin or a dead man live again, considering the elements, that is, these visible creatures, in which animals are generated from a mixture, and what dies does not live again.
**“according to the elements of the world”** — the literal sense, which concerns worldly things
**“and not according to Christ”** — that is, according to the truth of spiritual understanding
2.9:
**“For in him dwelleth all the fulness of the Godhead”** — not according to Christ, because in Christ dwells the fulness of the Godhead, as all, that is, in every mode of dwelling, so that the divinity is also personally united to him, which is not so in any creature
**“corporeally”**
• Hilary. “That the fulness dwelling in him be understood to be nothing other than Christ.”
• Bodily, that is, completely, so that he is the body and fulfilment of the shadows of the law. But whoever says that the observances of the flesh are necessary says that Christ is not the body of the shadows, nor God sufficient for all things.
**“Corporeally”** — Not because God is corporeal, but he used a figurative word, because in the temple made by hands he dwelt not corporeally but shadowily, that is, by prefiguring signs. Or corporeally: because God dwells in Christ’s body, which he took from the Virgin, as in a temple; but not so in the saints, because he is the head in which are all the senses, in these as it were touch alone, to whom the Spirit is given by measure, of whom it cannot be said: “The Word was made flesh,” nor is any of them called the only-begotten of God.
2.10:
**“And you are filled in him”** — who is so full
**“him”** — Those who deny it are against Christ.
**“filled”**
• by the gifts of the Spirit
• that they are not the elements themselves
**“who is the head of all principality”**
• as if: he who fills the heavenly citizens can fill you
• not only of men but also
2.11:
**“In whom”**
• you are filled not only with gifts
• He warned them not to fall away from Christ through philosophy; now he warns them not to be led astray by false apostles and receive the ceremonies of the law.
**“also you are circumcised with circumcision”** — purified from error and the world
**“not made by hand”**
• by human work
• as the legal circumcision was done
**“in despoiling”**
• remaining
• that is, stripped of the body, insofar as it was of the flesh, that is, subject to the flesh, serving the desires of the flesh; but now it is made spirit, serving him, or not made by hand, namely in the stripping of the skin, so that nothing is done there except that the skin is taken away
**“of the body of the flesh”**
• or skin; another reading
• because nothing is done there except that the skin is removed
• The body of the flesh: that is, the body which is flesh, because not every body is flesh.
**“but in the circumcision of Christ”** — where all vices are cut away, which only Christ does
2.12:
**“Buried with him”** — truly you have obtained this in Christ
**“in baptism”**
• so that they are not now seen as what they were, that is, old sinners, but as new righteous
• Buried with him in baptism: that is, they were baptized in the likeness of his burial.
**“In whom also you are risen again”** — in newness of life
**“by the faith”** — not through anything else
**“of the operation of God”**
• which God works
• Or, through the faith of the operation: that is, by believing the works of God. He explains one of the works of God, which is especially the work that those who wish to rise must believe, namely that he raised Christ.
**“By the faith of the operation of God”** — Of which they believe that by the example of Christ he will raise them. Whence: “who hath raised him up,” etc.
**“Who”** — behold, in whom
**“hath raised him up from the dead”** — he puts this first to prove that they will rise also into immortality
2.13:
**“And you”** — the Gentiles
**“whereas”** — although
**“were dead”** — not perceiving your evils
**“in your sins”** — those who abandoned the natural law
**“and the uncircumcision of your flesh”** — original sin, which the foreskin signifies
**“Uncircumcision”** — For what the foreskin signifies: that is, carnal sins.
**“hath quickened together”**
• according to body and soul
• already by the certainty of hope
**“with him”** — in the likeness of him
**“forgiving you”** — he quickened the dead, freely forgiving all things; which is a sign that he will also take away punishments
**“all offences”** — original sins and those that have been added
2.14:
**“Blotting out the handwriting that was against us”**
• the memory of the Scriptures
• He calls the handwriting the sin of Adam, which he took away and fastened to the cross, not only the other sins, because unless he took away this and the others, we would not be freed from death and hell. While the innocent is slain, sin is crucified. The decree is the sentence adverse to all men, in which it was said: “Thou shalt die the death,” etc.
**“Blotting out the handwriting of the decree that”** — He gave pardon not only to you Gentiles, but to us Jews also he forgave the transgressions that are from the law, and this by blotting out. The handwriting, that is, the memory of the transgression, which was from the decree, that is, from the law. For our conscience and the devil, to accuse us, were mindful of that transgression, and so this memory was against us, hurting us and tormenting us; but this having been washed away in baptism, neither does our conscience fear, nor has the devil anything to charge. Or the decree of God was: “But of the tree of knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat.” The handwriting of this violated decree, that is, the memory or sentence in which it was said, “thou shalt die the death,” God blotted out when he washed away the sin of the first parent by the blood of Christ.
**“of the decree”** — of the law
**“which”** — the decree
**“was contrary to us. And he hath taken the same out of the way”**
• since it did not help but made them guilty all the more
• decree or handwriting
**“fastening it”** — of all, so that no one further observes it
**“to the cross”** — when the innocent is killed, sin is crucified, that is, mortified. For the cross is not the death of the Saviour but of sin
**“fastening it to the cross”** — That it may now cease, since all the sacrifices have been fulfilled in the offering of the true lamb. Who then restored that? And as he freed us from the law and from the transgression of the law, so he also freed the ancient fathers from hell, lest anyone think they were saved by the law. And this is: Despoiling the principalities and powers. By taking away Abraham, Isaac and the other just. He led them over, first far from this kingdom to heaven, confidently, that is, with great confidence, with hope of victory. Triumphing, that is, overcoming them, which is not in secret. But openly. For if anyone looks to the perfection of the Church, the ancient enemy is plainly seen to be conquered.
2.15:
**“And despoiling the principalities”** — infernal
**“and the powers he hath exposed”**
• by washing away sins
• Or: he led over the principalities and powers, that is, he drove them out of the Church
**“confidently in open shew”**
• as God-man without sin
• Or: openly. Descending to hell with the angelic legions. IN HIMSELF, that is, in the presence of his majesty
**“triumphing”** — on the cross
**“them”** — the infernal princes
**“in himself”**
• offered up
• not in another
• Or according to another reading. Augustine. Putting off the flesh to the Father, and despoiling the powers, openly and confidently triumphing over them in himself. By the name of flesh in this place mortality is understood. According to that: “Flesh and blood cannot possess the kingdom of God.” Through this mortality the powers envious of us were condemned. Therefore Christ, putting off this mortality in the resurrection, is said to have despoiled the devilish powers (which were condemned through this mortality), because in himself, our head, he gave an example of what will be fulfilled in his whole body, that is, the Church, to be freed from the power of the devil, in the last resurrection.
• The same. In him also the powers, our enemies, invincible to us, are conquered, where invisible desires are conquered; for by the shedding of blood without guilt, the handwritings of all guilts were blotted out, by which the debtors who believe in him were before held by the devil; whence: “Which shall be shed for many.”
**“Triumphing over them in himself”** — Augustine. By his death. For by the one most true sacrifice offered for us, he extinguished whatever there was of guilts, by which the principalities and powers held us back to pay the punishments of life; whence, therefore, the devil received outwardly the power of killing the Lord’s flesh, from there his inner power, by which he held us, was slain.
2.16:
**“Let no man therefore”** — because all these things are in Christ
**“judge you”** — show to be damnable
**“in meat”** — taken or not taken, according to the rite of the Jews
**“or in drink, or in respect of a festival day”**
• that is, concerning this, that you observe no part
• not celebrated, when the law commands celebrating
**“or”** — namely
**“of the new moon, or of the sabbaths”** — or he says: because one alone was not observed, then it condemned, but now not. For that was the time of signifying, and this of making manifest
2.17:
**“Which are a shadow of things to come”** — some signs depending on the thing
**“Which are”** — Then there were precepts of this kind, which not to keep was sin; now they are testimonies and confirmation of the truth. Therefore the Scripture, which then was the exactor of works that signified, is now the witness of the things signified; and what was then observed as a forerunner is now read for confirmation.
**“but the body is of Christ”** — But the body, that is, the truth of this shadow. Is of Christ, that is, pertains to Christ. Or all those things are the body of Christ, that is, they signify the body of Christ, either that which he took from the Virgin or that which is the Church.
2.18:
**“Let no man”** — and because they are a shadow
**“seduce you, willing”**
• loving
• to persuade
• Unwilling, that is, loving those things which he has not seen, or willing, namely to persuade of what he has not seen, namely the ceremonies of the law whose reason he does not know.
**“in humility”** — because these are the things by which men can easily be seduced
**“and religion of angels”** — by which they seem to be messengers of God
**“which he hath not seen”** — those things which he never understood
**“walking in vain”**
• because whatever he does, he loses
• because not in Christ
**“puffed up”** — proud, whence it would be shameful
**“by the sense”** — that is, of sensuality
**“of his flesh.”** — not of reason
**“puffed up by the sense of the flesh”** — He understands nothing other than what sensuality grasps.
2.19:
**“And not holding the head”**
• Christ
• against what those say who preach the law
**“from which”** — from the head, that is, receiving from whose fullness
**“the whole body”** — the Church
**“by joints”** — through the bonds of charity
**“and bands”** — and the joinings of faith, hope and works, by which they are joined and alike
**“being supplied with nourishment and compacted, groweth”**
• by virtues and members
• CONSTRUCTED. Into one by joining, because they believe the same and work the same things. And SUPPLIED in serving. THROUGH BONDS, that is, through charity, without which members do not cohere, nor serve one another nor live.
**“unto the increase of God”**
• as much as God provides
• therefore
**“Unto the increase of God”** — God is increased as they return, as he was diminished by those who desert.
2.20:
**“If then you be dead”**
• wholly separated
• not a wretched death from Christ but a happy death
**“If you be dead”**
• He has hitherto warned those standing lest they be seduced; now he attacks those who already kept some of the law. As if: you, see that you are not seduced; but you others, say why you keep the law?
• He calls the creatures of this world “elements.” If, he says, when you received the faith of Christ, you were separated from sin and from the elements of the world, that is, from abstinence and from all superstition about the creatures of the world, why do you yet, etc. Or “with Christ” can be taken as “like Christ.”
**“with Christ”**
• through this, that you are with Christ
• because you have received the faith of Christ
• as Christ
**“from the elements”** — That is, from the law, which is the instruction of children who seek worldly things.
**“of this world why”** — As if they were ignorant before, why, with the truth now declared?
**“yet”** — Namely, with the truth known and received.
**“as though living in the world”** — As the Jews, who live to the world and not to God.
**“do you decree”**
• Legal observances to be kept.
• Saying one to another.
2.21:
**“Touch not”** — Such as a corpse, or a place where a menstruous woman has sat.
**“taste not”** — Such as a pig, or fish without scales.
**“handle not”** — With a certain eagerness and delight.
2.22:
**“Which all are”** — As if: you ought not to discriminate these things.
**“unto destruction”** — That is, they lead to death.
**“by the very use”** — If anyone uses them.
**“Which all are unto destruction by the very use”** — If anyone uses them in the Jewish rite, so as to abstain from these and use those, believing that he is justified thereby, they lead to death. I say these things are already existing according to the precept and doctrines of men, not of God. For after the truth came, God no longer commands these things, but the Pharisees do; and by authority they command them and by reasons they teach them.
**“according to the precepts and doctrines”** — Not because it is true.
**“of men”** — Not of God.
**“According to the precepts”** — As if: therefore their use and observance perish, because they are precepts and teachings of men, not of God.
2.23:
**“Which things have indeed”** — Because they put forward superstition and humility.
**“a shew”** — The appearance.
**“have indeed a shew of wisdom in superstition”** — That is, religion that goes beyond measure.
**“and humility”** — Because they show themselves humble.
**“Which things have indeed a shew”** — Or these have a reason of wisdom, not in truth but in falsehood, which abounds where there is no profit, but through human wisdom; and they are such. In humility: not that which is a virtue, but, as is understood from the Greek, that by which the mind has lowly thoughts, that is, useful and earthly ones, that is, by dejection of soul; and they are such. Not to sparing, that is, because in those observances there is much labour, which is empty; and they are not such. In honour of God, whose counsel is brought to nothing, nor of the saints, whose faith is destroyed; and they are not such. To the filling, because they take much away from them.
**“and”** — And because they are.
**“not sparing the body”**
• Because they say they do not spare the body.
• Because they say they do not care about human honor.
**“not in any honour”**
• And because they are not.
• They call others gluttons.
**“to the filling of the flesh”**
• Because they withhold many things from themselves.
• Or fattening.
**“In superstition”** — Ambrose. Religion is feigned, so that things which are false may seem true; it humbles minds on the earth, lest they be raised to the things above, and it harms the body whose head is Christ; not in honour, because they are cut off from the head, Christ, fulfilling the sense of the flesh. For the fatness is the carnal sense, a human tradition, by which it says that what the wisdom of the flesh hands down is enough.

3.1:
**“Therefore”** — Because they are dead to the elements, and because these things have no power.
**“if you be risen”** — The soul in reality, the body in hope.
**“with Christ”** — After the likeness of Christ.
**“seek the things that are above”**
• Do not think carnal things.
• that is, the spiritual things that are shown in them
• The things that are above, etc. These are the spiritual things signified by carnal observances. Or eternal glory, or the things that lead to it.
**“Seek the things that are above”** — Not by place but by merit of excellence.
**“where Christ is sitting at the right hand of God”** — that is, reigning in equality with the Father; and so the height of excellence is supreme, and by this it is certain that you can come there through him.
3.2:
**“Mind the things that are above”** — But have the things found delightful. And this is what he adds: Mind
**“Mind”** — also with understanding and charity
**“not the things that are upon the earth”** — those that are founded on earth, because you have died to these
3.3:
**“For you are dead”** — to earthly and perishable things
**“are dead”** — and therefore the things above are to be sought, not those upon the earth
**“and your life”** — chiefly to earthly and carnal things
**“is hid”**
• now
• and therefore to be sought
**“Your life is hid”** — That is, your time has not yet come, because summer has not yet come, that is, the coming of Christ, when fruitful trees will be separated from barren ones; but the time of those who love earthly things is always ready. But when Christ appears, this is our time.
**“with Christ”** — with Christ, who is eternal life
**“in God”** — in God, with whom Christ is one and the same
3.4:
**“When Christ shall appear, who is your life”** — When Christ shall appear, who is your life, he will be revealed to you so that you may see him clearly with the Father.
**“then you also shall appear”** — then you also shall appear, to yourselves and to others
**“with him in glory”** — Being.
3.5:
**“Mortify therefore”**
• and so that this may be: therefore
• After the arguments about the fullness of Christ, a general exhortation on conduct is added for all, lest they return to their former custom.
**“your members”**
• all sins; the one body; the single members
• Your members, that is, the parts of the old man. Or the lusts of the members.
**“that are upon the earth”** — are ruled by earthly and carnal things
**“fornication”**
• every intercourse outside lawful marriage
• which is according to nature
• Fornication, etc. He describes the sins that he calls members, so that after receiving the reasoning of truth they would give effort to a good life. It greatly harms to know the reason of truth and not to carry it out in deeds. For “he that knoweth the will of the Lord and doth it not, shall be beaten with many stripes.”
**“uncleanness”** — against nature
**“lust”** — a burning that runs through any shameful acts
**“evil concupiscence”** — concerning another’s property or wife
**“and covetousness”** — which, if it does not defile the body, yet defiles the soul
**“And covetousness”** — Under one name he forbids two very evil things, idolatry and covetousness, whose malice is not unlike, because covetousness is the root of all evils, and they are almost fulfilled in one work; for as idolatry strives to take glory from the one God, that he alone may not have the name of deity, so the covetous man stretches himself out against the things of God, to usurp alone what God made for all; both are enemies to God, because they deny to God what is his.
**“which is the service of idols”**
• that is, to be fled as much as idolatry, to which this vice is equal
• he serves things in place of God
3.6:
**“For which things”** — the aforesaid evils
**“the wrath of God cometh upon the children of unbelief”**
• or of distrust
• what then of those whom ignorance does not excuse, who will be punished more heavily as it were?
3.7:
**“In which you also”**
• as others
• He mentions this so that they may rejoice that they have escaped, and be careful from now on.
**“walked some time”** — and therefore more shamefully if you now return
**“when you lived in them”** — when you thought there was life in them
3.8:
**“but now”**
• when you have received Christ
• But now, etc. Above he forbade the graver sins; now the lesser ones, lest these be thought not to be dangerous.
• There are those who do not have the habit of drunkenness, yet sometimes get drunk; so there are those who do not have the habit of lying, and yet sometimes lie; and so it is in other things. He therefore forbids lying at times, and especially lying constantly.
**“you also”** — as all the faithful
**“put you all away”** — not only the great vices mentioned above but also all others, namely
**“anger”** — which is a sudden movement of the mind
**“indignation”** — against another who is exalted
**“malice”** — the feeling of anger and indignation
**“blasphemy”** — against a brother
**“filthy speech”** — or foul speaking
**“out of your mouth”** — even if it is conceived in the heart
3.9:
**“Lie not one to another”** — one to another
**“stripping yourselves”** — what is meant by each single thing
**“of the old man”**
• the old man, the old life in sins according to Adam
• the habit of sins
**“with his deeds”** — so that not even at times the act of sin is present
3.10:
**“And putting on the new”** — the habit of virtues, which does not lack acts
**“who is renewed”** — because he grows more and more and acquires the knowledge of God
**“Who is renewed”** — Augustine. The renewal of the mind is said to be according to God, as is read in the epistle to the Ephesians, or according to the image of God, as is read here. But it is said “according to God” lest it be thought to be made according to some other creature. “According to the image of God,” so that it may be understood to be made in that part where the image of God is, that is, in the mind; not that the image according to which we are renewed is one and that which is renewed another, but the same; as we say of some believer who departs from the body that he is dead according to the body, not according to the spirit, because he has died in the body or by the body, not in the soul or by the soul. As someone is called beautiful or strong according to the body, not according to the soul.
**“unto knowledge, according to the image of him”**
• that is, in the image, namely in reason, which is the image of God
• According to the image, that is, reason. As if to say: I advise nothing other than what your reason persuades. This is the image to which God created man, that he might be rational and always love heavenly things.
*Ambrose:* The image which he says is recreated by the knowledge of God, which is also in woman, is one thing, and that to which the first man was made is another. Whence above to the Corinthians: “The man indeed ought not to cover his head, because he is the image and glory of God; but the woman is the glory of the man.” That image is so that, as all things are from one God, so all men should be from one man.
**“that created him”** — in the knowledge of himself
**“him”** — the new man
3.11:
**“Where”** — in which new man
**“there is neither male nor female”**
• that is, the distinction of male and female
• Where there is neither male, etc. And the sense is this. In the new man no outward difference prejudices anyone, whether of sexes, or nations, or observances, or languages, or conditions; but Christ is all, that is, all the parts of the new man are the works of Christ. And Christ himself is in all the faithful who are new through him.
**“Where there is neither”** — According to the body there are males and females, but according to the spirit of the mind there are not; in which we are renewed according to the image of the creator.
**“Gentile nor Jew”**
• it harms or profits no one that they were born of these or of those.
• no one is excluded as unworthy.
**“circumcision nor uncircumcision”** — none are more worthy there because they have this, or less worthy because they do not have it.
**“Barbarian nor Scythian, bond nor free”** — no one is more worthy or less worthy there on account of these things.
**“But Christ is all”** — all parts of the new man are the works of Christ.
**“and in all”** — the faithful
3.12:
**“Put ye on therefore”** — because Christ is all things in all.
**“as”** — that is, truly
**“the elect of God”** — whom God chose from eternity
**“holy”**
• by participation in the sacraments
• and because they are already holy, and because God loved them
**“and beloved”** — by God
**“the bowels of mercy”** — a feeling of piety towards all
**“benignity”**
• a mind ready to do good
• the carrying out of mercy
**“humility”** — that they be humble in heart and in bearing
**“modesty”** — keeping measure in all things
**“patience”** — in bearing adversity
3.13:
**“Bearing with one another”** — one bear another’s burdens
**“and forgiving one another”** — if one offend another, let him not only not avenge but forgive.
**“if any have a complaint against another: even as the Lord hath forgiven you, so do you also”** — wholly and purely
**“even as the Lord hath forgiven you”** — In the sacrament of which thing Christ washed the feet of the disciples and said: I have given you an example, that you also may do likewise. Therefore let us forgive one another our offences and pray for one another’s offences, and so in a manner wash one another’s feet. And note that, so that they may have profit, he admonishes them to do these things, which lay up merit with God; fear makes one abstain from unlawful things. For he fears lest, doing evil, he be subjected to punishments. These things which he now admonishes them to do pertain to the advancement of merits. He therefore who abstains from unlawful things has praise; but he who restrains himself even from lawful things has praise and reward.
3.14:
**“But above all these things”**
• one must strive more for the virtue that is greater than all.
• seek charity more eagerly than the others, or which is above all.
**“have charity”** — Augustine. For it is the more eminent way, which surpasses knowledge and all precepts. This is the Lord’s seamless garment, woven from above. Seamless, lest it ever be unstitched, which has come to one, because charity gathers all into one.
**“which is the bond of perfection”** — the other things make one perfect; charity binds all together, so that they do not go away.
3.15:
**“And let the peace of Christ rejoice”**
• which Christ had and commands to be had, or which he made between God and men; let it be in your consciences, the cause of exultation, which will surely be so if charity is had, which has true peace and keeps it with a pure heart.
• Peace. It is necessary for the unity of the body, which it itself makes.
**“The peace of Christ”** — Peace can be spoken of, even if it does not have charity. But charity always has peace with it.
**“in your hearts, wherein also you are called in one”** — placed by it
**“body”** — of the Church
**“and be ye thankful”** — for all these things
**“be ye”** — to God
3.16:
**“The word of Christ”** — He sets down first by what means these things can be done, namely that they may teach and admonish prudently, because
**“dwell in you abundantly, in all wisdom”** — that you may have full understanding of the Scriptures
**“teaching”**
• you and others, about what is unknown
• about those things that are contained
**“and admonishing”** — about what is known
**“Teaching and admonishing”** — That teaching may be given to those who do not know, and admonition to those who know.
**“one another”** — about morals
**“hymns”** — about the praises of God
**“spiritual canticles”** — about the eternal good
**“singing in grace”** — taught and admonished by these, singing to the honour of God not only with the lips but with understanding; or attentive in grace, that is, in consideration of God’s benefits
**“in your hearts to God”** — to the honour of the Lord
3.17:
**“All whatsoever you do in word or in work”**
• because he commands God to be praised in the heart; now he commands the name of Christ to be exalted in words and deeds
• moreover
• All whatsoever, etc. Because above he commanded that God be praised in the heart, now he exhorts that the name of God be praised and exalted both in words and in deeds, so that our words and works may be without reproach, that the Lord may be magnified, under whose teaching the disciples are blameless.
**“do all in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ”** — for the glory of Christ, not your own
**“All things”** — Not only what you do in word or deed, but also all thoughts and whatever else there is; or whatever you do, do it all, that is, attributing it perfectly to God; and this is doing it in the name.
**“giving thanks”** — then truly
**“to God, and the Father”** — Not read.
**“Giving thanks”** — For then we truly give thanks to God through Christ if we keep the measure of his commandments.
**“by him”** — Christ, through whom God gave all things
3.18:
**“Wives”** — Hitherto he has admonished all in common concerning morals; now he passes to particular precepts, admonishing different persons separately to serve one another, not only by obeying, as wives their husbands, and children their parents, and servants their masters, but also by taking counsel, as husbands for their wives, fathers for their children, masters for their servants. This is domestic peace, and the concord of those dwelling together ordered by God, and clear justice, that those who excel in reason may excel in authority.
**“be subject to your husbands, as it behoveth”** — as perfectly as the Lord commanded
**“in the Lord”** — not against the Lord
3.19:
**“Husbands, love your wives”** — softens the rigour of lordship
**“and be not bitter”** — bitter
**“Be not bitter”** — By this he softens the rigour of lordship, so that a man, with the power by which he prevails in lordship over his wife, does not use it too severely.
3.20:
**“Children, obey your parents in all things: for this”** — if you obey in all things, yet only if it is in the Lord
**“is well pleasing to the Lord”** — or: for this pleases God
3.21:
**“Fathers, provoke not your children to indignation”**
• against you
• or wrath
**“Fathers, provoke not”** — He commands fathers to be moderate with their children, lest, being constrained by them, the children sin against them and offend God. For anger is an unconsidered thing, so that sometimes he who is angry does not spare even himself.
**“provoke not your children”** — with some harshness
**“lest they be discouraged”**
• or fainthearted
• not able to endure longer
3.22:
**“Servants”** — you also
**“obey in all things your masters”** — who rule according to the flesh
**“according to the flesh”** — not to say only to the spiritual ones
**“not serving to the eye, as pleasing men”** — not to God
**“pleasing men”** — wishing to please
**“but in simplicity of heart”** — with a pure intention, being inwardly such as they are outwardly
**“fearing God”** — whom you cannot deceive
3.23:
**“Whatsoever you do, do it from the heart”** — and not as fearing punishment from God, but from willing service
**“as”** — you would serve
**“Do it from the heart, as to the Lord, and not to men”** — Augustine. For God approves that innocence by which a man becomes innocent not through fear of punishment but through love of justice. For he who does not sin through fear, though he does not harm others, yet harms himself very greatly. Feigned innocence is not innocence; feigned equity is not equity, but a doubled sin, in which there are iniquity and pretence.
3.24:
**“Knowing”** — for this humiliation
**“that you shall receive of the Lord the reward of inheritance”** — for this humiliation
**“the Lord Christ”**
• besides the masters also
• of those who rule
**“Serve ye”** — in those things which he commands
3.25:
**“For he that doth wrong, shall receive for that which he hath done wrongfully”** — it is so, as I have said: one must serve, and not give up because of the cruelty of masters, since whoever does wrong, whether servant or master,
**“and there is no respect of persons with God”** — no one will be spared because of his greater rank

4.1:
**“Masters, that which is just”**
• for service
• Good rulers serve, because they rule not from desire to dominate but from the duty of counselling and providing benefits.
**“do to your servants that which is just and equal”** — by nature, so that you may consider them men
**“knowing”** — and demand such things as you wish to be demanded of you
**“knowing that you also have a master in heaven”** — not powerless
4.2:
**“Be instant in prayer”** — I have admonished different groups individually; but now all together in common
**“watching”** — also by night, or not slothful
**“in it”**
• prayer
• remaining
**“with thanksgiving”** — for past things
4.3:
**“Praying”** — I say, be instant
**“Praying withal for us also, that God may open unto us a door of speech”** — A door, that is, may he make my mouth open, which is given for this, that the word may come forth from it. It is open when it speaks many and great things.
**“to speak the mystery of Christ”** — to set forth that which is secret concerning Christ, that is, his nativity, etc.
**“for which also I am bound”** — because I set forth the secrets of Christ
4.4: **“That I may make it manifest as I ought to speak.”** — so as to speak, that I may openly make manifest what is hidden from unbelievers, so constantly and discreetly as it behooves me to speak, because I am an apostle
4.5:
**“With wisdom”**
• which you have
• One must live cautiously among the faithless, lest they be scandalized, lest an occasion of blaspheming be given them and they be stirred up to persecute.
**“Walk”**
• make progress
• you yourselves also
**“towards them”** — to be enlightened
**“that are without”** — outside the Church
**“redeeming the time”**
• not hindering
• Redeeming the time, that is, preparing for them in some ways the opportunity of preaching.
4.6:
**“Let your speech”** — with the time taken into account
**“always in grace”**
• that it may be pleasing to the hearers
• or, in preaching grace, not the law
**“seasoned with salt”** — of wisdom
**“seasoned with salt, that”** — so
**“that you may know how you ought to answer every man”** — because one way for the unlearned, another for the learned and for other persons
4.7:
**“All the things that concern me”** — tribulations on every side, or those that do not reach to the soul
**“will make known to you”** — therefore there was no need to write
**“Tychicus”** — through him it is believed he sent the letter
**“our dearest brother”** — in faith
**“and faithful minister”** — in preaching
**“and fellow servant”** — in adversities
**“in the Lord”**
• for the Lord’s sake
• and this
4.8:
**“Whom I have sent to you for this same purpose”** — to something similar
**“That”** — that is
**“he may know”** — beware, therefore,
**“the things that concern you, and comfort your hearts”**
• against the evils of the world
• That he may know the things that concern you, etc. He who sees himself known takes more care than he who sees himself unknown.
4.9:
**“With Onesimus, a most beloved and faithful brother, who is one of you”** — Tychicus and Onesimus
**“All things that are done here, they shall make known to you”** — or “they shall make known”
4.10:
**“Aristarchus, my fellow prisoner, saluteth you”** — that is, a sharer and companion of my labours
**“and Mark, the cousin german of Barnabus, touching whom”** — Mark or Barnabas
**“you have received”**
• that he had departed, and therefore you should not receive him, but if he has now come
• Or you have received: that he returned to me, and therefore if he has come.
**“commandments”** — these things
4.11:
**“And Jesus, that is called Justus”** — greets you
**“who are of the circumcision”** — these same men affirm concerning grace
**“these only”** — from the Jews
**“are”** — only now
**“my helpers in the kingdom of God”** — by preaching
**“who have been”** — placed in tribulation
**“a comfort to me”** — supplying my place
4.12:
**“Epaphras saluteth you, who is one of you, a servant of Christ Jesus”** — do not read
**“who is always solicitous for you in prayers”** — for whom he prays for you that you may persevere
**“that you may stand perfect, and full in all the will of God”** — that you add nothing beyond what God wills
4.13:
**“For I bear him testimony”** — he is anxious
**“that he hath much labour for you”** — not only by praying but also by other means; be therefore anxious for you
4.14: **“Luke, the most dear physician, saluteth you”** — the evangelist
4.15: **“Salute the brethren who are at Laodicea, and Nymphas”** — especially which he receives as preachers
4.16:
**“And when this epistle shall have been read with you, cause that it be read also in the church of the Laodiceans”** — Cause that it be read also in the church of the Laodiceans, etc. Ambrose. From this place we understand that the apostle’s instructions are general, and that his epistles were written for the profit of all men.
**“and that you read that which is of the Laodiceans”** — which I sent to them, or which they themselves sent to me, that you may see here the answer to those questions
4.17:
**“And say to Archippus”**
• be anxious
• Ambrose. He admonishes their prelate through them, that he who has received their church to govern should be careful for them. The letter is written for the sake of the people, and therefore it is not addressed to the ruler.
**“which thou hast received in the Lord”** — in those things that are of the Lord
**“that thou fulfill it”** — That, as he ceased because of their disobedience, so he may gird himself for their correction.
4.18:
**“The salutation of Paul with my own hand”** — that you may know the letter was sent by me
**“Be mindful of my bands”**
• for which cause I suffer, because I preach only faith; or that they may suffer likewise; or that they pray for him; or that they minister necessities; or that they show themselves such men that he would not grieve to suffer for them
• Be mindful of my bands, etc. Before he sets down the salutation, he sends ahead an exhortation, saying: Be mindful, etc.

1.1:
**“Paul and Sylvanus and Timothy”**
• helpers in instructing those who also rejoiced equally in their progress
• Silvanus and Timothy. The greeting is written in their names, but the sense and words of this epistle are the apostle’s alone.
**“to the church of the Thessalonians, in God the Father”**
• gathered together
• that is, the Church, is in God working
**“Thessalonians”** — Thessalonica is the metropolis of Macedonia.
**“and the Lord Jesus Christ”** — his Son
**“grace to you and peace”** — Do not expound what has been expounded; do not do what has been done.
**“Grace be to you and peace”** — After his custom he sets a greeting first; and when that is done he gives thanks for their good things, recalling not only their faith and works, but also the manner of their conversion and their endurance of evils; and to provoke them the more to perseverance, he also interposes something of his own labours, and the truth of the gospel, and his prudent conduct among them, and with how great affection he desires to see them; then he beseeches that the wicked be restrained from luxury and idleness and curiosity, and he confirms that the dead will rise again. Toward the end there is moral instruction.
1.2:
**“We give thanks”** — he strengthens the good, first giving thanks for their progress
**“to God”** — because the good things that are in you are good, and from God, from whom all good things come
**“always for you all; making a remembrance of you”** — that you may persevere
**“in our prayers”** — kept
1.3:
**“without ceasing”** — at set hours
**“Being mindful”** — hence thanks
**“of the work of your faith”**
• of confession
• the proper work of faith is confession
**“and labour”** — for oneself and neighbours
**“charity”** — toward God and neighbour
**“and of the enduring”** — against evils
**“of the hope”**
• which the appearance of glory makes
• hope is not disappointed, because it belongs to the Lord, who is able and willing to fulfil it
• Of the one existing.
**“of our Lord Jesus Christ before God and our Father”** — Therefore be as certain as if you already saw it, and so he encourages them. Or before God, because it pleases him well, not for the sight of men.
1.4:
**“Knowing”** — for these we give thanks to God, because we know that he loved and chose by grace alone
**“brethren beloved of God, your election”**
• that you are chosen
• by this we know
1.5:
**“For our gospel hath not been unto you in word only”** — by the showing of words
**“but in power also”** — of miracles
**“and in the Holy Ghost”** — Because through me you received the gifts of the Spirit not sparingly, but in fullness.
**“and in much fulness”** — so that in nothing they may seem lesser than the churches of the Jews
**“as”** — so we know this divine thing, that you are chosen by God, as you see this visible thing
**“as you know what manner of men we have been”** — afflicted
**“among you”** — among you
**“for your sakes”** — for your salvation
**“what manner of men we have been for your sakes”** — By this also, that we suffered as an example to you, it is plain that God loved and chose you.
1.6:
**“And you became followers of us”** — we suffered as an example to you
**“and of the Lord”** — who endured the cross
**“followers of us and of the Lord”** — For they bore reproaches and injuries from their own citizens, in confidence of things to come. Whence they are called imitators of the apostles and of the Lord himself, because the Lord also suffered the same from the Jews, and the apostles, following the Lord, suffered persecutions rejoicing, because they were “accounted worthy to suffer reproach for the name” of the Lord.
**“receiving”** — you
**“the word in much tribulation”** — tribulation did not make (you) let it go
**“much”** — mine, that is, and yours
**“with joy of the Holy Ghost”** — which the Holy Spirit did
1.7: **“So that you were made a pattern to all that believe”** — who by your example are not afraid to confess
1.8:
**“For from you”**
• a pattern to all
• that is, from the example of your patience this came about, that others preach the word of God openly
**“For from you was spread abroad the word of the Lord, not only in Macedonia, and in Achaia, but also in every place”** — adjoining
**“your faith”** — not only the word, but the perfection of faith which is toward God alone, as it is in the martyrs
**“which is towards God, is gone forth, so that we need not”** — for stirring up others
**“to speak any thing”** — about you or about us
1.9:
**“For they themselves”** — all others
**“relate of us”** — for the commendation of your faith
**“relate of us, what manner”** — how afflicted we were
**“what manner of entering in we had unto you; and how”** — how vehemently
**“how you turned”** — yet
**“to God from idols”** — to truth from pretence, to one from many
**“to serve the living and true God”** — Converted from God, that you may serve. So purely, as is fitting for the living and true God, who is in truth. God also lives eternally. And in this service you should wait, and desire nothing else to be given to you than to see him himself according to his divinity, which the wicked will not see. Whence Scripture says: “Let the wicked be taken away, that he see not the glory of God.”
**“whom”** — the Son
**“Jesus”** — saviour
1.10:
**“and to wait for his Son from heaven”** — about to come
**“he raised from the dead”** — the Father
**“who delivered us from the wrath to come”**
• by this made the saviour of his own
• because in baptism he forgives sins, and in the future will free them also from eternal punishment

2.1:
**“For yourselves know, brethren, our entrance in unto you, that it was not in vain”**
• therefore I say what manner of entrance, and do not expound its quality, for they themselves
• easy
• That it was not in vain. This you know of it, that it was not in worldly prosperity, which is vain, but in much anxiety amid adversities, and therefore we had confidence not in ourselves, who are frail, but in the Lord. I say we, who suffered at Philippi before we came to you. Behold, we suffered before we came to you and after as well, so that it might not be possible to trust in ourselves, and so our labour be in vain. Or: it was not in vain, that is, for no evils did I cease to speak; but although we had suffered before and were anxious among you, we did not fear, but had confidence in God to speak to you. By these things related of himself, and by their good beginnings, he admonishes them to remain in patience.
2.2:
**“at Philippi”** — Ambrose. He suffered the affliction he here recalls because of the spirit of divination which he had cast out of a girl.
**“we had confidence in our God”** — so also do you
**“to speak unto you the gospel of God in much carefulness”**
• we had confidence in God
• the preaching by which we exhort
2.3:
**“For our exhortation was not of error”** — but of truth
**“For our exhortation”** — Here he seems to begin against false apostles, recalling the truth of the gospel, then about his own prudent conduct among them.
**“nor of uncleanness”** — such as carnal observances after Christ, or intercourse with women, and other things which some were preaching
**“nor in deceit”** — by fraud, cunning, hypocrisy
**“In deceit”** — Truth too is in deceit, when it is preached not for love of truth and the profit of the hearers, but so that glory or some other gain may be acquired.
2.4:
**“But as we were approved by God that the gospel should be committed”** — thus truly and with pure intention, as those proved and chosen by God, to the end that it might be believed
**“to us”** — as to the faithful
**“the gospel: even so we speak, not as pleasing men”** — nor do we have the appearance of pleasing
**“but God”** — that we please him, not men
**“But God”** — We may please. Augustine, in the Book of Sentences of Prosper. Which we cannot avoid unless he himself work in us. For what power to harm the love of human glory has, no one feels except him who has declared war on it; for if it is easy for anyone not to desire praise while it is denied, it is yet difficult not to be delighted by it when it is offered.
**“who proveth”** — makes them proved
**“our hearts”** — we do not seek to please men
2.5:
**“For neither have we used, at any time, the speech of flattery”**
• by which others please men
• For neither have we used, at any time, the speech of flattery, etc. Augustine. In this he touches the false apostles, who wished themselves to be commended rather than the teaching of God. But the Apostle, who sought glory not in the present but in the future, made himself humble so that the preaching of God might be exalted.
**“as you know”** — not in deceit
**“An occasion”** — I do not say in covetousness, but neither did I do or say anything in which there would be occasion of covetousness. Hence God is witness, who knows the heart. For this is not so plain.
**“God is witness”** — Augustine. So then, whoever you are of perverse or crooked heart: if you say “by God,” you swear; if you say “God is witness,” you do not swear? What is “by God” but “God is witness”? What is “God is witness” but “by God”? And what is it to swear, but to render a right to God, when you swear by God? To render a right to your own safety, when you swear by your safety? To render a right to your children, when you swear by your children? And what do we owe to God, to our safety, to our children, but the right of charity, of truth, and not of falsehood? Above all when it is by God, that is a true oath.
2.6:
**“Nor sought we”** — neither covetousness nor glory
**“of men”** — but from God only
**“we might have been”** — which the false apostles did not
**“as the apostles of Christ: but”** — we seek none of these
2.7:
**“Whereas”** — although
**“burdensome to you”** — that you should minister to us
**“we became little ones”**
• in this is noted labour and humility
• humble
**“in the midst of you”**
• to all
• We might have been burdensome, etc. He presses the cause of the false apostles so far as to say that he declined it, though he was free to require support to put down those who had neither the means nor the shame to ask. But he calls the due of apostolic power a burden because of the false apostles, who, usurping it unduly, demanded it importunately from the people.
**“as if”**
• and this for good
• so anxiously
**“a nurse should”** — in this is love, not for reward
**“cherish her children”** — not those of others
**“her children”** — Augustine. Because a woman sometimes nurses those of others for reward, not from love, but her own children from affection.
2.8:
**“So”** — so also we sought nothing from labour, except your salvation
**“desirous”** — in all labour
**“of you”** — not your own things
**“we would gladly impart unto you not only the gospel of God”** — for the assertion of the gospel
**“but also our own souls”** — for you
**“because you were become most dear unto us”**
• receiving the faith of God, well joining you to us
• We were made little ones, and as a nurse. For mindful.
2.9:
**“For you remember, brethren, our labour and toil”** — for there is also labour without weariness
**“working night and day”** — with our hands
**“lest we should be chargeable to any of you”** — that he might repel the false
**“we preached among you the gospel of God”** — so before, as after the conversion, that he might form them
2.10:
**“You are witnesses, and God also, how holily”** — to us
**“and justly”** — doing what is owed to a neighbour
**“and without blame”** — not doing what is not owed
**“we have been to you that have believed”** — we were present to you who believed, when they were still to be brought up
2.11:
**“As you know”** — so also you know this, as also this other
**“in what manner, as a father doth his children”** — with such affection
2.12:
**“entreating and comforting you”** — if anyone was forsaken by sin or otherwise
**“We testified”** — or we adjured them under the witness of the saints
**“that you would walk”** — by advancing
**“worthy of God”** — worthily of God, following in works his will
**“who”** — what you ought to do
**“hath called you”** — when you were turned away
**“Hath called”** — By the calling which is according to purpose.
**“unto his kingdom and glory”** — that you might be of his kingdom, which he would rule here and afterwards crown in glory
2.13:
**“Therefore”** — Because he called you, we give thanks. I say he called, because it appears from this that you received them quickly and firmly.
**“we also give thanks to God”** — because God did this
**“without ceasing: because, that when you had received of us the word of the hearing”** — by hearing alone
**“of God”** — from God
**“of the hearing of God”** — What we heard from God; or in which God is heard.
**“you received it not as the word of men”** — as if it were from wise men
**“but (as it is indeed) the word of God, who”** — God
**“As it is indeed the word of God”** — For they received the word with such devotion that they proved they had understood it to be the teaching of God.
**“who worketh in you”** — daily good works
**“that have believed”** — about to come through faith in him
2.14:
**“For you”** — and that which works in you shows the effect
**“are become followers of the churches of God which are in Judea, in Christ Jesus”**
• in the instruction of Christ himself
• For you, brethren, are become followers, etc. He said many things against the false apostles. Now, that they not be moved by their own or the apostles' tribulation.
**“for you also have suffered the same things”** — imitators in this
**“from your own countrymen, even as they have from the Jews”** — who are in Judea
2.15:
**“who”** — Jews
**“So bitter have they been”** — As if you ought to endure such harsh men.
**“and the prophets, and have persecuted us”** — the apostles of Christ
**“have persecuted us, and please not God”** — in which they think they please God, which is not so
**“and are adversaries to all men”** — to the salvation of all
2.16:
**“Prohibiting us to speak to the Gentiles, that they may be saved”** — therefore they do this
**“to fill up”**
• they fill up, so that he who is in filth may become filthier still
• That they may fill up. Haimo. God gave the Jews forty years after the passion for penance. When these had passed, since they would not believe, their sins were filled up. Whence the Lord: “Fill ye up then the measure of your fathers.” When the Apostle said this, Jerusalem was standing and their sins were not yet filled up, but they were filled up when the Romans came. Whence he adds: The wrath of God is come. The wrath is the coming of the Romans, which wrath lasts upon them as captives to the end of the world. Or it has come upon them, and will last to the end, because this temporal punishment has come first, the eternal will follow.
**“is come”** — so that they may be blinded
**“Is come”** — Therefore they always fill up their sins, because the wrath of God has come upon them so that they are blinded.
**“for the wrath”**
• vengeance
• or sin or temporal punishment
**“of God upon them”** — overwhelming
**“to”** — and this to
**“to the end”**
• eternal punishment; or at the end the remnant will be saved
• Or to the end, because at the end of the age the Jews will be converted.
2.17:
**“But we”** — you, having suffered much
**“But we, brethren, being taken away from you”** — your cause, not ours
**“for a short time”** — before we knew your constancy
**“in face”**
• away
• by speech
**“in sight”** — the presence of the body
**“not in heart”**
• with the affection of love
• By mouth, by sight, etc. Mouth and sight cease, because I cannot speak with you; but heart and care do not rest.
