• Hating it, etc. We ought to hate and rebuke not the body but its being stained, so that we may render it unstained and from carnal make it spiritual; and because this is to be accomplished not by the power of our own will but by the grace of God, it is rightly added: But to him, etc.
1.24:
**“Now to him who is able to preserve you without sin”**
• in all your works
• in the present
**“and to present you”** — in the future
**“before the presence of his glory”** — before the angels who behold the glory of God
**“spotless”** — from all filth
**“with exceeding joy”** — Those whom he above admonished to serve God in fear, he says are to be established in exultation; because the more fearful we are about our deeds in the present, the more we shall rejoice in the future over the reward appointed.
1.25:
**“only”**
• to him
• to him who alone is creator and saviour by sending the Son
**“God our Saviour through Jesus Christ our Lord, be glory and magnificence”**
• let him ascribe
• Glory, magnificence. If you have the glory of pure faith and conscience, and magnificence in working, and empire over weakness or over demons, and the power of resisting vices or tormentors, impute it to God and not to yourselves, who before the times, and in the present, and after all times, is glorious in essence, magnificent in works, ruling over the willing and the unwilling alike, and powerful, whom nothing resists.

1.1:
He sets out a prologue, and takes up the greeting in both.
First he puts in, as it were, a prologue to commend the work, by which he makes the hearer attentive, well-disposed and teachable in any way; then, the greeting made, he enters upon the narrative.
**“The Revelation”**
• this is the revelation
• Apocalypse, that is, the revelation of the present and future state of the Church. It is of Jesus Christ.
• Approach according to the letter: “Apocalypse of Jesus Christ”, as if to say carefully: attend to this revelation, because it was given by God to Christ, by Christ to the angel, by the angel to John, by John to the Churches.
• This is the revelation of Christ himself, which he received from God, that, his revelation being made manifest, he might make known to his servants the things which must shortly come to pass, namely, that labors may be ended and rewards given; as if he were to say: Attend carefully to this revelation, because it was given by God to Christ, and by Christ to the angel, and by the angel to John, and by John it was given to the churches.
**“The Revelation of Jesus Christ”** — He prepares the hearers to be well-disposed and attentive, as also there: “John to the seven churches which are in Asia.”
**“Jesus”** — of the Saviour
**“Christ”** — of the king
**“which God gave unto him”**
• to Christ
• that is, the Son
**“God”**
• God the Father, as owing nothing
• that is, the Father, that he might make it plain
• Which God gave unto him, etc. According to the man, he received it from the Father, and from the Word joined to him, and from the Holy Spirit.
**“known”** — by word and example
**“to make”** — for making plain
**“his servants”**
• to the humble, not to Jews or philosophers
• not to Jews, not to philosophers
• that they may suffer tribulations
**“which must come to pass”**
• concerning these things
• By this he signifies that those things which are to be ended quickly receive their term, and those which are to be begun by Christ, namely the rewards, take their beginning; quickly, because all present time, compared with eternity, is as it were the smallest moment of a single breath.
**“which must”** — As if to say: it is both unavoidable that they happen, and profitable that they happen.
**“shortly”**
• or in a short time
• brief labour, hastened glory.
• It behoves that they suffer tribulations quickly.
• He says “quickly” so that they prepare themselves and suffering is not grievous, since labours are quickly to be ended and rewards to be given.
• He says “quickly” so that they may prepare themselves, lest suffering be grievous; labours are to be ended quickly and rewards to be given.
• which must come to pass quickly, namely the tribulations to come and quickly to pass away, also the rewards to follow
• He rightly says “quickly”, because all time of this life, compared with eternity, is momentary. Whence: the same John in his epistle says, “Little children, it is the last hour.”
**“and signified”**
• that is, showed by a sign
• by figures and as it were seals, so that they may be hidden from the wicked
• he sealed it in the faithful.
**“And signified”** — God the Father to the Son, and the Son to John, under a seal, that is, under writing, so that there be no room for thieves to pervert it, and so that it may be more pleasing to the faithful if they follow it with practice.
**“sending by his angel”**
• having the person of Christ
• sometimes speaking in his own person, as when he forbids being worshipped; sometimes in the person of Christ
• That angel appeared in the figure of Christ to blessed John, and John himself holds the figure of the Church.
**“to his servant John”**
• not proud but humble
• of the Church
• John is interpreted ‘grace of God’, because whatever he was, he ascribed not to himself but to the grace of God.
1.2:
**“Who hath given testimony”** — He who bears witness to the very words of Christ spoken, both concerning the Word, that is, the divinity, and concerning the humanity of Jesus Christ.
**“who hath given testimony”** — Although John had written a bare gospel, yet he had given many testimonies, preaching the Son of God.
**“the word of God”**
• that is, to the divinity
• that is, to the divinity, when he said: “In the beginning was the Word.”
• The Son of God is called the Word because, just as the meaning is made plain by words, so God the Father was made known through the works done by the Person.
• Saying: “In the beginning was the Word,” and again, “the true light,” etc., and again, “And the Word was made flesh.” The Son of God is called the Word because through him the Father was made manifest in the world, either bodily, as John saw Christ suffering, or by the mind alone, that he had been with the Father before all things; but what John did, the Church also does daily, bearing testimony to the humanity and divinity of Christ.
**“The word of God”** — The Son is called ‘the Word of God’ because through him the Father was made manifest in the world.
**“and the testimony of Jesus Christ”**
• that is, the flesh
• according to human nature
**“in his”** — that is, concerning these
**“what things soever he hath seen.”** — either fleshly or spiritually
**“In his, what things soever he hath seen”** — Concerning those things he saw with the body, as suffering, or by the mind alone, as having been with the Father before all things.
1.3:
**“Blessed”** — is.
**“that readeth”**
• as the lettered
• explains it to others.
**“Blessed is he, that readeth”** — Christ gave to me; blessed, however, is he who has received it from me.
**“and heareth”**
• as the laity and learners
• retains.
**“the words of this prophecy”**
• of the book
• Blessed is he who reads and hears, etc. Because this is the Apocalypse of Jesus Christ, etc.
• Those alone are blessed who hear so as to store it in the mind, and store it in the mind so as to fulfil it in deed, and fulfil it in deed so that they may possess eternal life.
**“That readeth”** — That is, he who relates to others what he has heard, because many can hear from one reader. Or they will hear, and in this he marks the hearers, because they are many.
**“and”** — reader and hearer
**“keepeth those things which are written in it.”**
• but
• by doing
**“Keepeth those things”**
• Thus I say, if he keeps them: “For not the hearers of the law are just, but the doers.”
• He who does not violate the faith of Christ and of the Church, and fears the threats and seeks the promises, is truly blessed, because the delay of labour is not long, and the rewards are near.
**“for the time is at hand.”** — namely of judgment.
1.4:
**“John to the seven churches”**
• To the seven churches and to the universal, because all things were made in seven days, and through seven days the totality of our life is willed. Or, literally, because there were seven cities in Asia, over whose churches he himself presided.
• writes.
• God gave to Christ, Christ to John, and John to the churches; or through seven, the whole Church, because seven signifies universality, or because they are enlightened by the sevenfold Spirit.
**“The seven churches”** — Principally to those over whom he had been appointed teacher, and by likeness to others.
**“which are in Asia”**
• that is, exaltation
• For Asia is interpreted as exaltation.
• all churches are in exaltation.
• Asia is interpreted as exaltation, and this signifies that the churches are in an exaltation of virtues.
• Asia is interpreted as exaltation, which signifies the Church exalted by virtues and raised above the riches which it spurns.
• This Asia is not the great one, that namely which is called “the third part of the world,” but a certain province where there were seven cities, and seven churches with seven bishops.
• Asia Minor is part of greater Asia, containing seven cities of which Ephesus is the metropolis. Paul preached the gospel in this lesser Asia, but afterwards, in the division of the apostles, John obtained it.
• Ephesus, the metropolitan see of all Asia, in which John presided.
**“In Asia”** — Asia is exaltation. The Church therefore is now in exaltation of virtues, or formerly of vices.
**“Grace”**
• be
• forgiveness of sins
**“and peace”** — rest from vices
**“Grace be unto you and peace”** — In the greeting he prepares the hearers to be well-disposed and attentive, as also in the prologue.
**“from him”** — that is, from Christ
**“that is”** — now in the elect
**“and that was”**
• with the Father
• for judgment
**“and from the seven spirits”**
• from the sevenfold Spirit, who indeed is one in nature, manifold in the distribution of graces
• And from the seven spirits. Spirit means the same as charity; whence forgiveness of sins is attributed to the Spirit, and other gifts which are gifts of the whole Trinity, so that we understand the Trinity to work from love alone.
• Who is, who was, etc. Eternally, though born in time, now unchangeable through his humanity, and once corruptible, such he is to come, although now he does not appear such.
• He is silent about the person of the Father, because no one had misunderstood God the creator; he sets forth the persons of the Son and the Holy Spirit, concerning whom all heresies arise in the churches.
**“which are before his throne”**
• that he may enlighten those in whom God sits.
• The thrones of God are the angels and holy men in whose minds the spirit rests through faith. Whence: “The soul of the just is the seat of wisdom.”
**“his throne”** — They are his angels and holy men, in whom God now sits and judges, so that he may not judge in the future.
1.5:
**“And from Jesus Christ”**
• about to say more, he repeats “of Christ” according to his humanity.
• Therefore he repeats “of Jesus Christ” because more is said of him; or, that he may be known as God in heaven who was called man and Christ on earth.
**“who is the faithful witness”**
• who did not deny that he is God, even in the face of impending death.
• that is, the true one, to whom he bore witness to the Father, saying: “The Father that abideth in me, he doth the works.”
**“the first begotten”**
• or faithful witness.
• First-begotten, etc. He says this against those who despaired at the death of Christ, like those who said: “But we hoped that it was he that should have redeemed Israel.”
**“of the dead”**
• of our works on the day of judgment, when he will say: “You saw me hungry and thirsty,” and “Come, you blessed of my Father,” etc.
• Therefore, because he rose from the dead so as not to die again, and so that others, namely his own, might follow him in this.
**“Of the dead”** — Who should not terrify you, because he has risen and is impassible; or, first of those who die to themselves, because he committed no sin.
**“and the prince of the kings of the earth.”**
• ruling over earthliness.
• That is, of the saints, who by good morals are kings on earth. All the elect are called kings of the earth who do not let vices rise up in them, but rule over them as just men.
**“The prince of the kings of the earth”** — Prince of earthly powers, able to remove them, and, for the benefit of his own or of the saints, allowing the wicked to serve.
**“who hath loved us”**
• especially preachers.
• suffering for us while we were worthless.
**“Who hath loved us”** — He commends the person of the Son, who made this revelation to John through the angel, as if to say: believe this revelation and the open exhortation which Christ made manifest, who suffered for us and rose again.
**“and washed us”**
• because by love alone he washed us.
• making us just, by forgiving sins.
**“from our sins”** — original or actual.
**“From our sins”** — Original or actual, not his but ours, because he did not sin.
**“in his own blood”**
• not of a calf, not of a ram, as in the old law.
• because when we were stained with sins, he washed us in his passion, so that he presents to himself a Church not having a spot.
• who can do all things with the Father.
1.6:
**“Kingdom”** — Powerful to resist vices, and offering ourselves to God for ourselves and for our brethren.
**“and priests”** — according as he is man.
**“to God and his Father.”** — according as he is God.
**“To him be glory”** — therefore, that he may be praised.
**“and empire”** — that you may obey him.
**“for ever and ever. Amen.”** — Amen is an adverb of affirmation among the Hebrews, as if to say: it is true that glory is due to him in heaven from the angels and on earth from the saints.
1.7:
**“Behold, he cometh with the clouds”**
• of heaven.
• That is, to the saints who dwell in heaven in mind, who were the clouds by raining upon others and working miracles. Or literally, for thus he ascended.
**“Behold, he cometh”** — And truly you ought to glorify, because he it is who is to come to reward. With the clouds, that is, with the saints, who were clouds, raining down doctrine upon others and working miracles. Or as he ascended in a cloud, so he will come in a cloud, by which we understand the clemency of God, because to the good it is refreshment and illumination, but to the wicked terror and blinding; which was also signified by the cloud by which the children of Israel were led out of Egypt.

**“and every eye shall see him”**
• good and bad.
• as much the good as the bad.
**“And every eye shall see him”** — Another translation has “every land shall see him,” as if to say: they shall see him such as the wicked did not believe would come.
**“Every eye”** — The good shall see him so that they may rejoice, the wicked so that they may be confounded.
**“and they also that pierced him”**
• that they may be the more tormented
• That is, the Jews who crucified him, with tongue and will.
**“and all the tribes of the earth shall bewail themselves because of him.”**
• all the earthly and given over to vices.
• That is, those who desire earthly things, because they are powerless to resist his rule, or are pleased; that is, they will grieve to see... founded upon him....
**“shall bewail”** — Or they shall dash themselves against him, unable to resist his rule, like a stone and earthen vessels; or they shall bewail themselves, that is, they shall grieve, looking upon those who are founded upon him, because they will not grieve so much for the torment itself as because they will be cast out from such fellowship.
**“Even so. Amen.”**
• and amen.
• which is to be confirmed by every tongue.
**“Even so. Amen”** — By these two adverbs, one of which is Greek, namely “etiam,” the Gentiles are signified; by “amen,” which is Hebrew, the Jews, who will all see God in judgment.
1.8:
**“I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end, saith the Lord God,”**
• Lord, I say.
• In the beginning with God.
**“I am”** — Truly he will come; and because he himself promises that he will come, or having given the greeting, he makes them attentive, as if to say: do not believe this from me, but from Christ himself.
**“Alpha, the beginning”** — Before whom no one is, or from whom all things began.
**“Omega, the end”** — After whom no one is, or in whom all things will be ended.
**“who is, and who was, and who is to come, the Almighty.”**
• to judgment.
• he says this after the manner of the prophets.
1.9:
**“I John”**
• from the person.
• Having finished the greeting, he goes on to the narration, setting down four things: the person, the place, the cause of that place, and the time, which serve to commend this revelation.
• As if to say: I know that you are afflicted, but by the example of Christ you should suffer patiently, so that you may be partakers of his kingdom.
**“your brother”** — the humility of the master.
**“and your partner”** — or: companion.
**“in tribulation, and in the kingdom, and patience in Christ Jesus”**
• by the example of Christ.
• Brother, partner, etc. In Christ. In the unity of faith, and because of that faith I was afflicted, as were others, whereby I patiently endured to arrive at the kingdom, having Christ as the example in all things.
**“was”** — was banished.
**“in the island, which is called Patmos,”**
• the place.
• Patmos, that is, a strait, namely tribulation, in which heavenly things are rather opened to the faithful.
• The Church is compared to an island, because as an island is battered by sea storms, so the Church is afflicted by the persecutions of the sea, that is, of worldly men.
**“for the word of God, and for the testimony of Jesus Christ”**
• cause
• For the word and the testimony, etc. That is, on account of the testimony given to his divinity and humanity.
1.10:
**“I was in the spirit”** — “in ecstasy of mind”
**“on the Lord's day”** — in hope of the future resurrection through the resurrection of Christ
**“day.”**
• time
• in faith of the Lord
**“On the Lord's day”** — The quality of things is usually marked by the time: as Abraham saw the angel at midday, for the fervour of faith; Lot in the evening, for the destruction of Sodom; Adam after midday; Solomon, who was not going to keep wisdom back, received it by night.
**“And I heard”** — I knew
**“behind me a great voice”** — because of revelation of future or great things
**“I heard behind me a voice”** — He hears behind him because, while he was led out from present things and stretched himself forward in true contemplation, he was warned to look back at others. Or he hears behind him because this was foretold by the law and the prophets; he understands the same thing.
**“as of a trumpet”**
• by which one is stirred to war
• because they are through the mouths of preachers, who are the trumpets
1.11:
**“saying”** — or saying
**“to me: What thou seest,”** — what you are about to see or already see
**“write in a book”**
• store it in your mind, or literally
• What thou seest, write, etc. A common admonition is given to John, which charged him to send to the churches of Asia in common, and through them all the other churches are to be understood; this common admonition continues as far as “And to the angel of Ephesus,” etc. Whether John saw this vision all alike and at one glance, or at different times, the angel could bestow either on him.
**“and send”** — here, then
**“to the seven churches which are in Asia”**
• that is, to
• that is, to all, because, as has been said, it expresses the whole body of the faithful
**“to Ephesus”**
• or to Ephesus and Smyrna, etc.
• that is, my will or my counsel, by which name every church is generally called Ephesus, in which is God’s will through faith and spirit and charity, etc.
**“Ephesus”** — “My will” is interpreted either as “deep fall” or as “counsel”.
**“and to Smyrna”**
• “song”
• that is, the song of those chosen
**“and to Pergamus”**
• “division of horns”
• that is, division of horns; the horns are of the body of Christ and of the devil. The body of Christ is the saints; the body of the devil is its members, among whom he makes divisions in the Church
**“and to Thyatira”** — enlightened
**“and to Sardis”** — “beginning of beauty”
**“and to Philadelphia”**
• that is, saving the inheritance of the Lord
• keeping, or saving
**“and to Laodicea.”** — lovable tribe
1.12:
**“And”** — therefore
**“I turned”**
• That is, I had a memory of those under me.
• I turned, etc. And therefore, because I heard the voice, I turned, etc.
• That is, I had a memory of those under me, or namely for their good.
**“that I might see”** — that I might understand
**“the voice”** — spiritual
**“that spoke with me.”** — because I turned
**“And turning I saw seven candlesticks”** — That is, the seven churches, burning and enlightened by the wisdom of the divine Word. As gold is proved by fire and, stretched by blows, is made a candlestick, so the Church, purified by tribulations and stretched by the acts of temptations, is perfected in longanimity. The Church is figured by gold because the divine wisdom shines in her; she has a lamp because she shines both by the word and is in Christ.
**“Seven candlesticks”** — That is, seven churches burning and enlightened by the wisdom of the divine Word.
**“golden”** — As gold tested by fire and beaten out is made into a candlestick, so the Church, purged by tribulations and stretched out by the blows of temptations to patience, will be perfected.
**“golden,”** — If it has a voice in the mouth and not in the work, it is indeed a candlestick, but not a golden one.
1.13:
**“and in the midst”** — that is, in common, because God offers himself to all, that is, he is ready to help.
**“seven golden candlesticks, one like to the Son of man”**
• he shows in himself the head that he demands from his own
• Or like the son of man, because he appeared not with sin, but in the likeness of sinful flesh.
• Christ, in whom are all things necessary for the governance of the Church.
**“one like to the Son of man”** — That is, an angel in the person of Christ, who is now not the son of man but like him, because “now dieth no more.”
**“clothed with a garment down to the feet”**
• that is, with the priestly vestment; by “poderes” understand the Church, with which God is clothed, which is talaris, that is, reaching down to the ankles, namely to the feet. That is, until the end of the world.
• Podere, that is, with the priestly vestment, that is, with the flesh in which he offered himself, and daily offers, presenting himself to God the Father. Or poderis is the Church, with which God is clothed as with a tunic that reaches to the feet, because it will last until the end of the world.
**“and girt about the paps with a golden girdle.”**
• with the girdle of charity, because he keeps love
• that is, girded in his heart with the girdle of charity
**“Girt about the paps”** — Daniel saw a man girded about the loins in the Old Testament, because there carnal things are restrained; here at the breasts, because in the New Testament even thoughts are judged.
1.14:
**“head”** — God
**“And his head and his hairs were white”**
• Christians
• That is, the whiteness of the innocence of the Son of God; or let us understand the head of the divinity, and the head as Christ himself, of whom Paul says: “The head of the man is Christ”; the white hairs are the perfections of the virtuous, who cleave more closely to their head, Christ, because they follow the simplicity and innocence of Christ their head.
**“his hairs were”** — That is, the saints made thin and cleaving to the head itself, or his thoughts.
**“as white wool”**
• pure charity
• that is, a garment against cold and vices
**“As white wool”** — Or as white wool is fit to take on any colours, so the saints are fit for tribulations.
**“and as snow.”**
• immortality with glory, more glorious than every creature
• By snow the newness of the resurrection is signified. Whence the Lord, on the mountain, showed the brightness of the resurrection, commending the snow.
**“Snow”** — Snow: the brightness of immortality, because it is whiter than every creature.
**“and his eyes”**
• That is, the faithful in the Church, who ought to see on both sides.
• That is, the apostles.
**“as a flame of fire,”** — The eyes of the Lord signify the seven gifts of the Holy Spirit, of which it is said through Zacharias: “Upon one stone are seven eyes”; and they are well called fiery because they kindle us to the love of God and are enlightened by divine thought. And the eyes are the spiritual men themselves in the Church.
**“Eyes”** — That is, the gifts of the Holy Spirit, which are Christ’s, of him who has and gives them. They belong to the Church that receives them, and they enlighten and make burn. Or the eyes are the spiritual men themselves in the Church, or the divine precepts.
1.15:
**“And his feet like unto”** — not to anyone but to
**“And his feet”** — That is, the last of the faithful, who through many shakings will not keep their former nature, like orichalcum, which is often set on fire and takes a better colour.
**“like unto fine brass, as in a burning furnace.”** — That is, the preachers, who are cleansed by tribulation like fine brass, because, as fine brass is brought forth from copper in the furnace of many cleansings to the color of gold, so also the saints are burned by the tribulation of the wicked, that they may be proved like the purest gold... of the many peoples preaching the word of God.
**“in a burning furnace”** — In another translation it is read: 'of Lebanon orichalcum', by which it is shown that in that region where the Lord was crucified, that tribulation will be most strong.
**“And his voice”** — That is, his preaching has the force of water, because it cleanses; or the voice which many peoples have already received, who are compared to water because of their flowing, you ought all the more to be steadfast. Or the voice giving many waters, that is, of graces; whence the voice follows.
1.16:
**“And he had in his right hand”** — That is, in eternal life.
**“seven stars”** — That is, the bishops of the seven churches, all preachers preaching ... eternity ... into the four parts of the world.
**“Stars”** — Stars: bishops, who ought to shine for others by word and by example of life; who, even if they have sinned, are called stars according to what they were appointed to be; whom he holds in his right hand, that is, in the greater gifts, which are signified by the right hand.
**“And from his mouth”**
• That is, from the preachers.
• Whence: “For it is not you that speak, but the Spirit of your Father that speaketh in you.”
**“From his mouth”** — That is, the preaching came out from the insinuation, which cuts both: in the Old Testament carnal works, in the New, lusts.
**“sword”** — That is, the word of God.
**“came out a sharp two edged sword.”**
• through preachers or the Scriptures
• because it divides the good from the wicked
**“And his face”**
• The just shall shine like him, that is, they will become like him.
• was
**“as the sun shineth in his power.”**
• The just shall shine like him, that is, they will become like him.
• As the sun shines in its power, that is, at noon without clouds. Or as Christ himself in the resurrection. Or when he will be fixed for eternity.
1.17:
**“And when”** — because
**“And when I had seen”** — Behold, John, who seemed to stand, having seen the Lord, fell as dead, because every holy man, the higher he raises himself to contemplate the divinity, the lower he falls within himself, because in comparison with God his own greatness, which he had believed in, is easily despised. Hence it is that Abraham, having seen the Lord, knew himself to be dust and ashes. So also Job: “With the hearing of the ear I have heard thee,” etc.
**“I had seen him”** — That is, I had understood his greatness.
**“I fell”** — Who cast aside concern for humanity, in the likeness of the last of the faithful.
**“I fell at his feet”** — That is, in comparison with that humanity I counted myself as nothing.
**“as dead”**
• although dead to the world, yet living to God
• Dead to the world, alive to God; or desiring nothing of earthly things.
**“he laid his right hand upon me”**
• That is, over the powers of my humanity.
• That is, his help, though the strengthening Spirit.
**“his right hand”** — Namely the Holy Spirit strengthening, that is, his help.
**“saying:”** — Admonishing me through the Scriptures.
**“Fear not. I am the First and the Last,”** — Beginning and end.
1.18:
**“And alive”**
• True life according to the divinity.
• Eternally.
**“Fear not”** — To suffer for me tribulations and death, because I, who had no need on my own account, since I am the first and the last, was dead and am living.
**“and was”** — According to the flesh.
**“dead”**
• On account of you.
• According to the body, for you.
**“and behold I am living”** — After the resurrection.
**“I am living”** — But you should not be terrified on that account, because I have plainly risen and shall die no more.
**“and have”** — And therefore I shall not allow you to be tempted beyond what you are able to bear, because I have power over the devil and over his members.
**“the keys”** — Power.
**“of death”**
• That is, of the devil.
• From the devil.
**“and of hell.”**
• From his ministry.
• He who has the key of any house lets in whom he will, and drives back from entering the house whom he will. Therefore he possesses the keys of death and of hell, because he frees from the damnation of everlasting death whom he will, and whom he will he justly allows to remain in the same peril of damnation.
• Of death and of hell. The devil is death, because he is the cause of sin; that is, of death; his ministers are hell, in whom he has a place.
1.19:
**“Write therefore the things which thou hast seen”**
• As the passion and the resurrection.
• That is, the past tribulations.
**“and which are”**
• The present tribulations and present help.
• Present.
**“and which must be done hereafter.”**
• That is, the tribulations which the saints will suffer.
• This is.
• Which must be done, etc. In the last of the faithful, by whose example these ought greatly to be encouraged.
1.20:
**“The mystery”**
• Or: mystery.
• Sacrament, that is, mystery, where one thing is seen and another is understood.
**“the seven stars, which thou sawest in my right hand, and”** — These are.
**“the seven golden candlesticks. The seven stars are the angels”**
• The angel opens the mysteries of certain figures; he does not open all of them, lest there be an entrance for thieves into the Sacred Scriptures.
• The angel opens the allegory in part, so as to teach that it ought to be sought everywhere.
**“the seven churches; and the seven candlesticks are the seven churches”** — This first vision is about the correction of the churches.

2.1:
**“And”** — John.
**“Unto the angel”** — That is, he writes to the bishop, at whose hand he requires the sins of the subjects, and without whose consent John himself does not presume to judge the subjects.
**“the angel”** — Note that in all these he speaks not only to the bishop but also to those committed to him.
**“Ephesus”** — Ephesus, according to the part of those who persevere well, is interpreted “will,” in whose works God delights; concerning them he proposes this, that by their example those who had fallen may be corrected; according as Ephesus is interpreted “counsel,” that is, “needing counsel,” or “deep fall,” or “my will.”
**“These things saith”** — although they have sinned, he still does not release them
**“who holdeth the seven stars in his right hand,”** — as one dividing gifts, or not yet at rest
**“seven”** — He begins singular admonitions, which, though singular, can also be universal, according to the different members of any church.
**“who walketh in the midst of the seven golden candlesticks”** — because they are not yet such that he may rest in them
2.2:
**“I know”** — that is, I approve
**“thy works, and thy labour”** — tribulation
**“and thy patience”** — because you do not murmur about the reward being delayed
**“and how thou canst not bear them that are evil”** — acting inhumanely against you
**“canst not bear”** — By the force of humanity. Or, you cannot bear the wicked without amending or expelling them.
**“and thou hast tried them”** — that is, you tested their teaching
**“hast tried them”** — Only those who are inside the church are tested.
**“who say they are apostles”** — sent by God, so that they may deceive more easily
**“and are not, and hast found them liars”** — by their evil preaching and evil life
2.3:
**“And thou hast patience”** — in the evils that they, being joined with them, inflict through earthly powers
**“and hast endured for”** — that is, through
**“hast endured for my name”** — Or, you did this not for human praise, but for the sake of my name to be glorified.
**“and hast not fainted.”** — this pertains to counsel
**“and hast not fainted”** — It notes that the cause of human failing would have been, had not help come first.
2.4:
**“But I have somewhat against thee”**
• contrary to the crown
• But I have somewhat, etc. Either the bishop in his own person, as to his feeling of weariness at the vices in his subjects; or the subjects, as to love of earthly things.
• Eli the priest was good and yet was condemned, because he was unwilling to correct his sons.
2.5:
**“Be mindful”** — for indeed it is against you
**“therefore from whence thou art fallen”** — from the fellowship of the faithful
**“and do penance”** — worthy fruits of penance
**“and do the first works”** — works similar to the first
**“Or else”** — but
**“I come to thee, and will move thy candlestick”** — that I may slay them in soul and body
**“will move thy candlestick”** — I will take away the virtues and gifts of the Holy Spirit through which the candlesticks are established.
**“out of its place”** — that is, in what is interpreted as will.
**“except thou do penance”** — here again, will.
2.6:
**“But this thou hast”**
• namely.
• Although this is against you, do not despair, because you have something good.
**“thou hatest the deeds of the Nicolaites, which I also hate”**
• that you hate it because you see that I too hate it.
• The deeds of the Nicolaites, that is, the common use of women and the eating of things sacrificed to idols.
**“of the Nicolaites”** — Nicolaus: a foolish people, that is, the Gentiles ignorant of God, openly using wives, who eat things sacrificed to idols and believe that Jove reigns; also heretics, foolish before God, to whom error is imputed as the worship of idols, and who commit fornication, serving the uncleanness of the flesh; and the foolish Jews; the foolish false Christians too, who, given to earthly things, worship the world.
2.7:
**“He, that hath an ear”**
• what I say to one I say to all.
• He that hath an ear, etc. Why is it to be heard? Because to the persevering Christ is the tree of life, being shade and strength, and giving fruit, that is, his body and blood, both here and especially in the future.
**“let him hear”** — the divine understanding.
**“what the Spirit”** — that is, the Trinity.
**“saith to the churches. To him that overcometh, I will give to eat of the tree of life, which is in the paradise of God.”** — in the garden of delights, that is, the Church.
**“my God”** — according to the humanity.
2.8:
**“And to the angel of the church of Smyrna write”** — Smyrna: Smyrna is interpreted as song, or as myrrh; also song, in which he delights; myrrh is so bitter that it even preserves bodies from putrefaction.
**“These things saith the First”** — He describes Christ as such as can avail for the consolation of those on whom tribulations are brought. He says: I am the first, as if to say: do not fail, for I, so great, suffered death for you, from which I rose again, that you also may expect the same.
2.9:
**“I know thy tribulation and thy poverty”** — according to the letter.
**“but thou art rich”** — in the hope of reward.
**“and thou art blasphemed”** — “No plague is more effective than a domestic enemy.”
**“by them that”** — the heap of misery, when the tribulated are defamed.
**“say they are Jews”** — confessing.
**“and are not”** — “If they were the children of Abraham, they would do the works of Abraham.”
**“but”** — but yet.
**“are the synagogue of Satan”** — that is, the congregation of Satan, that is, of the adversaries.
2.10:
**“Fear none of those things which thou shalt suffer”** — whether I shall suffer.
**“Behold, the devil will cast some of you into prison”** — he puts prison for every tribulation.
**“some of you”** — Here it is plain that it is understood not of one alone but of many.
**“that you may be tried”** — that you may be tried, that is, that you may be proved, or held in contempt by the devil and his members.
**“and you shall have tribulation ten days”**
• but, whatever they bring upon you, be
• Ten days, that is, the time of that war, for God, sending his own to battle, arms them with the decalogue. Or ten days, that is, all this time in which through seven days battle is waged against the three principal vices: avarice, covetousness, vainglory.
2.11:
**“He, that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith to the churches”** — because
**“He that shall overcome, shall not be hurt by the second death”** — that is, hell.
**“by the second death”** — The first death of the soul is in sins; the second is in punishments. The first death is of the body, when it is dissolved; the second, when it will be condemned in judgment.
2.12:
**“And to the angel of the church of Pergamus”**
• Pergamus is interpreted as ‘division of horns.’
• by horns is signified ‘some fight,’ so that in this Church the evil part attacked the good.
• so that they are divided from the wicked, keeping the unity of the Church.
**“of the church write: These things, saith he, that hath the sharp two edged sword”** — the romphea, the sword sharp on both sides, is the Lord’s sentence by which he will condemn the wicked in body and in soul.
**“sharp two edged”** — The two-edged rompheam (sword) requires that they have this sword in the choosing of the good and the rejecting of the wicked.
2.13:
**“I know where thou dwellest”** — in the midst of a perverse nation.
**“where”** — that is, there.
**“the seat of Satan is”** — that is, the congregation of Satan, that is, of the adversary.
**“and thou holdest fast”** — against disputers.
**“my name, and hast not denied my faith”**
• for some tribulation.
• tribulation is an illumination to the just.
**“Hast not denied”** — Tribulation is illumination to the just, correction to the stubborn, blinding to the obstinate.
**“Even in those days”** — in which you did this.
**“Antipas”** — who is.
**“my faithful witness”** — that is, he was a martyr.
**“who was slain among you”** — labour by his example.
**“where Satan dwelleth”** — as if: the conclusion, because they killed him.
2.14:
**“But”** — but although steadfast in this.
**“I have”** — if you be corrected.
**“against thee a few things”** — or in a few.
**“because thou hast there”** — you suffer, you do not expel.
**“them that hold the doctrine of Balaam”**
• ‘vain people.’
• Balaam, that is, heretics who teach earthly princes how they may overthrow those who see God. Or Balaam, that is, demons who teach the flesh how to deceive souls that see God.
**“who taught Balac”** — ‘crushing.’
**“to cast a stumblingblock before the children of Israel”** — to delight in various things.
**“to eat, and to commit fornication”** — with a demon, bodily or spiritually.
2.15:
**“So”** — likewise.
**“hast thou also them that hold”** — against those who attack.
**“the doctrine of the Nicolaites”**
• of heretics.
• in many copies it is added: which I hate
• Nicholas was a certain man who took a wife and put her away on account of avarice, and therefore taught others that they should have wives in common.
**“The doctrine of the Nicolaites”** — For he therefore repeats concerning the Nicolaites, to invite to penance, which he did not do above.
2.16:
**“In like manner”** — about this one as about that one
**“do penance”** — because
**“if not”**
• if you have done in some respect less than you ought
• if you have done less in some respect
**“I will come to thee quickly”** — who do not correct
**“and will fight against them”**
• that is, I will overcome
• that is, I will condemn them
**“with the sword of my mouth”** — that is, I will convict those fornicators of having sinned, saying: “Go into everlasting fire.”
2.17:
**“He, that hath an ear”** — of the heart
**“let him hear what the Spirit saith to the churches: To him that overcometh, I will give the hidden manna”** — another translation has “pearl”
**“manna”** — The eternal glory, of which all will say: What is this? “Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard.”
**“hidden”** — or myself, who was hidden in the manna
**“And”** — meanwhile
**“I will give him a white counter”**
• elsewhere “white”
• that is, making them white
• That is, a solid body, or himself bright, white with virtues and the hope of immortality.
**“A white counter”** — In Daniel the stone was cut out without hands. In Proverbs, a most pleasing jewel is the expectation of one who waits.
**“and in the counter, a new name”** — that is, “Christian”
**“new”** — in which nothing of the old Adam
**“written”** — in such a body
**“Written”** — By five letters, namely five wounds, it was shown in his body on the cross that he was a martyr.
**“which no man knoweth”**
• To what end? That he may be invited by this name.
• By the force of which, to what end, he is invited through this name
**“And in the counter, a new name written, which no man”** — Or, I add martyrdom beyond baptism, the power of which the hypocrite does not understand, who suffers for the praise of men.
**“but he that receiveth it”** — Christ himself, or the evangelical doctrine
**“But he that receiveth it”** — He who fulfils it by deed, for “he who saith that he knoweth him, and keepeth not his commandments, is a liar”
2.18:
**“And to the angel of the church of Thyatira”**
• is interpreted “enlightened,” or “living sacrifice”
• Thyatira: sacrifice; whence: “Present your bodies a living sacrifice.” Or Thyatira: enlightened; and by it is signified the whole Church enlightened through Christ, who is “the true light, which enlighteneth every man that cometh into this world.” Or Thyatira: inflamed, because in this Church some are truly inflamed and some are wicked.
**“write: These things saith the Son of God, who hath his eyes like to a flame of fire, and his feet”**
• whom it is necessary to imitate
• that is, the last faithful
2.19:
**“I know”** — that is, I have received
**“I know thy works, and thy faith, and thy charity”** — The Son of God has the gifts of the Holy Spirit, that is, he gives to whom he wills or takes away. Therefore let those who have already received those gifts see to it that they do not lose them through consent to evil. Or the order of charity and faith is reversed, not because charity is prior to faith.
**“thy works, and thy faith, and thy charity”** — First faith, from faith charity, from charity good works.
**“and thy ministry”** — in almsgiving
**“and thy patience”** — because from these comes tribulation
**“and thy last works”** — in all adversities
**“thy last works which are more than the former”** — because the untutored Church comes from lesser things to perfection
2.20:
**“But I have against thee a few things: because thou sufferest”** — you do not excommunicate
**“the woman Jezabel”** — soft and wanton
**“Jezabel”**
• “Flow of blood,” or “flowing,” or “dunghill”: as women at the time of their monthly course suffer a flow of blood, so the reprobate who conceives evil, as soon as it is time, brings it to completion; and when afterwards the flame is increased, he is called wholly flowing; and when he draws it into habit, he spreads a stench far and wide. And these are the three dead raised: one in the house, another outside the gate, the third in the sepulchre.
• The wife of Achab, or of this bishop; and through her are understood heretics who pretend to be good, but lead into softness and wantonness.
**“who calleth herself”** — according as she is said
**“a prophetess, to teach, and to seduce”** — in fact
**“my servants”** — imitating themselves
**“to commit fornication, and to eat of things sacrificed to idols”** — with women or with the demon
**“To commit fornication”** — Fornication is said to be fourfold: in the mind, “whosoever shall look on a woman to lust after her”; in the act itself; in the love of earthly things; in the worship of idols.
2.21: **“And I gave her a time that she might do penance”** — and because she is not willing to repent
2.22:
**“Behold, I will cast her”**
• by blinding
• that is, I will cast her with her works into perdition
**“into a bed”**
• into security of sinning
• Another translation puts “mourning” for “bed,” by which he designated eternal misery.
**“Into a bed”** — Into security in sinning, or the bed of sorrow.
**“and they that commit adultery with her”** — that is, they become like her by the works for which they will be punished
2.23:
**“And I will kill her children with death”** — namely condemning all her followers with eternal punishment
**“And all the churches shall know”** — in the future they will know in fact, what here they know only by faith
**“that I am he that searcheth the reins and hearts”** — punishing carnal desires and evil thoughts
**“and”** — they will know that
**“I will give to every one of you according to your works”** — good things to the good, evil things to the evil
**“your works”**
• or “their own”
• I do this to them.
2.24:
**“But to you I say”** — a change of person; an interposed sentence
**“And to the rest who are at Thyatira”** — from among you
**“Whosoever have not this doctrine”** — that there is no salvation without the law
**“and who have not known”** — have approved
**“the depths”** — pride
**“of Satan, as they say”** — certain men who went out of Judea
**“I will not put”**
• that I would send
• I will not put. Certain false teachers were terrifying them, because the Lord was still to send greater tribulations than they had suffered; against this he says that he will not send them, or legal observances.
**“upon you any other burthen”** — of the Old Law
2.25:
**“Yet”** — although they say this, “yet”
**“that which you have, hold fast”** — as if he said: labour that you not lose what he has already given, but strive for greater things
**“till I come”** — to repay
2.26:
**“And he that shall overcome”** — not yielding to them
**“and”** — and with this
**“and keep my works unto the end”** — of his life, or even to perfection
**“I will give him power”** — in this age
**“over the nations”** — living as Gentiles
2.27:
**“And he shall rule them with a rod of iron”** — with inflexible justice
**“and as the vessel of a potter they shall be broken”** — some so that they utterly perish, some so that they are changed for the better
**“As I also have received of my Father”** — according to his humanity
2.28:
**“and I will give him”** — in the future
**“I will give him the morning star”** — The morning star is Lucifer, who having risen announces the day, that is, Christ, who rising brought to the world the light of faith and of immortality; he will therefore give the morning star, himself, and the glory of resurrection, or the morning star is the first resurrection.

3.1:
**“And to the angel of the church of Sardis”** — “the beginning of beauty”, or “fitted to the beginning of beauty”
**“Sardis”** — “The beginning of beauty”: one who at first has little or no virtue, then is foul through vices; or a hypocrite, who is beautiful outwardly and deformed within. Or “the beginning of beauty” is having gone out from the world.
**“write: These things saith he, that hath the seven spirits of God and the seven stars: I know”** — that is, I know
**“I know thy works”** — I know thy works. And I know that in all your works you seek human praise.
**“that thou hast the name of being alive: and thou art dead”** — because whoever offends in one is guilty of all
3.2:
**“Be watchful”**
• that is, anxious for salvation
• Or therefore watch, because although you are unmoved in mind, or praiseworthy in mind, you are nevertheless not perfect unless you rouse the others; or it is not enough to confess Christ unless you also do works.
**“and strengthen the things that remain”** — or the rest
**“which are ready to die”** — or dead
**“remain”** — watch, I say: for not
**“For I find not thy works full before my God”**
• and because they are not full
• and therefore they are not pleasing
• For I find not thy works full before my God, etc. While they are without charity, or for praise, or because he commits a crime.
3.3:
**“Have in mind therefore in what manner thou hast received”** — you have begun to work
**“and heard: and observe”** — complete by work
**“heard”** — From the holy fathers, because: “He that offendeth in one is guilty of all”; or they received their reward; or: “And if I have not charity, I am nothing.”
**“and do penance”** — concerning what you had let go
**“If then thou shalt not watch, I will come to thee”** — blinding you
**“as a thief”** — that I may despoil and kill
**“and thou shalt not know at what hour I will come to thee”** — against you
3.4:
**“But thou hast a few names in Sardis”** — as a few named, that is, good people who are worthy of being named
**“which have not defiled their garments”**
• by criminal stain; or those who have wiped away a stain made by tears
• The garment of immortality and innocence, which they received in baptism, or their good works.
**“and”** — therefore
**“they shall walk”** — from virtue to virtue
**“with me in white, because they are worthy”** — as I commanded or foresaw
3.5:
**“He that shall overcome, shall thus”** — and likewise concerning the imitators of these
**“be clothed in white garments”** — that is, he shall likewise be clothed in white garments
**“I will not blot out”** — He blots out the reprobate, according to that: “And the Lord hardened the heart of Pharao.”
**“his name out of the book of life”** — I will not withdraw grace: he says less and means more
**“out of the book of life”** — The book of life is the foreknowledge of God, in which all things are fixed.
**“and I will confess his name before my Father”** — in good pleasure
**“I will confess his name”** — Saying: “Come, ye blessed of my Father,” or here: “He gave me to eat and to drink.”
**“and before his angels.”** — and in the joy of the angels
3.7:
**“And to the angel of the church of Philadelphia”** — ‘love of the brethren’ or ‘saluting the inheritance’
**“church, write: These things saith the Holy One and the true one, he that hath the key of David;”** — flesh from David, but also from Adam, not new, by whose merit all good things
**“These things saith”** — As if to say: labour for the conversion of the brethren as you have begun, because in what I promised: “Whatsoever you shall ask the Father in my name, he may give it you.” I am true in my promises; whence you may know that I will gather many for you as you desire.
**“he that openeth, and no man shutteth;”** — the hearts to faith or the Scriptures
**“shutteth”** — before swine, who would trample
**“and no man openeth.”**
• by withdrawing grace
• He shuts that we may seek, he opens that we may find; that the seeker may receive the fruit of his labour, and the giver have thanks for his goodness.
3.8:
**“I know”** — I approve
**“thy works.”**
• good
• and namely
**“A door opened”** — The hearts of men, previously hard. Or the obscure Scriptures. Or myself, who am the true door to life, whence the disciples, forbidden to speak and beaten, said: “We cannot but speak the things which we have seen.”
**“which no man can shut: because thou hast a little strength”**
• not proud, or small in comparison with the future, where there is no labour
• Behold, I have given before thee, etc., because thou hast a little strength, etc. I gave it deservedly, because you could not have it openly by yourself, because you have little strength.
**“and hast not denied my name.”**
• in distresses
• and because you are such
3.9:
**“who say they are Jews”** — They lost this name when they said of Christ: “We know not this man.”
**“but do lie.”** — in the sixth vision he speaks of the conversion of the angels
**“do lie”** — They strive to prove it by words and certain pretences.
**“Behold”** — how I will give
**“I will make them to”** — to faith
**“come and adore before thy feet.”**
• let them worship as his brethren adored Joseph
• Behold, I will make them come, etc. Ready to imitate your works through the likeness of their humility.
**“And they shall know that I have loved thee.”** — They shall know, etc. Placed outside, they did not believe God loved the Church, which he allowed to be afflicted; this he will now make the proof of love, that is, the assurance that you should not give way, because I come to reward.
3.10:
**“hast kept the word of my patience”** — A command about patience, which I showed in myself, praying for persecutors.
**“I will also keep thee”** — because you have kept
**“from the hour of the temptation, which shall come upon the whole world”** — From the hour of temptation which is to come, etc. That is, either the general persecution against Christians to come straight after Nero, or the last time of Antichrist.
**“to try them that dwell upon the earth.”** — To try, etc. As in what follows, often in the sixth place in order, so here in the sixth angel the last persecution is designated, in which some of the Jews are to be deceived, and some by the admonitions of Elias are to fulfil the law spiritually; they are believed about to overcome the enemy.
3.11:
**“Behold, I come quickly”** — But temptation will come, yet that you not give way, because I come to reward.
**“hold fast that which thou hast,”** — and therefore hold meanwhile what you have, namely faith and works
**“that no man take thy crown.”** — because
3.12:
**“a pillar”** — Firm in himself, and upholding others by word and example.
**“shall go out no more”** — Since God has a fixed number of his own, if anyone falls, another is brought in by his mercy, just as through the pride of the Jews the Gentiles came in.
**“no more”**
• I will not suffer him to depart any more
• The younger son, that is, the people of the Gentiles, had gone out; but reconciled by the death of the fatted calf, that is, by the blood of Christ, he shall not go out any more.
**“And I will write upon him”** — more than the mind of man can grasp
**“the name of my God”** — in a certain way will be God
**“new”** — Where there is no old age, but a full vision of peace.
**“of my God, the new Jerusalem”** — He will be called the city of God, “fortified with virtues.”
**“which cometh down out of heaven”** — From heaven. Concerning the conformity of the heavenly creatures.
**“from my God”** — because God sends all the virtues
**“and my new name.”**
• that is, a Christian, that is, anointed with grace
• because he has nothing of Adam
3.14:
**“And to the angel of the church of Laodicea”** — Laodicea is interpreted “vomiting” or “a lovable tribe”
**“write: These things saith the Amen, the faithful and true witness”** — a witness of what he heard from the Father, fearless. Or one in whom faith is to be placed in all things. Or a witness of our works before the Father.
**“and true”**
• in all words
• It is truth, because through him the promises of the Father are fulfilled.
**“who is the beginning of the creation of God:”** — of the first creation or re-creation
3.15:
**“I know thy works,”** — are not hidden from me
**“that thou art neither cold, nor hot.”**
• not with constant desire
• Neither cold nor hot, etc. Because you are not wholly ignorant of the faith, nor openly deny what you received.
**“I would thou wert cold”**
• because there is more hope of the cold
• He does not wish him cold simply, but such a one of whom greater hope is held.
3.16:
**“But because thou art lukewarm”** — growing torpid
**“and neither cold, nor hot, I will begin to vomit thee”**
• by excommunicating
• to remove from the fellowship of the saints
**“I will begin to vomit thee”** — About to speak of a wonderful thing, that the lukewarm were to be excommunicated, because they were believed good by men, he says he is truthful in all things, so that he may be believed in this; and if they wish to come to their senses he promises preservation, because he gave the first faith.
**“out of my mouth.”** — through my preachers in whom I speak
**“out of my mouth”** — He is vomited out of the mouth who is cast into worse things, or who dies impenitent.
3.17:
**“I am rich”** — Cleansed in baptism, or rich in divine knowledge, or in worldly knowledge.
**“and made wealthy”** — and filled to you with virtues
**“and have need of nothing”** — and I have added on my part
**“and knowest not, that thou art wretched, and miserable”** — since through your ignorance you perish
**“and poor”** — from works of virtue
**“and blind”** — because you do not recognize your vices
**“and naked.”** — from virtues, in the soul
3.18:
**“I counsel thee”** — but I do not deny mercy
**“although thou art such, yet”** — in other copies it is lacking
**“I counsel thee, although thou be such”** — Because such works do not lead to salvation.
**“to buy of me gold”** — myself, or charity
**“fire tried”** — placed in fire, or fiery
**“tried”** — with the fire of tribulation
**“that thou mayest be made rich”** — by works of virtues
**“and mayest be clothed in white garments”** — by the virtues themselves
**“mayest be clothed, and that the shame of thy nakedness may not appear”** — by virtues
**“The shame may not appear”** — It is better to blush here before a few than in the future before all, or I will not give up for shame.
**“and anoint thy eyes with eyesalve, that thou mayest see”** — the cause stated above
**“eyesalve”** — Our eyes are anointed that we may see, when we help the keenness of our understanding, by the remedy of good works, to know the clarity of the true light.
**“Anoint thy eyes with eyesalve”** — “The commandment of the Lord, enlightening the eyes”, or anoint with the gift of the Holy Spirit the mind which earthly things had shut in.
3.19:
**“Such as I love, I rebuke”** — I cause sin to be known
**“and chastise”** — I make them pure
**“Be zealous therefore”** — whom you see suffering adversity
**“and do penance”**
• do penance for lukewarmness
• and you ought to do so
3.20:
**“Behold, I stand at the gate”** — a closed heart
**“and knock”** — I rebuke
**“Behold, I stand at the gate, and knock”** — I wait, or I inspire, or I call through preachers.
**“If any man shall hear”** — by understanding
**“my voice, and open to me”** — to do the work
**“the door”** — through true faith
**“I will come in”** — in the secret of the heart
**“to him”** — through the infusion of grace
**“and will sup with him”** — because I will delight in his faith and work
**“and”** — through his justification
**“he with me”**
• because he will rejoice in my help, namely through the joy of a good conscience
• What more?
3.21:
**“to sit with me”** — To judge in them, in whom I sit and judge: this of prelates, and through prelates of subjects.
**“in my throne”**
• through whom the judicial power
• namely not only by the privilege of dignity but also by the uniformity of charity and will
**“as I also have overcome”** — Because his victory and his sitting is the cause of their victory and sitting.

4.1:
**“After these things I looked”**
• not in time but in order
• This vision is about the revelation of mysteries, for the revelation of secrets fittingly follows the corrected.
• This vision may be called the revelation of mysteries which are opened by the Spirit.
• In this second vision he treats of him who sits on the throne and of his adornment, and of the lamb opening the book, that is, the divine ordering concerning the restoring of the human race, and of him who looses the seven seals, that is, obscurities, so that when we have seen that God has bestowed so great an understanding of the Scriptures upon men, we may be grateful to him, and not fear to suffer for him.
• This vision is placed second, not first, because he now invites his own to tribulations which they cannot endure unless what was neglected is first corrected, which was in the first correction.
• Almost this whole vision concerns the last faithful, which greatly helps to encourage the present ones; it also brings in a few of those who suffered before the incarnation of Christ, which helps to the same end.
**“and behold”** — he could see, because
**“in heaven”** — That is, Scripture, which is the way to life. Or Christ is the door, whose mysteries were before closed, now opened to those who by faith and deed are heaven.
**“and the first voice which”**
• as far as the things I saw in this vision
• namely the Old Testament, which precedes the New
**“as it were, of a trumpet”** — Not disagreeing with my reason, by giving reasons.
**“speaking with me”** — exhorting to war, and also, as it applies to the same, that I should suffer
**“saying:”** — giving the reason why it is fitting to suffer
**“Come up hither, and I will shew thee the things which must be done hereafter”**
• you, being corrected, enlarge your mind toward these other things
• Or what must happen soon after these things, that is, among the last faithful. Or after these things I was in the Spirit.
**“I will shew thee”** — He says that those things which have already passed must still be done, as being about to remain in the same state in which they began; or, after correction, it is necessary to see the secrets by which they are encouraged to battle.
4.2:
**“I was in the spirit”** — and because I so desired
**“Immediately I was in the spirit”** — I did not resist, but cast off the care of all earthly things.
**“and behold there was a throne”** — The greater ones, in whom God sits and judges, he also sits in subjects, where others or certain ones were so fit that God might fittingly sit and rest in them.
**“and”** — as exceeding
**“sitting”** — Christ, walking above among the candlesticks, now sitting, that is judging the merits of individuals, of whom he worthily makes mention, whom he exhorted to fight.
4.3:
**“And he that sat”** — ready to judge
**“He that sat”** — Where there is only good, there is no need to judge, that is to discern; where good and evil are, there discernment is needed.
**“was to the sight like”** — Previously unknown, he appeared to the world in flesh, crushing enemies, giving strength to his own.
**“the jasper”** — the divinity enters and gives pasture to his own
**“and the sardine stone”** — flesh reddens in suffering
**“the jasper and the sardine stone”** — By the colour of the two stones he signifies God and man.
**“and a rainbow”**
• that is, peace
• As if to say: I saw them preparing themselves to receive God the sitter, and that they might not fail, I saw help; this is, there was a rainbow round about the seat, in sight like, etc., that is, peace, that is, the propitiation of God, which is round about, as a covering. This both baptism, which is the green colour, and the blood of Christ, which is the red colour, bring about. Or by these colours is signified the judgment by water that is past, and by fire that is to come, in which he will save his own.
**“was round about the throne, in sight like unto an emerald”** — emerald is green and red
**“in sight like unto an emerald”** — By the green colour of the emerald, which is the colour of water, baptism is understood; by its redness, the gifts of the Holy Spirit received in baptism, by which sins are burned away.
4.4:
**“And round about the throne”** — as appendages and agreeing in his judgment
**“four and twenty seats”**
• the lesser Church, both in the Old and in the New Testament
• Teachers are sometimes called twenty-four, sometimes twelve.
• All the teachers of the Old or New Law are called twelve on account of the faith of the Trinity, which they announce to the four parts of the world; or they become twenty-four, by six times four. The six refer to the works which he made in six days; the four to the gospels, that is, to what in the New and in the Old Testament worships the works of God.
**“Four and twenty seats”** — The twelve prophets, the twelve apostles, although there are more of each order.
**“and upon the seats”** — I saw
**“four and twenty ancients sitting, clothed”**
• or garments
• Clothed in robes, etc. Sins are covered and made white by virtues.
**“in white garments”** — which they put on in baptism, with which the elect are clothed
**“and on their heads”** — that is, in their minds
**“their crowns”** — or crowns
**“CROWNS”** — That is, victory through wisdom and charity, even toward enemies.
**“of gold.”** — or golden
4.5:
**“from the throne proceeded lightnings, and voices, and thunders”** — threats
**“From the throne”** — That is, the Church; that is, it rains lightnings, that is, miracles which terrify and enlighten.
**“Seven lamps”** — The gifts of the Holy Spirit, which kindle and illuminate, prepared for all those who are the seats of God.
**“going forth into all the earth.”** — in many copies this is omitted
4.6:
**“In the sight”** — Because they understand the sacrament and the thing of the sacrament, and receive no one except those whom they have seen and known to be fit.
**“as it were, a sea of glass like to crystal.”** — that is, devoted to contemplation of heavenly things and taking care of, or remembering, their subjects
**“A sea of glass”** — Baptism is bright with the sincerity of faith; after it the elect are led through the fire of tribulation to the firmness of good works, as crystal hardens from water.
**“in the midst of the throne, and round about the throne”** — round about, like sentinels
**“In the midst”** — A certain level plain, in likeness of a judge, who has a broad and spacious place where he sits and judges judgments.
**“of the throne”** — Jerusalem, like supporters: as man, as calf, as lion, as eagle.
**“Four”** — On account of the office of fourfold preaching.
**“living creatures”** — animate and inanimate
**“Living creatures”** — Christ, who was born, suffered, rose, and ascended. Faithful also, rational and gentle, as man. Bearing adversity without terror, as lion. Mortifying themselves, as calf. Seeking heavenly things, as eagle.
**“Full of eyes”** — Mindful of past sins, and taking care against the future; or having knowledge of those things that God has made, or will make at the end of the world; or of the Old and New Testament; or pleasing God and men.
**“before and behind.”** — because of the office
4.7:
**“And the first living creature was like a lion: and the second living creature like a calf: and the third living creature, having the face, as it were, of a man: and the fourth living creature was like an eagle flying.”**
• The lion is born dead, on the third day is quickened by the voice of the Father; so also Christ rose on the third day. And it was needful that he rise, because he was dead. And he could die, because he was man. And though man and dead, it was needful that he rise, because he is the eagle, that is, God.
• Because Ezechiel, who foresaw what was to come, put the man first, then the lion, because Christ in preaching was a lion; then the calf, because he was sacrificed; finally the eagle, because he ascended into the heavens. John, seeing things fulfilled, puts the lion first, as the foundation of the whole faith.
4.8:
**“And the four living creatures had each of them six wings”** — As if: they were well instructed so that they might preach these things about Christ.
**“six wings”** — The first wing is the natural law, the second the law of Moses, the third the prophets, the fourth the gospel, the fifth the institutions of the apostles, the sixth those of any whomsoever, as Augustine, Gregory, Ambrose, through which the Church seeks high things and from which preachers receive the foundation of all preaching. Or the six wings are the knowledge of the works of God made in six days, the knowledge of which those lift on high who work well in them.
**“round about and within”** — Or, by the letter they teach the simple; by allegory, the more perfect. Or because they shine in the middle, in the ends of the earth.
**“they are full of eyes”** — Because they keep themselves pure and form others by example.
**“they are full of eyes.”** — Or: they are full of eyes within, that is, in the conscience of purity; and around, that is, in the sight of men, blameless.
**“And”** — did not cease
**“they rested not day and night”** — in prosperity or in adversity, or continually
**“saying: Holy, holy, holy,”** — three times, because the Trinity in persons
**“Lord God Almighty”** — once, because the unity in majesty
**“who was”** — without beginning
**“and who is”** — unchangeable
**“who is to come”** — The Son will appear bodily; the whole Godhead will make itself manifest to the faithful.
4.9:
**“And when”** — that is, because
**“gave”** — attributed, and professed, and preached
**“those living creatures”** — preachers everywhere
**“glory”** — of their faith in the resurrection or in the ascension
**“and honour”** — of operation
**“and benediction”** — by the honour of operation or in the ascension
**“AND BENEDICTION”** — Of supernal reward, or in exaltation: as to him “every knee should bow, of heavenly, earthly” etc.
4.10:
**“fell down”** — humbled themselves
**“The four and twenty”**
• all judges of the Old and New Law
• who above were preachers; here, more justly, judges
**“ancients before him that sitteth on the throne.”** — that is, in good pleasure
**“And adored”** — What they did not have from themselves they asked of him, by voice and deed.
**“and cast their crowns before the throne, saying:”** — giving an example to others
**“saying”** — Attributing in the secret of the heart to God the victory over vices or tribulations.
4.11:
**“Thou art worthy”** — you are worthy, that we should refer
**“O Lord our God, to receive glory, and honour, and power,”** — which is above the blessing
**“because thou hast created all things, and for thy will”**
• according to
• The invisible things also, or the angels and souls, as he says they are spiritual, since he makes the impious into pious ones spiritually created.
**“hast created all things”** — Therefore all things are to be referred to you, because all things have their beginning from you.
**“were”** — In art, before they were formed in work.
**“and have been created.”** — in art, that is, in the wisdom of God they lived.
**“have been created”** — Existing visibly; some according to spiritual understanding or creation.
**“for thy will they were, and have been created”** — And not suddenly, but what was made was life in him.

5.1:
**“In the right hand”** — In the Son, through whom he made all things, to whom the intent of the whole book is directed.
**“of him that sat on the throne, a book written”**
• the divine disposition
• Or the book is the divine ordering concerning the restoring of men, which is written, that is, made manifest, within, that is, obscurely, in the Old Testament, as Moses: “You shall sacrifice a lamb in the evening,” there making manifest the restoration of us to come in the last age through the sacrifice of Christ, and outside plainly, that is, in the New Testament.
**“a book”** — That is, the two testaments, which are the same: the old, namely, signified outside, or because it promises outward things; the new, namely, signified within, or because at times it promises blessedness; or within, that is, in the more hidden things, namely for the more perfect, outside in the simpler words, namely for the less perfect.
**“written within and without”** — that is, also fortified
**“sealed”** — The Scriptures of the prophets were made closed and obscure, but afterwards opened through him.
**“with seals”** — That is, with all obscurities; or closed with the sevenfold Spirit, through whom faith is opened.
**“seven”**
• that is, the universalities
• He says seven because in what follows he will define those seven seals, namely the white horse, and the red, and the black, etc., which were opened and known at the beginning of the Church, which was the white horse on which Christ sat, and fortified by doctrine and example, and which the red horse assailed.
5.2:
**“And I saw”** — I heard
**“a strong angel”** — any of the earlier fathers
**“angel”** — The holy fathers understood at times the restoration of men arranged by God, and they longed to see when it would happen, but they did not know how it would happen, until, namely, it was revealed before it happened to some.
**“proclaiming”** — Inquiring, and announcing to others, and complaining through excessive longing that it is deferred so long.
**“with a loud voice: Who is worthy”** — to fulfil or to receive
**“to open the book, and to loose the seals thereof”** — the words of John
**“to open and to loose the seals”** — To remove the divine disposition or all the obscurities of the Scriptures.
5.3:
**“And no man was able”** — as an angel
**“neither on earth”** — as a man
**“neither under the earth”** — souls stripped from the body
**“to open”** — to fulfil
**“the book, nor to look on it”** — to understand perfectly. Whence: “Who shall declare his generation?”
5.4:
**“And I wept much, because no man was found worthy”** — because all were defiled
**“I wept much, because no man”** — This is in the person of the earlier fathers, who did not understand it, or grieved at the deferred restoration. Whence: “Many prophets and kings have desired to see the things that you see,” etc.
**“to open the book”** — through the incarnation
**“nor to see it”** — to understand perfectly
5.5:
**“And one of the ancients”** — Any prophet who, announcing the coming of Christ, comforts others.
**“Behold the lion”** — the devil
**“the lion hath prevailed”** — The lion, when he is chased through the mountains, flees, and with a knot which he has in his tail blots out his tracks, that he may not be found. So Christ fled through the mountains, that is, his divinity lay hidden from the Jews; having assumed flesh he covered his divinity, that it might not be recognised; the lion sleeps with open eyes, so Christ expired while his divinity lived.
**“of the tribe of Juda, the root of David”** — coming from David, or the firmament of David
**“to open”** — to this end, that he may open
5.6:
**“And”** — as he had foretold
**“I saw”** — he follows through how the lion conquered and where
**“and behold in the midst of the throne and of the four living creatures, and in the midst of the ancients, a Lamb”**
• Christ, who was the victim
• And behold, in the midst of the throne, etc. The Church, which is possessed by Christ as a throne, is fed as the living creatures, is honoured as the ancients in the judgment of power; built upon Christ himself, in the seven horns she is exalted in the kingdom of strength, in the seven eyes she is enlightened by signs and miracles.
**“standing”** — helping those who fight
**“as it were slain”** — As though slain: because, though dead, “he liveth by the power of God.” Or, he was slain as among his own, in whom he is daily put to death.
**“having seven horns and seven eyes”** — Because he gives the kingdom, which is signified by the horns. The eyes, because he gives light. Or the horns: the more eminent saints, founded on Christ the head, surpassing the flesh.
5.7:
**“And he came”**
• that is, the lamb
• Christ as man
**“and took”** — for the knowledge of men through the flesh
**“out of the right hand”** — from the Word united to himself
**“of him that sat on the throne”** — or 'of'
5.8:
**“And when”** — and because
**“he had opened the book, the four living creatures”** — that is, all preachers
**“and the four and twenty ancients”** — all judges
**“fell down before the Lamb”** — They fell down before the Lamb, etc. They thought humbly of themselves and imitate him; whence it follows: having every one, etc.
**“harps”** — The mortifications of vices and concupiscences.
**“having every one of them harps”** — In the harp, wood and strings; by the wood, the cross of Christ; by the strings, the flesh of the saints, which is stretched on the wood, while rendering the same sound through various torments they imitate the cross of Christ.
**“and golden vials”** — glad hearts, also toward love of enemies
**“full of odours”** — sweetly smelling
**“which are the prayers of saints. And they sang a new canticle, saying”**
• without sin
• They sang a new canticle, etc. With rejoicing the Church professes the New Testament in deed, while in his death she baptizes.
**“Thou art worthy”** — because free from sin
**“to open”** — or to receive
5.9:
**“Thou hast redeemed us”** — It is said of three orders, in which there are seventy-two tongues, in each of which many peoples, and in each people nations.
**“to open the book and to loose the seals thereof, for thou wast slain and hast redeemed us to God in thy blood, out of every tribe and tongue and people and nation”** — The three orders of those to be saved: Noe, Daniel, Job. Or the three orders of the nations: Greeks, Hebrews, Christians.
5.10:
**“And hast made us to our God a kingdom”** — reigning spiritually
**“and priests”** — offering ourselves and praying for others
**“and we shall reign on the earth”** — over the earth of the living, or over the earthly
5.11:
**“And I beheld, and I heard”** — I saw and I heard. Not only the living creatures and the elders, bearing witness by their office to the same thing, but I also heard.
**“the voice of angels”** — Of angels. That is, of the supernal spirits, who guard and protect the Church, who rejoice at the restored fellowship of the saints, who bear witness to Christ, and both at the nativity, when they appeared to the shepherds, and in the passion and in the resurrection and ascension, testified that the judge would come. Or the lesser angels, subjects in the Church, leading an angelic life, who surround and honour their preachers and their judges, consenting to their testimony and conforming themselves to it.
**“of many”**
• existing
• Of many. The more there are, the greater the witness and the greater the joy.
**“round about the throne and the living creatures and the ancients; and the number of them was thousands of thousands”** — that is, many thousands
**“thousands of thousands”** — Because what is finite with God is infinite to men.
5.12:
**“saying with a loud voice”** — as if to say: we are not ashamed to proclaim of you that
**“The Lamb that was slain is worthy to receive”** — exemption from sin
**“and divinity, and wisdom”** — because he was God, even though he seemed dead
**“wisdom”** — Knowledge of all things, as the Word united to him.
**“and strength”** — because he conquered the devil, remaining steadfast in the passion
**“and honour”** — in the resurrection
**“and glory”** — impassibility and immortality
**“and benediction”** — in the exaltation
5.13:
**“And”** — and to receive
**“every creature”** — “That in the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of those in heaven” etc.
**“which is in heaven, and on the earth”** — of those on earth
**“and under the earth”** — of those under the earth
**“and such as are in the sea”** — literally, or the world
**“and”** — and all things
**“I heard all saying: To him that sitteth”** — to the Trinity
**“on the throne”** — according to his humanity
**“and to the Lamb, benediction”** — exaltation
