**“Benediction”** — That is, the increase we have in good works, and the honour that follows from it, and the glory from the virtues we receive in baptism, and the power by which we resist concupiscence, be attributed not to us but to you.
**“and honour”** — impassibility
**“and glory”** — in the resurrection
**“and power”** — because he is almighty
5.14:
**“And”** — It belongs to preachers, by their office, to confirm the others.
**“And the four living creatures”** — All the elders and the living creatures give their assent, all together, by the testimony of the angels.
**“said: Amen.”** — a mark of confirmation
**“And the four and twenty ancients fell down on their faces”**
• in their hearts
• They fell on their faces, etc. They are not proud because they judge others, but they humble themselves.
**“and adored”** — in mind, mouth and work

6.1:
**“And I saw that the Lamb had opened one of the seven seals, and I heard one of the four living creatures”**
• And I saw. After the Lamb had fulfilled what had been foretold of him, and had made his Church firm in faith by the testimony of the prophets and angels, he opened to them the sense that they might understand the Scriptures, and makes known outwardly through preachers what it is fitting to suffer for this faith, and what helps, or what crowns, he sets before his own; because, the memory of the restoration having been made, if he were silent about tribulations, they might now fail, should tribulation rise up unexpectedly.
• They invite John, that is, the Church of the first ages, to follow.
**“That the Lamb had opened”** — It was sealed, because Christ opened all things either in himself or in his own. For he himself opened the senses of his own, that they might understand these seals in the Scriptures. In the first seal opened, from which a white horse went forth, is understood the whitening of the Church through baptism. In the second, the red horse, is opened the persecution of those who shed blood, whence tribulations rise up against the baptized. In the third, the black, the hidden persecution of heretics. In the fourth, the pale, that of false brethren, open and hidden.
**“saying, as it were the voice of thunder:”** — because it terrifies
**“Come, and see”** — And pass from the mystery, and see the truth or justice completed.
6.2:
**“Behold a white horse”** — The Church, made white in baptism, and especially the preachers who everywhere bear God.
**“and he that sat on him had a bow”** — the divine Scripture
**“A bow”** — That is, Christ has the Scripture, which enlightens his own and slays his enemies.
**“and there was a crown given him”**
• God is crowned in the saints, or according to his humanity
• that is, power
**“and he went forth conquering”** — among the Jews, or in himself
**“that he might conquer.”** — the nations with their members
**“And he went forth conquering that he might conquer”** — What the preachers do, they attribute to God.
6.3:
**“And when he had opened”** — And when he had opened, etc. The devil, seeing the Church set up to fill the place from which he himself had fallen, strives first to overthrow her openly.
**“the second seal,”** — in the order of seeing, not of time
6.4:
**“And there went out”** — because what he has in his heart he completes by work
**“A horse that was red”** — Contrary to the former, namely open persecutors and bloody ones.
**“and to him that sat thereon”** — that is, the devil
**“it was given that he should take”** — he took away
**“take peace from the earth”** — That is, it was permitted by God that he should take away all quiet of mind from those who are given over to earthly things.
**“and that they should kill one another”**
• with the material sword or of persuasion
• They should slay: great power of killing, because it reaches not only the lesser but also the greater, as against Peter.
6.5:
**“And when he had opened the third seal, I heard the third living creature saying: Come, and see. And behold a black horse”** — darkening their vices by certain good works
**“And behold a black horse”** — The devil, seeing that he has not prevailed by open persecutions, sends in heretics who contend with false arguments so that they may deceive more easily.
**“and he that sat on him”** — we attribute to the devil himself what his followers work through him
**“had a pair of scales in his hand.”** — what they preach is attested by work
**“A pair of scales”** — Because they say they have true discernment in the Scriptures.
6.6:
**“And I heard as it were a voice”** — of the angel standing there
**“And I heard as it were”** — Because here in the fight with heretics there is greater danger, help is held out.
**“in the midst of the four living creatures, saying: Two pounds”**
• that is, a vessel holding two sextarii, which is the Church, of two peoples, or having faith and works
• Two pounds of wheat, etc. I wish you faithful not to fear, you who before could be harmed, and you devils not to harm these, because you will not prevail, since two pounds of wheat, etc.
• By wheat we understand the greater martyrs, who are of two pounds. For besides martyrdom they have works and the love of God and neighbour, or faith and works. By barley, the lesser martyrs, namely those who have only faith in the Trinity without works and without any love, but are saved by faith alone in blood. These are three two-pound measures, through faith in the Trinity. Or otherwise: as wheat is first much ground and afterwards becomes the best bread, so Christ, being much tried by diverse persecutions, became for us the bread of life, giving us his body and blood. And so the faithful are ground by many tribulations, and, made the best food for God, become imitators of the wheat, that is, of Christ. Or they are full of wheat, that is, of wheaten preaching, because the preaching of the faith refreshes the hearts of the hearers as wheat in taste surpasses all crops. And those who are imitators of the wheat, preaching has brought forth for one penny, that is, those who with one mind obey the penny, that is, the decalogue, that is, the ten precepts of the law.
• The pound consists of twelve ounces, by which the twelve apostles are signified; by the two-pound measure, the twofold love of God and of neighbour. Or the two-pound measures are those who have the love of God and neighbour and the faith of the Trinity, and obey the four gospels; for three times four are twelve, the number of which the pound consists: by three, the faith of the holy Trinity; by four, having the four gospels; by the two-pound measure, the love of God and neighbour.
• By wheat we can understand the New Testament, by barley the Old. Wheat, that is, the New Testament, is said to be of two pounds on account of its twofold understanding, namely historical and spiritual, as if to say: fear not, you faithful, for perfection will be given you, by which you will be able to resist heretics.
**“of wheat”** — Wheat: the more perfect, who, ground down through tribulation, have been cooked by fire, a sweet food to God. Barley: the lesser in the same kind. Wine: those pressed indeed by the press, but not so thoroughly cooked, sharp only in themselves and intoxicating others to work well. Oil: those who do not intoxicate others, but anoint with pure prayers. Or wine and oil are confessors, for the fervour of charity and the sweetness of mercy which they have in themselves and toward others.
**“for a penny”** — bought with the blood of Christ
**“and thrice two pounds of barley”** — for at least it is necessary to have the faith of the holy Trinity
**“the wine”** — Likewise it is bought for one penny.
**“and the wine and the oil”** — That is, those who are refreshed. And therefore anointed with wine, that is, my blood, and with oil, that is, the Holy Spirit.
**“see thou hurt not”** — therefore
**“hurt not”** — any of them
6.7:
**“And when he had opened the fourth seal,”** — the secrets of the fourth seal
**“And when he had opened the fourth seal”** — The devil, seeing that he can make no headway either through open tribulations or through open heresies, sends ahead false brothers, who under the habit of religion take on the nature of the red and black horse, subverting the faith.
**“I heard the voice of the fourth living creature”** — the fourth state
6.8:
**“And behold a pale horse”** — that is, the dead, or hypocrites who afflict themselves
**“And he that sat upon him”** — That is, death, because through him death came. Or literally, because he kills some in the flesh and some in the soul.
**“upon him”** — namely the devil
**“his name was Death, and hell followed him.”** — And hell followed. That is, the insatiable imitate him in earthly things, or are to be placed in hell.
**“Over the four”** — That is, over all the wicked dwelling everywhere, or over Jews and Gentiles, heretics and false Christians.
**“parts of the earth,”**
• or of the world
• which power
**“to kill with sword,”** — by the sword, that is, by material means or by persuasions
**“with famine”** — of the divine Word
**“and with death”** — by poisonous words
**“and with the beasts of the earth.”** — by beastly ministers, or literally
6.9:
**“And when he had opened the fifth seal,”** — that is, when he had revealed the secrets of the Church as to the last state, namely in the time of Antichrist
**“And when he had opened the fifth”** — The tribulations that now threaten the faithful having been shown, lest they fail in any way, he consoles the patient by assuring them of the present crown.
**“I saw under”**
• behold the place
• That is, humbling themselves beneath their head; or under, that is, hidden, because no one in this life perceives how they are there.
**“the altar”** — Christ, upon whom they offer themselves, and whom they have as a defence. Or the souls themselves are the altar, from which a smoke goes up pleasing to God; and because they were smeared with blood, they are now existing beneath, that is, in a lesser dignity than they shall have in the future, because as yet they have received only one robe.
**“the souls of them that were slain”** — that is, under the protection of Christ, who is the altar
**“of them that were slain”** — Either by open martyrdom or by some anxieties.
**“for the word of God”** — that is, for the commandment of God, which they fulfilled
**“and”** — which is borne witness to before others
**“for the testimony which they held.”** — that is, they showed Christ by their deeds, imitating him.
6.10:
**“And they cried with a loud voice”** — with great longing
**“saying: How long, O Lord”** — by reason of power
**“How long”** — They desire the greater joy and fellowship of the saints, and consent to the justice of God in the condemnation of the wicked.
**“holy”** — loving holiness
**“and true.”** — in the promises
**“How long dost thou not judge and”**
• The words “does not judge and” are lacking in many copies.
• judging by making a distinction between good and evil.
**“dost thou not revenge our blood”** — namely by inflicting punishment on the shedders of our blood
**“revenge”** — by inflicting punishments
**“on them that dwell”** — by love
**“on the earth”** — in earthly things
6.11:
**“And white robes were given to every one of them.”** — the blessedness of the soul
**“And it was said to them”** — inspired by God
**“that they should rest”** — waited patiently
**“fellow servants, and their brethren”** — Servants for the Lord’s own cause; brothers ought to wait out of love.
**“who are to be slain, even as they.”** — namely because they have the same Lord
6.12:
**“And I saw, when he had opened the sixth seal, and behold there was a great earthquake,”** — in the persecution of Antichrist
**“And the sun”** — some faithful man
**“The sun”** — That is, those in whom God shines will be reckoned guilty, and sinners retaining their brightness in themselves, or because some will fall into darkness; or Christ the true sun, who will be dim in the time of Antichrist though now bright; that is, sparkling with no miracles.
**“became black”** — by tribulations
**“as sackcloth of hair:”** — because worthless teachers will be considered
**“As sackcloth of hair”** — A light placed in a sack does not shine outside; the faithful will not pour out the light of preaching.
**“and the whole moon”** — that is, the Church
**“became as blood.”** — because it will suffer everywhere
6.13:
**“And the stars from heaven”** — that is, those formerly bright
**“fell upon the earth”** — leaning on earthly things
**“as the fig tree casteth its green figs,”** — that is, light and empty fruits, because of lack of digesting heat
**“its green figs”** — That is, empty fruits. For God allows none to fall who serves him with true love.
**“when it is shaken by a great wind.”** — namely before they come to ripeness
6.14:
**“And the heaven”** — That is, Holy Scripture, because it will be hidden.
**“The heaven”** — That is, the Church will withdraw from evils in faith and work; whence: “Go out from her, my people, and touch not the unclean thing”, that is, out of Babylon.
**“departed as a book folded up.”** — concealing the preaching from the wicked
**“And every mountain”**
• eminent in virtue
• Or proud mountains. Islands, stirred by the business of the world, will be moved from the faith.
**“and the islands”** — that is, bruised by persecutions
**“were moved out of their places.”** — will be separated from evils in faith and work
6.15:
**“And the kings of the earth”** — that is, greater and lesser, resisting the flesh
**“and the princes”** — of the earth
**“and tribunes”** — who assign rights
**“The kings of the earth, and the princes, and tribunes”** — According to the diverse honours of the world: not willing to lose them, they will forsake the faith. The rich, fulfilling whatever they wickedly wish. The strong, in overthrowing others. The bondman of sin, free from justice. These, despairing of help from the saints, seek the help of demons, that those in whom they trusted may free them.
**“and the rich”** — by works
**“and the strong”** — against the temptation of the devil
**“and every bondman”** — that is, the married man or the servant of God
**“and every freeman, hid themselves”** — from sin or from marriage
**“in the dens”** — literally
6.16:
**“And they say to the mountains and the rocks:”**
• they will implore the help of the saints
• The good ask to be protected by the intercessions of the saints from the face of God in anger. He is called “angry” when he permits his own to be so afflicted. And such a tribulation permitted by God is called, as it were, the “face of the angry one.” Or the wicked ask the demons whom they have imitated to defend them from the wrath of the judge.
**“And they say to the mountains”** — They will seek the intercession of angels, who are mountains in eminence and rocks in firmness, so that by their prayers they may obtain the mercy of the judge.
**“Fall”** — with affection
**“upon us, and hide us”** — with prayers
**“from the face”** — that is, from the presence
**“of him that sitteth”** — of the Father, Son and Holy Spirit
**“upon the throne and from the wrath of the Lamb.”** — that is, of Christ the man
6.17:
**“For the great day of their wrath is come”** — it is necessary that you fall
**“of their”** — of the reprobate
**“and who shall be able to stand?”** — unless helped by your prayers

7.1:
**“After these things”** — does not denote a difference of visions but an order
**“I saw”** — After these things I saw, etc. Having described the many-sided war of the Church, he adds that during the time of this war the devil is ready to harm, but is restrained by God, so that his own people may not in any way grow sluggish or despair.
**“four”** — on account of the four kingdoms over which they rule
**“Four”** — For the four quarters of the world in which they do harm.
**“angels”** — because sent by God
**“Angels”** — The devil is called 'angel,' that is, one sent, both by God for the testing of the good and the deceiving of the wicked, and by the devil as prince for the overthrow of all.
**“standing”** — staying
**“on the four corners of the earth,”** — even in the most remote places
**“holding the four winds of the earth,”** — because of the four preachings, or because of the gospels
**“Holding the four winds”** — In time of tribulation nothing is more necessary than preaching, and therefore the devil strives to hold back the soul in every place.
**“Winds”** — The wind stirs up clouds; watering the earth it makes it fruitful and makes its face cheerful; so preaching does to the minds of men.
**“that they should not blow upon the earth,”** — to those dwelling on the earth, or given over to earthly things
**“nor upon the sea”** — contrary to the former and different from it
**“Upon the sea”** — To those dwelling on islands, or flowing in various vices.
**“nor”** — upon
**“nor on any tree.”** — that is, one who has already passed beyond earthliness, or who is already ready to bear fruit
7.2:
**“And I saw another angel”** — This angel is that stone cut without hands, which broke the statue made of four metals; this one looses the four winds.
**“ascending from the rising of the sun”** — because he announced new joys to the world
**“Ascending”** — From the time Christ expired, he ascended, when he bound the devil, and through preachers enlightened the world with faith, as the sun with light. Or he ascended from the rising of the sun, that is, advancing from the part of wisdom and age. Or from himself descending, because he took flesh not by the union of a man, but he himself created it, who is the rising of the sun, that is, of the Father.
**“having the sign of the living God”**
• the banner of the cross, or the power of working miracles and of forgiving sins
• Sign: that is, the cross by which he marks his own, or power equal to the Father, or immunity from sin, through which God appears, since every man is a sinner.
• The ancient fathers bore this sign, though not in deed, yet in faith.
• The sign is borne on the forehead, lest it be hidden in tribulation; for the signing of the breast is the confession of the heart.
• When an infant is catechized, he is anointed on the breast, that he may have the faith of the heart; on the brow, that he may not blush but confess: “For with the heart we believe unto justice; but with the mouth confession is made unto salvation.” On the shoulders, that he may bear the burden of Christ. On the crown of the head, that he may keep reason, which is the crown and head of the inner man.
**“and he cried with a loud voice”**
• for God to cry out is to act
• when he restrained the demons in the passion
**“to the four angels”** — that is, with great authority
**“to whom it was given”** — that is, permitted
**“to hurt”** — not as much as they wish
**“the earth and the sea,”** — that is, to the greedy, namely however to be converted
7.3:
**“Saying: Hurt not”** — as if: do not labour
**“the earth, nor the sea, nor the trees, till we sign the servants of our God in their foreheads.”** — until I inwardly and my people outwardly distinguish them by the sign of the cross
7.4:
**“And I heard the number of them that were signed”** — that is, I understood what sort were to be signed
**“an hundred forty-four thousand were signed,”** — on account of perfection
**“An hundred forty-four”** — He puts a finite number, because God comprehends all under a certain number.
**“of every tribe of the children of Israel”** — That is, from all who imitate the faith of Jacob.
7.5:
**“Of the tribe of Juda”**
• That is, children who, born and baptized, are saved by the sole confession of their spiritual fathers.
• Juda, “Confessing.” This is enough for those who are not kept here to live.
• Juda, who was first in the order of generation, was the fourth, by which it is signified that spiritual lineage is to be regarded. Antichrist will be born of the race of Dan, and therefore he is passed over here, that it may be shown that Antichrist is to be cast out from the whole number of the saints. Or Dan, passing over the judgment of the Hebrews, because after the truth came the legal observances passed away, and the Gentile people, forgetful of idols, rose up to the truth, Christ being born in the sixth age.
**“twelve thousand”** — By twelve we have those who are signed by the faith of the Trinity in the four parts of the world; and to show these perfect we multiply twelve by four, and it makes forty-eight; and that this perfection may be referred to the Trinity, we multiply forty-eight, and so it makes a hundred and sixty-four.
**“of the tribe of Ruben”** — seeing the son, that is, this work for those kept to labour
**“twelve thousand signed: of the tribe of Gad”** — girded, if tribulation threatens
7.6:
**“Of the tribe of Aser”** — that is, “blessed, not intent on worldly things”
**“twelve thousand signed: of the tribe of Nephthali”** — that is, breadth; that is, bestowing on others from his charity
**“twelve thousand signed: of the tribe of Manasses”** — that is, forgetful and not providing for what belongs to the use of life
7.7:
**“Of the tribe of Simeon”** — “Sorrow,” or “the hearing of mourning,” that is, always grieving over past sins and turning to the practice of virtue
**“twelve thousand signed: of the tribe of Levi”** — Levi, that is, “joined”; that is, also doing what is not enjoined on him.
**“twelve thousand signed: of the tribe of Issachar”** — Issachar, that is, reward; that is, tending towards recompense, as: “I have a desire to be dissolved and to be with Christ.”
7.8:
**“Of the tribe of Zabulon”** — Zabulon, that is, “dwelling of strength”; that is, not refusing labour, but sometimes for the need of their brethren descending from Mary to Martha.
**“Of the tribe of Joseph”** — That is, “increase”: enriching the Church with the number of saints.
**“Of the tribe of Benjamin”** — “Son of the right hand”; that is, reckoning all things as from the propitiation of God and nothing as from themselves.
7.9:
**“After these things I looked”**
• as it had been foretold, so I saw it fulfilled
• After this I saw, etc. Since he had seen those to be marked under a fixed number according to the figure, and only from the sons of Israel, he now teaches openly that by that number all the faithful are to be understood, and by the twelve tribes all nations are to be taken.
**“which no man could number”** — the number is certain to God, unknown to men
**“of all nations”** — that is, also of barbarians
**“and tribes”** — in each nation
**“and peoples”** — in one city
**“and tongues”** — in the same people there are different tongues
**“standing”** — That is, ready to obey God the judge; or also their prelates, this in the present.
**“before the throne, and in sight of”** — so that they may see
**“the Lamb”** — that is, of Christ the man
**“clothed with white robes”** — first in baptism, and afterwards with tears, this in the present
**“and palms in their hands”** — that is, the victories that follow from works; this of the future
7.10:
**“And they cried”** — and they cried out in the present, and especially in the future
**“with a loud voice”** — with great desire
**“Salvation to our God”** — We have salvation not through ourselves but through the Lamb; that is, remission of sins and good work and eternal glory.
**“upon the throne”** — that is, ourselves, in whom he judges
7.11:
**“And all the angels stood”**
• as helping
• He brings in the angels, rejoicing in the fellowship of the saints and confirming their testimony, inasmuch as they were the ones by whose office the multitude he had seen persevered in this faith. Or by the things said above let us understand the judges in the Churches; here, however, there is added what concerns their subjects.
**“All the angels”** — By the angels mentioned above can be understood the greater prelates; by these, the lesser prelates or only subjects. As there are angels and archangels, and yet all are angels, that is, messengers. So now too there are greater and lesser prelates, that is, archbishops and bishops.
**“round about the throne”** — that is, in his protection
**“and the ancients”** — of the preachers of the new and the old Testament
**“and the four living creatures; and they fell down”** — humbled themselves before God
**“in the sight”** — so that they might be looked upon
**“before the throne upon their faces”** — reasonably
7.12:
**“Saying: Amen. Benediction, and glory”** — that is, let there be truth to God, and blessing
**“Amen”**
• As if to say: if you ascribe to God, you do well. Or “Amen” is to be read with what follows thus: Amen, that is, truth in promises. And benediction, that is, the exaltation which he has above every creature, or our exaltation in virtues. And brightness, that is, impassibility, or yours in works.
• Benediction and glory, etc. As if he counts over all the benefits for which thanks are to be given.
**“and wisdom”** — by which he knows all things, or makes us knowing
**“and thanksgiving, honour”** — what he has in himself and gives to others
**“and power”** — that is, the power of resisting
**“and strength”** — the effect of power
**“to our God for ever and ever. Amen.”** — so be it, so be it
7.13:
**“And one of the ancients answered”** — satisfying the desire
**“one of the ancients”** — all the ancients, one, because they teach the same
**“And one answered”** — Seeing the crowd in such dignity, he is admonished to attend by what way it was able to ascend thither, so that the same may teach others to look.
**“and said to me”** — explaining
**“These that are clothed”** — because worthy
7.14:
**“And I said to him: My Lord, thou knowest”** — as if: I do not know, but teach me, for you know
**“And he said to me: These are they who are come”** — they come and are about to come
**“out of great tribulation, and have washed”** — because no one is without sin except Christ
**“their robes”** — because it does not pertain only to martyrs
**“THEIR ROBES”** — The innocence received in baptism, or their bodies.
**“and have made them white”** — through a new working
**“in the blood of the Lamb”** — in faith in the passion
7.15:
**“Therefore they are before the throne of God”** — before the Lord the judge; or in the fellowship of the angels
**“and they serve him day and night”** — continually; or here
**“in his temple”** — in the Church; or in heaven
**“and he that sitteth on”** — or “in”
**“the throne”** — or “by the throne”
**“shall dwell”** — or “shall dwell”
7.16:
**“They shall no more hunger nor thirst”** — because they will enjoy the living bread and the fountain of life
**“THEY SHALL NO MORE HUNGER NOR THIRST”** — He who gave knowledge to the angels will also give that same knowledge to them.
**“neither shall the sun fall on them”** — greater or lesser tribulation
7.17:
**“For the Lamb, which is in the midst of the throne, shall rule them, and shall lead them”** — from virtue to virtue in the present
**“lead them to the fountains of the waters of life”** — And through this in the future he will lead them to complete refreshment.
**“and God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes”** — He will wipe away every tear: every sorrow, whether for their sins, or for adversities, or exile, or the like.

8.1:
**“And when he had opened the seventh seal, there was silence in heaven”** — because after the death of Antichrist there will be peace in the Church
**“And when he had opened”** — In this third vision the matter is seven angels sounding trumpets for the destruction of enemies, and in likeness of those who by sounding trumpets destroyed the walls of Jericho. In which the intention is sufficiently plain. As if he would say: when I had understood the salvation of the just, on the other side I understood the damnation of the wicked, through the office of preaching enjoined on the good.
**“as it were for half an hour”** — because it will come quickly to judgment
8.2:
**“And I saw seven angels standing in the presence of God”**
• that is, labouring, not bowed down by fear
• Seven angels: those imbued either universally or with the sevenfold Spirit.
**“and there were given to them seven trumpets”**
• that is, the office of preaching
• Because the damnation of the wicked does not displease God.
8.3:
**“And”** — from whom
**“another”** — that is, greater
**“angel”** — Christ
**“came”** — that is, he joined humanity to himself
**“And another angel came”** — The angel stood before the altar, ready to sacrifice, after the likeness of a priest. Or Christ is the altar, who offered himself, and upon whom the Church offers prayers to God. He stood therefore before the altar, that is, before himself, because he has no mediator through whom he may please. Or he stood before the altar, that is, before there was an altar, that is, before he offered himself. He stood, that is, he approached his own, namely from the time of his birth. Or the altar is the Church, which, kindled with the fire of charity, sends its gifts to God through Christ.
**“having a golden censer”** — About to speak of the damnation of the wicked that will come from the preaching of the just, he first sets down a kind of excuse, lest blame for the damnation of the wicked be imputed to them, because as far as they themselves are concerned their preaching is good, and enjoined by a good teacher.
**“censer”** — That is, the apostles, who are vessels of fire, that is, of the Holy Spirit, and from whom go forth the prayers that are lifted up before God.
**“in his hand”** — that is, the apostles
**“and there was given to him”** — are offered by the saints to Christ
**“much incense”** — prayers pleasing to God
**“that he should offer of the prayers of all saints”**
• he would present them to the Father
• He said of the prayers, not prayers, because he does not present all of them to the Father, but he hears those that pertain to salvation.
**“Of the prayers of all saints”** — Because they sometimes ask for what should not be asked, as Paul did.
**“upon the golden altar”** — that is, in the good pleasure of him who sits on the throne
**“Before the altar”** — That is, to him who is above himself according to his humanity, according to which he is the altar, namely to the Trinity.
**“which is before the throne of God”** — “before God” is omitted in most copies
8.4:
**“And the smoke of the incense ascended”** — because it has been given to them so
**“Smoke”** — Compunction produced by zeal for prayer, kindled inwardly by the fire of the vision of God.
**“of the prayer of the saints”** — proceeding
**“from the hand”** — by the working
**“of the angel”** — whence it ascended
**“before God.”**
• Christ existing
• or Christ is the hand of God, through whom he made all things
8.5:
**“And”** — where
**“the angel took the censer and filled it with the fire of the altar”** — from the same Spirit with which he himself was full
**“And took and filled”** — Those whom he had taken to enlighten, Christ is said to take for that office.
**“and cast it on the earth:”** — that is, into those who were fit to bear fruit
**“and there were”** — by them
**“thunders”** — threats
**“and voices,”** — exhortations
**“and lightnings,”** — miracles
**“and a great earthquake”** — for some to good, for some to evil
8.6:
**“And the seven angels”** — all preachers imitating the apostles
**“who had the seven trumpets”** — the office of preaching
**“prepared themselves to sound the trumpet.”** — namely the company of the apostles in Judea
**“Prepared”** — That is, they first fulfilled by deed what they were about to say with the mouth. Or they prepared, that is, they foresaw what was fitting for each person.
8.7:
**“And the first angel”** — In the order of the narrative; or because this blindness of the Jews befell first, when the apostles were preaching.
**“sounded the trumpet”** — that is, terribly to the wicked, sweetly to the good
**“and there followed hail,”**
• therefore they were angry against the preachers
• that is, the scourge of persecution outwardly
**“And there followed hail”** — That is, preaching sweet to others seemed to them crushing and heavy.
**“and fire,”** — inwardly
**“mingled with blood,”** — because these two were the cause that they should kill them
**“and it was cast on the earth,”**
• this whole also, that is, hail, fire and blood, was sent
• namely by the wrath of God
**“On the earth”** — The Jews, a land tilled by the law and the prophets.
**“and the third part”**
• namely all the reprobate
• the evil ones prevail
**“And the third part”** — The two parts are the just, perfect and less perfect; but all the reprobate are to be understood in the third part.
**“of the earth was burnt up,”** — of those given to earthly things
**“of the trees”**
• that is, of the greater
• namely, as regards prelates who are neither contemplative nor active but given over to earthly things
• Of the trees. The greater trees are the Jews, who lived without reproach under the law.
**“was burnt up”** — blinded by God and condemned by his ministers
**“and all green grass”**
• that is, all who rest in the flower of the world and quickly burn
• that is, the lustful
**“was burnt up.”** — in the time of the martyrs
8.8:
**“And the second angel”**
• the order of preachers
• According to the order of the narrative, and according to how it was fulfilled: for the Jews were blinded and the apostles turned to the Gentiles.
**“sounded the trumpet”** — to the Gentiles
**“and behold”** — namely, by reason of its swelling
**“as it were a great mountain”** — the devil, the mountain, for loftiness
**“burning with fire”** — envy
**“burning”** — for harming
**“was cast”** — namely, by divine permission
**“into the sea,”** — that is, into the Gentiles, who are swollen with pride and tossed by idolatry
**“Into the sea”** — The Gentiles are the 'sea', that is, flowing in many vices; in whom, although the devil was there before, he is nonetheless truly said to be sent, because, some withdrawing, he strives to hold back others.
**“and the third part became”** — who received the teaching neither openly nor secretly
**“of the sea”** — that is, of sinners
**“blood”** — shedding blood
8.9:
**“and died”** — blinded
**“the third part died”** — Two parts, that is, all the good believed. A third, that is, all the reprobate were given over to a reprobate mind.
**“creatures”** — that is, the wise of the world or philosophers, who were converted neither by the guidance of reason nor by preaching
**“which had life”**
• that is, discernment
• Which had souls, etc. That is, of those Gentiles who were reckoned more worthy than others for certain good works.
**“in the sea”** — that is, of those governing others
8.10:
**“And the third”** — In the order of the narrative, and because this happened after those two; for after the devil could not blind all the Jews and Gentiles, he sent heretics among them, and overthrew some.
**“angel”** — namely, in the time of heretics
**“sounded the trumpet and fell from heaven”** — that is, the Church, or literally
**“a great star”** — That is, the heresiarch.
**“burning as it were a torch”** — That is, the devil envying, or a wise heretic.
**“and it fell”** — It burns and is consumed.
**“on the third part of the rivers and upon the fountains of waters”** — Those are called fountains in which the sum and, as it were, the origin of the whole faith is contained, as the gospel is. The rivers are what are drawn from it, as the expositions of them are, in which there are two senses of the faithful, the historical and the allegorical; the third is that of heretics, when they confirm their heresies by wrong expositions of the Scriptures.
8.11: **“And the name of the star is called”** — That is, bitterness.
8.12:
**“And the fourth angel”**
• That is, in the time of hypocrites.
• The fourth in the order of the narrative and in the order of the thing. For when the devil had blinded some of the Jews and Gentiles, and turned some to heresy, at last he went out to attack the very sons of the Church, and seized some both greater and lesser.
**“sounded the trumpet and the third part of the sun”**
• That is, the greater doctors.
• of prelates.
**“was smitten”**
• That is, blinded.
• by the withdrawal of grace.
**“and the third part of the moon”**
• the lesser preachers.
• That is, of clerics.
**“and the third part of the stars”**
• the simpler ones.
• That is, of religious.
**“so that the third part of them was darkened”** — so that they lose knowledge and good work.
**“and the day did not shine for a third part”** — enlightened by the greater ones.
**“and the night in like manner”**
• enlightened by the lesser ones.
• He has related these four damnations as past, as things which are seen daily in the Churches. But he has the three future ones foretold, to teach that in the last times heavier ones than the past are impending, which can also be turned to the consolation of those present.
8.13:
**“Of one eagle”** — The eagle is all preachers, who look with far-seeing mind and, going round the Church, fortify the future by preaching; they are all one because they all tend to the same thing.
**“through the midst of heaven”**
• or of heaven.
• That is, of the Church, which hides divine secrets within itself.
**“saying with a loud voice”** — because in the whole world, or with great steadfastness.
**“Woe, woe, woe to the inhabitants of the earth”**
• not to the sons of the Church.
• you will receive these three woes.

9.1:
**“And the fifth angel”**
• Here the angel proclaims that the devil fell.
• In the order of the narrative and of time. For this is the damnation of those whom the devil sends in to prepare the ways before the face of Antichrist.
**“And I saw”** — He explains the flame of heretics, of which he had said little, by what fuel it grew.
**“a star”** — That is, the devil falling, and toiling lest anyone go into his place, that is, into paradise.
**“from heaven”** — of the Church, or literally.
**“fall”** — by damnation.
**“upon the earth”** — ruling over earthly things
**“and there was given to him the key of the bottomless pit”** — their teaching overthrows many, blinding them
**“And there was given to them the key”** — The abyss, that is, the dark ones. The pit, that is, the deeper heretics, because they plunge others in with wrong opinions. Over these he is said to receive the key, that is, power, because then he will not be restrained by God as he is now; or the key is those princes through whom the heretics were working.
9.2:
**“he opened the bottomless pit and the smoke arose”** — He made the heresies that lay hidden in their hearts come forth.
**“as the smoke of a great furnace”** — that is, like the teaching of Antichrist
**“the smoke of the furnace”** — Like the teaching of Antichrist, who is a furnace purifying the good and reducing the wicked to ashes.
**“the sun and the air were darkened”** — And by this some are struck, some enlightening others, and some enlightened by them.
9.3:
**“And from the smoke there came out”** — throughout the whole world
**“locusts”** — that is, the disciples of Antichrist and of heretics
**“there came out locusts”** — Their disciples are compared to locusts, because they neither fly up into the heights through knowledge, nor walk firmly through good works, but leap in pride and fall back into punishments; and because they are gnawers of the good.
**“And power was given to them, as the scorpions of the earth have power”** — untaught in the faith and easy to deceive
**“as the scorpions have”** — The scorpion is fair of face, and stings secretly with its tail. Or he compares them to a scorpion because, as the scorpion with its tail, so heretics deceive through temporal things, which ought to come afterward, as the tail is the hinder part in an animal. Or he compares them for this reason: that when the scorpion stings it is not felt, afterwards it spreads its poison; so those deceived by heretics do not feel it, but at last are destroyed.
9.4:
**“It was commanded them that they should not hurt”** — Because God restrains their deceits, although they do not understand.
**“nor any”** — even some
**“green thing”** — already advanced
**“nor any tree”** — already bearing fruit
**“but”** — none at all
**“only the men who have not”** — in truth
**“the sign of God”** — in mind
**“on their foreheads”** — that is, who do not dare to confess openly
9.5:
**“And it was given”** — or 'given'
**“that they should not kill them but that they should be tormented”** — When heretics cannot overthrow anyone by deceit, they wish to overthrow them in some way; against them is God’s command that they may kill bodies but not deceive souls.
**“five months”**
• that is, in bodies needing the five senses
• Another reading says 'six months', on account of the six ages by which this life is divided.
**“their torment was as the torment of a scorpion”** — Although power to torment has been given, they do not torment openly, but accuse before the rulers of the world.
**“when he striketh a man”** — and by this the severity of the tribulation is hinted at
9.6:
**“And in those days men shall seek death”** — fearing a fall
**“and shall not find it”** — so that they may be made more approved
**“and they shall desire to die”** — not in any manner whatever will they seek, but will desire or long
**“and death shall fly from them”**
• this is said of prelates and subjects
• Because the care of the flock binds them to labour.
9.7:
**“And the shapes of the locusts”**
• that is, locusts in appearance
• that is, of heretics
• And the shapes of the locusts. Since he had shown how they harm both by deceits and by secret attack, and in both God’s restraint, now he shows what sort they are through whom they can work.
**“similes”** — were
**“Like the horses”** — Like horses. Because they are swift to run about and fierce to attack, and do not foresee whom they run into, whether neighbours or enemies.
**“prepared unto battle”** — over the teachers
**“and on their heads”** — that is, in their minds, where they take pride in themselves and before others
**“as it were, crowns”** — because not true crowns
**“As it were, crowns”** — As it were crowns. That is, victories gained over the fallen, not through true wisdom.
**“like gold”** — not of true gold, that is, wisdom
**“and their faces were as the faces”** — faces
**“of men.”** — because they show themselves to be pious men while inwardly they are fierce
9.8:
**“And they had hair as the hair of women.”** — because the manners of women are soft and pliant towards every vice
**“And they had hair”** — Hair. That is, fallen and effeminate morals, which cling to them and hang from them for the deception of others. Or the lesser hairs, whom they deceive who adhere to them.
**“And their teeth were as lions.”** — that is, they themselves tear others
**“their teeth were as lions”** — The teeth of lions. They have tearing and a stench.
9.9:
**“breastplates”** — Breastplates. That is, obstinate hearts, which the arrow of truth does not penetrate. Or opinions fortified with deceptions, which the truth breaks.
**“As the noise of chariots”** — As the noise of chariots. Different chariots are dragged by different horses to the same battle by different ways. So these, though by different heresies, attack the Church with one accord.
**“and many horses running to battle,”** — that is, the tumult of opinions which they make after they fail
9.10:
**“And they had tails like to scorpions”** — And they had tails like to scorpions. When their reason or tumult does not avail, they seek the help of princes, who are called tails, because to bind men they terrify and flatter. Or the tails are deceitful opinions, with which they flatter to a person’s face and secretly sting.
**“and there were stings in their tails”** — that is, sin, because they make people sin
**“and”** — as if to say: but only you good people, do not fear, because
**“and their power was to hurt men five months,”** — to the wicked, only according to the five senses
9.11:
**“And they had”** — Having shown what they are in themselves, he shows through whom these things can be done.
**“over them a king, the angel of the bottomless pit”** — the devil ruling over earthly things
**“whose name in Hebrew”** — As if to say: beware of this, Hebrews, Greeks, and Latins, and therefore every Church, because the gospel of Christ is written and received in one of these three languages.
**“is Abaddon, and in Greek Apollyon; in Latin Exterminans.”** — from the country of life
9.12:
**“One woe is past”** — One woe is past. In the order of narration and in the order of time; for this is the damnation of the wicked which will be in the time of Antichrist.
**“and behold there come yet two woes more hereafter.”** — or 'after this the sixth angel'
9.13:
**“from the four horns”** — By the four things preached of Christ, which are his nativity, passion, and resurrection, ascension, about which others are.
**“of the golden altar”** — The altar is Christ; the horns of the altar are the preachers who lift up Christ and are ready to die for him, as the blood was put upon the horns of the altar. Or otherwise: the Church, namely, offering herself in sacrifice, in which the horns are the defenders of others, who all tend to the same end; or the four horns are the gospels, which teach that the frauds of Antichrist are to be uncovered.
**“which is before the eyes of God,”**
• Or 'of God'.
• Upon which whatever is offered is received from God.
9.14:
**“saying”** — A voice saying. Heralds of past time forewarn those who will be in the time of Antichrist.
**“to the sixth angel, who had the trumpet: Loose”** — that is, that they be loosed in preaching, so that the elect may take heed for themselves.
**“Loose the four angels”** — For the four quarters of the world, or because they assail the four things preached about Christ.
**“Loose”** — Because Euphrates is a river encircling Babylon, that is, the worldly princes through whom the devil, since he was in them, worked secretly. He bids these be excommunicated, that he who was in them as if bound may work more openly through those handed over to him. Or the four angels are unclean spirits, reigning in the four parts of the world, who were restrained in the passion of Christ.
**“who are bound”** — The four mentioned above, namely the nativity, passion, resurrection and ascension.
9.15:
**“And”** — And so with those condemned.
**“the four angels were loosed, who were prepared for an hour, and a day,”**
• For an hour and a day. Or take the hour as half a year, the day as one year, the month as another year, and the year as a third; for the persecution of Antichrist will last three years and a half.
• continually and for long.
**“and a month, and a year”** — long and long.
**“for to kill the third part of men.”** — all the reprobate.
**“were loosed”** — That they might kill. With the devil loosed, many are cast down who strive to blind others.
9.16:
**“twenty thousand times ten thousand”** — The saints, made perfect by the ten precepts of the law, against whom a double number of evil men is set, because the evil are more numerous than the good.
**“And I heard the number of them.”** — And I heard, etc. And well I put it under a fixed number, because I heard, that is, understood, that there were more evil than good.
9.17:
**“And thus I saw the horses in the vision, and they that sat on them”** — the devils, or men established upon them.
**“And thus I saw”** — That is, as I had understood, that they rode to the destruction of others, so I understood that they did this through the devil, whom they carried as horses do; or the horses are the devil’s, upon whom the evil are established.
**“having breastplates of fire”** — on account of the fire of anger and of lust.
**“had breastplates”** — Fiery, that is, they armed them with sentences from which eternal punishment follows, where there is fire and smoke and stench. Or they had fiery breastplates, that is, the eternal punishment which never lets go of those it takes.
**“and of hyacinth”** — a stone of smoky colour.
**“and of brimstone, and the heads of the horses”** — that is, the greater among the devil’s ministers.
**“as the heads of lions”** — Above, in the plague of locusts, he saw the face of men; here, of lions, because the ministers of Antichrist, who are heretics, show some humanity in that they teach by words and signs; they also compel this by punishments to be confessed.
**“proceeded fire”** — The cause of eternal punishment. Or fire, that is, cupidity; smoke, that is, pride; sulphur, that is, the stench of evil works.
**“and smoke and brimstone.”** — because they tear with the mouth and stink, that is, openly evil in their preaching.
**“smoke and brimstone”** — That is why, since they are blind and set in darkness, on account of the stench of vices and evil deeds.
9.18:
**“And by these three plagues was slain the third part of men, by the fire and by the smoke and by the brimstone, which issued out of their mouths.”**
• truly, from the mouth, because
• The third part, etc. It is death, that is, all the reprobate of the Church. And likewise all Jews or pagans who were never baptized nor separated from the Church.
9.19:
**“For the power of the horses is in their mouths,”** — that is, by evil preaching.
**“and in their tails.”** — that is, in hidden deceptions, if they cannot openly.
**“like to serpents”** — Those who flatter with their face and secretly inject poison.
**“having heads”** — and truly they have power in their tails.
**“and with them they hurt.”** — others, the greater ones, who bite.
9.20:
**“And”** — they shall perish
**“the rest of the men, who were not slain by these plagues, did not do penance from the works of their hands,”** — because they therefore perish, because they did not do penance
**“that they should not adore devils”** — they did not do penance, so as not to stop adoring
**“and”** — which is more shameful

10.1:
**“And I saw another mighty angel”** — contrary to those
**“Mighty angel”** — Because a strong armed man has overcome the strong devil.
**“come down”** — For God indeed was in Christ, reconciling the world to himself
**“from heaven”** — That is, by the knowledge of angels.
**“clothed with a cloud”**
• That is, humbling himself by taking on flesh, or because he made himself knowable,
• hidden in the flesh, which is a refreshment to you against vices.
**“and a rainbow was on his head”** — He who has true knowledge of God considers him God.
**“And his face was as the sun, and his feet as pillars of fire.”** — because kindled by the Holy Spirit and illuminating others
**“as pillars of fire”** — That is, those in whom the image of God truly shines, as in contemplatives, or preaching.
10.2:
**“And he had in his hand”** — That all the Scriptures were fulfilled by his working: partly by preaching, partly by fulfilling what had been said of himself, and finally by opening their sense to his own.
**“and he set his right foot”** — that is, the firmer preachers
**“his right foot”** — That is, the firm bearers in faith and supporters of others.
**“upon the sea”** — that is, more prone to slipping into sin
**“and his left”** — that is, the less firm
**“his left foot upon the earth”** — That is, over those who in whatever way sustained, even if they did not believe.
**“upon the earth”** — This is: he placed greater and firmer preachers over greater sinners, lesser ones over lesser ones.
10.3:
**“And he cried with a loud voice”** — speaking of great things
**“as when”** — so terribly
**“as when a lion roareth”** — The voice of the lion shows his power and brings terror, as when a lion has made a furrow with its tail around the forest and roars, and no wild beast dares to come out; so Christ, enclosing his own in faith, roars lest anyone go out.
**“And when he had cried, seven thunders uttered their voices.”** — and therefore because these, sent by him, preached
10.4:
**“And when”** — that is, because
**“the seven thunders had uttered”** — all successors bringing terror
**“their voices”** — suited to their time, or which
**“I was about to write”** — Here he bears the person of those who in the time of Antichrist will wish to preach, by imitating those who went before.
**“And I heard”** — that is, I understood, because they will then understand
**“Seal up the things which”** — Divine inspiration, or angelic, for warning.
**“the seven thunders”** — That is, seals, so that it may be open to friends and hidden from enemies.
**“and write them not”** — That is, to make it manifest to unbelievers, in whom they have no place.
10.5:
**“And the angel, whom I saw standing upon the sea and upon the earth”** — And the angel, etc. When there will be so great a desolation in the Church that even preaching will be taken away, the faithful, lest they despair, receive consolation: that preaching is not withdrawn to the detriment of their salvation.
**“lifted up”** — That is, lifted up.
**“his hand”** — That is, the humanity which he had made.
10.6:
**“He swore”** — And by this he firmly establishes that he was God; for “if Christ is risen, we also shall rise.”
**“and the things which are in it”** — When he says, “he created the things that are in it,” he destroys the heresy of certain men who maintain that some things were not created by God but by a demon, like the toad.
**“and the sea, and the things which are therein”** — Because he who made all things out of nothing was able to recreate his own in a better state.
**“That time shall be no longer.”**
• Because they will be made immortal and impassible, whereas on the contrary time is for the ages of the greater ones.
• Time shall be no longer, etc. That is, no change, but eternal stability; the immortality of souls.
• Those last ones, considering this, will suffer willingly.
10.7:
**“But in the days of the voice of the seventh angel, when he shall begin to sound the trumpet”** — When he will preach what will not last long.
**“the mystery of God shall be finished”**
• Because in the time of Antichrist there will be so great a destruction, preaching is forbidden to those who will be in his time, although they wish to preach, since they too had from their predecessors the office of preaching. Those, however, preached for this reason, that they were appointed to it by Christ. And Christ appointed them because it was then the time for preaching, and he himself had come for this; but now behold the destruction of the time of Antichrist, contrary to the building up which Christ made, and by this consider that preaching is justly withdrawn.
• Or otherwise. Having described the cruelty of Antichrist, he adds the consolation they will then have: namely, that the faithful will consider such things about Christ in their heart, and this will be a consolation to them.
**“the mystery”** — That is, the reward of the saints, which is a secret: “which eye hath not seen, nor ear heard.”
**“as he hath declared”** — The intention of the prophets was first concerning the coming of the Lord and the consummation of the world.
10.8:
**“And I heard a voice”**
• Divine admonition.
• As if he said: the destruction that will be in the time of Antichrist having been shown, and preaching thereupon also withdrawn, and consolation on this account given to the faithful, he is bidden in the meantime to preach what he saw, as if it were said to him openly: behold, I have revealed all things to you; now go and preach, and do not avoid it because these things are harsh, nor be terrified by any tribulation, because you will not suffer as much as those will suffer who will persevere in the time of Antichrist; this is set down here for the consolation of the present Church, where a greater tribulation is announced.
**“from heaven again speaking to me”** — Concerning the same things.
**“and saying”** — Giving an account of the reason.
**“Go”** — He is admonished to understand what he knew well, so that through the admonition others who are to preach may be instructed.
**“and take”** — That is, understand it through it.
**“the book that is open”** — That is, to earn the grace of God.
**“from the hand of the angel who standeth”** — That is, ready to help all who approach.
**“who standeth upon the sea”** — Because it is hard to fulfil, for humanity is soft and fragile.
10.9:
**“And I went”**
• As one obedient, and he enlarged his mind.
• Because God, when he sees someone prepared, offers of his own accord what is necessary.
**“to the angel”** — That is, to the Scripture completed by God and made known to the faithful.
**“saying unto him”** — By work and by prayer.
**“that he should give me the book. And he said to me: Take the book”** — That is, by inquiring into the treatise and by working it out.
**“and eat it up: and it shall make thy belly bitter, but in thy mouth it shall be sweet as honey.”** — But it will be pleasing in thinking and preaching.
10.10:
**“And I took the book from the hand of the angel”** — That is, by following the work of Christ.
**“and ate it up: and it was in my mouth, sweet as honey”** — or sweet
10.11:
**“And he said to me: Thou must”**
• because you will go out of prison
• And he said to me, You must, etc. When I received it, though I understood it to be bitter, he warned me not to give it up even for death.

11.1:
**“And there was given me a reed”**
• Scripture written with a reed
• When he had enjoined the preaching, he gives helping Scriptures through which he may exercise it.
**“like unto a rod”** — that is, a sceptre, admonishing that he appoints kings
**“And it was said to me: Arise,”** — raise up to preach
**“Measure”** — That is, preach so, according to each one’s capacity, that you may establish the Church and in it an altar.
**“the temple of God, and the altar”** — that is, Christ
**“and them that adore therein.”** — that is, establish how they are to worship there
11.2:
**“The court”** — That is, false Christians who pretend to be the Church but deny it by their deeds.
**“cast out”** — by excommunicating, show that they are outside
**“and measure it not”** — withdraw the preaching altogether
**“because it is given unto the Gentiles”** — that is, they have become conformed to the Gentiles
**“and the holy city”** — and they themselves Gentiles
**“The holy city”** — That is, the Church, gathered to live justly and imbued with virtues, they will persecute for forty-two months, that is, three years and a half, in which Antichrist will reign; as if he said: know that all the persecutions which are in the present and which were in the past proceed from Antichrist, just as those will which will be in his time.
11.3:
**“And I will give unto my two”** — As if he said: when the tribulation is lesser you must not cease, because at the time when it is more grievous I will make them preach.
**“Unto my two witnesses”** — It concerns Elijah and Enoch, through whom other preachers are understood.
**“A thousand days”** — Note that these days do not make up three years and a half, just as Christ did not complete half a year of his preaching.
**“two hundred sixty”** — that is, for three years and a half, as Christ himself preached
**“clothed in sackcloth”** — that is, preaching penance and showing by example
11.4:
**“These are the two olive trees”**
• anointed in the Holy Spirit
• And you ought to preach after the example of these, for these men.
**“and the two candlesticks, before the Lord”** — kindling what pleases God
**“of the earth, that stand”** — giving light to others
11.5:
**“And if any man will hurt them”** — to call back from their purpose
**“fire”** — spiritual sentence
**“shall come out of their mouths, and shall devour”** — will condemn
**“their enemies. And if any man will hurt them”** — by bodily death
**“in this manner must he be slain.”** — that is, by spiritual sentence
11.6:
**“These have power to shut heaven”** — that is, the Scriptures which conceal mysteries
**“that it rain not in the days of their prophecy”** — because they will preach only in the fitting time.
**“over waters”** — That is, over their teachings, which are waters watering the faithful.
**“to turn them”** — as far as those whom they see rejected.
**“into blood”** — that is, sin.
**“Into blood”** — Into sin: either when what is heard is neglected, or when to be heard is even despised.
**“and to strike the earth”** — that is, earthly men.
**“with all plagues as often as they will.”** — remember the plagues of Egypt.
11.7:
**“And when they shall have finished their testimony”** — which will be for three years and a half.
**“the beast”** — Antichrist.
**“that ascendeth”** — that ascends: to the kingdom.
**“out of the abyss”** — through the dark ones.
**“shall make war against them”** — by disputations.
**“and shall overcome them, and kill them.”** — bodily.
11.8:
**“And their bodies shall lie in the streets”** — so that whoever see them may fear to be conformed to them.
**“of the city”** — Jerusalem.
**“great”** — once in virtues, now in malice.
**“which is called spiritually”** — that is, dumb, because no one will preach spiritually.
**“Egypt”** — That is, dark without knowledge of God.
**“where their Lord also”** — Christ.
**“their”** — Elijah and Enoch.
**“was crucified.”** — by contradicting the truth.
11.9:
**“And they shall see”** — some with their eyes, some by report.
**“of the tribes, and peoples, and tongues, and nations, shall see their bodies for three days and a half: and they shall not suffer their bodies to be laid in sepulchres.”** — so that their memory may not be kept.
11.10:
**“And they that dwell upon the earth shall rejoice over them, and make merry”** — the affliction of the just is the feast of the wicked.
**“And shall send gifts”** — Gifts literally, or mutual congratulations and conversations speaking of them.
**“one to another, because these two prophets tormented them”** — by contradicting iniquity.
**“them that dwelt upon the earth”** — or were dwelling.
11.11:
**“And after three days and a half”** — that is, three and a half years, namely after the death of Antichrist.
**“And after three days”** — Having shown their tribulation, by whose example he invited that man to preach, and if need be to suffer with them, he shows also their crowns, so that he may likewise make certain this John, or any other, of his own crown according to his measure.
**“the spirit of life”** — eternally giving life to all things.
**“from God entered”** — he is about to enter
**“into them. And they stood upon their feet”** — now immortal and impassible
**“Upon their feet”** — I.e., upon themselves, who before were not in need of anything to lean on, but will be firm.
**“and great fear”** — that is, infernal punishment or the reverence of God
**“fell”** — or “befell”
**“upon them”** — as a weight that presses down
**“that saw them”** — or “others”
11.12:
**“And they heard”** — thus glorified
**“a great voice”** — that is, of great power
**“A great voice”** — Which refreshes them and terrifies their enemies.
**“from heaven”** — from Christ or the archangel
**“saying”** — that is, doing these things
**“to them: Come up hither”** — that is, to the fellowship of the saints
11.13:
**“And at that hour there was made a great earthquake”** — that is, at the very time of their glorification, or in that hour when Elias and Enoch were slain
**“Earthquake”** — That is, earthly men were moved, that they may be punished in hell. Or, for the destruction of the Church, the teachers having been slain.
**“And the tenth part”** — That is, a man who seems appointed to this, so that the tenth order may be restored.
**“fell”** — into the punishments of the Church
**“were slain; names”** — Utterly destroyed in hell, or afterwards they did not come to their senses.
**“of men”** — whom God foreknew to death, so that the faithful may in no way be terrified
**“seven thousand”** — all perfected in wickedness
**“and the rest”** — when those fell into punishments or into sin
**“were cast into a fear”** — that is, into reverence of God, or they fear lest they fall
**“and gave glory to the God of heaven”**
• GLORY. That is, praises, to God for the salvation of the just and the damnation of the wicked.
• attributing nothing to themselves
11.15:
**“And the seventh angel”** — in the order of the narrative and of time
**“Was made”** — He who was before base and cast down now reigns, crowning the good and condemning the wicked.
**“of our Lord and of his Christ”** — that is, of the Father and the Son
**“And he shall reign”** — That is, his kingdom will remain in itself; not, as certain heretics think, that the saints will return to life in the world after a fixed time.
11.16:
**“The four and twenty ancients”** — Not only the lesser ones glorify God thus, but also the greater ones.
**“who in the sight of God”** — that is, considering what pleases God
**“sit”** — that is, they judge, which is in the present.
**“on their seats”** — that is, committed to them.
**“fell”** — that is, then they will humble themselves.
**“on their faces”** — that is, in their heart.
**“Fell on their faces”** — He falls on his face who in this life acknowledges his fault and weeps over it by repenting. He falls backward who in this life suddenly collapses and does not know to what punishments he is led.
**“and adored God”** — namely because here he had preserved them.
11.17:
**“saying: We give thee thanks, O Lord God Almighty”** — because you saved us and condemned our enemies.
**“who art”** — unchangeable.
**“and who wast”** — once, when you were despised.
**“and who art to come”** — by raising up the spirits of your own, by gathering the Church.
**“because thou hast taken to thee thy great power, and thou hast reigned”** — you defended your own from the devil.
11.18:
**“And”** — and for your kingdom.
**“the nations were angry, and thy wrath is come”** — against them.
**“and the time of the dead, that they should be judged”** — and the time has come to judge the dead, both of good and of evil.
**“and that thou shouldest render”** — the time has come.
**“reward to thy servants”** — that the good may be divided from the evil, or to judge as judges.
**“the prophets and the saints”** — providing for themselves and for others.
**“and to them that fear thy name”** — confirmed in faith.
**“little and great”** — and not so much the greater ones as whatever faithful ones.
**“and”** — and the time has come.
**“who have corrupted the earth”** — That is, themselves through evil works, and others through evil example.
11.19:
**“And the temple was opened”** — In this fourth vision he has his subject matter, a matter well adorned and having good aids, namely the battle of the Church, which is assailed by the devil both openly and secretly, and in all these things he shows that she overcomes; whereby he especially arms the faithful that they fail not in any tribulation.
**“And the temple of God was opened”** — It depends on the Church’s battle, and on the revelation of the woman, and depends on the third vision, which concerns the office of preaching that was enjoined.
**“The temple of God was opened”** — That is, the Holy Spirit was given, through whom the mysteries of the Church, which were prefigured by the second tabernacle, were revealed to the faithful.
**“in heaven”** — that is, the Church.
**“The ark”** — Christ is the ark “in whom all the treasures of wisdom are hidden,” who fulfilled the Old Testament and instituted the New.
**“of his testament in his temple”** — that is, in the Church which is in heaven through good living.
**“and there were”** — and understanding was given.
**“lightnings”** — miracles.
**“and voices”** — exhortations.
**“and an earthquake, and great hail”** — some to faith, some to wrath.
**“And great hail”** — Because the preaching seemed intolerable to some.

12.1:
**“And a great sign”**
• a figure signifying
• Sign. And from these things I saw that this proceeds, namely the grace of faith, that is, something great signifying.
• Here he makes mention of the revelation of the mysteries which were in the second vision, and of the enjoined office of preaching which we had in the third, that he may show this fourth, which is about the battle of the Church and the devil, to depend on these two, that is, the second and the third.
**“appeared in heaven”** — that is, in the Church
**“woman”** — that is, the Church
**“clothed with the sun”** — because she put on Christ, who illumines her
**“and the moon under her feet”** — all earthly things, which do not remain in the same state
**“The moon under her feet”** — Although it is supported by worldly things, nevertheless it does not aim at them.
**“and on her head”** — in Christ, or in the beginning of the Church
**“and on her head a crown”** — That is, the twelve apostles, by whom the world believed, or in whom it conquered the world.
12.2:
**“And being with child”** — that is, in the Virgin Mary
**“being”** — the Word of God
**“she cried”** — preached
**“travailing in birth”** — that is, desiring to bring forth others
**“was in pain”** — By preaching she suffers adversities, or is tormented by herself, that is, she mortifies her flesh, so that the preaching may be fit.
**“to be delivered”** — She brings forth when she sends her own into the light.
12.3:
**“And there was seen another sign in heaven”** — that is, in the Church to be assailed
**“and behold a great red dragon”** — because of the strength of great power
**“A great red dragon”** — He speaks not of the effect but of the power of the dragon.
**“red”** — because of murders
**“having seven heads”** — that is, all the princes through whom he works
**“and ten horns”** — And ten horns, etc. That is, kingdoms, riches, by which the princes attack the decalogue of the law.
**“and on his heads seven diadems”** — that is, all victories over the overthrown
12.4:
**“His tail”** — That is, the deceptions by which vices are hidden, as shameful things are hidden by a tail.
**“drew”** — from faith to unbelief
**“the third part”** — all the reprobate
**“of the stars”** — That is, of those who illumine the Church by teaching, not by life.
**“and cast them to the earth”** — that is, he enticed those drawn by love of earthly things
**“And the dragon”** — that is, the devil, trusting in such power
**“stood”** — not for an hour but laboring
**“before the woman”**
• against the Church
• Through the suffering, the devil believed the Church would be subjected to him.
**“Stood before the woman”** — She who was suffering pain, by which he believed she would soon cease.
**“who was ready to be delivered; that, when she should be delivered, her son”** — that is, had begotten someone in faith
**“he might devour”** — would draw back to sin
**“He might devour”** — The dragon was ready to devour, but could not, because one was born who forbade it.
12.5:
**“And she brought forth a man child, who was to rule all nations with an iron rod”** — in power or justice
**“And she brought forth”** — By carnal generation Christ came forth from Abraham and David. Or the Church brought forth a son, that is, the faith of Christ in the hearts of hearers.
**“iron rod”** — unbending
**“and her son was taken up”** — the flesh of the divinity
**“to God”** — to the equality of God
**“and to his throne”** — that he might judge with the Father
12.6:
**“And the woman”** — through the help of this son
**“fled”** — from the pleasures of the world
**“into the wilderness”** — the wilderness of the mind, with the tumult or pleasantness of the world despised
**“where she had a place prepared by God”** — forsaking the world, she is strengthened by God
**“that there”** — God
**“they should feed her”** — by the teaching of preaching
**“A thousand days”** — That is, for the whole time the Church endures, the preaching of Christ having been done in three years and a half.
12.7:
**“And there was”** — behold, another help
**“a great battle in heaven, Michael”** — the greater
**“and his angels”** — the lesser
**“fought”** — Sustaining the Church, by praying and bringing help.
12.8:
**“They prevailed not”** — To remove the help of the angels, because they could not lead the Church into sin.
**“neither was their place found any more in heaven”** — that is, in the Church as far as the good are concerned
12.9:
**“And that great dragon was cast out”** — by the help of these
**“that great dragon”** — for violence
**“serpent”** — for cunning
**“that old serpent”** — as if to say: beware of him, all of you
**“who is called the devil”** — that is, flowing apart from the good to the wicked
**“and Satan”** — that is, the adversary.
**“who seduceth the whole world”** — that is, the reprobate.
**“and he was cast unto the earth”** — falling from the faithful, he attacks more fiercely those who love earthly things.
12.10:
**“And I heard a loud voice”** — that is, exultation.
**“And I heard a voice”** — When he had shown that the devil in this hidden struggle was conquered by the Church with the help of the Son and of the angels, he adds the exultations of the angels themselves, or of the holy souls, over the victory of the brethren, that they may strive to conquer who hear the angels, or the holy souls, exult over their victory.
**“in heaven”** — in the angels or holy souls.
**“saying: Now is come”** — from the time of Christ; which is not in the nature of man.
**“salvation,”** — the forgiveness of sins in baptism.
**“and strength, and the kingdom of our God,”** — and he rules his own, directing them from virtue to virtue.
**“and the power of his Christ,”** — and he has accomplished all these things through Christ.
**“accused”** — It is the office of the devil to accuse, that is, to make men accusable through sin.
**“before our God”** — because nothing is hidden from God, by which he most terrifies.
**“day and night.”** — continually.
**“Day and night”** — Either by delighting them in prosperity or by saddening them in adversity.
12.11:
**“And they overcame”** — applying free will.
**“him”** — that is, his suggestion.
**“by the blood of the Lamb,”** — whom they imitate.
**“and by the word”** — because they do not keep silent where it is necessary.
**“of the testimony”** — that is, the faith to which Christ bore witness.
**“and they loved not their lives unto death.”** — that is, they did not so cherish their flesh that their souls should perish.
12.12:
**“Therefore rejoice, O heavens,”** — angels or saints.
**“and you that dwell therein.”** — the lesser saints dwell among the greater, or all dwell in the angels.
**“Woe to the earth, and to the sea,”** — that is, to those flowing into vices and fixed in the same vice.
**“is come down”** — From heaven, or from the lesser saints in whom temptation no longer has place.
**“the devil is come down unto you”** — to kill.
**“having great wrath, knowing that he hath but a short time.”** — whence he rages more fiercely.
**“knowing that he hath but a short time”** — Because he sees many being withdrawn from him and others put in their place.
12.13: **“And when the dragon saw”** — When the devil saw that he could not advance by hidden fraud, he attacks to overcome by open tribulation.
12.14:
**“And there were given to the woman”** — And there were given, etc. She who also has help against open tribulation from the same Son from whom she had it against secret attack.
**“two wings of a great eagle,”**
• the two testaments, or the two loves, or the two lives.
• eagles, who by the conduct of life seek heaven, and therefore have their gaze fixed on God.
**“that she might fly into the desert unto her place, where she is nourished for a time and times, and half a time”**
• that is, for three years and a half.
• For a time and times, etc. If the state of that Church which will be in the time of Antichrist is understood, “a time, and times, and half a time” is said in one way, for the preaching of Elias and Enoch. If the Church in general is understood, “a time, and times, and half a time” is said in another way, for the preaching of Christ made for three years and a half, by which preaching of Christ the Church is fed daily.
**“from the face of the serpent.”** — from the present assault.
12.15:
**“And”** — and although she was thus prepared.
**“the serpent cast out of his mouth”** — from the prompting.
**“after the woman,”** — because it does not reach her.
**“water as it were a river;”** — a flood of tribulation.
**“that he might cause her to be carried away by the river.”** — into sin.
12.16:
**“And the earth helped the woman”**
• or the saints by praying.
• Namely, Christ gave his Church the strength to endure.
**“and the earth opened”** — That is, she prepared herself and made herself fit to receive whatever they brought against her, in likeness to the opening of the mouth which he made in his passion, in which he set before his own an example of enduring.
**“the earth”** — the saints, steadfast as the earth.
**“swallowed up the river”** — That is, he destroyed all punishments in himself, having become immortal and impassible, which he does likewise in his own.
12.17:
**“And the dragon was angry”** — And the dragon was angry, etc. Because although he cannot overcome, he does not cease to envy and to seek a place to attack.
**“against the woman: and went to make war with the rest of her seed”** — with the lesser ones of the same Church.
**“who keep”** — they fulfil the works.
**“the commandments of God, and have”** — who, since they believe, do not fear to profess.

13.1:
**“And he stood”** — another reading: he stood.
**“And he stood upon the sand of the sea.”** — He did not, however, overcome all those lesser ones, but only upon the sand, that is, he made a stay among the unfruitful, in whom the signs of his footprints appear.
**“And I saw a beast coming up out of the sea”**
• Spiritually: Antichrist.
• or the sea is called the Jewish people, from whom Antichrist is born, namely of the tribe of Dan.
• that is, from the gathering of the wicked.
**“a beast”** — the whole body of the wicked.
**“coming up”**
• from the gathering of wicked princes.
• which is a prince, or exalting himself through other wicked men.
**“A beast”** — The beast is either specifically Antichrist, or generally the whole gathering of the wicked, or Antichrist entire, head and body.
**“having heads”** — that is, princes.
**“heads”** — For this, that he might be able to overcome them well, he set up such a retinue for himself.
**“seven”** — all the wicked.
**“and ten horns”** — that is, those through whom princes assail the Decalogue.
**“and upon his horns ten diadems,”** — because there is no commandment that is not broken by princes and of which they are not crowned.
**“and upon his heads”** — that is, the princes
**“names of blasphemy.”** — because they say that Christ was not God but a magician
**“names of blasphemy”** — It was full of various heresies, or concealing its vices under various pretences.
13.2:
**“And the beast, which I saw, was like to a leopard, and his feet”** — sent by the princes
**“as the feet of a bear”** — the greater in speech
**“and his mouth as the mouth of a lion.”** — because they devour and stink
**“And the dragon gave him”** — another by which they harm
**“his own strength”** — of performing miracles
**“and great power”** — of seducing many
13.3:
**“And I saw one”** — Antichrist
**“of his heads as it were slain to death”** — pretending himself as if dead
**“As it were slain”** — Antichrist will feign himself dead, and lying hidden for three days, will afterwards appear, saying that he has been raised.
**“his death's wound”** — in pretence
**“was healed”** — by the ascension
**“And his death's wound was healed”** — By magical art he will ascend into the air, the demons carrying him. And so the wound of his death will be healed, because he who was believed dead before will afterwards be reckoned living.
**“And all the earth was in admiration after the beast.”**
• imitating the beasts
• that is, Antichrist
13.4:
**“And they adored the dragon,”** — that is, the devil
