**“which gave power to the beast”** — because he gave the beast power to rise again, as it seemed
**“and they adored the beast”** — Antichrist
**“saying: Who”** — when he rose again
**“is like to the beast? and who shall be able to fight with him?”** — to resist his will
13.5:
**“And there was given to him”** — by the permission of God
**“a mouth speaking great things”** — exalting himself with great words
**“and blasphemies”** — because he will say that he is the Son of God
**“and power was given to him to do two and forty months.”** — that is, to act through months
**“And power was given”** — permitted
13.6:
**“And he opened his mouth”** — He broke out into such boldness that what before he dared to blaspheme secretly, he now dares to blaspheme openly.
**“unto blasphemies”** — by denying that God exists
**“against God,”** — that is, against God, or even to God
**“to blaspheme his name, and his tabernacle”** — that is, all those who are protected by those great ones
**“and his tabernacle”** — That is, all his teaching by which he appears praiseworthy.
**“them”** — or “them”
13.7: **“was given him to make war with the saints, and to overcome”** — bodily
13.8:
**“And all that dwell upon the earth adored”** — that is, given over to earthly things
**“whose names are not written”** — that is, the reprobate only
**“in the book of life of the Lamb”** — which book is the Lamb; for he himself is both the Lamb and the book
**“slain”** — In his own, as in Abel. Or because it was decreed before all things that he would be slain at the end of time. Or slain, that is, mystically in the lamb which Abel offered. Or he was foreshadowed in Abel himself, slain by his brother.
13.9:
**“If any man”** — as if to say: beware, all of you
**“have an ear”** — understanding
**“let him hear”** — let him understand
13.10:
**“He that shall lead into captivity”**
• into infernal punishments
• He who takes men captive now from the faith, at last from salvation: namely Antichrist or the devil himself.
**“he that shall kill by the sword, must”**
• or it will be necessary
• He that shall kill by the sword, etc. Antichrist and his followers kill with the material sword, and with the sword of persuasion, and they will perish by the sword of eternal judgment.
**“be killed by the sword. Here is the patience”**
• that is, with regard to punishments and reward
• By looking to the punishment of the wicked and the reward of the good, they become patient and hold to the faith.
**“Here is the patience”** — That is, they will keep patience and faith, because, he having been destroyed, they know they will be rewarded.
**“and the faith of the saints.”** — And I saw. Having described the tribulation that will come through Antichrist and his partners, he adds another that will come through his apostles, whom he will scatter throughout the whole world.
13.11:
**“And I saw”** — lesser than the former
**“another beast”** — false apostles
**“coming up”** — making progress into pride or perdition
**“out of the earth”** — through those who love earthly things
**“and he had two horns, like a lamb”** — because if anything good is seen in them, it will be pretence
**“two horns”** — Because they will pretend to have innocence, and a pure life, and true doctrine, and the miracles that Christ had and gave to his own. Or they will usurp to themselves the two testaments.
**“and he spoke as”** — That is, the false apostles will speak as the devil spoke in Antichrist.
13.12:
**“And he executed all the power”** — Because in all things they put their head, namely Antichrist, before themselves.
**“in his sight”** — that is, all the ways of deceiving by which Antichrist deceived
**“the earth”** — That is, earthly people who persist in love of earth. Or, earth according to the body, dwelling in it according to the soul.
**“and them that dwell therein, to adore the first beast”** — Antichrist
**“whose wound to death was healed”** — To adore the first beast, whose wound to death was healed. Because these also, by a feigned resurrection of their preaching, lay the foundation, as the apostles of Christ also did.
13.13:
**“And he did great signs”** — for the confirmation of his preaching
**“so that he made also fire”**
• Fire. That is, he will make an evil spirit come down upon his own, so that they speak in various tongues.
• As the Holy Spirit was given to the apostles in the form of fire, so they too will give an evil spirit in the form of fire.
**“in the sight of men”** — In the sight of men. That all may be able to see it, as the apostles received it in the upper room.
13.14:
**“And he seduced them that dwell on the earth, for the signs, which were given him to do”** — by the permission of God
**“in the sight of the beast”** — in invoking the name of Antichrist
**“saying”** — commanding
**“to them that dwell on the earth, that they should make the image”**
• conforming themselves to him
• or literally, that is, some statue
**“of the beast, which had the wound by the sword”** — of death
**“and lived.”** — rose again
13.15:
**“And it was given him”** — by the devil; by the promise of God
**“to give life to the image of the beast”** — conforming to Antichrist
**“and that ... should speak”** — in diverse tongues
**“the image of the beast”** — that is, those conforming to it
**“That the image should speak”** — He who by magic art will make the statue speak and foretell the future.
**“and should cause”** — and make it, through the princes of the world
**“that whosoever will not adore the image of the beast”** — that is, conforming themselves to it, or literally
**“should be slain”** — by death of the body
13.16:
**“And he shall make all, both little and great, rich and poor, freemen and bondmen”** — because they will say their God is to receive all and cast out no one
**“to have a character in their right hand, or on their foreheads”** — To have a mark, etc. They will put marks on the hand and on the forehead, so that all confess their God by word and deed.
13.17:
**“And that no man might buy or sell”** — literally, or to acquire the servants of God, or in the spiritual sense
**“but he that hath the character, or the name of the beast”** — because they were marked with his name and will confess him
**“or the number”** — or name
**“of his name”** — The number of the name. That is, those who look to him for a lesser, middling, or greatest reward.
13.18:
**“Here is wisdom”** — because an obscure matter makes them attentive
**“He that hath understanding”** — Since the book was published in Greek, the number is to be sought according to the Greeks, among whom all letters signify a number. His name is Antemos, which suits him who is called contrary to Christ: A one, N fifty, T three hundred, E five, M forty, O seventy, S two hundred. Or Arnoyme, that is, I deny, who denies that Christ is God, in which the number is the same: A one, R two hundred, N fifty, O seventy, Y four hundred, M forty, E five. Or Teytan, that is, sun giant, which truly belongs to Christ, but by usurpation to Antichrist: T three hundred, E five, I ten, again T three hundred, A one, N fifty. Or in Latin letters, Dic lux (Say: light), because he will say that he himself is the light: D five hundred, that is, one, C a hundred, L fifty, V five, X ten, and so the same sum. Six is the first perfect number, and signifies those less perfect who are married and in their own measure keep the ten commandments. Sixty signifies the moderately perfect, who, having left lawful marriages, remain in chastity and again fulfil the ten commandments in their own measure. A hundred signifies the most perfect, who do not violate the integrity of mind and body, and keep the ten commandments most perfectly. These yield fruit, some thirtyfold, some sixtyfold, some a hundredfold. And the disciples of Antichrist will then say that no one can be saved unless he offers Antichrist some of those fruits.
**“let him count the number”** — or name
**“of the beast. For it is the number of a man”** — although God seems to be shown by this; to the wise, a pure man will appear
**“and the number of him is six hundred sixty-six”** — Of all, the firstfruits; as from the flock the best horse, or from the fruits the firstfruits.

14.1:
**“And I beheld”** — Having shown the most grievous persecution that the Church will suffer from Antichrist and his apostles, he shows, for consolation, what helper it has and what kind of company he himself has.
**“and lo a lamb”** — Christ sacrificed for us
**“stood”** — as helping
**“upon mount Sion”** — that is, the Church, lofty in virtues and contemplating God
**“an hundred forty-four thousand”** — Most perfect in virginity, gathered in faith in the Trinity from the four parts of the world.
**“having”** — such as they were
**“his name”** — because they will be called Christians
**“and the name of his Father”** — because they will be called 'gods'
**“written”** — indelibly
**“on their foreheads”** — because they openly confess
14.2:
**“And I heard a voice”** — desire or for admonition
**“from heaven”** — from those who were with him
**“as the noise of many waters”** — that is, of many peoples, because they were gathered from many peoples
**“of great thunder”** — Because it terrifies those who flee to come to their fellowship.
**“and the voice which I heard”** — or 'was'
**“of harpers”** — Because they themselves trained themselves for this, to stretch out their devoted hearts upon the wood of the cross.
**“harping on their harps”** — not alien ones
**“harping”** — What they had from their office they fulfilled by their work.
14.3:
**“And they sung”** — That is, they will exult in the integrity of soul and body, a joy that will never grow old for them, but is always for them as new.
**“as it were a new canticle, before the throne”** — that is, in the presence of those on whom he sits
**“and before the four living creatures”** — that is, preachers
**“and the ancients”** — that is, judges
**“and no man could say the canticle”** — that is, to rejoice in their integrity
**“but those”** — that is, those virgins
**“hundred forty-four thousand, who were purchased from the earth”** — therefore, because you are of the earth, do not despair
**“who were purchased”** — That is, those whom the blood of Christ raised up to be virgins.
14.4:
**“These are they who were not defiled with women”** — with some filth of the world, or literally
**“for they are virgins. These follow the Lamb”** — that is, they imitate Christ
**“whithersoever he goeth”** — in integrity of soul and body
**“These were purchased from among men, the firstfruits to God”** — to the Father
**“and to the Lamb”** — Christ.
14.5:
**“And in their mouth”** — or of them.
**“there was found no”** — even if it was at some time.
**“found”** — it is found in those in whom it remains.
**“lie”** — of the word.
**“for they are without spot”** — in works.
**“before the throne of God”** — before God the judge.
14.6:
**“And I beheld”** — The attack made through the two beasts having been described, and the help of the Lamb having been set down and the dignity of his family shown, an admonition is added, that they should come to this family, and a warning that they should turn away from the other.
**“another”** — Another. That is, preachers who are other than Christ, that is, carrying out his office.
**“angel”** — a lesser one.
**“flying through the midst of heaven”** — withdrawing himself from earthly things.
**“through the midst of heaven”** — Through the common Church, which they draw along with them by words and examples.
**“having”** — from the office enjoined.
**“eternal gospel”** — and he had this for this reason.
**“The eternal gospel”** — That is, a preaching promising eternal things, leading those who fulfil it to eternity.
**“to preach unto them that sit upon the earth”** — that is, dwelling in contempt of the world.
**“and over every nation, and tribe, and tongue, and people”** — namely, every kind of variety of those who linger in earthly things.
14.7:
**“Saying with a loud voice”** — by persuasion.
**“Fear”** — with chaste love.
**“the Lord”** — not those beasts.
**“all his saints”** — The words all his saints are lacking in many copies.
**“and give him honour”** — or glory.
**“Fear and give him honour”** — By acting well, and by announcing him well, so that through you he may appear glorious.
**“because the hour of his judgment is come”** — As if you should not fail, because you will not suffer for a long time.
**“and adore ye him”** — by making yourselves conformed to him.
**“that made heaven and earth, the sea, and the fountains of waters”** — even if you fear failure, ask him for help.
14.8:
**“And another angel followed”**
• according to the different proclamation.
• Because preachers succeed one another.
**“is fallen”** — Placed twice, it signifies infinity, or it has the force by which total destruction is understood.
**“That great Babylon”** — that is, all those confused in vices.
**“great”** — because of the multitude or the pride
**“which made all nations to drink of the wine of the wrath of her fornication”**
• fortified with a perverse doctrine
• Pure wine is drunk while God here scourges for correction; the turbid wine is poured out when eternal damnation is inflicted.
**“the wine of the wrath of her fornication”** — That is, with vices, and especially idolatry, which is the sweet drink of sinners, with which they defile others and make them drunk, so that they do not walk the straight path; whence the wrath of God is owed to them.
**“made all nations to drink”** — living as Gentiles
14.9:
**“And the third angel”**
• not fearful
• He puts three for the faith of the Trinity, since these three can be considered in the same person.
**“followed them, saying with a loud voice: If any man shall adore the beast”** — that is, Antichrist
**“and his image”** — that is, he makes himself conformed to him
**“and receive his character”** — the sign of his name
**“in his forehead”** — who confess him
**“or in his hand”** — who is changed by work
14.10:
**“He also shall drink”** — as Babylon
**“of the wine of the wrath of God”** — from eternal damnation
**“which is mingled”** — As if to say: he who is not corrected by his vengeance, given for correction, will be punished with eternal pain.
**“in the cup”** — The cup is the vengeance of God, where above is the pure wine, which here avenges for correction; below is the dregs, that is, damnation, which the wicked will drink in the last times. So from the wine, that is, from the dregs, which he wants to show as turbid in comparison with the pure, he adds that it is mixed.
**“of his wrath”** — which God, angered, pours out
**“and shall be tormented with fire and brimstone”** — that is, with stench
**“in the sight of the holy angels”** — so that, when their brightness is seen, he may melt away
14.11:
**“And the smoke”** — that is, darkness
**“And the smoke of their torments”** — Because he enumerates certain things about the damnation of the wicked: he does not say this to describe damnation, but only to strike terror into those whom he deters from their fellowship.
**“shall ascend”** — will persevere
**“shall ascend up for ever and ever”** — When he says it ascends forever, he notes that the eternal punishment continues, where he adds: they have no rest.
**“neither have they rest”** — It is as if it is not surprising that those who adored Antichrist will be punished in his time, since his preceding ministers too will have the same penalty.
**“and whoever receiveth”** — likewise they have no rest
**“the character of his name”** — indiscriminately, any sign of the aforesaid things
14.12:
**“Here is the patience”** — that is, in view of the eternal pain
**“of the saints”** — and theirs
**“Here is the patience of the saints”** — That is, here the saints ought to suffer patiently, lest they come to eternal pain.
**“who keep”** — they complete by work
**“the commandments of God”** — of the twofold love
**“and the faith of Jesus”** — because they confess him to be God
14.13:
**“And I heard a voice from heaven, saying to me”** — as those wretched, but these happy
**“Write”** — in your heart, and of the hearers
**“Blessed are the dead”** — to the world
**“who die in the Lord”** — in confession of the Lord
**“who die”** — when body and soul are loosed
**“From henceforth now, saith”** — from the time of the resurrection
**“the Spirit”** — that is, the whole Trinity
**“that they may rest”** — that they may suffer no more
**“from their labours”** — of their labours, which they have suffered until now
**“for their works follow them”** — Works: that is, the rewards of works, which follow them; for while they were in the world, greater tribulations pressed on them for a greater crown, whence they were held so despised; but now they will suffer nothing.
14.14:
**“And I beheld”** — And I saw. Having shown the reward of the good, by which he invites them to their fellowship, he adds the damnation of the wicked, so that by fear he may lead to the same purpose.
**“And behold a white cloud”** — that is, the saints, or the Lord’s flesh
**“and upon”** — Christ sits above the saints, or the divinity above the humanity
**“the cloud one sitting”** — I say
**“like to the Son of man”** — because now impassible and immortal
**“one like to the Son of man”** — Because he was no longer truly the Son of man, being immortal.
**“having on his head”** — in himself, or in the divinity
**“a crown of gold”**
• in likeness of one triumphing
• because he conquered the devil by wisdom
**“and in his hand”** — by power
14.15:
**“And another angel”** — from Christ
**“Angel”** — That is, the saints who until now were hidden among the faithful appear in brightness, about to judge, praying with desire that God make the separation of the good and the wicked.
**“came out from the temple”** — in that the servant
**“Came out from the temple”** — The saints are said to come out of the temple when they now appear not as they once were, but as they are to remain forever.
**“crying with a loud voice to him that sat upon the cloud”** — to Christ
**“Thrust in thy sickle”**
• exercise judgement
• That is, the judicial sentence separating the wicked from the good.
**“and reap”** — that is, gather your own
**“because the hour is come”** — or: has come
**“Because the hour”** — Because it is now the right time, since the number of your people has been completed.
**“to reap, for the harvest of the earth is ripe”**
• or, has dried up
• because the wickedness of the wicked is preserved and no longer has a place
14.16: **“And he that sat on the cloud thrust his sickle into the earth, and the earth was reaped.”** — that is, he separated the good from the wicked
14.17:
**“And another angel”**
• the aforesaid saints having another office
• Since he had shown that God, who has the power of judging, is implored by the saints, and so judgment is made, he shows that the saints have the same power, and that Christ commands them to judge, and they obey the command.
**“Another angel”** — That is, Christ, who had been hidden and lowly among the faithful, appeared clear, and coming from the altar, that is, from a more secret place, which never happened to other saints, being known by all as consubstantial with God.
**“came out of the temple”** — showed what sort he was
**“which is in heaven”** — that is, from a secret place
**“he also having a sharp sickle”** — as Christ
14.18:
**“And another angel came out from the altar”** — that is, from the more secret place in which the saints are
**“who had power”** — as if he could well receive, because he could also give
**“over fire”** — that is, eternal punishment
**“and water”** — or over demons and wicked men
**“and cried with a loud voice”** — with a great command
**“to him”** — that is, to the saints
**“that had the sharp sickle”** — judicial power
**“saying: Thrust in”** — that is, exercise judgment
**“thy sharp sickle, and gather the clusters of the vineyard of the earth”**
• that is, separate those ripe in wickedness
• Thrust in thy sickle, and gather, etc. By the harvest of the earth and the grapes of the vine of these same wicked, condemnation is understood; but nevertheless by the vineyard we have those more definitely who worked evils with greater zeal, as greater care is applied to the vine than to the earth, so that it may bear fruit.
**“because the grapes thereof are ripe”** — because their malice is complete
14.19:
**“And”** — and with such a command
**“the angel thrust in his sharp sickle”** — namely, the company of the good
**“into the earth”** — into earthly men who are to be judged
**“and gathered the vineyard of the earth, and cast it into the great press of the wrath of God”** — that is, into hell, where many will suffer the wrath of God
**“And cast it into the great press”** — Whence the prophet: “out of the lake wherein there is no water,” that is, refreshment.
14.20:
**“And the press was trodden”** — that is, they are punished, placed in hell
**“without”** — because that punishment will not be purgatorial
**“the city”** — the Church and the congregation of the good, which is the sanctified city
**“and blood came out of the press, up to the horses' bridles”** — That is, as far as the rulers of the subjects.
**“And blood came out”** — Eternal punishment for sin; blood, not wine, which is put in the cellar of God.
**“Up to the bridles”** — That is, as far as the very rulers of the wicked, namely the devils, who are to be punished.
**“for a thousand and six hundred furlongs”** — That is, through all the voluptuous who play with vanities.
**“For a thousand and six hundred furlongs”** — All held by the games of the world, that is, by vices, who are either perfect in the simple sense, as we have through six, or more perfect, as through a hundred, or most perfect, as through a thousand.
**“a thousand”** — Perfect in evil.
**“and six hundred”** — Middling and even lesser.

15.1:
**“And I saw”**
• And I saw. In the three visions above, that is, the revelation of the mysteries, and the giving of the trumpets, and the battle of the woman against the devil from the beginning of the redemption, he has followed the order down to the day of judgment. But in these three following he dwells upon the last times, because of the former things it is said more fully in other divine Scriptures, but of these, little and more obscurely. In this fifth vision, therefore, the matter is the seven angels holding vials in which are contained the plagues, that is, the destructions of the wicked who will be in the time of Antichrist; which destruction especially exhorts those now present to suffer.
• In these three visions he speaks of three, though the four above-mentioned are four; but, the first, which was about the correction of the Churches, being omitted, he speaks of the other three, by way of consideration however.
**“another sign”** — That is, a figure signifying another thing.
**“in heaven, great and wonderful”** — Because those who are signified dwell in heaven.
**“And wonderful”** — It is wonderful that a man has such power that he can condemn others.
**“angels”** — Preachers.
**“Seven plagues”** — That is, all the blinding and destruction of those who will be in the time of Antichrist.
**“last”** — That is, enjoined on them by God.
**“For in them”** — They will truly be plagues, because they will exercise the wrath of God upon the wicked; and truly the last, because God will bring no others into the world after them.
15.2:
**“And”** — And with those angels.
**“I saw as it were a sea of glass mingled with fire”** — Because in it the baptized receive the Holy Spirit.
**“As it were a sea”** — That is, baptism, where purity of faith is required and men are cleansed from vices.
**“and them that had overcome the beast”** — That is, Antichrist.
**“and his image”** — That is, imitating his conformity, or his life.
**“and the number of his name”** — Who have not been deceived by these.
**“standing”** — They stand who keep the grace of baptism whole.
**“Having the harps”** — That is, mortifying the flesh, which God enjoined on them, or which he himself first did.
15.3:
**“And singing the canticle of Moses, the servant of God”** — Fulfilling it with exultation.
**“The canticle of Moses”** — That is, the old law; and it is exultation to those who understand well, that is, spiritually.
**“and the canticle of the Lamb”** — That is, the New Testament.
**“saying:”** — Admonishing others.
**“Great”** — In the first creation.
**“and wonderful”** — In the re-creation.
**“are thy works, O Lord God Almighty; just”** — Because they render to each according to his merit.
**“and true”** — because they lead where they promise
**“are thy ways”** — That is, the institutions of God, through which we come to God, or through which he comes to us, are just, because they repay each one according to his merit, and true because they lead where they promise.
**“O King of saints”** — or 'of ages'
15.4:
**“Who”** — therefore
**“shall not fear thee, O Lord”** — that is, out of fear he will serve you
**“and magnify thy name”**
• by work and by preaching
• and truly they will fear
**“For thou only art holy”**
• because you save freely
• and truly they will magnify
**“for all nations”** — some of all
**“shall come”** — by faith
**“and shall adore”** — “In spirit and in truth”
**“in thy sight”**
• in good pleasure
• and truly they will magnify
**“Thy judgments are manifest”** — Because you choose some and reject some, so that the faithful may know that they are from justice.
15.5:
**“And after these things”**
• namely, the things that were foretold
• Since he had shown that those angels have power to smite, and was about to tell what plagues they are to inflict, he first sets forth the cause by which he shows that those are worthy who are to suffer the plagues, namely that all the mysteries of the Church have been revealed to all who wish to enter, which these, by their evil desert, cannot understand.
**“I looked”** — that is, I knew by the Spirit revealing
**“and behold, the temple was opened”**
• that is, the hidden things or sacraments of Christ
• The temple was opened. That is, the mysteries of the Church are revealed, in which God dwells and which fight for the honour of God.
**“of the tabernacle”** — of the militant Church
**“of the testimony in heaven”** — that is, which contains in itself the Old and New Testament
15.6:
**“And the seven angels came out”** — that is, all preachers
**“And came out”** — And because they were thus open, preachers will go out and rebuke those who work evil.
**“having the seven plagues”** — that is, the fullness of understanding of the Scriptures, which are the plagues
**“out of the temple”** — after they have strengthened those who are the Church
**“clothed”** — sent by Jesus Christ
**“with linen”** — that is, Christ in baptism
**“clean”**
• because without sin
• in steadfastness
**“and white”**
• from vices
• because of their manner of life
**“and girt”**
• with virtues
• namely, as a sign of the office of prelates
**“about the breasts”** — also evil thoughts
**“with golden girdles”** — the bond of charity
15.7:
**“And one”** — Because what they will preach they will have from the teaching of the earlier fathers, who are all called one, because they teach one thing.
**“of the four living creatures”** — that is, the first preachers, or Christ himself, who was the four living creatures
**“gave to the seven angels”** — that is, to the preachers
**“seven golden vials”**
• that is, he made them vessels containing the wrath of God
• enlightened by divine wisdom
**“of the wrath”** — That is, of anger, because they correct; they rebuke with the wrath of God, threaten sinners, and sometimes even excommunicate.
**“of God, who liveth”** — namely, also powerful to punish
**“for ever and ever”** — that is, for eternity
15.8:
**“And the temple was filled”** — that is, Scripture, namely as far as the wicked are concerned
**“with smoke”** — by obscurity
**“from the majesty of God”** — by the presence of God
**“and from his power”** — because what he shuts, no one opens
**“and no man was able”**
• concerning the reprobate
• Smoke, etc. No man, etc. Although then all things will be open to the faithful, yet they will be closed and obscure to unbelievers.
**“to enter into the temple”** — namely, through true understanding, because their malice has blinded them
**“to enter”** — That is, to understand that hidden judgment of God, why he chooses some and rejects others, until at the end of the world the saints shall openly know. Or to enter the Church in the meantime, until the complete damnation of the wicked is fulfilled in the judgment, because afterwards it is certain they will not enter.
**“till the seven plagues of the seven angels were fulfilled”** — in punishment he opens the eyes that guilt shut

16.1:
**“I heard”** — That is, I understood the preachers who will carry out this vengeance, attributing it not to themselves but to the Lord, and affirming that it is done justly.
**“a great voice”** — that is, a divine inspiration or some admonition
**“out of the temple”** — in the Church or in heaven
**“saying to the seven angels: Go, and pour out”**
• for they ought not to preach unless they are sent
• Under the sixth seal and under the sixth angel he often spoke of the same evils, but with this regard, that he showed what kind and how great tribulations they would bring upon the saints; and if even there there was some word about the damnation of the wicked, he set it down incidentally, for the confirmation of those who suffer. But here he speaks only of the plagues which the saints themselves will bring upon the wicked.
**“Go, and pour out”** — You who are good, advance as far as concerns yourselves, and exercise damnation upon the wicked. Advance belongs to go; exercise, to pour out. Since these now preach, and what they preach is open, and yet some refuse to enter, they have an opportunity of smiting, and in this a divine admonition.
**“the seven vials of the wrath of God”** — that is, announce the due punishments to sinners
**“upon the earth.”** — upon earthly men
16.2:
**“And the first went”** — that is, the first order of preachers
**“and poured out his vial”** — his preaching
**“upon the earth.”** — literally, the apostles first preached to the Jews, that is, upon the Jews who love earthly things
**“and there fell a sore and grievous wound”**
• that is, a harmful condemnation
• namely, as regards the understanding of the blinded
**“wound”** — In obedience is the cause why that wound is made.
**“and grievous”**
• because they are unwilling to receive Christ
• namely, as regards the effect
**“upon men”** — namely, those who receive Antichrist instead of Christ
**“who had the character”** — that is, faith
**“of the beast”** — of Antichrist; or covetous men are signified, who live in the likeness of the beast
**“and upon them that adored”** — Psalm: “The idols of the Gentiles are silver and gold, the works of the hands of men.”
**“the image thereof.”** — that is, against those who will be conformed to his preachers
16.3:
**“And the second”** — in the office
**“poured out his vial”** — the preaching of divine vengeance
**“upon the sea.”**
• against those who crush the saints
• against the lustful
**“and there came blood”** — that is, the vengeance for the blood which they shed
**“And there came blood”** — That is, the condemnation of it is brought upon them for the blood which they shed.
**“blood”** — That is, that condemnation will be as of the dead, that is, irrevocable. For as the dead do not return to life, so that sentence of condemnation will not be revoked.
**“as it were of a dead man”** — because they will not rise again from that condemnation
**“and every living soul”** — that is, which seemed to live
**“every living soul”** — All who consent, who seem to live, because they do not openly persecute, but they will be condemned on account of their consent.
**“died in the sea.”** — that is, in the bitterness of the Gentile state
16.4:
**“And the third poured out his vial upon the rivers”** — that is, against the false apostles of Antichrist, who will corrupt the Scriptures, either the greater or the lesser ones
**“and the fountains of waters; and there was made blood.”**
• that is, vengeance and retribution for their sins
• Upon the rivers and the fountains of waters, etc.; and there was made blood. Because these likewise will be condemned for the blood they shed, either bodily or spiritually.
16.5:
**“I heard”** — That is, I understood the preachers themselves, who will make this vengeance, attributing it not to themselves but to the Lord and affirming that it is done justly.
**“angel”** — the guardian
**“of the waters”** — of the Scriptures or of the peoples
**“saying:”** — that is, praising with inward affection
**“Thou art just”** — namely, by keeping justice
**“O Lord”** — namely, by presiding over all
**“who art,”** — unchangeably
**“and who wast”** — that is, essentially
**“who art, and who wast”** — He does not say “who is to come,” because he understood that he is to come soon.
**“the Holy One,”** — that is, formally and effectively
**“because thou hast judged these things:”** — who through us condemned those wicked ones
16.6:
**“For they have shed the blood of saints and apostles”** — of the lesser ones
**“and prophets”** — of the greater ones
**“have shed, and thou hast given them blood to drink;”**
• that is, eternal and dreadful punishment, as blood
• Thou hast given them blood to drink, etc. That is, eternal punishment for the shedding of blood, which they are to earn by having taken delight in it.
16.7:
**“And I heard another”**
• that is, their disciple
• And I heard another, etc. What the masters say, the disciples confirm.
**“saying:”** — that is, approving
**“Yea”** — What you say is true.
**“Yea, O Lord God Almighty”** — From great affection they turn their speech to God.
**“true and just”** — For it is just that he who shed blood should drink the vengeance of blood.
**“thy judgments.”** — what they promise is effective
16.8:
**“And the fourth angel poured out his vial upon the sun,”**
• into vainglory
• Antichrist, who calls himself the sun of the world
**“and it was given”** — permitted by God
**“unto him”** — to Antichrist
**“with heat”** — that is, of ambition
**“to afflict men”** — with greater tribulation
**“and fire:”** — with lesser
16.9:
**“and men were scorched”** — that is, some failed in that tribulation
**“And men were scorched”** — Or the afflicted will afflict the tormentors with the heat of wrath, while they are found inseparable, and so they were scorched with envy and anger.
**“men”**
• that is, the faithful
• that is, the afflicted
**“with great heat, and they blasphemed”** — that is, in heart and mouth
**“the name of God, who hath power”** — because to whom he wills he gives, from whom he wills he takes away
**“over these plagues, neither did they penance”**
• that is, they did not come to their senses, nor did they confess their sin
• Neither did they penance, etc. Inwardly they grieved as penitents; outwardly they did not dare to confess.
**“to give him glory”** — Even though they grieved in heart, they did not dare to bring it forth.
16.10:
**“And the fifth angel”** — That is, the ministers.
**“poured out his vial upon the seat”** — That is, upon every body.
**“Upon the seat”** — Because they are bodies only and not spirits, upon whom he will sit, because he will give bodily and not spiritual things.
**“of the beast”** — Of Antichrist.
**“And his kingdom became”** — That is, the seat itself.
**“dark”** — That is, more blinded.
**“and they gnawed their tongues”**
• by detracting from the truth.
• That is, they were refreshed, each by the evil speech of the other.
• They gnawed their tongues, etc. All feeding on one another by mutual detraction.
**“for pain”** — That is, for the envy they have toward the saints.
16.11:
**“And they blasphemed”** — saying that he was a magician and a mere creature.
**“the God of heaven”** — That is, by the blows inflicted, by which they are blinded.
**“because of their pains and wounds”** — which they themselves caused by gnawing their tongues.
**“and did not penance for their works”** — That is, they remained impenitent to the end.
16.12:
**“And the sixth angel poured out his vial”** — That is, he preached the wrath of God.
**“upon that great river”** — upon all who abound in riches.
**“Euphrates”** — Euphrates is interpreted as ‘fertility’.
**“and dried up the water thereof”** — That is, they will preach that the abundance of the world is soon to be dried up.
**“that a way might be prepared for the kings from the rising of the sun”**
• namely, to attack the Church.
• That a way might be prepared, etc. Because, when the world is finished, there will be the resurrection of the faithful, who will come from the rising of the sun, that is, from Christ, when he begins to shine, that is, to manifest himself. Another translation has ‘to the king’, that is, to Christ.
16.13:
**“I saw”** — The pouring out of the vial upon these and upon themselves, that they are not corrected, but are hurled into greater blindness.
**“from the mouth of the dragon”** — from the words of Antichrist’s apostles.
**“and from the mouth of the beast”** — from the prompting of the devil.
**“and from the mouth of”** — that is, from the counsel.
**“the false prophet, three unclean spirits”** — namely, through the subtlety of their malice, by denying the faith of the Trinity.
**“Spirits”** — That is, all the impious, who on account of their excessive malice are to be called unclean spirits; or the demons themselves, whom they generate in the hearts of others. As the faithful generate the faith of Christ in the hearts of others by their teaching, so these generate the devil by their malice.
**“unclean”** — on account of their works of uncleanness.
**“Frogs”** — Frogs dwell in mud, and are noisy, and take rest from others; so do these too.
**“like frogs”** — such are the hypocrites
16.14:
**“For they are the spirits of devils”** — truly unclean
**“working signs”** — miracles
**“and they go forth”** — namely sent by Antichrist
**“unto the kings of the whole earth”** — of the world
**“to gather them”** — namely not as to unity of place but of consent and evil will
**“to battle”** — against the faithful
**“against the great day of the Almighty God”** — but to their own harm, how quickly they will be led to the day of judgment
16.15:
**“Behold, I come”** — he will truly come, because he himself testifies
**“as a thief”**
• as a thief, killing those sleeping
• and therefore
**“Blessed is he that watcheth”** — that is, who is anxious about his own salvation
**“and keepeth his garments”** — the innocence received in baptism
**“lest he walk naked”** — from virtues
**“walk”** — rise again
**“and they see”** — saints and angels
**“his shame”** — sins
16.16:
**“And he shall gather them together”**
• the devil himself, who is in all of them
• That is, they will make them have confidence in Antichrist, who is the refuge of all who wish to steal their faith from the saints, or in whom all evil men of various sects will glory.
**“go forth”** — He shall gather them together. The demons go forth, and the devil will gather them, because they are all one.
**“into a place”** — they go forth to gather and will gather
**“which in Hebrew is called Armagedon”** — 'mountain of thieves' or 'round mountain'
16.17:
**“And the seventh angel poured out his vial upon the air”** — that is, against the devils whose place is the air
**“And the seventh”** — And the seventh. Having shown upon whom the angels pour out their vials, he adds what befalls these evil ones through this outpouring, namely that here they will resist as much as they can, as though they had received increase from the very infusion; but at last they will be thrust down into hell.
**“and there came”** — that is, came into the open
**“a great voice”** — that is, announcing greatly
**“out of the temple”** — from the Church
**“from the throne”** — which the Church conceived from God
**“saying: It is done”** — all things are finished and the end of the world is at hand
16.18:
**“And there were”** — by those evil ones or by those good ones
**“lightnings”** — miracles
**“and voices,”** — flatteries
**“and thunders”** — threats
**“and there was a great earthquake”** — that is, the wicked will be stirred up against the saints
**“such an one as never had been since men were upon the earth”** — that is, from the time of Abel, who first trod the earth, that is, despised it, or who was the first just man
**“upon the earth”** — so base
**“such an earthquake, so great”** — that is, so grievous
16.19:
**“And the great city was divided”** — that is, the gathering of the reprobate
**“And the city was divided”** — Because of that condemnation and because of the sins that they add, the city itself is condemned, and its punishment is divided to each one according to merit: Jews, namely, and Gentiles, and false Christians.
**“into three parts”** — namely Jews, pagans, and wicked Christians
**“cities”** — That is, all gatherings of the wicked who remain in the first generation will be condemned.
**“and the cities”** — Carnal, not in the second, spiritual regeneration.
**“of the Gentiles”** — that is, of those living as Gentiles
**“fell. And great Babylon”** — that is, the gathering of sinners
**“came in remembrance before God”** — namely, to punish
**“came in remembrance”** — That is, God has remembered each of the sins of those whom before he seemed to have forgotten.
**“to give her the cup”** — So that God himself might give them a punishment measured out for the pleasures they had.
**“to give her the cup of the wine”** — God repays the wicked according to their merits, that is, what they have deserved, but not as much as they have deserved, so that in the repayment itself, where justice is evident, there may be mercy also: “All the ways of the Lord are mercy and truth.” To the good also he gives according to their merits, and more than they have deserved, so that there mercy may prevail over justice.
**“of the indignation of his wrath”** — who proceeds from him who is indignant and angry
16.20:
**“And every”** — And I saw that all who were afflicted for God in the world and eminent in virtues, in view of these punishments, avoided in their life the company of the impious, and therefore were not found in their punishments.
**“island”** — that is, the congregation of the saints
**“fled away”** — namely, the fellowship of the reprobate and their punishment
**“and the mountains were not found”** — namely, in punishment
16.21:
**“And great hail”** — that is, eternal punishment, which will crush
**“like a talent”** — A talent is great, of a hundred and twenty pounds; medium, seventy-two; small, fifty. He speaks of the medium one here, because sinners in seventy-two languages will not escape this vengeance.
**“came down”** — that is, weighty and measured
**“from heaven”** — namely, sent by God
**“upon men”** — that is, impatient and carnal
**“and men blasphemed”** — That is, placed in hell, although they know they are punished according to merit, they will nevertheless grieve that God has such power that he inflicts blows on them, and this is blasphemy.
**“men blasphemed God”** — namely, saying that he is unjust
**“for the plague of the hail: because it was exceeding great”** — that is, tormenting them intolerably

17.1:
**“And there came one”**
• through understanding
• When he had described the plagues which the preachers will bring in the time of Antichrist, and the eternal damnation which the wicked will suffer for it, he warns us to attend to the causes of that damnation, as if he said: I have shown you what will happen in that future; now beware, you who are present, for the same devil who will then deceive so openly deceives secretly every day, and to the same destruction to which he will lead those.
**“of the seven angels”** — Who had the seven vials, etc. Here the angel bears the part of the teacher, John that of the one speaking.
**“who had the seven vials, and spoke with me, saying: Come, I will shew thee”** — through understanding
**“The condemnation of the harlot”** — That is, the cause of the condemnation of the wicked, who, having abandoned the Creator, commit fornication with the demon, by worshipping idols, loving earthly things, and serving uncleanness.
**“harlot”** — This great harlot, that is, Antichrist and the wicked who will be in his time, who already sits upon the waters, that is, already reigns over the wicked of the present, of all of whom he is the head.
**“who sitteth”** — That is, who reigns over many peoples, whom lust draws to herself; whence the Lord to Job: “His strength,” that is, the devil’s, “is in his loins.” When he deceives men, whose seed-bed is in the loins; and in the navel, when he deceives women, whose seed is in the navel. Whence the prophet to Jerusalem as to a harlot: “in the day of thy nativity,” that is, in this time of the world, “thy navel was not cut,” that is, thou hast not restrained lust.
17.2:
**“With whom the kings of the earth have committed fornication”** — the princes of the world
**“have been made drunk”** — As a drunken man fears nothing, so those clinging to earthly things will be so blinded by love of the earth that they neither love God nor fear punishments.
**“who inhabit the earth, with the wine of her whoredom”** — of manifest fornication
17.3:
**“And he took me away in spirit into the desert”** — in the hearts of the reprobate, made a desert by the grace of God
**“in spirit”**
• in a spiritual vision
• because such things cannot be seen with bodily eyes
**“And I saw a woman sitting upon a scarlet coloured beast”** — A woman sitting upon the beast, etc. That is, those soft men who are conformed to Eve, from whom sin began, who have the devil as their foundation, who is bloody both in himself and in his own, or because they shed the blood of the saints, or misunderstand the words of God.
**“full of names of blasphemy”** — because they say that the evils they do do not displease God
**“having seven heads”** — That is, the senses; and afterwards error; and at last Antichrist, by which seven the devil leads men to sin.
**“and ten horns”** — That is, the ten kingdoms which will be in the time of Antichrist, by which other things are understood.
17.4:
**“And the woman”** — and through that beast this woman was such
**“was clothed round about with purple and scarlet”** — because they kill those unwilling to consent
**“clothed round about with purple”** — That is, with royal garment, because they say they are kings in order to deceive.
**“gold”** — Because they will seem enlightened by divine wisdom.
**“and precious stones”** — that is, with the carbuncle, that is, with the charity which they say they have
**“and pearls”** — with other virtues
**“a golden cup”** — That is, the divine Scripture by which the faithful are given drink to salvation.
**“full of the abomination”** — in wicked interpretations
17.5:
**“And on her forehead”** — Although she is so skilled at deceiving, yet, faithful, do not despair, because she has on her forehead, that is, in plain view, a sign which is a mystery only to the untaught.
**“a name was written:”** — That is, by giving the example of committing sins, on account of which earthly men are repelled from the salvation of the faithful.
**“A mystery;”** — namely, that is to say, this
**“Babylon the great,”** — that is, 'great confusion'
**“the mother of the fornications, and the abominations of the earth”** — Abominations, that is, those which according to those expositions must be cast off by men, because they teach uncleanness of the flesh and to fornicate away from God.
17.6:
**“And I saw”**
• that is, this
• I saw the sin of the world; I saw also one condemned for sin
**“drunk”** — That is, cast down by vengeance for the shedding of blood, so that from excessive pains she does not know where she is.
**“with the blood of the saints”** — of the lesser ones
**“and with the blood of the martyrs of Jesus”** — of those who do not fear to testify that Christ is God
**“And I wondered”** — Here John takes the person of those who, when they see the wicked exalted in the world, wonder when they hear the punishments which are promised to those wicked, and, since they are to be so punished, why God permits them to be exalted. But they are taught to understand that exaltation as given for greater blinding, and that at last eternal damnation is justly inflicted.
**“when I had seen”** — Otherwise “viderem.”
17.7:
**“And the angel said to me: Why dost thou wonder?”** — As if to say: do not wonder, but understand what it is.
**“I will tell thee”**
• That is, I will unfold it so that you may understand.
• That is, why these wicked ones are punished, and the devil who caused them to sin; which is unknown except to the learned.
**“The beast which carrieth her”** — The beast, that is, the devil. Carries, that is, rules the woman, that is, all the wicked who are made effeminate; for he who rules others is said to carry them as the burden of rule.
17.8:
**“The beast”** — that is, the devil, who makes men beastly
**“which thou sawest”**
• he reigned little
• before the coming of Christ
**“was”** — Before the coming of Christ the devil had very great power, but afterwards, although he did not wholly lose it, nevertheless he was not a little weakened.
**“and is not”** — because when Christ was born he lost his strength
**“shall come up”** — Because in the time of Antichrist he will receive power.
**“out of the abyss”** — he will have a place, because he will find wicked men
**“shall come up out of the bottomless pit”** — That is, through those who are deep in sins, he will rise into pride.
**“and go into destruction”** — Goes into destruction, because when Antichrist is dead he will no longer have room to tempt.
**“shall wonder, seeing the beast”** — When the wicked see their power so annihilated they will grieve, not as penitents but only wondering.
17.9:
**“And here is the understanding that hath wisdom.”** — As if to say: with respect to this punishment, you can guard yourselves.
**“The seven heads are seven mountains, upon which the woman sitteth, and they are seven kings:”** — because by these same things he rules hell
**“The seven heads”** — Because by these seven the devil raises men into pride, and on which unbelievers lean.
17.10:
**“Five are fallen”**
• childhood having passed
• Five are fallen. If Adam had persevered in obedience, the senses of the body would not have turned to any pleasure, namely an evil one; but through sin they have been so corrupted that it is now natural to seek things smooth to the touch, savoury to the taste, fragrant to the nose, beautiful to the sight. These are the five kings by whom the devil rules in childhood, because he was the cause why they were corrupted. These are the five husbands of the Samaritan woman. In youth error succeeds, for after a man has discretion, even if he sins, it is now imputed not to the senses but to error, of which the Lord says: “He whom thou now hast is not thy husband.”
**“one is”** — that is, in mature age, error
**“and the other is not yet come”** — Antichrist, who most of all causes sin
**“and when he is come”** — but he is not to be feared, because
**“he must remain a short”** — or brevi
**“a short time”** — or tempore
17.11:
**“And the beast”** — Antichrist
**“is of the seven”** — Because he sins in like manner and will be punished in like manner, and he is the eighth because he surpasses them all both in wickedness and in punishment.
17.12:
**“And the ten horns which thou sawest, are ten kings, who have not yet received a kingdom”** — in the time of Antichrist, as Daniel says: “There shall be ten kingdoms,” whose kings are marked by the horns
**“but shall receive power as kings”** — not truly kings but tyrants
**“one hour”** — therefore you should not fear
**“after the beast”** — those who will go second, from their own head, after the beast
17.13:
**“These have one design”** — denying Christ and believing in Antichrist
**“and their strength”** — which they have in themselves
**“and their power”** — which they will have over others
**“they shall deliver to the beast”** — because they will attribute everything to him
17.14:
**“These shall fight with the Lamb”** — by word and deed, so as to withdraw the faithful from themselves
**“and the Lamb shall overcome them”** — making their own steadfast and condemning them in their head
**“because he is Lord of lords”** — using evils for the profit of the faithful
**“and King of kings”** — and therefore he will conquer kings
**“and they that are with him are called”** — through the preachers
**“and elect”** — from eternity
**“and faithful”** — carrying out works
17.15:
**“And he said to me: The waters which thou sawest, where the harlot sitteth”** — that is, Antichrist already reigns through mystery
**“are peoples, and nations, and tongues”** — That is, the present evil men gathered from every diversity of people.
17.16:
**“And the ten horns which thou sawest in the beast: these shall hate the harlot”** — and therefore you ought not to be conformed to her, because those who now cling to her will at some time grieve
**“shall make her desolate”** — The devil’s comfort is the destruction of the wicked, whom he will destroy once the number of the impious is complete.
**“and naked”** — The devil has the power of making signs to deceive; he will lose this once the number of the good is complete, because afterwards temptation will have no place.
**“and shall eat her flesh”** — because together with them and for their sins the devil will be punished
**“flesh”** — Those who are fornicating are said to 'eat,' because they will delight in inflicting punishments.
**“shall burn her with fire”** — That is, they will be tormented for the pleasures of her which they have followed.
17.17:
**“For God hath given into their hearts”**
• For God has put into their hearts
• namely
**“to do that which pleaseth him: that they give their kingdom to the beast”** — that is, they permit themselves to be ruled by the devil
**“till the words of God be fulfilled”** — be accomplished by works
**“the words of God”** — the good and the evil will receive the promises
**“The words of God be fulfilled”** — Concerning the promise of rewards or punishments.
17.18:
**“And the woman which thou sawest, is the great city”** — that is, the multitude of evil men
**“which hath kingdom over the kings of the earth.”** — because the kings themselves are especially proud

18.1:
**“And after these things, I saw”** — In this sixth vision he treats of the last punishments which the wicked will suffer in hell for their several sins, and first he shows concerning Babylon, afterwards concerning the beast and the false prophets, and at last concerning the devil himself, in whom the end is plain. In him, the damned one, will be the end; he says that the one who is to carry out this damnation was preached by Christ, so that greater faith may be given to it.
**“And after these things, I saw another angel”** — That is, Christ.
**“come down”** — into the flesh.
**“from heaven”** — from the equality of the Father.
**“having great power: and the earth”** — That is, the Church.
**“is enlightened”** — with the darkness of ignorance driven out.
**“with his glory”** — by glorious preaching.
18.2:
**“And he cried”** — He preached.
**“with a strong voice”** — what he said will not lack effect.
**“is fallen, is fallen”** — Twice, for the double damnation of soul and body, or because they will be punished eternally.
**“saying: Babylon the great is fallen, is fallen”** — and therefore she will fall, because
**“is become the habitation of devils”** — a gathering of demons.
**“and the hold of every unclean spirit”** — because she keeps herself for the devil, or the devil keeps her for himself.
**“unclean spirit”** — Demons in wicked hearts are unclean because of the allurements of the flesh, and birds because of the pride of the mind, or because they range through the air.
18.3:
**“Because of the wine of the wrath of her fornication”** — That is, of the fornication for which God is angry.
**“all nations have drunk”** — That is, the princes of the world.
**“have committed fornication with her, and the merchants of the earth”** — That is, those who sell their souls for worldly ambition.
**“have been made rich by the power of her delicacies”** — From the power: that is, from the sins by which riches are acquired, because every rich man is either wicked or the heir of a wicked man.
18.4:
**“And I heard another voice”**
• That is, the divine inspiration, either of Christ or of his preachers.
• And I heard, etc. Having said that the damnation is future, he adds an admonition for those present.
**“from heaven, saying: Go out from her, my people”**
• do not do her works.
• Go out, etc. Because little time remains in which they will receive what they deserve.
**“and that you be not partakers of her sins”** — do not give consent to those who do them.
**“and that you receive not of her plagues”** — as if to say: if you are unlike her in life, you will not be like her in punishment.
18.5:
**“For her sins have reached unto heaven”**
• although he seemed to have forgotten while he allowed her to prosper.
• For her sins have reached unto heaven, etc. Sins reach as far as contempt of God through impenitence.
**“and the Lord hath remembered her iniquities”** — and therefore, because vengeance now pleases him so much.
18.6:
**“Render to her”** — As she has exercised my vengeance against you, who are to be purified, so avenge my wrong upon them.
**“double unto her double”** — That is, inflict on her soul and body greater punishments than she inflicted on you.
**“according to her works”** — according as they themselves sinned.
**“in the cup wherein she hath mingled, mingle ye double unto her”** — That is, as she inflicted torments on you, so you, by your judgment, on them.
18.7:
**“As much as she hath glorified”** — Because some have more and some less, for the sake of distinction he repeats what he had said above.
**“so much torment give ye to her”** — in the body
**“and sorrow”** — in the soul
**“because she saith in her heart: I sit”** — as not moving
**“as a queen”** — I have honour and dignity
**“and am no widow”** — Because I have consolation in temporal things.
**“and sorrow I shall not see”** — because she does not guard against future evils
18.8:
**“Therefore in one day”** — that is, on the day of judgment
**“death”** — The absence of life, that is, of God, because his presence is life.
**“and mourning”** — against this, that here they laughed
**“and famine”** — because they will lack God, who is refreshment
**“and she shall be burnt with the fire, because God is strong, who shall judge her”** — that is, not to be moved by any prayers
18.9:
**“And they shall weep”** — they will suffer grief in the mind
**“and bewail themselves”** — they will show grief of the body
**“shall weep and bewail”** — Against these, who have perpetual joy.
**“over her”** — because they were founded in her
**“the kings of the earth”** — that is, the princes of the world
**“The kings of the earth”** — Or those who ruled their earthly domain well, and yet at some time committed fornication with her, will grieve that they were never like those.
**“who have committed fornication, and lived in delicacies with her, when they shall see the smoke of her burning”** — “When they shall see the smoke, etc.” When riches have failed, which is the sign of the eternal fire of judgment. Or when they see their punishment raised beyond measure.
18.10:
**“standing afar off”** — in will
**“for fear of her torments”** — namely because they would wish to flee if they could
**“saying:”** — in soul and in body
**“Alas, alas, that great city Babylon”** — “a gathering of evils”
18.11:
**“And the merchants of the earth shall weep”** — either literally, or giving souls for earthly things
**“The merchants of the earth shall weep”** — Because they will grieve that those things perish, in which they reckoned their prosperity.
**“for no man shall buy their merchandise any more”** — they will grieve that the things pertaining to the senses of the body perish
18.12:
**“merchandise of gold and silver, and precious stones, and of pearls, and fine linen, and purple, and silk, and scarlet, and all thyine wood”**
• understand: and no one will buy
• Of gold and silver, etc. By gold, wisdom; by silver, the divine utterances. Christ is signified in the precious stone, the apostles in the pearls; in the white fine linen, the justifications of the saints; in the purple, martyrdom; in the silk, virginity; in the red scarlet, charity; in the incorruptible thyine wood, unfailing constancy; in the ivory, the beauty of virtues; in the brass, fortitude and longanimity; in the iron, the keenness of loftiness; in the marble, unconquered humility. These the reprobate pretend to have, and they grieve when what is understood in them fails. In the gold we take worldly wisdom; in the silver, eloquence; in the precious stone and pearls, false prophets and heresiarchs; in the fine linen, feigned justice; in the purple, the martyrs of heretics; in the silk, integrity of the flesh as a covering for a corrupt mind; in the scarlet, cruelty cloaked with a pretence of charity; in the thyine wood, obstinacy of mind feigning constancy; in the ivory, feigned beauty of virtues. In the brass, a firm preaching of perfidy in place of the right faith; in the iron, the keenness of deceit; in the marble, the strength of feigned subjection; in the spices of ointments and in the frankincense are figured the prayers of the saints, which the vain assiduity of heretics imitates in prayers. By the ointment, the incarnate divinity, which the harshness of false Christians imitates under a false gentleness. And when these are taken away the reprobate bewail them, as the heretics did the death of Arius. They pretend to have lost the fine flour and the wheat, when they have lost the cockle and the chaff. The beasts of burden signify the elect, who say with the psalmist: “I am become as a beast before thee.” The sheep: the saints, to whom it is said: “Behold I send you as sheep in the midst of wolves.” By the horses and chariots understand the preachers, according to Eliseus saying: “My father, the chariot of Israel and the driver thereof.” By the slaves, the elect who are subjected to the service of God. The reprobate grieve that they have lost the beasts of burden, horses and chariots, that is, those whom they reckon strong for carrying the burdens of others, when they have lost those weak for every good work; the fruits are the virtues of the saints. And they pretend to have every part of the beast.
**“or cedar”** — in many copies it is omitted
18.13:
**“and”** — and no one will buy
**“Cinnamon”** — In cinnamon is the fragrance of the virtues which they feign.
**“and amomum, and odours, and ointment, and frankincense, and wine”** — of the New Testament, which inebriates
**“and oil”** — the anointing of the Holy Spirit
**“likewise also wheat”** — Of Christ’s flesh, by which the faithful are truly satisfied, the reprobate are provoked.
**“and beasts, and sheep, and horses, and chariots, and slaves, and souls of men”**
• and no one will buy merchandise
• because they receive the same sacraments
**“slaves and souls”** — He distinguishes, because some become slaves in body only, as Joseph; some also in mind, as when an Egyptian sold to a Jew is circumcised according to their rite, or worships the idols of the pagans.
18.14:
**“And the fruits of the desire of thy soul are departed from thee”** — because even for small things, if they had them immoderately, they will be condemned
**“and all fat things”** — by the fat things, the fatness of the soul is understood
18.15: **“The merchants of these things”** — of men
18.17: **“For in one hour are so great riches come to nought; and every shipmaster”** — that is, some desire to have something certain, such as a bishopric
18.19:
**“And they cast dust”** — that is, the lust for earthly things
**“upon their heads”** — upon their minds, or by the likeness of the penitent
**“and cried, weeping and mourning, saying: Alas! alas! that great city, wherein all were made rich, that had ships at sea, by reason of her prices”** — or literally, all these things were seen of riches
18.20:
**“Rejoice over her, thou heaven, and ye holy apostles”** — that is, those privy to God’s secrets
**“Rejoice over her”** — After he foretold this future damnation for the impious, he bids the good to rejoice, that they may agree with the divine judgment; or because after these are condemned, their reward follows.
**“and prophets”** — in parts
**“for God hath judged your judgment on her”** — as she condemned you unjustly, she will be condemned justly
18.21:
**“And a mighty angel took up”** — Christ
**“And took up”** — God raises up the wicked, that he may punish them more heavily, or that they may fall.
**“a stone”** — because he conquered the brazen powers
**“as it were a great millstone”** — because they are rolled through worldly things
**“a stone, as it were a great millstone”** — Literally, all these things were also seen.
**“and cast”** — having hard hearts
**“into the sea”** — that is, into hell
**“saying: With such violence”** — that is, into hell now
**“shall Babylon, that great city, be thrown down”**
• With such violence, etc. After the individual punishments were described, the manner of damnation is shown to him, as it were: what I saw foretold, I also saw now fulfilled.
• That is, as you see in this figure; or the more they were exalted, the more heavily they will fall.
**“and shall be found no more at all”** — as some heretics think
18.22:
**“And the voice of harpers, and of musicians, and of them that play on the pipe, and on the trumpet, shall no more be heard at all in thee; and no craftsman”** — as to the practical
**“no craftsman of any art whatsoever”** — as to the theoretical
**“shall be found any more at all in thee”** — hence is the proof that the damned forget the knowledge they acquired.
**“and the sound of the mill shall be heard no more at all in thee”**
• there the most delicate breads will not be sought.
• and by this the pleasure of taste is removed.
18.23:
**“And the light of the lamp”** — as to sight.
**“shall shine no more at all in thee; and the voice of the bridegroom and the bride”** — that is, the joy of the wedding.
**“shall be heard”** — as to hearing.
**“no more at all in thee”** — and therefore.
**“for thy merchants”** — literally, or in the persuasions of sorcery.
**“Merchants”** — Because they, giving their souls for earthly things, exercised excessive power, which they can now no longer bear.
**“were the great men of the earth”** — this as to the concupiscible part.
**“for by thy enchantments”**
• this as to the rational part.
• that is, sorcery, that is, by evil persuasions by which you caused others to err.
**“all nations have been deceived”**
• some of all.
• and therefore again because.
18.24:
**“And in her”** — In her. Now he speaks to Babylon herself about her fall, as if sympathizing with her misery; now he turns to the hearers to exhort the faithful.
**“was found the blood of prophets and of saints”** — vengeance for blood.
**“and of all that were slain upon the earth”** — if a wicked man kills a wicked man, the wickedness of the one slain does not excuse the slayer.

19.1:
**“After these things”** — That is, he sees the damnation of the wicked completed, as he had heard from Christ that it was to be completed; now he adds that the saints rejoice over this damnation, as they had been admonished to rejoice in that verse: “Rejoice over her, O heaven,” by which a much heavier punishment of the wicked is understood.
**“of much people”** — of preachers.
**“in heaven”** — the Church of the saints.
**“saying: Alleluia”** — praise inexpressible in human words.
**“Alleluia”** — Therefore we say Alleluia because it is praise to our God, and because he has done such things for us; whence we ought to praise him preeminently.
**“Salvation, and glory”** — immortality and impassibility.
**“and power is to our God”**
• because he has overcome the devil.
• and therefore praise is his.
19.2:
**“For true and just are his judgments”**
• by giving what he promised.
• rendering to each according to merits.
**“who hath judged”** — by a judgment of condemnation.
**“the great harlot”** — from the gathering of the wicked.
**“which corrupted the earth with her fornication”** — that is, they themselves corrupted themselves, or one another.
**“and hath revenged the blood of his servants”** — which the impious multitude shed.
**“at her hands”** — require him
19.3:
**“And again they said: Alleluia”** — By this repetition we ought to understand eternal praise.
**“And her smoke ascendeth for ever and ever”** — he has judged, and they are punished eternally
19.4:
**“And the four and twenty ancients”** — all the holy judges: the twelve patriarchs, the twelve apostles
**“And the four and twenty”** — Not only the lesser saints praised God for this damnation, but also those greater ones who were judges and teachers of others in the Church.
**“and the four living creatures fell down and adored God that sitteth upon the throne, saying: Amen; Alleluia”** — it is true that God is so glorious
**“Amen”** — And he is truly to be praised for punishing our enemies in this way.
19.5:
**“And a voice”** — admonition
**“came out from the throne”**
• that is, from those in whom God sits
• And a voice from the throne, etc. Having spoken of the damnation of the wicked and the exultation of the saints, he adds an admonition to those present, as if to say: you have seen the damnation, you have seen the exultation; now take thought for your own salvation.
**“came out”** — for the hearing of all
**“saying: Give praise to our God, all ye his servants”** — or servants
**“little”** — Those who cannot penetrate the higher mysteries, nor can fulfil the counsel of God: “Sell all things and follow me.”
**“and great”** — with chaste love and filial fear
19.6:
**“And I heard as it were the voice of a great”** — those who were trumpets in the world now exult in heaven
**“And I heard as it were the voice”** — Having shown the joy the saints will have over the ruin of the wicked, the Church adds their other joy, which they will have over their own salvation, which she is about to speak of.
**“and as the voice of many waters”** — because they were gathered from many peoples
**“and as the voice of great thunders”** — because the exultation of the saints will terrify the wicked
**“saying, Alleluia: for the Lord our God the Almighty hath reigned.”** — as if to say: before this the wicked reigned
19.7:
**“Let us be glad”** — having the blessedness of the soul
**“and rejoice”** — glorified in the body
**“and give glory to him”** — that is, let us reckon that we have all things from God
**“for the marriage of the Lamb is come”** — that is, the Church is joined to Christ
**“and his wife hath prepared herself.”** — the Church of the saints, in reality, which before was the bride in hope
**“And his wife hath prepared”** — And it was fitting that they be joined, because the Church itself made herself fit to be received.
19.8:
**“And it is granted to her”** — In this life, so that she might be able to prepare herself.
**“And it was given him”** — Another reading: it was given to her to be clothed in shining fine linen, white with a white tooth.
**“that she should clothe herself with fine linen, glittering”** — justifications
**“and white.”** — because the knowledge of the saints is darkened by no stains
19.9:
**“And he said to me: Write: Blessed are they that are called to the marriage supper of the Lamb.”** — speaking of the future marriages, he invites those present to them
**“And he saith to me: These words of God are true.”** — not mine, and therefore true
19.10:
**“And I fell down before”** — Etc. Because I understood him to be greater than me, and was ready to obey, so you too obey me.
**“See thou do it not”** — In the old law he did not forbid himself to be adored; but after the ascension, seeing a man exalted above himself, he feared to be adored by a man.
**“I am thy fellow servant, and of thy brethren, who have the testimony of Jesus. Adore God.”** — I and you and all your brethren have one God and one Lord.
**“For the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy.”** — For the testimony of Jesus, etc. Whatever the prophets said bears witness to Christ.
19.11:
**“And I saw heaven”** — mysteries revealed, so that man can ascend to heaven and know God.
**“opened.”**
• and who opened this?
• I saw those called to the wedding; I saw also those who are able to come, for they have a good helper and good admonishers.
**“I saw heaven opened”** — The damnation of Babylon having been told, and the rejoicing which the saints will have from it, he next sets forth the damnation of Antichrist himself and of his apostles, which is there: “And the beast was taken.” And why will these be damned? Because they fought against Christ as much as they could; and yet Christ will be able to conquer well, because he has so great power according to the divinity and the humanity that no one can resist him; and therefore we ought to imitate him. Whence he himself also interposes an admonition: “And I saw an angel.”
**“And behold a white horse”** — A white horse. That is, the flesh of Christ, carrying the Word of God to battle against the devil.
**“and he that sat on him”** — that is, the divinity
**“was called faithful”** — because he fulfils promises
**“and true”** — because he is truth and makes men truthful
**“and with justice”** — because he repays each according to his works
**“doth he judge and fight.”** — in his own, against the devil
19.12:
**“And his eyes were as a flame”**
• that is, the gifts of the Holy Spirit or charity
• As a flame, etc. Because he burns up vices, and kindles and illumines.
• All these things without regard to anyone, so that we may only note what he is and what great power he has.
**“fire”** — in divinity
**“and on his head were many diadems”** — because through it he and his are crowned
**“being”** — God-man, or Jesus
**“a name written, which no man”** — the unbeliever
**“knoweth but himself.”** — and his own through him
19.13:
**“And he was clothed with a garment sprinkled with blood”** — that is, the suffering flesh, or the Church, by which he is slain in his martyrs.
**“The Word of God”** — That is, “For he spoke and they were made,” through whom the Father made all things, and through whom the Father made himself known to the world.
19.14:
**“And the armies”** — that is, the faithful fighting against the devil
**“that are in heaven”** — in the Church
**“followed”** — imitated
**“him on white horses, clothed in fine linen, white”** — that is, justice
**“and clean”**
• by progress in virtues
• Clothed in fine white and clean linen, that is, in clean bodies which are restrained from unlawful things, and are spurred by the goad of charity to good things, that is, to justice.
19.15:
**“And out of his mouth”** — that is, from the preaching
**“proceedeth a sharp two edged sword”** — The sword on both sides, that is, the divine sentence cutting off the wicked thoughts of the mind and the unlawful movements of the body; or the Old and New Testament.
**“that with it he may strike the nations.”** — some to death, some to life
**“And he shall rule them with a rod of iron”**
• that is, with unbending justice
• He shall rule them; or, the saints “from virtue to virtue,” the wicked from vice to vice
**“He treadeth the winepress”** — That is, rising again he destroyed the death which was brought upon the first man sinning by an angry God. Or the winepress is tribulation, which, that is, in which, he treads the saints placed there while he enlarges it, which God in anger brought upon Adam sinning; furious, he extends it over his offspring, but they become wine to be placed in God’s cellar, in which, being placed, they will not be the wine of wrath.
**“of the fierceness of the wrath of God the Almighty.”** — the fury, by the continuation of anger
19.16:
**“And he hath on his garment”** — that is, in his humanity
**“And on his garment”** — Or, in the hearts of the faithful, who are the garment of the Son: written, King of kings.
**“and on his thigh”** — to show that he was of the true line of the fathers before
**“written”** — indelibly
**“King of kings”** — that is, of the saints, who rule themselves and others
**“and Lord of lords.”** — who exercises lordship over subjects
19.17:
**“And I saw an angel”**
• preachers standing in the open
• The dignity of Christ having been shown, through which he will be able to overcome the devil, he adds an admonition about the present, as if to say: you must cleave to such a one.
**“standing in the sun”** — in the light of understanding of the Scriptures and in fervor
**“and he cried with a loud voice”** — that is, with intent
**“saying to all the birds”** — whose “conversation is in heaven”
**“to all the birds”** — To all the faithful, who are nimble and light in advancing good works.
**“that did fly”** — that is, they contemplated heavenly things
**“through the midst of heaven.”** — through the catholic faith, which is common
**“Come”** — By working well in the same faith, not following diverse heresies as the wicked do; or from the diverse parts of the world.
**“gather yourselves together”** — that is, work well
**“to the great supper of God”**
• that is, to God himself, who will be your refreshment
• And gather yourselves to the supper, etc. As if to say: you must be very careful, that you may be able to come to this supper, because unless you fight well you will succumb to the devil, since he is very ready to harm you; yet with God’s help you will be able to overcome him.
19.18:
**“That you may eat the flesh of kings”** — that you may take delight in the torment of the wicked, both greater and lesser
**“and the flesh of tribunes”** — of other judges
**“and the flesh of mighty men”** — in body
**“and the flesh of horses”** — of those subject to others
**“and of them that sit on them”** — of prelates
**“on them, and the flesh of all freemen”** — justice
**“and bondmen”** — of sin
19.19:
**“And I saw the beast”** — that is, Antichrist
**“and the kings of the earth”** — that is, his apostles
**“and their armies”** — that is, all who serve him
**“gathered together to make war with him that sat upon the horse, and with his army.”** — that is, blaspheming against Christ and his own, with tribulation and miracles
19.20:
**“And the beast was taken”** — that is, punished eternally
**“and with him the false prophet, who wrought signs before him, wherewith he seduced them who received the character of the beast”** — that is, who believed in him
**“and who adored”** — as the Jews who will receive him with joy
**“the image thereof.”** — conformity
**“These two were cast alive into the pool of fire, burning with brimstone.”** — because of the darkness
**“Were cast alive”** — Antichrist and his apostles will suffer greater punishments than others, in the likeness of one who is burned alive.
19.21:
**“And the rest”** — That is, their followers will be punished with a lesser punishment; or those who will be the rest, that is, converted to God, slain to the world, will live to God.
**“all the birds were filled”** — That is, all the saints rejoiced at their punishment, and at the progress of the brothers.

20.1:
