**“And I saw an angel”** — The damnation of Babylon and of Antichrist and of the false apostles having been told, he sets forth the damnation of the devil himself, and puts first the cause why, and the time at which he will be damned, and who will be able to conquer him, namely he who in his humble coming was able to bind him as much as he wished, and, glorified, was able to destroy him altogether.
**“angel”** — Christ
**“come down”** — humbling himself in the flesh
**“from heaven”** — by the secret of the Father
**“having”** — behold, an unavoidable power
**“the key of the bottomless pit”** — power over the devil
**“of the bottomless pit”** — The abyss: the dark hearts of the impious; or the devil himself. These the Lord permits to rage, and restrains.
**“and a great chain”** — the unavoidable power by which he binds all things
**“in his hand.”** — that is, by the working of the passion and resurrection
20.2:
**“And he laid hold on the dragon”** — by the violence of harming
**“laid hold on”** — That is, he showed that the devil had sinned, when the devil killed him who was free from sin.
**“serpent”** — by the deceit of deceiving
**“old”** — who has done harm since the beginning of the world
**“which is the devil”** — flowing downward
**“and Satan”** — adversary
**“and bound him”** — that is, he deprived him of his former power
**“bound him”** — It should be known that the devil was likewise bound in Abraham and other believers as in these present ones; but in those the hope of the Christ to come bound him, in these Christ himself, coming, bound him.
**“for a thousand years”** — that is, for the whole time from the incarnation to the end of the age
20.3:
**“And he cast him into the bottomless pit”** — the hearts of the reprobate
**“And he cast him into”** — Because, cast out by the faithful, he began to rule more fiercely over the wicked; hence it is read in the gospel that he entered into the swine.
**“and shut him up, and set a seal upon him”**
• that is, he forbade him the liberty of going out, except by the hidden judgment of God
• Sealed, that is, he set a seal, namely the sign of the cross, which so overcomes him that it drives him back from the faithful.
**“that he should no more seduce the nations, till the thousand years be finished.”** — that is, until Antichrist comes
**“And”** — because God so ordained
**“after that, he must be loosed a little time.”**
• therefore not to be feared
• And after that, he must, etc. That he may receive the power which he had before the coming of Christ.
20.4:
**“And I saw seats”** — the faithful subjects
**“And I beheld”** — Namely, with the devil bound, I saw the faithful loosed, and the lesser ones ready to obey their prelates, and the prelates judging their subjects.
**“I saw”** — In the time of binding, I saw the Church thus loosed to do good works; and at the same time I saw those who die for Christ at once enter into glory, never to go down to hell, as Abraham and the other prophets went down, although they were just.
**“and they sat upon them”** — the greater ones, reigning well
**“and judgment was given”** — and this because God enjoined this judgment upon them
**“unto them”** — the prelates
**“and the souls”** — I saw
**“of them that were beheaded”**
• the martyrs
• And the souls of them that were beheaded, etc. And likewise I saw the souls of those who did not adore.
**“for the testimony of Jesus”** — of his humanity
**“and for the word of God”** — that is, his divinity
**“and who had not adored the beast”** — that is, Antichrist
**“nor his image”** — that is, the false apostles
**“nor received his character”** — his sign
**“on their foreheads”** — even by open confession
**“or in their hands”** — in works
**“and lived and reigned”**
• in the present by grace, and in the future by glory
• And they lived and reigned. And I do not say they will live and reign in the future, but also in this present, namely from the time they were slain they lived and reigned with Christ.
20.5:
**“And the rest of the dead”** — that is, dead in soul
**“lived not”** — that is, they suffer eternal punishments
**“And the rest of the dead lived not”** — That is, they will suffer eternal punishments, and in this present, namely as soon as they die.
**“This is the first resurrection”** — Namely, that the devil is so bound, and that men rise again from sins, and that the souls of the dead at once enjoy eternal rest.
**“first”** — To distinguish it from that which will be together in soul and body.
**“till the thousand years be finished. This is the first resurrection.”** — What he had said of the beheaded, here he says of the other lesser ones.
20.6:
**“Blessed”** — because he has attained blessedness
**“and holy”** — because in it he will be steadfast
**“he that hath part”** — Although all cannot be perfect, nor will they be in the same brightness.
**“and”** — and truly blessed
**“second death”** — That is, the eternal damnation which will be in body and in soul, because it is in no way increased.
**“but they shall be priests”** — That is, offering eternal praises to the divinity and the humanity.
**“and shall reign”**
• in this present
• that is, they will rule themselves for the better
• not only in the future, of which there is no doubt
**“with him”** — with the Trinity and the humanity
20.7:
**“And when the thousand years shall be finished, Satan shall be loosed out of his prison”** — that is, he will recover his former power
**“out of his prison”** — That is, from the hearts of the reprobate, in whom he is now bound so that he does not serve as he wishes.
**“and shall go forth”** — that is, he will exercise power
**“and Magog”**
• uncovering
• that is, he will persecute both secretly and openly
**“Magog”** — That is, uncovered: all persecutors who hide the devil in themselves, and at last proceed to open persecution. Or literally, he will first seduce these two nations and through them proceed to others.
**“to battle”** — through whom he will fight openly
**“is as the sand of the sea”** — so innumerable and barren
20.8:
**“and seduce the nations”** — he will lead away from Christ to himself
**“which are over the four quarters of the earth, Gog”** — 'covered'
**“and shall gather them together”** — not locally but in mind
**“the number of whom”** — Gog and Magog
**“And they came up”** — that is, they will be proud
**“and encompassed”** — as though attacking, they could not enter
**“beloved”** — from God
20.9:
**“upon the breadth of the earth”** — that is, in the whole world
**“the camp of the saints”** — ready for battle
**“and the beloved city”**
• the Church of the saints
• And they encompassed the camp and the city: that is, the same saints fortified in virtues, and united in this war.
**“And there came down”** — as if not to be feared, because they will quickly perish
**“fire”** — a sudden destruction
**“from God out of heaven, and devoured them”** — so that they will not return
20.10:
**“and the devil, who seduced them, was cast into the pool of fire and brimstone”** — the deep punishment of hell
**“and the false prophet shall be tormented”** — he makes the devil and his followers alike in punishments, so that by this he may deter most of all
**“day and night”** — that is, constantly
**“Day and night”** — That is, with respect to the glory of the saints, which is day, and of their punishments, which is night.
20.11:
**“And I saw a great white throne”**
• the Church
• Having spoken of the destruction of the devil and his members, he adds the destruction of the world as a greater punishment for the wicked. For it is fitting that, the wicked being destroyed, the world should be destroyed, since it had been corrupted by them.
• Having often spoken of the glorification of the saints and the punishments of the wicked, he had not made mention of bodies, whether they were to be glorified or punished; this he shows openly here.
**“great”** — by its multitude
**“white”** — by immortality and impassibility
**“and one sitting upon it”** — namely Christ, sitting in those who will bring about this destruction
**“from whose face”** — in the presence
**“the earth fled away”** — from this appearance
**“and heaven”** — that is, the air
**“and there was no place found”** — according to its former state
**“for them”** — heaven and earth
20.12:
**“And I saw the dead, great and small”** — that is, the wicked, both greater and lesser
**“standing”** — bodily
**“in the presence of the throne”** — because the saints behold the merits of each
**“and the books”** — of knowledge
**“were opened; and another book was opened”**
• that is, the foreknowledge of God, which is now hidden
• The other book, that is, 'Christ,' who will then appear to all, powerful, and will give life to his own. Or the book 'of the foreknowledge of God,' because then the wicked will openly know that they were not predestined to the life which, while existing in the world, they promised themselves.
**“and the books were opened”** — The books, that is, 'the divine precepts,' which, because they have neglected them, they will know they are punished for their merit; or the books 'of the conscience of each,' which will be open to all.
**“which is the book of life; and the dead were judged”** — that is, the wicked
**“Out of those things which were written”**
• because to some a greater punishment will be given, to others a lesser
• By comparison with the saints the wicked will be condemned; they will read in them what they were unwilling to do.
20.13:
**“And the sea gave up”** — that is, the world
**“And gave”** — He wishes plainly to show that the bodies of the dead, however scattered they have been, will be made alive in that judgment, which some do not believe.
**“their dead”** — that is, the bodies of the dead
**“that were in it, and death”** — the devil
**“and hell”** — that is, the place of darkness
**“gave up their dead”** — that is, the souls of the dead
**“that were in them; and they were judged every one according to their works”** — without respect of persons
20.14:
**“And hell”**
• by the depths of vices
• that is, the place of darkness
**“and death”** — that is, the devil
**“This is the second death”** — As if to say: beware of the first death, because from that first one this second follows.
20.15: **“And whosoever was not found written in the book of life”** — that is, not predestined to faith

21.1:
**“And I beheld”** — In this seventh vision he treats of the renewal of the elements and the glorification of the saints, describing the merits by which the saints are so glorified.
**“a new heaven”** — that is, the air renewed
**“and a new earth”** — renewed
**“A new heaven and a new earth”** — That the air and the earth are changed is not doubtful, that it is done by fire. But about water there is doubt, for it is believed to have purification in itself.
**“For the first heaven”** — that is, that state in which they were before is no longer necessary
**“and the first earth was gone”** — according to the former state
**“and the sea is now no more”** — because coarseness and bitterness are taken away
21.2:
**“And I John saw the city”** — that is, the Church set in complete quiet
**“the holy Jerusalem”** — that is, firmly what it has, it will have
**“new”** — that is, immortal, impassible
**“coming down out of heaven”** — that is, God, who is peace, seeing fully
**“from God”** — because it understood that whatever good the Church has, it has received from the grace of God alone
**“prepared as a bride adorned”** — composed with virtues
**“as a bride adorned”** — As a bridegroom sends gifts to the bride before he leads her away, so Christ, before he receives the Church into glory, gives her faith and virtues and good works.
21.3:
**“And I heard a loud voice”** — that is, prophetic announcement
**“came out from the throne”**
• because it deals principally with secrets
• that is, from those in whom God sits
**“A great voice from the throne”** — Having said that he saw the renewal of the elements and the glorification of the saints, because it was unknown and would seem incredible, he adds the authority of the holy fathers who foretold this.
**“Behold”** — That is, it is evident that in the same glory will be the humanity of Christ in which he fought, and men who imitated him and made good use of reason.
**“the tabernacle of God with men”** — The humanity of Christ, in which he fought against the devil.
**“and he will dwell with them”** — that is, just as that eternal glory will be to him, so also to his own.
**“And they shall be his people”** — And they shall be his people. That is, offending in nothing, which cannot be while they are in the flesh.
**“and God himself with them shall be”** — according to the divinity, and present to them.
**“their God”** — because he will never be driven away from them, because they will never sin.
21.4:
**“And God shall wipe away all tears”**
• which according to the quality of various things.
• Every tear. As if to say: there is glory and no sadness, because both could not be there together.
**“from their eyes, and death”** — that is, the dissolution of soul and body.
**“And death”** — And death. Truly there will be no tears there, because there will be no cause of tears.
**“shall be no more, nor mourning”** — continual weeping.
**“nor crying”** — any disturbance.
**“nor sorrow”** — sudden and passing.
**“shall be any more, for the former things are passed away”** — that is, now there is no place for them, since there is no sin from which these things proceed.
21.5:
**“And he that sat on the throne said: Behold, new”** — as if to say: in plain view and at once.
**“I make all things”** — the things said above.
**“And he said to me: Write”** — namely in your heart and that of others.
**“And he said”** — As if he said: write whatever has been shown to me about this renewal; it was done for the profit of those present, to whom I have been ordered to write these things.
**“Write these words”** — Bidding him write and announce to others, he adds an exhortation that all should labor to belong to this renewal.
**“are most faithful”** — fit to be the ground on which faith may be had.
**“and true”** — because they will be fulfilled.
21.6:
**“And he said to me”** — I. Having set forth the authority of the saints concerning this renewal, he sets forth the authority of God himself.
**“It is done”** — what was to be completed has been completed.
**“Was made”** — Lest anyone should ask what would be after that renewal, he is told that nothing remains to be done.
**“I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end”** — that is, to the one who desires it.
**“Alpha and Omega”** — As if to say: I will be able to make this renewal, because I created all things, and in me all things will be consummated.
**“I will give of the fountain”**
• that is, myself.
• who is Christ himself.
**“of the water of life”** — because he makes it live.
**“freely”** — through grace alone.
21.7:
**“He that shall overcome shall possess”** — will firmly obtain.
**“To him that thirsteth, he that shall overcome”** — I will not give to the thirsty for an hour, but to the one who perseveres.
**“these things”** — immortal God
**“shall possess these things”** — That is, myself, who am the beginning of all blessedness.
**“and I will be his God”** — eternal satiety
**“and he shall be my”** — in the present through grace, and in the future through glory
**“son”** — which above is “people”
21.8:
**“But the fearful”** — those who despair of this renewal
**“The fearful”** — That is, those who flee from accepting the faith through fear of punishments, or abandon it once accepted.
**“and unbelieving, and the abominable”** — that is, excommunicated
**“and murderers, and whoremongers, and sorcerers, and idolaters, and all liars”** — for whom lying is in use
**“they shall have their portion”** — namely, those who share in it more or less
**“in the pool burning with fire and brimstone”** — according to the quality of the fault
**“which is the second death”** — of body and soul
21.9:
**“And there came one of the seven angels, who had the vials full of the seven last plagues”** — as regards the wicked
**“and spoke with me, saying: Come”** — enlarge the understanding
**“and I will shew thee the bride”**
• now through faith
• “Come, and I will shew thee,” etc. He describes the glory the saints are to have, and by what merit, or by what help, they are to receive it.
**“the wife of the Lamb”** — to be glorified and brought over in the future
21.10:
**“And he took me up in spirit to”** — Christ
**“great”** — as regards the humanity
**“to a great and high mountain”** — Christ is the ‘mountain,’ because the monument of his own is great, because he fills the whole world, and high because unconquerable.
**“and high”** — as regards the divinity
**“and he shewed me the holy city Jerusalem”** — in which God dwells through grace
**“He shewed me the holy city”** — And upon that mountain he showed the foundation of the Church.
**“coming down out of heaven from God”** — through the infusion of grace
21.11:
**“Having the glory of God”** — that is, knowledge of God
**“And the light thereof”** — that is, luminous works; it is a figure of hendiadys
**“The light”** — itself shining in its own way, like Christ, who was steadfast in purpose and shining in virtues
**“was like to a precious stone, as to the jasper stone”** — nothing there saddening but all delighting, like the greenness of jasper
**“the jasper stone”** — Hard here and green; so the Church shines by faith, and is made firm in it.
**“even as crystal”** — concealing nothing, because there is pure confession
21.12:
**“A wall”** — That is, Christ the defender, who is great in Sion, high with the Father. Or the defenders of others, who are great in conquering others, and others lest they be conquered.
**“having twelve gates”** — That is, the apostles or the prophets or the angels, messengers of truth.
**“twelve gates”** — That is, the patriarchs, by whose example others are led into the faith.
**“and in the gates”**
• that is, in the faith and in the footsteps of the prophets
• Or the gates: the apostles, who lead others into the Church. Angels, that is, subjects who, perfectly instructed, are set in the place of angels.
• The number of the twelve gates, which are comprehended under three through the four quarters of the world, pertains to the mystery of the twelve apostles, through whom the faith of the Trinity is spread abroad through the fourfold globe.
**“twelve angels”** — the apostles
**“and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel”** — that is, the memory of the holy fathers under the old law
**“names”** — That is, the memory of the holy fathers under the old law is in the apostles, because what those foretold as future these teach as fulfilled. Or all nations placed in the faith and love of the apostles; whence: “You are our epistle, written in our hearts.”
21.13: **“On the east”** — The east: the Jews, from whom the sun of justice arose; and in these there are three gates, because among these the faith of the Trinity was first announced by the apostles and prophets. The north: the cold Gentiles, who believed after the Jews. From the south, that is, from the brightness of faith which comes from the coming of Christ; from the west, that is, from the last age of the world, which through Elias and Enoch will receive the faith of the Trinity.
21.14:
**“And the wall of the city”**
• that is, in their memory and preaching
• or upon them
**“The wall”** — That is, the faith of Christ, which fortifies the city itself, has the twelve patriarchs through whom it is founded, because those first held this faith, and on them rest all who come to the faith.
**“the twelve names”** — because the faith and teaching of the apostles was founded upon the faith of the patriarchs
**“And in them, the twelve”** — Which faith these hold; those understood it to be coming and foretold it.
**“of the twelve apostles”** — whom they said would come
**“of the Lamb”** — the angel in the person of Christ
21.15:
**“And he that spoke with me”**
• according to my good pleasure
• And he that spoke, etc. I saw this city so fortified and adorned, and I saw there not all equal among themselves, yet each one perfect in his own measure.
**“had a measure of a reed of gold”** — The measuring reed, etc., that is, the divine Scripture composed by the wisdom of God, by which he touches and illumines the hearts of the faithful.
**“to measure the city and the gates thereof”** — that is, those who lead others to the faith
**“to measure the city”** — That is, he gives the lesser ones too understanding of the Scriptures themselves according to their measure.
**“and the wall”** — that is, the defenders of others
21.16:
**“lieth in a foursquare”** — The four sides: faith, hope, charity, work, which are equal, because as much as one believes, so much he hopes; as much as he hopes, so much he loves; as much as he loves, so much he works. It lies foursquare, therefore, because it is strong in faith, long-suffering in hope, broad in charity, effective in work. Or the four sides are the four principal virtues, of which one ought not to exceed another in a man: prudence, in desiring the good and avoiding the evil; after it comes temperance, that a man may draw himself back from pleasures; after these, fortitude, that he may do what he understands; then justice, that he may so temper his acts that he does not seem to himself too just or wise.
**“the length thereof”**
• that is, faith
• the explanation of the squaring
**“thereof is as great as the breadth”** — that is, charity, by which as much as one believes, so much one loves
**“and he measured the city”** — that is, the lesser Church
**“For a thousand and six hundred furlongs”** — Stadia is a place and a course; it signifies those striving for the prize.
**“twelve thousand”**
• as to beginners, those making progress, and the perfect
• That is, those who are perfect in the faith of the Trinity from the four quarters of the world.
**“and the length”**
• longsuffering
• that is, faith or longsuffering
**“and the breadth”** — that is, charity
**“and the height thereof”** — that is, hope or contemplation
**“are equal”** — as to the reason for eliciting the act, not as to merit
21.17:
**“And he measured the wall thereof”** — that is, their defenders
**“an hundred and forty-four cubits”** — the cubit, in which the hand signifies work
**“the measure of a man, which is of an angel”** — or because they are equal to the angels, or because of so great a multitude
**“The measure of a man, which is of an angel”** — According to the letter, it shows that the angel appeared to him in the form of a man, so that it plainly indicates that he who was signified, the true angel, that is, the Son of God, was also a true man.
21.18:
**“And the building of the wall thereof was of jasper stone”** — by the stone, Christ, or strong men in faith
**“The building of the wall thereof was of jasper stone”** — That is, if anyone is instructed so as to be a defender of others, he has this from the faith which he holds firmly and preaches, which the green jasper signifies, so that he may be a defender of others.
**“but the city itself”** — that is, the lesser Church
**“pure gold”**
• because: “The saints shall shine,” etc.
• Gold signifies wisdom; glass signifies the purity of faith, which promises with the mouth what it believes in the heart.
**“pure”** — as to the soul
**“like to clear glass”**
• because the hearts of the saints also will shine through
• as to the body
• He had said that in this city there are walls and gates and foundations, and that some of these are greater and others less among themselves; here he goes on to say what the wall itself is like, and what the city itself is like, and the foundations and gates.
21.19:
**“And the foundations of the wall of the city”** — that is, the prophets
**“were adorned with all manner of precious stones”** — that is, by every kind of virtue, or by imitators who adorn the Church with life and glory
**“And the first foundation was jasper”** — The green jasper signifies the unfading greenness of faith; or jasper is the faith of the saints, not withering, but always persevering in the greenness of work.
**“Sapphire”** — Like the clear sky, it sends forth a burning brightness when struck by the rays of the sun; it signifies “the height of the hope of the saints,” whose “conversation is in heaven,” who, renewed by the true sun, seek eternal things more ardently, and teach others to seek them, saying: “Our conversation is in heaven.”
**“Chalcedony”** — It has the colour of a pale lamp; it shines in the open air, in a house it is dim; it resists the devices of all engravers; heated by the ray of the sun or by rubbing with the fingers, it draws chaff to itself. It signifies the flame of the inward charity of the saints, who, despised outwardly, shine in secret; this charity does good things in hiding, and in the secret of its conscience, so far as it conceals itself and is hidden from others by its work, it does not shine. But when it is bidden to profit others, then it appears what brightness it has within. It resists engravers, because amid the adversities of the world it is strong and cannot be cut, and can be conquered by no one; or if anyone wishes to engrave and paint it with flattering praise, it resists. It does not yield to him, because it despises vain glory; and such men, warmed by the rays of the true sun, that is, Christ, or by the finger, that is, the Holy Spirit, as if handled, draw to themselves the chaff, that is, sinners and the frail, and join them to themselves.
**“An emerald”** — The fourth, of exceeding greenness, above all herbs and leaves, so that it makes even the surrounding air green. There are many kinds of it, but the most precious is found in Scythia, a desert region, which griffins guard, animals with the body of a lion, but with the feet, head and wings of an eagle; they have four feet with which they run on the earth like lions, and they fly through the air like birds; they guard the aforesaid stones, and take them away not for themselves but for men; against them the Arimaspian goes and fights and takes them from them. The griffins are the devil, who tries to take Christ, or the gem of faith, from the faithful. But against him fights that people having one eye, that is, Christ, who do not walk in two ways, nor have a double heart, and they seize Christ or his faith. It is called the fourth because of the four gospels.
21.20:
**“Sardonyx”** — The fifth is three-coloured: black at the bottom, white in the middle, red at the top; that is, the saints in suffering, outwardly red, inwardly white, but despised through humility; which, because it comes from weakness of the body, which is carried on by the five senses, is called fifth.
**“Sardius”** — The sixth, of a blood-red single colour, signifies the glory of martyrdom. The sixth, because on the sixth day of the week Christ was crucified. Or the sardius, having the appearance of red earth, signifies the saints who, though lofty in the understanding of the mind, yet remember their frailty, considering themselves sons of Adam, who is called red earth, who was made on the sixth day; whence the sardius also is brought in as the sixth.
**“Chrysolite”** — It has a golden brightness, and seems to send forth burning sparks; this is spiritual preaching amid miracles: the gold is heavenly wisdom, and the sparks which it sends forth are the exhortations or miracles by which they kindle to the love of God and neighbour. Because this is done through the Holy Spirit, it is placed in the seventh place. Hence also it is called chrysolite, because it shines like gold.
**“Beryl”** — The eighth is the work of those who preach. It shines like water struck by the sun. It even burns the hand of the one holding it, because he who is joined to a holy man is kindled by his way of life. Others also say that, because it is of two colours, green and pale, it signifies “the saints set in contemplation, green, but returning, through the care of earthly administration, to the paleness of the active life.”
**“A topaz”** — The ninth: the rarer, the more precious; and it has two colours, of gold and of heavenly brightness, shining most when touched by the splendour of the sun, surpassing the brightness of all gems, singularly drawing the gaze of those who look at it; if you make it dim by polishing it more, if you leave it to nature it is brighter, and nothing among riches is dearer to kings. It signifies the contemplative life, which holy kings prefer to all the riches of works and the gems of virtues, and toward it they chiefly direct their gaze, and the more, the more often they are enlightened by divine grace. The golden colour is from inward charity, the heavenly from the sweetness of contemplation, which always grows dim from the rubbing of the world; for scarcely can anyone be touched by sorrows and at the same time behold with a tranquil mind the joys of heaven. Or if you polish it, as if you honour and adorn them with the dignities of the world, you make them dim, because they have less leisure for contemplation, or are of less merit. And as in the eighth the active life, so in the ninth the contemplative, which is that of the angels, of whom there are nine orders. Some say that it has the colours of all stones, whence it has its name, because pan means “all”; and it is found on an island of Egypt, which is called Topazon; it signifies “the saints shining with all the colours of virtues.”
**“A chrysoprasus”** — It is born in India, of a mixture of green and gold. Some say it is also purple with golden drops; it signifies “those who by charity deserve the greenness of the eternal fatherland,” and they show another purple, of martyrdom; and because they follow the example of the Lord, they are in India, that is, near the rising of the sun, and they await to reign with Christ. They are in the number ten, and the decalogue will be fulfilled through the love which does not end; therefore in the chrysoprasus the work of martyrdom and its reward are signified. Chryson is called gold, passos, leek.
**“the tenth, a chrysoprasus”** — This gloss belongs to another page. The chrysoprasus is said to be of a green and golden colour; and because it is placed in the tenth place, it signifies certain doctors of the Church, who both taught us many things while placed in the body, and instructed many more by their writings. They instruct daily, as Jerome, Gregory, Ambrose, Augustine and other such. These can now rightly be called the lights of the Church. In their green colour the firmness of faith is understood, in the golden the brightness of wisdom. In the number ten the Old Testament is understood, as the ten precepts of the law. But because the Old Testament cannot be understood without the teaching of the New, since the special understanding in the Old is nothing other than the New Testament, it is fittingly placed in the tenth place, because they had the fullest knowledge of the Old and the New. We can understand something else also by the number ten. For the number ten both divides and orders and perfects all numbers; so these also in a certain way divided the Scriptures when they partitioned them by sentences and books in expounding. They ordered them when they opened their obscurities, and when they seemed ordered, they made manifest how right an order they had. And they perfected them when they supplied what seemed to be lacking.
**“A jacinth”** — The eleventh, which changes with the air, clear in fair weather, dim in cloud, signifies the most discerning doctors, adapting themselves to all qualities, characters, ages, understandings, as Paul, who said: “We speak wisdom among the perfect.” Likewise: “I could not speak to you,” etc. Likewise: “Who is weak?” etc. Likewise: “I became all things to all men, that I might gain all.”
**“An amethyst”** — The twelfth, purple, with a mixed colour of violet and rose, pouring forth certain little flames from itself. The purple colour signifies the condition of the heavenly kingdom and the principality of the angelic company, to which the saints are to come. The violet, the humble modesty of the saints, with the fragrance of good works. The rose, the precious death of the martyrs, who send out flames of charity not only among themselves but even to their enemies and persecutors. The amethyst therefore signifies the constant memory of the heavenly kingdom in the hearts of the humble, and that excellent virtue, that they pray even for their enemies and care for their salvation, which is the virtue of virtues. The variety of colours is the multiplicity of virtues.
21.21:
**“And the twelve gates”**
• since they are
• As if I had said that there are twelve gates, and since there are these twelve gates, that is, the prophets leading in to the faith of the Trinity from the four parts of the world, through each one, that is, through the instruction of each, there are pearls, that is, their imitators, who are called from whatever part of the world to the faith of the Trinity, and are resplendent in virtues.
• The twelve gates, that is, all who lead in, founded in the four parts of the world on the faith of the holy Trinity, each bring in twelve, that is, all from the four parts, to the faith of the holy Trinity; who are the pearls, that is, bright and solid.
**“are twelve pearls, one to each: and every several gate was of one several pearl”** — because they too, likewise, are bright in virtues
**“Every several gate”** — As if: for this, that they should be gates, they had to be pearls.
**“And the street of the city”**
• that is, the married
• that is, the simpler ones who use the world more loosely
• The street of the city, gold, that is, wisdom, or brightness, full and clean from criminal stain.
**“pure gold, as it were transparent glass”** — Transparent glass, that is, concealing no filth within itself; or because the wicked can know their wickedness in their works as in a mirror.
21.22:
**“And I saw no temple”** — that is, the place of prayer and offering, which will have no place there
**“And I saw no temple therein. For the Lord God Almighty is the temple thereof”** — that is, complete rest in every way
**“and the Lamb”** — likewise he is its temple
21.23:
**“And the city hath no need”** — by the light of faith
**“Hath no need”** — Here they need the sun and moon for the service of God; there they will not, for God will fully illuminate them.
**“nor of the moon”**
• acquired knowledge
• Or it does not need sun nor moon, that is, greater or lesser preachers.
**“to shine”** — to this end
**“in it, for the glory of God”** — that is, the Trinity
**“hath enlightened it, and the Lamb is the lamp thereof”** — that is, by the light, namely containing the deity
**“the Lamb is the lamp thereof”** — that is, the humanity
21.24:
**“And the nations shall walk”**
• for the enlightenment of others
• There will be such light in the future that the nations will walk until the end of the world, that is, they will be advanced from good to better.
**“the nations”** — the lesser and the subjects
**“in the light of it”** — In the light. In hope of this light, or through the light, or through the brightness, or through the rays of its knowledge.
**“and the kings of the earth”** — the greater ones
**“The kings of the earth”** — That is, those greater ones who rule their own earthly life and that of others.
**“shall bring their glory”** — that is, the things acquired, for which they will be crowned
**“and honour”** — purity of conscience
**“into it”** — for having it
21.25:
**“And the gates thereof”** — for seeing and praising God: understanding and affection
**“shall not be shut”**
• this concerns the future
• In the present, preaching is sometimes withdrawn, lest thieves enter and trample while it is night, that is, the place of ambushes; but because there the day is perpetual and all fear will be taken away.
**“by day: for there shall be no night there”** — through some adversity
21.26:
**“And they shall bring”**
• in the future itself
• that is, they will present to God the Father
**“They shall bring”** — In the likeness of victors who carry spoils into their cities.
**“glory”** — the nations glorified
**“and honour of the nations into it”** — that is, the purity of the consciences of the nations
21.27:
**“There shall not enter into it”** — or 'it'
**“There shall not enter”** — Having stated the honour of the city, lest any false brother presume to attain to any of these degrees, he determines who will enter and who will not.
**“any thing defiled”** — defiled with others through consent, as far as sin of the heart
**“abomination”** — that is, anything criminal
**“making”** — or as far as sin of deed
**“and maketh a lie”**
• he makes a lie who delights in finding lies
• or: as far as sin of the mouth
**“but”** — as if: what, one by one, no one will enter, except
**“they that are written in the book of life of the Lamb”** — that is, of humanity, through which it shall be given

22.1:
**“And he shewed me a river”** — eternal blessedness
**“And he shewed”** — After he has shown the site of the city, its dignity, and its walls and foundations, he describes the refreshment which God has provided for the city, both in the present, and most of all in the future, in the presence of the Godhead, or in the imitation of the life of the Lamb, who set before us an example in himself. A river, that is, flowing water, that is, eternal blessedness in the likeness of water; it is signified that one has come to this through the washing of baptism.
**“of water of life”** — because it refreshes after labour and gives eternal life
**“clear”** — because they will shine eternally
**“clear as crystal”** — on account of the transparency of hearts and bodies
**“proceeding from the throne of God and of the Lamb”** — that is, from the greater ones, who are the seats of God, to the lesser
**“from the throne of God”** — That is, from those in whom God will principally sit, because he is most of all in them, and through their instruction the lesser will be crowned.
22.2:
**“In the midst of the street thereof”** — that is, in the common (street) of those who have walked the broader way
**“and on both sides of the river”** — in the way and homeland of blessedness
**“the tree of life”** — Christ
**“on both sides of the river was the tree”** — On this side of the river, that is, in this life, we have the tree of life, that is, the body and blood of Christ, by which we are refreshed. Beyond the river, that is, in the future, we shall have him himself present. Or let us take by this side of the river the time before baptism, by beyond it that which was after baptism, that we may denote the faithful, saved through Christ both in the old and in the new law; which Moses signified, who led the children of Israel as far as the river Jordan, and Jesus the son of Nave, who led them from the river Jordan into the land of promise.
**“bearing twelve fruits”**
• the reward of immortality
• eternally
• The tree. Another reading: the tree of life yielding its fruit through twelve months, that is, through the twelve apostles, because Christ is the day and the year, the apostles the hours or months, as it is said there: “Are there not twelve hours of the day?”, as if he were to say: you are subject to me, and it is for me to provide, not you; and there are other trees there yielding their fruit, that is, the saints, who will render to those subject to them rewards according to merits.
**“the tree bearing fruits”** — As if: he himself gives refreshment; he also gives to those who would prepare them those to whom he himself will render; and this is “bearing twelve fruits.”
**“every month”** — through individual ages, or constantly
**“twelve fruits”** — That is, the prophets and apostles, bearing fruit in faith in the Trinity through the four parts of the world.
**“yielding its fruits”** — refreshment
**“and the leaves of the tree”** — that is, the precepts of Christ, which cover and adorn the fruit
**“and the leaves”** — As if: and what Christ will render as fruit, this will be such that the apostles, and after them others also, will scatter the leaves of Christ himself.
**“for the healing of the nations”** — if they are filled
22.3:
**“And there shall be no curse any more”**
• that is, the withdrawal of grace will not happen any more
• sin, on account of which one deserves a curse
**“but the throne of God and of the Lamb shall be in it”** — that is, God the Trinity and Christ as man will rest eternally in them
**“and his servants”** — not of fear but of love
**“shall serve him”** — they will in no way trouble them
22.4:
**“And they shall see his face”** — not in a riddle, as now, but as he is
**“and his name”** — they shall be called of God and of the Lamb
**“on their foreheads”** — that is, openly, as they have confessed him openly
22.5:
**“And night”** — some ignorance
**“shall be no more”** — that is, the teaching of the old law or of some ordinary preacher
**“nor the light of the sun, because the Lord God shall enlighten them”** — by the light of others
**“and shall reign”** — with him
**“for ever and ever”** — which is opposed to needing the light of others
22.6:
**“And he said to me”**
• the same angel who had shown the rest
• As at the beginning he set down the commendation of the vision, so now too at the end he sets it down.
**“These words”** — that is, whatever he showed me in words and figures
**“are most faithful and true”**
• because they will be fulfilled
• that is, fit to be given faith
**“the Lord God of the spirits of the prophets”** — And you should well believe, because he who has in his power the gifts of the Holy Spirit, through whom all the prophets spoke, said it.
**“sent his angel to shew”** — To shew his angel, etc. As the angel to John, so John commends to his disciples. As if he said: this announcement was not made to me for my own sake, but that you may believe me.
**“his servants”**
• not to kings, not to philosophers
• not in fear
**“the things which must be done shortly”** — because they cannot remain unfulfilled
22.7:
**“Behold I come quickly”**
• and they will truly come quickly, because he himself says
• and this he said: Blessed, etc.
**“Blessed is he that keepeth”** — fulfils it in deed
22.8:
**“And I, John”** — who am accustomed to say nothing false to you
**“who have heard”** — the words
**“and seen these things”** — the figures
**“And after I had heard and seen”**
• that is, I humbled myself
• And after, etc. Here he lets us understand that for these things we ought to hold him in reverence, not only him, but to worship God; and through keeping the words of the book, to attain the equality of the angels.
**“I fell down to adore before the feet of the angel, who shewed me these things”** — as if for this cause
22.9:
**“And he said to me: See”** — beware
**“thou do it not”** — on account of human nature exalted in Christ
**“for I am thy fellow servant”** — because of the one God.
**“and of thy brethren the prophets”**
• that is, of preachers.
• And of thy brethren the prophets, etc. They are not to be thought strangers to the office of prophecy who have the grace of interpreting, as Augustine, Jerome, Ambrose, Gregory.
**“and of them that keep the words of the prophecy of this book”** — that is, obedience of prophecy to preachers.
22.10:
**“And he saith to me: Seal not the words of the prophecy of this book”** — do not seal them, but set them out openly for all.
**“for the time is at hand”** — that is, in which it is necessary to gain brethren.
22.11:
**“He that hurteth, let him hurt”**
• let them inflict on good men what evil men inflict.
• He that hurteth, etc. Because it could be objected that it would be evil to prophesy to the wicked, since they would be punished more severely for it, it was said to him not to cease on that account, because it is just.
**“still”** — still: that is, after the showing of the book.
**“and he that is filthy”** — and he that is filthy: that is, in his own wickedness.
**“be filthy still”** — let him be filthy still: a permissive, not imperative, mood by the just judgment of God.
**“and he that is just, let him be justified still”**
• and he that is just, let him be justified still; or another reading: let him do justice.
• that is, let him who inflicts good on others inflict it more abundantly.
**“He that is filthy”** — Another reading: He that is in filth, let him be filthy still, and the just man let him be justified still.
**“and holy”** — in himself.
22.12:
**“Behold, I come quickly”** — truly the time is short.
**“and my reward is with me”** — namely.
**“to render to every man according to”** — or according to.
**“his works”**
• to one more, to another less.
• and I will be able to do it, because I etc.
22.13:
**“I am Alpha and Omega, the first”** — of all things.
**“and the last”** — of all creatures.
**“the beginning”** — from whom all things began.
**“and the end”** — in whom all things are completed.
22.14:
**“Blessed are they that wash their robes in the blood of the Lamb”** — I say it so: they wash, as etc.
**“Blessed are they that wash”** — Because he had said, “he that hurteth, let him hurt still; he that is filthy, let him be filthy still,” lest some wicked man should say: since I am wicked, why should I repent? He says that not only are they blessed who receive the greater persecution, but also those who have defiled their robes which they received in baptism, if afterwards they have washed them and repent that they have sinned.
**“that they may have a right to the tree of life”** — that they may be able to eat of the tree of life.
**“and may enter in by the gates”** — that is, the faith of the teachers.
**“may enter in by the gates into the city”** — but.
22.15:
**“Without”** — are.
**“are dogs”** — barking and unclean.
**“and sorcerers”** — literally
**“and unchaste, and murderers, and servers of idols”** — these are wretched and those blessed
**“and every one that loveth”** — by hearing
**“and maketh”** — finds
**“a lie”** — and this is to be believed by me, because
22.16:
**“I Jesus have sent my angel, to testify to you these things in the churches”** — and this is to be believed by me, because
**“I Jesus”** — He commended the book through the angel, by his own dignity, and now also by the authority of Christ himself, as if to say: let all who hear know that I, Jesus, have sent my angel to testify these things to you.
**“I am the root and stock”** — since he too was begotten by him
**“and the root”** — support
**“of David, the bright and morning star”** — that is, illuminating the night of this world
**“the bright and morning star”** — A bright star, that is, great brightness announcing the day, that is, future blessedness, through my resurrection made in the morning.
22.17:
**“And the spirit and the bride”**
• or: the bridegroom and the bride
• Here he also adds the testimony of the Trinity and of the faithful, as if to say: therefore you ought to receive it, because the spirit and the bride, etc.
**“And the spirit”** — that is, the Trinity, which is called “spirit” because of the excellence of its purity.
**“say: Come”** — for knowledge of the book
**“And he that heareth”** — understands the book
**“let him say”** — to others
**“Come”** — for knowledge of those things that are in this book
**“And he that thirsteth”**
• desires to believe in Christ
• And he that thirsteth. And yet not just anyone, but only he who thirsts, that is, desires to believe, let him come.
**“let him come”** — through true faith
**“And he that will, let him take the water of life”** — by preparing himself and by willing
**“He that will, let him take”** — And it is no labour, because the will alone suffices.
**“freely”** — without the price of merits
22.18:
**“For I testify”** — as if: the angel testified to me, and likewise I testify, etc.
**“I testify”** — Since he has placed the commendation through himself, through the angel, through Christ, through the Trinity, through the faithful, because he knew that some in Asia were adding or taking away something to foster their errors, he subjoins excommunication.
**“For I testify to every one that heareth the words of the prophecy of this book: If any man”** — namely, I testify this
**“shall add to these things”** — so that he may thereby foster error
**“God shall add unto him the plagues written in this book”** — concerning the bowls above and the trumpets
22.19: **“And if any man shall take away from the words of the book of this prophecy, God shall take away his part out of the book of life”** — or: from the tree
22.20:
**“saith”**
• As if to say: of excommunication.
• As if: I excommunicate, and Christ excommunicates, and the Church.
• As if he said: I excommunicate, and Jesus confirms.
**“He that”** — that is, Jesus.
**“giveth testimony of these things, saith, Surely I come quickly”**
• Take heed to yourselves, because I am coming.
• and now all things are as if true, and whoever changes them is excommunicated.
**“Amen”**
• conversion to God.
• Amen, that is, all the things that have been said are true; and therefore if anyone shall change them, let him be excommunicated.
**“Come, Lord Jesus”**
• to reward.
• “Come, O Lord, and delay not.”
• The apostle says to the Lord, out of the excessive affection of one longing, that he come to reward.
22.21:
**“The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all”**
• As above, it began with grace, so it ends.
• The words of the apostle, and he confirms that Christ will come soon.
**“The grace of our Lord”** — The apostle’s conclusion in the words of Christ.
**“Amen”**
• Emmanuel, Emmanuel.
• The names of the three magi are these in Hebrew: Apellius, Amarus, Damascus; in Greek: Galgalath, Magalath, Saracin.
• Apellius is interpreted as “gathering them”; Amarus, Damascus: blood of sackcloth; Galgalath: revelation or place of circumcision.

1.text: In the beginning God created heaven, and earth.

2.text: And the earth was void and empty, and darkness was upon the face of the deep; and the spirit of God moved over the waters.

3.text: And God said: Be light made. And light was made.

4.text: And God saw the light that it was good; and he divided the light from the darkness.

5.text: And he called the light Day, and the darkness Night; and there was evening and morning one day.

6.text: And God said: Let there be a firmament made amidst the waters: and let it divide the waters from the waters.

7.text: And God made a firmament, and divided the waters that were under the firmament, from those that were above the firmament, and it was so.

8.text: And God called the firmament, Heaven; and the evening and morning were the second day.

9.text: God also said: Let the waters that are under the heaven, be gathered together into one place: and let the dry land appear. And it was so done.

10.text: And God called the dry land, Earth; and the gathering together of the waters, he called Seas. And God saw that it was good.

11.text: And he said: Let the earth bring forth the green herb, and such as may seed, and the fruit tree yielding fruit after its kind, which may have seed in itself upon the earth. And it was so done.

12.text: And the earth brought forth the green herb, and such as yieldeth seed according to its kind, and the tree that beareth fruit, having seed each one according to its kind. And God saw that it was good.

13.text: And the evening and the morning were the third day.

14.text: And God said: Let there be lights made in the firmament of heaven, to divide the day and the night, and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days and years:

15.text: To shine in the firmament of heaven, and to give light upon the earth. And it was so done.

16.text: And God made two great lights: a greater light to rule the day; and a lesser light to rule the night: and the stars.

17.text: And he set them in the firmament of heaven to shine upon the earth.

18.text: And to rule the day and the night, and to divide the light and the darkness. And God saw that it was good.

19.text: And the evening and morning were the fourth day.

20.text: God also said: Let the waters bring forth the creeping creature having life, and the fowl that may fly over the earth under the firmament of heaven.

21.text: And God created the great whales, and every living and moving creature, which the waters brought forth, according to their kinds, and every winged fowl according to its kind. And God saw that it was good.

22.text: And he blessed them, saying: Increase and multiply, and fill the waters of the sea: and let the birds be multiplied upon the earth.

23.text: And the evening and morning were the fifth day.

24.text: And God said: Let the earth bring forth the living creature in its kind, cattle and creeping things, and beasts of the earth, according to their kinds. And it was so done.

25.text: And God made the beasts of the earth according to their kinds, and cattle, and every thing that creepeth on the earth after its kind. And God saw that it was good.

26.text: And he said: Let us make man to our image and likeness: and let him have dominion over the fishes of the sea, and the fowls of the air, and the beasts, and the whole earth, and every creeping creature that moveth upon the earth.

27.text: And God created man to his own image: to the image of God he created him: male and female he created them.

28.text: And God blessed them, saying: Increase and multiply, and fill the earth, and subdue it, and rule over the fishes of the sea, and the fowls of the air, and all living creatures that move upon the earth.

29.text: And God said: Behold I have given you every herb bearing seed upon the earth, and all trees that have in themselves seed of their own kind, to be your meat:

30.text: And to all beasts of the earth, and to every fowl of the air, and to all that move upon the earth, and wherein there is life, that they may have to feed upon. And it was so done.

31.text: And God saw all the things that he had made, and they were very good. And the evening and morning were the sixth day.

1.text: So the heavens and the earth were finished, and all the furniture of them.

2.text: And on the seventh day God ended his work which he had made: and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had done.

3.text: And he blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it: because in it he had rested from all his work which God created and made.

4.text: These are the generations of the heaven and the earth, when they were created, in the day that the Lord God made the heaven and the earth:

5.text: And every plant of the field before it sprung up in the earth, and every herb of the ground before it grew: for the Lord God had not rained upon the earth; and there was not a man to till the earth.

6.text: But a spring rose out of the earth, watering all the surface of the earth.

7.text: And the Lord God formed man of the slime of the earth: and breathed into his face the breath of life, and man became a living soul.

8.text: And the Lord God had planted a paradise of pleasure from the beginning: wherein he placed man whom he had formed.

9.text: And the Lord God brought forth of the ground all manner of trees, fair to behold, and pleasant to eat of: the tree of life also in the midst of paradise: and the tree of knowledge of good and evil.

10.text: And a river went out of the place of pleasure to water paradise, which from thence is divided into four heads.

11.text: The name of the one is Phison: that is it which compasseth all the land of Hevilath, where gold groweth.

12.text: And the gold of that land is very good: there is found bdellium, and the onyx stone.

13.text: And the name of the second river is Gehon: the same is it that compasseth all the land of Ethiopia.

14.text: And the name of the third river is Tigris: the same passeth along by the Assyrians. And the fourth river is Euphrates.

15.text: And the Lord God took man, and put him into the paradise of pleasure, to dress it, and to keep it.

16.text: And he commanded him, saying: Of every tree of paradise thou shalt eat:

17.text: But of the tree of knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat. For in what day soever thou shalt eat of it, thou shalt die the death.

18.text: And the Lord God said: It is not good for man to be alone: let us make him a help like unto himself.

19.text: And the Lord God having formed out of the ground all the beasts of the earth, and all the fowls of the air, brought them to Adam to see what he would call them: for whatsoever Adam called any living creature the same is its name.

20.text: And Adam called all the beasts by their names, and all the fowls of the air, and all the cattle of the field: but for Adam there was not found a helper like himself.

21.text: Then the Lord God cast a deep sleep upon Adam: and when he was fast asleep, he took one of his ribs, and filled up flesh for it.

22.text: And the Lord God built the rib which he took from Adam into a woman: and brought her to Adam.

23.text: And Adam said: This now is bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh; she shall be called woman, because she was taken out of man.

24.text: Wherefore a man shall leave father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife: and they shall be two in one flesh.

25.text: And they were both naked: to wit, Adam and his wife: and were not ashamed.

1.text: Now the serpent was more subtle than any of the beasts of the earth which the Lord God had made. And he said to the woman: Why hath God commanded you, that you should not eat of every tree of paradise?

2.text: And the woman answered him, saying: Of the fruit of the trees that are in paradise we do eat:

3.text: But of the fruit of the tree which is in the midst of paradise, God hath commanded us that we should not eat; and that we should not touch it, lest perhaps we die.

4.text: And the serpent said to the woman: No, you shall not die the death.

5.text: For God doth know that in what day soever you shall eat thereof, your eyes shall be opened: and you shall be as Gods, knowing good and evil.

6.text: And the woman saw that the tree was good to eat, and fair to the eyes, and delightful to behold: and she took of the fruit thereof, and did eat, and gave to her husband who did eat.

7.text: And the eyes of them both were opened: and when they perceived themselves to be naked, they sewed together fig leaves, and made themselves aprons.

8.text: And when they heard the voice of the Lord God walking in paradise at the afternoon air, Adam and his wife hid themselves from the face of the Lord God, amidst the trees of paradise.

9.text: And the Lord God called Adam, and said to him: Where art thou?

10.text: And he said: I heard thy voice in paradise; and I was afraid, because I was naked, and I hid myself.

11.text: And he said to him: And who hath told thee that thou wast naked, but that thou hast eaten of the tree whereof I commanded thee that thou shouldst not eat?

12.text: And Adam said: The woman, whom thou gavest me to be my companion, gave me of the tree, and I did eat.

13.text: And the Lord God said to the woman: Why hast thou done this? And she answered: The serpent deceived me, and I did eat.

14.text: And the Lord God said to the serpent: Because thou hast done this thing, thou art cursed among all cattle, and beasts of the earth: upon thy breast shalt thou go, and earth shalt thou eat all the days of thy life.

15.text: I will put enmities between thee and the woman, and thy seed and her seed: she shall crush thy head, and thou shalt lie in wait for her heel.

16.text: To the woman also he said: I will multiply thy sorrows, and thy conceptions: in sorrow shalt thou bring forth children, and thou shalt be under thy husband’s power, and he shall have dominion over thee.

17.text: And to Adam he said: Because thou hast hearkened to the voice of thy wife, and hast eaten of the tree, whereof I commanded thee that thou shouldst not eat, cursed is the earth in thy work; with labour and toil shalt thou eat thereof all the days of thy life.

18.text: Thorns and thistles shall it bring forth to thee; and thou shalt eat the herbs of the earth.

19.text: In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread till thou return to the earth, out of which thou wast taken: for dust thou art, and into dust thou shalt return.

20.text: And Adam called the name of his wife Eve: because she was the mother of all the living.

21.text: And the Lord God made for Adam and his wife, garments of skins, and clothed them.

22.text: And he said: Behold Adam is become as one of us, knowing good and evil: now, therefore, lest perhaps he put forth his hand, and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live for ever.

23.text: And the Lord God sent him out of the paradise of pleasure, to till the earth from which he was taken.

24.text: And he cast out Adam; and placed before the paradise of pleasure Cherubims, and a flaming sword, turning every way, to keep the way of the tree of life.

1.text: And Adam knew Eve his wife: who conceived and brought forth Cain, saying: I have gotten a man through God.

2.text: And again she brought forth his brother Abel. And Abel was a shepherd, and Cain a husbandman.

3.text: And it came to pass after many days, that Cain offered, of the fruits of the earth, gifts to the Lord.

4.text: Abel also offered of the firstlings of his flock, and of their fat: and the Lord had respect to Abel, and to his offerings.

5.text: But to Cain and his offerings he had no respect: and Cain was exceedingly angry, and his countenance fell.

6.text: And the Lord said to him: Why art thou angry? and why is thy countenance fallen?

7.text: If thou do well, shalt thou not receive? but if ill, shall not sin forthwith be present at the door? but the lust thereof shall be under thee, and thou shalt have dominion over it.

8.text: And Cain said to Abel his brother: Let us go forth abroad. And when they were in the field, Cain rose up against his brother Abel, and slew him.

9.text: And the Lord said to Cain: Where is thy brother Abel? And he answered, I know not: am I my brother’s keeper?

10.text: And he said to him: What hast thou done? the voice of thy brother’s blood crieth to me from the earth.

11.text: Now, therefore, cursed shalt thou be upon the earth, which hath opened her mouth and received the blood of thy brother at thy hand.

12.text: When thou shalt till it, it shall not yield to thee its fruit: a fugitive and a vagabond shalt thou be upon the earth.

13.text: And Cain said to the Lord: My iniquity is greater than that I may deserve pardon.

14.text: Behold thou dost cast me out this day from the face of the earth, and I shall be hidden from thy face, and I shall be a vagabond and a fugitive on the earth: every one, therefore, that findeth me, shall kill me.

15.text: And the Lord said to him: No, it shall not be so: but whosoever shall kill Cain, shall be punished sevenfold. And the Lord set a mark upon Cain, that whosoever found him should not kill him.

16.text: And Cain went out from the face of the Lord, and dwelt as a fugitive on the earth, at the east side of Eden.

17.text: And Cain knew his wife, and she conceived, and brought forth Henoch: and he built a city, and called the name thereof by the name of his son Henoch.

18.text: And Henoch begot Irad, and Irad begot Maviael, and Maviael begot Mathusael, and Mathusael begot Lamech:

19.text: Who took two wives: the name of the one was Ada, and the name of the other Sella.

20.text: And Ada brought forth Jabel: who was the father of such as dwell in tents, and of herdsmen.

21.text: And his brother’s name was Jubal; he was the father of them that play upon the harp and the organs.

22.text: Sella also brought forth Tubalcain, who was a hammerer and artificer in every work of brass and iron. And the sister of Tubalcain was Noema.

23.text: And Lamech said to his wives Ada and Sella: Hear my voice, ye wives of Lamech, hearken to my speech: for I have slain a man to the wounding of myself, and a stripling to my own bruising.

24.text: Sevenfold vengeance shall be taken for Cain: but for Lamech seventy times sevenfold.

25.text: Adam also knew his wife again: and she brought forth a son, and called his name Seth, saying: God hath given me another seed, for Abel whom Cain slew.

26.text: But to Seth also was born a son, whom he called Enos; this man began to call upon the name of the Lord.

1.text: This is the book of the generation of Adam. In the day that God created man, he made him to the likeness of God.

2.text: He created them male and female; and blessed them: and called their name Adam, in the day when they were created.

3.text: And Adam lived a hundred and thirty years, and begot a son to his own image and likeness, and called his name Seth.

4.text: And the days of Adam, after he begot Seth, were eight hundred years: and he begot sons and daughters.

5.text: And all the time that Adam lived came to nine hundred and thirty years, and he died.

6.text: Seth also lived a hundred and five years, and begot Enos.

7.text: And Seth lived after he begot Enos, eight hundred and seven years, and begot sons and daughters.

8.text: And all the days of Seth were nine hundred and twelve years, and he died.

9.text: And Enos lived ninety years, and begot Cainan.

10.text: After whose birth he lived eight hundred and fifteen years, and begot sons and daughters.

11.text: And all the days of Enos were nine hundred and five years, and he died.

12.text: And Cainan lived seventy years, and begot Malaleel.

13.text: And Cainan lived after he begot Malaleel, eight hundred and forty years, and begot sons and daughters.

14.text: And all the days of Cainan were nine hundred and ten years, and he died.

15.text: And Malaleel lived sixty-five years, and begot Jared.

16.text: And Malaleel lived after he begot Jared, eight hundred and thirty years, and begot sons and daughters.

17.text: And all the days of Malaleel were eight hundred and ninety-five years, and he died.

18.text: And Jared lived a hundred and sixty-two years, and begot Henoch.

19.text: And Jared lived after he begot Henoch, eight hundred years, and begot sons and daughters.

20.text: And all the days of Jared were nine hundred and sixty-two years, and he died.

21.text: And Henoch lived sixty-five years, and begot Mathusala.

22.text: And Henoch walked with God: and lived after he begot Mathusala, three hundred years, and begot sons and daughters.

23.text: And all the days of Henoch were three hundred and sixty-five years.

24.text: And he walked with God, and was seen no more: because God took him.

25.text: And Mathusala lived a hundred and eighty-seven years, and begot Lamech.

26.text: And Mathusala lived after he begot Lamech, seven hundred and eighty-two years, and begot sons and daughters.

27.text: And all the days of Mathusala were nine hundred and sixty-nine years, and he died.

28.text: And Lamech lived a hundred and eighty-two years, and begot a son.

29.text: And he called his name Noe, saying: This same shall comfort us from the works and labours of our hands on the earth, which the Lord hath cursed.

30.text: And Lamech lived after he begot Noe, five hundred and ninety-five years, and begot sons and daughters.

31.text: And all the days of Lamech came to seven hundred and seventy-seven years, and he died.

32.text: And all the days of Lamech came to seven hundred and seventy-seven years, and he died.

1.text: And after that men began to be multiplied upon the earth, and daughters were born to them,

2.text: The sons of God seeing the daughters of men, that they were fair, took to themselves wives of all which they chose.

3.text: And God said: My spirit shall not remain in man for ever, because he is flesh, and his days shall be a hundred and twenty years.

4.text: Now giants were upon the earth in those days. For after the sons of God went in to the daughters of men, and they brought forth children, these are the mighty men of old, men of renown.

5.text: And God seeing that the wickedness of men was great on the earth, and that all the thought of their heart was bent upon evil at all times,

6.text: It repented him that he had made man on the earth. And being touched inwardly with sorrow of heart,

7.text: He said: I will destroy man, whom I have created, from the face of the earth, from man even to beasts, from the creeping thing even to the fowls of the air, for it repenteth me that I have made them.

8.text: But Noe found grace before the Lord.

9.text: These are the generations of Noe: Noe was a just and perfect man in his generations, he walked with God.

10.text: And he begot three sons, Sem, Cham, and Japheth.

11.text: And the earth was corrupted before God, and was filled with iniquity.

12.text: And when God had seen that the earth was corrupted (for all flesh had corrupted its way upon the earth,)

13.text: He said to Noe: The end of all flesh is come before me, the earth is filled with iniquity through them, and I will destroy them with the earth.

14.text: Make thee an ark of timber planks: thou shalt make little rooms in the ark, and thou shalt pitch it within and without.

15.text: And thus shalt thou make it: The length of the ark shall be three hundred cubits: the breadth of it fifty cubits, and the height of it thirty cubits.

16.text: Thou shalt make a window in the ark, and in a cubit shalt thou finish the top of it: and the door of the ark thou shalt set in the side: with lower, middle chambers, and third stories shalt thou make it.

17.text: Behold I will bring the waters of a great flood upon the earth, to destroy all flesh, wherein is the breath of life, under heaven. All things that are in the earth shall be consumed.

18.text: And I will establish my covenant with thee, and thou shalt enter into the ark, thou and thy sons, and thy wife, and the wives of thy sons with thee.

19.text: And of every living creature of all flesh, thou shalt bring two of a sort into the ark, that they may live with thee: of the male sex, and the female.

20.text: Of fowls according to their kind, and of beasts in their kind, and of every thing that creepeth on the earth according to its kind; two of every sort shall go in with thee, that they may live.

21.text: Thou shalt take unto thee of all food that may be eaten, and thou shalt lay it up with thee: and it shall be food for thee and them.

22.text: And Noe did all things which God commanded him.

1.text: And the Lord said to him: Go in thou and all thy house into the ark: for thee I have seen just before me in this generation.

2.text: Of all clean beasts take seven and seven, the male and the female.

3.text: But of the beasts that are unclean two and two, the male and the female. Of the fowls also of the air seven and seven, the male and the female: that seed may be saved upon the face of the whole earth.

4.text: For yet a while, and after seven days, I will rain upon the earth forty days and forty nights; and I will destroy every substance that I have made, from the face of the earth.

5.text: And Noe did all things which the Lord had commanded him.

6.text: And he was six hundred years old, when the waters of the flood overflowed the earth.

7.text: And Noe went in and his sons, his wife and the wives of his sons with him into the ark, because of the waters of the flood.

8.text: And of beasts clean and unclean, and of fowls, and of every thing that moveth upon the earth,

9.text: Two and two went in to Noe into the ark, male and female, as the Lord had commanded Noe.

10.text: And after the seven days were passed, the waters of the flood overflowed the earth.

11.text: In the six hundredth year of the life of Noe, in the second month, in the seventeenth day of the month, all the fountains of the great deep were broken up, and the flood gates of heaven were opened:

12.text: And the rain fell upon the earth forty days and forty nights.

13.text: In the selfsame day Noe, and Sem, and Cham, and Japheth his sons: his wife, and the three wives of his sons with them, went into the ark:

14.text: They and every beast according to its kind, and all the cattle in their kind, and every thing that moveth upon the earth according to its kind, and every fowl according to its kind, all birds, and all that fly,

15.text: Went in to Noe into the ark, two and two of all flesh, wherein was the breath of life.

16.text: And they that went in, went in male and female of all flesh, as God had commanded him: and the Lord shut him in on the outside.

17.text: And the flood was forty days upon the earth, and the waters increased, and lifted up the ark on high from the earth.

18.text: For they overflowed exceedingly: and filled all on the face of the earth: and the ark was carried upon the waters.

19.text: And the waters prevailed beyond measure upon the earth: and all the high mountains under the whole heaven were covered.

20.text: The water was fifteen cubits higher than the mountains which it covered.

21.text: And all flesh was destroyed that moved upon the earth, both of fowl, and of cattle, and of beasts, and of all creeping things that creep upon the earth: and all men.

22.text: And all things wherein there is the breath of life on the earth, died.

23.text: And he destroyed all the substance that was upon the earth, from man even to beast, and the creeping things and fowls of the air: and they were destroyed from the earth: and Noe only remained, and they that were with him in the ark.

24.text: And the waters prevailed upon the earth a hundred and fifty days.

1.text: And God remembered Noe, and all the living creatures, and all the cattle which were with him in the ark, and brought a wind upon the earth, and the waters were abated.

2.text: The fountains also of the deep, and the flood gates of heaven were shut up, and the rain from heaven was restrained.

3.text: And the waters returned from off the earth going and coming: and they began to be abated after a hundred and fifty days.

4.text: And the ark rested in the seventh month, the seven and twentieth day of the month, upon the mountains of Armenia.

5.text: And the waters were going and decreasing until the tenth month: for in the tenth month, the first day of the month, the tops of the mountains appeared.

6.text: And after that forty days were passed, Noe, opening the window of the ark which he had made, sent forth a raven:

7.text: Which went forth and did not return, till the waters were dried up upon the earth.

8.text: He sent forth also a dove after him, to see if the waters had now ceased upon the face of the earth.

9.text: But she, not finding where her foot might rest, returned to him into the ark: for the waters were upon the whole earth: and he put forth his hand, and caught her, and brought her into the ark.

10.text: And having waited yet seven other days, he again sent forth the dove out of the ark.

11.text: And she came to him in the evening, carrying a bough of an olive tree, with green leaves, in her mouth. Noe therefore understood that the waters were ceased upon the earth.

12.text: And he stayed yet other seven days: and he sent forth the dove, which returned not any more unto him.

13.text: Therefore in the six hundredth and first year, the first month, the first day of the month, the waters were lessened upon the earth, and Noe opening the covering of the ark, looked, and saw that the face of the earth was dried.

14.text: In the second month, the seven and twentieth day of the month, the earth was dried.

15.text: And God spoke to Noe, saying:

16.text: Go out of the ark, thou and thy wife, thy sons, and the wives of thy sons with thee.

17.text: All living things that are with thee of all flesh, as well in fowls as in beasts, and all creeping things that creep upon the earth, bring out with thee, and go ye upon the earth: increase and multiply upon it.

18.text: So Noe went out, he and his sons: his wife, and the wives of his sons with him.

19.text: And all living things, and cattle, and creeping things that creep upon the earth, according to their kinds, went out of the ark.

20.text: And Noe built an altar unto the Lord: and taking of all cattle and fowls that were clean, offered holocausts upon the altar.

21.text: And the Lord smelled a sweet savour, and said: I will no more curse the earth for the sake of man: for the imagination and thought of man’s heart are prone to evil from his youth: therefore I will no more destroy every living soul as I have done.

22.text: All the days of the earth, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, night and day, shall not cease.

1.text: And God blessed Noe and his sons. And he said to them: Increase and multiply, and fill the earth.

2.text: And let the fear and dread of you be upon all the beasts of the earth, and upon all the fowls of the air, and all that move upon the earth: all the fishes of the sea are delivered into your hand.

3.text: And every thing that moveth and liveth shall be meat for you: even as the green herbs have I delivered them all to you:

4.text: Saving that flesh with blood you shall not eat.

5.text: For I will require the blood of your lives at the hand of every beast, and at the hand of man, at the hand of every man, and of his brother, will I require the life of man.

6.text: Whosoever shall shed man’s blood, his blood shall be shed: for man was made to the image of God.

7.text: But increase you and multiply, and go upon the earth, and fill it.

8.text: Thus also said God to Noe, and to his sons with him,

9.text: Behold I will establish my covenant with you, and with your seed after you:

10.text: And with every living soul that is with you, as well in all birds as in cattle and beasts of the earth, that are come forth out of the ark, and in all the beasts of the earth.

11.text: I will establish my covenant with you, and all flesh shall be no more destroyed with the waters of a flood, neither shall there be from henceforth a flood to waste the earth.

12.text: And God said: This is the sign of the covenant which I give between me and you, and to every living soul that is with you, for perpetual generations.

13.text: I will set my bow in the clouds, and it shall be the sign of a covenant between me, and between the earth.

14.text: And when I shall cover the sky with clouds, my bow shall appear in the clouds:

15.text: And I will remember my covenant with you, and with every living soul that beareth flesh: and there shall no more be waters of a flood to destroy all flesh.

16.text: And the bow shall be in the clouds, and I shall see it, and shall remember the everlasting covenant, that was made between God and every living soul of all flesh which is upon the earth.

17.text: And God said to Noe: This shall be the sign of the covenant which I have established between me and all flesh upon the earth.

18.text: And the sons of Noe who came out of the ark, were Sem, Cham, and Japheth: and Cham is the father of Chanaan.

19.text: These three are the sons of Noe: and from these was all mankind spread over the whole earth.

20.text: And Noe, a husbandman, began to till the ground, and planted a vineyard.

21.text: And drinking of the wine was made drunk, and was uncovered in his tent.

22.text: Which when Cham the father of Chanaan had seen, to wit, that his father’s nakedness was uncovered, he told it to his two brethren without.

23.text: But Sem and Japheth put a cloak upon their shoulders, and going backward, covered the nakedness of their father: and their faces were turned away, and they saw not their father’s nakedness.
