6.text: And the divider shall sit in Azotus, and I will destroy the pride of the Philistines.

7.text: And I will take away his blood out of his mouth, and his abominations from between his teeth: and even he shall be left to our God, and he shall be as a governor in Juda, and Accaron as a Jebusite.

8.text: And I will encompass my house with them that serve me in war, going and returning, and the oppressor shall no more pass through them: for now I have seen with my eyes.

9.text: Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Sion, shout for joy, O daughter of Jerusalem: BEHOLD THY KING will come to thee, the just and saviour: he is poor, and riding upon an ass, and upon a colt the foal of an ass.

10.text: And I will destroy the chariot out of Ephraim, and the horse out of Jerusalem, and the bow for war shall be broken: and he shall speak peace to the Gentiles, and his power shall be from sea to sea, and from the rivers even to the end of the earth.

11.text: Thou also by the blood of thy testament hast sent forth thy prisoners out of the pit, wherein is no water.

12.text: Return to the strong hold, ye prisoners of hope, I will render thee double as I declare today.

13.text: Because I have bent Juda for me as a bow, I have filled Ephraim: and I will raise up thy sons, O Sion, above thy sons, O Greece, and I will make thee as the sword of the mighty.

14.text: And the Lord God shall be seen over them, and his dart shall go forth as lightning: and the Lord God will sound the trumpet, and go in the whirlwind of the south.

15.text: The Lord of hosts will protect them: and they shall devour, and subdue with the stones of the sling: and drinking they shall be inebriated as it were with wine, and they shall be filled as bowls, and as the horns of the altar.

16.text: And the Lord their God will save them in that day, as the flock of his people: for holy stones shall be lifted up over his land.

17.text: For what is the good thing of him, and what is his beautiful thing, but the corn of the elect, and wine springing forth virgins?

1.text: Ask ye of the Lord rain in the latter season, and the Lord will make snows, and will give them showers of rain, to every one grass in the field.

2.text: For the idols have spoken what was unprofitable, and the diviners have seen a lie, and the dreamers have spoken vanity: they comforted in vain: therefore they were led away as a flock: they shall be afflicted, because they have no shepherd.

3.text: My wrath is kindled against the shepherds, and I will visit upon the buck goats: for the Lord of hosts hath visited his flock, the house of Juda, and hath made them as the horse of his glory in the battle.

4.text: Out of him shall come forth the corner, out of him the pin, out of him the bow of battle, out of him every exacter together.

5.text: And they shall be as mighty men, treading under foot the mire of the ways in battle: and they shall fight, because the Lord is with them, and the riders of horses shall be confounded.

6.text: And I will strengthen the house of Juda, and save the house of Joseph: and I will bring them back again, because I will have mercy on them: and they shall be as they were when I had cast them off, for I am the Lord their God, and will hear them.

7.text: And they shall be as the valiant men of Ephraim, and their heart shall rejoice as through wine: and their children shall see, and shall rejoice, and their heart shall be joyful in the Lord.

8.text: I will whistle for them, and I will gather them together, because I have redeemed them: and I will multiply them as they were multiplied before.

9.text: And I will sow them among peoples: and from afar they shall remember me: and they shall live with their children, and shall return.

10.text: And I will bring them back out of the land of Egypt, and will gather them from among the Assyrians: and will bring them to the land of Galaad, and Libanus, and place shall not be found for them.

11.text: And he shall pass over the strait of the sea, and shall strike the waves in the sea, and all the depths of the river shall be confounded, and the pride of Assyria shall be humbled, and the sceptre of Egypt shall depart.

12.text: I will strengthen them in the Lord, and they shall walk in his name, saith the Lord.

1.text: Open thy gates, O Libanus, and let fire devour thy cedars.

2.text: Howl, thou fir tree, for the cedar is fallen, for the mighty are laid waste: howl, ye oaks of Basan, because the fenced forest is cut down.

3.text: The voice of the howling of the shepherds, because their glory is laid waste: the voice of the roaring of the lions, because the pride of the Jordan is spoiled.

4.text: Thus saith the Lord my God: Feed the flock of the slaughter,

5.text: Which they that possessed, slew, and repented not, and they sold them, saying: Blessed be the Lord, we are become rich: and their shepherds spared them not.

6.text: And I will no more spare the inhabitants of the land, saith the Lord: behold I will deliver the men, every one into his neighbour’s hand, and into the hand of his king: and they shall destroy the land, and I will not deliver it out of their hand.

7.text: And I will feed the flock of slaughter for this, O ye poor of the flock. And I took unto me two rods, one I called Beauty, and the other I called a Cord, and I fed the flock.

8.text: And I cut off three shepherds in one month, and my soul was straitened in their regard: for their soul also varied in my regard.

9.text: And I said: I will not feed you: that which dieth, let it die: and that which is cut off, let it be cut off: and let the rest devour every one the flesh of his neighbour.

10.text: And I took my rod that was called Beauty, and I cut it asunder to make void my covenant, which I had made with all people.

11.text: And it was made void in that day: and so the poor of the flock that keep for me, understood that it is the word of the Lord.

12.text: And I said to them: If it be good in your eyes, bring hither my wages: and if not, be quiet. And they weighed for my wages thirty pieces of silver.

13.text: And the Lord said to me: Cast it to the statuary, a handsome price, that I was prized at by them. And I took the thirty pieces of silver, and I cast them into the house of the Lord to the statuary.

14.text: And I cut off my second rod that was called a Cord, that I might break the brotherhood between Juda and Israel.

15.text: And the Lord said to me: Take to thee yet the instruments of a foolish shepherd.

16.text: For behold I will raise up a shepherd in the land, who shall not visit what is forsaken, nor seek what is scattered, nor heal what is broken, nor nourish that which standeth, and he shall eat the flesh of the fat ones, and break their hoofs.

17.text: O shepherd, and idol, that forsaketh the flock: the sword upon his arm and upon his right eye: his arm shall quite wither away, and his right eye shall be utterly darkened.

1.text: The burden of the word of the Lord upon Israel. Thus saith the Lord, who stretcheth forth the heavens, and layeth the foundations of the earth, and formeth the spirit of man in him:

2.text: Behold I will make Jerusalem a lintel of surfeiting to all the people round about: and Juda also shall be in the siege against Jerusalem.

3.text: And it shall come to pass in that day, that I will make Jerusalem a burdensome stone to all people: all that shall lift it up shall be rent and torn, and all the kingdoms of the earth shall be gathered together against her.

4.text: In that day, saith the Lord, I will strike every horse with astonishment, and his rider with madness: and I will open my eyes upon the house of Juda, and will strike every horse of the nations with blindness.

5.text: And the governors of Juda shall say in their heart: Let the inhabitants of Jerusalem be strengthened for me in the Lord of hosts, their God.

6.text: In that day I will make the governors of Juda like a furnace of fire amongst wood, and as a firebrand amongst hay: and they shall devour all the people round about, to the right hand, and to the left: and Jerusalem shall be inhabited again in her own place in Jerusalem.

7.text: And the Lord shall save the tabernacles of Juda, as in the beginning: that the house of David, and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem, may not boast and magnify themselves against Juda.

8.text: In that day shall the Lord protect the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and he that hath offended among them in that day shall be as David: and the house of David, as that of God, as an angel of the Lord in their sight.

9.text: And it shall come to pass in that day, that I will seek to destroy all the nations that come against Jerusalem.

10.text: And I will pour out upon the house of David, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the spirit of grace, and of prayers: and they shall look upon me, whom they have pierced: and they shall mourn for him as one mourneth for an only son, and they shall grieve over him, as the manner is to grieve for the death of the firstborn.

11.text: In that day there shall be a great lamentation in Jerusalem like the lamentation of Adadremmon in the plain of Mageddon.

12.text: And the land shall mourn: families and families apart: the families of the house of David apart, and their women apart:

13.text: The families of the house of Nathan apart, and their women apart: the families of the house of Levi apart, and their women apart: the families of Semei apart, and their women apart.

14.text: All the rest of the families, families and families apart, and their women apart.

1.text: In that day there shall be a fountain open to the house of David, and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem: for the washing of the sinner, and of the unclean woman.

2.text: And it shall come to pass in that day, saith the Lord of hosts, that I will destroy the names of idols out of the earth, and they shall be remembered no more: and I will take away the false prophets, and the unclean spirit out of the earth.

3.text: And it shall come to pass, that when any man shall prophesy any more, his father and his mother that brought him into the world, shall say to him: Thou shalt not live: because thou hast spoken a lie in the name of the Lord. And his father, and his mother, his parents, shall thrust him through, when he shall prophesy.

4.text: And it shall come to pass in that day, that the prophets shall be confounded, every one by his own vision, when he shall prophesy, neither shall they be clad with a garment of sackcloth, to deceive:

5.text: But he shall say: I am no prophet, I am a husbandman: for Adam is my example from my youth.

6.text: And they shall say to him: What are these wounds in the midst of thy hands? And he shall say: With these I was wounded in the house of them that loved me.

7.text: Awake, O sword, against my shepherd, and against the man that cleaveth to me, saith the Lord of hosts: strike the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered: and I will turn my hand to the little ones.

8.text: And there shall be in all the earth, saith the Lord, two parts in it shall be scattered, and shall perish: but the third part shall be left therein.

9.text: And I will bring the third part through the fire, and will refine them as silver is refined: and I will try them as gold is tried. They shall call on my name, and I will hear them. I will say: Thou art my people: and they shall say: The Lord is my God.

1.text: Behold the days of the Lord shall come, and thy spoils shall be divided in the midst of thee.

2.text: And I will gather all nations to Jerusalem to battle, and the city shall be taken, and the houses shall be rifled, and the women shall be defiled: and half of the city shall go forth into captivity, and the rest of the people shall not be taken away out of the city.

3.text: Then the Lord shall go forth, and shall fight against those nations, as when he fought in the day of battle.

4.text: And his feet shall stand in that day upon the mount of Olives, which is over against Jerusalem toward the east: and the mount of Olives shall be divided in the midst thereof to the east, and to the west with a very great opening, and half of the mountain shall be separated to the north, and half thereof to the south.

5.text: And you shall flee to the valley of those mountains, for the valley of the mountains shall be joined even to the next, and you shall flee as you fled from the face of the earthquake in the days of Ozias king of Juda: and the Lord my God shall come, and all the saints with him.

6.text: And it shall come to pass in that day, that there shall be no light, but cold and frost.

7.text: And there shall be one day, which is known to the Lord, not day nor night: and in the time of the evening there shall be light.

8.text: And it shall come to pass in that day, that living waters shall go out from Jerusalem: half of them to the east sea, and half of them to the last sea: they shall be in summer and in winter.

9.text: And the Lord shall be king over all the earth: in that day there shall be one Lord, and his name shall be one.

10.text: And all the land shall return even to the desert, from the hill to Remmon to the south of Jerusalem: and she shall be exalted, and shall dwell in her own place, from the gate of Benjamin even to the place of the former gate, and even to the gate of the corners: and from the tower of Hananeel even to the king’s winepresses.

11.text: And people shall dwell in it, and there shall be no more an anathema: but Jerusalem shall sit secure.

12.text: And this shall be the plague wherewith the Lord shall strike all nations that have fought against Jerusalem: the flesh of every one shall consume away while they stand upon their feet, and their eyes shall consume away in their holes, and their tongue shall consume away in their mouth.

13.text: In that day there shall be a great tumult from the Lord among them: and a man shall take the hand of his neighbour, and his hand shall be clasped upon his neighbour’s hand.

14.text: And even Juda shall fight against Jerusalem: and the riches of all nations round about shall be gathered together, gold, and silver, and garments in great abundance.

15.text: And the destruction of the horse, and of the mule, and of the camel, and of the ass, and of all the beasts, that shall be in those tents, shall be like this destruction.

16.text: And all they that shall be left of all nations that came against Jerusalem, shall go up from year to year, to adore the King, the Lord of hosts, and to keep the feast of tabernacles.

17.text: And it shall come to pass, that he that shall not go up of the families of the land to Jerusalem, to adore the King, the Lord of hosts, there shall be no rain upon them.

18.text: And if the family of Egypt go not up nor come: neither shall it be upon them, but there shall be destruction wherewith the Lord will strike all nations that will not go up to keep the feast of tabernacles.

19.text: This shall be the sin of Egypt, and this the sin of all nations, that will not go up to keep the feast of tabernacles.

20.text: In that day that which is upon the bridle of the horse shall be holy to the Lord: and the caldrons in the house of the Lord shall be as the phials before the altar.

21.text: And every caldron in Jerusalem and Juda shall be sanctified to the Lord of hosts: and all that sacrifice shall come, and take of them, and shall seethe in them: and the merchant shall be no more in the house of the Lord of hosts in that day.

1.text: The burden of the word of the Lord to Israel by the hand of Malachias.

2.text: I have loved you, saith the Lord: and you have said: Wherein hast thou loved us? Was not Esau brother to Jacob, saith the Lord, and I have loved Jacob,

3.text: But have hated Esau? and I have made his mountains a wilderness, and given his inheritance to the dragons of the desert.

4.text: But if Edom shall say: We are destroyed, but we will return and build up what hath been destroyed: thus saith the Lord of hosts: They shall build up, and I will throw down: and they shall be called the borders of wickedness, and the people with whom the Lord is angry for ever.

5.text: And your eyes shall see, and you shall say: The Lord be magnified upon the border of Israel.

6.text: The son honoureth the father, and the servant his master: if then I be a father, where is my honour? and if I be a master, where is my fear? saith the Lord of hosts.

7.text: To you, O priests, that despise my name, and have said: Wherein have we despised thy name? You offer polluted bread upon my altar, and you say: Wherein have we polluted thee? In that you say: The table of the Lord is contemptible.

8.text: If you offer the blind for sacrifice, is it not evil? and if you offer the lame and the sick, is it not evil? offer it to thy prince, if he will be pleased with it, or if he will regard thy face, saith the Lord of hosts.

9.text: And now beseech ye the face of God, that he may have mercy on you, (for by your hand hath this been done,) if by any means he will receive your faces, saith the Lord of hosts.

10.text: Who is there among you, that will shut the doors, and will kindle the fire on my altar gratis? I have no pleasure in you, saith the Lord of hosts: and I will not receive a gift of your hand.

11.text: For from the rising of the sun even to the going down, my name is great among the Gentiles, and in every place there is sacrifice, and there is offered to my name a clean oblation: for my name is great among the Gentiles, saith the Lord of hosts.

12.text: And you have profaned it in that you say: The table of the Lord is defiled: and that which is laid thereupon is contemptible with the fire that devoureth it.

13.text: And you have said: Behold of our labour, and you puffed it away, saith the Lord of hosts, and you brought in of rapine the lame, and the sick, and brought in an offering: shall I accept it at your hands, saith the Lord?

14.text: Cursed is the deceitful man that hath in his flock a male, and making a vow offereth in sacrifice that which is feeble to the Lord: for I am a great King, saith the Lord of hosts, and my name is dreadful among the Gentiles.

1.text: And now, O ye priests, this commandment is to you.

2.text: If you will not hear, and if you will not lay it to heart, to give glory to my name, saith the Lord of hosts: I will send poverty upon you, and will curse your blessings, yea I will curse them, because you have not laid it to heart.

3.text: Behold, I will cast the shoulder to you, and I will scatter upon your face the dung of your solemnities, and it shall take you away with it.

4.text: And you shall know that I sent you this commandment, that my covenant might be with Levi, saith the Lord of hosts.

5.text: My covenant was with him of life and peace: and I gave him fear: and he feared me, and he was afraid before my name.

6.text: The law of truth was in his mouth, and iniquity was not found in his lips: he walked with me in peace, and in equity, and turned many away from iniquity.

7.text: For the lips of the priest shall keep knowledge, and they shall seek the law at his mouth: because he is the angel of the Lord of hosts.

8.text: But you have departed out of the way, and have caused many to stumble at the law: you have made void the covenant of Levi, saith the Lord of hosts.

9.text: Therefore have I also made you contemptible, and base before all people, as you have not kept my ways, and have accepted persons in the law.

10.text: Have we not all one father? hath not one God created us? why then doth every one of us despise his brother, violating the covenant of our fathers?

11.text: Juda hath transgressed, and abomination hath been committed in Israel, and in Jerusalem: for Juda hath profaned the holiness of the Lord, which he loved, and hath married the daughter of a strange god.

12.text: The Lord will cut off the man that hath done this, both the master, and the scholar, out of the tabernacles of Jacob, and him that offereth an offering to the Lord of hosts.

13.text: And this again have you done, you have covered the altar of the Lord with tears, with weeping, and bellowing, so that I have no more a regard to sacrifice, neither do I accept any atonement at your hands.

14.text: And you have said: For what cause? Because the Lord hath been witness between thee, and the wife of thy youth, whom thou hast despised: yet she was thy partner, and the wife of thy covenant.

15.text: Did not one make her, and she is the residue of his spirit? And what doth one seek, but the seed of God? Keep then your spirit, and despise not the wife of thy youth.

16.text: When thou shalt hate her put her away, saith the Lord the God of Israel: but iniquity shall cover his garment, saith the Lord of hosts, keep your spirit, and despise not.

17.text: You have wearied the Lord with your words, and you said: Wherein have we wearied him? In that you say: Every one that doth evil, is good in the sight of the Lord, and such please him: or surely where is the God of judgment?

1.text: Behold I send my angel, and he shall prepare the way before my face. And presently the Lord, whom you seek, and the angel of the testament, whom you desire, shall come to his temple. Behold he cometh, saith the Lord of hosts.

2.text: And who shall be able to think of the day of his coming? and who shall stand to see him? for he is like a refining fire, and like the fuller’s herb:

3.text: And he shall sit refining and cleansing the silver, and he shall purify the sons of Levi, and shall refine them as gold, and as silver, and they shall offer sacrifices to the Lord in justice.

4.text: And the sacrifice of Juda and of Jerusalem shall please the Lord, as in the days of old, and in the ancient years.

5.text: And I will come to you in judgment, and will be a speedy witness against sorcerers, and adulterers, and false swearers, and them that oppress the hireling in his wages; the widows, and the fatherless: and oppress the stranger, and have not feared me, saith the Lord of hosts.

6.text: For I am the Lord, and I change not: and you the sons of Jacob are not consumed.

7.text: For from the days of your fathers you have departed from my ordinances, and have not kept them: Return to me, and I will return to you, saith the Lord of hosts. And you have said: Wherein shall we return?

8.text: Shall a man afflict God? for you afflict me. And you have said: Wherein do we afflict thee? in tithes and in firstfruits.

9.text: And you are cursed with want, and you afflict me, even the whole nation of you.

10.text: Bring all the tithes into the storehouse, that there may be meat in my house, and try me in this, saith the Lord: if I open not unto you the flood-gates of heaven, and pour you out a blessing even to abundance.

11.text: And I will rebuke for your sakes the devourer, and he shall not spoil the fruit of your land: neither shall the vine in the field be barren, saith the Lord of hosts.

12.text: And all nations shall call you blessed: for you shall be a delightful land, saith the Lord of hosts.

13.text: Your words have been unsufferable to me, saith the Lord.

14.text: And you have said: What have we spoken against thee? You have said: He laboureth in vain that serveth God, and what profit is it that we have kept his ordinances, and that we have walked sorrowful before the Lord of hosts?

15.text: Wherefore now we call the proud people happy, for they that work wickedness are built up, and they have tempted God and are preserved.

16.text: Then they that feared the Lord spoke every one with his neighbour: and the Lord gave ear, and heard it: and a book of remembrance was written before him for them that fear the Lord, and think on his name.

17.text: And they shall be my special possession, saith the Lord of hosts, in the day that I do judgment: and I will spare them, as a man spareth his son that serveth him.

18.text: And you shall return, and shall see the difference between the just and the wicked: and between him that serveth God, and him that serveth him not.

1.text: For behold the day shall come kindled as a furnace: and all the proud, and all that do wickedly shall be stubble: and the day that cometh shall set them on fire, saith the Lord of hosts, it shall not leave them root, nor branch.

2.text: But unto you that fear my name, the Sun of justice shall arise, and health in his wings: and you shall go forth, and shall leap like calves of the herd.

3.text: And you shall tread down the wicked when they shall be ashes under the sole of your feet in the day that I do this, saith the Lord of hosts.

4.text: Remember the law of Moses my servant, which I commanded him in Horeb for all Israel, the precepts, and judgments.

5.text: Behold I will send you Elias the prophet, before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord.

6.text: And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers: lest I come, and strike the earth with anathema.

1.text: Now it came to pass, after that Alexander the son of Philip the Macedonian, who first reigned in Greece, coming out of the land of Cethim, had overthrown Darius king of the Persians and Medes:

2.text: He fought many battles, and took the strong holds of all, and slew the kings of the earth:

3.text: And he went through even to the ends of the earth, and took the spoils of many nations: and the earth was quiet before him. And he gathered a power, and a very strong army: and his heart was exalted and lifted up.

4.text: And he subdued countries of nations, and princes: and they became tributaries to him.

5.text: And after these things, he fell down upon his bed, and knew that he should die.

6.text: And he called his servants the nobles that were brought up with him from his youth: and he divided his kingdom among them, while he was yet alive.

7.text: And Alexander reigned twelve years, and he died.

8.text: And his servants made themselves kings every one in his place:

9.text: And they all put crowns upon themselves after his death, and their sons after them many years, and evils were multiplied in the earth.

10.text: And there came out of them a wicked root, Antiochus the Illustrious, the son of king Antiochus, who had been a hostage at Rome: and he reigned in the hundred and thirty-seventh year of the kingdom of the Greeks.

11.text: In those days there went out of Israel wicked men, and they persuaded many, saying: Let us go, and make a covenant with the heathens that are round about us: for since we departed from them, many evils have befallen us.

12.text: And the word seemed good in their eyes.

13.text: And some of the people determined to do this, and went to the king: and he gave them license to do after the ordinances of the heathens.

14.text: And they built a place of exercise in Jerusalem, according to the laws of the nations:

15.text: And they made themselves prepuces, and departed from the holy covenant, and joined themselves to the heathens, and were sold to do evil.

16.text: And the kingdom was established before Antiochus, and he had a mind to reign over the land of Egypt, that he might reign over two kingdoms.

17.text: And he entered into Egypt with a great multitude, with chariots and elephants, and horsemen, and a great number of ships:

18.text: And he made war against Ptolemee king of Egypt, but Ptolemee was afraid at his presence, and fled, and many were wounded unto death.

19.text: And he took the strong cities in the land of Egypt: and he took the spoils of the land of Egypt.

20.text: And after Antiochus had ravaged Egypt in the hundred and forty-third year, he returned and went up against Israel. And he went up to Jerusalem with a great multitude.

21.text: And he proudly entered into the sanctuary, and took away the golden altar, and the candlestick of light, and all the vessels thereof, and the table of proposition, and the pouring vessels, and the vials, and the little mortars of gold, and the veil, and the crowns, and the golden ornament that was before the temple: and he broke them all in pieces.

23.text: And he took the silver and gold, and the precious vessels: and he took the hidden treasures which he found: and when he had taken all away he departed into his own country.

24.text: And he made a great slaughter of men, and spoke very proudly.

25.text: And there was great mourning in Israel, and in every place where they were.

26.text: And the princes, and the ancients mourned, and the virgins and the young men were made feeble, and the beauty of the women was changed.

27.text: Every bridegroom took up lamentation: and the bride that sat in the marriage bed, mourned:

28.text: And the land was moved for the inhabitants thereof, and all the house of Jacob was covered with confusion.

29.text: And after two full years the king sent the chief collector of his tributes to the cities of Juda, and he came to Jerusalem with a great multitude.

30.text: And he spoke to them peaceable words in deceit: and they believed him. And he fell upon the city suddenly, and struck it with a great slaughter, and destroyed much people in Israel.

31.text: And he took the spoils of the city, and burnt it with fire, and threw down the houses thereof, and the walls thereof round about:

32.text: And they took the women captive, and the children, and the cattle they possessed.

33.text: And they built the city of David with a great and strong wall, and with strong towers, and made it a fortress for them:

34.text: And they placed there a sinful nation, wicked men, and they fortified themselves therein: and they stored up armour, and victuals, and gathered together the spoils of Jerusalem;

35.text: And laid them up there: and they became a great snare.

36.text: And this was a place to lie in wait against the sanctuary, and an evil devil in Israel.

37.text: And they shed innocent blood round about the sanctuary, and defiled the holy place.

38.text: And the inhabitants of Jerusalem fled away by reason of them, and the city was made the habitation of strangers, and she became a stranger to her own seed, and her children forsook her.

39.text: Her sanctuary was desolate like a wilderness, her festival days were turned into mourning, her sabbaths into reproach, her honours were brought to nothing.

40.text: Her dishonour was increased according to her glory, and her excellency was turned into mourning.

41.text: And king Antiochus wrote to all his kingdom, that all the people should be one: and every one should leave his own law. And all nations consented according to the word of king Antiochus.

43.text: And many of Israel consented to his service, and they sacrificed to idols, and profaned the sabbath.

44.text: And the king sent letters by the hands of messengers to Jerusalem, and to all the cities of Juda: that they should follow the law of the nations of the earth,

45.text: And should forbid holocausts and sacrifices, and atonements to be made in the temple of God. And should prohibit the sabbath, and the festival days, to be celebrated.

46.text: And he commanded the holy places to be profaned, and the holy people of Israel.

47.text: And he commanded altars to be built, and temples, and idols, and swine’s flesh to be immolated, and unclean beasts.

48.text: And that they should leave their children uncircumcised, and let their souls be defiled with all uncleannesses, and abominations, to the end that they should forget the law, and should change all the justifications of God.

50.text: And that whosoever would not do according to the word of king Antiochus should be put to death.

51.text: According to all these words he wrote to his whole kingdom, and he appointed rulers over the people that should force them to do these things. And they commanded the cities of Juda to sacrifice.

52.text: Then many of the people were gathered to them that had forsaken the law of the Lord: and they committed evils in the land:

53.text: And they drove away the people of Israel into lurking holes, and into the secret places of fugitives.

54.text: On the fifteenth day of the month Casleu, in the hundred and forty-fifth year, king Antiochus set up the abominable idol of desolation upon the altar of God, and they built altars throughout all the cities of Juda round about:

55.text: And they burnt incense, and sacrificed at the doors of the houses, and in the streets.

56.text: And they cut in pieces, and burnt with fire the books of the law of God:

57.text: And every one with whom the books of the testament of the Lord were found, and whosoever observed the law of the Lord, they put to death, according to the edict of the king.

58.text: Thus by their power did they deal with the people of Israel, that were found in the cities month after month.

59.text: And on the five and twentieth day of the month they sacrificed upon the altar of the idol that was over against the altar of God.

60.text: Now the women that circumcised their children, were slain according to the commandment of king Antiochus.

61.text: And they hanged the children about their necks in all their houses: and those that had circumcised them, they put to death.

62.text: And many of the people of Israel determined with themselves, that they would not eat unclean things: and they chose rather to die than to be defiled with unclean meats.

63.text: And they would not break the holy law of God, and they were put to death:

64.text: And there was very great wrath upon the people.

1.text: In those days arose Mathathias the son of John, the son of Simeon, a priest of the sons of Joarib, from Jerusalem, and he abode in the mountain of Modin.

2.text: And he had five sons: John who was surnamed Gaddis:

3.text: And Simon, who was surnamed Thasi:

4.text: And Judas, who was called Machabeus:

5.text: And Eleazar, who was surnamed Abaron: and Jonathan, who was surnamed Apphus.

6.text: These saw the evils that were done in the people of Juda, and in Jerusalem.

7.text: And Mathathias said: Woe is me, wherefore was I born to see the ruin of my people, and the ruin of the holy city, and to dwell there, when it is given into the hands of the enemies?

8.text: The holy places are come into the hands of strangers: her temple is become as a man without honour.

9.text: The vessels of her glory are carried away captive: her old men are murdered in the streets, and her young men are fallen by the sword of the enemies.

10.text: What nation hath not inherited her kingdom, and gotten of her spoils?

11.text: All her ornaments are taken away. She that was free is made a slave.

12.text: And behold our sanctuary, and our beauty, and our glory is laid waste, and the Gentiles have defiled them.

13.text: To what end then should we live any longer?

14.text: And Mathathias and his sons rent their garments, and they covered themselves with haircloth, and made great lamentation.

15.text: And they that were sent from king Antiochus came thither, to compel them that were fled into the city of Modin, to sacrifice, and to burn incense, and to depart from the law of God.

16.text: And many of the people of Israel consented, and came to them: but Mathathias and his sons stood firm.

17.text: And they that were sent from Antiochus, answering, said to Mathathias: Thou art a ruler, and an honourable, and great man in this city, and adorned with sons, and brethren.

18.text: Therefore come thou first, and obey the king’s commandment, as all nations have done, and the men of Juda, and they that remain in Jerusalem: and thou, and thy sons, shall be in the number of the king’s friends, and enriched with gold, and silver, and many presents.

19.text: Then Mathathias answered, and said with a loud voice: Although all nations obey king Antiochus, so as to depart every man from the service of the law of his fathers, and consent to his commandments:

20.text: I and my sons, and my brethren will obey the law of our fathers.

21.text: God be merciful unto us: it is not profitable for us to forsake the law, and the justices of God:

22.text: We will not hearken to the words of king Antiochus, neither will we sacrifice, and transgress the commandments of our law, to go another way.

23.text: Now as he left off speaking these words, there came a certain Jew in the sight of all to sacrifice to the idols upon the altar in the city of Modin, according to the king’s commandment.

24.text: And Mathathias saw and was grieved, and his reins trembled, and his wrath was kindled according to the judgment of the law, and running upon him he slew him upon the altar:

25.text: Moreover the man whom king Antiochus had sent, who compelled them to sacrifice, he slew at the same time, and pulled down the altar.

26.text: And shewed zeal for the law, as Phinees did by Zamri the son of Salomi.

27.text: And Mathathias cried out in the city with a loud voice, saying: Every one that hath zeal for the law, and maintaineth the testament, let him follow me.

28.text: So he, and his sons fled into the mountains, and left all that they had in the city.

29.text: Then many that sought after judgment, and justice, went down into the desert:

30.text: And they abode there, they and their children, and their wives, and their cattle: because afflictions increased upon them.

31.text: And it was told to the king’s men, and to the army that was in Jerusalem in the city of David, that certain men who had broken the king’s commandment, were gone away into the secret places in the wilderness, and that many were gone after them.

32.text: And forthwith they went out towards them, and made war against them on the sabbath day,

33.text: And they said to them: Do you still resist? come forth, and do according to the edict of king Antiochus, and you shall live.

34.text: And they said: We will not come forth, neither will we obey the king’s edict, to profane the sabbath day.

35.text: And they made haste to give them battle.

36.text: But they answered them not, neither did they cast a stone at them, nor stopped up the secret places,

37.text: Saying: Let us all die in our innocency: and heaven and earth shall be witnesses for us, that you put us to death wrongfully.

38.text: So they gave them battle on the sabbath: and they were slain with their wives, and their children, and their cattle, to the number of a thousand persons.

39.text: And Mathathias and his friends heard of it, and they mourned for them exceedingly.

40.text: And every man said to his neighbour: If we shall all do as our brethren have done, and not fight against the heathens for our lives, and our justifications: they will now quickly root us out of the earth.

41.text: And they determined in that day, saying: Whosoever shall come up against us to fight on the sabbath day, we will fight against him: and we will not all die, as our brethren that were slain in the secret places.

42.text: Then was assembled to them the congregation of the Assideans, the stoutest of Israel, every one that had a good will for the law.

43.text: And all they that fled from the evils, joined themselves to them, and were a support to them.

44.text: And they gathered an army, and slew the sinners in their wrath, and the wicked men in their indignation: and the rest fled to the nations for safety.

45.text: And Mathathias and his friends went round about, and they threw down the altars:

46.text: And they circumcised all the children whom they found in the confines of Israel that were uncircumcised: and they did valiantly.

47.text: And they pursued after the children of pride, and the work prospered in their hands:

48.text: And they recovered the law out of the hands of the nations, and out of the hands of the kings: and they yielded not the horn to the sinner.

49.text: Now the days drew near that Mathathias should die, and he said to his sons: Now hath pride and chastisement gotten strength, and the time of destruction, and the wrath of indignation:

50.text: Now therefore, O my sons, be ye zealous for the law, and give your lives for the covenant of your fathers.

51.text: And call to remembrance the works of the fathers, which they have done in their generations: and you shall receive great glory, and an everlasting name.

52.text: Was not Abraham found faithful in temptation, and it was reputed to him unto justice?

53.text: Joseph in the time of his distress kept the commandment, and he was made lord of Egypt.

54.text: Phinees our father, by being fervent in the zeal of God, received the covenant of an everlasting priesthood.

55.text: Jesus, whilst he fulfilled the word, was made ruler in Israel.

56.text: Caleb, for bearing witness before the congregation, received an inheritance.

57.text: David by his mercy obtained the throne of an everlasting kingdom.

58.text: Elias, while he was full of zeal for the law, was taken up into heaven.

59.text: Ananias and Azarias and Misael by believing, were delivered out of the flame.

60.text: Daniel in his innocency was delivered out of the mouth of the lions.

61.text: And thus consider through all generations: that none that trust in him fail in strength.

62.text: And fear not the words of a sinful man, for his glory is dung, and worms:

63.text: Today he is lifted up, and tomorrow he shall not be found, because he is returned into his earth; and his thought is come to nothing.

64.text: You therefore, my sons, take courage, and behave manfully in the law: for by it you shall be glorious.

65.text: And behold, I know that your brother Simon is a man of counsel: give ear to him always, and he shall be a father to you.

66.text: And Judas Machabeus who is valiant and strong from his youth up, let him be the leader of your army, and he shall manage the war of the people.

67.text: And you shall take to you all that observe the law: and revenge ye the wrong of your people.

68.text: Render to the Gentiles their reward, and take heed to the precepts of the law.

69.text: And he blessed them, and was joined to his fathers.

70.text: And he died in the hundred and forty-sixth year: and he was buried by his sons in the sepulchres of his fathers in Modin, and all Israel mourned for him with great mourning.

1.text: Then his son Judas, called Machabeus, rose up in his stead.

2.text: And all his brethren helped him, and all they that had joined themselves to his father, and they fought with cheerfulness the battle of Israel.

3.text: And he got his people great honour, and put on a breastplate as a giant, and girt his warlike armour about him in battles, and protected the camp with his sword.

4.text: In his acts he was like a lion, and like a lion’s whelp roaring for his prey.

5.text: And he pursued the wicked and sought them out, and them that troubled his people he burnt with fire:

6.text: And his enemies were driven away for fear of him, and all the workers of iniquity were troubled: and salvation prospered in his hand.

7.text: And he grieved many kings, and made Jacob glad with his works, and his memory is blessed for ever.

8.text: And he went through the cities of Juda, and destroyed the wicked out of them, and turned away wrath from Israel.

9.text: And he was renowned even to the utmost part of the earth, and he gathered them that were perishing.

10.text: And Apollonius gathered together the Gentiles, and a numerous and great army from Samaria, to make war against Israel.

11.text: And Judas understood it, and went forth to meet him: and he overthrew him, and killed him: and many fell down slain, the rest fled away.

12.text: And he took their spoils, and Judas took the sword of Apollonius, and fought with it all his lifetime.

13.text: And Seron captain of the army of Syria heard that Judas had assembled a company of the faithful, and a congregation with him,

14.text: And he said: I will get me a name, and will be glorified in the kingdom, and will overthrow Judas, and those that are with him, that have despised the edict of the king.

15.text: And he made himself ready: and the host of the wicked went up with him, strong succours, to be revenged of the children of Israel.

16.text: And they approached even as far as Bethoron: and Judas went forth to meet him, with a small company.

17.text: But when they saw the army coming to meet them, they said to Judas: How shall we, being few, be able to fight against so great a multitude and so strong, and we are ready to faint with fasting today?

18.text: And Judas said: It is an easy matter for many to be shut up in the hands of a few: and there is no difference in the sight of the God of heaven to deliver with a great multitude, or with a small company:

19.text: For the success of war is not in the multitude of the army, but strength cometh from heaven.

20.text: They come against us with an insolent multitude, and with pride, to destroy us, and our wives, and our children, and to take our spoils.

21.text: But we will fight for our lives and our laws:

22.text: And the Lord himself will overthrow them before our face: but as for you, fear them not.

23.text: And as soon as he had made an end of speaking, he rushed suddenly upon them: and Seron and his host were overthrown before him:

24.text: And he pursued him by the descent of Bethoron even to the plain, and there fell of them eight hundred men, and the rest fled into the land of the Philistines.

25.text: And the fear of Judas and of his brethren, and the dread of them fell upon all the nations round about them.

26.text: And his fame came to the king, and all nations told of the battles of Judas.

27.text: Now when king Antiochus heard these words, he was angry in his mind: and he sent and gathered the forces of all his kingdom, an exceeding strong army.

28.text: And he opened his treasury, and gave out pay to the army for a year: and he commanded them, that they should be ready for all things.

29.text: And he perceived that the money of his treasures failed, and that the tributes of the country were small because of the dissension, and the evil that he had brought upon the land, that he might take away the laws of old times:

30.text: And he feared that he should not have as formerly enough, for charges and gifts, which he had given before with a liberal hand: for he had abounded more than the kings that had been before him.

31.text: And he was greatly perplexed in mind, and purposed to go into Persia, and to take tributes of the countries, and to gather much money.

32.text: And he left Lysias, a nobleman of the blood royal, to oversee the affairs of the kingdom, from the river Euphrates even to the river of Egypt:

33.text: And to bring up his son Antiochus, till he came again.

34.text: And he delivered to him half the army, and the elephants: and he gave him charge concerning all that he would have done, and concerning the inhabitants of Judea, and Jerusalem:

35.text: And that he should send an army against them, to destroy and root out the strength of Israel, and the remnant of Jerusalem, and to take away the memory of them from that place:

36.text: And that he should settle strangers to dwell in all their coasts, and divide their land by lot.

37.text: So the king took the half of the army that remained, and went forth from Antioch the chief city of his kingdom, in the hundred and forty-seventh year: and he passed over the river Euphrates, and went through the higher countries.

38.text: Then Lysias chose Ptolemee the son of Dorymenus, and Nicanor, and Gorgias, mighty men of the king’s friends.

39.text: And he sent with them forty thousand men, and seven thousand horsemen: to go into the land of Juda, and to destroy it according to the king’s orders.

40.text: So they went forth with all their power, and came, and pitched near Emmaus in the plain country.

41.text: And the merchants of the countries heard the fame of them: and they took silver and gold in abundance, and servants: and they came into the camp, to buy the children of Israel for slaves: and there were joined to them the forces of Syria, and of the land of the strangers.

42.text: And Judas and his brethren saw that evils were multiplied, and that the armies approached to their borders: and they knew the orders the king had given to destroy the people and utterly abolish them.

43.text: And they said every man to his neighbour: Let us raise up the low condition of our people, and let us fight for our people, and our sanctuary.

44.text: And the assembly was gathered that they might be ready for battle: and that they might pray, and ask mercy and compassion.

45.text: Now Jerusalem was not inhabited, but was like a desert: there was none of her children that went in or out: and the sanctuary was trodden down: and the children of strangers were in the castle, there was the habitation of the Gentiles: and joy was taken away from Jacob, and the pipe and harp ceased there.

46.text: And they assembled together, and came to Maspha over against Jerusalem: for in Maspha was a place of prayer heretofore in Israel.

47.text: And they fasted that day, and put on haircloth, and put ashes upon their heads: and they rent their garments:

48.text: And they laid open the books of the law, in which the Gentiles searched for the likeness of their idols:

49.text: And they brought the priestly ornaments, and the firstfruits and tithes, and stirred up the Nazarites that had fulfilled their days:

50.text: And they cried with a loud voice toward heaven, saying: What shall we do with these, and whither shall we carry them?

51.text: For thy holies are trodden down, and are profaned, and thy priests are in mourning, and are brought low.

52.text: And behold the nations are come together against us to destroy us: thou knowest what they intend against us.

53.text: How shall we be able to stand before their face, unless thou, O God, help us?

54.text: Then they sounded with trumpets, and cried out with a loud voice.

55.text: And after this Judas appointed captains over the people, over thousands, and over hundreds, and over fifties, and over tens.

56.text: And he said to them that were building houses, or had betrothed wives, or were planting vineyards, or were fearful, that they should return every man to his house, according to the law.

57.text: So they removed the camp, and pitched on the south side of Emmaus.

58.text: And Judas said: Gird yourselves, and be valiant men, and be ready against the morning, that you may fight with these nations that are assembled against us to destroy us and our sanctuary.

59.text: For it is better for us to die in battle, than to see the evils of our nation, and of the holies:

60.text: Nevertheless as it shall be the will of God in heaven so be it done.

1.text: Then Gorgias took five thousand men, and a thousand of the best horsemen: and they removed out of the camp by night.

2.text: That they might come upon the camp of the Jews, and strike them suddenly: and the men that were of the castle were their guides.

3.text: And Judas heard of it, and rose up, he and the valiant men, to attack the king’s forces that were in Emmaus.

4.text: For as yet the army was dispersed from the camp.

5.text: And Gorgias came by night into the camp of Judas, and found no man, and he sought them in the mountains: for he said: These men flee from us.

6.text: And when it was day, Judas shewed himself in the plain with three thousand men only, who neither had armour nor swords.

7.text: And they saw the camp of the Gentiles that it was strong, and the men in breastplates, and the horsemen round about them, and these were trained up to war.

8.text: And Judas said to the men that were with him: Fear ye not their multitude, neither be ye afraid of their assault.

9.text: Remember in what manner our fathers were saved in the Red Sea, when Pharao pursued them with a great army.

10.text: And now let us cry to heaven: and the Lord will have mercy on us, and will remember the covenant of our fathers, and will destroy this army before our face this day:

11.text: And all nations shall know that there is one that redeemeth and delivereth Israel.

12.text: And the strangers lifted up their eyes, and saw them coming against them.

13.text: And they went out of the camp to battle, and they that were with Judas sounded the trumpet.

14.text: And they joined battle: and the Gentiles were routed, and fled into the plain.

15.text: But all the hindmost of them fell by the sword, and they pursued them as far as Gezeron, and even to the plains of Idumea, and of Azotus, and of Jamnia: and there fell of them to the number of three thousand men.

16.text: And Judas returned again with his army that followed him,

17.text: And he said to the people: Be not greedy of the spoils: for there is war before us:

18.text: And Gorgias and his army are near us in the mountain: but stand ye now against our enemies, and overthrow them, and you shall take the spoils afterwards with safety.

19.text: And as Judas was speaking these words, behold part of them appeared looking forth from the mountain.

20.text: And Gorgias saw that his men were put to flight, and that they had set fire to the camp: for the smoke that was seen declared what was done.

21.text: And when they had seen this, they were seized with great fear, seeing at the same time Judas and his army in the plain ready to fight.

22.text: So they all fled away into the land of the strangers.

23.text: And Judas returned to take the spoils of the camp, and they got much gold, and silver, and blue silk, and purple of the sea, and great riches.

24.text: And returning home they sung a hymn, and blessed God in heaven, because he is good, because his mercy endureth for ever.

25.text: So Israel had a great deliverance that day.

26.text: And such of the strangers as escaped, went and told Lysias all that had happened.

27.text: And when he heard these things, he was amazed and discouraged: because things had not succeeded in Israel according to his mind, and as the king had commanded.

28.text: So the year following Lysias gathered together threescore thousand chosen men, and five thousand horsemen, that he might subdue them.

29.text: And they came into Judea, and pitched their tents in Bethoron, and Judas met them with ten thousand men.

30.text: And they saw that the army was strong, and he prayed, and said: Blessed art thou, O Saviour of Israel, who didst break the violence of the mighty by the hand of thy servant David, and didst deliver up the camp of the strangers into the hands of Jonathan the son of Saul and of his armourbearer.

31.text: Shut up this army in the hands of thy people Israel, and let them be confounded in their host and their horsemen.

32.text: Strike them with fear, and cause the boldness of their strength to languish, and let them quake at their own destruction.

33.text: Cast them down with the sword of them that love thee: and let all that know thy name, praise thee with hymns.

34.text: And they joined battle: and there fell of the army of Lysias five thousand men.

35.text: And when Lysias saw that his men were put to flight, and how bold the Jews were, and that they were ready either to live, or to die manfully, he went to Antioch, and chose soldiers, that they might come again into Judea with greater numbers.

36.text: Then Judas, and his brethren said: Behold our enemies are discomfited: let us go up now to cleanse the holy places and to repair them.

37.text: And all the army assembled together, and they went up into mount Sion.

38.text: And they saw the sanctuary desolate, and the altar profaned, and the gates burnt, and shrubs growing up in the courts as in a forest, or on the mountains, and the chambers joining to the temple thrown down.

39.text: And they rent their garments, and made great lamentation, and put ashes on their heads:

40.text: And they fell face down to the ground on their faces, and they sounded with the trumpets of alarm, and they cried towards heaven.

41.text: Then Judas appointed men to fight against them that were in the castle, till they had cleansed the holy places.

42.text: And he chose priests without blemish, whose will was set upon the law of God:

43.text: And they cleansed the holy places, and took away the stones that had been defiled into an unclean place.

44.text: And he considered about the altar of holocausts that had been profaned, what he should do with it.

45.text: And a good counsel came into their minds, to pull it down: lest it should be a reproach to them, because the Gentiles had defiled it; so they threw it down.

46.text: And they laid up the stones in the mountain of the temple in a convenient place, till there should come a prophet, and give answer concerning them.

47.text: Then they took whole stones according to the law, and built a new altar according to the former:

48.text: And they built up the holy places, and the things that were within the temple: and they sanctified the temple, and the courts.

49.text: And they made new holy vessels, and brought in the candlestick, and the altar of incense, and the table into the temple.

50.text: And they put incense upon the altar, and lighted up the lamps that were upon the candlestick, and they gave light in the temple.

51.text: And they set the loaves upon the table, and hung up the veils, and finished all the works that they had begun to make.

52.text: And they arose before the morning on the five and twentieth day of the ninth month (which is the month of Casleu) in the hundred and forty-eighth year.

53.text: And they offered sacrifice according to the law upon the new altar of holocausts which they had made.

54.text: According to the time, and according to the day wherein the heathens had defiled it, in the same was it dedicated anew with canticles, and harps, and lutes, and cymbals.

55.text: And all the people fell upon their faces, and adored, and blessed up to heaven, him that had prospered them.

56.text: And they kept the dedication of the altar eight days, and they offered holocausts with joy, and sacrifices of salvation, and of praise.

57.text: And they adorned the front of the temple with crowns of gold, and escutcheons, and they renewed the gates, and the chambers, and hanged doors upon them.

58.text: And there was exceeding great joy among the people, and the reproach of the Gentiles was turned away.

59.text: And Judas, and his brethren, and all the church of Israel decreed, that the day of the dedication of the altar should be kept in its season from year to year for eight days, from the five and twentieth day of the month of Casleu, with joy and gladness.

60.text: They built up also at that time mount Sion, with high walls, and strong towers round about, lest the Gentiles should at any time come, and tread it down as they did before.

61.text: And he placed a garrison there to keep it, and he fortified it to secure Bethsura, that the people might have a defence against Idumea.

1.text: Now it came to pass, when the nations round about heard that the altar and the sanctuary were built up as before, that they were exceeding angry.

2.text: And they thought to destroy the generation of Jacob that were among them, and they began to kill some of the people, and to persecute them.

3.text: Then Judas fought against the children of Esau in Idumea, and them that were in Acrabathane: because they beset the Israelites around about, and he made a great slaughter of them.

4.text: And he remembered the malice of the children of Bean: who were a snare and a stumblingblock to the people, by lying in wait for them in the way.

5.text: And they were shut up by him in towers, and he set upon them, and devoted them to utter destruction, and burnt their towers with fire, and all that were in them.

6.text: Then he passed over to the children of Ammon, where he found a mighty power, and much people, and Timotheus was their captain:

7.text: And he fought many battles with them, and they were discomfited in their sight, and he smote them:

8.text: And he took the city of Gazer and her towns, and returned into Judea.

9.text: And the Gentiles that were in Galaad, assembled themselves together against the Israelites that were in their quarters to destroy them: and they fled into the fortress of Datheman.

10.text: And they sent letters to Judas and his brethren, saying, The heathens that are round about are gathered together against us, to destroy us:

11.text: And they are preparing to come, and to take the fortress into which we are fled: and Timotheus is the captain of their host.

12.text: Now therefore come, and deliver us out of their hands, for many of us are slain.

13.text: And all our brethren that were in the places of Tubin, are killed: and they have carried away their wives, and their children, captives, and taken their spoils, and they have slain there almost a thousand men.

14.text: And while they were yet reading these letters, behold there came other messengers out of Galilee with their garments rent, who related according to these words:

15.text: Saying, that they of Ptolemais, and of Tyre, and of Sidon, were assembled against them, and all Galilee is filled with strangers, in order to consume us.

16.text: Now when Judas and all the people heard these words, a great assembly met together to consider what they should do for their brethren that were in trouble, and were assaulted by them.

17.text: And Judas said to Simon his brother: Choose thee men, and go, and deliver thy brethren in Galilee: and I, and my brother Jonathan will go into the country of Galaad.

18.text: And he left Joseph the son of Zacharias, and Azarias captains of the people with the remnant of the army in Judea to keep it:

19.text: And he commanded them, saying: Take ye the charge of this people: but make no war against the heathens, till we return.

20.text: Now three thousand men were allotted to Simon, to go into Galilee: and eight thousand to Judas to go into the land of Galaad.

21.text: And Simon went into Galilee, and fought many battles with the heathens: and the heathens were discomfited before his face, and he pursued them even to the gate of Ptolemais.

22.text: And there fell of the heathens almost three thousand men, and he took the spoils of them,

23.text: And he took with him those that were in Galilee and in Arbatis with their wives, and children, and all that they had, and he brought them into Judea with great joy.

24.text: And Judas Machabeus, and Jonathan his brother passed over the Jordan, and went three days’ journey through the desert.

25.text: And the Nabutheans met them, and received them in a peaceable manner, and told them all that happened to their brethren in the land of Galaad,

26.text: And that many of them were shut up in Barasa, and in Bosor, and in Alima, and in Casphor, and in Mageth, and in Carnaim: all these strong and great cities.

27.text: Yea, and that they were kept shut up in the rest of the cities of Galaad, and that they had appointed to bring their army on the morrow near to these cities, and to take them and to destroy them all in one day.

28.text: Then Judas and his army suddenly turned their march into the desert, to Bosor, and took the city: and he slew every male by the edge of the sword, and took all their spoils, and burnt it with fire.

29.text: And they removed from thence by night, and went till they came to the fortress.

30.text: And it came to pass that early in the morning, when they lifted up their eyes, behold there were people without number, carrying ladders and engines to take the fortress, and assault them.

31.text: And Judas saw that the fight was begun, and the cry of the battle went up to heaven like a trumpet, and a great cry out of the city:

32.text: And he said to his host: Fight ye today for your brethren.

33.text: And he came with three companies behind them, and they sounded their trumpets, and cried out in prayer.

34.text: And the host of Timotheus understood that it was Machabeus, and they fled away before his face: and they made a great slaughter of them: and there fell of them in that day almost eight thousand men.

35.text: And Judas turned aside to Maspha, and assaulted, and took it, and he slew every male thereof, and took the spoils thereof, and burnt it with fire.

36.text: From thence he marched, and took Casbon, and Mageth, and Bosor, and the rest of the cities of Galaad.

37.text: But after this Timotheus gathered another army, and camped over against Raphon beyond the torrent.

38.text: And Judas sent men to view the army: and they brought him word, saying: All the nations, that are round about us, are assembled unto him an army exceeding great:

39.text: And they have hired the Arabians to help them, and they have pitched their tents beyond the torrent, ready to come to fight against thee. And Judas went to meet them.

40.text: And Timotheus said to the captains of his army: When Judas and his army come near the torrent of water, if he pass over unto us first, we shall not be able to withstand him: for he will certainly prevail over us.

41.text: But if he be afraid to pass over, and camp on the other side of the river, we will pass over to them and shall prevail against him.

42.text: Now when Judas came near the torrent of water, he set the scribes of the people by the torrent, and commanded them, saying: Suffer no man to stay behind: but let all come to the battle.

43.text: And he passed over to them first, and all the people after him, and all the heathens were discomfited before them, and they threw away their weapons, and fled to the temple that was in Carnaim.

44.text: And he took that city, and the temple he burnt with fire, with all things that were therein: and Carnaim was subdued, and could not stand against the face of Judas.

45.text: And Judas gathered together all the Israelites that were in the land of Galaad, from the least even to the greatest, and their wives, and children, and an army exceeding great, to come into the land of Juda.

46.text: And they came as far as Ephron: now this was a great city situate in the way, strongly fortified, and there was no means to turn from it on the right hand or on the left, but the way was through the midst of it.

47.text: And they that were in the city, shut themselves in, and stopped up the gates with stones: and Judas sent to them with peaceable words,

48.text: Saying: Let us pass through your land, to go into our country: and no man shall hurt you: we will only pass through on foot. But they would not open to them.

49.text: Then Judas commanded proclamation to be made in the camp, that they should make an assault every man in the place where he was.

50.text: And the men of the army drew near, and he assaulted that city all the day, and all the night, and the city was delivered into his hands:

51.text: And they slew every male with the edge of the sword, and he razed the city, and took the spoils thereof, and passed through all the city over them that were slain.

52.text: Then they passed over the Jordan to the great plain that is over against Bethsan.

53.text: And Judas gathered together the hindmost, and he exhorted the people all the way through, till they came into the land of Juda.

54.text: And they went up to mount Sion with joy and gladness, and offered holocausts, because not one of them was slain, till they had returned in peace.

55.text: Now in the days that Judas and Jonathan were in the land of Galaad, and Simon his brother in Galilee before Ptolemais,

56.text: Joseph the son of Zacharias, and Azarias captain of the soldiers, heard of the good success, and the battles that were fought.

57.text: And he said: Let us also get us a name, and let us go fight against the Gentiles that are round about us.

58.text: And he gave charge to them that were in his army, and they went towards Jamnia.

59.text: And Gorgias and his men went out of the city, to give them battle.

60.text: And Joseph and Azarias were put to flight, and were pursued unto the borders of Judea: and there fell, on that day, of the people of Israel about two thousand men, and there was a great overthrow of the people:

61.text: Because they did not hearken to Judas, and his brethren, thinking that they should do manfully.

62.text: But they were not of the seed of those men by whom salvation was brought to Israel.

63.text: And the men of Juda were magnified exceedingly in the sight of all Israel, and of all the nations where their name was heard.

64.text: And people assembled to them with joyful acclamations.

65.text: Then Judas and his brethren went forth and attacked the children of Esau, in the land toward the south, and he took Chebron, and her towns: and he burnt the walls thereof and the towers all round it.

66.text: And he removed his camp to go into the land of the aliens, and he went through Samaria.

67.text: In that day some priests fell in battle, while desiring to do manfully they went out unadvisedly to fight.

68.text: And Judas turned to Azotus into the land of the strangers, and he threw down their altars, and he burnt the statues of their gods with fire: and he took the spoils of the cities, and returned into the land of Juda.

1.text: Now king Antiochus was going through the higher countries, and he heard that the city of Elymais in Persia was greatly renowned, and abounding in silver and gold.

2.text: And that there was in it a temple, exceeding rich: and coverings of gold, and breastplates, and shields which king Alexander, son of Philip the Macedonian that reigned first in Greece, had left there.

3.text: Lo, he came, and sought to take the city and to pillage it: But he was not able, because the design was known to them that were in the city.

4.text: And they rose up against him in battle, and he fled away from thence, and departed with great sadness, and returned towards Babylonia.

5.text: And whilst he was in Persia, there came one that told him, how the armies that were in the land of Juda were put to flight:

6.text: And that Lysias went with a very great power, and was put to flight before the face of the Jews, and that they were grown strong by the armour, and power, and store of spoils, which they had gotten out of the camps which they had destroyed:

7.text: And that they had thrown down the abomination which he had set up upon the altar in Jerusalem, and that they had compassed about the sanctuary with high walls as before, and Bethsura also his city.

8.text: And it came to pass when the king heard these words, that he was struck with fear, and exceedingly moved: and he laid himself down upon his bed, and fell sick for grief, because it had not fallen out to him as he imagined.

9.text: And he remained there many days: for great grief came more and more and more upon him, and he made account that he should die.

10.text: And he called for all his friends, and said to them: Sleep is gone from my eyes, and I am fallen away, and my heart is cast down for anxiety.

11.text: And I said in my heart: Into how much tribulation am I come, and into what floods of sorrow, wherein now I am: I that was pleasant and beloved in my power!

12.text: But now I remember the evils that I have done in Jerusalem, from whence also I took away all the spoils of gold, and of silver that were in it, and I sent to destroy the inhabitants of Juda without cause.

13.text: I know therefore that for this cause these evils have found me: and behold I perish with great grief in a strange land.

14.text: Then he called Philip, one of his friends, and he made him regent over all his kingdom.

15.text: And he gave him the crown, and his robe, and his ring, that he should go to Antiochus his son, and should bring him up for the kingdom.

16.text: So king Antiochus died there in the year one hundred and forty-nine.

17.text: And Lysias understood that the king was dead, and he set up Antiochus his son to reign, whom he brought up young: and he called his name Eupator.

18.text: Now they that were in the castle, had shut up the Israelites round about the holy places: and they were continually seeking their hurt, and to strengthen the Gentiles.

19.text: And Judas purposed to destroy them: and he called together all the people, to besiege them.

20.text: And they came together, and besieged them in the year one hundred and fifty, and they made battering slings and engines.

21.text: And some of the besieged got out: and some wicked men of Israel joined themselves unto them.

22.text: And they went to the king, and said: How long dost thou delay to execute the judgment, and to revenge our brethren?

23.text: We determined to serve thy father and to do according to his orders, and obey his edicts:

24.text: And for this they of our nation are alienated from us, and have slain as many of us as they could find, and have spoiled our inheritances.

25.text: Neither have they put forth their hand against us only, but also against all our borders.

26.text: And behold they have approached this day to the castle of Jerusalem to take it, and they have fortified the stronghold of Bethsura:

27.text: And unless thou speedily prevent them, they will do greater things than these, and thou shalt not be able to subdue them.

28.text: Now when the king heard this, he was angry: and he called together all his friends, and the captains of his army, and them that were over the horsemen.

29.text: There came also to him from other realms, and from the islands of the sea hired troops.

30.text: And the number of his army was an hundred thousand footmen, and twenty thousand horsemen, and thirty-two elephants, trained to battle.

31.text: And they went through Idumea, and approached to Bethsura, and fought many days, and they made engines: but they sallied forth and burnt them with fire, and fought manfully.

32.text: And Judas departed from the castle, and removed the camp to Bethzacharam, over against the king’s camp.

33.text: And the king rose before it was light, and made his troops march on fiercely towards the way of Bethzacharam: and the armies made themselves ready for the battle, and they sounded the trumpets:

34.text: And they shewed the elephants the blood of grapes, and mulberries to provoke them to fight.

35.text: And they distributed the beasts by the legions: and there stood by every elephant a thousand men in coats of mail, and with helmets of brass on their heads: and five hundred horsemen set in order were chosen for every beast.

36.text: These before the time wheresoever the beast was, they were there: and withersoever it went, they went, and they departed not from it.

37.text: And upon the beast, there were strong wooden towers, which covered every one of them: and engines upon them: and upon every one thirty-two valiant men, who fought from above; and an Indian to rule the beast.

38.text: And the rest of the horsemen he placed on this side and on that side at the two wings, with trumpets to stir up the army, and to hasten them forward that stood thick together in the legions thereof.

39.text: Now when the sun shone upon the shields of gold, and of brass, the mountains glittered therewith, and they shone like lamps of fire.

40.text: And part of the king’s army was distinguished by the high mountains, and the other part by the low places: and they marched on warily and orderly.

41.text: And all the inhabitants of the land were moved at the noise of their multitude, and the marching of the company, and the rattling of the armour, for the army was exceeding great and strong.

42.text: And Judas and his army drew near for battle: and there fell of the king’s army six hundred men.

43.text: And Eleazar the son of Saura saw one of the beasts harnessed with the king’s harness: and it was higher than the other beasts: and it seemed to him that the king was on it:

44.text: And he exposed himself to deliver his people and to get himself an everlasting name.

45.text: And he ran up to it boldly in the midst of the legion, killing on the right hand, and on the left, and they fell by him on this side and that side.

46.text: And he went between the feet of the elephant, and put himself under it: and slew it, and it fell to the ground upon him, and he died there.

47.text: Then they seeing the strength of the king and the fierceness of his army, turned away from them.

48.text: But the king’s army went up against them to Jerusalem: and the king’s army pitched their tents against Judea and mount Sion.

49.text: And he made peace with them that were in Bethsura: and they came forth out of the city, because they had no victuals, being shut up there, for it was the year of rest to the land.

50.text: And the king took Bethsura: and he placed there a garrison to keep it.

51.text: And he turned his army against the sanctuary for many days: and he set up there battering slings, and engines and instruments to cast fire, and engines to cast stones and javelins, and pieces to shoot arrows, and slings.

52.text: And they also made engines against their engines, and they fought for many days.

53.text: But there were no victuals in the city, because it was the seventh year: and such as had stayed in Judea of them that came from among the nations, had eaten the residue of all that which had been stored up.

54.text: And there remained in the holy places but a few, for the famine had prevailed over them: and they were dispersed every man to his own place.

55.text: Now Lysias heard that Philip, whom king Antiochus while he lived had appointed to bring up his son Antiochus, and to reign, to be king,

56.text: Was returned from Persia, and Media, with the army that went with him, and that he sought to take upon him the affairs of the kingdom:

57.text: Wherefore he made haste to go, and say to the king and to the captains of the army: We decay daily, and our provision of victuals is small, and the place that we lay siege to is strong, and it lieth upon us to take order for the affairs of the kingdom.

58.text: Now therefore let us come to an agreement with these men, and make peace with them and with all their nation.

59.text: And let us covenant with them, that they may live according to their own laws as before. For because of our despising their laws, they have been provoked, and have done all these things.

60.text: And the proposal was acceptable in the sight of the king, and of the princes: and he sent to them to make peace: and they accepted of it.

61.text: And the king and the princes swore to them: and they came out of the stronghold.

62.text: Then the king entered into mount Sion, and saw the strength of the place: and he quickly broke the oath that he had taken, and gave commandment to throw down the wall round about.

63.text: And he departed in haste, and returned to Antioch, where he found Philip master of the city: and he fought against him, and took the city.

1.text: In the hundred and fifty-first year Demetrius the son of Seleucus departed from the city of Rome, and came up with a few men into a city of the sea coast, and reigned there.

2.text: And it came to pass, as he entered into the house of the kingdom of his fathers, that the army seized upon Antiochus, and Lysias, to bring them unto him.

3.text: And when he knew it, he said: Let me not see their face.

4.text: So the army slew them. And Demetrius sat upon the throne of his kingdom:

5.text: And there came to him the wicked and ungodly men of Israel: And Alcimus was at the head of them, who desired to be made high priest.

6.text: And they accused the people to the king, saying: Judas and his brethren have destroyed all thy friends, and he hath driven us out of our land.
