4.text: Came to king Demetrius in the year one hundred and fifty, presenting unto him a crown of gold, and a palm, and besides these, some boughs which seemed to belong to the temple. And that day indeed he held his peace.

5.text: But having gotten a convenient time to further his madness, being called to counsel by Demetrius, and asked what the Jews relied upon, and what were their counsels,

6.text: He answered thereunto: They among the Jews that are called Assideans, of whom Judas Machabeus is captain, nourish wars, and raise seditions, and will not suffer the realm to be in peace.

7.text: For I also being deprived of my ancestors’ glory (I mean of the high priesthood) am now come hither:

8.text: Principally indeed out of fidelity to the king’s interests, but in the next place also to provide for the good of my countrymen: for all our nation suffereth much from the evil proceedings of those men.

9.text: Wherefore, O king, seeing thou knowest all these things, take care, I beseech thee, both of the country, and of our nation, according to thy humanity which is known to all men,

10.text: For as long as Judas liveth, it is not possible that the state should be quiet.

11.text: Now when this man had spoken to this effect, the rest also of the king’s friends, who were enemies of Judas, incensed Demetrius against him.

12.text: And forthwith he sent Nicanor, the commander over the elephants, governor into Judea:

13.text: Giving him in charge, to take Judas himself: and disperse all them that were with him, and to make Alcimus the high priest of the great temple.

14.text: Then the Gentiles who had fled out of Judea from Judas, came to Nicanor by flocks, thinking the miseries and calamities of the Jews to be the welfare of their affairs.

15.text: Now when the Jews heard of Nicanor’s coming, and that the nations were assembled against them, they cast earth upon their heads, and made supplication to him, who chose his people to keep them for ever, and who protected his portion by evident signs.

16.text: Then at the commandment of their captain, they forthwith removed from the place where they were, and went to the town of Dessau, to meet them.

17.text: Now Simon the brother of Judas had joined battle with Nicanor, but was frightened with the sudden coming of the adversaries.

18.text: Nevertheless Nicanor hearing of the valour of Judas’ companions, and the greatness of courage with which they fought for their country, was afraid to try the matter by the sword.

19.text: Wherefore he sent Posidonius, and Theodotius, and Matthias before to present and receive the right hands.

20.text: And when there had been a consultation thereupon, and the captain had acquainted the multitude with it, they) were all of one mind to consent to covenants.

21.text: So they appointed a day upon which they might commune together by themselves: and seats were brought out, and set for each one.

22.text: But Judas ordered men to be ready in convenient places, lest some mischief might be suddenly practiced by the enemies: so they made an agreeable conference.

23.text: And Nicanor abode in Jerusalem, and did no wrong, but sent away the flocks of the multitudes that had been gathered together.

24.text: And Judas was always dear to him from the heart, and he was well affected to the man.

25.text: And he desired him to marry a wife, and to have children. So he married: he lived quietly, and they lived in common.

26.text: But Alcimus seeing the love they had one to another, and the covenants, came to Demetrius, and told him that Nicanor assented to the foreign interest, for that he meant to make Judas, who was a traitor to the kingdom, his successor.

27.text: Then the king being in a rage and provoked with this man’s wicked accusations, wrote to Nicanor, signifying, that he was greatly displeased with the covenant of friendship: and that he commanded him nevertheless to send Machabeus prisoner in all haste to Antioch.

28.text: When this was known, Nicanor was in a consternation, and took it grievously that he should make void the articles that were agreed upon, having received no injury from the man.

29.text: But because he could not oppose the king, he watched an opportunity to comply with the orders.

30.text: But when Machabeus perceived that Nicanor was more stern to him, and that when they met together as usual he behaved himself in a rough manner: and was sensible that this rough behaviour came not of good, he gathered together a few of his men, and hid himself from Nicanor.

31.text: But he finding himself notably prevented by the man, came to the great and holy temple: and commanded the priests that were offering the accustomed sacrifices, to deliver him the man.

32.text: And when they swore unto him, that they knew not where the man was whom he sought, he stretched out his hand to the temple,

33.text: And swore, saying: Unless you deliver Judas prisoner to me, I will lay this temple of God even with the ground, and will beat down the altar, and I will dedicate this temple to Bacchus.

34.text: And when he had spoken thus he departed. But the priests stretching forth their hands to heaven, called upon him that was ever the defender of their nation, saying in this manner:

35.text: Thou, O Lord of all things, who wantest nothing, wast pleased that the temple of thy habitation should be amongst us.

36.text: Therefore now, O Lord the holy of all holies, keep this house for ever undefiled which was lately cleansed.

37.text: Now Razias, one of the ancients of Jerusalem, was accused to Nicanor, a man that was a lover of the city, and of good report, who for his affection was called the father of the Jews.

38.text: This man, for a long time, had held fast his purpose of keeping himself pure in the Jews’ religion, and was ready to expose his body and life, that he might persevere therein.

39.text: So Nicanor being willing to declare the hatred that he bore the Jews, sent five hundred soldiers to take him.

40.text: For he thought by insnaring him to hurt the Jews very much.

41.text: Now as the multitude sought to rush into his house, and to break open the door, and to set fire to it, when he was ready to be taken, he struck himself with his sword:

42.text: Choosing to die nobly rather than to fall into the hands of the wicked, and to suffer abuses unbecoming his noble birth.

43.text: But whereas through haste he missed of giving himself a sure wound, and the crowd was breaking into the doors, he ran boldly to the wall, and manfully threw himself down to the crowd:

44.text: But they quickly making room for his fall, he came upon the midst of the neck.

45.text: And as he had yet breath in him, being inflamed in mind he arose: and while his blood ran down with a great stream, and he was grievously wounded, he ran through the crowd:

46.text: And standing upon a steep rock, when he was now almost without blood, grasping his bowels with both hands, he cast them upon the throng, calling upon the Lord of life and spirit, to restore these to him again: and so he departed this life.

1.text: But when Nicanor understood that Judas was in the places of Samaria, he purposed to set upon him with all violence on the sabbath day.

2.text: And when the Jews that were constrained to follow him, said: Do not act so fiercely and barbarously, but give honour to the day that is sanctified: and reverence him that beholdeth all things:

3.text: That unhappy man asked, if there were a mighty One in heaven, that had commanded the sabbath day to be kept.

4.text: And when they answered: There is the living Lord himself in heaven, the mighty One, that commanded the seventh day to be kept,

5.text: Then he said: And I am mighty upon the earth, and I command to take arms, and to do the king’s business. Nevertheless he prevailed not to accomplish his design.

6.text: So Nicanor being puffed up with exceeding great pride, thought to set up a public monument of his victory over Judas.

7.text: But Machabeus ever trusted with all hope that God would help them.

8.text: And he exhorted his people not to fear the coming of the nations, but to remember the help they had before received from heaven, and now to hope for victory from the Almighty.

9.text: And speaking to them out of the law, and the prophets, and withal putting them in mind of the battles they had fought before, he made them more cheerful:

10.text: Then after he had encouraged them, he shewed withal the falsehood of the Gentiles, and their breach of oaths.

11.text: So he armed every one of them, not with defence of shield and spear, but with very good speeches and exhortations, and told them a dream worthy to be believed, whereby he rejoiced them all.

12.text: Now the vision was in this manner: Onias who had been high priest, a good and virtuous man, modest in his looks, gentle in his manners, and graceful in his speech, and who from a child was exercised in virtues, holding up his hands, prayed for all the people of the Jews:

13.text: After this there appeared also another man, admirable for age, and glory, and environed with great beauty and majesty:

14.text: Then Onias answering, said: This is a lover of his brethren, and of the people of Israel: this is he that prayeth much for the people, and for all the holy city, Jeremias the prophet of God.

15.text: Whereupon Jeremias stretched forth his right hand, and gave to Judas a sword of gold, saying:

16.text: Take this holy sword a gift from God, wherewith thou shalt overthrow the adversaries of my people Israel.

17.text: Thus being exhorted with the words of Judas, which were very good, and proper to stir up the courage, and strengthen the hearts of the young men, they resolved to fight, and to set upon them manfully: that valour might decide the matter, because the holy city and the temple were in danger.

18.text: For their concern was less for their wives, and children, and for their brethren, and kinsfolks: but their greatest and principal fear was for the holiness of the temple.

19.text: And they also that were in the city, had no little concern for them that were to be engaged in battle.

20.text: And now when all expected what judgment would be given, and the enemies were at hand, and the army was set in array, the beasts and the horsemen ranged in convenient places,

21.text: Machabeus considering the coming of the multitude, and the divers preparations of armour, and the fierceness of the beasts, stretching out his hands to heaven, called upon the Lord, that worketh wonders, who giveth victory to them that are worthy, not according to the power of their arms, but according as it seemeth good to him.

22.text: And in his prayer he said after this manner: Thou, O Lord, who didst send thy angel in the time of Ezechias king of Juda, and didst kill a hundred and eighty-five thousand of the army of Sennacherib:

23.text: Send now also, O Lord of heaven, thy good angel before us, for the fear and dread of the greatness of thy arm,

24.text: That they may be afraid, who come with blasphemy against thy holy people. And thus he concluded his prayer.

25.text: But Nicanor, and they that were with him came forward, with trumpets and songs.

26.text: But Judas, and they that were with him, encountered them, calling upon God by prayers:

27.text: So fighting with their hands, but praying to the Lord with their hearts, they slew no less than five and thirty thousand, being greatly cheered with the presence of God.

28.text: And when the battle was over, and they were returning with joy, they understood that Nicanor was slain in his armour.

29.text: Then making a shout, and a great noise, they blessed the Almighty Lord in their own language.

30.text: And Judas, who was altogether ready, in body and mind, to die for his countrymen, commanded that Nicanor’s head, and his hand with the shoulder should be cut off, and carried to Jerusalem.

31.text: And when he was come thither, having called together his countrymen, and the priests to the altar, he sent also for them that were in the castle,

32.text: And shewing them the head of Nicanor, and the wicked hand, which he had stretched out, with proud boasts, against the holy house of the Almighty God,

33.text: He commanded also, that the tongue of the wicked Nicanor, should be cut out and given by pieces to birds, and the hand of the furious man to be hanged up over against the temple.

34.text: Then all blessed the Lord of heaven, saying: Blessed be he that hath kept his own place undefiled.

35.text: And he hung up Nicanor’s head in the top of the castle, that it might be an evident and manifest sign of the help of God.

36.text: And they all ordained by a common decree, by no means to let this day pass without solemnity: But to celebrate the thirteenth day of the month of Adar, called, in the Syrian language, the day before Mardochias’ day.

37.text: So these things being done with relation to Nicanor, and from that time the city being possessed by the Hebrews, I also will here make an end of my narration.

38.text: Which if I have done well, and as it becometh the history, it is what I desired: but if not so perfectly, it must be pardoned me.

39.text: For as it is hurtful to drink always wine, or always water, but pleasant to use sometimes the one, and sometimes the other: so if the speech be always nicely framed, it will not be grateful to the readers. But here it shall be ended.

1.text: The former treatise I made, O Theophilus, of all things which Jesus began to do and to teach,

2.text: Until the day on which, giving commandments by the Holy Ghost to the apostles whom he had chosen, he was taken up.

3.text: To whom also he shewed himself alive after his passion, by many proofs, for forty days appearing to them, and speaking of the kingdom of God.

4.text: And eating together with them, he commanded them, that they should not depart from Jerusalem, but should wait for the promise of the Father, which you have heard (saith he) by my mouth.

5.text: For John indeed baptized with water, but you shall be baptized with the Holy Ghost, not many days hence.

6.text: They therefore who were come together, asked him, saying: Lord, wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel?

7.text: But he said to them: It is not for you to know the times or moments, which the Father hath put in his own power:

8.text: But you shall receive the power of the Holy Ghost coming upon you, and you shall be witnesses unto me in Jerusalem, and in all Judea, and Samaria, and even to the uttermost part of the earth.

9.text: And when he had said these things, while they looked on, he was raised up: and a cloud received him out of their sight.

10.text: And while they were beholding him going up to heaven, behold two men stood by them in white garments.

11.text: Who also said: Ye men of Galilee, why stand you looking up to heaven? This Jesus who is taken up from you into heaven, shall so come, as you have seen him going into heaven.

12.text: Then they returned to Jerusalem from the mount that is called Olivet, which is nigh Jerusalem, within a sabbath day’s journey.

13.text: And when they were come in, they went up into an upper room, where abode Peter and John, James and Andrew, Philip and Thomas, Bartholomew and Matthew, James of Alpheus, and Simon Zelotes, and Jude the brother of James.

14.text: All these were persevering with one mind in prayer with the women, and Mary the mother of Jesus, and with his brethren.

15.text: In those days Peter rising up in the midst of the brethren, said: (now the number of persons together was about an hundred and twenty:)

16.text: Men, brethren, the scripture must needs be fulfilled, which the Holy Ghost spoke before by the mouth of David concerning Judas, who was the leader of them that apprehended Jesus:

17.text: Who was numbered with us, and had obtained part of this ministry.

18.text: And he indeed hath possessed a field of the reward of iniquity, and being hanged, burst asunder in the midst: and all his bowels gushed out.

19.text: And it became known to all the inhabitants of Jerusalem: so that the same field was called in their tongue, Haceldama, that is to say, The field of blood.

20.text: For it is written in the book of Psalms: Let their habitation become desolate, and let there be none to dwell therein. And his bishopric let another take.

21.text: Wherefore of these men who have companied with us all the time that the Lord Jesus came in and went out among us,

22.text: Beginning from the baptism of John, until the day wherein he was taken up from us, one of these must be made a witness with us of his resurrection.

23.text: And they appointed two, Joseph, called Barsabas, who was surnamed Justus, and Matthias.

24.text: And praying, they said: Thou, Lord, who knowest the hearts of all men, shew whether of these two thou hast chosen,

25.text: To take the place of this ministry and apostleship, from which Judas hath by transgression fallen, that he might go to his own place.

26.text: And they gave them lots, and the lot fell upon Matthias, and he was numbered with the eleven apostles.

1.text: And when the days of the Pentecost were accomplished, they were all together in one place:

2.text: And suddenly there came a sound from heaven, as of a mighty wind coming, and it filled the whole house where they were sitting.

3.text: And there appeared to them parted tongues as it were of fire, and it sat upon every one of them:

4.text: And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and they began to speak with divers tongues, according as the Holy Ghost gave them to speak.

5.text: Now there were dwelling at Jerusalem, Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven.

6.text: And when this was noised abroad, the multitude came together, and were confounded in mind, because that every man heard them speak in his own tongue.

7.text: And they were all amazed, and wondered, saying: Behold, are not all these, that speak, Galileans?

8.text: And how have we heard, every man our own tongue wherein we were born?

9.text: Parthians, and Medes, and Elamites, and inhabitants of Mesopotamia, Judea, and Cappadocia, Pontus and Asia,

10.text: Phrygia, and Pamphylia, Egypt, and the parts of Libya about Cyrene, and strangers of Rome,

11.text: Jews also, and proselytes, Cretes, and Arabians: we have heard them speak in our own tongues the wonderful works of God.

12.text: And they were all astonished, and wondered, saying one to another: What meaneth this?

13.text: But others mocking, said: These men are full of new wine.

14.text: But Peter standing up with the eleven, lifted up his voice, and spoke to them: Ye men of Judea, and all you that dwell in Jerusalem, be this known to you, and with your ears receive my words.

15.text: For these are not drunk, as you suppose, seeing it is but the third hour of the day:

16.text: But this is that which was spoken of by the prophet Joel:

17.text: And it shall come to pass, in the last days, (saith the Lord,) I will pour out of my Spirit upon all flesh: and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, and your young men shall see visions, and your old men shall dream dreams.

18.text: And upon my servants indeed, and upon my handmaids will I pour out in those days of my spirit, and they shall prophesy.

19.text: And I will shew wonders in the heaven above, and signs on the earth beneath: blood and fire, and vapour of smoke.

20.text: The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before the great and manifest day of the Lord come.

21.text: And it shall come to pass, that whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord, shall be saved.

22.text: Ye men of Israel, hear these words: Jesus of Nazareth, a man approved of God among you, by miracles, and wonders, and signs, which God did by him, in the midst of you, as you also know:

23.text: This same being delivered up, by the determinate counsel and foreknowledge of God, you by the hands of wicked men have crucified and slain.

24.text: Whom God hath raised up, having loosed the sorrows of hell, as it was impossible that he should be holden by it.

25.text: For David saith concerning him: I foresaw the Lord before my face: because he is at my right hand, that I may not be moved.

26.text: For this my heart hath been glad, and my tongue hath rejoiced: moreover my flesh also shall rest in hope.

27.text: Because thou wilt not leave my soul in hell, nor suffer thy Holy One to see corruption.

28.text: Thou hast made known to me the ways of life: thou shalt make me full of joy with thy countenance.

29.text: Ye men, brethren, let me freely speak to you of the patriarch David; that he died, and was buried; and his sepulchre is with us to this present day.

30.text: Whereas therefore he was a prophet, and knew that God hath sworn to him with an oath, that of the fruit of his loins one should sit upon his throne.

31.text: Foreseeing this, he spoke of the resurrection of Christ. For neither was he left in hell, neither did his flesh see corruption.

32.text: This Jesus hath God raised again, whereof all we are witnesses.

33.text: Being exalted therefore by the right hand of God, and having received of the Father the promise of the Holy Ghost, he hath poured forth this which you see and hear.

34.text: For David ascended not into heaven; but he himself said: The Lord said to my Lord, sit thou on my right hand,

35.text: Until I make thy enemies thy footstool.

36.text: Therefore let all the house of Israel know most certainly, that God hath made both Lord and Christ, this same Jesus, whom you have crucified.

37.text: Now when they had heard these things, they had compunction in their heart, and said to Peter, and to the rest of the apostles: What shall we do, men and brethren?

38.text: But Peter said to them: Do penance, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ, for the remission of your sins: and you shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost.

39.text: For the promise is to you, and to your children, and to all that are far off, whomsoever the Lord our God shall call.

40.text: And with very many other words did he testify and exhort them, saying: Save yourselves from this perverse generation.

41.text: They therefore that received his word, were baptized; and there were added in that day about three thousand souls.

42.text: And they were persevering in the doctrine of the apostles, and in the communication of the breaking of bread, and in prayers.

43.text: And fear came upon every soul: many wonders also and signs were done by the apostles in Jerusalem, and there was great fear in all.

44.text: And all they that believed, were together, and had all things common.

45.text: Their possessions and goods they sold, and divided them to all, according as every one had need.

46.text: And continuing daily with one accord in the temple, and breaking bread from house to house, they took their meat with gladness and simplicity of heart;

47.text: Praising God, and having favour with all the people. And the Lord increased daily together such as should be saved.

1.text: Now Peter and John went up into the temple at the ninth hour of prayer.

2.text: And a certain man who was lame from his mother’s womb, was carried: whom they laid every day at the gate of the temple, which is called Beautiful, that he might ask alms of them that went into the temple.

3.text: He, when he had seen Peter and John about to go into the temple, asked to receive an alms.

4.text: But Peter with John fastening his eyes upon him, said: Look upon us.

5.text: But he looked earnestly upon them, hoping that he should receive something of them.

6.text: But Peter said: Silver and gold I have none; but what I have, I give thee: In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, arise, and walk.

7.text: And taking him by the right hand, he lifted him up, and forthwith his feet and soles received strength.

8.text: And he leaping up, stood, and walked, and went in with them into the temple, walking, and leaping, and praising God.

9.text: And all the people saw him walking and praising God.

10.text: And they knew him, that it was he who sat begging alms at the Beautiful gate of the temple: and they were filled with wonder and amazement at that which had happened to him.

11.text: And as he held Peter and John, all the people ran to them to the porch which is called Solomon’s, greatly wondering.

12.text: But Peter seeing, made answer to the people: Ye men of Israel, why wonder you at this? or why look you upon us, as if by our strength or power we had made this man to walk?

13.text: The God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, the God of our fathers, hath glorified his Son Jesus, whom you indeed delivered up and denied before the face of Pilate, when he judged he should be released.

14.text: But you denied the Holy One and the Just, and desired a murderer to be granted unto you.

15.text: But the author of life you killed, whom God hath raised from the dead, of which we are witnesses.

16.text: And in the faith of his name, this man, whom you have seen and known, hath his name strengthened; and the faith which is by him, hath given this perfect soundness in the sight of you all.

17.text: And now, brethren, I know that you did it through ignorance, as did also your rulers.

18.text: But those things which God before had shewed by the mouth of all the prophets, that his Christ should suffer, he hath so fulfilled.

19.text: Be penitent, therefore, and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out.

20.text: That when the times of refreshment shall come from the presence of the Lord, and he shall send him who hath been preached unto you, Jesus Christ,

21.text: Whom heaven indeed must receive, until the times of the restitution of all things, which God hath spoken by the mouth of his holy prophets, from the beginning of the world.

22.text: For Moses said: A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you of your brethren, like unto me: him you shall hear according to all things whatsoever he shall speak to you.

23.text: And it shall be, that every soul which will not hear that prophet, shall be destroyed from among the people.

24.text: And all the prophets, from Samuel and afterwards, who have spoken, have told of these days.

25.text: You are the children of the prophets, and of the testament which God made to our fathers, saying to Abraham: And in thy seed shall all the kindreds of the earth be blessed.

26.text: To you first God, raising up his Son, hath sent him to bless you; that every one may convert himself from his wickedness.

1.text: And as they were speaking to the people, the priests, and the officer of the temple, and the Sadducees, came upon them,

2.text: Being grieved that they taught the people, and preached in Jesus the resurrection from the dead:

3.text: And they laid hands upon them, and put them in hold till the next day; for it was now evening.

4.text: But many of them who had heard the word, believed; and the number of the men was made five thousand.

5.text: And it came to pass on the morrow, that their princes, and ancients, and scribes, were gathered together in Jerusalem;

6.text: And Annas the high priest, and Caiphas, and John, and Alexander, and as many as were of the kindred of the high priest.

7.text: And setting them in the midst, they asked: By what power, or by what name, have you done this?

8.text: Then Peter, filled with the Holy Ghost, said to them: Ye princes of the people, and ancients, hear:

9.text: If we this day are examined concerning the good deed done to the infirm man, by what means he hath been made whole:

10.text: Be it known to you all, and to all the people of Israel, that by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom you crucified, whom God hath raised from the dead, even by him this man standeth here before you whole.

11.text: This is the stone which was rejected by you the builders, which is become the head of the corner.

12.text: Neither is there salvation in any other. For there is no other name under heaven given to men, whereby we must be saved.

13.text: Now seeing the constancy of Peter and of John, understanding that they were illiterate and ignorant men, they wondered; and they knew them that they had been with Jesus.

14.text: Seeing the man also who had been healed standing with them, they could say nothing against it.

15.text: But they commanded them to go aside out of the council; and they conferred among themselves,

16.text: Saying: What shall we do to these men? for indeed a known miracle hath been done by them, to all the inhabitants of Jerusalem: it is manifest, and we cannot deny it.

17.text: But that it may be no farther spread among the people, let us threaten them that they speak no more in this name to any man.

18.text: And calling them, they charged them not to speak at all, nor teach in the name of Jesus.

19.text: But Peter and John answering, said to them: If it be just in the sight of God, to hear you rather than God, judge ye.

20.text: For we cannot but speak the things which we have seen and heard.

21.text: But they threatening, sent them away, not finding how they might punish them, because of the people; for all men glorified what had been done, in that which had come to pass.

22.text: For the man was above forty years old, in whom that miraculous cure had been wrought.

23.text: And being let go, they came to their own company, and related all that the chief priests and ancients had said to them.

24.text: Who having heard it, with one accord lifted up their voice to God, and said: Lord, thou art he that didst make heaven and earth, the sea, and all things that are in them.

25.text: Who, by the Holy Ghost, by the mouth of our father David, thy servant, hast said: Why did the Gentiles rage, and the people meditate vain things?

26.text: The kings of the earth stood up, and the princes assembled together against the Lord and his Christ.

27.text: For of a truth there assembled together in this city against thy holy child Jesus, whom thou hast anointed, Herod, and Pontius Pilate, with the Gentiles and the people of Israel,

28.text: To do what thy hand and thy counsel decreed to be done.

29.text: And now, Lord, behold their threatenings, and grant unto thy servants, that with all confidence they may speak thy word,

30.text: By stretching forth thy hand to cures, and signs, and wonders to be done by the name of thy holy Son Jesus.

31.text: And when they had prayed, the place was moved wherein they were assembled; and they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and they spoke the word of God with confidence.

32.text: And the multitude of believers had but one heart and one soul: neither did any one say that aught of the things which he possessed, was his own; but all things were common unto them.

33.text: And with great power did the apostles give testimony of the resurrection of Jesus Christ our Lord; and great grace was in them all.

34.text: For neither was there any one needy among them. For as many as were owners of lands or houses, sold them, and brought the price of the things they sold,

35.text: And laid it down before the feet of the apostles. And distribution was made to every one, according as he had need.

36.text: And Joseph, who, by the apostles, was surnamed Barnabas, (which is, by interpretation, The son of consolation,) a Levite, a Cyprian born,

37.text: Having land, sold it, and brought the price, and laid it at the feet of the apostles.

1.text: But a certain man named Ananias, with Saphira his wife, sold a piece of land,

2.text: And by fraud kept back part of the price of the land, his wife being privy thereunto: and bringing a certain part of it, laid it at the feet of the apostles.

3.text: But Peter said: Ananias, why hath Satan tempted thy heart, that thou shouldst lie to the Holy Ghost, and by fraud keep part of the price of the land?

4.text: Whilst it remained, did it not remain to thee? and after it was sold, was it not in thy power? Why hast thou conceived this thing in thy heart? Thou hast not lied to men, but to God.

5.text: And Ananias hearing these words, fell down, and gave up the ghost. And there came great fear upon all that heard it.

6.text: And the young men rising up, removed him, and carrying him out, buried him.

7.text: And it was about the space of three hours after, when his wife, not knowing what had happened, came in.

8.text: And Peter said to her: Tell me, woman, whether you sold the land for so much? And she said: Yea, for so much.

9.text: And Peter said unto her: Why have you agreed together to tempt the Spirit of the Lord? Behold the feet of them who have buried thy husband are at the door, and they shall carry thee out.

10.text: Immediately she fell down before his feet, and gave up the ghost. And the young men coming in, found her dead: and carried her out, and buried her by her husband.

11.text: And there came great fear upon the whole church, and upon all that heard these things.

12.text: And by the hands of the apostles were many signs and wonders wrought among the people. And they were all with one accord in Solomon’s porch.

13.text: But of the rest no man durst join himself unto them; but the people magnified them.

14.text: And the multitude of men and women who believed in the Lord, was more increased:

15.text: Insomuch that they brought forth the sick into the streets, and laid them on beds and couches, that when Peter came, his shadow at the least, might overshadow any of them, and they might be delivered from their infirmities.

16.text: And there came also together to Jerusalem a multitude out of the neighbouring cities, bringing sick persons, and such as were troubled with unclean spirits; who were all healed.

17.text: Then the high priest rising up, and all they that were with him, (which is the heresy of the Sadducees,) were filled with envy.

18.text: And they laid hands on the apostles, and put them in the common prison.

19.text: But an angel of the Lord by night opening the doors of the prison, and leading them out, said:

20.text: Go, and standing speak in the temple to the people all the words of this life.

21.text: Who having heard this, early in the morning, entered into the temple, and taught. And the high priest coming, and they that were with him, called together the council, and all the ancients of the children of Israel; and they sent to the prison to have them brought.

22.text: But when the ministers came, and opening the prison, found them not there, they returned and told,

23.text: Saying: The prison indeed we found shut with all diligence, and the keepers standing before the doors; but opening it, we found no man within.

24.text: Now when the officer of the temple and the chief priests heard these words, they were in doubt concerning them, what would come to pass.

25.text: But one came and told them: Behold, the men whom you put in prison are in the temple standing, and teaching the people.

26.text: Then went the officer with the ministers, and brought them without violence; for they feared the people, lest they should be stoned.

27.text: And when they had brought them, they set them before the council. And the high priest asked them,

28.text: Saying: Commanding we commanded you, that you should not teach in this name; and behold, you have filled Jerusalem with your doctrine, and you have a mind to bring the blood of this man upon us.

29.text: But Peter and the apostles answering, said: We ought to obey God, rather than men.

30.text: The God of our fathers hath raised up Jesus, whom you put to death, hanging him upon a tree.

31.text: Him hath God exalted with his right hand, to be Prince and Saviour, to give repentance to Israel, and remission of sins.

32.text: And we are witnesses of these things and the Holy Ghost, whom God hath given to all that obey him.

33.text: When they had heard these things, they were cut to the heart, and they thought to put them to death.

34.text: But one in the council rising up, a Pharisee, named Gamaliel, a doctor of the law, respected by all the people, commanded the men to be put forth a little while.

35.text: And he said to them: Ye men of Israel, take heed to yourselves what you intend to do, as touching these men.

36.text: For before these days rose up Theodas, affirming himself to be somebody, to whom a number of men, about four hundred, joined themselves: who was slain; and all that believed him were scattered, and brought to nothing.

37.text: After this man, rose up Judas of Galilee, in the days of the enrolling, and drew away the people after him: he also perished; and all, even as many as consented to him, were dispersed.

38.text: And now, therefore, I say to you, refrain from these men, and let them alone; for if this council or this work be of men, it will come to nought;

39.text: But if it be of God, you cannot overthrow it, lest perhaps you be found even to fight against God. And they consented to him.

40.text: And calling in the apostles, after they had scourged them, they charged them that they should not speak at all in the name of Jesus; and they dismissed them.

41.text: And they indeed went from the presence of the council, rejoicing that they were accounted worthy to suffer reproach for the name of Jesus.

42.text: And every day they ceased not in the temple, and from house to house, to teach and preach Christ Jesus.

1.text: And in those days, the number of the disciples increasing, there arose a murmuring of the Greeks against the Hebrews, for that their widows were neglected in the daily ministration.

2.text: Then the twelve calling together the multitude of the disciples, said: It is not reason that we should leave the word of God, and serve tables.

3.text: Wherefore, brethren, look ye out among you seven men of good reputation, full of the Holy Ghost and wisdom, whom we may appoint over this business.

4.text: But we will give ourselves continually to prayer, and to the ministry of the word.

5.text: And the saying was liked by all the multitude. And they chose Stephen, a man full of faith, and of the Holy Ghost, and Philip, and Prochorus, and Nicanor, and Timon, and Parmenas, and Nicolas, a proselyte of Antioch.

6.text: These they set before the apostles; and they praying, imposed hands upon them.

7.text: And the word of the Lord increased; and the number of the disciples was multiplied in Jerusalem exceedingly: a great multitude also of the priests obeyed the faith.

8.text: And Stephen, full of grace and fortitude, did great wonders and signs among the people.

9.text: Now there arose some of that which is called the synagogue of the Libertines, and of the Cyrenians, and of the Alexandrians, and of them that were of Cilicia and Asia, disputing with Stephen.

10.text: And they were not able to resist the wisdom and the spirit that spoke.

11.text: Then they suborned men to say, they had heard him speak words of blasphemy against Moses and against God.

12.text: And they stirred up the people, and the ancients, and the scribes; and running together, they took him, and brought him to the council.

13.text: And they set up false witnesses, who said: This man ceaseth not to speak words against the holy place and the law.

14.text: For we have heard him say, that this Jesus of Nazareth shall destroy this place, and shall change the traditions which Moses delivered unto us.

15.text: And all that sat in the council, looking on him, saw his face as if it had been the face of an angel.

1.text: Then the high priest said: Are these things so?

2.text: Who said: Ye men, brethren, and fathers, hear. The God of glory appeared to our father Abraham, when he was in Mesopotamia, before he dwelt in Charan.

3.text: And said to him: Go forth out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and come into the land which I shall shew thee.

4.text: Then he went out of the land of the Chaldeans, and dwelt in Charan. And from thence, after his father was dead, he removed him into this land, wherein you now dwell.

5.text: And he gave him no inheritance in it; no, not the pace of a foot: but he promised to give it him in possession, and to his seed after him, when as yet he had no child.

6.text: And God said to him: That his seed should sojourn in a strange country, and that they should bring them under bondage, and treat them evil four hundred years.

7.text: And the nation which they shall serve will I judge, said the Lord; and after these things they shall go out, and shall serve me in this place.

8.text: And he gave him the covenant of circumcision, and so he begot Isaac, and circumcised him the eighth day; and Isaac begot Jacob; and Jacob the twelve patriarchs.

9.text: And the patriarchs, through envy, sold Joseph into Egypt; and God was with him,

10.text: And delivered him out of all his tribulations: and he gave him favour and wisdom in the sight of Pharao, the king of Egypt; and he appointed him governor over Egypt, and over all his house.

11.text: Now there came a famine upon all Egypt and Chanaan, and great tribulation; and our fathers found no food.

12.text: But when Jacob had heard that there was corn in Egypt, he sent our fathers first:

13.text: And at the second time, Joseph was known by his brethren, and his kindred was made known to Pharao.

14.text: And Joseph sending, called thither Jacob, his father, and all his kindred, seventy-five souls.

15.text: So Jacob went down into Egypt; and he died, and our fathers.

16.text: And they were translated into Sichem, and were laid in the sepulchre, that Abraham bought for a sum of money of the sons of Hemor, the son of Sichem.

17.text: And when the time of the promise drew near, which God had promised to Abraham, the people increased, and were multiplied in Egypt,

18.text: Till another king arose in Egypt, who knew not Joseph.

19.text: This same dealing craftily with our race, afflicted our fathers, that they should expose their children, to the end they might not be kept alive.

20.text: At the same time was Moses born, and he was acceptable to God: who was nourished three months in his father’s house.

21.text: And when he was exposed, Pharao’s daughter took him up, and nourished him for her own son.

22.text: And Moses was instructed in all the wisdom of the Egyptians; and he was mighty in his words and in his deeds.

23.text: And when he was full forty years old, it came into his heart to visit his brethren, the children of Israel.

24.text: And when he had seen one of them suffer wrong, he defended him; and striking the Egyptian, he avenged him who suffered the injury.

25.text: And he thought that his brethren understood that God by his hand would save them; but they understood it not.

26.text: And the day following, he shewed himself to them when they were at strife; and would have reconciled them in peace, saying: Men, ye are brethren; why hurt you one another?

27.text: But he that did the injury to his neighbour thrust him away, saying: Who hath appointed thee prince and judge over us?

28.text: What, wilt thou kill me, as thou didst yesterday kill the Egyptian?

29.text: And Moses fled upon this word, and was a stranger in the land of Madian, where he begot two sons.

30.text: And when forty years were expired, there appeared to him in the desert of mount Sina, an angel in a flame of fire in a bush.

31.text: And Moses seeing it, wondered at the sight. And as he drew near to view it, the voice of the Lord came unto him, saying:

32.text: I am the God of thy fathers; the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob. And Moses being terrified, durst not behold.

33.text: And the Lord said to him: Loose the shoes from thy feet, for the place wherein thou standest, is holy ground.

34.text: Seeing I have seen the affliction of my people which is in Egypt, and I have heard their groaning, and am come down to deliver them. And now come, and I will send thee into Egypt.

35.text: This Moses, whom they refused, saying: Who hath appointed thee prince and judge? him God sent to be prince and redeemer by the hand of the angel who appeared to him in the bush.

36.text: He brought them out, doing wonders and signs in the land of Egypt, and in the Red Sea, and in the desert forty years.

37.text: This is that Moses who said to the children of Israel: A prophet shall God raise up to you of your own brethren, as myself: him shall you hear.

38.text: This is he that was in the church in the wilderness, with the angel who spoke to him on mount Sina, and with our fathers; who received the words of life to give unto us.

39.text: Whom our fathers would not obey; but thrust him away, and in their hearts turned back into Egypt,

40.text: Saying to Aaron: Make us gods to go before us. For as for this Moses, who brought us out of the land of Egypt, we know not what is become of him.

41.text: And they made a calf in those days, and offered sacrifices to the idol, and rejoiced in the works of their own hands.

42.text: And God turned, and gave them up to serve the host of heaven, as it is written in the books of the prophets: Did you offer victims and sacrifices to me for forty years, in the desert, O house of Israel?

43.text: And you took unto you the tabernacle of Moloch, and the star of your god Rempham, figures which you made to adore them. And I will carry you away beyond Babylon.

44.text: The tabernacle of the testimony was with our fathers in the desert, as God ordained for them, speaking to Moses, that he should make it according to the form which he had seen.

45.text: Which also our fathers receiving, brought in with Jesus, into the possession of the Gentiles, whom God drove out before the face of our fathers, unto the days of David.

46.text: Who found grace before God, and desired to find a tabernacle for the God of Jacob.

47.text: But Solomon built him a house.

48.text: Yet the most High dwelleth not in houses made by hands, as the prophet saith:

49.text: Heaven is my throne, and the earth my footstool. What house will you build me? saith the Lord; or what is the place of my resting?

50.text: Hath not my hand made all these things?

51.text: You stiffnecked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, you always resist the Holy Ghost: as your fathers did, so do you also.

52.text: Which of the prophets have not your fathers persecuted? And they have slain them who foretold of the coming of the Just One; of whom you have been now the betrayers and murderers:

53.text: Who have received the law by the disposition of angels, and have not kept it.

54.text: Now hearing these things, they were cut to the heart, and they gnashed with their teeth at him.

55.text: But he, being full of the Holy Ghost, looking up steadfastly to heaven, saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing on the right hand of God. And he said: Behold, I see the heavens opened, and the Son of man standing on the right hand of God.

57.text: And they crying out with a loud voice, stopped their ears, and with one accord ran violently upon him.

58.text: And casting him forth without the city, they stoned him; and the witnesses laid down their garments at the feet of a young man, whose name was Saul.

59.text: And they stoned Stephen, invoking, and saying: Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.

60.text: And falling on his knees, he cried with a loud voice, saying: Lord, lay not this sin to their charge. And when he had said this, he fell asleep in the Lord. And Saul was consenting to his death.

1.text: And at that time there was raised a great persecution against the church which was at Jerusalem; and they were all dispersed through the countries of Judea, and Samaria, except the apostles.

2.text: And devout men took order for Stephen’s funeral, and made great mourning over him.

3.text: But Saul made havock of the church, entering in from house to house, and dragging away men and women, committed them to prison.

4.text: They therefore that were dispersed, went about preaching the word of God.

5.text: And Philip going down to the city of Samaria, preached Christ unto them.

6.text: And the people with one accord were attentive to those things which were said by Philip, hearing, and seeing the miracles which he did.

7.text: For many of them who had unclean spirits, crying with a loud voice, went out.

8.text: And many, taken with the palsy, and that were lame, were healed.

9.text: There was therefore great joy in that city. Now there was a certain man named Simon, who before had been a magician in that city, seducing the people of Samaria, giving out that he was some great one:

10.text: To whom they all gave ear, from the least to the greatest, saying: This man is the power of God, which is called great.

11.text: And they were attentive to him, because, for a long time, he had bewitched them with his magical practices.

12.text: But when they had believed Philip preaching of the kingdom of God, in the name of Jesus Christ, they were baptized, both men and women.

13.text: Then Simon himself believed also; and being baptized, he adhered to Philip. And being astonished, wondered to see the signs and exceeding great miracles which were done.

14.text: Now when the apostles, who were in Jerusalem, had heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent unto them Peter and John.

15.text: Who, when they were come, prayed for them, that they might receive the Holy Ghost.

16.text: For he was not as yet come upon any of them; but they were only baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.

17.text: Then they laid their hands upon them, and they received the Holy Ghost.

18.text: And when Simon saw, that by the imposition of the hands of the apostles, the Holy Ghost was given, he offered them money,

19.text: Saying: Give me also this power, that on whomsoever I shall lay my hands, he may receive the Holy Ghost. But Peter said to him:

20.text: Keep thy money to thyself, to perish with thee, because thou hast thought that the gift of God may be purchased with money.

21.text: Thou hast no part nor lot in this matter. For thy heart is not right in the sight of God.

22.text: Do penance therefore for this thy wickedness; and pray to God, that perhaps this thought of thy heart may be forgiven thee.

23.text: For I see thou art in the gall of bitterness, and in the bonds of iniquity.

24.text: Then Simon answering, said: Pray you for me to the Lord, that none of these things which you have spoken may come upon me.

25.text: And they indeed having testified and preached the word of the Lord, returned to Jerusalem, and preached the gospel to many countries of the Samaritans.

26.text: Now an angel of the Lord spoke to Philip, saying: Arise, go towards the south, to the way that goeth down from Jerusalem into Gaza: this is desert.

27.text: And rising up, he went. And behold a man of Ethiopia, an eunuch, of great authority under Candace the queen of the Ethiopians, who had charge over all her treasures, had come to Jerusalem to adore.

28.text: And he was returning, sitting in his chariot, and reading Isaias the prophet.

29.text: And the Spirit said to Philip: Go near, and join thyself to this chariot.

30.text: And Philip running thither, heard him reading the prophet Isaias. And he said: Thinkest thou that thou understandest what thou readest?

31.text: Who said: And how can I, unless some man shew me? And he desired Philip that he would come up and sit with him.

32.text: And the place of the scripture which he was reading was this: He was led as a sheep to the slaughter; and like a lamb without voice before his shearer, so openeth he not his mouth.

33.text: In humility his judgment was taken away. His generation who shall declare, for his life shall be taken from the earth?

34.text: And the eunuch answering Philip, said: I beseech thee, of whom doth the prophet speak this? of himself, or of some other man?

35.text: Then Philip, opening his mouth, and beginning at this scripture, preached unto him Jesus.

36.text: And as they went on their way, they came to a certain water; and the eunuch said: See, here is water: what doth hinder me from being baptized?

37.text: And Philip said: If thou believest with all thy heart, thou mayest. And he answering, said: I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God.

38.text: And he commanded the chariot to stand still; and they went down into the water, both Philip and the eunuch: and he baptized him.

39.text: And when they were come up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord took away Philip; and the eunuch saw him no more. And he went on his way rejoicing.

40.text: But Philip was found in Azotus; and passing through, he preached the gospel to all the cities, till he came to Caesarea.

1.text: And Saul, as yet breathing out threatenings and slaughter against the disciples of the Lord, went to the high priest,

2.text: And asked of him letters to Damascus, to the synagogues: that if he found any men and women of this way, he might bring them bound to Jerusalem.

3.text: And as he went on his journey, it came to pass that he drew nigh to Damascus; and suddenly a light from heaven shined round about him.

4.text: And falling on the ground, he heard a voice saying to him: Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?

5.text: Who said: Who art thou, Lord? And he: I am Jesus whom thou persecutest. It is hard for thee to kick against the goad.

6.text: And he trembling and astonished, said: Lord, what wilt thou have me to do?

7.text: And the Lord said to him: Arise, and go into the city, and there it shall be told thee what thou must do. Now the men who went in company with him, stood amazed, hearing indeed a voice, but seeing no man.

8.text: And Saul arose from the ground; and when his eyes were opened, he saw nothing. But they leading him by the hands, brought him to Damascus.

9.text: And he was there three days, without sight, and he did neither eat nor drink.

10.text: Now there was a certain disciple at Damascus, named Ananias. And the Lord said to him in a vision: Ananias. And he said: Behold I am here, Lord.

11.text: And the Lord said to him: Arise, and go into the street that is called Strait, and seek in the house of Judas, one named Saul of Tarsus. For behold he prayeth.

12.text: (And he saw a man named Ananias coming in, and putting his hands upon him, that he might receive his sight.)

13.text: But Ananias answered: Lord, I have heard by many of this man, how much evil he hath done to thy saints in Jerusalem.

14.text: And here he hath authority from the chief priests to bind all that invoke thy name.

15.text: And the Lord said to him: Go thy way; for this man is to me a vessel of election, to carry my name before the Gentiles, and kings, and the children of Israel.

16.text: For I will shew him how great things he must suffer for my name’s sake.

17.text: And Ananias went his way, and entered into the house. And laying his hands upon him, he said: Brother Saul, the Lord Jesus hath sent me, he that appeared to thee in the way as thou camest; that thou mayest receive thy sight, and be filled with the Holy Ghost.

18.text: And immediately there fell from his eyes as it were scales, and he received his sight; and rising up, he was baptized.

19.text: And when he had taken meat, he was strengthened. And he was with the disciples that were at Damascus, for some days.

20.text: And immediately he preached Jesus in the synagogues, that he is the Son of God.

21.text: And all that heard him, were astonished, and said: Is not this he who persecuted in Jerusalem those that called upon this name: and came hither for that intent, that he might carry them bound to the chief priests?

22.text: But Saul increased much more in strength, and confounded the Jews who dwelt at Damascus, affirming that this is the Christ.

23.text: And when many days were passed, the Jews consulted together to kill him.

24.text: But their laying in wait was made known to Saul. And they watched the gates also day and night, that they might kill him.

25.text: But the disciples taking him in the night, conveyed him away by the wall, letting him down in a basket.

26.text: And when he was come into Jerusalem, he essayed to join himself to the disciples; and they all were afraid of him, not believing that he was a disciple.

27.text: But Barnabas took him, and brought him to the apostles, and told them how he had seen the Lord, and that he had spoken to him; and how in Damascus he had dealt confidently in the name of Jesus.

28.text: And he was with them coming in and going out in Jerusalem, and dealing confidently in the name of the Lord.

29.text: He spoke also to the Gentiles, and disputed with the Greeks; but they sought to kill him.

30.text: Which when the brethren had known, they brought him down to Caesarea, and sent him away to Tarsus.

31.text: Now the church had peace throughout all Judea, and Galilee, and Samaria; and was edified, walking in the fear of the Lord, and was filled with the consolation of the Holy Ghost.

32.text: And it came to pass that Peter, as he passed through, visiting all, came to the saints who dwelt at Lydda.

33.text: And he found there a certain man named Eneas, who had kept his bed for eight years, who was ill of the palsy.

34.text: And Peter said to him: Eneas, the Lord Jesus Christ healeth thee: arise, and make thy bed. And immediately he arose.

35.text: And all that dwelt at Lydda and Saron, saw him: who were converted to the Lord.

36.text: And in Joppe there was a certain disciple named Tabitha, which by interpretation is called Dorcas. This woman was full of good works and almsdeeds which she did.

37.text: And it came to pass in those days that she was sick, and died. Whom when they had washed, they laid her in an upper chamber.

38.text: And forasmuch as Lydda was nigh to Joppe, the disciples hearing that Peter was there, sent unto him two men, desiring him that he would not be slack to come unto them.

39.text: And Peter rising up, went with them. And when he was come, they brought him into the upper chamber. And all the widows stood about him weeping, and shewing him the coats and garments which Dorcas made them.

40.text: And they all being put forth, Peter kneeling down prayed, and turning to the body, he said: Tabitha, arise. And she opened her eyes; and seeing Peter, she sat up.

41.text: And giving her his hand, he lifted her up. And when he had called the saints and the widows, he presented her alive.

42.text: And it was made known throughout all Joppe; and many believed in the Lord.

43.text: And it came to pass, that he abode many days in Joppe, with one Simon a tanner.

1.text: And there was a certain man in Caesarea, named Cornelius, a centurion of that which is called the Italian band;

2.text: A religious man, and fearing God with all his house, giving much alms to the people, and always praying to God.

3.text: This man saw in a vision manifestly, about the ninth hour of the day, an angel of God coming in unto him, and saying to him: Cornelius.

4.text: And he, beholding him, being seized with fear, said: What is it, Lord? And he said to him: Thy prayers and thy alms are ascended for a memorial in the sight of God.

5.text: And now send men to Joppe, and call hither one Simon, who is surnamed Peter:

6.text: He lodgeth with one Simon a tanner, whose house is by the sea side. He will tell thee what thou must do.

7.text: And when the angel who spoke to him was departed, he called two of his household servants, and a soldier who feared the Lord, of them that were under him.

8.text: To whom when he had related all, he sent them to Joppe.

9.text: And on the next day, whilst they were going on their journey, and drawing nigh to the city, Peter went up to the higher parts of the house to pray, about the sixth hour.

10.text: And being hungry, he was desirous to taste somewhat. And as they were preparing, there came upon him an ecstasy of mind.

11.text: And he saw the heaven opened, and a certain vessel descending, as it were a great linen sheet let down by the four corners from heaven to the earth:

12.text: Wherein were all manner of fourfooted beasts, and creeping things of the earth, and fowls of the air.

13.text: And there came a voice to him: Arise, Peter; kill and eat.

14.text: But Peter said: Far be it from me; for I never did eat any thing that is common and unclean.

15.text: And the voice spoke to him again the second time: That which God hath cleansed, do not thou call common.

16.text: And this was done thrice; and presently the vessel was taken up into heaven.

17.text: Now, whilst Peter was doubting within himself, what the vision that he had seen should mean, behold the men who were sent from Cornelius, inquiring for Simon’s house, stood at the gate.

18.text: And when they had called, they asked, if Simon, who is surnamed Peter, were lodged there.

19.text: And as Peter was thinking of the vision, the Spirit said to him: Behold three men seek thee.

20.text: Arise, therefore, get thee down and go with them, doubting nothing: for I have sent them.

21.text: Then Peter, going down to the men, said: Behold, I am he whom you seek; what is the cause for which you are come?

22.text: Who said: Cornelius, a centurion, a just man, and one that feareth God, and having good testimony from all the nation of the Jews, received an answer of an holy angel, to send for thee into his house, and to hear words of thee.

23.text: Then bringing them in, he lodged them. And the day following he arose, and went with them: and some of the brethren from Joppe accompanied him.

24.text: And the morrow after, he entered into Caesarea. And Cornelius waited for them, having called together his kinsmen and special friends.

25.text: And the morrow after, he entered into Caesarea. And Cornelius waited for them, having called together his kinsmen and special friends.

26.text: But Peter lifted him up, saying: Arise, I myself also am a man.

27.text: And talking with him, he went in, and found many that were come together.

28.text: And he said to them: You know how abominable it is for a man that is a Jew, to keep company or to come unto one of another nation: but God hath shewed to me, to call no man common or unclean.

29.text: For which cause, making no doubt, I came when I was sent for. I ask, therefore, for what cause you have sent for me?

30.text: And Cornelius said: Four days ago, unto this hour, I was praying in my house, at the ninth hour, and behold a man stood before me in white apparel, and said:

31.text: Cornelius, thy prayer is heard, and thy alms are had in remembrance in the sight of God.

32.text: Send therefore to Joppe, and call hither Simon, who is surnamed Peter: he lodgeth in the house of Simon a tanner, by the sea side.

33.text: Immediately therefore I sent to thee: and thou hast done well in coming. Now therefore all we are present in thy sight, to hear all things whatsoever are commanded thee by the Lord.

34.text: And Peter opening his mouth, said: In very deed I perceive, that God is not a respecter of persons.

35.text: But in every nation, he that feareth him, and worketh justice, is acceptable to him.

36.text: God sent the word to the children of Israel, preaching peace by Jesus Christ: (he is Lord of all.)

37.text: You know the word which hath been published through all Judea: for it began from Galilee, after the baptism which John preached,

38.text: Jesus of Nazareth: how God anointed him with the Holy Ghost, and with power, who went about doing good, and healing all that were oppressed by the devil, for God was with him.

39.text: And we are witnesses of all things that he did in the land of the Jews and in Jerusalem, whom they killed, hanging him upon a tree.

40.text: Him God raised up the third day, and gave him to be made manifest,

41.text: Not to all the people, but to witnesses preordained by God, even to us, who did eat and drink with him after he arose again from the dead;

42.text: And he commanded us to preach to the people, and to testify that it is he who was appointed by God, to be judge of the living and of the dead.

43.text: To him all the prophets give testimony, that by his name all receive remission of sins, who believe in him.

44.text: While Peter was yet speaking these words, the Holy Ghost fell on all them that heard the word.

45.text: And the faithful of the circumcision, who came with Peter, were astonished, for that the grace of the Holy Ghost was poured out upon the Gentiles also.

46.text: For they heard them speaking with tongues, and magnifying God.

47.text: Then Peter answered: Can any man forbid water, that these should not be baptized, who have received the Holy Ghost, as well as we?

48.text: And he commanded them to be baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Then they desired him to tarry with them some days.

1.text: And the apostles and brethren, who were in Judea, heard that the Gentiles also had received the word of God.

2.text: And when Peter was come up to Jerusalem, they that were of the circumcision contended with him,

3.text: Saying: Why didst thou go in to men uncircumcised, and didst eat with them?

4.text: But Peter began and declared to them the matter in order, saying:

5.text: I was in the city of Joppe praying, and I saw in an ecstasy of mind a vision, a certain vessel descending, as it were a great sheet let down from heaven by four corners, and it came even unto me.

6.text: Into which looking, I considered, and saw fourfooted creatures of the earth, and beasts, and creeping things, and fowls of the air:

7.text: And I heard also a voice saying to me: Arise, Peter; kill and eat.

8.text: And I said: Not so, Lord; for nothing common or unclean hath ever entered into my mouth.

9.text: And the voice answered again from heaven: What God hath made clean, do not thou call common.

10.text: And this was done three times: and all were taken up again into heaven.

11.text: And behold, immediately there were three men come to the house wherein I was, sent to me from Caesarea.

12.text: And the Spirit said to me, that I should go with them, nothing doubting. And these six brethren went with me also: and we entered into the man’s house.

13.text: And he told us how he had seen an angel in his house, standing, and saying to him: Send to Joppe, and call hither Simon, who is surnamed Peter,

14.text: Who shall speak to thee words, whereby thou shalt be saved, and all thy house.

15.text: And when I had begun to speak, the Holy Ghost fell upon them, as upon us also in the beginning.

16.text: And I remembered the word of the Lord, how that he said: John indeed baptized with water, but you shall be baptized with the Holy Ghost.

17.text: If then God gave them the same grace, as to us also who believed in the Lord Jesus Christ; who was I, that could withstand God?

18.text: Having heard these things, they held their peace, and glorified God, saying: God then hath also to the Gentiles given repentance unto life.

19.text: Now they who had been dispersed by the persecution that arose on occasion of Stephen, went about as far as Phenice and Cyprus and Antioch, speaking the word to none, but to the Jews only.

20.text: But some of them were men of Cyprus and Cyrene, who, when they were entered into Antioch, spoke also to the Greeks, preaching the Lord Jesus.

21.text: And the hand of the Lord was with them: and a great number believing, were converted to the Lord.

22.text: And the tidings came to the ears of the church that was at Jerusalem, touching these things: and they sent Barnabas as far as Antioch.

23.text: Who, when he was come, and had seen the grace of God, rejoiced: and he exhorted them all with purpose of heart to continue in the Lord.

24.text: For he was a good man, and full of the Holy Ghost and of faith. And a great multitude was added to the Lord.

25.text: And Barnabas went to Tarsus to seek Saul: whom, when he had found, he brought to Antioch.

26.text: And they conversed there in the church a whole year; and they taught a great multitude, so that at Antioch the disciples were first named Christians.

27.text: And in these days there came prophets from Jerusalem to Antioch:

28.text: And one of them named Agabus, rising up, signified by the Spirit, that there should be a great famine over the whole world, which came to pass under Claudius.

29.text: And the disciples, every man according to his ability, purposed to send relief to the brethren who dwelt in Judea:

30.text: Which also they did, sending it to the ancients, by the hands of Barnabas and Saul.

1.text: And at the same time, Herod the king stretched forth his hands, to afflict some of the church.

2.text: And he killed James, the brother of John, with the sword.

3.text: And seeing that it pleased the Jews, he proceeded to take up Peter also. Now it was in the days of the Azymes.

4.text: And when he had apprehended him, he cast him into prison, delivering him to four files of soldiers to be kept, intending, after the pasch, to bring him forth to the people.

5.text: Peter therefore was kept in prison. But prayer was made without ceasing by the church unto God for him.

6.text: And when Herod would have brought him forth, the same night Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains: and the keepers before the door kept the prison.

7.text: And behold an angel of the Lord stood by him: and a light shined in the room: and he striking Peter on the side, raised him up, saying: Arise quickly. And the chains fell off from his hands.

8.text: And the angel said to him: Gird thyself, and put on thy sandals. And he did so. And he said to him: Cast thy garment about thee, and follow me.

9.text: And going out, he followed him, and he knew not that it was true which was done by the angel: but thought he saw a vision.

10.text: And passing through the first and the second ward, they came to the iron gate that leadeth to the city, which of itself opened to them. And going out, they passed on through one street: and immediately the angel departed from him.

11.text: And Peter coming to himself, said: Now I know in very deed, that the Lord hath sent his angel, and hath delivered me out of the hand of Herod, and from all the expectation of the people of the Jews.

12.text: And considering, he came to the house of Mary the mother of John, who was surnamed Mark, where many were gathered together and praying.

13.text: And when he knocked at the door of the gate, a damsel came to hearken, whose name was Rhode.

14.text: And as soon as she knew Peter’s voice, she opened not the gate for joy, but running in she told that Peter stood before the gate.

15.text: But they said to her: Thou art mad. But she affirmed that it was so. Then said they: It is his angel.

16.text: But Peter continued knocking. And when they had opened, they saw him, and were astonished.

17.text: But he beckoning to them with his hand to hold their peace, told how the Lord had brought him out of prison, and he said: Tell these things to James, and to the brethren. And going out, he went into another place.

18.text: Now when day was come, there was no small stir among the soldiers, what was become of Peter.

19.text: And when Herod had sought for him, and found him not; having examined the keepers, he commanded they should be put to death; and going down from Judea to Caesarea, he abode there.

20.text: And he was angry with the Tyrians and the Sidonians. But they with one accord came to him, and having gained Blastus, who was the king’s chamberlain, they desired peace, because their countries were nourished by him.

21.text: And upon a day appointed, Herod being arrayed in kingly apparel, sat in the judgment seat, and made an oration to them.

22.text: And the people made acclamation, saying: It is the voice of a god, and not of a man.

23.text: And forthwith an angel of the Lord struck him, because he had not given the honour to God: and being eaten up by worms, he gave up the ghost.

24.text: But the word of the Lord increased and multiplied.

25.text: And Barnabas and Saul returned from Jerusalem, having fulfilled their ministry, taking with them John, who was surnamed Mark.

1.text: Now there were in the church which was at Antioch, prophets and doctors, among whom was Barnabas, and Simon who was called Niger, and Lucius of Cyrene, and Manahen, who was the foster brother of Herod the tetrarch, and Saul.

2.text: And as they were ministering to the Lord, and fasting, the Holy Ghost said to them: Separate me Saul and Barnabas, for the work whereunto I have taken them.

3.text: Then they, fasting and praying, and imposing their hands upon them, sent them away.

4.text: So they being sent by the Holy Ghost, went to Seleucia: and from thence they sailed to Cyprus.

5.text: And when they were come to Salamina, they preached the word of God in the synagogues of the Jews. And they had John also in the ministry.

6.text: And when they had gone through the whole island, as far as Paphos, they found a certain man, a magician, a false prophet, a Jew, whose name was Bar-jesu:

7.text: Who was with the proconsul Sergius Paulus, a prudent man. He sending for Barnabas and Saul, desired to hear the word of God.

8.text: But Elymas the magician (for so his name is interpreted) withstood them, seeking to turn away the proconsul from the faith.

9.text: Then Saul, otherwise Paul, filled with the Holy Ghost, looking upon him,

10.text: Said: O full of all guile, and of all deceit, child of the devil, enemy of all justice, thou ceasest not to pervert the right ways of the Lord.

11.text: And now behold, the hand of the Lord is upon thee, and thou shalt be blind, not seeing the sun for a time. And immediately there fell a mist and darkness upon him, and going about, he sought some one to lead him by the hand.

12.text: Then the proconsul, when he had seen what was done, believed, admiring at the doctrine of the Lord.

13.text: Now when Paul and they that were with him had sailed from Paphos, they came to Perge in Pamphylia. And John departing from them, returned to Jerusalem.

14.text: But they passing through Perge, came to Antioch in Pisidia: and entering into the synagogue on the sabbath day, they sat down.

15.text: And after the reading of the law and the prophets, the rulers of the synagogue sent to them, saying: Ye men, brethren, if you have any word of exhortation to make to the people, speak.

16.text: Then Paul rising up, and with his hand bespeaking silence, said: Ye men of Israel, and you that fear God, give ear.

17.text: The God of the people of Israel chose our fathers, and exalted the people when they were sojourners in the land of Egypt, and with an high arm brought them out from thence,

18.text: And for the space of forty years endured their manners in the desert.

19.text: And destroying seven nations in the land of Chanaan, divided their land among them, by lot,

20.text: As it were, after four hundred and fifty years: and after these things, he gave unto them judges, until Samuel the prophet.

21.text: And after that they desired a king: and God gave them Saul the son of Cis, a man of the tribe of Benjamin, forty years.

22.text: And when he had removed him, he raised them up David to be king: to whom giving testimony, he said: I have found David, the son of Jesse, a man according to my own heart, who shall do all my wills.

23.text: Of this man’s seed God according to his promise, hath raised up to Israel a Saviour, Jesus:

24.text: John first preaching, before his coming, the baptism of penance to all the people of Israel.

25.text: And when John was fulfilling his course, he said: I am not he, whom you think me to be: but behold, there cometh one after me, whose shoes of his feet I am not worthy to loose.

26.text: Men, brethren, children of the stock of Abraham, and whosoever among you fear God, to you the word of this salvation is sent.

27.text: For they that inhabited Jerusalem, and the rulers thereof, not knowing him, nor the voices of the prophets, which are read every sabbath, judging him have fulfilled them.

28.text: And finding no cause of death in him, they desired of Pilate, that they might kill him.

29.text: And when they had fulfilled all things that were written of him, taking him down from the tree, they laid him in a sepulchre.

30.text: But God raised him up from the dead the third day:

31.text: Who was seen for many days, by them who came up with him from Galilee to Jerusalem, who to this present are his witnesses to the people.

32.text: And we declare unto you, that the promise which was made to our fathers,

33.text: This same God hath fulfilled to our children, raising up Jesus, as in the second psalm also is written: Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee.

34.text: And to shew that he raised him up from the dead, not to return now any more to corruption, he said thus: I will give you the holy things of David faithful.

35.text: And therefore, in another place also, he saith: Thou shalt not suffer thy holy one to see corruption.

36.text: For David, when he had served in his generation, according to the will of God, slept: and was laid unto his fathers, and saw corruption.

37.text: But he whom God hath raised from the dead, saw no corruption.

38.text: Be it known therefore to you, men, brethren, that through him forgiveness of sins is preached to you: and from all the things, from which you could not be justified by the law of Moses.

39.text: In him every one that believeth, is justified.

40.text: Beware, therefore, lest that come upon you which is spoken in the prophets:

41.text: Behold, ye despisers, and wonder, and perish: for I work a work in your days, a work which you will not believe, if any man shall tell it you.

42.text: And as they went out, they desired them, that on the next sabbath, they would speak unto them these words.

43.text: And when the synagogue was broken up, many of the Jews, and of the strangers who served God, followed Paul and Barnabas: who speaking to them, persuaded them to continue in the grace of God.

44.text: But the next sabbath day, the whole city almost came together, to hear the word of God.

45.text: And the Jews seeing the multitudes, were filled with envy, and contradicted those things which were said by Paul, blaspheming.

46.text: Then Paul and Barnabas said boldly: To you it behoved us first to speak the word of God: but because you reject it, and judge yourselves unworthy of eternal life, behold we turn to the Gentiles.

47.text: For so the Lord hath commanded us: I have set thee to be the light of the Gentiles; that thou mayest be for salvation unto the utmost part of the earth.

48.text: And the Gentiles hearing it, were glad, and glorified the word of the Lord: and as many as were ordained to life everlasting, believed.

49.text: And the word of the Lord was published throughout the whole country.

50.text: But the Jews stirred up religious and honourable women, and the chief men of the city, and raised persecution against Paul and Barnabas: and cast them out of their coasts.

51.text: But they, shaking off the dust of their feet against them, came to Iconium.

52.text: And the disciples were filled with joy and with the Holy Ghost.

1.text: And it came to pass in Iconium, that they entered together into the synagogue of the Jews, and so spoke that a very great multitude both of the Jews and of the Greeks did believe.

2.text: But the unbelieving Jews stirred up and incensed the minds of the Gentiles against the brethren.

3.text: A long time therefore they abode there, dealing confidently in the Lord, who gave testimony to the word of his grace, granting signs and wonders to be done by their hands.
