1.text: What advantage then hath the Jew, or what is the profit of circumcision?

2.text: Much every way. First indeed, because the words of God were committed to them.

3.text: For what if some of them have not believed? shall their unbelief make the faith of God without effect? God forbid.

4.text: But God is true; and every man a liar, as it is written, That thou mayest be justified in thy words, and mayest overcome when thou art judged.

5.text: But if our injustice commend the justice of God, what shall we say? Is God unjust, who executeth wrath?

6.text: (I speak according to man.) God forbid: otherwise how shall God judge this world?

7.text: For if the truth of God hath more abounded through my lie, unto his glory, why am I also yet judged as a sinner?

8.text: And not rather (as we are slandered, and as some affirm that we say) let us do evil, that there may come good? whose damnation is just.

9.text: What then? Do we excel them? No, not so. For we have charged both Jews, and Greeks, that they are all under sin.

10.text: As it is written: There is not any man just.

11.text: There is none that understandeth, there is none that seeketh after God.

12.text: All have turned out of the way; they are become unprofitable together: there is none that doth good, there is not so much as one.

13.text: Their throat is an open sepulchre; with their tongues they have dealt deceitfully. The venom of asps is under their lips.

14.text: Whose mouth is full of cursing and bitterness:

15.text: Their feet swift to shed blood:

16.text: Destruction and misery in their ways:

17.text: And the way of peace they have not known:

18.text: There is no fear of God before their eyes.

19.text: Now we know, that what things soever the law speaketh, it speaketh to them that are in the law; that every mouth may be stopped, and all the world may be made subject to God.

20.text: Because by the works of the law no flesh shall be justified before him. For by the law is the knowledge of sin.

21.text: But now without the law the justice of God is made manifest, being witnessed by the law and the prophets.

22.text: Even the justice of God, by faith of Jesus Christ, unto all and upon all them that believe in him: for there is no distinction:

23.text: For all have sinned, and do need the glory of God.

24.text: Being justified freely by his grace, through the redemption, that is in Christ Jesus,

25.text: Whom God hath proposed to be a propitiation, through faith in his blood, to the shewing of his justice, for the remission of former sins,

26.text: Through the forbearance of God, for the shewing of his justice in this time; that he himself may be just, and the justifier of him, who is of the faith of Jesus Christ.

27.text: Where is then thy boasting? It is excluded. By what law? Of works? No, but by the law of faith.

28.text: For we account a man to be justified by faith, without the works of the law.

29.text: Is he the God of the Jews only? Is he not also of the Gentiles? Yes, of the Gentiles also.

30.text: For it is one God, that justifieth circumcision by faith, and uncircumcision through faith.

31.text: Do we, then, destroy the law through faith? God forbid: but we establish the law.

1.text: What shall we say then that Abraham hath found, who is our father according to the flesh.

2.text: For if Abraham were justified by works, he hath whereof to glory, but not before God.

3.text: For what saith the scripture? Abraham believed God, and it was reputed to him unto justice.

4.text: Now to him that worketh, the reward is not reckoned according to grace, but according to debt.

5.text: But to him that worketh not, yet believeth in him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is reputed to justice, according to the purpose of the grace of God.

6.text: As David also termeth the blessedness of a man, to whom God reputeth justice without works:

7.text: Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, and whose sins are covered.

8.text: Blessed is the man to whom the Lord hath not imputed sin.

9.text: This blessedness then, doth it remain in the circumcision only, or in the uncircumcision also? For we say that unto Abraham faith was reputed to justice.

10.text: How then was it reputed? When he was in circumcision, or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision.

11.text: And he received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the justice of the faith, which he had, being uncircumcised; that he might be the father of all them that believe, being uncircumcised, that unto them also it may be reputed to justice:

12.text: And might be the father of circumcision; not to them only, that are of the circumcision, but to them also that follow the steps of the faithful, that is in the uncircumcision of our father Abraham.

13.text: For not through the law was the promise to Abraham, or to his seed, that he should be heir of the world; but through the justice of faith.

14.text: For if they who are of the law be heirs, faith is made void, the promise is made of no effect.

15.text: For the law worketh wrath. For where there is no law, neither is there transgression.

16.text: Therefore is it of faith, that according to grace the promise might be firm to all the seed; not to that only which is of the law, but to that also which is of the faith of Abraham, who is the father of us all,

17.text: (As it is written: I have made thee a father of many nations,) before God, whom he believed, who quickeneth the dead; and calleth those things that are not, as those that are.

18.text: Who against hope believed in hope; that he might be made the father of many nations, according to that which was said to him: So shall thy seed be.

19.text: And he was not weak in faith; neither did he consider his own body now dead, whereas he was almost an hundred years old, nor the dead womb of Sara.

20.text: In the promise also of God he staggered not by distrust; but was strengthened in faith, giving glory to God:

21.text: Most fully knowing, that whatsoever he has promised, he is able also to perform.

22.text: And therefore it was reputed to him unto justice.

23.text: Now it is not written only for him, that it was reputed to him unto justice,

24.text: But also for us, to whom it shall be reputed, if we believe in him, that raised up Jesus Christ, our Lord, from the dead,

25.text: Who was delivered up for our sins, and rose again for our justification.

1.text: Being justified therefore by faith, let us have peace with God, through our Lord Jesus Christ:

2.text: By whom also we have access through faith into this grace, wherein we stand, and glory in the hope of the glory of the sons of God.

3.text: And not only so; but we glory also in tribulations, knowing that tribulation worketh patience;

4.text: And patience trial; and trial hope;

5.text: And hope confoundeth not: because the charity of God is poured forth in our hearts, by the Holy Ghost, who is given to us.

6.text: For why did Christ, when as yet we were weak, according to the time, die for the ungodly?

7.text: For scarce for a just man will one die; yet perhaps for a good man some one would dare to die.

8.text: But God commendeth his charity towards us; because when as yet we were sinners, according to the time,

9.text: Christ died for us; much more therefore, being now justified by his blood, shall we be saved from wrath through him.

10.text: For if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son; much more, being reconciled, shall we be saved by his life.

11.text: And not only so; but also we glory in God, through our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom we have now received reconciliation.

12.text: Wherefore as by one man sin entered into this world, and by sin death; and so death passed upon all men, in whom all have sinned.

13.text: For until the law sin was in the world; but sin was not imputed, when the law was not.

14.text: But death reigned from Adam unto Moses, even over them also who have not sinned after the similitude of the transgression of Adam, who is a figure of him who was to come.

15.text: But not as the offence, so also the gift. For if by the offence of one, many died; much more the grace of God, and the gift, by the grace of one man, Jesus Christ, hath abounded unto many.

16.text: And not as it was by one sin, so also is the gift. For judgment indeed was by one unto condemnation; but grace is of many offences, unto justification.

17.text: For if by one man’s offence death reigned through one; much more they who receive abundance of grace, and of the gift, and of justice, shall reign in life through one, Jesus Christ.

18.text: Therefore, as by the offence of one, unto all men to condemnation; so also by the justice of one, unto all men to justification of life.

19.text: For as by the disobedience of one man, many were made sinners; so also by the obedience of one, many shall be made just.

20.text: Now the law entered in, that sin might abound. And where sin abounded, grace did more abound.

21.text: That as sin hath reigned to death; so also grace might reign by justice unto life everlasting, through Jesus Christ our Lord.

1.text: What shall we say, then? shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound?

2.text: God forbid. For we that are dead to sin, how shall we live any longer therein?

3.text: Know you not that all we, who are baptized in Christ Jesus, are baptized in his death?

4.text: For we are buried together with him by baptism into death; that as Christ is risen from the dead by the glory of the Father, so we also may walk in newness of life.

5.text: For if we have been planted together in the likeness of his death, we shall be also in the likeness of his resurrection.

6.text: Knowing this, that our old man is crucified with him, that the body of sin may be destroyed, to the end that we may serve sin no longer.

7.text: For he that is dead is justified from sin.

8.text: Now if we be dead with Christ, we believe that we shall live also together with Christ:

9.text: Knowing that Christ rising again from the dead, dieth now no more, death shall no more have dominion over him.

10.text: For in that he died to sin, he died once; but in that he liveth, he liveth unto God:

11.text: So do you also reckon, that you are dead to sin, but alive unto God, in Christ Jesus our Lord.

12.text: Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body, so as to obey the lusts thereof.

13.text: Neither yield ye your members as instruments of iniquity unto sin; but present yourselves to God, as those that are alive from the dead, and your members as instruments of justice unto God.

14.text: For sin shall not have dominion over you; for you are not under the law, but under grace.

15.text: What then? Shall we sin, because we are not under the law, but under grace? God forbid.

16.text: Know you not, that to whom you yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants you are whom you obey, whether it be of sin unto death, or of obedience unto justice.

17.text: But thanks be to God, that you were the servants of sin, but have obeyed from the heart, unto that form of doctrine, into which you have been delivered.

18.text: Being then freed from sin, we have been made servants of justice.

19.text: I speak an human thing, because of the infirmity of your flesh. For as you have yielded your members to serve uncleanness and iniquity, unto iniquity; so now yield your members to serve justice, unto sanctification.

20.text: For when you were the servants of sin, you were free men to justice.

21.text: For when you were the servants of sin, you were free men to justice.

22.text: But now being made free from sin, and become servants to God, you have your fruit unto sanctification, and the end life everlasting.

23.text: For the wages of sin is death. But the grace of God, life everlasting, in Christ Jesus our Lord.

1.text: Know you not, brethren, (for I speak to them that know the law,) that the law hath dominion over a man, as long as it liveth?

2.text: For the woman that hath an husband, whilst her husband liveth is bound to the law. But if her husband be dead, she is loosed from the law of her husband.

3.text: Therefore, whilst her husband liveth, she shall be called an adulteress, if she be with another man: but if her husband be dead, she is delivered from the law of her husband; so that she is not an adulteress, if she be with another man.

4.text: Therefore, my brethren, you also are become dead to the law, by the body of Christ; that you may belong to another, who is risen again from the dead, that we may bring forth fruit to God.

5.text: For when we were in the flesh, the passions of sins, which were by the law, did work in our members, to bring forth fruit unto death.

6.text: But now we are loosed from the law of death, wherein we were detained; so that we should serve in newness of spirit, and not in the oldness of the letter.

7.text: What shall we say, then? Is the law sin? God forbid. But I do not know sin, but by the law; for I had not known concupiscence, if the law did not say: Thou shalt not covet.

8.text: But sin taking occasion by the commandment, wrought in me all manner of concupiscence. For without the law sin was dead.

9.text: And I lived some time without the law. But when the commandment came, sin revived,

10.text: And I died. And the commandment that was ordained to life, the same was found to be unto death to me.

11.text: For sin, taking occasion by the commandment, seduced me, and by it killed me.

12.text: Wherefore the law indeed is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good.

13.text: Was that then which is good, made death unto me? God forbid. But sin, that it may appear sin, by that which is good, wrought death in me; that sin, by the commandment, might become sinful above measure.

14.text: For we know that the law is spiritual; but I am carnal, sold under sin.

15.text: For that which I work, I understand not. For I do not that good which I will; but the evil which I hate, that I do.

16.text: If then I do that which I will not, I consent to the law, that it is good.

17.text: Now then it is no more I that do it, but sin that dwelleth in me.

18.text: For I know that there dwelleth not in me, that is to say, in my flesh, that which is good. For to will, is present with me; but to accomplish that which is good, I find not.

19.text: For the good which I will, I do not; but the evil which I will not, that I do.

20.text: Now if I do that which I will not, it is no more I that do it, but sin that dwelleth in me.

21.text: I find then a law, that when I have a will to do good, evil is present with me.

22.text: For I am delighted with the law of God, according to the inward man:

23.text: But I see another law in my members, fighting against the law of my mind, and captivating me in the law of sin, that is in my members.

24.text: Unhappy man that I am, who shall deliver me from the body of this death?

25.text: The grace of God, by Jesus Christ our Lord. Therefore, I myself, with the mind serve the law of God; but with the flesh, the law of sin.

1.text: There is now therefore no condemnation to them that are in Christ Jesus, who walk not according to the flesh.

2.text: For the law of the spirit of life, in Christ Jesus, hath delivered me from the law of sin and of death.

3.text: For what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh; God sending his own Son, in the likeness of sinful flesh and of sin, hath condemned sin in the flesh;

4.text: That the justification of the law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not according to the flesh, but according to the spirit.

5.text: For they that are according to the flesh, mind the things that are of the flesh; but they that are according to the spirit, mind the things that are of the spirit.

6.text: For the wisdom of the flesh is death; but the wisdom of the spirit is life and peace.

7.text: Because the wisdom of the flesh is an enemy to God; for it is not subject to the law of God, neither can it be.

8.text: And they who are in the flesh, cannot please God.

9.text: But you are not in the flesh, but in the spirit, if so be that the Spirit of God dwell in you. Now if any man have not the Spirit of Christ, he is none of his.

10.text: And if Christ be in you, the body indeed is dead, because of sin; but the spirit liveth, because of justification.

11.text: And if the Spirit of him that raised up Jesus from the dead, dwell in you; he that raised up Jesus Christ from the dead, shall quicken also your mortal bodies, because of his Spirit that dwelleth in you.

12.text: Therefore, brethren, we are debtors, not to the flesh, to live according to the flesh.

13.text: For if you live according to the flesh, you shall die: but if by the Spirit you mortify the deeds of the flesh, you shall live.

14.text: For whosoever are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God.

15.text: For you have not received the spirit of bondage again in fear; but you have received the spirit of adoption of sons, whereby we cry: Abba (Father).

16.text: For the Spirit himself giveth testimony to our spirit, that we are the sons of God.

17.text: And if sons, heirs also; heirs indeed of God, and joint heirs with Christ: yet so, if we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified with him.

18.text: For I reckon that the sufferings of this time are not worthy to be compared with the glory to come, that shall be revealed in us.

19.text: For the expectation of the creature waiteth for the revelation of the sons of God.

20.text: For the creature was made subject to vanity, not willingly, but by reason of him that made it subject, in hope:

21.text: Because the creature also itself shall be delivered from the servitude of corruption, into the liberty of the glory of the children of God.

22.text: For we know that every creature groaneth and travaileth in pain, even till now.

23.text: And not only it, but ourselves also, who have the firstfruits of the Spirit, even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption of the sons of God, the redemption of our body.

24.text: For we are saved by hope. But hope that is seen, is not hope. For what a man seeth, why doth he hope for?

25.text: But if we hope for that which we see not, we wait for it with patience.

26.text: Likewise the Spirit also helpeth our infirmity. For we know not what we should pray for as we ought; but the Spirit himself asketh for us with unspeakable groanings.

27.text: And he that searcheth the hearts, knoweth what the Spirit desireth; because he asketh for the saints according to God.

28.text: And we know that to them that love God, all things work together unto good, to such as, according to his purpose, are called to be saints.

29.text: For whom he foreknew, he also predestinated to be made conformable to the image of his Son; that he might be the firstborn amongst many brethren.

30.text: And whom he predestinated, them he also called. And whom he called, them he also justified. And whom he justified, them he also glorified.

31.text: What shall we then say to these things? If God be for us, who is against us?

32.text: He that spared not even his own Son, but delivered him up for us all, how hath he not also, with him, given us all things?

33.text: Who shall accuse against the elect of God? God that justifieth.

34.text: Who is he that shall condemn? Christ Jesus that died, yea that is risen also again; who is at the right hand of God, who also maketh intercession for us.

35.text: Who then shall separate us from the love of Christ? Shall tribulation? or distress? or famine? or nakedness? or danger? or persecution? or the sword?

36.text: (As it is written: For thy sake we are put to death all the day long. We are accounted as sheep for the slaughter.)

37.text: But in all these things we overcome, because of him that hath loved us.

38.text: For I am sure that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come, nor might,

39.text: Nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.

1.text: I speak the truth in Christ, I lie not, my conscience bearing me witness in the Holy Ghost:

2.text: That I have great sadness, and continual sorrow in my heart.

3.text: For I wished myself to be an anathema from Christ, for my brethren, who are my kinsmen according to the flesh,

4.text: Who are Israelites, to whom belongeth the adoption as of children, and the glory, and the testament, and the giving of the law, and the service of God, and the promises:

5.text: Whose are the fathers, and of whom is Christ, according to the flesh, who is over all things, God blessed for ever. Amen.

6.text: Not as though the word of God hath miscarried. For all are not Israelites that are of Israel:

7.text: Neither are all they that are the seed of Abraham, children; but in Isaac shall thy seed be called:

8.text: That is to say, not they that are the children of the flesh, are the children of God; but they, that are the children of the promise, are accounted for the seed.

9.text: For this is the word of promise: According to this time will I come; and Sara shall have a son.

10.text: And not only she. But when Rebecca also had conceived at once, of Isaac our father.

11.text: For when the children were not yet born, nor had done any good or evil (that the purpose of God, according to election, might stand,)

12.text: Not of works, but of him that calleth, it was said to her: The elder shall serve the younger.

13.text: As it is written: Jacob I have loved, but Esau I have hated.

14.text: What shall we say then? Is there injustice with God? God forbid.

15.text: For he saith to Moses: I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy; and I will shew mercy to whom I will shew mercy.

16.text: So then it is not of him that willeth, nor of him that runneth, but of God that sheweth mercy.

17.text: For the scripture saith to Pharao: To this purpose have I raised thee, that I may shew my power in thee, and that my name may be declared throughout all the earth.

18.text: Therefore he hath mercy on whom he will; and whom he will, he hardeneth.

19.text: Thou wilt say therefore to me: Why doth he then find fault? for who resisteth his will?

20.text: O man, who art thou that repliest against God? Shall the thing formed say to him that formed it: Why hast thou made me thus?

21.text: Or hath not the potter power over the clay, of the same lump, to make one vessel unto honour, and another unto dishonour?

22.text: What if God, willing to shew his wrath, and to make his power known, endured with much patience vessels of wrath, fitted for destruction,

23.text: That he might shew the riches of his glory on the vessels of mercy, which he hath prepared unto glory?

24.text: Even us, whom also he hath called, nor only of the Jews, but also of the Gentiles.

25.text: As in Osee he saith: I will call that which was not my people, my people; and her that was not beloved, beloved; and her that had not obtained mercy, one that hath obtained mercy.

26.text: And it shall be, in the place where it was said unto them, You are not my people; there they shall be called the sons of the living God.

27.text: And Isaias crieth out concerning Israel: If the number of the children of Israel be as the sand of the sea, a remnant shall be saved.

28.text: For he shall finish his word, and cut it short in justice; because a short word shall the Lord make upon the earth.

29.text: And as Isaias foretold: Unless the Lord of Sabaoth had left us a seed, we had been made as Sodom, and we had been like unto Gomorrha.

30.text: What then shall we say? That the Gentiles, who followed not after justice, have attained to justice, even the justice that is of faith.

31.text: But Israel, by following after the law of justice, is not come unto the law of justice.

32.text: Why so? Because they sought it not by faith, but as it were of works. For they stumbled at the stumblingstone.

33.text: As it is written: Behold I lay in Sion a stumblingstone and a rock of scandal; and whosoever believeth in him shall not be confounded.

1.text: Brethren, the will of my heart, indeed, and my prayer to God, is for them unto salvation.

2.text: For I bear them witness, that they have a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge.

3.text: For they, not knowing the justice of God, and seeking to establish their own, have not submitted themselves to the justice of God.

4.text: For the end of the law is Christ, unto justice to every one that believeth.

5.text: For Moses wrote, that the justice which is of the law, the man that shall do it, shall live by it.

6.text: But the justice which is of faith, speaketh thus: Say not in thy heart, Who shall ascend into heaven? that is, to bring Christ down;

7.text: Or who shall descend into the deep? that is, to bring up Christ again from the dead.

8.text: But what saith the scripture? The word is nigh thee, even in thy mouth, and in thy heart. This is the word of faith, which we preach.

9.text: For if thou confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and believe in thy heart that God hath raised him up from the dead, thou shalt be saved.

10.text: For, with the heart, we believe unto justice; but, with the mouth, confession is made unto salvation.

11.text: For the scripture saith: Whosoever believeth in him, shall not be confounded.

12.text: For there is no distinction of the Jew and the Greek: for the same is Lord over all, rich unto all that call upon him.

13.text: For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord, shall be saved.

14.text: How then shall they call on him, in whom they have not believed? Or how shall they believe him, of whom they have not heard? And how shall they hear, without a preacher?

15.text: And how shall they preach unless they be sent, as it is written: How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace, of them that bring glad tidings of good things!

16.text: But all do not obey the gospel. For Isaias saith: Lord, who hath believed our report?

17.text: Faith then cometh by hearing; and hearing by the word of Christ.

18.text: But I say: Have they not heard? Yes, verily, their sound hath gone forth into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the whole world.

19.text: But I say: Hath not Israel known? First, Moses saith: I will provoke you to jealousy by that which is not a nation; by a foolish nation I will anger you.

20.text: But Isaias is bold, and saith: I was found by them that did not seek me: I appeared openly to them that asked not after me.

21.text: But to Israel he saith: All the day long have I spread my hands to a people that believeth not, and contradicteth me.

1.text: I say then: Hath God cast away his people? God forbid. For I also am an Israelite of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.

2.text: God hath not cast away his people, which he foreknew. Know you not what the scripture saith of Elias; how he calleth on God against Israel?

3.text: Lord, they have slain thy prophets, they have dug down thy altars; and I am left alone, and they seek my life.

4.text: But what saith the divine answer to him? I have left me seven thousand men, that have not bowed their knees to Baal.

5.text: Even so then at this present time also, there is a remnant saved according to the election of grace.

6.text: And if by grace, it is not now by works: otherwise grace is no more grace.

7.text: What then? That which Israel sought, he hath not obtained: but the election hath obtained it; and the rest have been blinded.

8.text: As it is written: God hath given them the spirit of insensibility; eyes that they should not see; and ears that they should not hear, until this present day.

9.text: And David saith: Let their table be made a snare, and a trap, and a stumbling block, and a recompense unto them.

10.text: And David saith: Let their table be made a snare, and a trap, and a stumbling block, and a recompense unto them.

11.text: I say then, have they so stumbled, that they should fall? God forbid. But by their offence, salvation is come to the Gentiles, that they may be emulous of them.

12.text: Now if the offence of them be the riches of the world, and the diminution of them, the riches of the Gentiles; how much more the fulness of them?

13.text: For I say to you, Gentiles: as long indeed as I am the apostle of the Gentiles, I will honour my ministry,

14.text: If, by any means, I may provoke to emulation them who are my flesh, and may save some of them.

15.text: For if the loss of them be the reconciliation of the world, what shall the receiving of them be, but life from the dead?

16.text: For if the firstfruit be holy, so is the lump also: and if the root be holy, so are the branches.

17.text: And if some of the branches be broken, and thou, being a wild olive, art ingrafted in them, and art made partaker of the root, and of the fatness of the olive tree,

18.text: Boast not against the branches. But if thou boast, thou bearest not the root, but the root thee.

19.text: Thou wilt say then: The branches were broken off, that I might be grafted in.

20.text: Well: because of unbelief they were broken off. But thou standest by faith: be not highminded, but fear.

21.text: For if God hath not spared the natural branches, fear lest perhaps he also spare not thee.

22.text: See then the goodness and the severity of God: towards them indeed that are fallen, the severity; but towards thee, the goodness of God, if thou abide in goodness, otherwise thou also shalt be cut off.

23.text: And they also, if they abide not still in unbelief, shall be grafted in: for God is able to graft them in again.

24.text: For if thou wert cut out of the wild olive tree, which is natural to thee; and, contrary to nature, were grafted into the good olive tree; how much more shall they that are the natural branches, be grafted into their own olive tree?

25.text: For I would not have you ignorant, brethren, of this mystery, (lest you should be wise in your own conceits), that blindness in part has happened in Israel, until the fulness of the Gentiles should come in.

26.text: And so all Israel should be saved, as it is written: There shall come out of Sion, he that shall deliver, and shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob.

27.text: And this is to them my covenant: when I shall take away their sins.

28.text: As concerning the gospel, indeed, they are enemies for your sake: but as touching the election, they are most dear for the sake of the fathers.

29.text: For the gifts and the calling of God are without repentance.

30.text: For as you also in times past did not believe God, but now have obtained mercy, through their unbelief;

31.text: So these also now have not believed, for your mercy, that they also may obtain mercy.

32.text: For God hath concluded all in unbelief, that he may have mercy on all.

33.text: O the depth of the riches of the wisdom and of the knowledge of God! How incomprehensible are his judgments, and how unsearchable his ways!

34.text: For who hath known the mind of the Lord? Or who hath been his counsellor?

35.text: Or who hath first given to him, and recompense shall be made him?

36.text: For of him, and by him, and in him, are all things: to him be glory for ever. Amen.

1.text: I BESEECH you therefore, brethren, by the mercy of God, that you present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, pleasing unto God, your reasonable service.

2.text: And be not conformed to this world; but be reformed in the newness of your mind, that you may prove what is the good, and the acceptable, and the perfect will of God.

3.text: For I say, by the grace that is given me, to all that are among you, not to be more wise than it behoveth to be wise, but to be wise unto sobriety, and according as God hath divided to every one the measure of faith.

4.text: For as in one body we have many members, but all the members have not the same office:

5.text: So we being many, are one body in Christ, and every one members one of another.

6.text: And having different gifts, according to the grace that is given us, either prophecy, to be used according to the rule of faith;

7.text: Or ministry, in ministering; or he that teacheth, in doctrine;

8.text: He that exhorteth, in exhorting; he that giveth, with simplicity; he that ruleth, with carefulness; he that sheweth mercy, with cheerfulness.

9.text: Let love be without dissimulation. Hating that which is evil, cleaving to that which is good.

10.text: Loving one another with the charity of brotherhood, with honour preventing one another.

11.text: In carefulness not slothful. In spirit fervent. Serving the Lord.

12.text: Rejoicing in hope. Patient in tribulation. Instant in prayer.

13.text: Communicating to the necessities of the saints. Pursuing hospitality.

15.text: Rejoice with them that rejoice; weep with them that weep.

16.text: Being of one mind one towards another. Not minding high things, but consenting to the humble. Be not wise in your own conceits.

17.text: To no man rendering evil for evil. Providing good things, not only in the sight of God, but also in the sight of all men.

18.text: If it be possible, as much as is in you, have peace with all men.

19.text: Revenge not yourselves, my dearly beloved; but give place unto wrath, for it is written: Revenge is mine, I will repay, saith the Lord.

20.text: But if thy enemy be hungry, give him to eat; if he thirst, give him to drink. For, doing this, thou shalt heap coals of fire upon his head.

21.text: Be not overcome by evil, but overcome evil by good.

1.text: Let every soul be subject to higher powers: for there is no power but from God: and those that are, are ordained of God.

2.text: Therefore he that resisteth the power, resisteth the ordinance of God. And they that resist, purchase to themselves damnation.

3.text: For princes are not a terror to the good work, but to the evil. Wilt thou then not be afraid of the power? Do that which is good: and thou shalt have praise from the same.

4.text: For he is God’s minister to thee, for good. But if thou do that which is evil, fear: for he beareth not the sword in vain. For he is God’s minister: an avenger to execute wrath upon him that doth evil.

5.text: Wherefore be subject of necessity, not only for wrath, but also for conscience’ sake.

6.text: For therefore also you pay tribute. For they are the ministers of God, serving unto this purpose.

7.text: Render therefore to all men their dues. Tribute, to whom tribute is due: custom, to whom custom: fear, to whom fear: honour, to whom honour.

8.text: Owe no man any thing, but to love one another. For he that loveth his neighbour, hath fulfilled the law.

9.text: For Thou shalt not commit adultery: Thou shalt not kill: Thou shalt not steal, Thou shalt not bear false witness: Thou shalt not covet: and if there be any other commandment, it is comprised in this word, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.

10.text: The love of our neighbour worketh no evil. Love therefore is the fulfilling of the law.

11.text: And that knowing the season; that it is now the hour for us to rise from sleep. For now our salvation is nearer than when we believed.

12.text: The night is passed, and the day is at hand. Let us therefore cast off the works of darkness, and put on the armour of light.

13.text: Let us walk honestly, as in the day: not in rioting and drunkenness, not in chambering and impurities, not in contention and envy:

14.text: But put ye on the Lord Jesus Christ, and make not provision for the flesh in its concupiscences.

1.text: Now him that is weak in faith, take unto you: not in disputes about thoughts.

2.text: For one believeth that he may eat all things: but he that is weak, let him eat herbs.

3.text: Let not him that eateth, despise him that eateth not: and he that eateth not, let him not judge him that eateth. For God hath taken him to him.

4.text: Who art thou that judgest another man’s servant? To his own lord he standeth or falleth. And he shall stand: for God is able to make him stand.

5.text: For one judgeth between day and day: and another judgeth every day: let every man abound in his own sense.

6.text: He that regardeth the day, regardeth it unto the Lord. And he that eateth, eateth to the Lord: for he giveth thanks to God. And he that eateth not, to the Lord he eateth not, and giveth thanks to God.

7.text: For none of us liveth to himself; and no man dieth to himself.

8.text: For whether we live, we live unto the Lord; or whether we die, we die unto the Lord. Therefore, whether we live, or whether we die, we are the Lord’s.

10.text: But thou, why judgest thou thy brother? or thou, why dost thou despise thy brother? For we shall all stand before the judgment seat of Christ.

11.text: For it is written: As I live, saith the Lord, every knee shall bow to me, and every tongue shall confess to God.

12.text: Therefore every one of us shall render account to God for himself.

13.text: Let us not therefore judge one another any more. But judge this rather, that you put not a stumblingblock or a scandal in your brother’s way.

14.text: Let us not therefore judge one another any more. But judge this rather, that you put not a stumblingblock or a scandal in your brother’s way.

15.text: For if, because of thy meat, thy brother be grieved, thou walkest not now according to charity. Destroy not him with thy meat, for whom Christ died.

16.text: Let not then our good be evil spoken of.

17.text: For the kingdom of God is not meat and drink; but justice, and peace, and joy in the Holy Ghost.

18.text: For he that in this serveth Christ, pleaseth God, and is approved of men.

19.text: Therefore let us follow after the things that are of peace; and keep the things that are of edification one towards another.

20.text: Destroy not the work of God for meat. All things indeed are clean: but it is evil for that man who eateth with offence.

21.text: It is good not to eat flesh, and not to drink wine, nor any thing whereby thy brother is offended, or scandalized, or made weak.

22.text: Hast thou faith? Have it to thyself before God. Blessed is he that condemneth not himself in that which he alloweth.

23.text: But he that discerneth, if he eat, is condemned; because not of faith. For all that is not of faith is sin.

1.text: Now we that are stronger, ought to bear the infirmities of the weak, and not to please ourselves.

2.text: Let every one of you please his neighbour unto good, to edification.

3.text: For Christ did not please himself, but as it is written: The reproaches of them that reproached thee, fell upon me.

4.text: For what things soever were written, were written for our learning: that through patience and the comfort of the scriptures, we might have hope.

5.text: Now the God of patience and of comfort grant you to be of one mind one towards another, according to Jesus Christ:

6.text: That with one mind, and with one mouth, you may glorify God and the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.

7.text: Wherefore receive one another, as Christ also hath received you unto the honour of God.

8.text: For I say that Christ Jesus was minister of the circumcision for the truth of God, to confirm the promises made unto the fathers.

9.text: But that the Gentiles are to glorify God for his mercy, as it is written: Therefore will I confess to thee, O Lord, among the Gentiles, and will sing to thy name.

10.text: And again he saith: Rejoice, ye Gentiles, with his people.

11.text: And again: Praise the Lord, all ye Gentiles; and magnify him, all ye people.

12.text: And again Isaias saith: There shall be a root of Jesse; and he that shall rise up to rule the Gentiles, in him the Gentiles shall hope.

13.text: Now the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing; that you may abound in hope, and in the power of the Holy Ghost.

14.text: And I myself also, my brethren, am assured of you, that you also are full of love, replenished with all knowledge, so that you are able to admonish one another.

15.text: But I have written to you, brethren, more boldly in some sort, as it were putting you in mind: because of the grace which is given me from God.

16.text: That I should be the minister of Christ Jesus among the Gentiles; sanctifying the gospel of God, that the oblation of the Gentiles may be made acceptable and sanctified in the Holy Ghost.

17.text: I have therefore glory in Christ Jesus towards God.

18.text: For I dare not to speak of any of those things which Christ worketh not by me, for the obedience of the Gentiles, by word and deed,

19.text: By the virtue of signs and wonders, in the power of the Holy Ghost, so that from Jerusalem round about as far as unto Illyricum, I have replenished the gospel of Christ.

20.text: And I have so preached this gospel, not where Christ was named, lest I should build upon another man’s foundation.

21.text: But as it is written: They to whom he was not spoken of, shall see, and they that have not heard shall understand.

22.text: For which cause also I was hindered very much from coming to you, and have been kept away till now.

23.text: But now having no more place in these countries, and having a great desire these many years past to come unto you,

24.text: When I shall begin to take my journey into Spain, I hope that as I pass, I shall see you, and be brought on my way thither by you, if first, in part, I shall have enjoyed you:

25.text: But now I shall go to Jerusalem, to minister unto the saints.

26.text: For it hath pleased them of Macedonia and Achaia to make a contribution for the poor of the saints that are in Jerusalem.

27.text: For it hath pleased them; and they are their debtors. For if the Gentiles have been made partakers of their spiritual things, they ought also in carnal things to minister to them.

28.text: When therefore I shall have accomplished this, and consigned to them this fruit, I will come by you into Spain.

29.text: And I know, that when I come to you, I shall come in the abundance of the blessing of the gospel of Christ.

30.text: I beseech you therefore, brethren, through our Lord Jesus Christ, and by the charity of the Holy Ghost, that you help me in your prayers for me to God,

31.text: That I may be delivered from the unbelievers that are in Judea, and that the oblation of my service may be acceptable in Jerusalem to the saints.

32.text: That I may come to you with joy, by the will of God, and may be refreshed with you.

33.text: Now the God of peace be with you all. Amen.

1.text: And I commend to you Phebe, our sister, who is in the ministry of the church, that is in Cenchrae:

2.text: That you receive her in the Lord as becometh saints; and that you assist her in whatsoever business she shall have need of you. For she also hath assisted many, and myself also.

3.text: Salute Prisca and Aquila, my helpers in Christ Jesus,

4.text: (Who have for my life laid down their own necks: to whom not I only give thanks, but also all the churches of the Gentiles,)

5.text: And the church which is in their house. Salute Epenetus, my beloved: who is the firstfruits of Asia in Christ.

6.text: Salute Mary, who hath laboured much among you.

7.text: Salute Andronicus and Junias, my kinsmen and fellow prisoners: who are of note among the apostles, who also were in Christ before me.

8.text: Salute Ampliatus, most beloved to me in the Lord.

9.text: Salute Urbanus, our helper in Christ Jesus, and Stachys, my beloved.

10.text: Salute Urbanus, our helper in Christ Jesus, and Stachys, my beloved. Salute them that are of Aristobulus’ household. Salute Herodian, my kinsman. Salute them that are of Narcissus’ household, who are in the Lord.

11.text: Salute them that are of Aristobulus’ household. Salute Herodian, my kinsman. Salute them that are of Narcissus’ household, who are in the Lord.

12.text: Salute Tryphaena and Tryphosa, who labour in the Lord. Salute Persis, the dearly beloved, who hath much laboured in the Lord.

13.text: Salute Rufus, elect in the Lord, and his mother and mine.

14.text: Salute Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermas, Patrobas, Hermes, and the brethren that are with them.

15.text: Salute Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympias; and all the saints that are with them.

16.text: Salute one another with an holy kiss. All the churches of Christ salute you.

17.text: Now I beseech you, brethren, to mark them who make dissensions and offences contrary to the doctrine which you have learned, and avoid them.

18.text: For they that are such, serve not Christ our Lord, but their own belly; and by pleasing speeches and good words, seduce the hearts of the innocent.

19.text: For your obedience is published in every place. I rejoice therefore in you. But I would have you to be wise in good, and simple in evil.

20.text: And the God of peace crush Satan under your feet speedily. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.

21.text: Timothy, my fellow labourer, saluteth you, and Lucius, and Jason, and Sosipater, my kinsmen.

22.text: I Tertius, who wrote this epistle, salute you in the Lord.

23.text: Caius, my host, and the whole church, saluteth you. Erastus, the treasurer of the city, saluteth you, and Quartus, a brother.

24.text: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.

25.text: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.

26.text: (Which now is made manifest by the scriptures of the prophets, according to the precept of the eternal God, for the obedience of faith,) known among all nations;

27.text: To God the only wise, through Jesus Christ, to whom be honour and glory for ever and ever. Amen.

1.text: Paul, called to be an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and Sosthenes a brother,

2.text: To the church of God that is at Corinth, to them that are sanctified in Christ Jesus, called to be saints, with all that invoke the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, in every place of theirs and ours.

3.text: Grace to you, and peace from God our Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ.

4.text: I give thanks to my God always for you, for the grace of God that is given you in Christ Jesus,

5.text: That in all things you are made rich in him, in all utterance, and in all knowledge;

6.text: As the testimony of Christ was confirmed in you,

7.text: So that nothing is wanting to you in any grace, waiting for the manifestation of our Lord Jesus Christ.

8.text: Who also will confirm you unto the end without crime, in the day of the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.

9.text: God is faithful: by whom you are called unto the fellowship of his Son Jesus Christ our Lord.

10.text: Now I beseech you, brethren, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you all speak the same thing, and that there be no schisms among you; but that you be perfect in the same mind, and in the same judgment.

11.text: For it hath been signified unto me, my brethren, of you, by them that are of the house of Chloe, that there are contentions among you.

12.text: Now this I say, that every one of you saith: I indeed am of Paul; and I am of Apollo; and I am of Cephas; and I of Christ.

13.text: Is Christ divided? Was Paul then crucified for you? or were you baptized in the name of Paul?

14.text: I give God thanks, that I baptized none of you but Crispus and Caius;

15.text: Lest any should say that you were baptized in my name.

16.text: And I baptized also the household of Stephanus; besides, I know not whether I baptized any other.

17.text: For Christ sent me not to baptize, but to preach the gospel: not in wisdom of speech, lest the cross of Christ should be made void.

18.text: For the word of the cross, to them indeed that perish, is foolishness; but to them that are saved, that is, to us, it is the power of God.

19.text: For it is written: I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and the prudence of the prudent I will reject.

20.text: Where is the wise? Where is the scribe? Where is the disputer of this world? Hath not God made foolish the wisdom of this world?

21.text: For seeing that in the wisdom of God the world, by wisdom, knew not God, it pleased God, by the foolishness of our preaching, to save them that believe.

22.text: For both the Jews require signs, and the Greeks seek after wisdom:

23.text: But we preach Christ crucified, unto the Jews indeed a stumblingblock, and unto the Gentiles foolishness:

24.text: But unto them that are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God, and the wisdom of God.

25.text: For the foolishness of God is wiser than men; and the weakness of God is stronger than men.

26.text: For see your vocation, brethren, that there are not many wise according to the flesh, not many mighty, not many noble:

27.text: But the foolish things of the world hath God chosen, that he may confound the wise; and the weak things of the world hath God chosen, that he may confound the strong.

28.text: And the base things of the world, and the things that are contemptible, hath God chosen, and things that are not, that he might bring to nought things that are:

29.text: That no flesh should glory in his sight.

30.text: But of him are you in Christ Jesus, who of God is made unto us wisdom, and justice, and sanctification, and redemption:

31.text: That, as it is written: He that glorieth, may glory in the Lord.

1.text: And I, brethren, when I came to you, came not in loftiness of speech or of wisdom, declaring unto you the testimony of Christ.

2.text: For I judged not myself to know anything among you, but Jesus Christ, and him crucified.

3.text: And I was with you in weakness, and in fear, and in much trembling.

4.text: And my speech and my preaching was not in the persuasive words of human wisdom, but in shewing of the Spirit and power;

5.text: That your faith might not stand on the wisdom of men, but on the power of God.

6.text: Howbeit we speak wisdom among the perfect: yet not the wisdom of this world, neither of the princes of this world that come to nought;

7.text: But we speak the wisdom of God in a mystery, a wisdom which is hidden, which God ordained before the world, unto our glory:

8.text: Which none of the princes of this world knew; for if they had known it, they would never have crucified the Lord of glory.

9.text: But, as it is written: That eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither hath it entered into the heart of man, what things God hath prepared for them that love him.

10.text: But to us God hath revealed them, by his Spirit. For the Spirit searcheth all things, yea, the deep things of God.

11.text: For what man knoweth the things of a man, but the spirit of a man that is in him? So the things also that are of God no man knoweth, but the Spirit of God.

12.text: Now we have received not the spirit of this world, but the Spirit that is of God; that we may know the things that are given us from God.

13.text: Which things also we speak, not in the learned words of human wisdom; but in the doctrine of the Spirit, comparing spiritual things with spiritual.

15.text: But the spiritual man judgeth all things; and he himself is judged of no man.

16.text: For who hath known the mind of the Lord, that we may instruct him? But we have the mind of Christ.

1.text: And I, brethren, could not speak to you as unto spiritual, but as unto carnal. As unto little ones in Christ,

2.text: I gave you milk to drink, not meat; for you were not able as yet. But neither indeed are you now able; for you are yet carnal.

3.text: For, whereas there is among you envying and contention, are you not carnal, and walk according to man?

4.text: For while one saith, I indeed am of Paul; and another, I am of Apollo; are you not men? What then is Apollo, and what is Paul?

5.text: The ministers of him whom you have believed; and to every one as the Lord hath given.

6.text: I have planted, Apollo watered, but God gave the increase.

7.text: Therefore, neither he that planteth is any thing, nor he that watereth; but God that giveth the increase.

8.text: Now he that planteth, and he that watereth, are one. And every man shall receive his own reward, according to his own labour.

9.text: For we are God’s coadjutors: you are God’s husbandry; you are God’s building.

10.text: According to the grace of God that is given to me, as a wise architect, I have laid the foundation; and another buildeth thereon. But let every man take heed how he buildeth thereupon.

11.text: For other foundation no man can lay, but that which is laid; which is Christ Jesus.

12.text: Now if any man build upon this foundation, gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, stubble:

13.text: Every man’s work shall be manifest; for the day of the Lord shall declare it, because it shall be revealed in fire; and the fire shall try every man’s work, of what sort it is.

14.text: If any man’s work abide, which he hath built thereupon, he shall receive a reward.

15.text: If any man’s work burn, he shall suffer loss; but he himself shall be saved, yet so as by fire.

16.text: Know you not, that you are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwelleth in you?

17.text: But if any man violate the temple of God, him shall God destroy. For the temple of God is holy, which you are.

18.text: Let no man deceive himself: if any man among you seem to be wise in this world, let him become a fool, that he may be wise.

19.text: For the wisdom of this world is foolishness with God. For it is written: I will catch the wise in their own craftiness.

20.text: And again: The Lord knoweth the thoughts of the wise, that they are vain.

21.text: Let no man therefore glory in men.

22.text: For all things are yours, whether it be Paul, or Apollo, or Cephas, or the world, or life, or death, or things present, or things to come; for all are yours;

23.text: And you are Christ’s; and Christ is God’s.

1.text: Let a man so account of us as of the ministers of Christ, and the dispensers of the mysteries of God.

2.text: Here now it is required among the dispensers, that a man be found faithful.

3.text: But to me it is a very small thing to be judged by you, or by man’s day; but neither do I judge my own self.

4.text: For I am not conscious to myself of any thing, yet am I not hereby justified; but he that judgeth me, is the Lord.

5.text: Therefore judge not before the time; until the Lord come, who both will bring to light the hidden things of darkness, and will make manifest the counsels of the hearts; and then shall every man have praise from God.

6.text: But these things, brethren, I have in a figure transferred to myself and to Apollo, for your sakes; that in us you may learn, that one be not puffed up against the other for another, above that which is written.

7.text: For who distinguisheth thee? Or what hast thou that thou hast not received? And if thou hast received, why dost thou glory, as if thou hadst not received it?

8.text: You are now full; you are now become rich; you reign without us; and I would to God you did reign, that we also might reign with you.

9.text: For I think that God hath set forth us apostles, the last, as it were men appointed to death: we are made a spectacle to the world, and to angels, and to men.

10.text: We are fools for Christ’s sake, but you are wise in Christ; we are weak, but you are strong; you are honourable, but we without honour.

11.text: Even unto this hour we both hunger and thirst, and are naked, and are buffeted, and have no fixed abode;

12.text: And we labour, working with our own hands: we are reviled, and we bless; we are persecuted, and we suffer it.

13.text: We are blasphemed, and we entreat; we are made as the refuse of this world, the offscouring of all even until now.

14.text: I write not these things to confound you; but I admonish you as my dearest children.

15.text: For if you have ten thousand instructors in Christ, yet not many fathers. For in Christ Jesus, by the gospel, I have begotten you.

16.text: Wherefore I beseech you, be ye followers of me, as I also am of Christ.

17.text: For this cause have I sent to you Timothy, who is my dearest son and faithful in the Lord; who will put you in mind of my ways, which are in Christ Jesus; as I teach everywhere in every church.

18.text: As if I would not come to you, so some are puffed up.

19.text: But I will come to you shortly, if the Lord will: and will know, not the speech of them that are puffed up, but the power.

20.text: For the kingdom of God is not in speech, but in power.

21.text: What will you? shall I come to you with a rod; or in charity, and in the spirit of meekness?

1.text: It is absolutely heard, that there is fornication among you, and such fornication as the like is not among the heathens; that one should have his father’s wife.

2.text: And you are puffed up; and have not rather mourned, that he might be taken away from among you, that hath done this deed.

3.text: I indeed, absent in body, but present in spirit, have already judged, as though I were present, him that hath so done,

4.text: In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, you being gathered together, and my spirit, with the power of our Lord Jesus;

5.text: To deliver such a one to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, that the spirit may be saved in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.

6.text: Your glorying is not good. Know you not that a little leaven corrupteth the whole lump?

7.text: Purge out the old leaven, that you may be a new paste, as you are unleavened. For Christ our pasch is sacrificed.

8.text: Therefore let us feast, not with the old leaven, nor with the leaven of malice and wickedness; but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.

9.text: I wrote to you in an epistle, not to keep company with fornicators.

10.text: I mean not with the fornicators of this world, or with the covetous, or the extortioners, or the servers of idols; otherwise you must needs go out of this world.

11.text: But now I have written to you, not to keep company, if any man that is named a brother, be a fornicator, or covetous, or a server of idols, or a railer, or a drunkard, or an extortioner: with such a one, not so much as to eat.

12.text: For what have I to do to judge them that are without? Do not you judge them that are within?

13.text: For them that are without, God will judge. Put away the evil one from among yourselves.

1.text: Dare any of you, having a matter against another, go to be judged before the unjust, and not before the saints?

2.text: Know you not that the saints shall judge this world? And if the world shall be judged by you, are you unworthy to judge the smallest matters?

3.text: Know you not that we shall judge angels? how much more things of this world?

4.text: If therefore you have judgments of things pertaining to this world, set them to judge, who are the most despised in the church.

5.text: I speak to your shame. Is it so that there is not among you any one wise man, that is able to judge between his brethren?

6.text: But brother goeth to law with brother, and that before unbelievers.

7.text: Already indeed there is plainly a fault among you, that you have lawsuits one with another. Why do you not rather take wrong? Why do you not rather suffer yourselves to be defrauded?

8.text: But you do wrong and defraud, and that to your brethren.

9.text: Know you not that the unjust shall not possess the kingdom of God? Do not err: neither fornicators, nor idolaters, nor adulterers,

10.text: Nor the effeminate, nor liers with mankind, nor thieves, nor covetous, nor drunkards, nor railers, nor extortioners, shall possess the kingdom of God.

11.text: And such some of you were; but you are washed, but you are sanctified, but you are justified in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, and the Spirit of our God.

12.text: All things are lawful to me, but all things are not expedient. All things are lawful to me, but I will not be brought under the power of any.

13.text: Meat for the belly, and the belly for the meats; but God shall destroy both it and them: but the body is not for fornication, but for the Lord, and the Lord for the body.

14.text: Now God hath both raised up the Lord, and will raise us up also by his power.

15.text: Know you not that your bodies are the members of Christ? Shall I then take the members of Christ, and make them the members of an harlot? God forbid.

16.text: Know you not that your bodies are the members of Christ? Shall I then take the members of Christ, and make them the members of an harlot? God forbid.

17.text: But he who is joined to the Lord, is one spirit.

18.text: Fly fornication. Every sin that a man doth, is without the body; but he that committeth fornication, sinneth against his own body.

19.text: Or know you not, that your members are the temple of the Holy Ghost, who is in you, whom you have from God; and you are not your own?

20.text: For you are bought with a great price. Glorify and bear God in your body.

1.text: Now concerning the thing whereof you wrote to me: It is good for a man not to touch a woman.

2.text: But for fear of fornication, let every man have his own wife, and let every woman have her own husband.

3.text: Let the husband render the debt to his wife, and the wife also in like manner to the husband.

4.text: The wife hath not power of her own body, but the husband. And in like manner the husband also hath not power of his own body, but the wife.

5.text: Defraud not one another, except, perhaps, by consent, for a time, that you may give yourselves to prayer; and return together again, lest Satan tempt you for your incontinency.

6.text: But I speak this by indulgence, not by commandment.

7.text: For I would that all men were even as myself: but every one hath his proper gift from God; one after this manner, and another after that.

8.text: But I say to the unmarried, and to the widows: It is good for them if they so continue, even as I.

9.text: But if they do not contain themselves, let them marry. For it is better to marry than to be burnt.

10.text: But to them that are married, not I but the Lord commandeth, that the wife depart not from her husband.

11.text: And if she depart, that she remain unmarried, or be reconciled to her husband. And let not the husband put away his wife.

12.text: For to the rest I speak, not the Lord. If any brother hath a wife that believeth not, and she consent to dwell with him, let him not put her away.

13.text: And if any woman hath a husband that believeth not, and he consent to dwell with her, let her not put away her husband.

14.text: For the unbelieving husband is sanctified by the believing wife; and the unbelieving wife is sanctified by the believing husband: otherwise your children should be unclean; but now they are holy.

15.text: But if the unbeliever depart, let him depart. For a brother or sister is not under servitude in such cases. But God hath called us in peace.

16.text: For how knowest thou, O wife, whether thou shalt save thy husband? Or how knowest thou, O man, whether thou shalt save thy wife?

17.text: But as the Lord hath distributed to every one, as God hath called every one, so let him walk: and so in all churches I teach.

18.text: Is any man called, being circumcised? let him not procure uncircumcision. Is any man called in uncircumcision? let him not be circumcised.

19.text: Circumcision is nothing, and uncircumcision is nothing: but the observance of the commandments of God.

20.text: Let every man abide in the same calling in which he was called.

21.text: Wast thou called, being a bondman? care not for it; but if thou mayest be made free, use it rather.

22.text: For he that is called in the Lord, being a bondman, is the freeman of the Lord. Likewise he that is called, being free, is the bondman of Christ.

23.text: You are bought with a price; be not made the bondslaves of men.

24.text: Brethren, let every man, wherein he was called, therein abide with God.

25.text: Now concerning virgins, I have no commandment of the Lord; but I give counsel, as having obtained mercy of the Lord, to be faithful.

26.text: I think therefore that this is good for the present necessity, that it is good for a man so to be.

27.text: Art thou bound to a wife? seek not to be loosed. Art thou loosed from a wife? seek not a wife.

28.text: But if thou take a wife, thou hast not sinned. And if a virgin marry, she hath not sinned: nevertheless, such shall have tribulation of the flesh. But I spare you.

29.text: This therefore I say, brethren; the time is short; it remaineth, that they also who have wives, be as if they had none;

30.text: And they that weep, as though they wept not; and they that rejoice, as if they rejoiced not; and they that buy, as though they possessed not;

31.text: And they that use this world, as if they used it not: for the fashion of this world passeth away.

32.text: But I would have you to be without solicitude. He that is without a wife, is solicitous for the things that belong to the Lord, how he may please God.

33.text: But he that is with a wife, is solicitous for the things of the world, how he may please his wife: and he is divided.

34.text: And the unmarried woman and the virgin thinketh on the things of the Lord, that she may be holy both in body and in spirit. But she that is married thinketh on the things of the world, how she may please her husband.

35.text: And this I speak for your profit: not to cast a snare upon you; but for that which is decent, and which may give you power to attend upon the Lord, without impediment.

36.text: But if any man think that he seemeth dishonoured, with regard to his virgin, for that she is above the age, and it must so be: let him do what he will; he sinneth not, if she marry.

37.text: For he that hath determined being steadfast in his heart, having no necessity, but having power of his own will; and hath judged this in his heart, to keep his virgin, doth well.

38.text: Therefore, both he that giveth his virgin in marriage, doth well; and he that giveth her not, doth better.

39.text: A woman is bound by the law as long as her husband liveth; but if her husband die, she is at liberty: let her marry to whom she will; only in the Lord.

40.text: But more blessed shall she be, if she so remain, according to my counsel; and I think that I also have the spirit of God.

1.text: Now concerning those things that are sacrificed to idols, we know that we all have knowledge. Knowledge puffeth up; but charity edifieth.

2.text: And if any man think that he knoweth any thing, he hath not yet known as he ought to know.

3.text: But if any man love God, the same is known by him.

4.text: But as for the meats that are sacrificed to idols, we know that an idol is nothing in the world, and that there is no God but one.

5.text: For although there be that are called gods, either in heaven or on earth (for there be gods many, and lords many).

6.text: Yet to us there is but one God, the Father, of whom are all things, and we unto him; and one Lord Jesus Christ, by whom are all things, and we by him.

7.text: But there is not knowledge in every one. For some until this present, with conscience of the idol: eat as a thing sacrificed to an idol, and their conscience, being weak, is defiled.

8.text: But meat doth not commend us to God. For neither, if we eat, shall we have the more; nor, if we eat not, shall we have the less.

9.text: But take heed lest perhaps this your liberty become a stumblingblock to the weak.

10.text: For if a man see him that hath knowledge sit at meat in the idol’s temple, shall not his conscience, being weak, be emboldened to eat those things which are sacrificed to idols?

11.text: And through thy knowledge shall the weak brother perish, for whom Christ hath died?

12.text: Now when you sin thus against the brethren, and wound their weak conscience, you sin against Christ.

13.text: Wherefore, if meat scandalize my brother, I will never eat flesh, lest I should scandalize my brother.

1.text: Am not I free? Am not I an apostle? Have not I seen Christ Jesus our Lord? Are not you my work in the Lord?

2.text: And if unto others I be not an apostle, but yet to you I am. For you are the seal of my apostleship in the Lord.

3.text: My defence with them that do examine me is this.

4.text: Have not we power to eat and to drink?

5.text: Have we not power to carry about a woman, a sister, as well as the rest of the apostles, and the brethren of the Lord, and Cephas?

6.text: Or I only and Barnabas, have not we power to do this?

7.text: Who serveth as a soldier at any time, at his own charges? Who planteth a vineyard, and eateth not of the fruit thereof? Who feedeth the flock, and eateth not of the milk of the flock?

8.text: Speak I these things according to man? Or doth not the law also say these things?

9.text: For it is written in the law of Moses: Thou shalt not muzzle the mouth of the ox that treadeth out the corn. Doth God take care for oxen?

10.text: Or doth he say this indeed for our sakes? For these things are written for our sakes: that he that plougheth, should plough in hope; and he that thrasheth, in hope to receive fruit.

11.text: If we have sown unto you spiritual things, is it a great matter if we reap your carnal things?

12.text: If others be partakers of this power over you, why not we rather? Nevertheless, we have not used this power: but we bear all things, lest we should give any hindrance to the gospel of Christ.

13.text: Know you not, that they who work in the holy place, eat the things that are of the holy place; and they that serve the altar, partake with the altar?

14.text: So also the Lord ordained that they who preach the gospel, should live by the gospel.

15.text: But I have used none of these things. Neither have I written these things, that they should be so done unto me: for it is good for me to die, rather than that any man should make my glory void.

16.text: For if I preach the gospel, it is no glory to me, for a necessity lieth upon me: for woe is unto me if I preach not the gospel.

17.text: For if I do this thing willingly, I have a reward: but if against my will, a dispensation is committed to me:

18.text: What is my reward then? That preaching the gospel, I may deliver the gospel without charge, that I abuse not my power in the gospel.

19.text: For whereas I was free as to all, I made myself the servant of all, that I might gain the more.

20.text: And I became to the Jews, a Jew, that I might gain the Jews:

21.text: To them that are under the law, as if I were under the law, (whereas myself was not under the law,) that I might gain them that were under the law. To them that were without the law, as if I were without the law, (whereas I was not without the law of God, but was in the law of Christ,) that I might gain them that were without the law.

22.text: To the weak I became weak, that I might gain the weak. I became all things to all men, that I might save all.

23.text: And I do all things for the gospel’s sake: that I may be made partaker thereof.

24.text: Know you not that they that run in the race, all run indeed, but one receiveth the prize? So run that you may obtain.

25.text: And every one that striveth for the mastery, refraineth himself from all things: and they indeed that they may receive a corruptible crown; but we an incorruptible one.

26.text: I therefore so run, not as at an uncertainty: I so fight, not as one beating the air:

27.text: But I chastise my body, and bring it into subjection: lest perhaps, when I have preached to others, I myself should become a castaway.

1.text: For I would not have you ignorant, brethren, that our fathers were all under the cloud, and all passed through the sea.

2.text: And all in Moses were baptized, in the cloud, and in the sea:

3.text: And did all eat the same spiritual food,

4.text: And all drank the same spiritual drink; (and they drank of the spiritual rock that followed them, and the rock was Christ.)

5.text: But with most of them God was not well pleased: for they were overthrown in the desert.

6.text: Now these things were done in a figure of us, that we should not covet evil things as they also coveted.

7.text: Neither become ye idolaters, as some of them, as it is written: The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.

8.text: Neither let us commit fornication, as some of them committed fornication, and there fell in one day three and twenty thousand.

9.text: Neither let us tempt Christ: as some of them tempted, and perished by the serpents.

10.text: Neither do you murmur: as some of them murmured, and were destroyed by the destroyer.

11.text: Now all these things happened to them in figure: and they are written for our correction, upon whom the ends of the world are come.

12.text: Wherefore he that thinketh himself to stand, let him take heed lest he fall.

13.text: Let no temptation take hold on you, but such as is human. And God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that which you are able: but will make also with temptation issue, that you may be able to bear it.

14.text: Wherefore, my dearly beloved, fly from the service of idols.

15.text: I speak as to wise men: judge ye yourselves what I say.

16.text: The chalice of benediction, which we bless, is it not the communion of the blood of Christ? And the bread, which we break, is it not the partaking of the body of the Lord?

17.text: For we, being many, are one bread, one body, all that partake of one bread.

18.text: Behold Israel according to the flesh: are not they, that eat of the sacrifices, partakers of the altar?

19.text: What then? Do I say, that what is offered in sacrifice to idols, is any thing? Or, that the idol is any thing?

20.text: But the things which the heathens sacrifice, they sacrifice to devils, and not to God. And I would not that you should be made partakers with devils.

21.text: You cannot drink the chalice of the Lord, and the chalice of devils: you cannot be partakers of the table of the Lord, and of the table of devils.

22.text: Do we provoke the Lord to jealousy? Are we stronger than he? All things are lawful for me, but all things are not expedient.

23.text: All things are lawful for me, but all things do not edify.

24.text: Let no man seek his own, but that which is another’s.

25.text: Whatsoever is sold in the shambles, eat; asking no question for conscience’ sake.

26.text: The earth is the Lord’s, and the fulness thereof.

27.text: If any of them that believe not, invite you, and you will be willing to go; eat of any thing that is set before you, asking no question for conscience’ sake.

28.text: But if any man say: This has been sacrificed to idols, do not eat of it for his sake that told it, and for conscience’ sake.

29.text: Conscience, I say, not thy own, but the other’s. For why is my liberty judged by another man’s conscience?

30.text: If I partake with thanksgiving, why am I evil spoken of, for that for which I give thanks?

31.text: Therefore, whether you eat or drink, or whatsoever else you do, do all to the glory of God.

32.text: Be without offence to the Jews, and to the Gentiles, and to the church of God:

33.text: As I also in all things please all men, not seeking that which is profitable to myself, but to many, that may be saved.

1.text: Be ye followers of me, as I also am of Christ.

2.text: Now I praise you, brethren, that in all things you are mindful of me: and keep my ordinances as I have delivered them to you.

3.text: But I would have you know, that the head of every man is Christ; and the head of the woman is the man; and the head of Christ is God.

4.text: Every man praying or prophesying with his head covered, disgraceth his head.

5.text: But every woman praying or prophesying with her head not covered, disgraceth her head: for it is all one as if she were shaven.

6.text: For if a woman be not covered, let her be shorn. But if it be a shame to a woman to be shorn or made bald, let her cover her head.

7.text: The man indeed ought not to cover his head, because he is the image and glory of God; but the woman is the glory of the man.

8.text: For the man is not of the woman, but the woman of the man.

9.text: For the man was not created for the woman, but the woman for the man.

10.text: Therefore ought the woman to have a power over her head, because of the angels.

11.text: But yet neither is the man without the woman, nor the woman without the man, in the Lord.

12.text: For as the woman is of the man, so also is the man by the woman: but all things of God.

13.text: You yourselves judge: doth it become a woman, to pray unto God uncovered?

14.text: Doth not even nature itself teach you, that a man indeed, if he nourish his hair, it is a shame unto him?

15.text: But if a woman nourish her hair, it is a glory to her; for her hair is given to her for a covering.

16.text: But if any man seem to be contentious, we have no such custom, nor the church of God.

17.text: Now this I ordain: not praising you, that you come together not for the better, but for the worse.

18.text: For first of all I hear that when you come together in the church, there are schisms among you; and in part I believe it.

19.text: For there must be also heresies: that they also, who are approved, may be made manifest among you.

20.text: When you come therefore together into one place, it is not now to eat the Lord’s supper.

21.text: For every one taketh before his own supper to eat. And one indeed is hungry and another is drunk.

22.text: What, have you not houses to eat and to drink in? Or despise ye the church of God; and put them to shame that have not? What shall I say to you? Do I praise you? In this I praise you not.

23.text: For I have received of the Lord that which also I delivered unto you, that the Lord Jesus, the same night in which he was betrayed, took bread.

24.text: And giving thanks, broke, and said: Take ye, and eat: this is my body, which shall be delivered for you: this do for the commemoration of me.

25.text: In like manner also the chalice, after he had supped, saying: This chalice is the new testament in my blood: this do ye, as often as you shall drink, for the commemoration of me.

26.text: For as often as you shall eat this bread, and drink the chalice, you shall shew the death of the Lord, until he come.

27.text: Therefore whosoever shall eat this bread, or drink the chalice of the Lord unworthily, shall be guilty of the body and of the blood of the Lord.

28.text: But let a man prove himself: and so let him eat of that bread, and drink of the chalice.

29.text: For he that eateth and drinketh unworthily, eateth and drinketh judgment to himself, not discerning the body of the Lord.

30.text: Therefore are there many infirm and weak among you, and many sleep.

31.text: But if we would judge ourselves, we should not be judged.

32.text: But whilst we are judged, we are chastised by the Lord, that we be not condemned with this world.

33.text: Wherefore, my brethren, when you come together to eat, wait for one another.

34.text: If any man be hungry, let him eat at home; that you come not together unto judgment. And the rest I will set in order, when I come.

1.text: Now concerning spiritual things, my brethren, I would not have you ignorant.

2.text: You know that when you were heathens, you went to dumb idols, according as you were led.

3.text: Wherefore I give you to understand, that no man, speaking by the Spirit of God, saith Anathema to Jesus. And no man can say the Lord Jesus, but by the Holy Ghost.

4.text: Now there are diversities of graces, but the same Spirit;
