5.text: And there are diversities of ministries, but the same Lord;

6.text: And there are diversities of operations, but the same God, who worketh all in all.

7.text: And the manifestation of the Spirit is given to every man unto profit.

8.text: To one indeed, by the Spirit, is given the word of wisdom: and to another, the word of knowledge, according to the same Spirit;

9.text: To another, faith in the same spirit; to another, the grace of healing in one Spirit;

10.text: To another, the working of miracles; to another, prophecy; to another, the discerning of spirits; to another, diverse kinds of tongues; to another, interpretation of speeches.

11.text: But all these things one and the same Spirit worketh, dividing to every one according as he will.

12.text: For as the body is one, and hath many members; and all the members of the body, whereas they are many, yet are one body, so also is Christ.

13.text: For in one Spirit were we all baptized into one body, whether Jews or Gentiles, whether bond or free; and in one Spirit we have all been made to drink.

14.text: For the body also is not one member, but many.

15.text: If the foot should say, because I am not the hand, I am not of the body; is it therefore not of the body?

16.text: And if the ear should say, because I am not the eye, I am not of the body; is it therefore not of the body?

17.text: If the whole body were the eye, where would be the hearing? If the whole were hearing, where would be the smelling?

18.text: But now God hath set the members every one of them in the body as it hath pleased him.

19.text: And if they all were one member, where would be the body?

20.text: But now there are many members indeed, yet one body.

21.text: And the eye cannot say to the hand: I need not thy help; nor again the head to the feet: I have no need of you.

22.text: Yea, much more those that seem to be the more feeble members of the body, are more necessary.

23.text: And such as we think to be the less honourable members of the body, about these we put more abundant honour; and those that are our uncomely parts, have more abundant comeliness.

24.text: But our comely parts have no need: but God hath tempered the body together, giving to that which wanted the more abundant honour,

25.text: That there might be no schism in the body; but the members might be mutually careful one for another.

26.text: And if one member suffer any thing, all the members suffer with it; or if one member glory, all the members rejoice with it.

27.text: Now you are the body of Christ, and members of member.

28.text: And God indeed hath set some in the church; first apostles, secondly prophets, thirdly doctors; after that miracles; then the graces of healing, helps, governments, kinds of tongues, interpretations of speeches.

29.text: Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all doctors?

30.text: Are all workers of miracles? Have all the grace of healing? Do all speak with tongues? Do all interpret?

31.text: But be zealous for the better gifts. And I shew unto you yet a more excellent way.

1.text: If I speak with the tongues of men, and of angels, and have not charity, I am become as sounding brass, or a tinkling cymbal.

2.text: And if I should have prophecy and should know all mysteries, and all knowledge, and if I should have all faith, so that I could remove mountains, and have not charity, I am nothing.

3.text: And if I should distribute all my goods to feed the poor, and if I should deliver my body to be burned, and have not charity, it profiteth me nothing.

4.text: Charity is patient, is kind: charity envieth not, dealeth not perversely; is not puffed up;

5.text: Is not ambitious, seeketh not her own, is not provoked to anger, thinketh no evil;

6.text: Rejoiceth not in iniquity, but rejoiceth with the truth;

7.text: Beareth all things, believeth all things, hopeth all things, endureth all things.

8.text: Charity never falleth away: whether prophecies shall be made void, or tongues shall cease, or knowledge shall be destroyed.

9.text: For we know in part, and we prophesy in part.

10.text: But when that which is perfect is come, that which is in part shall be done away.

11.text: When I was a child, I spoke as a child, I understood as a child, I thought as a child. But, when I became a man, I put away the things of a child.

12.text: We see now through a glass in a dark manner; but then face to face. Now I know in part; but then I shall know even as I am known.

13.text: And now there remain faith, hope, and charity, these three: but the greatest of these is charity.

1.text: Follow after charity, be zealous for spiritual gifts; but rather that you may prophesy.

2.text: For he that speaketh in a tongue, speaketh not unto men, but unto God: for no man heareth. Yet by the Spirit he speaketh mysteries.

3.text: But he that prophesieth, speaketh to men unto edification, and exhortation, and comfort.

4.text: He that speaketh in a tongue, edifieth himself: but he that prophesieth, edifieth the church.

5.text: And I would have you all to speak with tongues, but rather to prophesy. For greater is he that prophesieth, than he that speaketh with tongues: unless perhaps he interpret, that the church may receive edification.

6.text: But now, brethren, if I come to you speaking with tongues, what shall I profit you, unless I speak to you either in revelation, or in knowledge, or in prophecy, or in doctrine?

7.text: Even things without life that give sound, whether pipe or harp, except they give a distinction of sounds, how shall it be known what is piped or harped?

8.text: For if the trumpet give an uncertain sound, who shall prepare himself to the battle?

9.text: So likewise you, except you utter by the tongue plain speech, how shall it be known what is said? For you shall be speaking into the air.

10.text: There are, for example, so many kinds of tongues in this world; and none is without voice.

11.text: If then I know not the power of the voice, I shall be to him to whom I speak a barbarian; and he that speaketh, a barbarian to me.

12.text: So you also, forasmuch as you are zealous of spirits, seek to abound unto the edifying of the church.

13.text: And therefore he that speaketh by a tongue, let him pray that he may interpret.

14.text: For if I pray in a tongue, my spirit prayeth, but my understanding is without fruit.

15.text: What is it then? I will pray with the spirit, I will pray also with the understanding; I will sing with the spirit, I will sing also with the understanding.

16.text: Else if thou shalt bless with the spirit, how shall he that holdeth the place of the unlearned say, Amen, to thy blessing? because he knoweth not what thou sayest.

17.text: For thou indeed givest thanks well, but the other is not edified.

18.text: I thank my God I speak with all your tongues.

19.text: But in the church I had rather speak five words with my understanding, that I may instruct others also; than ten thousand words in a tongue.

20.text: Brethren, do not become children in sense: but in malice be children, and in sense be perfect.

21.text: In the law it is written: In other tongues and other lips I will speak to this people; and neither so will they hear me, saith the Lord.

22.text: Wherefore tongues are for a sign, not to believers, but to unbelievers; but prophecies not to unbelievers, but to believers.

23.text: If therefore the whole church come together into one place, and all speak with tongues, and there come in unlearned persons or infidels, will they not say that you are mad?

24.text: But if all prophesy, and there come in one that believeth not, or an unlearned person, he is convinced of all, he is judged of all.

25.text: The secrets of his heart are made manifest; and so, falling down on his face, he will adore God, affirming that God is among you indeed.

26.text: How is it then, brethren? When you come together, every one of you hath a psalm, hath a doctrine, hath a revelation, hath a tongue, hath an interpretation: let all things be done to edification.

27.text: If any speak with a tongue, let it be by two, or at the most by three, and in course, and let one interpret.

28.text: But if there be no interpreter, let him hold his peace in the church, and speak to himself and to God.

29.text: And let the prophets speak, two or three; and let the rest judge.

30.text: But if any thing be revealed to another sitting, let the first hold his peace.

31.text: For you may all prophesy one by one; that all may learn, and all may be exhorted:

32.text: And the spirits of the prophets are subject to the prophets.

33.text: For God is not the God of dissension, but of peace: as also I teach in all the churches of the saints.

34.text: Let women keep silence in the churches: for it is not permitted them to speak, but to be subject, as also the law saith.

35.text: But if they would learn any thing, let them ask their husbands at home. For it is a shame for a woman to speak in the church.

36.text: Or did the word of God come out from you? Or came it only unto you?

37.text: If any seem to be a prophet, or spiritual, let him know the things that I write to you, that they are the commandments of the Lord.

38.text: But if any man know not, he shall not be known.

39.text: Wherefore, brethren, be zealous to prophesy; and forbid not to speak with tongues.

40.text: But let all things be done decently, and according to order.

1.text: Now I make known unto you, brethren, the gospel which I preached to you, which also you have received, and wherein you stand;

2.text: By which also you are saved, if you hold fast after what manner I preached unto you, unless you have believed in vain.

3.text: For I delivered unto you first of all, which I also received: how that Christ died for our sins, according to the scriptures:

4.text: And that he was buried, and that he rose again the third day, according to the scriptures:

5.text: And that he was seen by Cephas; and after that by the eleven.

6.text: Then he was seen by more than five hundred brethren at once: of whom many remain until this present, and some are fallen asleep.

7.text: After that, he was seen by James, then by all the apostles.

8.text: And last of all, he was seen also by me, as by one born out of due time.

9.text: For I am the least of the apostles, who am not worthy to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the church of God.

10.text: But by the grace of God, I am what I am; and his grace in me hath not been void, but I have laboured more abundantly than all they: yet not I, but the grace of God with me.

11.text: For whether I, or they, so we preach, and so you have believed.

12.text: Now if Christ be preached, that he arose again from the dead, how do some among you say, that there is no resurrection of the dead?

13.text: But if there be no resurrection of the dead, then Christ is not risen again.

14.text: And if Christ be not risen again, then is our preaching vain, and your faith is also vain.

15.text: And if Christ be not risen again, then is our preaching vain, and your faith is also vain.

16.text: For if the dead rise not again, neither is Christ risen again.

17.text: And if Christ be not risen again, your faith is vain, for you are yet in your sins.

18.text: Then they also that are fallen asleep in Christ, are perished.

19.text: If in this life only we have hope in Christ, we are of all men most miserable.

20.text: But now Christ is risen from the dead, the firstfruits of them that sleep:

21.text: For by a man came death, and by a man the resurrection of the dead.

22.text: And as in Adam all die, so also in Christ all shall be made alive.

23.text: But every one in his own order: the firstfruits Christ, then they that are of Christ, who have believed in his coming.

24.text: Afterwards the end, when he shall have delivered up the kingdom to God and the Father, when he shall have brought to nought all principality, and power, and virtue.

25.text: For he must reign, until he hath put all his enemies under his feet.

26.text: And the enemy death shall be destroyed last: For he hath put all things under his feet. And whereas he saith,

27.text: All things are put under him; undoubtedly, he is excepted, who put all things under him.

28.text: And when all things shall be subdued unto him, then the Son also himself shall be subject unto him that put all things under him, that God may be all in all.

29.text: Otherwise what shall they do that are baptized for the dead, if the dead rise not again at all? why are they then baptized for them?

30.text: Why also are we in danger every hour?

31.text: I die daily, I protest by your glory, brethren, which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord.

32.text: If (according to man) I fought with beasts at Ephesus, what doth it profit me, if the dead rise not again? Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we shall die.

33.text: Be not seduced: Evil communications corrupt good manners.

34.text: Awake, ye just, and sin not. For some have not the knowledge of God, I speak it to your shame.

35.text: But some man will say: How do the dead rise again? or with what manner of body shall they come?

36.text: Senseless man, that which thou sowest is not quickened, except it die first.

37.text: And that which thou sowest, thou sowest not the body that shall be; but bare grain, as of wheat, or of some of the rest.

38.text: But God giveth it a body as he will: and to every seed its proper body.

39.text: All flesh is not the same flesh: but one is the flesh of men, another of beasts, another of birds, another of fishes.

40.text: And there are bodies celestial, and bodies terrestrial: but, one is the glory of the celestial, and another of the terrestrial.

41.text: One is the glory of the sun, another the glory of the moon, and another the glory of the stars. For star differeth from star in glory.

42.text: So also is the resurrection of the dead. It is sown in corruption, it shall rise in incorruption.

43.text: It is sown in dishonour, it shall rise in glory. It is sown in weakness, it shall rise in power.

44.text: It is sown a natural body, it shall rise a spiritual body. If there be a natural body, there is also a spiritual body, as it is written:

45.text: The first man Adam was made into a living soul; the last Adam into a quickening spirit.

46.text: Yet that was not first which is spiritual, but that which is natural; afterwards that which is spiritual.

47.text: The first man was of the earth, earthly: the second man, from heaven, heavenly.

48.text: Such as is the earthly, such also are the earthly: and such as is the heavenly, such also are they that are heavenly.

49.text: Therefore as we have borne the image of the earthly, let us bear also the image of the heavenly.

50.text: Now this I say, brethren, that flesh and blood cannot possess the kingdom of God: neither shall corruption possess incorruption.

51.text: Behold, I tell you a mystery. We shall all indeed rise again: but we shall not all be changed.

52.text: In a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet: for the trumpet shall sound, and the dead shall rise again incorruptible: and we shall be changed.

53.text: For this corruptible must put on incorruption; and this mortal must put on immortality.

54.text: And when this mortal hath put on immortality, then shall come to pass the saying that is written: Death is swallowed up in victory.

55.text: O death, where is thy victory? O death, where is thy sting?

56.text: Now the sting of death is sin: and the power of sin is the law.

57.text: But thanks be to God, who hath given us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.

58.text: Therefore, my beloved brethren, be ye steadfast and unmoveable; always abounding in the work of the Lord, knowing that your labour is not in vain in the Lord.

1.text: Now concerning the collections that are made for the saints, as I have given order to the churches of Galatia, so do ye also.

2.text: On the first day of the week let every one of you put apart with himself, laying up what it shall well please him; that when I come, the collections be not then to be made.

3.text: And when I shall be with you, whomsoever you shall approve by letters, them will I send to carry your grace to Jerusalem.

4.text: And if it be meet that I also go, they shall go with me.

5.text: Now I will come to you, when I shall have passed through Macedonia. For I shall pass through Macedonia.

6.text: And with you perhaps I shall abide, or even spend the winter: that you may bring me on my way whithersoever I shall go.

7.text: For I will not see you now by the way, for I trust that I shall abide with you some time, if the Lord permit.

8.text: But I will tarry at Ephesus until Pentecost.

9.text: For a great door and evident is opened unto me: and many adversaries.

10.text: Now if Timothy come, see that he be with you without fear, for he worketh the work of the Lord, as I also do.

11.text: Let no man therefore despise him, but conduct ye him on his way in peace: that he may come to me. For I look for him with the brethren.

12.text: And touching our brother Apollo, I give you to understand, that I much entreated him to come unto you with the brethren: and indeed it was not his will at all to come at this time. But he will come when he shall have leisure.

13.text: Watch ye, stand fast in the faith, do manfully, and be strengthened.

14.text: Let all your things be done in charity.

15.text: And I beseech you, brethren, you know the house of Stephanas, and of Fortunatus, and of Achaicus, that they are the firstfruits of Achaia, and have dedicated themselves to the ministry of the saints:

16.text: That you also be subject to such, and to every one that worketh with us, and laboureth.

17.text: And I rejoice in the presence of Stephanas, and Fortunatus, and Achaicus, because that which was wanting on your part, they have supplied.

18.text: For they have refreshed both my spirit and yours. Know them, therefore, that are such.

19.text: The churches of Asia salute you. Aquila and Priscilla salute you much in the Lord, with the church that is in their house, with whom I also lodge.

20.text: All the brethren salute you. Salute one another with a holy kiss.

21.text: The salutation of me Paul, with my own hand.

22.text: If any man love not our Lord Jesus Christ, let him be anathema, maranatha.

23.text: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.

24.text: My charity be with you all in Christ Jesus. Amen.

1.text: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and Timothy our brother: to the church of God that is at Corinth, with all the saints that are in all Achaia:

2.text: Grace unto you and peace from God our Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ.

3.text: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies, and the God of all comfort.

4.text: Who comforteth us in all our tribulation; that we also may be able to comfort them who are in all distress, by the exhortation wherewith we also are exhorted by God.

5.text: For as the sufferings of Christ abound in us: so also by Christ doth our comfort abound.

6.text: Now whether we be in tribulation, it is for your exhortation and salvation: or whether we be comforted, it is for your consolation: or whether we be exhorted, it is for your exhortation and salvation, which worketh the enduring of the same sufferings which we also suffer.

7.text: That our hope for you may be steadfast: knowing that as you are partakers of the sufferings, so shall you be also of the consolation.

8.text: For we would not have you ignorant, brethren, of our tribulation, which came to us in Asia, that we were pressed out of measure above our strength, so that we were weary even of life.

9.text: But we had in ourselves the answer of death, that we should not trust in ourselves, but in God who raiseth the dead.

10.text: Who hath delivered and doth deliver us out of so great dangers: in whom we trust that he will yet also deliver us.

11.text: You helping withal in prayer for us: that for this gift obtained for us, by the means of many persons, thanks may be given by many in our behalf.

12.text: For our glory is this, the testimony of our conscience, that in simplicity of heart and sincerity of God, and not in carnal wisdom, but in the grace of God, we have conversed in this world: and more abundantly towards you.

13.text: For we write no other things to you than what you have read and known. And I hope that you shall know unto the end:

14.text: As also you have known us in part, that we are your glory, as you also are ours, in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.

15.text: And in this confidence I had a mind to come to you before, that you might have a second grace:

16.text: And to pass by you into Macedonia, and again from Macedonia to come to you, and by you to be brought on my way towards Judea.

17.text: Whereas then I was thus minded, did I use lightness? Or, the things that I purpose, do I purpose according to the flesh, that there should be with me, It is, and It is not?

18.text: But God is faithful, for our preaching which was to you, was not, It is, and It is not.

19.text: For the Son of God, Jesus Christ who was preached among you by us, by me, and Sylvanus, and Timothy, was not, It is and It is not, but, It is, was in him.

20.text: For all the promises of God are in him, It is; therefore also by him, amen to God, unto our glory.

21.text: Now he that confirmeth us with you in Christ, and that hath anointed us, is God:

22.text: Who also hath sealed us, and given the pledge of the Spirit in our hearts.

23.text: But I call God to witness upon my soul, that to spare you, I came not any more to Corinth:

24.text: not because we exercise dominion over your faith: but we are helpers of your joy: for in faith you stand.

1.text: But I determined this with myself, not to come to you again in sorrow.

2.text: For if I make you sorrowful, who is he then that can make me glad, but the same who is made sorrowful by me?

3.text: And I wrote this same to you; that I may not, when I come, have sorrow upon sorrow, from them of whom I ought to rejoice: having confidence in you all, that my joy is the joy of you all.

4.text: For out of much affliction and anguish of heart, I wrote to you with many tears: not that you should be made sorrowful: but that you might know the charity I have more abundantly towards you.

5.text: And if any one have caused grief, he hath not grieved me; but in part, that I may not burden you all.

6.text: To him who is such a one, this rebuke is sufficient, which is given by many:

7.text: So that on the contrary, you should rather forgive him and comfort him, lest perhaps such a one be swallowed up with overmuch sorrow.

8.text: Wherefore, I beseech you, that you would confirm your charity towards him.

9.text: For to this end also did I write, that I may know the experiment of you, whether you be obedient in all things.

10.text: And to whom you have pardoned any thing, I also. For, what I have pardoned, if I have pardoned any thing, for your sakes have I done it in the person of Christ.

11.text: That we be not overreached by Satan. For we are not ignorant of his devices.

12.text: And when I was come to Troas for the gospel of Christ, and a door was opened unto me in the Lord,

13.text: I had no rest in my spirit, because I found not Titus my brother; but bidding them farewell, I went into Macedonia.

14.text: Now thanks be to God, who always maketh us to triumph in Christ Jesus, and manifesteth the odour of his knowledge by us in every place.

15.text: For we are the good odour of Christ unto God, in them that are saved, and in them that perish.

16.text: To the one indeed the odour of death unto death: but to the others the odour of life unto life. And for these things who is so sufficient?

17.text: For we are not as many, adulterating the word of God; but with sincerity, but as from God, before God, in Christ we speak.

1.text: Do we begin again to commend ourselves? Or do we need (as some do) epistles of commendation to you, or from you?

2.text: You are our epistle, written in our hearts, which is known and read by all men:

3.text: Being manifested, that you are the epistle of Christ, ministered by us, and written not with ink, but with the Spirit of the living God; not in tables of stone, but in the fleshly tables of the heart.

4.text: And such confidence we have, through Christ, towards God.

5.text: Not that we are sufficient to think any thing of ourselves, as of ourselves: but our sufficiency is from God.

6.text: Who also hath made us fit ministers of the new testament, not in the letter, but in the spirit. For the letter killeth, but the spirit quickeneth.

7.text: Now if the ministration of death, engraven with letters upon stones, was glorious; so that the children of Israel could not steadfastly behold the face of Moses, for the glory of his countenance, which is made void:

8.text: How shall not the ministration of the spirit be rather in glory?

9.text: For if the ministration of condemnation be glory, much more the ministration of justice aboundeth in glory.

10.text: For even that which was glorious in this part was not glorified, by reason of the glory that excelleth.

11.text: For if that which is done away was glorious, much more that which remaineth is in glory.

12.text: Having therefore such hope, we use much confidence:

13.text: And not as Moses put a veil upon his face, that the children of Israel might not steadfastly look on the face of that which is made void.

14.text: But their senses were made dull. For, until this present day, the selfsame veil, in the reading of the old testament, remaineth not taken away (because in Christ it is made void).

15.text: But even until this day, when Moses is read, the veil is upon their heart.

16.text: But when they shall be converted to the Lord, the veil shall be taken away.

17.text: Now the Lord is a Spirit. And where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty.

18.text: But we all beholding the glory of the Lord with open face, are transformed into the same image from glory to glory, as by the Spirit of the Lord.

1.text: Therefore, seeing we have this ministration, according as we have obtained mercy, we faint not;

2.text: But we renounce the hidden things of dishonesty, not walking in craftiness, nor adulterating the word of God; but by manifestation of the truth commending ourselves to every man’s conscience, in the sight of God.

3.text: And if our gospel be also hid, it is hid to them that are lost,

4.text: In whom the god of this world hath blinded the minds of unbelievers, that the light of the gospel of the glory of Christ, who is the image of God, should not shine unto them.

5.text: For we preach not ourselves, but Jesus Christ our Lord; and ourselves your servants through Jesus.

6.text: For God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, hath shined in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God, in the face of Christ Jesus.

7.text: But we have this treasure in earthen vessels, that the excellency may be of the power of God, and not of us.

8.text: In all things we suffer tribulation, but are not distressed; we are straitened, but are not destitute;

9.text: We suffer persecution, but are not forsaken; we are cast down, but we perish not:

10.text: Always bearing about in our body the mortification of Jesus, that the life also of Jesus may be made manifest in our bodies.

11.text: For we who live are always delivered unto death for Jesus’ sake; that the life also of Jesus may be made manifest in our mortal flesh.

12.text: So then death worketh in us, but life in you.

13.text: But having the same spirit of faith, as it is written: I believed, for which cause I have spoken; we also believe, for which cause we speak also:

14.text: Knowing that he who raised up Jesus, will raise us up also with Jesus, and place us with you.

15.text: For all things are for your sakes; that the grace abounding through many, may abound in thanksgiving unto the glory of God.

16.text: For which cause we faint not; but though our outward man is corrupted, yet the inward man is renewed day by day.

17.text: For that which is at present momentary and light of our tribulation, worketh for us above measure exceedingly an eternal weight of glory.

18.text: While we look not at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen. For the things which are seen, are temporal; but the things which are not seen, are eternal.

1.text: For we know, if our earthly house of this habitation be dissolved, that we have a building of God, a house not made with hands, eternal in heaven.

2.text: For in this also we groan, desiring to be clothed upon with our habitation that is from heaven.

3.text: Yet so that we be found clothed, not naked.

4.text: For we also, who are in this tabernacle, do groan, being burthened; because we would not be unclothed, but clothed upon, that that which is mortal may be swallowed up by life.

5.text: Now he that maketh us for this very thing, is God, who hath given us the pledge of the Spirit.

6.text: Therefore having always confidence, knowing that, while we are in the body, we are absent from the Lord.

7.text: (For we walk by faith, and not by sight.)

8.text: But we are confident, and have a good will to be absent rather from the body, and to be present with the Lord.

9.text: And therefore we labour, whether absent or present, to please him.

10.text: For we must all be manifested before the judgment seat of Christ, that every one may receive the proper things of the body, according as he hath done, whether it be good or evil.

11.text: Knowing therefore the fear of the Lord, we use persuasion to men; but to God we are manifest. And I trust also that in your consciences we are manifest.

12.text: We commend not ourselves again to you, but give you occasion to glory in our behalf; that you may have somewhat to answer them who glory in face, and not in heart.

13.text: For whether we be transported in mind, it is to God; or whether we be sober, it is for you.

14.text: For the charity of Christ presseth us: judging this, that if one died for all, then all were dead.

15.text: And Christ died for all; that they also who live, may not now live to themselves, but unto him who died for them, and rose again.

16.text: Wherefore henceforth, we know no man according to the flesh. And if we have known Christ according to the flesh; but now we know him so no longer.

17.text: If then any be in Christ a new creature, the old things are passed away, behold all things are made new.

18.text: But all things are of God, who hath reconciled us to himself by Christ; and hath given to us the ministry of reconciliation.

19.text: For God indeed was in Christ, reconciling the world to himself, not imputing to them their sins; and he hath placed in us the word of reconciliation.

20.text: For Christ therefore we are ambassadors, God as it were exhorting by us. For Christ, we beseech you, be reconciled to God.

21.text: Him, who knew no sin, he hath made sin for us, that we might be made the justice of God in him.

1.text: And we helping do exhort you, that you receive not the grace of God in vain.

2.text: For he saith: In an accepted time have I heard thee; and in the day of salvation have I helped thee. Behold, now is the acceptable time; behold, now is the day of salvation.

3.text: Giving no offence to any man, that our ministry be not blamed:

4.text: But in all things let us exhibit ourselves as the ministers of God, in much patience, in tribulation, in necessities, in distresses,

5.text: In stripes, in prisons, in seditions, in labours, in watchings, in fastings,

6.text: In chastity, in knowledge, in longsuffering, in sweetness, in the Holy Ghost, in charity unfeigned,

7.text: In the word of truth, in the power of God; by the armour of justice on the right hand and on the left;

8.text: By honour and dishonour, by evil report and good report; as deceivers, and yet true; as unknown, and yet known;

9.text: As dying, and behold we live; as chastised, and not killed;

10.text: As sorrowful, yet always rejoicing; as needy, yet enriching many; as having nothing, and possessing all things.

11.text: Our mouth is open to you, O ye Corinthians, our heart is enlarged.

12.text: You are not straitened in us, but in your own bowels you are straitened.

13.text: But having the same recompense, (I speak as to my children,) be you also enlarged.

14.text: Bear not the yoke with unbelievers. For what participation hath justice with injustice? Or what fellowship hath light with darkness?

15.text: And what concord hath Christ with Belial? Or what part hath the faithful with the unbeliever?

16.text: And what agreement hath the temple of God with idols? For you are the temple of the living God; as God saith: I will dwell in them, and walk among them; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.

17.text: Wherefore, Go out from among them, and be ye separate, saith the Lord, and touch not the unclean thing:

18.text: And I will receive you; and I will be a Father to you; and you shall be my sons and daughters, saith the Lord Almighty.

1.text: Having therefore these promises, dearly beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from all defilement of the flesh and of the spirit, perfecting sanctification in the fear of God.

2.text: Receive us. We have injured no man, we have corrupted no man, we have overreached no man.

3.text: I speak not this to your condemnation. For we have said before, that you are in our hearts, to die together, and to live together.

4.text: Great is my confidence for you, great is my glorying for you. I am filled with comfort: I exceedingly abound with joy in all our tribulation.

5.text: For also when we were come into Macedonia, our flesh had no rest, but we suffered all tribulation; combats without, fears within.

6.text: But God, who comforteth the humble, comforted us by the coming of Titus.

7.text: And not by his coming only, but also by the consolation, wherewith he was comforted in you, relating to us your desire, your mourning, your zeal for me, so that I rejoiced the more.

8.text: For although I made you sorrowful by my epistle, I do not repent; and if I did repent, seeing that the same epistle (although but for a time) did make you sorrowful;

9.text: Now I am glad: not because you were made sorrowful; but because you were made sorrowful unto penance. For you were made sorrowful according to God, that you might suffer damage by us in nothing.

10.text: For the sorrow that is according to God worketh penance, steadfast unto salvation; but the sorrow of the world worketh death.

11.text: For behold this selfsame thing, that you were made sorrowful according to God, how great carefulness it worketh in you; yea defence, yea indignation, yea fear, yea desire, yea zeal, yea revenge: in all things you have shewed yourselves to be undefiled in the matter.

12.text: Wherefore although I wrote to you, it was not for his sake that did the wrong, nor for him that suffered it; but to manifest our carefulness that we have for you

13.text: Before God: therefore we were comforted. But in our consolation, we did the more abundantly rejoice for the joy of Titus, because his spirit was refreshed by you all.

14.text: And if I have boasted any thing to him of you, I have not been put to shame; but as we have spoken all things to you in truth, so also our boasting that was made to Titus is found a truth.

15.text: And his bowels are more abundantly towards you; remembering the obedience of you all, how with fear and trembling you have received him.

16.text: And his bowels are more abundantly towards you; remembering the obedience of you all, how with fear and trembling you have received him.

1.text: Now we make known unto you, brethren, the grace of God, that hath been given in the churches of Macedonia.

2.text: That in much experience of tribulation, they have had abundance of joy; and their very deep poverty hath abounded unto the riches of their simplicity.

3.text: For according to their power (I bear them witness), and beyond their power, they were willing.

4.text: With much entreaty begging of us the grace and communication of the ministry that is done toward the saints.

5.text: And not as we hoped, but they gave their own selves first to the Lord, then to us by the will of God:

6.text: Insomuch, that we desired Titus, that as he had begun, so also he would finish among you this same grace.

7.text: That as in all things you abound in faith, and word, and knowledge, and all carefulness; moreover also in your charity towards us, so in this grace also you may abound.

8.text: I speak not as commanding; but by the carefulness of others, approving also the good disposition of your charity.

9.text: For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that being rich he became poor, for your sakes; that through his poverty you might be rich.

10.text: And herein I give my advice; for this is profitable for you, who have begun not only to do, but also to be willing, a year ago.

11.text: Now therefore perform ye it also in deed; that as your mind is forward to be willing, so it may be also to perform, out of that which you have.

12.text: For if the will be forward, it is accepted according to that which a man hath, not according to that which he hath not.

13.text: For I mean not that others should be eased, and you burthened, but by an equality.

14.text: In this present time let your abundance supply their want, that their abundance also may supply your want, that there may be an equality,

15.text: As it is written: He that had much, had nothing over; and he that had little, had no want.

16.text: And thanks be to God, who hath given the same carefulness for you in the heart of Titus.

17.text: For indeed he accepted the exhortation; but being more careful, of his own will he went unto you.

18.text: We have sent also with him the brother, whose praise is in the gospel through all the churches.

19.text: And not that only, but he was also ordained by the churches companion of our travels, for this grace, which is administered by us, to the glory of the Lord, and our determined will:

20.text: Avoiding this, lest any man should blame us in this abundance which is administered by us.

21.text: For we forecast what may be good not only before God, but also before men.

22.text: And we have sent with them our brother also, whom we have often proved diligent in many things; but now much more diligent, with much confidence in you,

23.text: Either for Titus, who is my companion and fellow labourer towards you, or our brethren, the apostles of the churches, the glory of Christ.

24.text: Wherefore shew ye to them, in the sight of the churches, the evidence of your charity, and of our boasting on your behalf.

1.text: For concerning the ministry that is done towards the saints, it is superfluous for me to write unto you.

2.text: For I know your forward mind: for which I boast of you to the Macedonians. That Achaia also is ready from the year past, and your emulation hath provoked very many.

3.text: Now I have sent the brethren, that the thing which we boast of concerning you, be not made void in this behalf, that (as I have said) you may be ready:

4.text: Lest, when the Macedonians shall come with me, and find you unprepared, we (not to say ye) should be ashamed in this matter.

5.text: Therefore I thought it necessary to desire the brethren that they would go to you before, and prepare this blessing before promised, to be ready, so as a blessing, not as covetousness.

6.text: Now this I say: He who soweth sparingly, shall also reap sparingly: and he who soweth in blessings, shall also reap blessings.

7.text: Every one as he hath determined in his heart, not with sadness, or of necessity: for God loveth a cheerful giver.

8.text: And God is able to make all grace abound in you; that ye always, having all sufficiency in all things, may abound to every good work,

9.text: As it is written: He hath dispersed abroad, he hath given to the poor: his justice remaineth for ever.

10.text: And he that ministereth seed to the sower, will both give you bread to eat, and will multiply your seed, and increase the growth of the fruits of your justice:

11.text: That being enriched in all things, you may abound unto all simplicity, which worketh through us thanksgiving to God.

12.text: Because the administration of this office doth not only supply the want of the saints, but aboundeth also by many thanksgivings in the Lord,

13.text: By the proof of this ministry, glorifying God for the obedience of your confession unto the gospel of Christ, and for the simplicity of your communicating unto them, and unto all.

14.text: And in their praying for you, being desirous of you, because of the excellent grace of God in you.

15.text: Thanks be to God for his unspeakable gift.

1.text: Now I Paul myself beseech you, by the mildness and modesty of Christ, who in presence indeed am lowly among you, but being absent, am bold toward you.

2.text: But I beseech you, that I may not be bold when I am present, with that confidence wherewith I am thought to be bold, against some, who reckon us as if we walked according to the flesh.

3.text: For though we walk in the flesh, we do not war according to the flesh.

4.text: For the weapons of our warfare are not carnal, but mighty to God unto the pulling down of fortifications, destroying counsels,

5.text: And every height that exhalteth itself against the knowledge of God, and bringing into captivity every understanding unto the obedience of Christ;

6.text: And having in readiness to revenge all disobedience, when your obedience shall be fulfilled.

7.text: See the things that are according to outward appearance. If any man trust to himself, that he is Christ’s, let him think this again with himself, that as he is Christ’s, so are we also.

8.text: For if also I should boast somewhat more of our power, which the Lord hath given us unto edification, and not for your destruction, I should not be ashamed.

9.text: But that I may not be thought as it were to terrify you by epistles,

10.text: (For his epistles indeed, say they, are weighty and strong; but his bodily presence is weak, and his speech contemptible,)

11.text: Let such a one think this, that such as we are in word by epistles, when absent, such also we will be indeed when present.

12.text: For we dare not match, or compare ourselves with some, that commend themselves; but we measure ourselves by ourselves, and compare ourselves with ourselves.

13.text: But we will not glory beyond our measure; but according to the measure of the rule, which God hath measured to us, a measure to reach even unto you.

14.text: For we stretch not ourselves beyond our measure, as if we reached not unto you. For we are come as far as to you in the gospel of Christ.

15.text: Not glorying beyond measure in other men’s labours; but having hope of your increasing faith, to be magnified in you according to our rule abundantly;

16.text: Yea, unto those places that are beyond you, to preach the gospel, not to glory in another man’s rule, in those things that are made ready to our hand.

17.text: But he that glorieth, let him glory in the Lord.

18.text: For not he who commendeth himself, is approved, but he, whom God commendeth.

1.text: Would to God you could bear with some little of my folly: but do bear with me.

2.text: For I am jealous of you with the jealousy of God. For I have espoused you to one husband that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ.

3.text: But I fear lest, as the serpent seduced Eve by his subtilty, so your minds should be corrupted, and fall from the simplicity that is in Christ.

4.text: For if he that cometh preacheth another Christ, whom we have not preached; or if you receive another Spirit, whom you have not received; or another gospel which you have not received; you might well bear with him.

5.text: For I suppose that I have done nothing less than the great apostles.

6.text: For although I be rude in speech, yet not in knowledge; but in all things we have been made manifest to you.

7.text: Or did I commit a fault, humbling myself, that you might be exalted? Because I preached unto you the gospel of God freely?

8.text: I have taken from other churches, receiving wages of them for your ministry.

9.text: And, when I was present with you, and wanted, I was chargeable to no man: for that which was wanting to me, the brethren supplied who came from Macedonia; and in all things I have kept myself from being burthensome to you, and so I will keep myself.

10.text: The truth of Christ is in me, that this glorying shall not be broken off in me in the regions of Achaia.

11.text: Wherefore? Because I love you not? God knoweth it.

12.text: But what I do, that I will do, that I may cut off the occasion from them that desire occasion, that wherein they glory, they may be found even as we.

13.text: For such false apostles are deceitful workmen, transforming themselves into the apostles of Christ.

14.text: And no wonder: for Satan himself transformeth himself into an angel of light.

15.text: Therefore it is no great thing if his ministers be transformed as the ministers of justice, whose end shall be according to their works.

16.text: I say again, (let no man think me to be foolish, otherwise take me as one foolish, that I also may glory a little.)

17.text: That which I speak, I speak not according to God, but as it were in foolishness, in this matter of glorying.

18.text: Seeing that many glory according to the flesh, I will glory also.

19.text: For you gladly suffer the foolish; whereas yourselves are wise.

20.text: For you suffer if a man bring you into bondage, if a man devour you, if a man take from you, if a man be lifted up, if a man strike you on the face.

21.text: I speak according to dishonour, as if we had been weak in this part. Wherein if any man dare (I speak foolishly), I dare also.

22.text: They are Hebrews: so am I. They are Israelites: so am I. They are the seed of Abraham: so am I.

23.text: They are the ministers of Christ (I speak as one less wise). I am more; in many more labours, in prisons more frequently, in stripes above measure, in deaths often.

24.text: Of the Jews five times did I receive forty stripes, save one.

25.text: Thrice was I beaten with rods, once I was stoned, thrice I suffered shipwreck, a night and a day I was in the depth of the sea.

26.text: In journeying often, in perils of waters, in perils of robbers, in perils from my own nation, in perils from the Gentiles, in perils in the city, in perils in the wilderness, in perils in the sea, in perils from false brethren.

27.text: In labour and painfulness, in much watchings, in hunger and thirst, in fastings often, in cold and nakedness.

28.text: Besides those things which are without: my daily instance, the solicitude for all the churches.

29.text: Who is weak, and I am not weak? Who is scandalized, and I am not on fire?

30.text: If I must needs glory, I will glory of the things that concern my infirmity.

31.text: The God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who is blessed for ever, knoweth that I lie not.

32.text: At Damascus, the governor of the nation under Aretas the king, guarded the city of the Damascenes, to apprehend me.

33.text: And through a window in a basket was I let down by the wall, and so escaped his hands.

1.text: If I must glory (it is not expedient indeed), but I will come to visions and revelations of the Lord.

2.text: I know a man in Christ above fourteen years ago (whether in the body, I know not, or out of the body, I know not; God knoweth), such a one caught up to the third heaven.

3.text: And I know such a man (whether in the body, or out of the body, I know not: God knoweth),

4.text: That he was caught up into paradise, and heard secret words, which it is not granted to man to utter.

5.text: For such an one I will glory; but for myself I will glory nothing, but in my infirmities.

6.text: For though I should have a mind to glory, I shall not be foolish; for I will say the truth. But I forbear, lest any man should think of me above that which he seeth in me, or any thing he heareth from me.

7.text: And lest the greatness of the revelations should exalt me, there was given me a sting of my flesh, an angel of Satan, to buffet me.

8.text: For which thing thrice I besought the Lord, that it might depart from me.

9.text: And he said to me: My grace is sufficient for thee; for power is made perfect in infirmity. Gladly therefore will I glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may dwell in me.

10.text: For which cause I please myself in my infirmities, in reproaches, in necessities, in persecutions, in distresses, for Christ. For when I am weak, then am I powerful.

11.text: I am become foolish: you have compelled me. For I ought to have been commended by you: for I have no way come short of them that are above measure apostles, although I be nothing.

12.text: Yet the signs of my apostleship have been wrought on you, in all patience, in signs, and wonders, and mighty deeds.

13.text: For what is there that you have had less than the other churches, but that I myself was not burthensome to you? Pardon me this injury.

14.text: Behold now the third time I am ready to come to you; and I will not be burthensome unto you. For I seek not the things that are yours, but you. For neither ought the children to lay up for the parents, but the parents for the children.

15.text: But I most gladly will spend and be spent myself for your souls; although loving you more, I be loved less.

16.text: But be it so: I did not burthen you: but being crafty, I caught you by guile.

17.text: Did I overreach you by any of them whom I sent to you?

18.text: I desired Titus, and I sent with him a brother. Did Titus overreach you? Did we not walk with the same spirit? did we not in the same steps?

19.text: Of old, think you that we excuse ourselves to you? We speak before God in Christ; but all things, my dearly beloved, for your edification.

20.text: For I fear lest perhaps when I come I shall not find you such as I would, and that I shall be found by you such as you would not. Lest perhaps contentions, envyings, animosities, dissensions, detractions, whisperings, swellings, seditions, be among you.

21.text: Lest again, when I come, God humble me among you: and I mourn many of them that sinned before, and have not done penance for the uncleanness, and fornication, and lasciviousness, that they have committed.

1.text: Behold, this is the third time I am coming to you: In the mouth of two or three witnesses shall every word stand.

2.text: I have told before, and foretell, as present, and now absent, to them that sinned before, and to all the rest, that if I come again, I will not spare.

3.text: Do you seek a proof of Christ that speaketh in me, who towards you is not weak, but is mighty in you?

4.text: For although he was crucified through weakness, yet he liveth by the power of God. For we also are weak in him: but we shall live with him by the power of God towards you.

5.text: Try your own selves if you be in the faith; prove ye yourselves. Know you not your own selves, that Christ Jesus is in you, unless perhaps you be reprobates?

6.text: But I trust that you shall know that we are not reprobates.

7.text: Now we pray God, that you may do no evil, not that we may appear approved, but that you may do that which is good, and that we may be as reprobates.

8.text: For we can do nothing against the truth; but for the truth.

9.text: For we rejoice that we are weak, and you are strong. This also we pray for, your perfection.

10.text: Therefore I write these things, being absent, that, being present, I may not deal more severely, according to the power which the Lord hath given me unto edification, and not unto destruction.

11.text: For the rest, brethren, rejoice, be perfect, take exhortation, be of one mind, have peace; and the God of peace and of love shall be with you.

12.text: Salute one another with a holy kiss. All the saints salute you.

14.text: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, and the charity of God, and the communication of the Holy Ghost be with you all. Amen.

1.text: Paul, an apostle, not of men, neither by man, but by Jesus Christ, and God the Father, who raised him from the dead,

2.text: And all the brethren who are with me, to the churches of Galatia.

3.text: Grace be to you, and peace from God the Father, and from our Lord Jesus Christ,

4.text: Who gave himself for our sins, that he might deliver us from this present wicked world, according to the will of God and our Father:

5.text: To whom is glory for ever and ever. Amen.

6.text: I wonder that you are so soon removed from him that called you into the grace of Christ, unto another gospel.

7.text: Which is not another, only there are some that trouble you, and would pervert the gospel of Christ.

8.text: But though we, or an angel from heaven, preach a gospel to you besides that which we have preached to you, let him be anathema.

9.text: As we said before, so now I say again: If any one preach to you a gospel, besides that which you have received, let him be anathema.

10.text: For do I now persuade men, or God? Or do I seek to please men? If I yet pleased men, I should not be the servant of Christ.

11.text: For I give you to understand, brethren, that the gospel which was preached by me is not according to man.

12.text: For neither did I receive it of man, nor did I learn it; but by the revelation of Jesus Christ.

13.text: For you have heard of my conversation in time past in the Jews’ religion: how that, beyond measure, I persecuted the church of God, and wasted it.

14.text: And I made progress in the Jews’ religion above many of my equals in my own nation, being more abundantly zealous for the traditions of my fathers.

15.text: But when it pleased him, who separated me from my mother’s womb, and called me by his grace,

16.text: To reveal his Son in me, that I might preach him among the Gentiles, immediately I condescended not to flesh and blood.

17.text: Neither went I to Jerusalem, to the apostles who were before me: but I went into Arabia, and again I returned to Damascus.

18.text: Neither went I to Jerusalem, to the apostles who were before me: but I went into Arabia, and again I returned to Damascus.

19.text: But other of the apostles I saw none, saving James the brother of the Lord.

20.text: Now the things which I write to you, behold, before God, I lie not.

21.text: Afterwards I came into the regions of Syria and Cilicia.

22.text: And I was unknown by face to the churches of Judea, which were in Christ:

23.text: But they had heard only: He, who persecuted us in times past, doth now preach the faith which once he impugned:

24.text: And they glorified God in me.

1.text: Then, after fourteen years, I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, taking Titus also with me.

2.text: And I went up according to revelation; and communicated to them the gospel, which I preach among the Gentiles, but apart to them who seemed to be some thing: lest perhaps I should run, or had run in vain.

3.text: But neither Titus, who was with me, being a Gentile, was compelled to be circumcised.

4.text: But because of false brethren unawares brought in, who came in privately to spy our liberty, which we have in Christ Jesus, that they might bring us into servitude.

5.text: To whom we yielded not by subjection, no not for an hour, that the truth of the gospel might continue with you.

6.text: But of them who seemed to be some thing, (what they were some time, it is nothing to me, God accepteth not the person of man,) for to me they that seemed to be some thing added nothing.

7.text: But contrariwise, when they had seen that to me was committed the gospel of the uncircumcision, as to Peter was that of the circumcision.

8.text: (For he who wrought in Peter to the apostleship of the circumcision, wrought in me also among the Gentiles.)

9.text: And when they had known the grace that was given to me, James and Cephas and John, who seemed to be pillars, gave to me and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship: that we should go unto the Gentiles, and they unto the circumcision:

10.text: Only that we should be mindful of the poor: which same thing also I was careful to do.

11.text: But when Cephas was come to Antioch, I withstood him to the face, because he was to be blamed.

12.text: For before that some came from James, he did eat with the Gentiles: but when they were come, he withdrew and separated himself, fearing them who were of the circumcision.

13.text: And to his dissimulation the rest of the Jews consented, so that Barnabas also was led by them into that dissimulation.

14.text: But when I saw that they walked not uprightly unto the truth of the gospel, I said to Cephas before them all: If thou, being a Jew, livest after the manner of the Gentiles, and not as the Jews do, how dost thou compel the Gentiles to live as do the Jews?

15.text: We by nature are Jews, and not of the Gentiles sinners.

16.text: But knowing that man is not justified by the works of the law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ; we also believe in Christ Jesus, that we may be justified by the faith of Christ, and not by the works of the law: because by the works of the law no flesh shall be justified.

17.text: But if while we seek to be justified in Christ, we ourselves also are found sinners; is Christ then the minister of sin? God forbid.

18.text: For if I build up again the things which I have destroyed, I make myself a prevaricator.

19.text: For I, through the law, am dead to the law, that I may live to God: with Christ I am nailed to the cross.

20.text: And I live, now not I; but Christ liveth in me. And that I live now in the flesh: I live in the faith of the Son of God, who loved me, and delivered himself for me.

21.text: I cast not away the grace of God. For if justice be by the law, then Christ died in vain.

1.text: O senseless Galatians, who hath bewitched you that you should not obey the truth, before whose eyes Jesus Christ hath been set forth, crucified among you?

2.text: This only would I learn of you: Did you receive the Spirit by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith?

3.text: Are you so foolish, that, whereas you began in the Spirit, you would now be made perfect by the flesh?

4.text: Have you suffered so great things in vain? If it be yet in vain.

5.text: He therefore who giveth to you the Spirit, and worketh miracles among you; doth he do it by the works of the law, or by the hearing of the faith?

6.text: As it is written: Abraham believed God, and it was reputed to him unto justice.

7.text: Know ye therefore, that they who are of faith, the same are the children of Abraham.

8.text: And the scripture, foreseeing, that God justifieth the Gentiles by faith, told unto Abraham before: In thee shall all nations be blessed.

9.text: Therefore they that are of faith, shall be blessed with faithful Abraham.

10.text: For as many as are of the works of the law, are under a curse. For it is written: Cursed is every one, that abideth not in all things, which are written in the book of the law to do them.

11.text: But that in the law no man is justified with God, it is manifest: because the just man liveth by faith.

12.text: But the law is not of faith: but, He that doth those things, shall live in them.

13.text: Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us: for it is written: Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree:

14.text: That the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles through Christ Jesus: that we may receive the promise of the Spirit by faith.

15.text: Brethren (I speak after the manner of man,) yet a man’s testament, if it be confirmed, no man despiseth, nor addeth to it.

16.text: To Abraham were the promises made and to his seed. He saith not, And to his seeds, as of many: but as of one, And to thy seed, which is Christ.

17.text: Now this I say, that the testament which was confirmed by God, the law which was made after four hundred and thirty years, doth not disannul, to make the promise of no effect.

18.text: For if the inheritance be of the law, it is no more of promise. But God gave it to Abraham by promise.

19.text: Why then was the law? It was set because of transgressions, until the seed should come, to whom he made the promise, being ordained by angels in the hand of a mediator.

20.text: Now a mediator is not of one: but God is one.

21.text: Was the law then against the promises of God? God forbid. For if there had been a law given which could give life, verily justice should have been by the law.

22.text: But the scripture hath concluded all under sin, that the promise, by the faith of Jesus Christ, might be given to them that believe.

23.text: But before the faith came, we were kept under the law shut up, unto that faith which was to be revealed.

24.text: Wherefore the law was our pedagogue in Christ, that we might be justified by faith.

25.text: But after the faith is come, we are no longer under a pedagogue.

26.text: For you are all the children of God by faith, in Christ Jesus.

27.text: For as many of you as have been baptized in Christ, have put on Christ.

28.text: There is neither Jew nor Greek: there is neither bond nor free: there is neither male nor female. For you are all one in Christ Jesus.

29.text: And if you be Christ’s, then are you the seed of Abraham, heirs according to the promise.

1.text: Now I say, as long as the heir is a child, he differeth nothing from a servant, though he be lord of all;

2.text: But is under tutors and governors until the time appointed by the father:

3.text: So we also, when we were children, were serving under the elements of the world.

4.text: But when the fulness of the time was come, God sent his Son, made of a woman, made under the law:

5.text: That he might redeem them who were under the law: that we might receive the adoption of sons.

6.text: And because you are sons, God hath sent the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying: Abba, Father.

7.text: Therefore now he is not a servant, but a son. And if a son, an heir also through God.

8.text: But then indeed, not knowing God, you served them, who, by nature, are not gods.

9.text: But now, after that you have known God, or rather are known by God: how turn you again to the weak and needy elements, which you desire to serve again?

10.text: You observe days, and months, and times, and years.

11.text: I am afraid of you, lest perhaps I have laboured in vain among you.

12.text: Be ye as I, because I also am as you: brethren, I beseech you: you have not injured me at all.

13.text: And you know, how through infirmity of the flesh, I preached the gospel to you heretofore: and your temptation in my flesh,

14.text: You despised not, nor rejected: but received me as an angel of God, even as Christ Jesus.

15.text: Where is then your blessedness? For I bear you witness, that, if it could be done, you would have plucked out your own eyes, and would have given them to me.

16.text: Am I then become your enemy, because I tell you the truth?

17.text: They are zealous in your regard not well: but they would exclude you, that you might be zealous for them.

18.text: But be zealous for that which is good in a good thing always: and not only when I am present with you.

19.text: My little children, of whom I am in labour again, until Christ be formed in you.

20.text: And I would willingly be present with you now, and change my voice: because I am ashamed for you.

21.text: Tell me, you that desire to be under the law, have you not read the law?

22.text: For it is written that Abraham had two sons: the one by a bondwoman, and the other by a free woman.

23.text: But he who was of the bondwoman, was born according to the flesh: but he of the free woman, was by promise.

24.text: Which things are said by an allegory. For these are the two testaments. The one from mount Sina, engendering unto bondage; which is Agar:

25.text: For Sina is a mountain in Arabia, which hath affinity to that Jerusalem which now is, and is in bondage with her children.

26.text: But that Jerusalem, which is above, is free: which is our mother.

27.text: For it is written: Rejoice, thou barren, that bearest not: break forth and cry, thou that travailest not: for many are the children of the desolate, more than of her that hath a husband.

28.text: Now we, brethren, as Isaac was, are the children of promise.

29.text: But as then he, that was born according to the flesh, persecuted him that was after the spirit; so also it is now.

30.text: But what saith the scripture? Cast out the bondwoman and her son; for the son of the bondwoman shall not be heir with the son of the free woman.

31.text: So then, brethren, we are not the children of the bondwoman, but of the free: by the freedom wherewith Christ has made us free.

1.text: Stand fast, and be not held again under the yoke of bondage.

2.text: Behold, I Paul tell you, that if you be circumcised, Christ shall profit you nothing.

3.text: And I testify again to every man circumcising himself, that he is a debtor to the whole law.

4.text: You are made void of Christ, you who are justified in the law: you are fallen from grace.

5.text: For we in spirit, by faith, wait for the hope of justice.

6.text: For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision availeth any thing, nor uncircumcision: but faith that worketh by charity.

7.text: You did run well, who hath hindered you, that you should not obey the truth?

8.text: This persuasion is not from him that calleth you.

9.text: A little leaven corrupteth the whole lump.

10.text: I have confidence in you in the Lord: that you will not be of another mind: but he that troubleth you, shall bear the judgment, whosoever he be.

11.text: And I, brethren, if I yet preach circumcision, why do I yet suffer persecution? Then is the scandal of the cross made void.

12.text: I would they were even cut off, who trouble you.

13.text: For you, brethren, have been called unto liberty: only make not liberty an occasion to the flesh, but by charity of the spirit serve one another.

14.text: For all the law is fulfilled in one word: Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.

15.text: But if you bite and devour one another; take heed you be not consumed one of another.

16.text: I say then, walk in the spirit, and you shall not fulfill the lusts of the flesh.

17.text: For the flesh lusteth against the spirit: and the spirit against the flesh; for these are contrary one to another: so that you do not the things that you would.

18.text: But if you are led by the spirit, you are not under the law.

19.text: Now the works of the flesh are manifest, which are fornication, uncleanness, immodesty, luxury,

20.text: Idolatry, witchcrafts, enmities, contentions, emulations, wraths, quarrels, dissensions, sects,

21.text: Envies, murders, drunkenness, revellings, and such like. Of the which I foretell you, as I have foretold to you, that they who do such things shall not obtain the kingdom of God.

22.text: But the fruit of the Spirit is, charity, joy, peace, patience, benignity, goodness, longanimity,

23.text: Mildness, faith, modesty, continency, chastity. Against such there is no law.

24.text: And they that are Christ’s, have crucified their flesh, with the vices and concupiscences.

25.text: If we live in the Spirit, let us also walk in the Spirit.

26.text: Let us not be made desirous of vain glory, provoking one another, envying one another.

1.text: Brethren, and if a man be overtaken in any fault, you, who are spiritual, instruct such a one in the spirit of meekness, considering thyself, lest thou also be tempted.

2.text: Bear ye one another’s burdens; and so you shall fulfill the law of Christ.

3.text: For if any man think himself to be some thing, whereas he is nothing, he deceiveth himself.

4.text: But let every one prove his own work, and so he shall have glory in himself only, and not in another.

5.text: For every one shall bear his own burden.

6.text: And let him that is instructed in the word, communicate to him that instructeth him, in all good things.

7.text: Be not deceived, God is not mocked.

8.text: Be not deceived, God is not mocked.

9.text: And in doing good, let us not fail. For in due time we shall reap, not failing.

10.text: Therefore, whilst we have time, let us work good to all men, but especially to those who are of the household of the faith.

11.text: See what a letter I have written to you with my own hand.

12.text: For as many as desire to please in the flesh, they constrain you to be circumcised, only that they may not suffer the persecution of the cross of Christ.

13.text: For neither they themselves who are circumcised, keep the law; but they will have you to be circumcised, that they may glory in your flesh.

14.text: But God forbid that I should glory, save in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ; by whom the world is crucified to me, and I to the world.

15.text: For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision availeth any thing, nor uncircumcision, but a new creature.

16.text: And whosoever shall follow this rule, peace on them, and mercy, and upon the Israel of God.

17.text: From henceforth let no man be troublesome to me; for I bear the marks of the Lord Jesus in my body.

18.text: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit, brethren. Amen.

1.text: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ, by the will of God, to all the saints who are at Ephesus, and to the faithful in Christ Jesus.

2.text: Grace be to you, and peace from God the Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ.

3.text: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who hath blessed us with spiritual blessings in heavenly places, in Christ:

4.text: As he chose us in him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and unspotted in his sight in charity.

5.text: Who hath predestinated us unto the adoption of children through Jesus Christ unto himself: according to the purpose of his will:

6.text: Unto the praise of the glory of his grace, in which he hath graced us in his beloved son.

7.text: In whom we have redemption through his blood, the remission of sins, according to the riches of his grace,

8.text: Which hath superabounded in us in all wisdom and prudence,

9.text: That he might make known unto us the mystery of his will, according to his good pleasure, which he hath purposed in him,

10.text: In the dispensation of the fulness of times, to re-establish all things in Christ, that are in heaven and on earth, in him.

11.text: In whom we also are called by lot, being predestinated according to the purpose of him who worketh all things according to the counsel of his will.

12.text: That we may be unto the praise of his glory, we who before hoped in Christ:

13.text: In whom you also, after you had heard the word of truth, (the gospel of your salvation;) in whom also believing, you were signed with the holy Spirit of promise,

14.text: Who is the pledge of our inheritance, unto the redemption of acquisition, unto the praise of his glory.

15.text: Wherefore I also, hearing of your faith that is in the Lord Jesus, and of your love towards all the saints,

16.text: Cease not to give thanks for you, making commemoration of you in my prayers,

17.text: That the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of glory, may give unto you the spirit of wisdom and of revelation, in the knowledge of him:

18.text: The eyes of your heart enlightened, that you may know what the hope is of the glory of his inheritance in the saints.

19.text: And what is the exceeding greatness of his power towards us, who believe according to the operation of the might of his power,

20.text: Which he wrought in Christ, raising him up from the dead, and setting him on his right hand in the heavenly places.

21.text: Above all principality, and power, and virtue, and dominion, and every name that is named, not only in this world, but also in that which is to come.

22.text: And he hath subjected all things under his feet, and hath made him head over all the church,

23.text: Which is his body, and the fulness of him who is filled all in all.

1.text: And you, when you were dead in your offences, and sins,

2.text: Wherein in time past you walked according to the course of this world, according to the prince of the power of this air, of the spirit that now worketh on the children of unbelief:

3.text: In which also we all conversed in time past, in the desires of our flesh, fulfilling the will of the flesh and of our thoughts, and were by nature children of wrath, even as the rest:

4.text: But God, (who is rich in mercy,) for his exceeding charity wherewith he loved us,

5.text: Even when we were dead in sins, hath quickened us together in Christ, (by whose grace you are saved,)

6.text: And hath raised us up together, and hath made us sit together in the heavenly places, through Christ Jesus.

7.text: That he might shew in the ages to come the abundant riches of his grace, in his bounty towards us in Christ Jesus.

8.text: For by grace you are saved through faith, and that not of yourselves, for it is the gift of God;

9.text: Not of works, that no man may glory.

10.text: For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus in good works, which God hath prepared that we should walk in them.

11.text: For which cause be mindful that you, being heretofore Gentiles in the flesh, who are called uncircumcision by that which is called circumcision in the flesh, made by hands;

12.text: That you were at that time without Christ, being aliens from the conversation of Israel, and strangers to the testament, having no hope of the promise, and without God in this world.

13.text: But now in Christ Jesus, you, who some time were afar off, are made nigh by the blood of Christ.

14.text: For he is our peace, who hath made both one, and breaking down the middle wall of partition, the enmities in his flesh:

15.text: Making void the law of commandments contained in decrees; that he might make the two in himself into one new man, making peace;

16.text: And might reconcile both to God in one body by the cross, killing the enmities in himself.

17.text: And coming, he preached peace to you that were afar off, and peace to them that were nigh.

18.text: For by him we have access both in one Spirit to the Father.

19.text: Now therefore you are no more strangers and foreigners; but you are fellow citizens with the saints, and the domestics of God,

20.text: Built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone:

21.text: In whom all the building, being framed together, groweth up into an holy temple in the Lord.

22.text: In whom you also are built together into an habitation of God in the Spirit.

1.text: For this cause, I Paul, the prisoner of Jesus Christ, for you Gentiles;

2.text: If yet you have heard of the dispensation of the grace of God which is given me towards you:

3.text: How that, according to revelation, the mystery has been made known to me, as I have written above in a few words;

4.text: As you reading, may understand my knowledge in the mystery of Christ,

5.text: Which in other generations was not known to the sons of men, as it is now revealed to his holy apostles and prophets in the Spirit:

6.text: That the Gentiles should be fellow heirs, and of the same body, and co-partners of his promise in Christ Jesus, by the gospel:

7.text: Of which I am made a minister, according to the gift of the grace of God, which is given to me according to the operation of his power:

8.text: To me, the least of all the saints, is given this grace, to preach among the Gentiles, the unsearchable riches of Christ,

9.text: And to enlighten all men, that they may see what is the dispensation of the mystery which hath been hidden from eternity in God, who created all things:

10.text: That the manifold wisdom of God may be made known to the principalities and powers in heavenly places through the church,

11.text: According to the eternal purpose, which he made, in Christ Jesus our Lord:

12.text: In whom we have boldness and access with confidence by the faith of him.

13.text: Wherefore I pray you not to faint at my tribulations for you, which is your glory.

14.text: For this cause I bow my knees to the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ,

15.text: Of whom all paternity in heaven and earth is named,

16.text: That he would grant you, according to the riches of his glory, to be strengthened by his Spirit with might unto the inward man,

17.text: That Christ may dwell by faith in your hearts; that being rooted and founded in charity,

18.text: You may be able to comprehend, with all the saints, what is the breadth, and length, and height, and depth:

19.text: To know also the charity of Christ, which surpasseth all knowledge, that you may be filled unto all the fulness of God.

20.text: Now to him who is able to do all things more abundantly than we desire or understand, according to the power that worketh in us;

21.text: To him be glory in the church, and in Christ Jesus unto all generations, world without end. Amen.

1.text: I therefore, a prisoner in the Lord, beseech you that you walk worthy of the vocation in which you are called,

2.text: With all humility and mildness, with patience, supporting one another in charity.

3.text: Careful to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.

4.text: One body and one Spirit; as you are called in one hope of your calling.

5.text: One Lord, one faith, one baptism.

6.text: One God and Father of all, who is above all, and through all, and in us all.

7.text: But to every one of us is given grace, according to the measure of the giving of Christ.

8.text: Wherefore he saith: Ascending on high, he led captivity captive; he gave gifts to men.

9.text: Now that he ascended, what is it, but because he also descended first into the lower parts of the earth?

10.text: He that descended is the same also that ascended above all the heavens, that he might fill all things.

11.text: And he gave some apostles, and some prophets, and other some evangelists, and other some pastors and doctors,

12.text: For the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry, for the edifying of the body of Christ:

13.text: Until we all meet into the unity of faith, and of the knowledge of the Son of God, unto a perfect man, unto the measure of the age of the fulness of Christ;

14.text: That henceforth we be no more children tossed to and fro, and carried about with every wind of doctrine by the wickedness of men, by cunning craftiness, by which they lie in wait to deceive.

15.text: But doing the truth in charity, we may in all things grow up in him who is the head, even Christ:

16.text: From whom the whole body, being compacted and fitly joined together, by what every joint supplieth, according to the operation in the measure of every part, maketh increase of the body, unto the edifying of itself in charity.

17.text: This then I say and testify in the Lord: That henceforward you walk not as also the Gentiles walk in the vanity of their mind,

18.text: Having their understanding darkened, being alienated from the life of God through the ignorance that is in them, because of the blindness of their hearts.
