19.text: Who despairing, have given themselves up to lasciviousness, unto the working of all uncleanness, unto covetousness.

20.text: But you have not so learned Christ;

21.text: If so be that you have heard him, and have been taught in him, as the truth is in Jesus:

22.text: To put off, according to former conversation, the old man, who is corrupted according to the desire of error.

23.text: And be renewed in the spirit of your mind:

24.text: And put on the new man, who according to God is created in justice and holiness of truth.

25.text: Wherefore putting away lying, speak ye the truth every man with his neighbour; for we are members one of another.

26.text: Be angry, and sin not. Let not the sun go down upon your anger.

27.text: Give not place to the devil.

28.text: He that stole, let him now steal no more; but rather let him labour, working with his hands the thing which is good, that he may have something to give to him that suffereth need.

29.text: Let no evil speech proceed from your mouth; but that which is good, to the edification of faith, that it may administer grace to the hearers.

30.text: And grieve not the holy Spirit of God: whereby you are sealed unto the day of redemption.

31.text: Let all bitterness, and anger, and indignation, and clamour, and blasphemy, be put away from you, with all malice.

32.text: And be ye kind one to another; merciful, forgiving one another, even as God hath forgiven you in Christ.

1.text: Be ye therefore followers of God, as most dear children;

2.text: And walk in love, as Christ also hath loved us, and hath delivered himself for us, an oblation and a sacrifice to God for an odour of sweetness.

3.text: But fornication, and all uncleanness, or covetousness, let it not so much as be named among you, as becometh saints:

4.text: Or obscenity, or foolish talking, or scurrility, which is to no purpose; but rather giving of thanks.

5.text: For know you this and understand, that no fornicator, or unclean, or covetous person (which is a serving of idols), hath inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and of God.

6.text: Let no man deceive you with vain words. For because of these things cometh the anger of God upon the children of unbelief.

7.text: Be ye not therefore partakers with them.

8.text: For you were heretofore darkness, but now light in the Lord. Walk then as children of the light.

9.text: For the fruit of the light is in all goodness, and justice, and truth;

10.text: Proving what is well pleasing to God:

11.text: And have no fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness, but rather reprove them.

12.text: For the things that are done by them in secret, it is a shame even to speak of.

13.text: But all things that are reproved, are made manifest by the light; for all that is made manifest is light.

14.text: Wherefore he saith: Rise thou that sleepest, and arise from the dead: and Christ shall enlighten thee.

15.text: See therefore, brethren, how you walk circumspectly: not as unwise,

16.text: But as wise: redeeming the time, because the days are evil.

17.text: Wherefore become not unwise, but understanding what is the will of God.

18.text: And be not drunk with wine, wherein is luxury; but be ye filled with the holy Spirit,

19.text: Speaking to yourselves in psalms, and hymns, and spiritual canticles, singing and making melody in your hearts to the Lord;

20.text: Giving thanks always for all things, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, to God and the Father:

21.text: Being subject one to another, in the fear of Christ.

22.text: Let women be subject to their husbands, as to the Lord:

23.text: Because the husband is the head of the wife, as Christ is the head of the church. He is the saviour of his body.

24.text: Therefore as the church is subject to Christ, so also let the wives be to their husbands in all things.

25.text: Husbands, love your wives, as Christ also loved the church, and delivered himself up for it:

26.text: That he might sanctify it, cleansing it by the laver of water in the word of life:

27.text: That he might present it to himself a glorious church, not having spot or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy, and without blemish.

28.text: So also ought men to love their wives as their own bodies. He that loveth his wife, loveth himself.

29.text: For no man ever hated his own flesh; but nourisheth and cherisheth it, as also Christ doth the church:

30.text: Because we are members of his body, of his flesh, and of his bones.

31.text: For this cause shall a man leave his father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife, and they shall be two in one flesh.

32.text: This is a great sacrament; but I speak in Christ and in the church.

33.text: Nevertheless let every one of you in particular love his wife as himself: and let the wife fear her husband.

1.text: Children, obey your parents in the Lord, for this is just.

2.text: Honour thy father and thy mother, which is the first commandment with a promise:

3.text: That it may be well with thee, and thou mayest be long lived upon earth.

4.text: And you, fathers, provoke not your children to anger; but bring them up in the discipline and correction of the Lord.

5.text: Servants, be obedient to them that are your lords according to the flesh, with fear and trembling, in the simplicity of your heart, as to Christ:

6.text: Not serving to the eye, as it were pleasing men, but, as the servants of Christ doing the will of God from the heart,

7.text: With a good will serving, as to the Lord, and not to men.

8.text: Knowing that whatsoever good thing any man shall do, the same shall he receive from the Lord, whether he be bond, or free.

9.text: And you, masters, do the same things to them, forbearing threatenings, knowing that the Lord both of them and you is in heaven; and there is no respect of persons with him.

10.text: Finally, brethren, be strengthened in the Lord, and in the might of his power.

11.text: Put you on the armour of God, that you may be able to stand against the deceits of the devil.

12.text: For our wrestling is not against flesh and blood; but against principalities and powers, against the rulers of the world of this darkness, against the spirits of wickedness in the high places.

13.text: Therefore take unto you the armour of God, that you may be able to resist in the evil day, and to stand in all things perfect.

14.text: Stand therefore, having your loins girt about with truth, and having on the breastplate of justice,

15.text: And your feet shod with the preparation of the gospel of peace:

16.text: In all things taking the shield of faith, wherewith you may be able to extinguish all the fiery darts of the most wicked one.

17.text: And take unto you the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit (which is the word of God).

18.text: By all prayer and supplication praying at all times in the spirit; and in the same watching with all instance and supplication for all the saints:

19.text: And for me, that speech may be given me, that I may open my mouth with confidence, to make known the mystery of the gospel.

20.text: For which I am an ambassador in a chain, so that therein I may be bold to speak according as I ought.

21.text: But that you also may know the things that concern me, and what I am doing, Tychicus, my dearest brother and faithful minister in the Lord, will make known to you all things:

22.text: Whom I have sent to you for this same purpose, that you may know the things concerning us, and that he may comfort your hearts.

23.text: Peace be to the brethren and charity with faith, from God the Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.

24.text: Grace be with all them that love our Lord Jesus Christ in incorruption. Amen.

1.text: Paul and Timothy, the servants of Jesus Christ; to all the saints in Christ Jesus, who are at Philippi, with the bishops and deacons.

2.text: Grace be unto you, and peace from God our Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ.

3.text: I give thanks to my God in every remembrance of you,

4.text: Always in all my prayers making supplication for you all, with joy;

5.text: For your communication in the gospel of Christ from the first day until now.

6.text: Being confident of this very thing, that he, who hath begun a good work in you, will perfect it unto the day of Christ Jesus.

7.text: As it is meet for me to think this for you all, for that I have you in my heart; and that in my bands, and in the defence and confirmation of the gospel, you all are partakers of my joy.

8.text: For God is my witness, how I long after you all in the bowels of Jesus Christ.

9.text: And this I pray, that your charity may more and more abound in knowledge, and in all understanding:

10.text: That you may approve the better things, that you may be sincere and without offence unto the day of Christ,

11.text: Filled with the fruit of justice, through Jesus Christ, unto the glory and praise of God.

12.text: Now, brethren, I desire you should know, that the things which have happened to me, have fallen out rather to the furtherance of the gospel:

13.text: So that my bands are made manifest in Christ, in all the court, and in all other places;

14.text: And many of the brethren in the Lord, growing confident by my bands, are much more bold to speak the word of God without fear.

15.text: Some indeed, even out of envy and contention; but some also for good will preach Christ.

16.text: Some out of charity, knowing that I am set for the defence of the gospel.

17.text: And some out of contention preach Christ not sincerely: supposing that they raise affliction to my bands.

18.text: But what then? So that by all means, whether by occasion, or by truth, Christ be preached: in this also I rejoice, yea, and will rejoice.

19.text: For I know that this shall fall out to me unto salvation, through your prayer, and the supply of the Spirit of Jesus Christ,

20.text: According to my expectation and hope; that in nothing I shall be confounded, but with all confidence, as always, so now also shall Christ be magnified in my body, whether it be by life, or by death.

21.text: For to me, to live is Christ; and to die is gain.

22.text: And if to live in the flesh, this is to me the fruit of labour, and what I shall choose I know not.

23.text: But I am straitened between two: having a desire to be dissolved and to be with Christ, a thing by far the better.

24.text: But to abide still in the flesh, is needful for you.

25.text: And having this confidence, I know that I shall abide, and continue with you all, for your furtherance and joy of faith:

26.text: That your rejoicing may abound in Christ Jesus for me, by my coming to you again.

27.text: Only let your conversation be worthy of the gospel of Christ: that, whether I come and see you, or, being absent, may hear of you, that you stand fast in one spirit, with one mind labouring together for the faith of the gospel.

28.text: And in nothing be ye terrified by the adversaries: which to them is a cause of perdition, but to you of salvation, and this from God:

29.text: For unto you it is given for Christ, not only to believe in him, but also to suffer for him.

30.text: Having the same conflict as that which you have seen in me, and now have heard of me.

1.text: If there be therefore any consolation in Christ, if any comfort of charity, if any society of the spirit, if any bowels of commiseration:

2.text: Fulfill ye my joy, that you may be of one mind, having the same charity, being of one accord, agreeing in sentiment.

3.text: Let nothing be done through contention, neither by vain glory: but in humility, let each esteem others better than themselves:

4.text: Each one not considering the things that are his own, but those that are other men’s.

5.text: For let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ Jesus:

6.text: Who being in the form of God, thought it not robbery to be equal with God:

7.text: But emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, being made in the likeness of men, and in habit found as a man.

8.text: He humbled himself, becoming obedient unto death, even to the death of the cross.

9.text: For which cause God also hath exalted him, and hath given him a name which is above all names:

10.text: That in the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of those that are in heaven, on earth, and under the earth:

11.text: And that every tongue should confess that the Lord Jesus Christ is in the glory of God the Father.

12.text: Wherefore, my dearly beloved, (as you have always obeyed, not as in my presence only, but much more now in my absence,) with fear and trembling work out your salvation.

13.text: For it is God who worketh in you, both to will and to accomplish, according to his good will.

14.text: And do ye all things without murmurings and hesitations;

15.text: That you may be blameless, and sincere children of God, without reproof, in the midst of a crooked and perverse generation; among whom you shine as lights in the world.

16.text: Holding forth the word of life to my glory in the day of Christ, because I have not run in vain, nor laboured in vain.

17.text: Yea, and if I be made a victim upon the sacrifice and service of your faith, I rejoice, and congratulate with you all.

18.text: And for the selfsame thing do you also rejoice, and congratulate with me.

19.text: And I hope in the Lord Jesus to send Timothy unto you shortly, that I also may be of good comfort, when I know the things concerning you.

20.text: For I have no man so of the same mind, who with sincere affection is solicitous for you.

21.text: For all seek the things that are their own; not the things that are Jesus Christ’s.

22.text: Now know ye the proof of him, that as a son with the father, so hath he served with me in the gospel.

23.text: Him therefore I hope to send unto you immediately, so soon as I shall see how it will go with me.

24.text: And I trust in the Lord, that I myself also shall come to you shortly.

25.text: But I have thought it necessary to send to you Epaphroditus, my brother and fellow labourer, and fellow soldier, but your apostle, and he that hath ministered to my wants.

26.text: For indeed he longed after you all: and was sad, for that you had heard that he was sick.

27.text: For indeed he was sick, nigh unto death; but God had mercy on him; and not only on him, but on me also, lest I should have sorrow upon sorrow.

28.text: Therefore I sent him the more speedily: that seeing him again, you may rejoice, and I may be without sorrow.

29.text: Receive him therefore with all joy in the Lord; and treat with honour such as he is.

30.text: Because for the work of Christ he came to the point of death: delivering his life, that he might fulfill that which on your part was wanting towards my service.

1.text: As to the rest, my brethren, rejoice in the Lord. To write the same things to you, to me indeed is not wearisome, but to you it is necessary.

2.text: Beware of dogs, beware of evil workers, beware of the concision.

3.text: For we are the circumcision, who in spirit serve God; and glory in Christ Jesus, not having confidence in the flesh.

4.text: Though I might also have confidence in the flesh. If any other thinketh he may have confidence in the flesh, I more,

5.text: Being circumcised the eighth day, of the stock of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, an Hebrew of the Hebrews; according to the law, a Pharisee:

6.text: According to zeal, persecuting the church of God; according to the justice that is in the law, conversing without blame.

7.text: But the things that were gain to me, the same I have counted loss for Christ.

8.text: Furthermore I count all things to be but loss for the excellent knowledge of Jesus Christ my Lord; for whom I have suffered the loss of all things, and count them but as dung, that I may gain Christ:

9.text: And may be found in him, not having my justice, which is of the law, but that which is of the faith of Christ Jesus, which is of God, justice in faith:

10.text: That I may know him, and the power of his resurrection, and the fellowship of his sufferings, being made conformable to his death,

11.text: If by any means I may attain to the resurrection which is from the dead.

12.text: Not as though I had already attained, or were already perfect; but I follow after, if I may by any means apprehend, wherein I am also apprehended by Christ Jesus.

13.text: Brethren, I do not count myself to have apprehended. But one thing I do: forgetting the things that are behind, and stretching forth myself to those that are before,

14.text: I press towards the mark, to the prize of the supernal vocation of God in Christ Jesus.

15.text: Let us therefore, as many as are perfect, be thus minded; and if in any thing you be otherwise minded, this also God will reveal to you.

16.text: Nevertheless whereunto we are come, that we be of the same mind, let us also continue in the same rule.

17.text: Be ye followers of me, brethren, and observe them who walk so as you have our model.

18.text: For many walk, of whom I have told you often (and now tell you weeping), that they are enemies of the cross of Christ;

19.text: Whose end is destruction; whose God is their belly; and whose glory is in their shame; who mind earthly things.

20.text: But our conversation is in heaven; from whence also we look for the Saviour, our Lord Jesus Christ,

21.text: Who will reform the body of our lowness, made like to the body of his glory, according to the operation whereby also he is able to subdue all things unto himself.

1.text: Therefore, my dearly beloved brethren, and most desired, my joy and my crown; so stand fast in the Lord, my dearly beloved.

2.text: I beg of Evodia, and I beseech Syntyche, to be of one mind in the Lord.

3.text: And I entreat thee also, my sincere companion, help those women who have laboured with me in the gospel, with Clement and the rest of my fellow labourers, whose names are in the book of life.

4.text: Rejoice in the Lord always; again, I say, rejoice.

5.text: Let your modesty be known to all men. The Lord is nigh.

6.text: Be nothing solicitous; but in every thing, by prayer and supplication, with thanksgiving, let your petitions be made known to God.

7.text: And the peace of God, which surpasseth all understanding, keep your hearts and minds in Christ Jesus.

8.text: For the rest, brethren, whatsoever things are true, whatsoever modest, whatsoever just, whatsoever holy, whatsoever lovely, whatsoever of good fame, if there be any virtue, if any praise of discipline, think on these things.

9.text: The things which you have both learned, and received, and heard, and seen in me, these do ye, and the God of peace shall be with you.

10.text: Now I rejoice in the Lord exceedingly, that now at length your thought for me hath flourished again, as you did also think; but you were busied.

11.text: I speak not as it were for want. For I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, to be content therewith.

12.text: I know both how to be brought low, and I know how to abound: (everywhere, and in all things I am instructed) both to be full, and to be hungry; both to abound, and to suffer need.

13.text: I can do all these things in him who strengtheneth me.

14.text: Nevertheless you have done well in communicating to my tribulation.

15.text: And you also know, O Philippians, that in the beginning of the gospel, when I departed from Macedonia, no church communicated with me as concerning giving and receiving, but you only:

16.text: For unto Thessalonica also you sent once and again for my use.

17.text: Not that I seek the gift, but I seek the fruit that may abound to your account.

18.text: But I have all, and abound: I am filled, having received from Epaphroditus the things you sent, an odour of sweetness, an acceptable sacrifice, pleasing to God.

19.text: And may my God supply all your want, according to his riches in glory in Christ Jesus.

20.text: Now to God and our Father be glory world without end. Amen.

21.text: Salute ye every saint in Christ Jesus.

22.text: The brethren who are with me, salute you. All the saints salute you; especially they that are of Caesar’s household.

23.text: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.

1.text: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ, by the will of God, and Timothy, a brother,

2.text: To the saints and faithful brethren in Christ Jesus, who are at Colossa.

3.text: Grace be to you and peace from God our Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ. We give thanks to God, and the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, praying always for you.

4.text: Hearing your faith in Christ Jesus, and the love which you have towards all the saints.

5.text: For the hope that is laid up for you in heaven, which you have heard in the word of the truth of the gospel,

6.text: Which is come unto you, as also it is in the whole world, and bringeth forth fruit and groweth, even as it doth in you, since the day you heard and knew the grace of God in truth.

7.text: As you learned of Epaphras, our most beloved fellow servant, who is for you a faithful minister of Christ Jesus;

8.text: Who also hath manifested to us your love in the spirit.

9.text: Therefore we also, from the day that we heard it, cease not to pray for you, and to beg that you may be filled with the knowledge of his will, in all wisdom, and spiritual understanding:

10.text: That you may walk worthy of God, in all things pleasing; being fruitful in every good work, and increasing in the knowledge of God:

11.text: Strengthened with all might, according to the power of his glory, in all patience and longsuffering with joy,

12.text: Giving thanks to God the Father, who hath made us worthy to be partakers of the lot of the saints in light:

13.text: Who hath delivered us from the power of darkness, and hath translated us into the kingdom of the Son of his love,

14.text: In whom we have redemption through his blood, the remission of sins;

15.text: Who is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature:

16.text: For in him were all things created in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible, whether thrones, or dominations, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him and in him.

17.text: And he is before all, and by him all things consist.

18.text: And he is the head of the body, the church, who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead; that in all things he may hold the primacy:

19.text: Because in him, it hath well pleased the Father, that all fulness should dwell;

20.text: And through him to reconcile all things unto himself, making peace through the blood of his cross, both as to the things that are on earth, and the things that are in heaven.

21.text: And you, whereas you were some time alienated and enemies in mind in evil works:

22.text: Yet now he hath reconciled in the body of his flesh through death, to present you holy and unspotted, and blameless before him:

23.text: If so ye continue in the faith, grounded and settled, and immoveable from the hope of the gospel which you have heard, which is preached in all the creation that is under heaven, whereof I Paul am made a minister.

24.text: Who now rejoice in my sufferings for you, and fill up those things that are wanting of the sufferings of Christ, in my flesh, for his body, which is the church:

25.text: Whereof I am made a minister according to the dispensation of God, which is given me towards you, that I may fulfill the word of God:

26.text: The mystery which hath been hidden from ages and generations, but now is manifested to his saints,

27.text: To whom God would make known the riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles, which is Christ, in you the hope of glory.

28.text: Whom we preach, admonishing every man, and teaching every man in all wisdom, that we may present every man perfect in Christ Jesus.

29.text: Wherein also I labour, striving according to his working which he worketh in me in power.

1.text: For I would have you know, what manner of care I have for you and for them that are at Laodicea, and whosoever have not seen my face in the flesh:

2.text: That their hearts may be comforted, being instructed in charity, and unto all riches of fulness of understanding, unto the knowledge of the mystery of God the Father and of Christ Jesus:

3.text: In whom are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.

4.text: Now this I say, that no man may deceive you by loftiness of words.

5.text: For though I be absent in body, yet in spirit I am with you; rejoicing, and beholding your order, and the steadfastness of your faith which is in Christ.

6.text: As therefore you have received Jesus Christ the Lord, walk ye in him;

7.text: Rooted and built up in him, and confirmed in the faith, as also you have learned, abounding in him in thanksgiving.

8.text: Beware lest any man cheat you by philosophy, and vain deceit; according to the tradition of men, according to the elements of the world, and not according to Christ:

9.text: For in him dwelleth all the fulness of the Godhead corporeally;

10.text: And you are filled in him, who is the head of all principality and power:

11.text: In whom also you are circumcised with circumcision not made by hand, in despoiling of the body of the flesh, but in the circumcision of Christ:

12.text: Buried with him in baptism, in whom also you are risen again by the faith of the operation of God, who hath raised him up from the dead.

13.text: And you, when you were dead in your sins, and the uncircumcision of your flesh; he hath quickened together with him, forgiving you all offences:

14.text: Blotting out the handwriting of the decree that was against us, which was contrary to us. And he hath taken the same out of the way, fastening it to the cross:

15.text: And despoiling the principalities and powers, he hath exposed them confidently in open shew, triumphing over them in himself.

16.text: Let no man therefore judge you in meat or in drink, or in respect of a festival day, or of the new moon, or of the sabbaths,

17.text: Which are a shadow of things to come, but the body is of Christ.

18.text: Let no man seduce you, willing in humility, and religion of angels, walking in the things which he hath not seen, in vain puffed up by the sense of his flesh,

19.text: And not holding the head, from which the whole body, by joints and bands, being supplied with nourishment and compacted, groweth unto the increase of God.

20.text: If then you be dead with Christ from the elements of this world, why do you yet decree as though living in the world?

21.text: Touch not, taste not, handle not:

22.text: Which all are unto destruction by the very use, according to the precepts and doctrines of men.

23.text: Which things have indeed a shew of wisdom in superstition and humility, and not sparing the body; not in any honour to the filling of the flesh.

1.text: Therefore, if you be risen with Christ, seek the things that are above; where Christ is sitting at the right hand of God:

2.text: Mind the things that are above, not the things that are upon the earth.

3.text: For you are dead; and your life is hid with Christ in God.

4.text: When Christ shall appear, who is your life, then you also shall appear with him in glory.

5.text: Mortify therefore your members which are upon the earth; fornication, uncleanness, lust, evil concupiscence, and covetousness, which is the service of idols.

6.text: For which things the wrath of God cometh upon the children of unbelief,

7.text: In which you also walked some time, when you lived in them.

8.text: But now put you also all away: anger, indignation, malice, blasphemy, filthy speech out of your mouth.

9.text: Lie not one to another: stripping yourselves of the old man with his deeds,

10.text: And putting on the new, him who is renewed unto knowledge, according to the image of him that created him.

11.text: Where there is neither Gentile nor Jew, circumcision nor uncircumcision, Barbarian nor Scythian, bond nor free. But Christ is all, and in all.

12.text: Put ye on therefore, as the elect of God, holy, and beloved, the bowels of mercy, benignity, humility, modesty, patience:

13.text: Bearing with one another, and forgiving one another, if any have a complaint against another: even as the Lord hath forgiven you, so do you also.

14.text: But above all these things have charity, which is the bond of perfection:

15.text: And let the peace of Christ rejoice in your hearts, wherein also you are called in one body: and be ye thankful.

16.text: Let the word of Christ dwell in you abundantly, in all wisdom: teaching and admonishing one another in psalms, hymns, and spiritual canticles, singing in grace in your hearts to God.

17.text: All whatsoever you do in word or in work, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, giving thanks to God and the Father by him.

18.text: Wives, be subject to your husbands, as it behoveth in the Lord.

19.text: Husbands, love your wives, and be not bitter towards them.

20.text: Children, obey your parents in all things: for this is well pleasing to the Lord.

21.text: Fathers, provoke not your children to indignation, lest they be discouraged.

22.text: Servants, obey in all things your masters according to the flesh, not serving to the eye, as pleasing men, but in simplicity of heart, fearing God.

23.text: Whatsoever you do, do it from the heart, as to the Lord, and not to men:

24.text: Knowing that you shall receive of the Lord the reward of inheritance. Serve ye the Lord Christ.

25.text: For he that doth wrong, shall receive for that which he hath done wrongfully: and there is no respect of persons with God.

1.text: Masters, do to your servants that which is just and equal: knowing that you also have a master in heaven.

2.text: Be instant in prayer; watching in it with thanksgiving:

3.text: Praying withal for us also, that God may open unto us a door of speech to speak the mystery of Christ (for which also I am bound;)

4.text: That I may make it manifest as I ought to speak.

5.text: Walk with wisdom towards them that are without, redeeming the time.

6.text: Let your speech be always in grace seasoned with salt: that you may know how you ought to answer every man.

7.text: All the things that concern me, Tychicus, our dearest brother, and faithful minister and fellow servant in the Lord, will make known to you,

8.text: Whom I have sent to you for this same purpose, that he may know the things that concern you, and comfort your hearts,

9.text: With Onesimus, a most beloved and faithful brother, who is one of you. All things that are done here, they shall make known to you.

10.text: Aristarchus, my fellow prisoner, saluteth you, and Mark, the cousin german of Barnabus, touching whom you have received commandments; if he come unto you, receive him:

11.text: And Jesus, that is called Justus: who are of the circumcision: these only are my helpers in the kingdom of God; who have been a comfort to me.

12.text: Epaphras saluteth you, who is one of you, a servant of Christ Jesus, who is always solicitous for you in prayers, that you may stand perfect, and full in all the will of God.

13.text: For I bear him testimony that he hath much labour for you, and for them that are at Laodicea, and them at Hierapolis.

14.text: Luke, the most dear physician, saluteth you: and Demas.

15.text: Salute the brethren who are at Laodicea, and Nymphas, and the church that is in his house.

16.text: And when this epistle shall have been read with you, cause that it be read also in the church of the Laodiceans: and that you read that which is of the Laodiceans.

17.text: And say to Archippus: Take heed to the ministry which thou hast received in the Lord, that thou fulfill it.

18.text: The salutation of Paul with my own hand. Be mindful of my bands. Grace be with you. Amen.

1.text: Paul and Sylvanus and Timothy: to the church of the Thessalonians, in God the Father, and in the Lord Jesus Christ.

2.text: Grace be to you and peace. We give thanks to God always for you all; making a remembrance of you in our prayers without ceasing,

3.text: Being mindful of the work of your faith, and labour, and charity, and of the enduring of the hope of our Lord Jesus Christ before God and our Father:

4.text: Knowing, brethren beloved of God, your election:

5.text: For our gospel hath not been unto you in word only, but in power also, and in the Holy Ghost, and in much fulness, as you know what manner of men we have been among you for your sakes.

6.text: And you became followers of us, and of the Lord; receiving the word in much tribulation, with joy of the Holy Ghost:

7.text: So that you were made a pattern to all that believe in Macedonia and in Achaia.

8.text: For from you was spread abroad the word of the Lord, not only in Macedonia, and in Achaia, but also in every place, your faith which is towards God, is gone forth, so that we need not to speak any thing.

9.text: For they themselves relate of us, what manner of entering in we had unto you; and how you turned to God from idols, to serve the living and true God.

10.text: For they themselves relate of us, what manner of entering in we had unto you; and how you turned to God from idols, to serve the living and true God.

1.text: For yourselves know, brethren, our entrance in unto you, that it was not in vain:

2.text: But having suffered many things before, and been shamefully treated (as you know) at Philippi, we had confidence in our God, to speak unto you the gospel of God in much carefulness.

3.text: For our exhortation was not of error, nor of uncleanness, nor in deceit:

4.text: But as we were approved by God that the gospel should be committed to us: even so we speak, not as pleasing men, but God, who proveth our hearts.

5.text: For neither have we used, at any time, the speech of flattery, as you know; nor taken an occasion of covetousness, God is witness:

6.text: Nor sought we glory of men, neither of you, nor of others.

7.text: Whereas we might have been burdensome to you, as the apostles of Christ: but we became little ones in the midst of you, as if a nurse should cherish her children:

8.text: So desirous of you, we would gladly impart unto you not only the gospel of God, but also our own souls: because you were become most dear unto us.

9.text: For you remember, brethren, our labour and toil: working night and day, lest we should be chargeable to any of you, we preached among you the gospel of God.

10.text: You are witnesses, and God also, how holily, and justly, and without blame, we have been to you that have believed:

11.text: As you know in what manner, entreating and comforting you, (as a father doth his children,)

12.text: We testified to every one of you, that you would walk worthy of God, who hath called you unto his kingdom and glory.

13.text: Therefore, we also give thanks to God without ceasing: because, that when you had received of us the word of the hearing of God, you received it not as the word of men, but (as it is indeed) the word of God, who worketh in you that have believed.

14.text: For you, brethren, are become followers of the churches of God which are in Judea, in Christ Jesus: for you also have suffered the same things from your own countrymen, even as they have from the Jews,

15.text: Who both killed the Lord Jesus, and the prophets, and have persecuted us, and please not God, and are adversaries to all men;

16.text: Prohibiting us to speak to the Gentiles, that they may be saved, to fill up their sins always: for the wrath of God is come upon them to the end.

17.text: But we, brethren, being taken away from you for a short time, in sight, not in heart, have hastened the more abundantly to see your face with great desire.

18.text: For we would have come unto you, I Paul indeed, once and again: but Satan hath hindered us.

19.text: For what is our hope, or joy, or crown of glory? Are not you, in the presence of our Lord Jesus Christ at his coming?

20.text: For you are our glory and joy.

1.text: For which cause, forbearing no longer, we thought it good to remain at Athens alone:

2.text: And we sent Timothy, our brother, and the minister of God in the gospel of Christ, to confirm you and exhort you concerning your faith:

3.text: That no man should be moved in these tribulations: for yourselves know, that we are appointed thereunto.

4.text: For even when we were with you, we foretold you that we should suffer tribulations, as also it is come to pass, and you know.

5.text: For this cause also, I, forbearing no longer, sent to know your faith: lest perhaps he that tempteth should have tempted you, and our labour should be made vain.

6.text: But now when Timothy came to us from you, and related to us your faith and charity, and that you have a good remembrance of us always, desiring to see us as we also to see you;

7.text: Therefore we were comforted, brethren, in you, in all our necessity and tribulation, by your faith,

8.text: Because now we live, if you stand in the Lord.

9.text: For what thanks can we return to God for you, in all the joy wherewith we rejoice for you before our God,

10.text: For what thanks can we return to God for you, in all the joy wherewith we rejoice for you before our God,

11.text: Now God himself and our Father, and our Lord Jesus Christ, direct our way unto you.

12.text: And may the Lord multiply you, and make you abound in charity towards one another, and towards all men: as we do also towards you,

13.text: To confirm your hearts without blame, in holiness, before God and our Father, at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, with all his saints. Amen.

1.text: For the rest therefore, brethren, we pray and beseech you in the Lord Jesus, that as you have received from us, how you ought to walk, and to please God, so also you would walk, that you may abound the more.

2.text: For you know what precepts I have given to you by the Lord Jesus.

3.text: For this is the will of God, your sanctification; that you should abstain from fornication;

4.text: That every one of you should know how to possess his vessel in sanctification and honour:

5.text: Not in the passion of lust, like the Gentiles that know not God:

6.text: And that no man overreach, nor circumvent his brother in business: because the Lord is the avenger of all these things, as we have told you before, and have testified.

7.text: For God hath not called us unto uncleanness, but unto sanctification.

8.text: Therefore, he that despiseth these things, despiseth not man, but God, who also hath given his holy Spirit in us.

9.text: But as touching the charity of brotherhood, we have no need to write to you: for yourselves have learned of God to love one another.

10.text: For indeed you do it towards all the brethren in all Macedonia. But we entreat you, brethren, that you abound more:

11.text: And that you use your endeavour to be quiet, and that you do your own business, and work with your own hands, as we commanded you: and that you walk honestly towards them that are without; and that you want nothing of any man’s.

12.text: And we will not have you ignorant, brethren, concerning them that are asleep, that you be not sorrowful, even as others who have no hope.

13.text: For if we believe that Jesus died, and rose again; even so them who have slept through Jesus, will God bring with him.

14.text: For this we say unto you in the word of the Lord, that we who are alive, who remain unto the coming of the Lord, shall not prevent them who have slept.

15.text: For the Lord himself shall come down from heaven with commandment, and with the voice of an archangel, and with the trumpet of God: and the dead who are in Christ, shall rise first.

16.text: Then we who are alive, who are left, shall be taken up together with them in the clouds to meet Christ, into the air, and so shall we be always with the Lord.

17.text: Wherefore, comfort ye one another with these words.

1.text: But of the times and moments, brethren, you need not, that we should write to you;

2.text: For yourselves know perfectly, that the day of the Lord shall so come, as a thief in the night.

3.text: For when they shall say, peace and security; then shall sudden destruction come upon them, as the pains upon her that is with child, and they shall not escape.

4.text: But you, brethren, are not in darkness, that that day should overtake you as a thief.

5.text: For all you are the children of light, and children of the day: we are not of the night, nor of darkness.

6.text: Therefore, let us not sleep, as others do; but let us watch, and be sober.

7.text: For they that sleep, sleep in the night; and they that are drunk, are drunk in the night.

8.text: But let us, who are of the day, be sober, having on the breastplate of faith and charity, and for a helmet the hope of salvation.

9.text: For God hath not appointed us unto wrath, but unto the purchasing of salvation by our Lord Jesus Christ,

10.text: Who died for us; that, whether we watch or sleep, we may live together with him.

11.text: For which cause comfort one another; and edify one another, as you also do.

12.text: And we beseech you, brethren, to know them who labour among you, and are over you in the Lord, and admonish you:

13.text: That you esteem them more abundantly in charity, for their work’s sake. Have peace with them.

14.text: And we beseech you, brethren, rebuke the unquiet, comfort the feeble minded, support the weak, be patient towards all men.

15.text: See that none render evil for evil to any man; but ever follow that which is good towards each other, and towards all men.

16.text: Always rejoice.

17.text: Pray without ceasing.

18.text: In all things give thanks; for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you all.

19.text: Extinguish not the spirit.

20.text: Despise not prophecies.

21.text: But prove all things; hold fast that which is good.

22.text: From all appearance of evil refrain yourselves.

23.text: And may the God of peace himself sanctify you in all things; that your whole spirit, and soul, and body, may be preserved blameless in the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.

24.text: He is faithful who hath called you, who also will do it.

25.text: Brethren, pray for us.

26.text: Salute all the brethren with a holy kiss.

27.text: I charge you by the Lord, that this epistle be read to all the holy brethren.

1.text: Paul, and Sylvanus, and Timothy, to the church of the Thessalonians in God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.

2.text: Grace unto you, and peace from God our Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ.

3.text: We are bound to give thanks always to God for you, brethren, as it is fitting, because your faith groweth exceedingly, and the charity of every one of you towards each other, aboundeth:

4.text: So that we ourselves also glory in you in the churches of God, for your patience and faith, and in all your persecutions and tribulations, which you endure,

5.text: For an example of the just judgment of God, that you may be counted worthy of the kingdom of God, for which also you suffer.

6.text: Seeing it is a just thing with God to repay tribulation to them that trouble you:

7.text: And to you who are troubled, rest with us when the Lord Jesus shall be revealed from heaven, with the angels of his power:

8.text: In a flame of fire, giving vengeance to them who know not God, and who obey not the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ.

9.text: Who shall suffer eternal punishment in destruction, from the face of the Lord, and from the glory of his power:

10.text: When he shall come to be glorified in his saints, and to be made wonderful in all them who have believed; because our testimony was believed upon you in that day.

11.text: Wherefore also we pray always for you; that our God would make you worthy of his vocation, and fulfill all the good pleasure of his goodness and the work of faith in power;

12.text: That the name of our Lord Jesus may be glorified in you, and you in him, according to the grace of our God, and of the Lord Jesus Christ.

1.text: And we beseech you, brethren, by the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, and of our gathering together unto him:

2.text: That you be not easily moved from your sense, nor be terrified, neither by spirit, nor by word, nor by epistle, as sent from us, as if the day of the Lord were at hand.

3.text: Let no man deceive you by any means, for unless there come a revolt first, and the man of sin be revealed, the son of perdition,

4.text: Who opposeth, and is lifted up above all that is called God, or that is worshipped, so that he sitteth in the temple of God, shewing himself as if he were God.

5.text: Remember you not, that when I was yet with you, I told you these things?

6.text: And now you know what withholdeth, that he may be revealed in his time.

7.text: For the mystery of iniquity already worketh; only that he who now holdeth, do hold, until he be taken out of the way.

8.text: And then that wicked one shall be revealed whom the Lord Jesus shall kill with the spirit of his mouth; and shall destroy with the brightness of his coming, him,

9.text: Whose coming is according to the working of Satan, in all power, and signs, and lying wonders,

10.text: And in all seduction of iniquity to them that perish; because they receive not the love of the truth, that they might be saved. Therefore God shall send them the operation of error, to believe lying:

11.text: That all may be judged who have not believed the truth, but have consented to iniquity.

12.text: But we ought to give thanks to God always for you, brethren, beloved of God, for that God hath chosen you firstfruits unto salvation, in sanctification of the spirit, and faith of the truth:

13.text: Whereunto also he hath called you by our gospel, unto the purchasing of the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ.

14.text: Therefore, brethren, stand fast; and hold the traditions which you have learned, whether by word, or by our epistle.

15.text: Now our Lord Jesus Christ himself, and God and our Father, who hath loved us, and hath given us everlasting consolation, and good hope in grace,

16.text: Exhort your hearts, and confirm you in every good work and word.

1.text: For the rest, brethren, pray for us, that the word of God may run, and may be glorified, even as among you;

2.text: And that we may be delivered from importunate and evil men; for all men have not faith.

3.text: But God is faithful, who will strengthen and keep you from evil.

4.text: And we have confidence concerning you in the Lord, that the things which we command, you both do, and will do.

5.text: And the Lord direct your hearts, in the charity of God, and the patience of Christ.

6.text: And we charge you, brethren, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you withdraw yourselves from every brother walking disorderly, and not according to the tradition which they have received of us.

7.text: For yourselves know how you ought to imitate us: for we were not disorderly among you;

8.text: Neither did we eat any man’s bread for nothing, but in labour and in toil we worked night and day, lest we should be chargeable to any of you.

9.text: Not as if we had not power: but that we might give ourselves a pattern unto you, to imitate us.

10.text: For also when we were with you, this we declared to you: that, if any man will not work, neither let him eat.

11.text: For we have heard there are some among you who walk disorderly, working not at all, but curiously meddling.

12.text: Now we charge them that are such, and beseech them by the Lord Jesus Christ, that, working with silence, they would eat their own bread.

13.text: But you, brethren, be not weary in well doing.

14.text: And if any man obey not our word by this epistle, note that man, and do not keep company with him, that he may be ashamed:

15.text: Yet do not esteem him as an enemy, but admonish him as a brother.

16.text: Now the Lord of peace himself give you everlasting peace in every place. The Lord be with you all.

17.text: The salutation of Paul with my own hand; which is the sign in every epistle. So I write.

18.text: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.

1.text: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ, according to the commandment of God our Saviour, and of Christ Jesus our hope:

2.text: To Timothy, his beloved son in faith. Grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father, and from Christ Jesus our Lord.

3.text: As I desired thee to remain at Ephesus when I went into Macedonia, that thou mightest charge some not to teach otherwise,

4.text: Not to give heed to fables and endless genealogies: which furnish questions rather than the edification of God, which is in faith.

5.text: Now the end of the commandment is charity, from a pure heart, and a good conscience, and an unfeigned faith.

6.text: From which things some going astray, are turned aside unto vain babbling:

7.text: Desiring to be teachers of the law, understanding neither the things they say, nor whereof they affirm.

8.text: But we know that the law is good, if a man use it lawfully:

9.text: Knowing this, that the law is not made for the just man, but for the unjust and disobedient, for the ungodly, and for sinners, for the wicked and defiled, for murderers of fathers, and murderers of mothers, for manslayers,

10.text: For fornicators, for them who defile themselves with mankind, for menstealers, for liars, for perjured persons, and whatever other thing is contrary to sound doctrine,

11.text: Which is according to the gospel of the glory of the blessed God, which hath been committed to my trust.

12.text: I give thanks who hath strengthened me, even to Christ Jesus our Lord, for that he hath counted me faithful, putting me in the ministry;

13.text: Who before was a blasphemer, and a persecutor, and contumelious. But I obtained the mercy of God, because I did it ignorantly in unbelief.

14.text: Now the grace of our Lord hath abounded exceedingly with faith and love, which is in Christ Jesus.

15.text: A faithful saying, and worthy of all acceptation, that Christ Jesus came into this world to save sinners, of whom I am the chief.

16.text: But for this cause have I obtained mercy: that in me first Christ Jesus might shew forth all patience, for the information of them that shall believe in him unto life everlasting.

17.text: Now to the king of ages, immortal, invisible, the only God, be honour and glory for ever and ever. Amen.

18.text: This precept I commend to thee, O son Timothy; according to the prophecies going before on thee, that thou war in them a good warfare,

19.text: Having faith and a good conscience, which some rejecting have made shipwreck concerning the faith.

20.text: Of whom is Hymeneus and Alexander, whom I have delivered up to Satan, that they may learn not to blaspheme.

1.text: I desire therefore, first of all, that supplications, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings be made for all men:

2.text: For kings, and for all that are in high station: that we may lead a quiet and a peaceable life in all piety and chastity.

3.text: For this is good and acceptable in the sight of God our Saviour,

4.text: Who will have all men to be saved, and to come to the knowledge of the truth.

5.text: For there is one God, and one mediator of God and men, the man Christ Jesus:

6.text: Who gave himself a redemption for all, a testimony in due times.

7.text: Whereunto I am appointed a preacher and an apostle, (I say the truth, I lie not,) a doctor of the Gentiles in faith and truth.

8.text: I will therefore that men pray in every place, lifting up pure hands, without anger and contention.

9.text: In like manner women also in decent apparel: adorning themselves with modesty and sobriety, not with plaited hair, or gold, or pearls, or costly attire,

10.text: But as it becometh women professing godliness, with good works.

11.text: Let the woman learn in silence, with all subjection.

12.text: But I suffer not a woman to teach, nor to use authority over the man: but to be in silence.

13.text: For Adam was first formed; then Eve.

14.text: And Adam was not seduced; but the woman being seduced, was in the transgression.

15.text: Yet she shall be saved through childbearing; if she continue in faith, and love, and sanctification, with sobriety.

1.text: A faithful saying: if a man desire the office of a bishop, he desireth a good work.

2.text: It behoveth therefore a bishop to be blameless, the husband of one wife, sober, prudent, of good behaviour, chaste, given to hospitality, a teacher,

3.text: Not given to wine, no striker, but modest, not quarrelsome, not covetous, but

4.text: One that ruleth well his own house, having his children in subjection with all chastity.

5.text: But if a man know not how to rule his own house, how shall he take care of the church of God?

6.text: Not a neophyte: lest being puffed up with pride, he fall into the judgment of the devil.

7.text: Moreover he must have a good testimony of them who are without: lest he fall into reproach and the snare of the devil.

8.text: Deacons in like manner chaste, not double tongued, not given to much wine, not greedy of filthy lucre:

9.text: Holding the mystery of faith in a pure conscience.

10.text: And let these also first be proved: and so let them minister, having no crime.

11.text: The women in like manner chaste, not slanderers, but sober, faithful in all things.

12.text: Let deacons be the husbands of one wife: who rule well their children, and their own houses.

13.text: For they that have ministered well, shall purchase to themselves a good degree, and much confidence in the faith which is in Christ Jesus.

14.text: These things I write to thee, hoping that I shall come to thee shortly.

15.text: But if I tarry long, that thou mayest know how thou oughtest to behave thyself in the house of God, which is the church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth.

16.text: And evidently great is the mystery of godliness, which was manifested in the flesh, was justified in the spirit, appeared unto angels, hath been preached unto the Gentiles, is believed in the world, is taken up in glory.

1.text: Now the Spirit manifestly saith, that in the last times some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to spirits of error, and doctrines of devils,

2.text: Speaking lies in hypocrisy, and having their conscience seared,

3.text: Forbidding to marry, to abstain from meats, which God hath created to be received with thanksgiving by the faithful, and by them that have known the truth.

4.text: For every creature of God is good, and nothing to be rejected that is received with thanksgiving:

5.text: For it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer.

6.text: These things proposing to the brethren, thou shalt be a good minister of Christ Jesus, nourished up in the words of faith, and of the good doctrine which thou hast attained unto.

7.text: But avoid foolish and old wives’ fables: and exercise thyself unto godliness.

8.text: For bodily exercise is profitable to little: but godliness is profitable to all things, having promise of the life that now is, and of that which is to come.

9.text: A faithful saying and worthy of all acceptation.

10.text: For therefore we labor and are reviled, because we hope in the living God, who is the Saviour of all men, especially of the faithful.

11.text: These things command and teach.

12.text: Let no man despise thy youth: but be thou an example of the faithful in word, in conversation, in charity, in faith, in chastity.

13.text: Till I come, attend unto reading, to exhortation, and to doctrine.

14.text: Neglect not the grace that is in thee, which was given thee by prophesy, with imposition of the hands of the priesthood.

15.text: Meditate upon these things, be wholly in these things: that thy profiting may be manifest to all.

16.text: Take heed to thyself and to doctrine: be earnest in them. For in doing this thou shalt both save thyself and them that hear thee.

1.text: An ancient man rebuke not, but entreat him as a father: young men, as brethren:

2.text: Old women, as mothers: young women, as sisters, in all chastity.

3.text: Honour widows, that are widows indeed.

4.text: But if any widow have children, or grandchildren, let her learn first to govern her own house, and to make a return of duty to her parents: for this is acceptable before God.

5.text: But she that is a widow indeed, and desolate, let her trust in God, and continue in supplications and prayers night and day.

6.text: For she that liveth in pleasures, is dead while she is living.

7.text: And this give in charge, that they may be blameless.

8.text: But if any man have not care of his own, and especially of those of his house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel.

9.text: Let a widow be chosen of no less than threescore years of age, who hath been the wife of one husband.

10.text: Having testimony for her good works, if she have brought up children, if she have received to harbour, if she have washed the saints’ feet, if she have ministered to them that suffer tribulation, if she have diligently followed every good work.

11.text: But the younger widows avoid. For when they have grown wanton in Christ, they will marry:

12.text: Having damnation, because they have made void their first faith.

13.text: And withal being idle they learn to go about from house to house: and are not only idle, but tattlers also, and busybodies, speaking things which they ought not.

14.text: I will therefore that the younger should marry, bear children, be mistresses of families, give no occasion to the adversary to speak evil.

15.text: For some are already turned aside after Satan.

16.text: If any of the faithful have widows, let him minister to them, and let not the church be charged: that there may be sufficient for them that are widows indeed.

17.text: Let the priests that rule well, be esteemed worthy of double honour: especially they who labour in the word and doctrine:

18.text: For the scripture saith: Thou shalt not muzzle the ox that treadeth out the corn: and, The labourer is worthy of his reward.

19.text: For the scripture saith: Thou shalt not muzzle the ox that treadeth out the corn: and, The labourer is worthy of his reward.

20.text: Them that sin reprove before all: that the rest also may have fear.

21.text: I charge thee before God, and Christ Jesus, and the elect angels, that thou observe these things without prejudice, doing nothing by declining to either side.

22.text: Impose not hands lightly upon any man, neither be partaker of other men’s sins. Keep thyself chaste.

23.text: Do not still drink water, but use a little wine for thy stomach’s sake, and thy frequent infirmities.

24.text: Some men’s sins are manifest, going before to judgment: and some men they follow after.

25.text: In like manner also good deeds are manifest: and they that are otherwise, cannot be hid.

1.text: Whosoever are servants under the yoke, let them count their masters worthy of all honour; lest the name of the Lord and his doctrine be blasphemed.

2.text: But they that have believing masters, let them not despise them, because they are brethren; but serve them the rather, because they are faithful and beloved, who are partakers of the benefit. These things teach and exhort.

3.text: If any man teach otherwise, and consent not to the sound words of our Lord Jesus Christ, and to that doctrine which is according to godliness,

4.text: He is proud, knowing nothing, but sick about questions and strifes of words; from which arise envies, contentions, blasphemies, evil suspicions,

5.text: Conflicts of men corrupted in mind, and who are destitute of the truth, supposing gain to be godliness.

6.text: But godliness with contentment is great gain.

7.text: For we brought nothing into this world: and certainly we can carry nothing out.

8.text: But having food, and wherewith to be covered, with these we are content.

9.text: For they that will become rich, fall into temptation, and into the snare of the devil, and into many unprofitable and hurtful desires, which drown men into destruction and perdition.

10.text: For the desire of money is the root of all evils; which some coveting have erred from the faith, and have entangled themselves in many sorrows.

11.text: But thou, O man of God, fly these things: and pursue justice, godliness, faith, charity, patience, mildness.

12.text: Fight the good fight of faith: lay hold on eternal life, whereunto thou art called, and hast confessed a good confession before many witnesses.

13.text: I charge thee before God, who quickeneth all things, and before Christ Jesus, who gave testimony under Pontius Pilate, a good confession,

14.text: That thou keep the commandment without spot, blameless, unto the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ,

15.text: Which in his times he shall shew who is the Blessed and only Mighty, the King of kings, and Lord of lords;

16.text: Who only hath immortality, and inhabiteth light inaccessible, whom no man hath seen, nor can see: to whom be honour and empire everlasting. Amen.

17.text: Charge the rich of this world not to be highminded, nor to trust in the uncertainty of riches, but in the living God, (who giveth us abundantly all things to enjoy,)

18.text: To do good, to be rich in good works, to give easily, to communicate to others,

19.text: To lay up in store for themselves a good foundation against the time to come, that they may lay hold on the true life.

20.text: O Timothy, keep that which is committed to thy trust, avoiding the profane novelties of words, and oppositions of knowledge falsely so called.

21.text: Which some promising, have erred concerning the faith. Grace be with thee. Amen.

1.text: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ, by the will of God, according to the promise of life, which is in Christ Jesus.

2.text: To Timothy my dearly beloved son, grace, mercy, and peace, from God the Father, and from Christ Jesus our Lord.

3.text: I give thanks to God, whom I serve from my forefathers with a pure conscience, that without ceasing, I have a remembrance of thee in my prayers, night and day.

4.text: Desiring to see thee, being mindful of thy tears, that I may be filled with joy,

5.text: Calling to mind that faith which is in thee unfeigned, which also dwelt first in thy grandmother Lois, and in thy mother Eunice, and I am certain that in thee also.

6.text: For which cause I admonish thee, that thou stir up the grace of God which is in thee, by the imposition of my hands.

7.text: For God hath not given us the spirit of fear: but of power, and of love, and of sobriety.

8.text: Be not thou therefore ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, nor of me his prisoner: but labour with the gospel, according to the power of God,

9.text: Who hath delivered us and called us by his holy calling, not according to our works, but according to his own purpose and grace, which was given us in Christ Jesus before the times of the world.

10.text: But is now made manifest by the illumination of our Saviour Jesus Christ, who hath destroyed death, and hath brought to light life and incorruption by the gospel:

11.text: Wherein I am appointed a preacher, and an apostle, and teacher of the Gentiles.

12.text: For which cause I also suffer these things: but I am not ashamed. For I know whom I have believed, and I am certain that he is able to keep that which I have committed unto him, against that day.

13.text: Hold the form of sound words, which thou hast heard of me in faith, and in the love which is in Christ Jesus.

14.text: Keep the good thing committed to thy trust by the Holy Ghost, who dwelleth in us.

15.text: Thou knowest this, that all they who are in Asia, are turned away from me: of whom are Phigellus and Hermogenes.

16.text: The Lord give mercy to the house of Onesiphorus: because he hath often refreshed me, and hath not been ashamed of my chain:

17.text: But when he was come to Rome, he carefully sought me, and found me.

18.text: The Lord grant unto him to find mercy of the Lord in that day: and in how many things he ministered unto me at Ephesus, thou very well knowest.

1.text: Thou therefore, my son, be strong in the grace which is in Christ Jesus:

2.text: And the things which thou hast heard of me by many witnesses, the same commend to faithful men, who shall be fit to teach others also.

3.text: Labour as a good soldier of Christ Jesus.

4.text: No man, being a soldier to God, entangleth himself with secular businesses; that he may please him to whom he hath engaged himself.

5.text: For he also that striveth for the mastery, is not crowned, except he strive lawfully.

6.text: The husbandman, that laboureth, must first partake of the fruits.

7.text: Understand what I say: for the Lord will give thee in all things understanding.

8.text: Be mindful that the Lord Jesus Christ is risen again from the dead, of the seed of David, according to my gospel.

9.text: Wherein I labour even unto bands, as an evildoer; but the word of God is not bound.

10.text: Therefore I endure all things for the sake of the elect, that they also may obtain the salvation, which is in Christ Jesus, with heavenly glory.

11.text: A faithful saying: for if we be dead with him, we shall live also with him.

12.text: If we suffer, we shall also reign with him. If we deny him, he will also deny us.

13.text: If we believe not, he continueth faithful, he can not deny himself.

14.text: Of these things put them in mind, charging them before the Lord. Contend not in words, for it is to no profit, but to the subverting of the hearers.

15.text: Carefully study to present thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly handling the word of truth.

16.text: But shun profane and vain babblings: for they grow much towards ungodliness.

17.text: And their speech spreadeth like a canker: of whom are Hymeneus and Philetus:

18.text: Who have erred from the truth, saying, that the resurrection is past already, and have subverted the faith of some.

19.text: But the sure foundation of God standeth firm, having this seal: the Lord knoweth who are his; and let every one depart from iniquity who nameth the name of the Lord.

20.text: But in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and silver, but also of wood and earth: and some indeed unto honour, but some unto dishonour.

21.text: If any man therefore shall cleanse himself from these, he shall be a vessel unto honour, sanctified and profitable to the Lord, prepared unto every good work.

22.text: But flee thou youthful desires, and pursue justice, faith, charity, and peace, with them that call on the Lord out of a pure heart.

23.text: And avoid foolish and unlearned questions, knowing that they beget strifes.

24.text: But the servant of the Lord must not wrangle: but be mild towards all men, apt to teach, patient,

25.text: With modesty admonishing them that resist the truth: if peradventure God may give them repentance to know the truth,

26.text: And they may recover themselves from the snares of the devil, by whom they are held captive at his will.

1.text: Know also this, that, in the last days, shall come dangerous times.

2.text: Men shall be lovers of themselves, covetous, haughty, proud, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, ungrateful, wicked,

3.text: Without affection, without peace, slanderers, incontinent, unmerciful, without kindness,

4.text: Traitors, stubborn, puffed up, and lovers of pleasures more than of God:

5.text: Having an appearance indeed of godliness, but denying the power thereof. Now these avoid.

6.text: For of these sort are they who creep into houses, and lead captive silly women laden with sins, who are led away with divers desires:

7.text: Ever learning, and never attaining to the knowledge of the truth.

8.text: Now as Jannes and Mambres resisted Moses, so these also resist the truth, men corrupted in mind, reprobate concerning the faith.

9.text: But they shall proceed no farther; for their folly shall be manifest to all men, as theirs also was.

10.text: But thou hast fully known my doctrine, manner of life, purpose, faith, longsuffering, love, patience,

11.text: Persecutions, afflictions: such as came upon me at Antioch, at Iconium, and at Lystra: what persecutions I endured, and out of them all the Lord delivered me.

12.text: And all that will live godly in Christ Jesus, shall suffer persecution.

13.text: But evil men and seducers shall grow worse and worse: erring, and driving into error.

14.text: But continue thou in those things which thou hast learned, and which have been committed to thee: knowing of whom thou hast learned them;

15.text: And because from thy infancy thou hast known the holy scriptures, which can instruct thee to salvation, by the faith which is in Christ Jesus.

16.text: All scripture, inspired of God, is profitable to teach, to reprove, to correct, to instruct in justice,

17.text: That the man of God may be perfect, furnished to every good work.

1.text: I charge thee, before God and Jesus Christ, who shall judge the living and the dead, by his coming, and his kingdom:

2.text: Preach the word: be instant in season, out of season: reprove, entreat, rebuke in all patience and doctrine.

3.text: For there shall be a time, when they will not endure sound doctrine; but, according to their own desires, they will heap to themselves teachers, having itching ears:

4.text: And will indeed turn away their hearing from the truth, but will be turned unto fables.

5.text: But be thou vigilant, labour in all things, do the work of an evangelist, fulfill thy ministry. Be sober.

6.text: For I am even now ready to be sacrificed: and the time of my dissolution is at hand.

7.text: I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith.

8.text: As to the rest, there is laid up for me a crown of justice, which the Lord the just judge will render to me in that day: and not only to me, but to them also that love his coming. Make haste to come to me quickly.

9.text: For Demas hath left me, loving this world, and is gone to Thessalonica:

10.text: Crescens into Galatia, Titus into Dalmatia.

11.text: Only Luke is with me. Take Mark, and bring him with thee: for he is profitable to me for the ministry.

12.text: But Tychicus I have sent to Ephesus.

13.text: The cloak that I left at Troas, with Carpus, when thou comest, bring with thee, and the books, especially the parchments.

14.text: Alexander the coppersmith hath done me much evil: the Lord will reward him according to his works:

15.text: Whom do thou also avoid, for he hath greatly withstood our words.

16.text: At my first answer no man stood with me, but all forsook me: may it not be laid to their charge.

17.text: But the Lord stood by me, and strengthened me, that by me the preaching may be accomplished, and that all the Gentiles may hear: and I was delivered out of the mouth of the lion.

18.text: The Lord hath delivered me from every evil work: and will preserve me unto his heavenly kingdom, to whom be glory for ever and ever. Amen.

19.text: Salute Prisca and Aquila, and the household of Onesiphorus.

20.text: Erastus remained at Corinth. And Trophimus I left sick at Miletus.

21.text: Make haste to come before winter. Eubulus and Pudens, and Linus and Claudia, and all the brethren, salute thee.

22.text: The Lord Jesus Christ be with thy spirit. Grace be with you. Amen.

1.text: Paul, a servant of God, and an apostle of Jesus Christ, according to the faith of the elect of God and the acknowledging of the truth, which is according to godliness:

2.text: Unto the hope of life everlasting, which God, who lieth not, hath promised before the times of the world:

3.text: But hath in due times manifested his word in preaching, which is committed to me according to the commandment of God our Saviour:

4.text: To Titus my beloved son, according to the common faith, grace and peace from God the Father, and from Christ Jesus our Saviour.

5.text: For this cause I left thee in Crete, that thou shouldest set in order the things that are wanting, and shouldest ordain priests in every city, as I also appointed thee:

6.text: If any be without crime, the husband of one wife, having faithful children, not accused of riot, or unruly.

7.text: For a bishop must be without crime, as the steward of God: not proud, not subject to anger, not given to wine, no striker, not greedy of filthy lucre:

8.text: But given to hospitality, gentle, sober, just, holy, continent:

9.text: Embracing that faithful word which is according to doctrine, that he may be able to exhort in sound doctrine, and to convince the gainsayers.

10.text: For there are also many disobedient, vain talkers, and seducers: especially they who are of the circumcision:

11.text: Who must be reproved, who subvert whole houses, teaching things which they ought not, for filthy lucre’s sake.

12.text: One of them a prophet of their own, said, The Cretians are always liars, evil beasts, slothful bellies.

13.text: This testimony is true. Wherefore rebuke them sharply, that they may be sound in the faith;

14.text: Not giving heed to Jewish fables and commandments of men, who turn themselves away from the truth.

15.text: All things are clean to the clean: but to them that are defiled, and to unbelievers, nothing is clean: but both their mind and their conscience are defiled.

16.text: They profess that they know God: but in their works they deny him; being abominable, and incredulous, and to every good work reprobate.

1.text: But speak thou the things that become sound doctrine:

2.text: That the aged men be sober, chaste, prudent, sound in faith, in love, in patience.

3.text: The aged women, in like manner, in holy attire, not false accusers, not given to much wine, teaching well:

4.text: That they may teach the young women to be wise, to love their husbands, to love their children,

5.text: To be discreet, chaste, sober, having a care of the house, gentle, obedient to their husbands, that the word of God be not blasphemed.

6.text: Young men, in like manner, exhort that they be sober.

7.text: In all things shew thyself an example of good works, in doctrine, in integrity, in gravity,

8.text: The sound word that can not be blamed: that he, who is on the contrary part, may be afraid, having no evil to say of us.

9.text: Exhort servants to be obedient to their masters, in all things pleasing, not gainsaying:

10.text: Not defrauding, but in all things shewing good fidelity, that they may adorn the doctrine of God our Saviour in all things:

11.text: For the grace of God our Saviour hath appeared to all men;

12.text: Instructing us, that, denying ungodliness and worldly desires, we should live soberly, and justly, and godly in this world,

13.text: Looking for the blessed hope and coming of the glory of the great God and our Saviour Jesus Christ,

14.text: Who gave himself for us, that he might redeem us from all iniquity, and might cleanse to himself a people acceptable, a pursuer of good works.

15.text: These things speak, and exhort and rebuke with all authority. Let no man despise thee.

1.text: Admonish them to be subject to princes and powers, to obey at a word, to be ready to every good work.

2.text: To speak evil of no man, not to be litigious, but gentle: shewing all mildness towards all men.

3.text: For we ourselves also were some time unwise, incredulous, erring, slaves to divers desires and pleasures, living in malice and envy, hateful, and hating one another.

4.text: But when the goodness and kindness of God our Saviour appeared:

5.text: Not by the works of justice, which we have done, but according to his mercy, he saved us, by the laver of regeneration, and renovation of the Holy Ghost;

6.text: Whom he hath poured forth upon us abundantly, through Jesus Christ our Saviour:

7.text: That, being justified by his grace, we may be heirs, according to hope of life everlasting.

8.text: It is a faithful saying: and these things I will have thee affirm constantly: that they, who believe in God, may be careful to excel in good works. These things are good and profitable unto men.

9.text: But avoid foolish questions, and genealogies, and contentions, and strivings about the law. For they are unprofitable and vain.

10.text: A man that is a heretic, after the first and second admonition, avoid:

11.text: Knowing that he, that is such an one, is subverted, and sinneth, being condemned by his own judgment.

12.text: When I shall send to thee Artemas or Tychicus, make haste to come unto me to Nicopolis. For there I have determined to winter.

13.text: Send forward Zenas, the lawyer, and Apollo, with care, that nothing be wanting to them.

14.text: And let our men also learn to excel in good works for necessary uses: that they be not unfruitful.

15.text: All that are with me salute thee: salute them that love us in the faith. The grace of God be with you all. Amen.

1.text: Paul, a prisoner of Christ Jesus, and Timothy, a brother: to Philemon, our beloved and fellow labourer;

2.text: And to Appia, our dearest sister, and to Archippus, our fellow soldier, and to the church which is in thy house:

3.text: Grace to you and peace from God our Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ.

4.text: I give thanks to my God, always making a remembrance of thee in my prayers.

5.text: Hearing of thy charity and faith, which thou hast in the Lord Jesus, and towards all the saints:

6.text: That the communication of thy faith may be made evident in the acknowledgment of every good work, that is in you in Christ Jesus.

7.text: For I have had great joy and consolation in thy charity, because the bowels of the saints have been refreshed by thee, brother.

8.text: Wherefore though I have much confidence in Christ Jesus, to command thee that which is to the purpose:

9.text: For charity sake I rather beseech, whereas thou art such a one, as Paul an old man, and now a prisoner also of Jesus Christ.

10.text: I beseech thee for my son, whom I have begotten in my bands, Onesimus,

11.text: Who hath been heretofore unprofitable to thee, but now is profitable both to me and thee,

12.text: Whom I have sent back to thee. And do thou receive him as my own bowels.

13.text: Whom I would have retained with me, that in thy stead he might have ministered to me in the bands of the gospel:

14.text: But without thy counsel I would do nothing: that thy good deed might not be as it were of necessity, but voluntary.

15.text: For perhaps he therefore departed for a season from thee, that thou mightest receive him again for ever:

16.text: Not now as a servant, but instead of a servant, a most dear brother, especially to me: but how much more to thee both in the flesh and in the Lord?

17.text: If therefore thou count me a partner, receive him as myself.

18.text: And if he hath wronged thee in any thing, or is in thy debt, put that to my account.

19.text: I Paul have written it with my own hand: I will repay it: not to say to thee, that thou owest me thy own self also.

20.text: Yea, brother. May I enjoy thee in the Lord. Refresh my bowels in the Lord.

21.text: Trusting in thy obedience, I have written to thee: knowing that thou wilt also do more than I say.

22.text: But withal prepare me also a lodging. For I hope that through your prayers I shall be given unto you.

23.text: There salute thee Epaphras, my fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus;

24.text: Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, and Luke my fellow labourers.

25.text: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.
